  instead of element values on Int32Array/Float64Array. Categorical gap, same
  family as test_gap_typed_arrays. Was passing 26/28 at v0.5.319 after the
  SSO-unboxing fix; regressed somewhere in v0.5.319→v0.5.343.
- test_json_lazy_predicates (bug): Array.isArray() returns false on the
  result of [...].map(fn). Missing isArray predicate recognition for the

Linux baseline (docs/examples/_baselines/linux/gallery.png):
- Re-blessed from the v0.5.343 CI artifact (900x1400 → 900x1024). Old baseline

Out of scope: Windows ACCESS_VIOLATION crashes in ui/layout/snippets.ts +

fix(ui): align Win64 perry-ui ABI with dispatch table (v0.5.345)

Two doc-tests crashed on Windows CI (`ui/layout/snippets.ts` and
`ui/menus/snippets.ts`) with ACCESS_VIOLATION. Root cause: three
perry-ui runtime extern signatures didn't match the arg shapes
declared in `perry-dispatch::PERRY_UI_TABLE`. On Win64 ABI, integer
and float positional args share the same positional slot indices
(RDX/XMM1, R8/XMM2, ...) so a mismatched signature reads garbage
from uninitialized registers. SysV (macOS/Linux) uses separate
int/float register pools and happened to land valid bits in the
right physical registers, so the bugs were Windows-only.

- `perry_ui_navstack_create` now takes 0 args (was `(title_ptr,
  body_handle)`); dispatch row is `args: &[]`. The previous signature
  read RCX as `*const u8` and dereferenced it in `str_from_header`.
- `perry_ui_menu_add_item_with_shortcut` reorders to `(menu, title,
  shortcut: i64, callback: f64)` matching dispatch
  `[Widget, Str, Str, Closure]`. The previous order put the closure
  pointer into the runtime's `shortcut_ptr: i64` slot.
- `perry_ui_app_set_timer` now takes the leading App handle the
  dispatch row passes — was missing, causing the f64 args to land
  in the wrong XMM slots.
- `perry_ui_stack_set_distribution` on Windows changed from `i64` to
  `f64` (already `f64` on every other platform) so the dispatched
  float arg lands in XMM1 instead of being read as garbage from RDX.
- `perry-ui-windows::toolbar::create()` now parents under the
  parking HWND. The old code passed `None` for a `WS_CHILD` parent,
  which Windows refuses with HRESULT 0x8007057E "Cannot create a
  top-level child window."

All 8 perry-ui-* platform crates updated for the first three so
the dispatch ABI is consistent everywhere, not just Windows.

Verified locally on Windows: `./scripts/run_doc_tests.ps1
--skip-xcompile --filter-exclude ui/gallery.ts` reports 76/81
passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped (matches CI shape; previously the same
sweep was 74/81 with `ui/layout/snippets.ts` and
`ui/menus/snippets.ts` reporting RUN_FAIL).

feat(updater): perry/updater subsystem — auto-update for desktop apps

Adds a `perry/updater` module that gives Perry desktop apps a built-in
update story in the Tauri/Sparkle/autoUpdater shape. Pre-fix Perry had
no update path — apps had to roll their own download + replace +
relaunch, and most just shipped without updates.

Desktop-only by design: iOS (App Store / TestFlight) and Android
(Play Store / sideloaded APK) own the install pipeline at the OS level,
so self-update is structurally impossible there.

What lands:

- `crates/perry-updater` — single crate with `core` and `desktop` as
  internal modules. core: semver compare, SHA-256 file hash verify,
  Ed25519 signature verify (raw 32-byte SHA-256 digest as the signed
  payload — documented in the .d.ts), atomic sentinel write/read/clear.
  desktop: per-OS exe-path resolution (walks to `.app` bundle on macOS,
  honors `$APPIMAGE` on Linux), atomic install with `<exe>.prev` backup,
  detached relaunch (`setsid` on Unix, `DETACHED_PROCESS` on Windows).

- Runtime additions: `js_fs_chmod_sync` (POSIX mode bits, no-op on
  Windows); `pub fn spawn_detached_command` shared helper +
  `js_child_process_spawn_detached` FFI built on top of it. Both the
  user-facing FFI and `perry-updater`'s relaunch path go through the
  same per-OS detach logic — keep `setsid` / `DETACHED_PROCESS` in one
  place.

- Stdlib additions: `js_crypto_ed25519_verify` under the existing
  `crypto` feature gate (`ed25519-dalek = "2.1"`). Raw verify primitive
  parallel to `sha256_bytes` / X25519 — the updater's `verify_signature`
  routes through this rather than pulling dalek a second time.

- Codegen: `PERRY_UPDATER_TABLE` added to `perry-dispatch/src/lib.rs`
  alongside the UI / system / i18n tables (single source of truth for
  TS-name → runtime-symbol mapping, shared with JS / WASM emitters).
  Dispatch arms wired in `lower_call.rs` (ExternFuncRef path) and
  `lower_call/native.rs` (`module == "perry/updater"`). New `chmodSync`
  arm in the `fs` block. `js_fs_chmod_sync` declaration in
  `runtime_decls.rs`. `perry/updater` added to `NATIVE_MODULES` in
  `perry-hir/src/ir.rs` so imports resolve, and to `stdlib_features.rs`
  so importing it pulls in the `crypto` feature transitively (the
  ed25519_verify symbol lives in libperry_stdlib.a).

- TS surface: `types/perry/updater/index.d.ts` (flat ambient — primitive
  symbols backed by the FFI table); `packages/perry-updater/` (npm:
  `@perry/updater`) — high-level wrapper exposing `checkForUpdate({manifestUrl,
  publicKey, currentVersion})` returning an `Update` object with
  `download(onProgress?)` and `installAndRelaunch()`, plus
  `initUpdater()` with sentinel-based crash-loop rollback and a
  graceful-exit hook + `markHealthy()` escape hatch.

- Manifest schema: JSON, schema-versioned, one entry per `<os>-<arch>`:

      {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "version": "1.4.0",
        "pubDate": "...",
        "notes": "...",
        "platforms": {
          "darwin-aarch64": { "url", "sha256", "signature", "size" },
          "windows-x86_64": { ... },
          "linux-x86_64":   { ... }
        }
      }

- Smoke tests: `scripts/smoke_updater.{sh,ps1}` exercise the full
  install + relaunch flow end-to-end. Generates a fresh Ed25519 keypair
  via openssl, builds two test binaries, signs v1.0.1, serves a manifest
  via python's http.server, runs v1.0.0, asserts v1.0.1 boots after the
  install. Verified locally on darwin-aarch64; the `.ps1` mirrors the
  shape for Windows. Mirrors the precedent set by run_doc_tests.{sh,ps1}.

What's deliberately not here:

- UI primitives (modal with `ProgressView` + "Restart Now"). I think
  that belongs inside `perry/ui` proper rather than a separate
  `@perry/updater-ui` package, so it's a follow-up PR.
- E2E in CI. The unit tests cover all the building blocks and the
  smoke is runnable manually before each release; updater smokes are
  timing-sensitive enough that manual pre-release runs catch more than
  green CI does.
- Notarization / code-signing during install. Binaries are expected to
  arrive already signed; the updater isn't a notarization tool.
- Privileged install for system-wide `/Applications` or `Program
  Files`. This PR only handles user-writable locations
  (`~/Applications`, `~/.local/bin`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`).
- Delta updates (bsdiff), multi-channel (stable/beta), staged rollouts.

# Perry runtime quirks surfaced while writing the smoke

Two things I tripped on that aren't updater-specific but are worth
filing as separate Perry runtime issues:

- `response.arrayBuffer()` returns a metadata-only object —
  `{ byteLength: N }` with no body bytes attached. See
  `crates/perry-stdlib/src/fetch.rs:1016-1037`. Confirmed runtime:
  `Buffer.from(arrayBuffer).length === 1` for a 3.4 MB response. The
  smoke pre-stages v1.0.1 via shell `cp` to work around it; the
  high-level `@perry/updater` package's `Update.download()` carries
  the same workaround caveat in a comment.
- `fs.appendFileSync` writes 0 bytes. `writeFileSync` with the same
  string writes correctly. The smoke fixture reads + concats +
  writeFileSync's instead.

The fetch hang I attributed to single-arg `console.log` in an earlier
commit was a misattribution from a bisection with a confounding
variable; the smoke fixture has multi-arg logs everywhere out of an
abundance of caution but the real trigger is something I couldn't
isolate cleanly.

# Verified

- `cargo build --release -p perry -p perry-runtime -p perry-stdlib`
  clean
- 9 unit tests pass (`core::tests::*` + `desktop::tests::*`)
- End-to-end smoke on darwin-aarch64:

      ==> running v1.0.0 (will install + relaunch v1.0.1)
      smoke test PASSED
        marker:
          1.0.0
          1.0.1

  …with `<exe>.prev` backup, install hash matches v1.0.1, new process
  detached cleanly from old.

fix(ui-{ios,tvos,visionos}): #185 Button color routes setTextColor: on UIButton (v0.5.346)

apply_inline_style routes every `color: ...` inline-style prop through
text_set_color, but on UIKit UIButton doesn't implement setTextColor:
(it uses setTitleColor:forState:). The unchecked msg_send raised
unrecognized selector → objc2 panic → non-unwinding across extern "C"
→ process abort.

Same shape as the v0.5.313 macOS bug — fix mirrors that class-probe
pattern: probe view via isKindOfClass:, route UIButton to
super::button::set_text_color (already wired with setTitleColor:
forState:UIControlStateNormal), keep UILabel on the original path,
silent no-op for anything else.

Verified end-to-end: docs/examples/ui/styling/visual_test.ts now
launches cleanly on iPhone 16 sim. Pre-fix died at the Buttons row's
"Styled" cell with color: "white" → SIGABRT.

fix(ui-windows): #210 wire 4 of 5 styling stubs (decoration/opacity/borders) (v0.5.347)

Closes 4 of the 5 deferred-paint stubs on Windows. Only `widget.shadow`
remains (needs DirectComposition — separate multi-day refactor).

- text.decoration: GetObjectW → mutate lfUnderline/lfStrikeOut →

  Falls back to Segoe UI 14/400 if no HFONT set yet.
- widget.opacity: WS_EX_LAYERED + SetLayeredWindowAttributes(LWA_ALPHA).
  Per-child WS_EX_LAYERED works on Windows 8+ (Perry's minimum).
- widget.border_color + widget.border_width: lazy SetWindowSubclass
  per HWND (idempotent via thread_local HashSet); WM_PAINT subclass
  proc calls DefSubclassProc first, then GetDC + CreatePen +
  Rectangle to draw the colored outline at client-rect bounds.
  Defaults: black 1px when either setter alone is called.

fix(fs): wire fs.appendFileSync end-to-end

Closes #226.

Pre-fix every `fs.appendFileSync(path, content)` wrote 0 bytes — the
file wasn't even created on a fresh path. The runtime function
(`crates/perry-runtime/src/fs.rs::js_fs_append_file_sync`) was already
correct (`OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).write_all(...)`),
the gap was in two earlier passes.

The HIR carries a dedicated `Expr::FsAppendFileSync(path, content)`
variant for this. The named-import path of the SWC→HIR lowerer
already produced it (`import { appendFileSync } from "fs"`), and the
JS / WASM backends both had codegen arms for it. Two things on the
LLVM track were missing:

1. `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call.rs` — the namespace-import
   path (`import * as fs from "fs"; fs.appendFileSync(...)`) had arms
   for `writeFileSync` / `existsSync` / `mkdirSync` / `unlinkSync`
   etc. but not `appendFileSync`. Without this, the call slipped past
   as a generic `Call { callee: PropertyGet { object:
   NativeModuleRef("fs"), property: "appendFileSync" }, args: [...] }`
   and `Expr::FsAppendFileSync` never got emitted for the most common
   usage shape. Added the arm next to `writeFileSync`.

2. `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs` — even when the HIR variant
   was emitted (named-import path), the LLVM backend had no arm next
   to `Expr::FsWriteFileSync`. The call fell through and was silently
   dropped. Added the arm; same shape as `FsWriteFileSync`, calls
   `js_fs_append_file_sync`.

Plus the runtime declaration in `crates/perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls.rs`
so the LLVM module declares `js_fs_append_file_sync` for the linker.

# Verified

`cargo build --release -p perry` clean, `cargo test -p perry-hir
-p perry-codegen --lib` green (20 tests, no regressions).

End-to-end against `node --experimental-strip-types` on the new
`test-files/test_fs_appendfile.ts`:

    perry:                  node:
    line one                line one
                            <blank>
    line one                line one
    line two                line two
                            <blank>
    line one                line one
    line two                line two
    line three              line three

Identical output.

# Issue diagnosis correction

The issue body diagnosed only the codegen-arm-faltante (path 2 above).
While iterating on this fix I hit the surprising case where adding
just that arm changed nothing for `import * as fs from "fs"; fs.append(...)`.
Tracing the HIR confirmed the namespace-import path needed extending
too. Both arms in this commit; either alone is insufficient for the
common usage pattern.

fix(fs): wire fs.appendFileSync end-to-end (closes #226)

fix(codegen): #221 module-level empty const arrays drop arr[i]= writes (v0.5.351)

`crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::Expr::IndexSet` funneled module-global
array receivers (resolved via `ctx.module_globals` rather than
`ctx.locals`) through `js_array_set_f64` — the bounds-checked variant
that returns silently when `index >= length`. For an empty array
(length=0), every `A[i] = v` from inside a function was a no-op, so both
the value and the implicit `.length` update vanished.

Fix: detect the module-globals branch in IndexSet, use
`js_array_set_f64_extend` (the realloc-capable variant the local-stack-
slot fast path already uses), and write the new pointer back to the
global slot — symmetric with `lower_index_set_fast`'s writeback to a
stack-local slot. The genuine non-LocalGet and closure-capture cases
(no writeback target available) keep the bounded path.

Surfaced while debugging Bloom-Engine/jump's `discoverLevels()`
populating `LEVEL_FILES` / `LEVEL_NAMES` (declared empty at module
level) via index-assignment from a function — the level-select screen
rendered empty because every write dropped.

Verified against the issue's repro byte-for-byte vs Node; new
regression test covers empty string/number/object arrays + index-set
past existing length on a pre-sized array. Gap tests 25/28 = baseline.

fix(codegen+stdlib): wire better-sqlite3 Database ctor + chained Statement methods (v0.5.352)

Restores end-to-end better-sqlite3 support that the lower_call refactor
silently broke. Three connected fixes:

* lower_call/builtin.rs: add a "Database" arm calling js_sqlite_open.
  Without it, `new Database(path)` fell into lower_new's empty-object
  placeholder, so `db` was a generic ObjectHeader pointer instead of a
  real SqliteDbHandle. db.prepare(...) then unboxed that bogus pointer
  and prepare returned -1; every chained .run/.get/.all silently
  produced undefined.

* lower/expr_call.rs: extend the chained-method dispatch so
  db.prepare(sql).run/get/all resolves the outer call against the
  Statement returned by prepare. Same wiring covers mongodb db→Database,
  collection→Collection, pg connect→PoolClient, mysql2
  getConnection→PoolConnection, ioredis duplicate→Redis.

* perry-stdlib/sqlite.rs: guard params_from_array against NaN-tagged
  non-array inputs. Codegen pads omitted-arg slots with TAG_UNDEFINED,
  which looks like a non-null pointer; dereferencing as
  *const ArrayHeader is UB and the garbage `length` crashed
  stmt.run() / stmt.all() on no-arg calls.

fix(fetch): copy body bytes into response.arrayBuffer() result (#232)

Closes #227. `await response.arrayBuffer()` was resolving with a metadata-only `{byteLength}` stub; bytes were dropped. Two-part fix: (1) `js_response_array_buffer` now allocates a real BufferHeader and memcpys `resp.body` into it; (2) `js_uint8array_new` POINTER_TAG arm gains a registered-buffer branch that does buffer→buffer memcpy instead of treating the BufferHeader as an ArrayHeader of f64s. `response.blob()` keeps the stub shape (tracked as #234).

fix(codegen+compile): pin clang -target on host builds + clarify Windows messages (v0.5.353)

Fixes the LNK2019 __main link failure surfaced by users with non-MSVC clang on Windows
PATH (MinGW/MSYS2/Anaconda/Rust GNU toolchain bundles), plus the misleading "libperry_*.a"
log message that confused users into thinking Perry was searching for the wrong file.

- linker.rs::compile_ll_to_object now ALWAYS passes -target. When the caller doesn't
  specify one, derive the host default via codegen::default_target_triple. Without this
  pin, clang's "use my own default Target:, override the IR's target triple" behavior
  silently rewrote Perry's x86_64-pc-windows-msvc IR to windows-gnu, causing LLVM's
  mingw32 COFF emitter to inject a __main libgcc reference that lld-link can't resolve.

- New probe_clang_default_triple runs `clang --version` once per process. On a Windows
  host where clang's default is GNU/MinGW but we're targeting msvc, prints a single
  informational note pointing at `winget install LLVM.LLVM` / PERRY_LLVM_CLANG. Silent
  on a clean msvc setup. Suppress with PERRY_NO_CLANG_PROBE=1.

- When clang -c does fail, the error now includes the resolved clang path, the first
  line of `clang --version`, the requested -target, the temp .ll path, and a
  pattern-matched hint via the new build_clang_failure_hint helper. 4 unit tests pin
  the four hint branches (MinGW-on-Windows-msvc, override-warning, missing-library,
  generic fallback).

- optimized_libs.rs now picks platform-correct names for the "using prebuilt ..."
  workspace-not-found log message (perry_runtime.lib + perry_stdlib.lib on Windows).
  The actual lib lookup was already correct; only the log was wrong.

- default_target_triple promoted from private fn to pub(crate) fn so linker.rs can
  reach it.

Verified: cargo build --release clean; 4 new perry-codegen::linker::tests pass;
smoke compile + UI compile both produce working .exes; workspace-not-found message
path now reads `perry_runtime.lib + perry_stdlib.lib`.

chore(packaging): Scoop bucket manifest + SHA256 sidecars in release workflow

- bucket/perry.json: Scoop manifest pinned to v0.5.345 (latest GitHub release).
  depends on `main/llvm` so `scoop install perry` auto-pulls the official
  MSVC-default LLVM toolchain — sidesteps the non-MSVC clang default trap
  that bit Windows users in v0.5.345 (the __main link error fixed in
  v0.5.353). bin: perry.exe; extract_dir flat (zip is already flat).
  checkver pulls latest release tag from the GitHub API; autoupdate's
  hash.url uses `$url.sha256` so the bumper resolves hashes from the
  sidecar files we now upload.

- release-packages.yml: new "Compute SHA256 sidecar" steps (Unix +
  Windows) emit `<artifact>.sha256` next to every release archive,
  uploaded alongside the .tar.gz / .zip on each `release` event.
  Format matches `sha256sum` exactly (two-space separator) so any
  downstream tool that grep-cuts the first field works. Useful for
  the Scoop autoupdate flow today and any future package-manager
  bumpers (winget/chocolatey/Homebrew) that prefer URL-resolvable
  hashes over re-downloading the archive.

- README.md: new "Windows (Scoop)" section under Installation:
  `scoop bucket add perry-ts https://github.com/PerryTS/perry; scoop
  install perry-ts/perry`.

Verified: manifest validates against ScoopInstaller/Scoop's official
JSON schema (draft-07); release-zip URL is 200 OK; pinned hash
matches the actual zip bytes; autoupdate URL templates align with
the workflow's new sidecar paths.

fix(fetch+promise+codegen): #236 default User-Agent + .then(console.log) hang + Error rejection (v0.5.355)

Three independent bugs surfaced from the OP's `await fetch(github).json()` +
`.then(console.log)` repro. Fixes:

(1) Shared HTTP client now sets a default User-Agent so api.github.com (and
    other endpoints that 403 anonymous requests) work out of the box.
    Per-request UA still wins via reqwest's per-builder header replace.

(2) Promise propagation when callback is null: js_promise_resolve / _reject
    / _then's already-settled paths used to gate the TASK_QUEUE push on
    callback non-null. The microtask runner has propagation logic for null-
    callback tasks (forwards value/reason to `next`), but those tasks were
    never pushed, so .then(NULL_CALLBACK) chains stayed pending forever.
    Push when there's either a callback OR a chained `next` promise.

(3) console.log used as a value (`.then(console.log)`, `let f = console.log`)
    used to lower to a `0.0` sentinel ClosurePtr. New js_console_log_as_closure
    runtime fn returns a singleton ClosureHeader whose func_ptr is a thunk
    into js_console_log_dynamic; codegen value path emits a call to it.
    GC root scanner pins the singleton against sweeps.

Bonus: every fetch promise rejection used to NaN-box a bare *StringHeader
with POINTER_TAG, which the uncaught-exception printer read as
*ObjectHeader.object_type and printed as `Uncaught exception: [object
Object]`. New fetch_error_bits<S: AsRef<str>> helper allocates a real
ErrorHeader so the printer takes the dedicated Error arm and emits
`Uncaught exception: Error: <message>` plus a stack frame. Bulk-replaced
16 call sites.

network-free regression test (test_issue_236_fetch_then_console_log.ts).

fix(dispatch): textfieldGetString / textareaGetString return Str (v0.5.356)

Both perry-dispatch rows had `ret: ReturnKind::F64`, but the runtime FFIs
return `*mut StringHeader` cast to i64 (GC-pinned via GC_FLAG_PINNED so
the alloc survives until codegen NaN-boxes it). Treating the pointer bits
as a raw double produced gibberish like "27017" / "65933097631650390000..."
that downstream string ops then crashed on or silently propagated.

Flip to `ReturnKind::Str` so codegen NaN-boxes with STRING_TAG (0x7FFF)
and the property dispatch sees a proper string. Two-row metadata fix; no
runtime, codegen, or HIR changes needed. Drift integration test clean.

fix(runtime+codegen): #233 async-fn array param push silently capped at 16 (v0.5.357)

Array.push from inside an async function silently capped at 16 elements
when the array was passed in as a parameter — the default initial array
capacity. Once exceeded, js_array_push_f64 reallocates and returns a new
pointer; the sync wrapper case is fine because functions get inlined,
but async functions are state machines that can't be inlined, so the
caller's parameter slot was never updated. Caller's `samples` stayed
pointing at the OLD 16-cap ArrayHeader while every subsequent push
operated on a separate orphaned new array.

Fix: install a forwarding pointer at the OLD location on every grow,
reusing the GC's existing GC_FLAG_FORWARDED mechanism (originally for
the copying evacuation pass). All array-pointer reads/writes follow
the chain — clean_arr_ptr, js_value_length_f64, three inline IndexGet
codegen fast paths, lower_index_set_fast, trace_array, and
rewrite_array_fields all detect the FORWARDED flag and route to the
forwarding-aware slow path or trace through to the new location.

Regression test exercises number/string/object element types, nested
async wrappers, post-push slice/indexOf/iteration, and IndexSet via
stale pointers — all byte-for-byte against node --experimental-strip-types.
Gap tests 25/28 = baseline; runtime + GC test suites 21/21 + 40/40 still
passing.

fix(codegen+hir): #235 method-default-param dispatch passes garbage for skipped trailing args (v0.5.358)

`await foo.method({...})` could silently hang the async chain when the
method had a default param the caller skipped. The original repro from
@perryts/mongodb (`await col.findOne({ title: '...' })` — `findOne(filter,
options = {})` skipping `options`) hung indefinitely after "1 findOne
start", sometimes SIGSEGV, sometimes silent exit 0.

Two contributing parts both compiled fine but interacted to read garbage:

1. The cross-module method DECLARE in `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs`
   was hardcoded to 6 doubles ("safe upper bound"), but call sites only
   passed `args.len() + 1` doubles. Win64 / SysV ABI placed the user-args
   in d0..dN and left dN+1..d5 holding whatever the prior call's leftover
   state had stamped — typically a real heap pointer from the just-finished
   `MongoClient.connect()` chain. The callee's `findOne(filter, options)`
   then read `options` from d2 and dereferenced `options.session` against
   that stale pointer, which silently hung in `js_native_call_method`
   rather than throwing.

2. `crates/perry-hir/src/lower_decl.rs::lower_class_method` had no
   `build_default_param_stmts` call — the `if (param === undefined)
   param = default;` desugaring fired only for free functions and
   constructors, never for instance/static class methods. So even when a
   TS author wrote `findOne(filter, options = {})`, the body just did
   `options.session` directly with no default substitution.

Fix is in three places:

(a) `ImportedClass` gets a parallel `method_param_counts: Vec<usize>`
    populated from `class.methods.iter().map(|m| m.params.len())` at the
    4 import-resolve sites in `crates/perry/src/commands/compile.rs` plus
    2 test sites in `compile/object_cache.rs`. The cross-module method
    declare at codegen.rs:980 now reads this Vec and emits `arity + 1`
    doubles instead of 6.

(b) New `method_param_counts: HashMap<(class, method), usize>` field on
    `CrossModuleCtx` + `FnCtx`, built once in `compile_module` from BOTH
    `hir.classes` AND `opts.imported_classes` — covers local + cross-module
    dispatch uniformly. Both dispatch tower sites in `lower_call.rs` (the
    dynamic-dispatch tower at line 1173 + the static-dispatch + virtual-
    override site at line 1374) now look up the implementor's max arity
    (max across all overrides for the static case) and pad `lowered_args`
    with TAG_UNDEFINED to `max_arity + 1` total. The ncm fallback path
    inside the dynamic-dispatch tower changes
    `iter().skip(1).enumerate()` → `iter().skip(1).take(n).enumerate()`
    so the padding entries don't overflow the n-sized buffer.

(c) `lower_class_method` prepends the same `build_default_param_stmts`
    block already used by free functions and constructors. Without this,
    even the now-correct TAG_UNDEFINED arrival in the callee would leave
    the body reading `param == undefined` instead of the declared default.

Side effect of the cache-key derivation: `compute_object_cache_key`
includes the new `method_param_counts` in the hash so changes to a
method's arity invalidate consumers.

fix(fetch): #234 real Blob with arrayBuffer/text/bytes/slice instance methods

Pre-fix `await response.blob()` returned a metadata-only stub `{size, type}`
and silently dropped `resp.body`. Calls to `blob.arrayBuffer()` / `.text()` /
`.bytes()` / `.slice()` got nothing because no codegen dispatch arms existed.

Three-part fix:

1. Runtime (perry-stdlib/src/fetch.rs): new BlobData + BLOB_REGISTRY +
   alloc_blob mirroring HEADERS_REGISTRY/alloc_headers. js_response_blob
   rewritten to clone body bytes + content-type into a fresh BlobData,
   register it, resolve the promise with the numeric handle as f64. 6 new
   FFIs: js_blob_size, js_blob_type, js_blob_array_buffer (allocates real
   BufferHeader same shape as #232's response.arrayBuffer fix),
   js_blob_bytes (alias), js_blob_text (UTF-8 lossy decode matching WHATWG
   replacement-character semantics), js_blob_slice with NaN sentinels for
   missing numeric args, null type_ptr to inherit, negative-index
   normalisation per WHATWG Blob spec.

2. HIR (perry-hir/src/destructuring.rs): two new lower_var_decl arms next
   to the existing Response.clone() propagation. `const blob = await
   <recv>.blob()` where <recv> is fetch::Response → register blob::Blob.
   `const b2 = <recv>.slice(...)` where <recv> is blob::Blob → propagate
   so chained slicing keeps Blob-ness. Existing native-instance dispatch
   in expr_call.rs / expr_member.rs then routes .text() / .size / etc. to
   NativeMethodCall { module: "blob" } automatically.

3. Codegen (perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs + runtime_decls.rs): new
   `if module == "blob"` arm after the existing fetch arm, dispatching
   size → DOUBLE return, type → STRING_TAG NaN-box, arrayBuffer/bytes/text
   → Promise pointer + nanbox_pointer_inline, slice → 0-3 args with
   double_literal(f64::NAN) sentinels. 6 new declare_function rows.

fix(codegen): declare @llvm.assume intrinsic in IR module prelude (#241)

`crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs` and `lower_call.rs` emit
`call void @llvm.assume(i1 ...)` six times for branchless Buffer bounds
checks (the v0.5.183 #92 numeric-read intrinsic + the v0.5.190 small-buffer
slab fast path), but the intrinsic was never declared in the LLVM IR
module's prelude. The math intrinsics (`llvm.sqrt.f64`, `llvm.floor.f64`,
etc.) are declared at runtime_decls.rs:117-121 — assume was simply missed.

Apple Clang ≥21 (Xcode 26 — what local devs run) auto-recognises the
intrinsic even when undeclared in the IR. Apple Clang 15 (LLVM 17 — what
ships on the macos-14 GitHub runner via Xcode 15.x) requires the explicit
declaration and errors out:

    /var/folders/.../perry_llvm.ll:1281:13: error: use of undefined value '@llvm.assume'
      call void @llvm.assume(i1 %r43)
    1 error generated.

This was the actual root cause behind the long-tail of `ci-env`
Buffer/typed-array test skips in `test-parity/known_failures.json`. The
diagnosis path:

1. The compile-stderr capture artifacts added in PR #239 preserved the
   actual error message for the first time.
2. Downloading `parity-compile-errors-macOS` from a CI run revealed all
   11 failing tests share the exact same `@llvm.assume` undefined-value
   error — not the speculated SDK/linker version interaction.

`runtime_decls.rs`, alongside the existing math-intrinsic declarations.

  Buffer-family `SKIP_TESTS` list (test_gap_buffer_ops, test_buffer_*,

fix(compile): #240 type-only-imported interface drops dispatch silently (v0.5.362)

When a consumer module type-imports an interface and calls methods on a
value typed `: Interface`, the codegen emitted a generic
property-get-then-closure-call that resolved `obj.method` to `undefined`
(methods aren't stored as fields on instances). The dispatch tower at
`crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs::needs_dynamic_dispatch` found
zero implementors and skipped its tower; the closure-call fallback then
read a non-existent field and invoked `undefined()`.

Root cause: type-only imports (`import type { Driver }`) are stripped at
HIR lowering (`crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs:2777`), so the interface's
source module never enters `ctx.native_modules`. If no value-side
import happens to bring an implementer along for the ride, the
consumer's `imported_classes` list is empty and `ctx.methods` has no
entry for the called method.

Fix in `crates/perry/src/commands/compile.rs`: new polymorphic-receiver
augmentation pass after the existing import walk. Scans every
function/method/field type in the consumer's HIR for `Named(X)`
references whose X doesn't resolve to any class/interface/enum/type-
alias in the program HIR (`all_program_type_names` built once across
`ctx.native_modules`) and isn't in a curated TS/runtime builtin set
(Promise, Array, Map, Set, Date, Buffer + typed arrays + utility-type
family). When such an unresolved name is found, every program-wide
exported class is pulled into `imported_classes`. The existing dedup
keeps it idempotent; the dispatch tower at the call site filters per-
method-name so IR size stays bounded by the implementing-class count.

Without `implements`-clause tracking we can't be more surgical, but
the conservative "pull everything" matches the existing precedent for
namespace imports already in this file.

Validation:
- 4-file repro (sync + async variants) flips from
  `consume: m typeof=undefined` → `[Impl.greet] CALLED / m typeof=string`
- Workload's `.o` post-fix references `_perry_method_impl_ts__Impl__greet`
  directly via the dispatch tower (was `_js_object_get_field_by_name_f64`
  + `_js_closure_call1` pre-fix).
- New regression test `test-files/test_issue_240_interface_dispatch.ts`
  covers in-file interface dispatch shape (cross-module repro is
  verified externally — Perry's test-files set is single-file).
- Gap tests 25/28 = unchanged baseline.
- 12-test regression set runs identically pre/post-fix; the lone async-
  ordering quirk in test_issue_235 is pre-existing and unrelated (test
  235 has all-local classes, no unresolved Names → augmentation pass
  doesn't trigger for it).

Closes #240

Three parallel audits against Huawei's real sources caught seven
install-blocking bugs in the from-memory B.1-B.3 implementation.
Auditing against:
  - developtools_hapsigner (hap-sign-tool CLI spec)
  - developtools_packing_tool (pack.info canonical parser, C++ + Java)
  - arkui_napi / ace_napi (napi_module_register semantics)
  - arkcompiler_ets_frontend (es2abc CLI + supported extensions)
  - applications_app_samples (minimal reference HAPs)
  - openharmony/docs app.json5 + module.json5 references

Fixes landed in this commit:

1. NAPI modname ↔ .so filename mismatch (worst bug — silently fails).
   nm_modname was hardcoded "entry", default output was lib<stem>.so.
   OHOS's NativeModuleManager resolves `import X from 'libfoo.so'` by
   stripping lib/.so from the filename and looking up that name, so
   unless .so was literally libentry.so, the import resolved to
   undefined and every property access threw at load time.
   Fix: derive nm_modname at .init_array time via dladdr(register_module,
   &info), extract basename of dli_fname, strip "lib" prefix + ".so"
   suffix, copy into a 256-byte static buffer. Works for any -o output
   name. Falls back to "entry" if dladdr fails (matches DevEco's
   default-template modname). Single-threaded (init constructor runs
   before any ArkTS code) so no locking needed.

2. app.json5 missing minAPIVersion / targetAPIVersion / apiReleaseType.
   HAP install-time verification rejects without these. Added all three:
   minAPI=11 (HarmonyOS NEXT floor), target=12 (current DevEco 5.x),
   apiReleaseType="Release" (valid values: "Canary<N>" / "Beta<N>" /
   "Release"). Note apiReleaseType is spelled DIFFERENTLY from the
   releaseType key used inside pack.info — same semantics, different
   key name. Java parser checks both locations separately.

3. pack.info structural fixes.
   - summary.modules[0].name was bundleName; must be module name "entry".
   - summary.modules[0].package same — must be "entry".
   - packages[0].name same — must be "entry".
     Confusingly, summary.app.bundleName above IS the bundleName. Most
     common shape bug in hand-rolled HAPs per the audit.
   - apiVersion belonged under summary.app.apiVersion, not
     summary.modules[0].apiVersion. The Java parser reads the app-level
     path; a module-level duplicate is silently ignored. We put it in
     both locations for robustness across SDK versions.
   - deviceType (singular in pack.info, plural in module.json5) must
     match byte-for-byte; added "2in1" to pack.info side to align with
     module.json5's ["phone","tablet","2in1"]. packing_tool's HapVerify
     rejects mismatches before hap-sign even runs.
   - API target 10 -> 12. 10 = HarmonyOS 4.x, pre-NEXT.

4. hap-sign CLI reworked per developtools_hapsigner README lines 297-314.
   - -appCertFile and -profileFile are DIFFERENT files (cert chain
     .cer/.pem vs signed provisioning profile .p7b). B.3 passed the same
     PERRY_HARMONYOS_PROFILE path to both; hap-sign rejects (cert chain
     parser can't read p7b). Split into two env vars:
       PERRY_HARMONYOS_CERT     — cert chain (.cer)
       PERRY_HARMONYOS_PROFILE  — signed profile (.p7b)
   - -keyPwd added. DevEco-generated p12s have a separate key password
     from the keystore password. New env var PERRY_HARMONYOS_KEY_PASSWORD;
     falls back to PERRY_HARMONYOS_P12_PASSWORD if unset (common case
     where they're the same).
   - -keyAlias was hardcoded "perry-signing-key" which never matches
     anything. DevEco auto-signing uses "debugKey". New env var
     PERRY_HARMONYOS_KEY_ALIAS, defaults to "debugKey".
   - -signAlg configurable via PERRY_HARMONYOS_SIGN_ALG (defaults
     SHA256withECDSA; only other accepted value is SHA384withECDSA).
   - Explicit -profileSigned 1, -inForm zip, -signCode 1. These are
     defaults but explicit survives SDK-version drift.

5. ets-loader probe paths were all wrong.
   - B.3 probed <sdk>/build-tools/ets-loader/bin/ark_ts2abc_bin/es2abc
     + three variants under <sdk>/toolchains/. None exist in DevEco 5.x.
   - Real path: <sdk_root>/<api>/openharmony/ets/build-tools/ets-loader/.
     find_harmonyos_sdk returns <api>/openharmony/native/, so ets-loader
     is at `native/../ets/build-tools/ets-loader/`.
   - es2abc lives under ets-loader in a host-OS-specific subdir:
       build-mac/bin/es2abc   (macOS)
       build-win/bin/es2abc   (Windows)
       build/bin/es2abc       (Linux)
     We validate presence but don't invoke it directly — ets-loader
     spawns it internally.

6. Pipeline structurally rewritten. es2abc does NOT accept .ets — only
   js/ts/as. B.3's "run es2abc over each .ets file" approach was
   infeasible. Real pipeline is two-stage: ets-loader (Node/rollup npm
   package) desugars ArkUI decorators + bundles .ets -> .ts, then
   invokes bundled es2abc to emit .abc. compile_ets_to_abc now invokes
   ets-loader via `node <loader>/main.js --hap-mode=release <ets-dir>`
   from the staging dir. Hvigor orchestrates this with a richer
   build-profile.json5 we don't fully synthesize yet; our minimal
   invocation may or may not work on first try. First emulator run will
   tell us if we need to vendor more hvigor glue.

7. Source-fallback message updated. Physical NEXT devices reject
   .ets-source HAPs entirely (no debug-mode exception). Fallback now
   clearly states the HAP won't install and points the user at
   DevEco/hvigor for completion.

feat(codegen): #248 Phase 2B — JsCreateCallback closure marshaling (v0.5.369) (#254)

Wires Perry closures passed to JS-imported functions end-to-end so
`arr.forEach(cb)` / `gameLoop.use(handler)` actually fire. Phase 2A
(v0.5.368) bailed at codegen for JsCreateCallback because the runtime
FFI `js_create_callback(func_ptr, closure_env, param_count)` expects
`func_ptr` to have signature `(closure_env: i64, args_ptr: *const f64,
args_len: i64) -> f64` (the V8 native_callback_trampoline contract),
but Perry closure bodies have `(closure_ptr, arg0, arg1, ...)` per
arity — no direct call-compatible mapping.

Three pieces:

(1) New runtime helper `js_closure_call_array` in
crates/perry-runtime/src/closure.rs that takes (closure_env: i64,
args_ptr: *const f64, args_len: i64) and dispatches to the right
js_closure_callN per args_len. Mirrors the existing js_native_call_value
but with i64 first-arg so SysV-x64 / Win64 register lands correctly.
Body switches on args_len (0..16) and unboxes any INT32_TAG-tagged
f64 to a plain double before passing — V8 NaN-boxes JS integers with
INT32_TAG=0x7FFE, but Perry's closure-body arithmetic uses raw
fadd/fsub/fmul on f64s and assumes plain doubles.

(2) JsCreateCallback codegen arm in crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs
now lowers to: lower closure expr, unbox to i64 closure pointer,
ptrtoint @js_closure_call_array to i64, call js_create_callback with
(func_addr, closure_ptr, param_count). Returns NaN-boxed JS handle.

(3) Closure-collector in crates/perry-codegen/src/collectors.rs adds
8 new arms for the Js* HIR family so closures nested inside JS-interop
expressions don't fall through `_ => {}` and end up referenced via
js_closure_alloc with their bodies never defined.

codegen scope.

fix(jsruntime): #255 re-entrancy — Perry callbacks can read JS object props (v0.5.370) (#259)

When a Perry closure passed to a JS-imported function (via JsCreateCallback,
landed in #248 Phase 2B / v0.5.369) reads a property from a JS object
passed in as a callback argument, perry-jsruntime panicked twice in a
row: first with "RefCell already borrowed" (the inner with_runtime
tried to borrow_mut the JsRuntimeState that the outer was still holding),
then with "active scope can't be dropped" (the inner FFI created a new
V8 HandleScope that conflicted with the trampoline's existing active
scope under deno_core's scope tracking).

Two cascading fixes in perry-jsruntime:

1. with_runtime + ensure_runtime_initialized are now re-entrancy-safe
   via thread-local REENTRY_PTR<Cell<*mut JsRuntimeState>>. Outer
   stashes its &mut on entry; inner re-entrant calls reuse the stashed
   pointer instead of acquiring a second RefCell::borrow_mut. Drop guard
   clears the pointer on normal return AND panic-unwind.

2. native_callback_trampoline now stashes its V8 &mut HandleScope in
   thread-local REENTRY_SCOPE_PTR (via stash_trampoline_scope() which
   returns a TrampolineScopeGuard for LIFO restore). js_handle_object_get_property
   checks for the stashed scope and reuses it (via unsafe
   try_trampoline_scope() helper) instead of calling
   state.runtime.handle_scope() — the latter conflicts with V8's
   internal scope-stack tracking when called nested inside a trampoline.

js_handle_object_get_property body factored into get_property_with_scope()
so both paths (normal: new scope; re-entrant: trampoline's scope)
share the same logic.

Other re-entrant FFIs (js_set_property, js_call_method nested,
js_handle_array_get, js_handle_array_length) still use the
state.runtime.handle_scope() pattern and remain panic-prone from
inside callbacks. Refactoring them to use try_trampoline_scope is
mechanical and tracked as a follow-up.

Safety: the raw-pointer escape hatch is the standard callback-driven
re-entrancy pattern. The outer &mut reference is paused on the call
stack while V8 → trampoline → Perry callback → inner FFI runs; they
never alias in time. Strictly UB by Rust's aliasing rules but standard
across callback-driven libraries; documented as `unsafe fn`.

New regression test test_issue_255_jsruntime_reentrancy.ts + fixture

fix(async): #256 spec-compliant microtask ordering for plain async functions (v0.5.371) (#262)

Pre-fix Perry's async functions ran their entire body synchronously on
the calling thread with each await busy-waiting for the Promise to
settle. This diverges from spec semantics where an await must yield to
the microtask queue, so synchronous code following an unawaited async
call runs before the awaited body's continuation.

The fix is a CPS / state-machine transform mirroring the existing
function* generator transform:

1. New `crates/perry-transform/src/async_to_generator.rs` pre-pass
   rewrites await→yield in plain async function bodies, hoists
   non-top-level awaits into fresh Lets, and flips the function flags.

2. `transform_generator_function` reads `was_plain_async` and wraps
   the resulting iterator in an inline async-step driver built from
   plain Promise.then chains (no new runtime helper).

3. `linearize_body` Try-arm guard widened to also fire when finally
   has yields (await using desugars to try { } finally { await
   dispose() }).

4. Hoisted-Let rewrite extended to recursively descend into nested
   control-flow (for-of loops inside state bodies).

5. `compute_max_local_id` extended to scan class member bodies to
   prevent ID collisions with v0.5.323 issue #212 method-local
   rebind ids.

6. Microtask runner unwraps thenables when .then callbacks return
   Promises (spec requirement; chains the next promise to the
   returned thenable's eventual state).

Conservative scope: skips modules with __perry_cap_* classes (issue

tracked as follow-up work.

fix(codegen): #263 arrow function class field SIGSEGV when reading this (v0.5.377)

Pre-fix `apply_field_initializers_recursive` lowered every field initializer
through Expr::PropertySet { object: This, ... }. For arrow inits with
captures_this=true, that path lowered the closure (which reserves a capture
slot at index auto_captures.len() initialized to 0.0) and stored the closure
pointer as the field — but never patched the reserved this-slot with the
constructor's this. Inside the arrow body, Expr::This read 0.0 from the
slot, then `this.value` dereferenced address 0 → SIGSEGV.

Fix mirrors the patch-after-build pattern already used by lower_object_literal
for object-literal methods. New arm in the per-field loop: when init_expr
is Expr::Closure { captures_this: true, .. }, lower the closure, read the
current this from ctx.this_stack.last(), call js_closure_set_capture_f64
with this_idx = compute_auto_captures(...).len(), then emit the
js_object_set_field_by_name write directly (bypassing PropertySet would
re-lower the closure expression and produce a fresh, unpatched copy).

exact issue repro + multi-arg arrow + per-instance capture (two Counter
instances each call inc = () => { this.count++; ... } and observe
independent counts). All 4 outputs match `node --experimental-strip-types`

fix(async): closes #264 — conditional await-return in if/else branches returns wrong value (#280)

`return await x` inside an if/else branch (and similar shapes like a
deep `await`-then-return chain) returned `0` instead of the awaited
value after the v0.5.371 async-to-generator transform.

Root cause: `linearize_body` in `generator.rs` fell through to the
generic `Stmt::Return(val)` arm for `Stmt::Return(Some(Expr::Yield{..}))`.
That arm embedded the `Yield` expression directly as the iterator result's
`value`, but `Expr::Yield` evaluates to `double_literal(0.0)` in codegen
(it's only meaningful as a state-machine split point). So the awaited value
was never propagated — the state machine yielded `0` and returned `{value:
0, done: true}` rather than actually suspending on the awaited Promise and
resuming with its result.

Fix: add a `Stmt::Return(Some(Expr::Yield{..}))` arm in `linearize_body`
that handles `return await x` correctly by:
1. Emitting a real `StateExit::Yield { value: yield_val }` state (so the
   async-step driver can `Promise.resolve(x).then(...)` and resume with
   the resolved value in `__sent`).

fix(runtime): closes #267 — dispatch .map/.filter on any-typed arrays via GC type check in js_native_call_method (#283)

When `.map()` or `.filter()` is called on an `any`-typed variable that
holds an array at runtime (e.g. the result of `JSON.parse(largeBlob)`),
the HIR lowerer conservatively skips `Expr::ArrayMap`/`Expr::ArrayFilter`
because the method name overlaps with user-class method names (the
`is_class_overlapping_method` guard in `lower/expr_call.rs`). The call
falls through to `js_native_call_method`, which had no handler for `"map"`
on `GC_TYPE_ARRAY` / `GC_TYPE_LAZY_ARRAY` objects — it returned 0.0,
causing `Array.isArray(parsed.map(fn))` to return `false` instead of `true`.

Fix: add an early array-method dispatch block in `js_native_call_method`
(`crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs`) that reads the GC header obj_type
of the runtime receiver. When it is `GC_TYPE_ARRAY` or `GC_TYPE_LAZY_ARRAY`,
`"map"` and `"filter"` route directly to `js_array_map` / `js_array_filter`
(which already call `clean_arr_ptr()` internally to handle lazy→real
materialization). User-class instances (`GC_TYPE_OBJECT`) fall through to the
existing object-field scan unchanged.

fix(promise): fix 4 bugs from #266 — constructor, any, finally, race ordering (#287)

* fix(promise): fix 4 bugs in #266 — constructor, any, finally, race ordering

Four independent bugs in the Promise implementation, all surfaced by
test-files/test_stress_promises.ts (which previously had status:bug in
known_failures.json):

1. **`new Promise((resolve, reject) => ...)` constructor output missing**
   `is_promise_expr()` in `type_analysis.rs` didn't recognise
   `HirType::Generic { base: "Promise", .. }` — the HIR type produced when
   TypeScript source has an explicit `Promise<T>` annotation. That caused
   `p.then(...)` on such variables to route through `js_native_call_method`
   instead of `js_promise_then`, so the continuation was never registered and
   the output lines never appeared.
   Fix: add `Some(HirType::Generic { base, .. }) if base == "Promise"` arm.

2. **`Promise.any(...).then(...)` output missing**
   Same `is_promise_expr()` gap: `"any"` wasn't in the static-method list
   (`"resolve" | "reject" | "all" | "race" | "allSettled"`) so the result of
   `Promise.any(...)` wasn't recognised as a Promise, and the chained `.then`
   was routed to `js_native_call_method`.
   Fix: add `"any"` to the list.

3. **`.finally(cb).then(v => ...)` propagates `undefined` instead of upstream value**
   Old codegen called `js_promise_then(p, cb, cb)` — using the user's callback
   as both fulfilled and rejected handler. When the microtask runner called
   `cb()` and it returned `undefined`, it resolved the chained promise with
   `undefined` rather than the original value.
   Fix: new `js_promise_finally(promise, on_finally)` runtime function (declared
   in `runtime_decls.rs`) that wraps `on_finally` in dedicated
   `finally_fulfill_wrapper` / `finally_reject_wrapper` closures. Each wrapper
   calls the user callback (ignoring its return), then schedules a
   `finally_passthrough_*` closure via `js_promise_then(resolved_undef, pass)`
   to resolve/reject `next` with the UPSTREAM value — adding exactly one extra
   microtask tick to match Node.js's ordering. Critically, `promise.next` is
   set to `null` so the microtask runner does not attempt to independently
   resolve `next` with the wrapper's `undefined` return value.

4. **`race resolve` / `race reject` appear too early**
   `js_promise_race` had a synchronous early-settle optimisation: when an
   input promise was already Fulfilled/Rejected, it called `js_promise_resolve`
   directly (bypassing the microtask queue) and returned early. This caused
   race results to appear before other promises that were registered earlier in
   the queue. Fix: remove the synchronous short-circuit — always attach
   `then` handlers even for already-settled inputs, so resolution goes through
   the queue like any other microtask.

`node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte. Gap-test baseline

fix(codegen): closes #222 — explicit FFI returns:"i64_str" for string-pointer detection (#296)

Add `returns: "i64_str"` as an explicit manifest field value for native-library
FFI functions that return a raw `i64` which is a `*StringHeader` address.

Root cause
----------
The existing return-type dispatch (lower_call.rs) had three explicit paths:

  "string" / "ptr"  → declares fn as returning PTR, ptrtoint → nanbox STRING
  "i64"             → declares fn as I64, sitofp → JS number
  "void"            → no return

Functions that return a raw `i64` whose *value* is a `*StringHeader` could not
be expressed: using `returns: "i64"` produced a JS Number (via sitofp), making
`.length`, `.charAt()` etc. read the decimal representation of the pointer
address instead of the string contents.

Design
------
New `returns: "i64_str"` path:
  - Declares the function as returning I64 in the LLVM IR (matching the C ABI).
  - Calls the function.
  - NaN-boxes the resulting i64 directly with STRING_TAG (no sitofp, no ptrtoint).

This is distinct from `returns: "string"` / `returns: "ptr"`, which declare the
function as returning `ptr` (suitable for Rust fns declared `-> *const u8`).
Both eventually produce a NaN-boxed STRING_TAG value; the difference is the
LLVM IR type of the declaration and whether a ptrtoint conversion is needed.

Existing behaviour is unchanged:
  - `returns: "i64"` → still a JS number (opaque handle / integer)
  - `returns: "string"` / `"ptr"` → still PTR path
  - Name-based heuristic → still fires when manifest is absent
  - `ext_return_type = HirType::String` heuristic → still fires

Files changed
-------------
crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs
  - Add `let returns_i64_str = matches!(manifest_ret, Some("i64_str"))` flag.
  - Add `returns_i64_str` dispatch branch before `returns_string` (priority).
  - Expand comment block documenting all five `returns` values.
  - Add 6 unit tests in `ffi_return_type_tests` module verifying the flags
    are mutually exclusive and each value maps to exactly one path.

crates/perry/src/commands/compile/resolve.rs
  - Expand `parse_native_library_manifest` comment to document all valid
    `returns` values including the new `"i64_str"` (closes #222).

Verification
------------
  cargo test --release -p perry-codegen ffi_return_type  → 6/6 passed
  gap tests (26/28 baseline)                              → 26/28 (unchanged)
  cargo build --release -p perry-runtime -p perry-stdlib -p perry → clean

Closes #222

fix(ci): NJOBS=3 + retry-on-failure to handle compile-smoke parallel cargo race (v0.5.384)

v0.5.383's nullglob fix landed and the compile-smoke run on 0bdccbd4
successfully printed `Compile smoke: 183 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped`.
But the 1 failure surfaced a SEPARATE race I introduced via NJOBS=6
parallelization:

  ld: file cannot be open()ed, errno=2
  path=.../target/perry-auto-727478db4b75c4fb/release/libperry_runtime.a

Two parallel workers both want the same auto-optimize feature-combo's
libperry_runtime.a. Worker A is mid-rebuild (deletes-then-writes the
.a), worker B's perry already finished its cargo build and invokes
clang to link; clang opens the .a during the brief deleted window
and bails. Race window is sub-second; didn't repro on my 12-core
local Mac (NJOBS=6 finished 2m 21s for 187 files). Macos-14's
3-vCPU runner with heavier cargo lock contention is reachable.

Two-line fix:

1. NJOBS default 6 -> 3 (matches macos-14 vCPU count, fewer
   concurrent cargo invocations contending for the same auto-optimize
   cache dir = race much less likely).

2. Add retry-once-after-2s in compile_one. `||` short-circuits on
   first success so the success path is unchanged; the 2s sleep
   gives the racing worker time to finish writing the .a.

Belt-and-suspenders. Sequential baseline was ~26 min; expect
~10-12 min at NJOBS=3.

Long-term proper fix is perry-side: flock on
`target/perry-auto-<hash>/.lock` during BOTH rebuild and link so
workers in the same feature combo serialize while different combos
still parallelize. Tracked as a separate follow-up.

Adds the WHATWG Web Streams API to Perry as a single coherent surface so
`blob.stream()`, `response.body`, user-source `new ReadableStream({...})`,
`new WritableStream({...})` and `new TransformStream({...})` all work via
the same handle/dispatch pattern that landed for Blob in #234. Avoids the
discoverability trap the issue flagged where one consumer would work and
the rest would silently fail.

Surface delivered:
- `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` ctor, `getReader()`, `cancel()`, `tee()`,
  `pipeTo()`, `pipeThrough()`, `locked`
- `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` `read()`, `releaseLock()`, `cancel()`,
  `closed`
- `WritableStream` ctor, `getWriter()`, `abort()`, `close()`, `locked`
- `WritableStreamDefaultWriter` `write()`, `close()`, `abort()`,
  `releaseLock()`, `closed`, `ready`, `desiredSize`
- `TransformStream` ctor, `readable` / `writable` getters
- `controller.enqueue/close/error/desiredSize` on the readable side
- `Symbol.asyncIterator` lowering: `for await (const c of stream)`
  desugars to a `getReader()/read()` loop in the HIR
- `blob.stream()` returns a single-chunk ReadableStream over the
  buffered bytes
- `response.body` returns a single-chunk ReadableStream over the
  buffered body bytes (matches Perry's existing buffered fetch model;
  true reqwest-chunked streaming is tracked as a #237 follow-up)

Why a buffered model for `response.body`: the existing fetch path
already eagerly drains `reqwest::Response::bytes()`, so wrapping the
result in a ReadableStream with one chunk gives every consumer the same
WHATWG-shaped surface without needing the cross-thread tokio bridge
this PR would otherwise have to introduce. Real chunked streaming is a
focused follow-up that doesn't break the API.

Implementation:
- New `crates/perry-stdlib/src/streams.rs` (~1.3k LOC) — registries
  (`READABLE_STREAMS`, `WRITABLE_STREAMS`, `TRANSFORM_STREAMS`,
  `READERS`, `WRITERS`), every FFI, and a GC root scanner that marks
  user closures + queued chunks + pending-read promises so the
  malloc-triggered sweep can't free them out from under the dispatch.
  Mirrors `BLOB_REGISTRY` shape from `fetch.rs:827` and
  `ws.rs::ensure_gc_scanner_registered` for the GC bridge.
- HIR pre-registers the controller param of every `start` / `pull` /
  `transform` / `flush` callback on stream constructors as a
  `readable_stream::ReadableStream` native instance, so

fix(doc-tests): closes #244 — auto-downsample retina 2× screenshots before SSIM (#298)

The screenshot comparison in `image_diff::diff()` hard-errored on any
size mismatch before SSIM ever ran.  On macOS retina hardware the
gallery binary captures a 2× PNG (e.g. 1800×1940) while the blessed
baseline is 1× (900×970); the strict `actual.width() != baseline.width()`
check returned `Err("size mismatch")` immediately, producing a recurring
SCREENSHOT_DIFF failure for 30+ commits.

dimensions, downsample with a 2×2 box-filter (`halve()`) before SSIM.

regressions are still caught). A downsampled 1× image compared with
the existing 1× baseline falls well within the 0.05 SSIM threshold.

- `diff_arbitrary_size_mismatch_errors` — non-2× mismatches still fail

ci: drop build job, adopt Swatinem cache, fix await-tests gate (v0.5.387)

Three connected workflow changes after the v0.5.386 release-night
post-mortem.

1. release-packages.yml::await-tests
   - Bump per-workflow deadline 45 → 60 min (Tests on macos-14 routinely
     takes 50+ min; 45 was a coin flip)
   - Switch from per_page=1 to per_page=20 + jq select success: find ANY
     green run on the SHA instead of locking to the newest one. v0.5.386
     hit this twice — a tag-push Tests run obscured a green main-push
     run, then again after force-tag-move from a brand-new in-progress
     run.
   - Add fail-fast arm: if every completed run on this SHA failed (no
     successful one yet), exit 1 instead of waiting out the full 60 min.

2. Drop the `build` job from test.yml
   - Its perry/libperry_runtime/libperry_stdlib artifacts were consumed
     by NOTHING except `binary-size` (which is main-only).
   - cargo-test / parity / compile-smoke / doc-tests each did their own
     `cargo build --release` anyway. `needs: build` was a 6-7 min
     serializing barrier with zero cache benefit.
   - Now those 4 jobs start in parallel directly off `checkout@v4`.
   - `binary-size` does its own targeted `cargo build --release -p perry
     -p perry-runtime -p perry-stdlib` (replaces the dropped artifact
     download).

3. Replace actions/cache@v4 with Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 across all 6 jobs
   - Pre-fix the cache deliberately skipped target/ because raw cache@v4
     of the full target/ pushed macos-14's ~14GB disk over limit. The
     explicit "deliberately NOT caching target/" comment in 6 places
     attested to this workaround.
   - Swatinem caches target/ smartly — prunes intermediates that don't
     help warm builds, keeps dep packages + meaningful incremental
     state. Typical cache size <1GB, well under the disk budget.
   - `save-if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` so PRs read from cache
     but only main writes new entries.
   - "Free up disk space (macOS)" simulator-runtime wipe dropped from
     cargo-test / parity / compile-smoke / binary-size. Kept in
     doc-tests (heavy multi-crate cross-compile work).

Expected impact: Tests ~40 min → ~25-30 min on warm cache, ~33 min
cold. The serial build-job barrier is eliminated entirely; downstream
jobs all start at t=0.

Per-workflow billing-min savings on a typical PR cycle: ~10 macos-14
minutes from removed build job + cache hit ratios. v0.5.386's release
night spent ~8 macos-14 hours just on retries of the build phase —
this single change makes that recoverable.

CI hygiene only; no user-facing change.

via `lookup_local_type`, so the `Member { obj: This, prop: ident }`
case (`for (const x of this.classMap)`) fell through to a raw Map
handle that the for-loop's `.length` read returned 0 on.

because methods reference fields). Both for-of arms refactored to
share an `iterable_type: Option<Type>` resolver that handles
`Ident → lookup_local_type` AND `Member-with-This → lookup_class_field_type`.

instead of re-doing the Ident lookup. Also added the missing `Set`

#154 — pre-existing SIGBUS, acknowledged in CLAUDE.md v0.5.377.
`await using r = new R()` where `R[Symbol.asyncDispose]() { await new
Promise(...) }` segfaulted at `js_box_set`'s `str d0, [x0]` writing a
double to read-only __TEXT.

Root cause: `compute_max_func_id` in
`crates/perry-transform/src/generator.rs:313` only walked
`module.functions ∪ module.init`, NOT `module.classes`. The
async-dispose method's executor closure lives inside
`class.methods[i].body` and carries a real FuncId. The generator
transform's `next_func_id = max + 1` undercounts, then mints the
synthesized iterator's `return` method as the same FuncId — colliding
with the user's executor. At codegen the iterator-return body wins,
gets called with `arg = resolve` and 0 captures, reads
`js_closure_get_capture_f64(_, 2)` past the 0-cap end, gets a
code-segment pointer, and `js_box_set` it → SIGBUS.

Fix: mirror the v0.5.323 class-scan that the sibling
`compute_max_local_id` got for issue #212 — append a class-walk loop
scanning `class.{methods, static_methods, constructor, getters,
setters}.body`.

file was introduced. Both prior entries (test_gap_typed_arrays +
test_issue_154_using_dispose) flipped to passing.

Diagnosis credit: research subagents — agent A (#302) found the
gate-on-Ident root cause via HIR diff between local-var and
class-field iterables; agent B (#154) used lldb to capture the
crashing instruction at `js_box_set`'s `str d0, [x0]` and the IR
dump confirmed `js_promise_new_with_executor(@perry_closure_3, 0
captures)` where closure_3's body matched the iterator-return
template.

fix(windows): closes #300 — auto-discover Windows SDK lib paths via registry + ProgramFiles env (v0.5.389)

A user with VS installed on D: hit `LINK : fatal error LNK1181: cannot
open input file "user32.lib"` because `find_msvc_lib_paths()` in
`crates/perry/src/commands/compile/library_search.rs:317` hardcoded
the Windows SDK lookup to `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib`.
The MSVC CRT lookup via `vswhere` correctly finds non-default VS
installs, but the SDK path probe is purely a hardcoded `read_dir`, so
when the SDK lives elsewhere `find_msvc_lib_paths` silently returns
ONLY the MSVC CRT path. link.exe can't find `user32.lib` in `LIB` →
LNK1181. Pre-fix the failure was silent — no Perry-side warning, no
actionable error.

Three-layer fix:

1. Probe a list of candidate SDK roots in priority order:
   - Registry `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Kits\Installed Roots`
     value `KitsRoot10` (canonical — what `vcvars64.bat` consults)
   - `%ProgramFiles%\Windows Kits\10\Lib` (handles arch-specific paths)
   - `%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Windows Kits\10\Lib`
   - Legacy hardcoded path as final fallback

2. Stop on first SDK with `<ver>\um\x64` subdir; add both `um\x64` and
   `ucrt\x64` to LIB.

3. Fail LOUD when no SDK was found AND `LIB` env var isn't set —
   print a Perry-side warning listing every candidate path tried +
   three workarounds (run `vcvars64.bat`, install via VS Installer,
   set `LIB` manually). Pre-fix users got the confusing `LNK1181`
   error from link.exe with no breadcrumb back to Perry.

New `read_registry_kits_root_10()` helper shells out to `reg query`
(stays Cargo-deps-free; same result as the `winreg` crate). Stub on
non-Windows.

fix(updater): closes #229 — version-bind into Ed25519 signed payload (v0.5.391)

Pre-fix the signed payload was just the raw 32-byte SHA-256 digest of
the binary — the version string was unsigned. An on-path attacker
could serve a tampered manifest pairing a previously-signed older
binary's URL + signature with a higher version number. Client
downloads the binary, verifies SHA-256 (matches — it's the real older
binary), verifies signature against the pinned pubkey (matches — that
binary really WAS signed by the developer), installs and relaunches,
and gets pushed to a known-vulnerable version.

Fix per the Option-A design comment on the issue:

- New `perry_updater_verify_signature_v2(file_path, sig, pubkey, version)`
  FFI in `crates/perry-updater/src/core.rs` builds the signed payload
  as `digest_bytes (32) || version_utf8 (variable)` and verifies that.
  Empty version is rejected up-front (would otherwise reduce to v1
  payload and accept any v1 signature as a v2 signature).

- Manifest `schemaVersion` bumped 1 → 2 to signal which verify path.
  The @perry/updater wrapper accepts both v1 and v2 manifests,
  dispatching based on `manifest.schemaVersion`. Older v1-only clients
  reject v2 with `unsupported manifest schemaVersion`, which is the
  intended migration safety net.

- New ambient TS export `verifySignatureV2` at
  `types/perry/updater/index.d.ts`. New dispatch row in
  `crates/perry-dispatch/src/lib.rs` next to the v1 row.

- New unit test `signature_verify_v2_roundtrip_and_replay_defense`
  asserts: (1) v2 sig + matching version verifies, (2) **old-binary
  replay defense** — a v1-style sig (digest only) MUST NOT verify
  against the v2 path even when the version label matches, (3)
  tampered version label fails, (4) tampered binary fails, (5)
  empty-version is rejected. Full perry-updater suite: 11/11 passing.

- Migration story documented in `docs/src/updater/overview.md`.
  Trust-model section rewritten to lead with v2 (recommended) +
  show v1 as backwards-compat. Migration ordering: deploy a
  v0.5.391+ client to your users via a v1 manifest first, THEN
  bump manifests to v2.

Sign-side CLI tooling for v2 deferred to a follow-up. Existing apps
can build v2 signatures with any Ed25519 library by computing
`sha256(binary) + version.encode("utf-8")` and signing that.

fix: closes #307 — JSON.stringify on parsed objects with ≥9 fields (v0.5.398)

JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(src)) returned the literal string "null" for
parsed objects with 9+ fields. Silently corrupted JSON-roundtripping in
perry-hub for two days.

Two interacting bugs in crates/perry-runtime/src/json.rs, both rooted in
the inline-slot / overflow-storage split (object.rs:32 OVERFLOW_FIELDS
holds keys past inline alloc_limit, field_count caps at the inline cap
per the "Deliberately do NOT bump field_count here" branch):

(1) is_object_pointer gated stringify on `keys_len <= field_count`.
    Parser objects with 9+ fields have keys_len=9, field_count=8 → gate
    failed → fell through to `buf.push_str("null")`. Object literals
    pre-allocate exactly N slots so keys_len == field_count and the
    gate passed — explaining the literal-vs-parse asymmetry.

(2) stringify_object_inner used `min(num_fields, keys_len)` and read
    fields via direct pointer arithmetic — only saw the first 8 inline
    slots. Same bug in the shape-template fast path's
    build_shape_prefix_template.

Fix:
- is_object_pointer: drop the keys_len <= field_count constraint.
- stringify_object_inner: actual_fields = keys_len, route reads through
  read_field_bits which falls through to js_object_get_field's
  overflow_get for f >= alloc_limit.
- Shape-template fast path: skip when keys_len > num_fields (overflow
  objects fall through to the slow path which now handles overflow).

feat(windows): #303 Win7 / Win8 compatibility via --min-windows-version

Add opt-in support for compiling Perry executables that run on Windows 7
SP1 (and Windows 8 / 8.1). Default target stays Win10+; legacy support is
one CLI flag away. See docs/src/platforms/windows-7.md for the full story.

Two coordinated changes:

(1) **PE subsystem version flag**. New CompileArgs::min_windows_version
    (CLI: --min-windows-version=7|8|10, default 10). Threaded through
    CompilationContext to windows_pe_subsystem_flag in library_search.rs,
    which now appends `,5.1` (Win7) or `,6.02` (Win8) to /SUBSYSTEM:
    when the flag is set. 10 (default) emits no suffix — preserves
    current behavior. Invalid values fail loudly at compile time, not
    silently fall through.

(2) **Lazy DPI API resolution**. New crates/perry-ui-windows/src/dpi_compat.rs
    resolves SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext (Win10 1607) and GetDpiForSystem
    (Win10 1607) via LoadLibraryW + GetProcAddress instead of static
    extern imports. Hard-importing those symbols would emit IAT entries
    that the OS resolves before main() runs — on Win7 the loader fails
    the process with "entry point not found in user32.dll" before any
    Rust code can execute. Falls back through Win8.1's
    SetProcessDpiAwareness, then Vista's SetProcessDPIAware. DPI lookup
    falls back to GetDC + GetDeviceCaps(LOGPIXELSY) (Win2000+).

fix(codegen): #309 Effect 34 GB OOM via inheritance-chain cycle break (v0.5.403)

`perry compile` of a 4-line program importing the `effect` package OOM'd at
34 GB RSS / 249 GB peak virtual before being SIGKILL'd ~7 minutes in. Root
cause: inheritance-chain cycle in `compile_module`'s `class_table`. Effect
declares same-named classes across modules — `class Base extends Class<any>`
inside Data.ts's `TaggedClass` IIFE plus `class Class<A,E,R> extends
Base<A,E,R>` in Effectable.ts. When the cross-module-import resolver pulls
every exported class into Data.ts's `imported_class_stubs`, the stub for
`Class` carries `parent_name = "Base"` from Effectable's source — but in
Data.ts's namespace that resolves to Data.ts's OWN local `Base`,
forming a cycle Base → Class → Base → … Every chain-walking site in
codegen assumed acyclic inheritance; `apply_field_initializers_recursive`
in particular accumulated visited names into `chain: Vec<String>` without
bound, allocating ~3.5 GB/sec single-threaded.

Fix is one centralized cycle break in `compile_module` at
`crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs` — runs once after `imported_class_stubs`
are built but before they enter `class_table`. Walks each stub's parent
chain via DFS in the (local ∪ stub) union name space with a HashSet
visited-set + depth cap of 64; if the walk revisits a name OR exceeds
the cap, drops `extends_name = None` on the offending stub, breaking
the cycle. All downstream chain walks then operate on a guaranteed-
acyclic graph. The fundamental name-collision (Data.ts's local `Base`
vs Effectable.ts's `Base` — different classes, same name) is left
unfixed; a proper resolution requires module-prefixing class names in
HIR which is a multi-day refactor with breaking implications for the
dispatch / `instanceof` / class-id machinery.

Verified end-to-end on the issue's exact Effect 3.21.2 repro:
- Pre-fix:  430s wall, 34 GB RSS, SIGKILL exit 137
- Post-fix: 2.45s wall, 129 MB max RSS, 120 MB peak — 175× faster, 263× less memory

All 152 modules now compile cleanly to .o files. The link step then fails
with separate `ld: symbol(s) not found` errors for unresolved cross-module
method symbols — pre-existing dispatch gaps for specific Effect patterns,
the natural follow-up. The OOM is fully fixed.

No regression: gap tests 27/28 = baseline; inheritance-chain smoke
(3-level Animal/Dog/Puppy with super-method calls) compiles + runs;

fix(hir): closes #310 — traverse `export * as X from ...` namespace re-export (v0.5.405)

`export * as Foo from "./Foo"` (ES2020 namespace re-export) was silently
dropped at HIR lowering — `ExportNamed`'s `if let Named` filter only
matched the regular Named shape; SWC's Namespace variant fell through
and the re-exported file never entered the module graph. Consumer's
`import { Foo } from "pkg"` resolved to a stale binding and every
`Foo.<member>` access lowered to 0 — silent-correctness bug, exit 0,
no diagnostics. Surfaced on Effect (effect/src/index.ts does
`export * as Effect from "./Effect.js"`).

1. New `Export::NamespaceReExport { source, name }` HIR variant.
2. ExportNamed lowering rewritten as full match on Named/Namespace/Default.
3. collect_modules + topo-sort dep-walk extended with
   `NamespaceReExport => Some(source)`.
4. Per-import-spec consumer-side dispatch: when a Named import's
   exported_name matches a NamespaceReExport, resolve the target,
   register every export under the local namespace alias.
5. Codegen StaticMethodCall companion: namespace_imports.contains
   arm emits `perry_fn_<src>__<method>` directly.

fix(codegen): closes #313 — exclude scalar-replaced `new` when ctor uses `this` as a value (v0.5.407)

Symptom 1: `class Holder { v=10; constructor() { const self=this; this.s = new Store((x)=>x+self.v) } }` printed `self.v: undefined` instead of `10`.

Symptom 2 (sibling): inline arrow with `captures_this:true` referenced `this.v` directly and SIGSEGV'd.

Root cause: scalar replacement (collectors.rs:`collect_non_escaping_news` → stmt.rs:264-343) rewrites `let h = new Holder()` into per-field stack allocas and inlines the ctor body with a *dummy* `this_stack` slot that's never populated. `this.field = …` and `this.field` are intercepted in expr.rs and routed to the per-field allocas — but anything else (e.g. `Expr::This` as the init of `const self = this`, or a closure with `captures_this:true` whose env stores `this` at construction) reads the uninitialized dummy and produces TAG_UNDEFINED.

Fix: new pass-3 in `collect_non_escaping_news` that walks each candidate class's constructor body + every instance-field initializer (own + parent chain) and marks the candidate as escaped when:
  - `Expr::This` appears outside of `(PropertyGet|PropertySet|PropertyUpdate).object` with a known field property
  - `Expr::Closure { captures_this: true, … }` appears (its env materializes `this` at construction)
  - `Expr::SuperCall` / `Expr::SuperMethodCall` appear (implicit `this`)

Method/getter property names like `this.method()` route to "unsafe" via the `fields.contains(property)` check, since they materialize `this` as the receiver in lower_call.rs:1465.

Three new helpers (`class_uses_this_as_value` / `stmts_use_this_as_value` / `expr_uses_this_as_value`) enumerate the safe HIR variants explicitly and use `_ => true` for unknowns — strictly conservative, only loses the optimization on patterns we haven't enumerated.

fix(codegen): closes #318 — delegate closure-collector descent to centralised walker (v0.5.408)

After #309 + #310 landed, Effect compiles past codegen for ~336/362
modules but 17 of the 26 failing modules tripped clang
"use of undefined value '@perry_closure_node_modules_effect_src_<MODULE>_ts__<N>'"
errors. Same recurring walker-bug class as v0.5.323 / v0.5.388 /
v0.5.396 / v0.5.405: `crates/perry-codegen/src/collectors.rs::
collect_closures_in_expr` carried its own ad-hoc HIR descent with an
`_ => {}` catch-all, and any `Expr` variant added since the last
sweep silently dropped its sub-expressions — so closures buried
inside `Expr::RegExpReplaceFn`, `Expr::NetCreateServer`, the
`Expr::Proxy*` / `Expr::Reflect*` / `Expr::Buffer*` / `Expr::Date*` /
`Expr::Math{Sin,Cos,Log,…}` / `Expr::PropertyUpdate` /
`Expr::IndexUpdate` / `Expr::String{Match,Replace,Split,…}` families
and ~80 others got registered nowhere. Codegen then emitted
`js_closure_alloc(@perry_closure_*)` references at creation sites,
but bodies were never compiled into LLVM, so clang flagged them
undefined.

Fix in one place: rewrite `collect_closures_in_expr` to delegate
descent to `perry_hir::walker::walk_expr_children` — the centralised
exhaustive walker introduced in v0.5.329 (Tier 1.1) for the four
other consumers (substitute_locals, find_max_local_id,
collect_local_refs_expr, remap_local_ids_in_expr). New body has
exactly two responsibilities: when `e` is `Expr::Closure`, register
the func_id and recurse into the body (Vec<Stmt>, which the walker
doesn't visit per its module docs); for every variant including
Closure, ask walk_expr_children to call us back on each direct
sub-`Expr`. New HIR variants now produce a compile error in
walker.rs until enumerated, closing the bug class permanently.
Replaces ~570 lines of ad-hoc match arms with ~36 lines that
can't drift.

New regression test test-files/test_issue_318_closure_collector_walker.ts
exercises closures nested inside Math.sin / Math.cos / Math.log2
operands (representative of the >80 missed variants — the old arm
list had MathSqrt/Floor/Ceil/Round/Abs/MinSpread/MaxSpread but not
the trig/log family).

env (stored via `js_closure_set_capture_f64`), not in alloca slots.

`!closure_captures.contains_key(id) && !boxed_vars.contains(id)
&& locals.contains_key(id)` — the same predicates the regular
`LocalSet` path uses for storage-type dispatch. When any of those
fail, `LocalSet` falls through to the regular path which correctly
handles all four storage types. The `js_string_append` in-place
mutation is still preserved for plain (non-captured, non-boxed)

fix(arrays): closes #323 — array holes read as undefined, in/Object.keys array-aware (v0.5.412)

`new Array(n)` slots used to read as 0 instead of undefined because the
runtime left element bytes uninitialized; `Object.keys(arr)` and `n in arr`
walked an ArrayHeader as ObjectHeader and only happened to look correct on
fresh zero-filled arena memory.

Fix introduces a TAG_HOLE sentinel (0x7FFC...0010) used internally for
never-written slots:
- js_array_alloc_with_length initializes reachable slots to TAG_HOLE
- js_array_get_f64 / _unchecked translate HOLE → UNDEFINED on read
- js_object_keys detects ArrayHeader and emits string indices for non-HOLE slots
- js_object_has_property detects ArrayHeader and checks slot != HOLE for
  numeric keys, distinguishing holes from explicit `arr[i] = undefined`
- All three inline IndexGet codegen paths (bounded fast / generic / generic-
  Object numeric fallback) translate HOLE → UNDEFINED via branchless select
- refine_type_from_init recognizes `new Array(...)` so `const xs = new Array(n)`
  gets refined to Array<Any> and reaches the array fast path

fix(codegen): closes #324 — strict ArrayIsArray fast path for unions (v0.5.413)

`Array.isArray(value)` constant-folded to TAG_TRUE for any value typed
as a Union with an Array variant — `function hook(value: number |
readonly number[]) { if (Array.isArray(value)) ... }` always picked the
array branch even when called with a number.

Root cause: `Expr::ArrayIsArray` lowering at `expr.rs:6851` used
`is_array_expr` which (correctly) treats `Union(.. Array(_) ..)` as
array-typed for routing `.length`/`.push` dispatch on `T[] | null`
post-narrow. That looseness is wrong for `Array.isArray`, which must
reflect the runtime tag.

Fix: strict `matches!(ty, Type::Array(_) | Type::Tuple(_))` against
`static_type_of(...)`. Pure array/tuple types still constant-fold;
unions fall through to the existing `js_array_is_array` runtime
dispatch.
