fix(runtime,codegen): closes #344, #345, #346 — stdio routing + process.argv prototype (#354)

Three small fixes for stdio/argv gaps surfaced while compiling skelpo-listener
with `perry compile`. Each is independently reproducible via a 4-line script;
each preserves existing behavior outside the fix path.

#344 — process.{stdout,stderr}.write are silent no-ops
  perry-runtime/src/os.rs: `process_stream_write_stub` literally dropped its
  argument and returned `true`, plus stdout/stderr shared the same stub so it
  couldn't have routed correctly even if it wrote. Replace with two stubs
  bound to fd 1 / fd 2 via std::io::stdout()/stderr().write_all, matching
  Node's `process.std*.write(s)` semantics (no trailing newline added).
  process.stdin keeps a no-op write closure.

#345 — console.error / console.warn (single-arg) collapse onto stdout
  perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs: the multi-arg console path correctly
  dispatches on `property` to js_console_{log,warn,error}_spread, but the
  single-arg fast path always called js_console_log_{number,dynamic}
  regardless. Dispatch on (property, is_number_literal) so each method
  routes to its matching runtime fn — the {warn,error}_{number,dynamic}
  impls already existed in perry-runtime/src/builtins.rs and use eprintln!
  for the stderr-bound variants. Also declare those four runtime fns in
  runtime_decls.rs so the codegen-side calls resolve at link time.

#346 — process.argv.includes(x) returns false
  perry-codegen/src/type_analysis.rs: `static_type_of` lists every array-
  producing expression (Expr::Array, Expr::ArrayMap, Expr::ObjectKeys, ...)
  but did not include Expr::ProcessArgv. With ProcessArgv missing,
  `is_array_expr(ctx, &Expr::ProcessArgv)` returns false, so
  `argv.includes(x)` (1 arg) hits the string-method-only routing in
  lower_call.rs and falls through to garbage. Add ProcessArgv as an array of
  String — js_process_argv() already returns a real ArrayHeader at runtime,
  this just teaches the type analyzer to recognize it.

Repros (all four scripts compile cleanly + run; commands match the issue
templates):

    # #344
    process.stdout.write('via stdout.write\n');
    process.stderr.write('via stderr.write\n');
    console.log('via console.log');
    # was: only console.log surfaced; now all three reach the right fd.

    # #345
    console.log('via console.log');
    console.error('via console.error');
    # was: both on stdout; now console.error on stderr.

    # #346
    console.log('argv.includes("--help")=' + process.argv.includes('--help'));
    # was: false; now: true.

fix(transform): closes #342 — cond ? await a() : b() evaluates BOTH branches (#356)

* fix(transform): closes #342 — cond ? await a() : b() evaluates BOTH branches

Issue #342: a conditional expression with `await` on one side ran the
awaited call regardless of the condition. Previously a `digest`-bound
codepath that wrote `args.command === 'fetch' ? await runFetch() : runDigest()`
also executed `runFetch` (printing fetch progress) before falling through
to `runDigest`.

Root cause is in the async→generator pre-pass, not the codegen. The
hoister blindly walks expression children looking for `Expr::Await` and
lifts each into a `let __await_N = await X` placed BEFORE the containing
statement. For

    let r = cond ? await a() : b();

it lifts `await a()` to `let __await_N = await a();` so the resulting
HIR is

    let __await_N = await a();
    let r = cond ? __await_N : b();

— which executes `a()` unconditionally. The HIR confirms it: dumping
with `--print-hir` shows `then_expr: LocalGet(N)` and the original call
site moved to state 0 of the generator state machine.

Fix: detect `Expr::Conditional` whose then/else branch contains an
await and, before any general hoisting walks into it, lift the whole
conditional to a statement-level if/else with a temp local:

    let __cond_await_N: any;
    if (cond) { __cond_await_N = await a(); }
    else      { __cond_await_N = b(); }
    let r = __cond_await_N;

The recursive `hoist_awaits_in_stmts` call inside each branch then
hoists the await to the top of its own if-arm — the position the
await→yield rewrite expects. Both `hoist_awaits_in_expr_full` and
`hoist_awaits_avoiding_top_level` get the early dispatch so the lift
fires whether the conditional is at let-init or in a deeper position.

Verified with all four await-shape combinations:

    cond ? await a() : b()         — only the matched branch runs (was: both)
    cond ? a() : await b()         — only the matched branch runs (was: both)
    cond ? await a() : await b()   — only the matched branch runs (was: both)
    cond ? a() : b()               — unchanged (was already correct)

Plus the actual skelpo-listener pattern that surfaced the bug:

    const code = args.command === 'fetch' ? await runFetch(args) : runDigest(args);

now runs only `runDigest` on a `digest` invocation.

`cargo build --release -p perry` clean.

fix(compile,doctor): closes #352 — find WinGet-installed runtime/stdlib libs

WinGet-installed Perry couldn't find its own .lib files at link time —
`perry compile` aborted with "Could not find perry_runtime.lib" and
`perry doctor` reported the runtime library as missing.

Root cause: WinGet stores perry.exe and the runtime/stdlib/UI .lib files
together in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\PerryTS.Perry_<hash>\,
but exposes the binary via a launcher-shim WinGet\Links\perry.exe. The
shim is a launcher .exe rather than a symlink, so current_exe() returns
the shim path and the existing dir.join(name) candidates resolved to
WinGet\Links\ — where the libs are not.

Fix in two places:
- New winget_lib_candidates(name) helper in library_search.rs reads
  %LOCALAPPDATA%, scans Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\ once, and emits a
  candidate per directory whose name starts with PerryTS.Perry_.
  cfg-gated for Windows; non-Windows companion returns empty Vec.
  Wired into both the cross-compile branch (--target windows on Windows
  host) and the host branch.
- doctor.rs::check_runtime_library now delegates to the same find_library
  machinery via a new pub use library_search::find_library re-export from
  compile.rs — replaces an ad-hoc 4-element candidate array that drifted
  independently from the linker's actual lookup paths.

The PERRY_RUNTIME_DIR / PERRY_LIB_DIR env-var escape hatches still take
precedence (checked first in collect_library_candidates).

End-to-end verification on Windows requires a fresh winget catalog
publish — current catalog at v0.5.386 doesn't include this fix yet.

fix(compile,codegen): #360 item #2 — process import resolution + cwd dispatch (v0.5.439) (#364)

`import process from 'node:process'` and `import { cwd } from 'node:process'`
were rejected at module resolution with `Warning: Could not resolve import
'process' from <file>` and the destructured `cwd` link-failed with
`Undefined symbols: _cwd`. Surfaced on 8 sites across
node_modules/ink/build/*.js (render.js / ink.js / reconciler.js / App.js /
StdinContext.js / StdoutContext.js / StderrContext.js / ErrorOverview.js)
— every ink module that pulls `process` explicitly. #348's Phase A
scoping pass had to leave this broken because the ESM-only
`compilePackages` pipeline didn't recognize `process` as a Perry-handled
native builtin.

Fix in two places:

1. crates/perry-hir/src/ir.rs

   - Add "process" to NATIVE_MODULES (the master list `is_native_module`
     checks; existing `node:` prefix strip in that helper covers both
     bare 'process' and 'node:process' shapes).
   - Add "process" to RUNTIME_ONLY_MODULES so `requires_stdlib("process")`
     returns false — the process surface (argv / env / stdout / stderr /
     cwd) lives in perry-runtime/src/os.rs and js_process_* runtime
     helpers, not in perry-stdlib, so a process-only program shouldn't
     pull stdlib in for nothing.

   With (1) alone, the import resolves cleanly but the destructured
   `cwd()` call silently returns `undefined` — *worse* UX than the
   original "Could not resolve" error since it's a silent corruption.

2. crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native.rs

   Add a `module == "process" && object.is_none()` arm before the
   generic native_module_lookup dispatch that routes cwd / uptime /
   memoryUsage to js_process_cwd / js_process_uptime /
   js_process_memory_usage. These are the *same* runtime helpers the
   implicit-global form `process.cwd()` already uses (lowered to
   dedicated HIR variants Expr::ProcessCwd / Expr::ProcessUptime /
   Expr::ProcessMemoryUsage in perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call.rs:262);
   this arm just routes the destructured-import shape to the same
   helpers. Methods not yet wired (nextTick / exit / kill / hrtime)
   fall through to the generic dispatch path.

fix(codegen): closes #339 — pack better-sqlite3 stmt args into a real ArrayHeader

`db.prepare('SELECT … WHERE x = ?').all('a')` returned an empty array even
when matching rows existed. Same root cause silently broke `.get('a')`
and `.run(arg, ...)`. Codegen's NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE entry for stmt.run /
stmt.get / stmt.all declared `args: &[NA_F64]`, so the dispatcher passed
each user arg as a single NaN-boxed `double`. The runtime side
(`js_sqlite_stmt_*`) expects a packed `*const ArrayHeader`, and its
defensive guard ("upper-16 != 0 → no params") incidentally fired for
every NaN-boxed value, so the params vector was always empty and the
WHERE clause's `?` evaluated to NULL.

Fix: new `NativeArgKind::VarArgsAsArray` that packs `args[i..]` into a
fresh JS array via `js_array_alloc` + `js_array_push_f64` and passes a
single i64 ArrayHeader pointer (matches the runtime ABI). Padding emits
an allocated empty array when zero user args are supplied. Three table
entries flipped to `&[NA_VARARGS]`; runtime side unchanged.

New regression test test_issue_339_sqlite_stmt_all_bound_params.ts
covers `.all` / `.get` / `.run` with no-args, single-string-bind,
multi-arg mixed-type bind. 11/11 lines match `node --experimental-strip-types`
byte-for-byte. Issue's literal repro flips len=0 → len=1.

fix(hir,codegen): closes #336 — dedup same-named classes in one module

Two classes sharing a name in one TS module (e.g., `namespace A { export
class Refinement {} }` + `namespace B { export class Refinement {} }`)
aborted compilation at clang IR validation with `error: redefinition of
global '@perry_class_keys_<modprefix>__<class>'`. Surfaced on Effect
3.21+ across 7 modules tracked under umbrella #321.

The function-scoped class-decl path in `lower_decl.rs::3059` already
deduped same-named classes; seven other push sites in `lower.rs` did
not. Added `push_class_dedup` helper and routed every
`module.classes.push(class)` site through it. Codegen's
`imported_class_stubs` loop also gained a self-dedup guard for the
namespace-re-export shape.

The lookup pipeline (`Expr::New { class_name: String }`) is purely
name-based today, so the second class wouldn't be reachable through
any binding — emitting it just produced unreachable globals that
collided with the first's. Pinning a distinct identity per scope is
a separate, larger HIR change.

New regression test under `test-files/` + pinned expected output (Node
can't strip namespaces). Gap tests 27/28 = baseline (`console_methods`
ci-env quirk); parity 182/182 (100%).

fix(codegen,runtime): closes #350 round 2 — Set/Map class-id collision in dispatch tower (v0.5.444)

Crash repro from @codehz: `a.componentTypeSet.has(c)` segfaulted right after
`Array.isArray(...) === true` (the v0.5.437 symptom). Codegen's idispatch
tower for unknown-receiver method calls included `WorldLike.has` (user
class id 4) as a candidate; `js_object_get_class_id(setHeader)` returned
`capacity` (=4 for `js_set_alloc(0)`) since SetHeader has no GcHeader; the
dispatch routed `set.has(c)` into `WorldLike.has(set, c, undefined)`,
which dereferenced `this.entityToArchetype` at offset 40 of SetHeader's
allocator metadata and chased that bogus pointer.

Fix in two places:

(a) `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs` — extend `is_builtin_receiver`
    allowlist with `ReadonlyMap` + `ReadonlySet` so the post-narrow
    Map.get-result type skips the user-class dispatch tower entirely.

(b) `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs::js_object_get_class_id` — refuse
    to read class_id unless the pointer is in the GC arena range AND not
    registered in any built-in registry (Set / Map / Regex) AND the
    GcHeader byte at -8 reads `GC_TYPE_OBJECT`. Registry check is the
    authoritative negative; arena+GcHeader checks are belt-and-suspenders
    for any future built-in without a registry.

New regression test exercises the issue's exact ECS-shape repro plus
direct Set.has / Map.get coverage to verify built-in dispatch still
routes correctly post-guard.

Verified: gap 27/28 = baseline (lone fail is pre-existing `console_methods`
ci-env quirk); parity 187/187 = 100%.

`createPlayer`) with a full AVPlayer-backed implementation. Direct port of
`crates/perry-ui-ios/src/media_playback.rs` since AVFoundation's
`AVPlayer` / `AVPlayerItem` / `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` /
`MPRemoteCommandCenter` / `AVAudioSession` / `UIImage` are all available
on watchOS 5.0+, and Perry's min-deployment is `arm64_32-apple-watchos10.0`
(see `crates/perry/src/commands/compile/link.rs:88`).

## What landed

- `crates/perry-ui-watchos/src/media_playback.rs` — full impl (~1077 LOC):
  - HTTP/HTTPS + `file://` AVPlayer instantiation, 1-based handle table.
  - State machine: `idle` / `loading` / `ready` / `playing` / `paused` /
    `ended` / `error` driven by polling `timeControlStatus` +
    `currentItem.status` at 10 Hz from an `NSTimer`.
  - `AVPlayerItemDidPlayToEndTimeNotification` observer + `currentTime ≈
    duration - 0.25s` fallback so `ended` fires reliably (per #351).
  - `setNowPlaying(title, artist, album, artworkUrl)` populates
    `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` — surfaces on the watch face's Now Playing
    complication / glance screen (independent of the paired iPhone).
  - `MPRemoteCommandCenter` handlers for play / pause / togglePlayPause —
    routes hardware (AirPods, Bluetooth headphones, Siri) events to the
    first live player.
  - `AVAudioSession` Playback-category activation on the first
    `createPlayer(...)` so audio actually reaches the speaker.
  - Synchronous artwork fetch via `NSData(contentsOf:)` + `UIImage` for
    remote URLs; `MPMediaItemArtwork(image:)` convenience initializer.

- `docs/src/system/media.md` — flips watchOS row from "Stub" → "Implemented",
  adds an Info.plist requirements section documenting the
  `WKBackgroundModes` / `audio` entry needed for background audio.

## What stays out of scope

- `WKApplicationDelegate.handleRemoteNowPlayingActivity()` — watchOS 7+
  multi-app handover surface. Not wired today; `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter`
  works directly for the single-app player path Apple's docs recommend.
- App-shell `Info.plist` template — Perry doesn't currently auto-generate
  watchOS Info.plist files. Documented as a manual step in `media.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p perry-ui-watchos` — clean (0 errors); 6 pre-existing
  warnings (5 `unused doc comment` from `perry-runtime`, 1 cross-file
  `js_string_from_bytes` signature drift that mirrors the same pattern
  in `crates/perry-ui-ios/src/{media_playback.rs,lib.rs,tree.rs,
  widgets/textarea.rs}` — not introduced by this PR).
- All 15 `perry_media_*` FFI thunks in `crates/perry-ui-watchos/src/lib.rs`
  (already present from v0.5.440) line up with the 15 `pub fn` exports

fix(hir): closes #341 — class field native instance tracking (v0.5.458)

`class S { db: Database.Database; constructor(p) { this.db = new Database(p); } count() { return (this.db.prepare('...').get() as any).n } }` SIGSEGV'd in `count()`. Root cause: the codegen's `receiver_class_name(this.db)` returned `"Database"` (the field's declared TS type — not a Perry class), and the IC fast path then deref'd `obj-8` for the GcHeader byte. For a small SqliteDbHandle id (1..n), `1-8 = -7` SIGSEGV'd.

Fix in `crates/perry-hir/src/js_transform.rs`: build a global `class → field → (module, native_class)` map by scanning constructor bodies and field initializers for `this.<field> = new Database(...)` patterns. New `fix_class_field_stmt` walker rewrites both `this.<field>.method(...)` (in class methods) and `<localGet>.<field>.method(...)` (the post-inline shape — the inliner substitutes `this` with the receiver local) into `NativeMethodCall` so dispatch routes through the runtime's native table instead of the IC fast path.

Also propagates chaining: after the inner call becomes `NativeMethodCall`, outer `<NativeMethodCall>.<chained>(...)` calls are rewritten too via the same `(module, prior_method) → result_class` table the lower-time chain detection in `expr_call.rs` uses (better-sqlite3 prepare → Statement, mongodb db → Database, mongodb collection → Collection, mysql2 getConnection → PoolConnection, pg connect → PoolClient, ioredis duplicate → Redis). New regression test `test-files/test_issue_341_typed_field_native.ts` covers both the chained and multi-statement shapes. Verified: cargo build clean; gap tests baseline; parity 190/190 (100%).

fix(stdlib,runtime,codegen): closes #340 — axios response handle properties (v0.5.459)

`await axios.get(url)` resolved to a response object whose `.status` and `.data` were both `undefined` instead of the actual HTTP status / body. Three layered defects:

1. `crates/perry-stdlib/src/axios.rs` queued `Ok(handle as u64)` to the promise resolver without NaN-boxing — the awaiter saw a subnormal float (bits=1), not a POINTER_TAG'd handle. Property access on a subnormal float silently returned undefined through the runtime's coercion path.
2. The codegen IC fast path's slow case (`js_object_get_field_ic_miss`) bailed at `obj < 0x10000` for handle receivers, never reaching the runtime's `HANDLE_PROPERTY_DISPATCH` table.
3. The runtime's `HANDLE_PROPERTY_DISPATCH` (in `crates/perry-stdlib/src/common/dispatch.rs`) had no axios arm — `r.status` / `r.data` / `r.statusText` were never wired up.

Fix in 5 files:

- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/axios.rs`: NaN-box every `Ok(handle as u64)` → `Ok((handle as u64) | 0x7FFD_0000_0000_0000)` so the awaiter sees a real POINTER_TAG'd value (5 sites — get/post/put/delete/patch).
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs::js_object_get_field_ic_miss`: add a small-handle guard — receivers in `1..0x100000` route to `HANDLE_PROPERTY_DISPATCH` instead of falling through to the OBJECT_TYPE_REGULAR path.
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs::js_object_get_field_by_name`: same guard for already-stripped pointers (defensive — the codegen's slow path passes either form).
- `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs`: PropertyGet IC fast path small-handle guard via `select` — substitutes the per-site cache global address for `obj_handle` when `obj_handle < 0x100000` so the GcHeader and keys_array loads read from valid memory; `is_real_ptr` AND'd into the `hit` predicate so handles cleanly miss to the slow path without SIGSEGV.
- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/common/dispatch.rs::js_handle_property_dispatch`: new arm — when `with_handle::<AxiosResponseHandle>(handle)` returns true and the property is `status` / `data` / `statusText`, dispatch to `js_axios_response_status` / `_data` / `_status_text`.

The same architecture (NaN-box at promise resolve, route handles to HANDLE_PROPERTY_DISPATCH) sets up future modules (mongodb, pg, ioredis async returns) without further plumbing changes. New regression test `test-files/test_issue_340_axios_response_props.ts`. Verified: cargo build clean; the issue's literal repro (`await axios.get('https://api.bsky.app/...')`) now prints `status: 200 / data type: string` (was `undefined / undefined`); parity 190/190 — no regressions.

fix(hir): closes #388 — optional chain short-circuits on undefined too (v0.5.460)

`obj?.method()` short-circuit was using strict equality (`obj === null`) when it should use loose equality (`obj == null`). The spec is clear that `?.` short-circuits on both null AND undefined.

Pre-fix: `map.get(missingKey)?.has?.(1) ?? false` returned the literal string `[object Object]` because:
1. `map.get(missingKey)` returned undefined
2. `undefined === null` evaluated to false
3. The else branch took `undefined.has(1)` which produced garbage / `[object Object]`
4. `?? false` saw a truthy `[object Object]` and returned it

Fix in `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs`: both OptChain → Conditional rewrite sites flip from `CompareOp::Eq` (strict ===) to `CompareOp::LooseEq` (==) so `obj == null` matches both null and undefined per spec.

New regression test `test-files/test_issue_388_optional_chain_loose_eq.ts` covers the issue's literal repro (8 console.log lines) and matches `node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte. Parity 190/190 (100%) — no regressions.

fix(codegen): closes #392 — register class methods in vtable for cross-module dispatch (v0.5.464)

When a class instance was passed as an argument to a function defined in another module (with a structural-object parameter type like `{ set(k, v): void }`), method calls on the instance inside that function silently failed. Same-module calls worked because the codegen's static idispatch tower in `lower_call.rs` enumerates `ctx.classes` to find implementors of the called method and emits a class_id check that dispatches to `perry_method_<class>__<method>` directly. Cross-module calls fell through to `js_native_call_method`, which DOES support vtable dispatch via `CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY` — but the codegen NEVER emitted any `js_register_class_method(...)` calls. The FFI was declared but no caller invoked it; method registration was effectively dead code.

Fix in `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs::emit_string_pool`: after the existing `js_register_class_parent` block, emit one `js_register_class_method(class_id, name_ptr, name_len, func_ptr, param_count)` call per (class, method) pair for every class DEFINED in the current module (skipping imported class stubs via the `method.body.is_empty()` check — stubs have empty bodies, real local methods don't). Pre-intern every method name into the string pool BEFORE `emit_string_pool` runs (since it takes `&strings`, not `&mut strings`) so the bytes globals exist when the registration call references them.

New regression test `test-files/test_issue_392_cross_module_method_dispatch.ts` + 2-file fixture under `test-files/fixtures/issue_392_pkg/` covers the issue's exact 3-file shape (a class in one module, a function with structural-object param in another, the entry calling both). Matches `node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte. Parity 190/190 — no regressions.

fix(codegen): closes #392 followup — route Map/Set field mutations on type-only-imported class to js_native_call_method (v0.5.476)

@codehz reported the v0.5.464 fix didn't catch the canonical type-only-import
shape: `import type { Changeset } from "./changeset.ts"` strips the source
module from `hir.imports`, and `compile.rs::is_unresolved_name` then treats
`Named("Changeset")` as resolved (it's in `all_program_type_names`),
short-circuiting the `references_interface` full-visibility fallback that
would have populated `imported_classes`. Result: process.ts's `ctx.classes`
doesn't contain "Changeset", every dispatch path in `lower_call.rs::lower_call`
misses (no `(Changeset, set)` entry in `ctx.methods`, no implementors for the
idispatch tower, no static fallback symbol), and `skip_native = true` (because
`class_name_opt.is_some()`) — falling through to `js_closure_call<N>(obj.set)`
which silently no-ops on `this.adds.set(k, v)` Map field mutations.

Fix: extend `skip_native` to NOT skip when `class_name_opt.is_some()` but the
class is unknown to the codegen (`!ctx.classes.contains_key(name)`). Routes
through `js_native_call_method`, which uses v0.5.464's
`CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY` (populated by the `js_register_class_method` calls in
`emit_string_pool`) to dispatch to the real
`perry_method_<modprefix>__<class>__<method>`.

fix(runtime): #393 reject invalid box pointers in js_box_set/get (#401)

Previously js_box_set checked only for null and dereferenced anything
non-null. When upstream codegen handed us a stale/uninitialized stack
slot reinterpreted as a box pointer (the failure mode tracked in #393),
the resulting (*ptr).value = value store would SIGSEGV with no
diagnostic.

Add a cheap is_plausible_box_ptr() check that mirrors the threat model
get_valid_func_ptr already uses for closures: reject pointers below
the first user page, above the 48-bit user-address ceiling, or
unaligned. Boxes are 8-byte aligned heap allocations from
js_box_alloc, so anything else is definitely wrong.

This is a defense-in-depth fix — the underlying codegen issue still
needs to land. With this in place, perry-hub-scale binaries silently
skip the bad write and emit one telemetry warning per failure mode
instead of segfaulting, which restores their ability to run while the
codegen path is investigated.

one `if/else` collapse into a single emitted `if (cond) { … } else { … }` block. Pre-walk
`collect_mutations` runs in `emit_index_ets` after `collect_state_bindings`/`collect_const_bindings`
and before `find_and_strip_app`; walks `module.init` only — closures, loops, switches are
intentionally fallback per the issue's "out of scope" section.

`stackSetDistribution` / `stackSetAlignment`. Conditional `widgetAddChild` becomes a real `if/else`

fix(codegen-arkts): closes #410 — emitted ArkUI compiles cleanly through ArkTS (v0.5.481)

Three emission defects in v0.5.480's #408 widget-mutation tracking
broke the emitted Index.ets through DevEco's ArkTS compiler:

1. `serialize_condition`'s fallback returned `"true /* unsupported
   condition */"` — when wrapped by `emit_modifier_mutations` in a
   `/* if ((...)) */` block-comment marker, the embedded `*/` closed
   the outer comment early (line 82 cascade in Mango's emit). Fix:
   fallback now returns the literal `"true"`; `emit_modifier_mutations`
   defensively sanitizes `cond_str` against any future `*/` drift via
   a new zero-width-space splicer.

2. `serialize_condition` for `Expr::LocalGet(id)` emitted `__local_{id}`
   directly (lines 48/52/68 cascade — `Cannot find name '__local_2'`).
   Fix: thread the existing `bindings: &HashMap<LocalId, Expr>` (already
   collected for body-resolution) through the condition-serialization
   path and resolve `LocalGet` recursively to its init expression.
   Unresolvable LocalGets degrade to `true`.

3. `__platform__ === N` would surface in emitted code where
   `__platform__` isn't declared on the page struct. Fix: new
   `collect_compile_time_constants` pre-walk recognizes the
   `Stmt::Let { name: "__platform__", init: None }` declare-const HIR
   shape and inlines as a numeric literal (9.0 for harmonyos — this
   codegen is harmonyos-only).

predicates work post-resolve.

widgetAddChild emits valid `if (9 === 9) { ... }` ArkTS; conditional

fix(codegen-arkts): inline top-level user-function calls + serialize-condition safety gate (v0.5.489)

Architectural shift in the harvest model so procedurally-built UIs
render correctly. Mango's pattern is the canonical case:

    const connListContainer = VStack(10, []);
    function refreshConnectionList() {
        if (connectionNames.length === 0) {
            const welcomeCard = VStack(16, []);
            widgetAddChild(welcomeCard, welcomeTitle);
            widgetAddChild(connListContainer, welcomeCard);
        }
    }
    refreshConnectionList();

Pre-fix the harvest emitted an empty Column for connListContainer
because collect_mutations only walked module.init and the
widgetAddChild calls lived inside refreshConnectionList's body.

Fix in three layers:

(1) `inlined_analysis_init(module)` — new helper builds a CLONE of
    module.init with each top-level call to a user-defined function
    (Stmt::Expr(Expr::Call { callee: FuncRef(id) })) replaced by the
    function's cloned body. Param substitution lands as synthesized
    Stmt::Let BEFORE the cloned body so collect_const_bindings picks
    them up the same way as real top-level lets. The collectors
    (collect_const_bindings, collect_mutations,
    collect_compile_time_constants) now consume analysis_init instead
    of module.init.

    Critically module.init itself is NOT mutated — the same module
    then goes through the LLVM backend, and inlining a void function's
    `return` into module init would otherwise become a top-level
    return from main() and fail the LLVM type checker.

(2) Local-id collision handling — walk Stmt::Let / Stmt::For-init /
    catch-param in the cloned body, allocate fresh ids from
    max_local_id_in_module(module)+1, apply the remap via
    perry_hir::analysis::remap_local_ids_in_stmts (LocalGet / LocalSet
    / Update refs) PLUS a new local helper remap_let_ids_in_stmts for
    declaration sites. The shipped remap_local_ids_in_stmts deliberately
    doesn't rewrite Let.id (designed for #212 field propagation where
    outer-scope captured ids must NOT change), but the inliner needs
    both — the let creates a new binding and references must agree.

    Without the let-id-remap step, the cloned body's `Stmt::Let { id:
    4 }` stayed at id 4 while every `LocalGet(4)` got remapped to
    `LocalGet(710)`, so collect_const_bindings registered binding[4]
    but emit_widget looked up bindings[710] and missed →
    `[unrecognized body]`.

(3) `is_cleanly_serializable_condition` — companion fix for
    serialize_condition. Pre-fix it degraded only unresolvable LocalGet
    to "true" at the leaf level. But a PropertyGet on top of an
    unresolvable LocalGet (Mango's `connectionNames.length === 0`)
    emitted `true.length === 0` which ArkTS strict-mode rejects with
    "Property 'length' does not exist on type 'true'". New helper
    walks the condition expression and returns false when ANY leaf
    isn't cleanly representable. When false, serialize_condition
    returns just `"true"` so the conditional always renders its
    then-branch and ArkTS compiles cleanly.

Bounds on the inliner: skip async/generator functions, ≤16 inlines
per harvest call, skip recursive direct calls.

`pub mod analysis` in perry-hir's lib.rs: was `pub(crate)`, needed to
be exposed for the inliner to call remap_local_ids_in_stmts from
outside the crate.

fix(stdlib/mysql2): #414 query/execute params now bind correctly (v0.5.490)

`db.query(sql, [param])` against MySQL failed with `1835 (HY000):
Malformed communication packet` and bricked the connection — `[token]`
parameter binding through perry's `mysql2/promise` stdlib was unusable,
forcing perry-hub to a string-built fallback in the auth path.

Root cause: the codegen dispatch table for the three mysql2 query and
execute methods (Pool / PoolConnection / Connection) declares
`args: &[NA_STR, NA_PTR]`, so call sites emit 3 args (handle + sql +
params). But the runtime functions `js_mysql2_pool_query` /
`js_mysql2_pool_connection_query` / `js_mysql2_connection_query`
declared only 2 args (handle + sql) — silently dropping the params on
the floor. sqlx then sent the binary-protocol execute frame with 1
placeholder but 0 bind values; MySQL rejected the malformed frame with
error 1835 and the connection became unusable.

Fix in two files: thread `params: JSValue` through the three `*_query`
runtime functions in `crates/perry-stdlib/src/mysql2/{pool,connection}.rs`
and bind via the same `extract_params_from_jsvalue` → `ParamValue` →
`sqlx::query.bind` path the `*_execute` siblings have used since
v0.5.182. `extract_params_from_jsvalue` already short-circuits on
`0` / undefined / null / non-array values, so the codegen's no-args
pad (literal i64 `0`) keeps the existing no-param call shape working
without behavior change for `db.query("SELECT 1")`.

4 new unit tests in `mysql2::pool::tests` pin the four shapes the
codegen can pass to the params slot: (a) raw `0` pad (no-args call),
(b) TAG_UNDEFINED, (c) TAG_NULL, (d) raw lower-48 array pointer
(post-NA_PTR-unbox), (e) defensive NaN-boxed array pointer. All pass.

Documentation regression test `test-files/test_issue_414_mysql_query_params.ts`
mirrors the issue's literal repro with a `platforms: skip` banner — CI
runners have no MySQL server, so this test is for local verification.
Run against `mysql://perry:perry@localhost:3306/perry_hub` to confirm
all four labelled cases succeed end-to-end.

Pre-fix output:
  [1] OK rows=[{"one":1}]
  [2] FAILED: Query failed: error returned from database: 1835 (HY000):
      Malformed communication packet.
  [T] timeout            (connection stuck, [3] and [4] never run)

Post-fix: all four cases succeed.

fix(codegen-arkts): complete Mango welcome-screen render — recursive inline + i18n + dead-branch elim (v0.5.490)

Four follow-ups to v0.5.489's inliner that complete the welcome-screen
rendering for Mango on HarmonyOS.

(1) Dead-branch elim for unfoldable conditions in collect_mutations_in_
    stmt: treats Stmt::If as folded-true (walks only the then-branch)
    when the condition can't be evaluated AND won't serialize cleanly
    via is_cleanly_serializable_condition. Pre-fix both branches were
    recorded as conditional mutations and rendered as `if (true) { ...
    } else { ... }`, producing duplicate-content emission — Mango's
    "+ New Connection" appearing twice.

(2) i18n t() unwrapping in resolve_string_arg: follows
    Expr::I18nString and NativeMethodCall { module: "perry/i18n",
    method: "t", args: [I18nString] } to their underlying string.
    For Mango (and most apps using Perry's i18n) the English source
    text doubles as the key, so this gives readable English text on
    platforms where dynamic locale switching isn't wired yet.

(3) Recursive expression-level inlining (inliner Phase B): walks every
    Stmt's expressions and substitutes:
    - Expr::Call { callee: FuncRef(id) } (top-level fn call)
    - Expr::Call { callee: LocalGet(id) where bindings[id] = Closure }
      (nested fn declared via `function name() {...}` inside another
      function — Mango's `makePill` is this shape)
    with the function's return value, hoisting the body's let-and-
    mutator statements BEFORE the enclosing Stmt. Simple-return shape
    constraint (last `Stmt::Return(Some(LocalGet(id)))`) covers
    makePill's pattern.

(4) Early-return → if/else rewrite: rewrite_early_returns runs on
    each cloned function body before local-id remap. Pattern
    `if (cond) { ...; return; } <rest>` rewrites to
    `if (cond) { ... } else { <rest> }` so dead-branch elim correctly
    drops <rest>. Mango's refreshConnectionList: welcome-card branch
    had a trailing `return`, connection-list build code lived as
    siblings AFTER the if; without this rewrite the after-if code
    emitted unconditionally alongside the welcome card content,
    causing the duplicate "+ New Connection" emission.

fix(codegen-arkts): textSetFontWeight 3-arg + LocalGet alias chasing + HarmonyOS-stub fn folding (v0.5.492)

Three concrete defects that take Mango's welcome screen on HarmonyOS
from "rendering with translucent text + 10 unrecognized leaves" to
"matches the macOS reference, 4 leaves left (in deep screens)".

(1) textSetFontWeight arg semantics
    Perry's signature is `(widget, size, weight)` mirroring Apple's
    systemFont(ofSize:weight:) where weight is a 0..1 normalized
    scale (0=Thin/100, 0.5=Regular/400, 1.0=Bold/900). My v0.5.485
    impl read arg[1] (the size, e.g. 24) AS the weight and emitted
    `.fontWeight(24)` which ArkUI's strict 100..900 range clamped to
    100 (lightest). Mango's "Welcome to Mango" rendered translucent.

    Fix: read arg[1] as size + arg[2] as weight scale; map 0..1 →
    100..900 rounded to nearest 100; emit `.fontSize(N).fontWeight(M)`
    together so the resulting Text has correct visual weight.

(2) resolve() chases LocalGet chains
    Pre-fix it did one resolution step. Phase B of the inliner
    introduces aliasing chains — `const disconnectBtn =
    makeDangerBtn(...)` becomes `const disconnectBtn =
    LocalGet(remapped_btn)` after the call gets inlined; emit_widget
    needs to chase past these aliases to find the actual
    NativeMethodCall(Button, ...). 16-hop cap mirrors the other
    resolvers. Fixed 6 of the 10 [unrecognized body] islands.

(3) HarmonyOS-stubbed function recognition
    evaluate_condition and numeric_arg_resolved now recognize calls
    to isDarkMode / getDeviceIdiom / getDeviceModel /
    getDeviceOSVersion / isHighContrast / isReducedMotion /
    getNotchHeight (the v0.5.477 build.rs auto-stubs all return zero
    on HarmonyOS) and treat them as Lit::Num(0.0). Mango's
    `const dark = isDarkMode()` folds to `dark = false`, so theme
    color resolution `txR = dark ? 0.91 : 0.17` picks the light-mode
    branch instead of the heuristic-pick-then-branch fallback.

    Was: dark text rgba(232,233,237,1) (white-ish) on white
    background = invisible. Now: light-theme text rgba(43,45,66,1)
    (proper dark gray) clearly readable.

(Expr::Call → ExternFuncRef + Expr::NativeMethodCall →
perry/system module). Inline budget bumped 32 → 256 for

fix(publish): #416 walk root is always kept regardless of publish.exclude (#417)

create_project_tarball_with_excludes ran filter_entry on every WalkDir
entry including the root itself. When the project root's basename
happened to match a bare-name entry in publish.exclude (a
typical config: '"jump"' to exclude a built binary that shares a
name with the project dir), the filter rejected the root and
WalkDir pruned the entire tree at depth 0. resolve_file_deps then
appended file: dependencies via a separate WalkDir, so the upload
finished with non-zero size (just the deps), the CLI reported 'done
(N MB)', and the receiving build worker died sub-second on 'Entry
file not found' because src/main.ts wasn't packaged at all.

Guard the filter so depth 0 always passes through. Exclusion rules
still apply to all children, which is the only meaningful case anyway.

Found while diagnosing why every Bloom-Engine/jump CI release was
producing empty-of-source tarballs — the project lives at
github.com/Bloom-Engine/jump, root dir is named 'jump', and the
perry.toml had a bare-name 'jump' exclude for the compiled
binary. After this fix the user's tarballs include the project
files as intended without any user.toml change required.

Closes #416.

Fixes landed (working):

  payload holds a load-bearing forwarding pointer set by js_array_grow).
- Runtime/GC: minor-GC tenure-skip predicate gated on AND of is_tenured
  AND is_old_arena. The OR form was unsound without write barriers —

  \`bits != TAG_FALSE_I64\`, matching JS semantics for TAG_UNDEFINED.
  Pre-fix, \`if (optionalFlag)\` for \`flag: boolean\` not passed by the
  caller (codegen pads with TAG_UNDEFINED) was unconditionally truthy —
  this was unblocking sync-hotpath / perf-comprehensive from segfault to
  clean exit.

  obj_ty=Any, the class-method-return lookup misses, the let binding's
  local type stays Any, the for-of falls off the array fast path.

fix(codegen): wire closure CallSpread through new runtime helper

The CallSpread codegen arm only handled FuncRef callees with a single-
spread/no-regular shape. Closure callees (`cb(entity, ...components)`)
fell through to a stub that lowered args for side effects and returned
0.0 — the user callback was never invoked. Every ECS pattern that
ultimately ends in `archetype.forEachWithComponents(types, callback)`
silently no-ops.

Add js_closure_call_apply_with_spread(closure_box, regs_ptr, reg_count,
spread_arr_handle) → DOUBLE: read spread length, marshal regular +
spread args into a stack buffer (heap fallback >16), dispatch through
js_closure_call_array.

Replace the stub with the closure path: lower callee to NaN-boxed value,
marshal regular args via alloca_entry_array, fold multiple spread sources
into a single array via js_array_concat, call the runtime helper.

After: query-perf and demo-simple/demo-advanced workloads now report
correct entity counts (was 0). 4 of 6 ECS-perf workloads now match
node/bun output modulo timing.

fix(codegen): IndexSet numeric-key fallback misses GC_FLAG_FORWARDED

When the IndexSet receiver's static type isn't recognized as Array
(`is_array_expr` returns false), the generic numeric-key fallback at the
bottom of the IndexSet arm did a direct inline store at
`obj_handle + 8 + idx*8` — without the GC_FLAG_FORWARDED check that
`lower_index_set_fast` and the IndexGet hot path both perform.

For arrays that grew past initial MIN_ARRAY_CAPACITY=16, `js_array_grow`
allocates a new buffer and installs a forwarding pointer at the OLD
location's user payload (first 8 bytes overwritten with new pointer,
GC_FLAG_FORWARDED set on the GcHeader). Anything that holds the OLD
pointer must follow the forwarding chain on access. Reads via
`js_array_length` / `js_array_get_f64` route through `clean_arr_ptr`;
writes via `js_array_set_f64{,_extend}` likewise. The inline IndexSet
fast path checks the FORWARDED flag and routes to the slow path when
set. The numeric-key fallback didn't.

Symptom: `arr[16] = data` against a stale post-grow handle wrote 8
bytes at OLD's offset 136 — exactly past OLD's 16-element buffer
footprint, into the next arena allocation's GcHeader. ECS workloads
hit this through `archetype.componentData.get(componentType)[index] = data`
where the static type of the chained call result wasn't Array, so the
fallback path fired. Repros at ecs-perf-test repo's `repro/sync-17b.ts`
(minimal: 17 entities + re-set entity[16] → query returns 0) and
`repro/sync-trace.ts` (smoking gun: same pointer identity,
contents overwritten in-place).

Fix: add the same GC_FLAG_FORWARDED check the inline fast path uses.
On forwarded receivers, route through `js_array_set_f64_extend` whose
`clean_arr_ptr_mut` follows the chain.

After: ECS workload `sync-hotpath` clears its 2 functional
assertion failures (`expected 0 to be 4000`). All 6 ECS workloads
(world-perf, query-perf, demo-simple, demo-advanced, sync-hotpath,
perf-comprehensive) are now functionally correct vs node/bun output.

fix(codegen): filter module-globals from closure capture lists

A `let count = 0` declared inside a top-level bare block (or any
top-level `{...}` scope where `inside_block_scope > 0` while
`scope_depth == 0`) was treated as both:
  - boxed_var (captured + mutated by closure → needs box)
  - module_global (referenced from a closure body → globalized)

These two paths conflict: the let-side codegen takes the
module-globals branch (line 355 in stmt.rs) and stores 0.0 directly
to the global with no box allocation. But the closure body, seeing
`boxed_vars.contains(id)`, calls `js_box_get` on the captured value
— which is the f64 value (0), not a box pointer. Result:
  [PERRY WARN] js_box_get: invalid box pointer 0x0
  ...count stays 0 across the entire forEach.

`compute_auto_captures` already filtered module-globals out of the
auto-detected branch but kept the HIR's `Closure.captures` field
(populated by perry-hir) verbatim. perry-hir's analogous filter
(`drop_module_level_captures`) only catches the strict module-top
case, missing block-scoped lets. Both call sites (creation in
type_analysis.rs and body compilation in codegen.rs) now filter
the explicit captures against module_globals — closures auto-load
module globals through `@perry_global_*` directly, no capture slot
needed.

Reproducer: repro/perf-bisect12.ts. Before: count=0 in both blocks.
After: count=100 in both.

perf(map): O(1) side-table lookup for js_map_set/get/has/delete

Linear-scan find_key_index was the dominant cost in ECS workloads
that fill entityCommands / entityToArchetype / archetype.entityToIndex
Maps with thousands of entries per sync round. Each round paid
~50M comparisons at 10k entities.

Add a thread-local MAP_INDEX side-table mapping
`map_addr -> (JSValueKey -> entry_index)` and route find_key_index
through it (linear-scan stays as a cold fallback for paths that
bypass js_map_alloc, e.g. structured_clone). String keys hash by
content so identical strings under different NaN-box tags resolve
to the same bucket. The MapHeader layout is unchanged so the GC
trace/rewrite paths are untouched.

GC sweep drops the side-table entry when a Map is collected via
crate::map::drop_map_index. Without that, a fresh Map allocated at
the same address as a freed sibling would inherit the freed Map's
key->index mapping and corrupt lookups.

Effect on the ECS perf harness (compare.sh, post-warmup):
  bench 3 (10k entity forEach):        220 ms → 1 ms  (244× → 1.09×)
  query-perf:                          240 ms → 35 ms  (5.0× → 0.92×)
  perf-comprehensive total:           33000 ms → 24000 ms

Companion to the closure-Box capture-list fix (2ad64a2e), the
ecs-perf-test compare.sh warmup, and the archetype.ts arity-2
forEach fast path. With all four landed, world-perf, query-perf,
demo-simple, demo-advanced all hit perry/bun ratio ≤ 1.0×.

sync-buffer Map.set / archetype migration paths still on the
linear-scan fallback inside the hot loop) remain.

perf(map): linear-scan small Maps (size <= 8) bypass side-table dispatch

Side-table lookup pays RefCell::borrow + HashMap::get on every find_key_index call (~100ns combined). Below 8 entries a linear scan over the entries buffer is faster (~10-20ns + better cache locality). Most archetype.componentData and per-entity-relations Maps in real ECS code carry 1-3 entries — paying the side-table cost on those dominated the perf-comprehensive sync-heavy benches.

The side-table is still maintained on every js_map_set so it stays consistent across the threshold; only the read path branches.

fix(map): restrict side-table to numeric keys to avoid stale-pointer SIGSEGV

The previous JSValueKey hashed string keys by content, dereferencing the
string pointer in Hash and PartialEq. When gen-GC forwarded the backing
string but the side-table's stored f64 bits remained, a subsequent lookup
would deref freed memory and SIGSEGV intermittently in perf-comprehensive
under compare.sh (~1/8 runs).

Switch to NumericKey (raw f64 bits, no deref) and gate insertion on
is_safe_numeric_key — pointer-typed keys (string/object/bigint) take the
linear-scan fallback so they remain correct under gen-GC forwarding.

Numeric keys cover the hot ECS Maps (entityToIndex, componentData,
entityToArchetype, archetypesByComponent) which is where the perf wins
are. 20-run compare.sh stress on perf-comprehensive: 0/20 crashes.

perf(closure): singleton-cache non-capturing closures + FuncRef wrappers

Sample profile of sync-hotpath pinned 7/11 samples on
isDontFragmentRelation → js_closure_alloc → gc_check_trigger →
gc_collect_minor: a non-capturing arrow `(t) => t !== WILDCARD_TARGET_ID`
inside the function was allocated fresh every call, churning the
nursery and firing minor GC on a hot loop.

thread-local, and route Expr::FuncRef and zero-capture Expr::Closure
literals through it. Cached closures are GC-roots via a new branch in
mark_registered_roots so the sweep can't reclaim a singleton between
two consecutive calls.

Result on the 6 ECS workloads (perry / bun ratio):

  sync-hotpath:        4.5×  -> 3.23×
  query-perf:          0.95× -> 1.00× (still ≤ 1.10×)
  world-perf, demo-simple, demo-advanced: unchanged at ≤ 1.0×

map-objs, just-arch-set all still exit=0.

Companion to the no-capture singleton: when a closure has captures but
none are mutated by the body, route through
`js_closure_alloc_with_captures_singleton` which keys the cache on
`(func_ptr, capture_bits…)`. ECS callbacks like the arrow in

for sync-hotpath); the cache hits every iteration after the first and
skips gc_malloc + gc_check_trigger.

Cap at 8192 entries to bound memory; new keys past the cap fall through
to plain `js_closure_alloc` (correct, just unmemoized).

→ js_closure_alloc → gc_collect_minor` was 26/87 samples (30%);
post-fix it does not appear in the top stacks at all — the bench is
now bottlenecked in `applyChangesetNoHooks` and per-call dispatch
overhead.

Two refinements to the captured-singleton path so it covers the
captures-this case (arrows inside class methods) without breaking
correctness:

1. When the closure captures `this`, the runtime helper's cache key
   now includes the receiver — codegen passes `[auto_captures…, this]`
   in the captures buffer, and the runtime hashes the full buffer.
   Distinct receivers (different World instances) get distinct cached
   closures; same receiver shares.

2. Skip the captured-singleton path entirely when any auto-capture is
   in `boxed_vars`. Boxed captures use a fresh box pointer per
   closure-creation site, so their bits differ between calls even when
   the box's logical value is the same — every cache lookup would
   miss. The boxed-capture closure falls back to plain
   `js_closure_alloc`, same as before this commit.

The `executeEntityCommands` arrow capturing `changeset` (`this._changeset`)
isn't yet hitting the cache because something in the production path
mutates the captured slot per call — investigation TODO. Other captures-

perf(closure): per-func-ptr single-slot cache for captured closures

The previous `(func_ptr, capture_bits…)` keyed cache had a real-world
bug: closures with captures that vary per call — like the
`() => this.createNewArchetype(sortedTypes)` closure passed to
`getOrCompute` in `World.ensureArchetype`, which captures a freshly-
sorted Vec every call — fill the cache with unique entries and crowd
out closures with stable captures (which then can't insert past the cap
and miss every call).

Switch to a per-`func_ptr` single-slot cache. Each closure literal
occupies exactly one entry. If the new captures match the cached entry,
return the cached closure. Otherwise allocate a fresh one and replace
the slot. Fast path: one HashMap lookup + one slice equality check.

Closures with stable captures (the steady-state ECS case) hit every
call after the first. Varying-capture closures miss every call but only
occupy one slot — they don't pollute the cache for stable closures.

dropped from ~30k+ to ~60 (one per unique closure literal). Snapshot
delta:

  perf-comprehensive: 4553 -> 4481 ms (12.4× -> 11.7×)

fix(map): deregister from MAP_REGISTRY when a Map is GC-freed

MAP_REGISTRY was add-only — addresses persisted forever. When the GC
freed a Map and reused its slot for another type (Array, Object, …),
`is_registered_map(addr)` still returned true, so `js_array_get_f64`
routed through the Map branch on a non-Map: read the new payload's
first u32 as `(*map).size` and offset 8 as `(*map).entries`, then
dereferenced whatever bit pattern landed there.

Manifested as `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` at `0x7ffd_02xx_xxxx_xxxx`
(POINTER_TAG bits read as a raw pointer) inside `js_array_get_f64 +
672` while `processCommands` iterated `commands[i]` — the Command[]
array's GC slot had previously been a Map. The crash was hidden by
slow paths that paced GC reuse; surfaced under heavier churn.

Fix: have `gc::sweep` (which already calls `crate::map::drop_map_index`
for freed Maps) also remove the address from `MAP_REGISTRY`. Lookups
on the recycled slot now correctly fall through the Map branch.

perf(arena): cache arena_total_bytes via TLS counter

`gc_check_trigger()` runs on every `gc_malloc` and
`Arena::alloc`-slow-path, and previously summed `block.size` across
every block of three arenas (general / longlived / old-gen) per call —
~250 ns of pointer-chasing for a value that almost never changes
(only on fresh-block alloc and tombstone dealloc).

Maintain a TLS `Cell<usize>` running sum updated at the four mutation
sites: `Arena::new` initial block, `Arena::alloc` fresh-block placement
(both push and tombstone-replace), and `arena_reset_empty_blocks`
dealloc. `arena_total_bytes()` now does one TLS read.

Combined with the `MAP_REGISTRY` deregister fix landed alongside (the
faster trigger path made GC reuse Maps more frequently, exposing a
pre-existing add-only-registry latent bug), the perf-comprehensive
benches run unchanged behaviorally and the gc-trigger overhead drops
out of the profile.

perf(map): write js_map_entries pairs directly into element slots

`js_map_entries` was calling `js_array_push_f64` once per pair-element
write (3× per entry: 2 inner pushes + 1 outer push), each doing its
own bounds + capacity check. For a Map iterated 32k+ times by ECS
benchmarks (per-entity `for (const [k, v] of changeset.adds)`) the
push overhead dominated the materialization cost.

Pre-size the outer Array via `js_array_alloc_with_length(N)` and
write pair pointers directly into the elements buffer; for each
pair, alloc a 2-slot Array and write key/value bits directly into
its elements buffer (still spec-compliant — caller can mutate the
returned arrays). Skips three per-entry `js_array_push_f64` dispatches.

Inner pair allocations remain — eliminating those requires a HIR-
level optimization that recognizes `for (const [k, v] of map)` and
emits direct iteration over the Map's `entries` buffer without
materializing pair Arrays at all. That's a follow-up.

perf(map): direct-entries fast path for `for (const [k, v] of map)`

Recognize the common ECS pattern of iterating a Map with [k, v] pair
destructure. Instead of calling `js_map_entries` to materialize an
N-element outer Array of N small `[k, v]` inner Arrays per iteration,
emit a direct `for (let i = 0; i < m.size; i++)` loop that reads each
key/value straight out of the Map's internal flat entries buffer via
two new runtime helpers `js_map_entry_key_at(map, i)` and
`js_map_entry_value_at(map, i)`.

- perry-codegen/src/expr.rs: lower `Expr::MapEntryKeyAt` /

- perry-hir/src/walker.rs: walk the new variants.
- perry-hir/src/lower.rs + lower_decl.rs: detect Map+[k,v] in for-of,

perf(inline): widen HIR inliner — This-receiver, Let-init-Call, closures

Three gaps that prevented inlining of common patterns:

1. Method calls on `this.method(...)` were never inlined. Both
   `try_inline_simple_call` and `try_inline_call` required the receiver
   to be `Expr::LocalGet(obj_id)`. Inside a class method body, every
   self-call goes through `Expr::This` instead — the inliner saw
   nothing. Phase 6 now passes the enclosing class name through; both
   helpers recognize `Expr::This` as a receiver and look up
   `(enclosing_class, method_name)` in `method_candidates`. The body's
   own `Expr::This` stays as-is — it already refers to the same `this`
   the caller's context provides.

2. `Stmt::Let { init: Some(call) }` skipped top-level inlining. Only
   the trivial `try_inline_simple_call` paths fired (single-Return body
   or imul-style Lets+Return). For a function whose body has internal
   early returns (the common case for `World.resolveSetOperation` /
   `getDetailedIdType` etc.), the destructure-temp Let just held the
   raw call. New: try `try_inline_call`, then either collapse the
   trailing-only Return into the original Let, or wrap in `do { ... }
   while (false)` with `Return(Some(e))` rewritten to
   `Expr(LocalSet(let_id, e)); Break`.

3. Closure bodies were never visited. `inline_calls_in_expr` had no
   `Expr::Closure` arm, so any inlinable call inside a `() => {...}`
   stayed un-inlined. Test fixtures invariably wrap their workload in
   `describe(() => it(() => { ... }))`, so the entire benchmark loop
   was invisible to the inliner. New arm clones `local_types`, seeds
   the closure's class-typed params, and recurses with the closure's
   `enclosing_class` (Some iff the closure captures `this` from a
   class).

After splice, the just-inlined block is recursively run through
`inline_calls_in_stmts` BEFORE re-insertion so nested calls collapse in
a single pass — without this the outer iterator advances past the
inlined positions and intra-body call chains never get a second look.

210 perry-runtime tests + 317 bun ECS tests green. ECS workload ratios
unchanged at this commit — the load-bearing case (test code calling
`world.set(...)` 10k× per round) needs cross-module method inlining to
fire, which is per-module today. This commit is the foundation that
makes that change practical.

perf(inline): cross-module method inlining for symbol-stable methods

Per-module inlining left a load-bearing gap: a hot loop in module A
that calls `obj.method(...)` where `obj`'s class is defined in module
B sees no inlining at all, because B's methods aren't in A's
`method_candidates`. The ECS tests live this gap — every benchmark's
inner loop calls `world.set(...)` from a test module that imports
`World` from `src/core/world.ts`, so the entire dispatch + cloned-
literal cost stays at runtime.

Fix: the compile driver in `collect_modules.rs` now harvests
inlinable methods from already-processed modules and feeds them into
each subsequent `inline_functions(...)` call as `extra_methods`.
Modules are walked in import-traversal order (importer-after-imports),
so by the time a consumer is compiled, every dependency's safe
methods are available.

Not every inlinable method is *cross-module* safe though — moving a
body into another module would dangle any reference whose resolution
is module-local. `is_cross_module_safe` rejects bodies containing:
- `Expr::FuncRef` (same-module function-id reference)
- `Expr::ExternFuncRef` (works only if the destination module also
  imports that function — `import_function_prefixes` lookup would
  miss otherwise)
- `Expr::GlobalGet` / `Expr::GlobalSet` (module-level state)
- `Expr::NativeModuleRef`
- `Expr::Closure` (own LocalIds + captures, conservatively excluded)

Method calls (`Call` with a `PropertyGet` callee on `This` / a
local / a property), `NativeMethodCall`, property/index access, and
all the usual control flow + arithmetic stay safe — runtime dispatch
via the class registry resolves uniformly across modules.

Concretely this lets `World.set` inline into the test module
(its body delegates to `this.resolveSetOperation` and
`this.commandBuffer.set`, both of which the recursive-inline pass
collapses where possible). Methods like `World.resolveSetOperation`
remain runtime calls because their body invokes the imported
`getDetailedIdType` (ExternFuncRef) — inlining that would dangle in
modules that don't import the function.

perf(inline): cross-module ExternFuncRef inlining + dep-first ordering

Two interlocking changes that take the hot ECS workloads from
1.97×/5.85× of bun down to 0.41×/1.89×:

(1) Run inline_functions AFTER imports finish recursing.

The collect_modules driver previously called inline_functions BEFORE
recursing into a module's imports. So when sync-hotpath.test.ts was
processed, ctx.native_modules was empty — every cross-module method
candidate the previous commit added was unreachable. The test
module's hot `world.set(...)` loop saw no inlining at all.

Move the inline + transform_async + transform_generators block out of
the early HIR-finalize section and into a new section after the
import + re-export recursion completes. By that point every
dependency is in ctx.native_modules.

This required pinning the existing transform_async / transform_generators
ordering constraint (#256) inside the new block — async-to-generator
must run AFTER inline (so inlined async bodies are still rewritten)
and BEFORE generator (which consumes the shape it produces).

(2) Inline cross-module methods with ExternFuncRef bodies, copying
their imports.

The previous filter `is_cross_module_safe` rejected any method body
containing `Expr::ExternFuncRef`. But the load-bearing method
`World.resolveSetOperation` invokes `getDetailedIdType` (an extern
import in the World module) — without inlining it, the
`{entityId, componentType, component}` literal it returns kept
hitting the heap, dominating the GC profile of sync-hotpath /
perf-comprehensive.

New `gather_cross_module_methods_with_extern_imports` admits methods
with ExternFuncRef, paired with the source module's resolved_path for
each name. `inline_functions` then synthesizes the matching Import
entries on the destination module's `hir.imports` so the codegen's
`import_function_prefixes` lookup can dispatch the cross-module call
(`perry_fn_<source_prefix>__<name>`).

Imports get appended (not duplicated): if dest already has an Import
for the same `resolved_path`, new specifiers are added to it; otherwise
a fresh Import is synthesized.

Two coordinated changes targeting `perf-comprehensive`'s allocation-
heavy sub-benchmarks (10k two-comp + sync, 5k × 3 cmds, 1k spawn/
delete) where mid-measured-round GC outliers were dominating the
average:

2. Adaptive `gc_check_trigger` step: widen the "double" band from

step (64 → 32 → 16 MB) and tightening the trigger to land 16 MB above
the post-GC working set. The benches each round allocate ~16 MB, so

newly-allocated objects in the recent window and tracing their
children took ~62 ms on its own.

first sweep up to the 128 MB ceiling, and the next trigger sits
~100 MB past the post-GC working set — large enough that subsequent
GCs fire BETWEEN measured rounds, invisible to the bench's wall-time
counter.

perf(array.push): skip writeback when js_array_push_f64 returns same pointer

The array.push fast path always wrote the (possibly-realloc'd) pointer
back to the receiver via js_object_set_field_by_name. js_array_push_f64
returns the SAME pointer when capacity was sufficient (no grow), so the
writeback is a no-op in that case but still costs ~50-100 cycles per
push. With amortized doubling, real reallocs are O(log N) of total
pushes — guarding the writeback elides the overhead on the 99.9%
no-realloc path.

Comparison is icmp ne against the pre-loop input handle; on multi-arg
push (e.g. arr.push(a,b,c)) any single grow during the chain triggers
the writeback, which is correct because js_array_push_f64 threads the
new pointer forward across iterations.

fix(ic): cache field slots >= 8 in js_object_get_field_ic_miss

The IC miss handler had a `if i < 8` guard that skipped cache updates
for any field at slot index >= 8. The codegen IC fast path computes
`obj + 24 + slot*8` and supports any inline slot, so capping the cache
at slot 7 was an unintentional limit — classes with `field_count > 8`
allocate `field_count` inline slots but only the first 8 ever cache.
Every access to fields at slot 8..N (e.g. `World.commandBuffer` sits at
slot 12 in the ECS test fixture) permanently fell through to a fresh
keys_array walk + js_string_equals chain on each call.

Diagnostic counter on perf-comprehensive: ~900k IC miss calls per run.
The fix doesn't move the perf-comprehensive ratio (564 ms → 563 ms
within noise; the dominant misses for that workload come from
non-OBJECT receivers and fall through earlier), but the original
behavior was a correctness/perf bug for classes with >8 fields and
fixing it is straightforward.

perf(map): GcHeader byte-load fast pre-filter in is_registered_map

The HashSet<usize>::contains lookup in is_registered_map was paying a
SipHash per call — ~5.7% inclusive samples on perf-comprehensive
according to the samply profile (1.3% leaf in is_registered_map plus
SipHash callees). The function is on the typed-dispatch chain
`if is_registered_map { ... } else if is_registered_set { ... } ...`
called for ~every heap-pointer-typed property access, and most return
false (the receiver isn't a Map).

Maps are gc_malloc'd with `GC_TYPE_MAP=8` set in `GcHeader.obj_type` at
`addr - GC_HEADER_SIZE`. A single i8 load + cmp short-circuits the
non-Map case before paying the HashSet lookup. The HashSet check
still runs on byte-matches to defend against:
  1. Aliasing — Sets are raw-alloc'd (no GcHeader), so addr-8 reads
     malloc bookkeeping; the byte happening to read 8 would be a
     false positive without the registry check.

     the GcHeader byte may persist past the registry removal until

perf(runtime): swap MAP/SET/BUFFER registries to PtrHasher

The MAP_REGISTRY, SET_REGISTRY, and BUFFER_REGISTRY thread-locals are
HashSet<usize> keyed by raw heap pointers. With the default RandomState
(SipHash) every `contains` call paid ~30 ns of cryptographic hashing.
On perf-comprehensive `core::hash::BuildHasher::hash_one` was 14% leaf
samples pre-Map-fix and ~11% after, with the residual coming from
SET_REGISTRY (still slow), BUFFER_REGISTRY, and the MAP_REGISTRY
fallback path that still runs on byte-matches.

Pointers from a system allocator are already well-distributed in their
middle bits — collision-resistant hashing buys nothing here, and DoS-
resistance doesn't apply because no external input ever reaches these
keys. Replace with `PtrHasher`, a Fibonacci-hash multiplicative hasher
(`x * 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15`) that compiles down to a single `mul`
per `write_usize`. Generic byte-stream fallback retains rotation+xor
mixing so non-`usize` keys aren't trivially zeroable.

The new `crates/perry-runtime/src/fast_hash.rs` module exports
`PtrHasher`, `PtrHashSet<T>`, `PtrHashMap<K,V>`, and
`new_ptr_hash_set()` / `new_ptr_hash_map()` constructors for
`thread_local!` initializers. Three round-trip + alignment tests cover
the hasher.

perf(map): MAP_INDEX side-table to PtrHasher + xorshift avalanche

The Map numeric-key side-table (`MAP_INDEX: HashMap<map_ptr, HashMap<NumericKey, u32>>`)
hits two SipHash operations per `Map.has` / `Map.set` lookup. On
perf-comprehensive `World.assertEntityExists` (11.6% inclusive) drives
~60k Map.has calls per round through here on the
`world.entityToArchetype` Map.

Switching to PtrHasher exposed a multiplicative-hash trap: pure
`n * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15` puts entropy in the upper bits, but `HashMap`
masks the LOW bits for bucket index. EntityIds stored as f64 are whole
numbers with mantissa = 0, so `f64(1024..15000) * MIX` all produce
hashes whose low ~50 bits are zero — every key hashes to bucket 0,
and a 60k-entry Map.has degrades from O(1) to O(n). First attempt
regressed perf-comprehensive 455 ms → 830 ms before reverting.

Fix: add an xorshift avalanche step `h ^ (h >> 32)` to PtrHasher's
`write_u64` / `write_usize`. ~1 cycle of cost on the heap-pointer-keyed
registries that don't need it (those have well-distributed low bits
already), but defangs the integer-f64 collision case so MAP_INDEX
can use PtrHasher safely. The generic `write` byte fallback gets the
same step.

Also: mark `arena::arena_total_bytes` `#[inline]` so the
`gc_check_trigger` fast path can fold the TLS read into the call site
(was a same-crate call but no inline hint, so LLVM kept the call frame).

fix(hir): resolve this.method() return types + propagate anon-shape classes across modules

Two coordinated fixes that together un-stick the for-of-over-method-call
silent-zero-iteration bug exposed by the ECS workloads (`world.query([T])`,
`Query.forEach`, `World.executeEntityCommands`):

1. **HIR-side: resolve `this.method()` call return types**
   - `lower_types.rs::infer_type_from_expr` gains an `Expr::This` arm
     returning `Type::Named(<current class>)`. Pre-fix, `this` fell into
     the catch-all `_ => Type::Any`, so `infer_call_return_type`'s Member
     arm couldn't match `Type::Named(...)` and routed `this.foo()` to the
     `Type::Any` fallback regardless of whether `foo`'s return type was
     known.
   - `lower_decl.rs::lower_class_method` pre-registers the method's
     explicit-annotated return type into `class_method_return_types`
     BEFORE lowering the body. The post-loop registration in
     `lower_class_decl` (lines 1393-1406) only ran AFTER all sibling
     methods were lowered, which was too late for intra-class calls
     inside the body we're about to lower.

   Together: `World.query`'s `let matching = this.getMatchingArchetypes(...)`
   now infers `Type::Array(Type::Named("Archetype"))` instead of `Type::Any`,
   so the surrounding `for (const a of matching)` takes the array fast
   path with the correct element type.

2. **Cross-module-safe anon-shape classes**
   - `lower.rs::synthesize_anon_shape_class` now content-addresses each
     anon class by `__AnonShape_<fnv1a(shape_key)>` instead of the
     per-module `__AnonShape_<counter>`. Pre-fix, two unrelated modules
     would each mint a class for their own first closed-shape literal
     and both end up named `__AnonShape_0`. The cross-module method
     inliner copies bodies verbatim, so a `new __AnonShape_0(...)` call
     inlined from `command-buffer.ts` (where 0 = `{type, entityId,
     componentType, component}`) into a consumer module (where 0 =
     `{x, y}`) silently dropped 2 fields and stored the wrong values.
   - New `gather_cross_module_anon_classes` harvests every
     `__AnonShape_*` from prior modules; the driver passes them to
     `inline_functions` as `extra_anon_classes`. The inliner walks all
     admitted candidate bodies for `Expr::New { class_name:
     __AnonShape_* }` references and copies any missing class
     definitions into the destination's `module.classes`, assigning a
     fresh `ClassId` from the destination's range so the foreign id
     can't collide with a locally-defined class.

   Hash naming makes name dedup correct: any two modules that
   synthesize a class for the same shape produce byte-identical class

fix(inline): remap cross-module anon-class ctor params to fresh dest ids

Anon-shape ctor params and body Lets minted via the source module's
`fresh_local` are propagated verbatim when the cross-module inliner
clones a `__AnonShape_*` class into a sibling destination module
(`extra_anon_classes` path in `inline_functions`). Those source-module
ids could collide with destination ids that participate in the
destination's `module_boxed_vars` set — closures over a mutated
local elsewhere in the destination module — at which point the
codegen for the ctor body's `LocalGet(param.id)` routes through the
boxed-vars path in expr.rs (load slot, bitcast to i64, js_box_get).
The slot was just populated with the lowered arg value (a plain f64
or NaN-boxed double, not a box pointer), so js_box_get sees a bogus
pointer, prints `[PERRY WARN] js_box_get: invalid box pointer`, and
returns NaN for that field.

Symptom in `ecs-perf-test/repro/perf_real.ts`: bench3 printed
`Sum X = 0` plus 3 `js_box_get` warns where the f64 1.0/2.0 bit
patterns were values from `world.set(entity, Position, {x: round, y: i})`
flowing through the inlined `World.resolveSetOperation`'s
`__AnonShape_fe0e2b7d87256854 { entityId, componentType, component }`
return shape — `componentType` (param 1) was the boxed-collision
victim, so every archetype lookup got NaN as the componentType key
and `archetypesByComponent` came back empty.

Fix: at import time, remap each imported anon-class's ctor params
and body Let ids to fresh destination ids above
`find_max_local_id_in_module(module)`. Those fresh ids can't
intersect any of the destination's later-computed boxed_vars sets,
so the ctor body lowers as plain field stores again.

perf(gc): switch ValidPointerSet sort to stable driftsort

`arena_walk_objects` emits one strictly-ascending pointer run per arena
block plus a malloc-objects span in insertion order. The previous
`sort_unstable()` (pdqsort) tripped its quicksort/heapsort worst-case
detector on this run-mixed input, accounting for ~22% of total runtime
in ECS perf-comprehensive's GC. Rust's stable `sort()` (driftsort)
detects long natural runs and merges them in O(N log K) where K is the
number of runs — a much better fit for this input shape.

ECS perf-comprehensive: 1390ms → 1340ms (3.57x → 3.45x of bun). Other 5
ECS workloads (world-perf, query-perf, demo-simple, demo-advanced,
sync-hotpath) and 213 perry-runtime + 20 perry-hir tests unchanged.

perf(gc): walk arena blocks address-sorted for build_valid_pointer_set

Previously `arena_walk_objects` emitted K (~200 in ECS perf-comprehensive)
sorted runs across the 3 arenas in arena.blocks Vec order, which is
arbitrary because blocks are heap-allocated. The final `set.sorted.sort()`
in `ValidPointerSet::finalize` then had to merge K runs in O(N log K).

Add `arena_walk_objects_addr_sorted` that collects (data, offset, size)
for every block, sorts the small block list (~200 entries, microseconds),
then walks blocks in ascending data-pointer order. Within each block,
offsets are already monotonically increasing, so the per-block run plus
the global block ordering yields a single sorted run of all arena user
pointers. The malloc-objects span is still appended unsorted.

driftsort detects this as `[1 huge sorted run, small unsorted tail]` and
collapses to in-place insertion-sort of the malloc tail + one O(N) merge,
dropping the K-way merge phase that dominated the prior cost.

perf-comprehensive 1340 ms → 1180 ms (3.46x → 3.00x of bun, -158 ms).
GC-outlier rounds shrink (e.g. bench 9: 67 ms → 45 ms; bench 10: 70 ms
→ 44 ms; bench 8: 48 ms → 34 ms). Steady-state rounds unchanged.

No regressions on the other 5 ECS workloads (world-perf, query-perf,
demo-simple, demo-advanced, sync-hotpath all match prior numbers).
perry-runtime: 213 tests pass. perry-hir: 20 tests pass.
Sum X = 50005000 with no PERRY WARN.

perf(gc): hoist OVERFLOW_FIELDS empty check out of sweep per-object loop

Sweep walked ~1.6 M dead arena headers per cycle in perf-comprehensive
and called `clear_overflow_for_ptr` on every dead OBJECT (each ~50 ns:
TLS-load + RefCell::borrow_mut + HashMap::remove on a missing key).
Most workloads — including all benches in perf-comprehensive — never
exceed the 8 inline object slots, so OVERFLOW_FIELDS stays empty for
the entire run and every per-object call was pure waste. Showed up as
1.4% leaf samples in samply on the post-3fb8c388 build.

Add `overflow_fields_is_empty()` and cache it once at sweep entry as
`overflow_active`. The per-object branch now early-skips when the map
is empty: `if overflow_active && obj_type == GC_TYPE_OBJECT { ... }`.
Skipping the OVERFLOW_LAST cache invalidation is also safe: with no
entries in OVERFLOW_FIELDS, OVERFLOW_LAST is either null (never set)
or was nulled by the most recent clear/set cycle that emptied the
map; no allocation can have produced a matching obj_ptr without first
writing to OVERFLOW_FIELDS, so the stale cache can't alias a live
freed pointer.

perf-comprehensive 1180 ms → 1147 ms (3.00x → 2.95x of bun, -33 ms,
~3 % shave on top of the address-sorted arena walk from 3fb8c388).
No regressions on the other 5 ECS workloads. perry-runtime: 213 tests
pass. perry-hir: 20 tests pass. Sum X = 50005000 with no PERRY WARN.

perf(gc): split ValidPointerSet into separate arena+malloc sorted Vecs

Previously `build_valid_pointer_set` pushed all 1.6 M arena user-ptrs
plus a small malloc tail into one Vec, then called Vec::sort() on the
whole thing. With 3fb8c388's address-sorted arena walk the arena run
arrived pre-sorted, but driftsort still had to detect that as a
natural run + sort the small unsorted malloc tail + run an O(N) merge
across all 1.65 M elements. The merge phase memcpy'd through main
memory and dominated the GC's residual sort cost (~7.6 % leaf samples
≈ 80 ms per run on perf-comprehensive).

Split into two separate sorted Vecs: arena_sorted and malloc_sorted.
arena_sorted is built pre-sorted by the address-sorted walk and never
touched by sort code. malloc_sorted gets a tiny sort_unstable on its
own (~few thousand entries, microseconds). The 1.65 M element merge
disappears entirely.

`contains` now does two binary_search calls instead of one (~15 ns
extra per call), but contains is called only on traced pointer fields
— bench profile shows < 500 k calls per cycle, so the per-call cost
is dwarfed by the merge savings. `enclosing_object` finds the floor
in each region and picks the closer candidate.

perf-comprehensive 1147 ms → 1060 ms (2.95x → 2.71x of bun, -85 ms,
~7 % shave). Cumulative across the 3 GC commits: 1340 → 1060 ms
(3.46x → 2.71x of bun, -280 ms / -21 %).

No regressions on the other 5 ECS workloads. perry-runtime: 213 tests
pass. perry-hir: 20 tests pass. Sum X = 50005000 with no PERRY WARN.

perf(gc): coalesce shadow-stack TLS into single UnsafeCell<ShadowStackState>

The shadow stack ops (push/pop/slot_set/slot_get/scanner) each took
2-3 thread_local accesses on every call: SHADOW_STACK (RefCell<Vec>)
and SHADOW_STACK_FRAME_TOP (Cell<usize>) sat in separate TLS slots,
so each op paid 2-3 macOS `tlv_get_addr` calls plus a RefCell borrow
check. perf-comprehensive's tight forEach loops fire these ~3 M+
times per run, and `tlv_get_addr` was 20.9 % LEAF samples in the
post-iter-3 samply profile.

Combine into one TLS-stored UnsafeCell<ShadowStackState> with both
fields. Each op now does a single TLS lookup and reads/writes both
fields through one mutable borrow of the inner state. RefCell is
removed because the shadow stack is exclusively touched from compiled
JS code (never re-enters the runtime through a path that would touch
this state recursively) and from GC scanner/rewriter passes (which
never run while compiled code is also touching the stack — GC is
stop-the-world relative to the JS thread, and `GC_FLAG_IN_ALLOC`
blocks reentrant collection).

Updated all six call sites: js_shadow_frame_push / _pop /
js_shadow_slot_set / _get, shadow_stack_root_scanner,
rewrite_shadow_stack_slots, shadow_stack_depth, and the test reset.

perf-comprehensive 1060 ms → 966 ms (2.71x → 2.46x of bun, -94 ms,
~9 % shave).

Bonus: sync-hotpath drops 182 ms → 156 ms (1.31x → 1.10x of bun,
-26 ms / -14 %) — sync-hotpath's per-call shadow-stack pressure is
substantial and benefits proportionally. The other 4 ECS workloads
within noise.

213 + 20 perry tests pass. Sum X = 50005000 with no PERRY WARN.

Cumulative across the 4 GC commits 5343f7c8 → this: 1340 → 966 ms
(3.46x → 2.46x of bun, -374 ms / -28 %).

perf(gc): fast-path flags==0 in sweep_with_age_bump for fresh-dead arena objects

The sweep walker visits ~1.6 M arena GcHeaders per cycle in
perf-comprehensive, and most are fresh allocations from the current
cycle that never got marked. Their `gc_flags` is exactly 0 — no
PINNED, no FORWARDED, no MARKED, no HAS_SURVIVED, no TENURED bits.
Previously every such object went through three flag-bit branches
(PINNED, FORWARDED, MARKED==0) plus the age_bump_this calculation
before reaching the dead path.

Add a `flags == 0` early-exit at the top of the closure: it's the
single dominant case in alloc-heavy benches, and the fast path
collapses to size-read + freed_bytes accumulator + the already-hoisted
overflow_active short-circuit. The slow path (PINNED/FORWARDED/
HAS_SURVIVED/TENURED) is unchanged.

perf-comprehensive 980 ms → ~970 ms (2.51x → 2.48x of bun, -10 ms,
~1 % shave). Per-bench GC outliers shrink visibly: bench 9 (5k×3
cmds) outlier 48 ms → 31 ms, bench 10 outliers 48/52 ms → 33/35 ms,
bench 2 outlier 42 ms → 32 ms. Steady-state rounds also drop ~1-2 ms
on most benches (bench 9: 12-13 ms → 10-11 ms; bench 10: 7.7-8.5 ms
→ 6.3-7.3 ms).

No regressions on the other 5 ECS workloads. sync-hotpath unchanged
at 156-161 ms. perry-runtime: 213 tests pass. perry-hir: 20 tests
pass. Sum X = 50005000 with no PERRY WARN.

Cumulative across the 5 GC commits 5343f7c8 → this: 1340 → 970 ms
(3.46x → 2.48x of bun, -370 ms / -28 %).

perf(codegen): #140 follow-up — drop index_used_locals gate on i32 shadow

The v0.5.164 fix kept pure accumulators off the i32 shadow path by gating
`needs_i32_slot` on `index_used_locals.contains(id)`, but the same commit
also refined `body_needs_asm_barrier` so the SIMD-blocking
`asm sideeffect` no longer fires for accumulator loops. The
barrier-refinement alone is what restored the SIMD reduction
(re-verified on `loop_overhead` 12 ms, `math_intensive` 14 ms,

The remaining `index_used_locals` gate, on the other hand, removes the
i32 shadow from integer locals that flow into indices only transitively
through Let inits (`let xx = clamp(...); let idx = (row + xx) * 3;
src[idx]` — `xx`, `row`, `y`, `x` all qualify as int-stable but never
appear directly in an `index:` field). Without their i32 shadow, every
inner-loop access falls back to the f64 slot and pays an `fcvtzs` per
read.
