identified `83f05fff` as the first bad commit at 2450 ms vs. v0.5.163's

back to within ~10% of the v0.5.81 honest_bench era baseline).

plus the `module_globals`/`boxed_vars` exclusions already keep the right

perf(codegen): inline Buffer/Uint8Array .length via buffer_data_slots

The v0.5.83 `is_array || is_string` GC-type-byte gate on the inline
`.length` PropertyGet path correctly routes Buffer/Uint8Array through
`js_value_length_f64` (no GC header to read), but in tight inner loops
like image_conv's FNV-1a hash —

    for (let i = 0; i < dst.length; i++)

— that becomes a function call per iteration over 24M bytes, defeating
both LICM (the call has unknown side-effects) and the LoopVectorizer.

When the receiver is a `LocalGet` with a pre-computed `buffer_data_slot`
entry (set by `Stmt::Let` for non-escaping `const x = Buffer.alloc(N)` /
`new Uint8Array(N)`), emit the same inline shape `Expr::Uint8ArrayGet`
already uses for indexed reads:

    let dp  = load PTR from slot
    let hp  = gep i8 dp, -8       (BufferHeader.length sits just before data)
    let l32 = load_invariant I32 hp
    sitofp i32 -> double

`!invariant.load` lets LICM hoist the read out of the surrounding loop;
the function call drops away. Placed BEFORE the generic `is_array_expr ||
is_string_expr || Named/Tuple` arm so the buffer_data_slot path wins
without disturbing the existing GC-type guard.

Measured (image_convolution, 5-run median):
- before this commit: 670 ms
- after:              540 ms (-130 ms, -19%)

ECS smoke tests still match Bun byte-for-byte (query-perf 500 entities,
sync-hotpath 4000, perf-comprehensive 10k+migration). Suite benchmarks
loop_overhead 12 ms, math_intensive 15 ms, nested_loops 18 ms,
array_write 10 ms, array_read 18 ms — all within noise of pre-fix.

perf(codegen): #50 follow-up — skip init eval for flat-const row aliases

`let krow = KERNEL[ky+2]` for a flat-const 2D `KERNEL` registers
`krow_id → (KERNEL_id, ky+2)` in `array_row_aliases` (stmt.rs:140-154)
so subsequent `krow[kx+2]` reads lower through `try_lower_flat_const_index_get`
into a direct GEP on the `[N x i32]` global. But the let-site itself
still went through `lower_expr(init_expr)` to populate `krow`'s
double slot — emitting the generic Array IndexGet with the v0.5.357
lazy/forwarded cond_br guard:

    arr.lazy.54: %r = call double @js_array_get_f64(...)
    arr.fast.55: %r = (bounds-checked inline load)
    arr.merge.56: phi ...

That `js_array_get_f64` call has unknown side-effects, blocking LICM
and the LoopVectorizer on the surrounding y/x loop nest in
image_convolution. Even though every actual read of `krow` skips the
slot value entirely (the alias detection runs first), the dead init
expression's call survived DCE.

When this Let registered as a row alias, store TAG_UNDEFINED in the
slot directly and skip the init evaluation. The slot is now provably
dead — DCE removes the store; the `js_array_get_f64` call is never
emitted. Pathological non-alias reads (`console.log(krow)`) still
return `undefined` instead of leaving the slot uninitialized.

The explicit cleanup blocks downstream of `lower_expr` (shadow-stack
mirror, i32-counter mirror, buffer_data_slot for `BufferAlloc`) all
key off the init expression's shape and don't apply to row-alias lets,
so the `else if` branch covers them as before.

Measured (5-run median):
- image_conv:    540 ms (-0 ms — LLVM was DCE-ing the dead path
                 already; clean IR matters mainly for downstream
                 optimization passes that aren't gated on the call)
- array_write:    5 ms (was 10 ms)
- array_read:    14 ms (was 18 ms)
- loop_overhead, math_intensive, nested_loops: unchanged

perf-comprehensive 10k+migration). Dropped the `js_array_get_f64`
call site from image_conv's IR (verified via PERRY_LLVM_KEEP_IR=1).

perf(json): cap lazy-parse auto-mode at 16 MB

Lazy parse is a win on workloads that touch only a subset of a parsed
top-level array — the tape build cost is one-shot O(n), but each unread
element saves a full subtree materialization. For workloads that
iterate the whole array — the canonical "filter every record, stringify
the result" shape (`benchmarks/honest_bench/workloads/1_json_pipeline`,
server log dumps, ETL) — lazy is strictly slower than direct: tape walk
+ sparse-cache management on every access plus a forced materialize at
the end is more work than the direct parser's single tree build. The
existing cumulative-walk-steps trigger in `lazy_get` only catches
*random* access (~n/2 steps per call after ~4 calls trips the 2× cap);
sequential access contributes 1 step per call and never trips.

Add an upper bound on the auto-mode size window: lazy fires above 1 KB
(small parses don't pay the tape build) and below 16 MB. Above 16 MB,
empirical workload shape skews heavily toward iterate-all, and the
direct parser's tree-build is faster end-to-end than tape + materialize.

Tuned against `honest_bench`:

  - small fixture (21 KB → still lazy):    7-10 ms (matches pre-fix)
  - full fixture (108 MB → now direct):    3.3 s (was 8.0 s, -59%)

Both produce hash b7e8a588, the original v0.5.81 baseline output.

Escape hatches unchanged: `PERRY_JSON_TAPE=1` forces lazy regardless
of size, `=0` forces direct as a correctness fallback.

ECS smoke tests still match Bun (query-perf 500, perf-comprehensive
10k+migration 4000+0). The remaining 1.7 s gap to v0.5.81 baseline
on the full fixture is from accumulated runtime/GC regressions
unrelated to the lazy-parse heuristic and needs separate investigation.

perf(codegen): skip shadow-frame push/pop when slot_count == 0

Phase A sub-phase 3a wires `enable_shadow_frame(slot_count)` into every
user function, with `slot_count` derived from
`collect_pointer_typed_locals(params, body)`. Leaf math helpers
(clampIdx, clampU8, imul32, …) all return 0 — they have no
pointer-typed locals — but the original code still emitted a
`js_shadow_frame_push(0)` + matching `js_shadow_frame_pop(handle)`
pair. The frame would carry only a (prev_top, slot_count=0) header
with no GC roots, so the calls are pure overhead: TLS access + Vec
push + counter bump on entry, mirror on every ret.

When a slot_count=0 function is `alwaysinline` (Perry's small-leaf
heuristic, ≤ 8 statements — exactly the shape of clamp helpers), the
push/pop pair gets duplicated into every caller's hot loop. Visible
in image_convolution's optimized IR:

  for.body.42:
    %r2.i53 = tail call i64 @js_shadow_frame_push(i32 0)
    %r5.i54 = icmp slt i32 %r826.4, -272
    br i1 %r5.i54, label %if.then.1.i63, label %if.merge.3.i55
  if.then.1.i63:
    tail call void @js_shadow_frame_pop(i64 %r2.i53)
    ...

…inside the per-pixel kx/ky double loop, executed ~622M times for a
3840×2160 5×5 blur. Each call hits the SHADOW thread-local Cell.

Skip emission when `slot_count == 0`: no shadow_frame_slot →
to_ir()'s ret-rewriting pass also skips emitting the matching pop, so
the frame is fully elided. Functions that DO have pointer-typed
locals (params/lets that are NaN-boxed pointers — closures, parsed
JSON, fetch results) keep the push/pop pair as before, with their
real GC roots still tracked.

Measured (5-run median, image_convolution warmed):
  - before this commit: 540 ms
  - after:              430 ms (-110 ms, -20%)

Other benches unchanged (loop_overhead 12 ms, math_intensive 14 ms,
nested_loops 18 ms, fibonacci 312-318 ms, mandelbrot 22-23 ms,
function_calls 10 ms, array_read 16-17 ms, array_write 7-9 ms);
ECS query-perf 500, sync-hotpath 4000, perf-comprehensive 10k+migration
all still match Bun.

perf(codegen): teach stmt_preserves_array_length about Buffer reads/writes

`for (let i = 0; i < dst.length; i++) dst[i]` is the canonical Buffer
hot loop — image_convolution's FNV-1a checksum runs it across 24 M
bytes. `lower_for`'s `classify_for_length_hoist` peephole hoists
`dst.length` into a stack slot and switches the loop counter to an
i32 slot when it fires; without it, the cond block emits
`fcmp olt double %i.dbl, %len.dbl` on every iteration.

The peephole walks the loop body via `stmt_preserves_array_length`
to verify the array's length is invariant. The walker enumerates
HIR variants explicitly and falls through to a conservative
`_ => false` for anything unhandled. `Expr::Uint8ArrayGet`,
`Expr::Uint8ArraySet`, `Expr::BufferIndexGet`, and
`Expr::BufferIndexSet` weren't in the enumeration, so any body that
read or wrote a Buffer rejected the peephole — even when the body
provably doesn't touch the bounded array's length (Buffer.alloc is
fixed-capacity and the GEP fast path doesn't extend it).

Add the four Buffer/Uint8Array variants as `walk(array) && walk(index)
[ && walk(value)]`. The bounded-index pair gets registered, the i32
counter gets allocated, and the cond block emits `icmp slt i32`.

Verified on a minimal 24 M-byte Buffer scan:
- before: `fcmp olt double` per iter, ~30 ms walk
- after: `icmp slt i32` per iter, ~10 ms walk

Image_conv 5-run median: 540 ms → 460 ms (-80 ms, -15%). ECS smoke
tests still match Bun (query-perf 500, perf-comprehensive 10k).

perf(codegen): teach stmt_preserves_array_length about FuncRef + Math.* intrinsics

Follow-up to cf540b92 — image_convolution's FNV-1a checksum body ALSO
uses `Math.imul(h, 0x01000193)` which lowers to `Expr::MathImul`, not
`Expr::Call { callee: FuncRef }`. Both shapes were rejected by the
default `_ => false` arm, blocking `lower_for`'s
`classify_for_length_hoist` peephole on the
`for (let i = 0; i < dst.length; i++)` checksum loop.

Add explicit arms for:

  - `Expr::FuncRef(_)`        — bare function reference, no side effect
  - `Expr::MathImul(a, b)`    — Math.imul (32-bit integer multiply)
  - `Expr::MathPow(a, b)`     — Math.pow
  - `Expr::MathMin(elems)`    — Math.min(...values)
  - `Expr::MathMax(elems)`    — Math.max(...values)
  - `Expr::Math{Abs,Sqrt,Floor,Ceil,Round}(a)` — pure unary math

All recurse via `walk()` to verify the bounded array isn't passed as
an operand. The `Call { callee, args }` arm already conservatively
rejects when an arg is `LocalGet(arr_id)`, so calling a user function
that mutates the array via a closure capture is still caught — these
new arms only widen coverage to inert numeric intrinsics.

Verified on image_conv FNV-1a: pre-opt cond block now emits
`icmp slt i32` instead of `fcmp olt double`. ECS smoke tests still
match Bun. Image_conv 5-run median: 460 ms → 450 ms (small additional
gain on top of cf540b92; the FNV pass was already short relative to
the convolution kernel).

perf(codegen): inline ArrayPush fast path for local-bound arrays

The runtime's `js_array_push_f64` does `clean_arr_ptr_mut` (heap-range
check + forwarding chain walk + length/capacity sanity check + lazy
detect) before every store. For an array bound to a plain heap
pointer in a local slot — the canonical `out.push(...)` shape over a
local variable — that's 5–7 dependent memory loads of pure overhead
on every push, which in JSON-pipeline-style workloads runs in the
millions.

Add an inline shape that mirrors `lower_index_set_fast`:

    if (gc_flags & FORWARDED): call js_array_push_f64 (slow)
    else:
      length   = load i32, arr+0
      capacity = load i32, arr+4
      if (length < capacity):
        store double value, arr+8+length*8
        store i32 (length+1), arr+0
        done
      else:
        call js_array_push_f64 (grow path)

Gates on the array being non-boxed, non-captured-by-closure, and
present as a local alloca slot — the closure/box paths still need
their dedicated write-back machinery for the realloc case, and
those run cold relative to the local-array hot loop. The fast
inbounds branch needs no slot write-back since the array pointer
doesn't change unless we grow; the FORWARDED and realloc branches
both call the runtime and write the new head back to the slot via
the existing fall-through logic.

perf(gc): bump bytes trigger after gc-suppressed parse, not just malloc count

\`gc_bump_malloc_trigger\` is called after JSON.parse / JSON.parse-typed
finishes its gc_suppressed window — it raised the malloc-count trigger
to (current_objects + step) so the next allocation didn't immediately
trip GC on the freshly created parse output. But it left the
arena-bytes trigger at its initial 128 MB threshold.

For the honest_bench json_pipeline full fixture (108 MB / 500k records),
the parse output itself lifts arena_total to ~108 MB. The iterate+
rebuild pass that follows allocates a ~70 MB result array + per-record
literals. Bytes-trigger crosses 128 MB after only ~20 MB of new
allocations, fires GC, and each cycle walks the entire 400 MB live
heap (records + intermediates + result) for a marking pass. \`PERRY_GC_DIAG=1\`
showed 4 such cycles dominating the workload at ~800 ms cumulative.

Add a sibling bytes-trigger bump that mirrors the malloc-count rebase:
trigger = arena_total_bytes + GC_STEP_BYTES (initial 128 MB, doubles up
to 1 GB on mostly-garbage sweep evidence). Only raise — never lower —
so we can't accidentally trip a pending collection that the existing
trigger had already armed.

Effect: the post-parse working set itself now has to grow by another
\`step\` before the first GC fires. For json_pipeline_full, iterate+
rebuild completes inside one GC cycle instead of four.

perf(codegen): forward-closure pass on integer_locals (-22% on image_conv)

\`collect_integer_locals\` seeds candidates from a few syntactic
patterns — Integer literals, \`(expr) | 0\`, clamp-call returns,
non-mutable bitwise — then iterates a disqualifier pass that removes
candidates whose write-set turns out to contain a non-int value.
But it never *adds* to the seed set after the initial pass.

That misses transitive int-stable Lets. The image_convolution
clamp-pattern shows the cost cleanly:

    const W = 3840;                  // seeded (Integer literal)
    const hi = W - 1;                // NOT seeded (Sub isn't a seed
                                     // pattern, even though it is
                                     // is_int32_producing_expr against
                                     // current candidates)
    let xx: number = undefined;       // seeded (this commit's earlier
                                     // Undefined arm)
    do {
      ...
      LocalSet(xx, LocalGet(hi))    // disqualifier looks up hi:
                                     // not in candidates → marks
                                     // this as a non-int write →
                                     // removes xx from candidates
    } while (false);

With xx out of integer_locals, every downstream use of \`xx\` (notably
\`idx = (row + xx) * 3\`) computes in DOUBLE: the inner kernel's
address generation does \`fadd → fmul → fptosi i32\` per kx
iteration instead of \`add i32\` chains. 622 M kernel iters × the
extra fp roundtrip costs ~100 ms.

Add a forward closure pass that runs *between* seeding and
disqualification: walk every \`Stmt::Let { id, init: Some(e), .. }\`,
and if \`is_int32_producing_expr(e, current_candidates, ...)\` returns
true, add \`id\` to the candidate set. Iterate to a fixed point. This
lifts \`hi = W - 1\` once \`W\` is in the set, then any Let whose init
reduces to is_int32_producing_expr over \`hi\` lands on the next
pass, and so on.

Disqualification still runs after, so a candidate that picks up a
non-int write later still gets dropped — the closure pass only
*adds*, never overrides the safety net.

perf(codegen): i32 init path + immutable i32-shadow on Let (image_conv -41 ms)

Two related changes that finish the int-arithmetic story for Let
initialization:

1. **i32 init path** at \`Stmt::Let\`. The original code always
   went through \`lower_expr → store double → fptosi to seed i32\`.
   Even when the local has an i32 shadow slot AND the init is
   \`is_int32_producing_expr\`, computation happened in DOUBLE
   first. Now: if the local has an i32 slot AND
   \`can_lower_expr_as_i32\` says yes, compute via
   \`lower_expr_as_i32\` directly, store the i32 to the shadow,
   sitofp once to seed the double slot. \`fadd → fmul → fptosi\`
   chain becomes \`add → mul → sitofp\`.

2. **Drop the \`*mutable\` gate on \`needs_i32_slot\`.** The
   v0.5.164 comment cited \`const SEED = 0x9E3779B9 >>> 0\` as a
   reason to skip immutable lets — but \`>>> 0\` is intentionally
   not seeded into integer_locals (collect_integer_let_ids
   excludes it precisely to avoid the u32→i32 saturation
   round-trip), so SEED never enters this code path. Integer-stable
   immutable lets that DO get seeded (Integer literal / clamp call /
   Add/Sub/Mul over int candidates after the forward-closure pass)
   can't legitimately overflow i32 in any reachable workload.

   image_convolution's \`const row = yy * W;\` is the canonical
   case: yy is the clampIdx-result (now in integer_locals via
   the earlier Undefined-init seed), W is \`const W = 3840\`
   (Integer-literal seed). Both reachable as i32. Without an
   i32 slot on row, every \`(row + xx) * 3\` in the inner kx
   body had to round-trip through fptosi(double) → multiply.
   With the slot, row computes and reads in i32 throughout.

\`row + xx\` is \`add i32\`, \`(row + xx) * 3\` is \`mul i32\`, and
the byte loads from the buffer use the i32 directly. The DOUBLE

fix(codegen): exclude `>>> 0` from i32-shadow + channel-vector SIMD reduction

Two changes — the fix is load-bearing for correctness; the SIMD reduction
is the perf intent of this iteration.

## Correctness fix: u32 results don't fit signed i32 slots

The 4f895dd8 commit (i32 init path + drop \`*mutable\` gate) silently
broke FNV-1a-class checksum output:

  - image_conv:        \`checksum=-2886948b\` (should be \`2ba2e053\`)
  - json_pipeline_full: \`hash=-48175a78\`     (should be \`b7e8a588\`)

Two seed paths needed the same JS-spec exclusion that the original
\`(expr) | 0\` mutable arm already had:

1. **\`collect_integer_let_ids\`'s immutable-bitwise seed** —
   \`(!mutable && is_bitwise_expr(init))\` accepts UShr-by-0, so
   \`const hash = h >>> 0\` lands in \`integer_locals\`. Pre-4f895dd8
   that was harmless because \`needs_i32_slot\` required \`*mutable\`,
   so const lets never got an i32 shadow. After 4f895dd8 they do —
   the slot stores the i32 value, sign-extends the high bit, and
   \`hash.toString(16)\` prints the negative form.

   Fix: gate the immutable-bitwise seed on \`!is_ushr_zero(init)\`.

2. **\`returns_int_expr\`** (drives \`returns_int_functions\` →
   \`clamp_fn_ids\` → \`is_int32_producing_expr\`'s Call arm) accepted
   any bitwise op including UShr. Functions that end in
   \`return h >>> 0\` (FNV-1a, CRC, Murmur, …) were marked as
   int-producing, so \`const hash = fnv1a32(s)\` flowed through the
   forward-closure pass into \`integer_locals\`, then onto an i32
   slot. Same sign-extension corruption.

   Fix: drop UShr from \`returns_int_expr\`'s op set. Other bitwise
   ops (\`&\`, \`|\`, \`^\`, \`<<\`, \`>>\`) all produce signed i32 per
   JS spec — safe to round-trip.

Verified: \`checksum=2ba2e053\` and \`hash=b7e8a588\` match Bun + Node
byte-for-byte after the fix. Tested on every honest_bench workload
plus ECS smoke tests (query-perf, sync-hotpath, perf-comprehensive
all match Bun).

## Channel-vector SIMD reduction

Pattern detector + emitter for the canonical 3-channel image-kernel
shape:

    rAcc += src[idx + 0] * k;
    gAcc += src[idx + 1] * k;
    bAcc += src[idx + 2] * k;

\`try_match_channel_reduction\` walks 3 (or 4) consecutive
\`Stmt::Expr(LocalSet)\` and verifies:

  - All targets are distinct, integer-stable accumulators
  - Each value is \`Add(LocalGet(target), Mul(Uint8ArrayGet, k))\`
  - Same array, same factor, consecutive integer offsets
  - Array has a \`buffer_data_slot\` (pre-computed data ptr)

\`lower_channel_reduction\` emits a \`<4 x i32>\` SIMD multiply-add:

    %bytes = <load 3 bytes via gep + assume + zext>
    %k_splat = shufflevector <insertelement, k>, zeroinitializer
    %mul = mul <4 x i32> %bytes, %k_splat
    %acc_vec = <load 3 i32 accs into vector>
    %new = add <4 x i32> %acc_vec, %mul
    <extractelement and store back to per-channel i32 + double slots>

The detector is narrow enough (consecutive offsets, identical array
and factor, distinct integer-stable targets, buffer_data_slot
required) that it only fires on real image/audio/numeric kernels —
no regressions on JSON pipeline, ECS, or suite benchmarks.

Wired into \`lower_stmts\` via a peek-ahead loop instead of a
straight per-statement walk so we can consume N statements at once
when the pattern matches.

Measured (5-run median, image_conv warmed):
  - before fix (correctness broken): 345 ms with wrong checksum
  - after fix, no SIMD:                410 ms with correct checksum
  - after fix, with channel SIMD:      400 ms with correct checksum

The SIMD save is modest (10 ms) because LLVM SLP was already doing
some of this implicitly; the explicit form gives more control and
will benefit other multi-channel kernels (audio resampling, color
ops, NEON-friendly reductions) without depending on the cost model.

perf(transform): static-trip-count for-loop full-unroll + smart channel-SIMD gate

image_convolution closes 80-90 ms of the gap to Zig — 400 ms → 310-330 ms
median (22% improvement). Two changes that compound:

1. New `perry-transform::unroll::unroll_static_loops` pass detects
   `for (let i = LO; i {<,<=} HI; i++)` where LO and HI are integer
   literals and trip count ≤ 8, replaces the loop with N copies of the
   body and substitutes every `LocalGet(i)` with `Integer(LO + n)` per
   iteration. Wired into `collect_modules.rs` after the inliner so any
   inlined function bodies' loops also get unrolled.

   Image_convolution's 5×5 blur kernel (`for ky in -2..2 { for kx in
   -2..2 { … KERNEL[ky+2][kx+2] … } }`) becomes 25 inlined chunks per
   pixel. The `KERNEL[N][M]` access then constant-folds via Perry's
   existing flat-const-array machinery to integer literals (1, 4, 7,
   16, 26, 41).

   Safety guards: bodies with `break`/`continue` AT DEPTH 0 are
   rejected (would target the unrolled loop, no enclosing loop post-
   unroll). Inside an inner `while`/`do-while`/`for`/`switch` —
   including the inliner-emitted `do { … return-rewrite-to-break … }
   while (false)` wrappers around clampIdx/clampU8 — break and
   continue target their inner construct and survive unroll intact;
   depth-tracked. Closures referencing the IV / try blocks / labeled
   stmts / writes to the IV inside the body are all rejected.
   `MAX_TRIP_COUNT = 8` keeps the per-pixel inlined body bounded
   (5×5 = 25 stmts; 7×7 = 49; 8×8 = 64).

2. Companion gate in `perry-codegen/src/stmt.rs::lower_stmts`: when
   the function being lowered carries `was_unrolled = true`, skip the
   manual `<4 x i32>` channel-vector reduction added in 817c4b56.
   Post-unroll the kernel coefficients are compile-time literals;
   forcing `<4 x i32>` per chunk fights LLVM's freedom to (a) replace
   mul-by-1 with no-op, (b) replace mul-by-4/16 with `shl #2`/`shl #4`,
   (c) choose its own vectorization shape across the 25-chunk body.

   Measured: with manual SIMD post-unroll = 350-360 ms; without =
   310-320 ms — a +50 ms savings on image_conv. Pre-unroll the manual
   reduction is still a 10 ms win, so it stays as the default
   fallback for non-unrolled functions.

   Plumbing: `was_unrolled: bool` added to `perry_hir::Function` and
   `init_was_unrolled: bool` to `perry_hir::Module` (image_conv puts
   the kernel directly at module init, not inside a function).
   Threaded through every `FnCtx` construction site in `codegen.rs` —
   `compile_function` reads `f.was_unrolled`, `compile_method` reads
   `method.was_unrolled`, `compile_module_entry` reads
   `hir.init_was_unrolled`, `compile_static_method` reads
   `f.was_unrolled`, closures default to `false`.

fix(codegen): #435 — i32-shadow gate skips pure accumulators (v0.5.496)

`is_int32_producing_expr` accepted `Add | Sub | Mul` over int-stable
operands, so any integer accumulator written via these operators
ended up in `integer_locals` and got an i32 shadow whose reads
silently truncated 64-bit sums / products / strided counters to 32
bits. Fix: `collect_index_used_locals` now takes a transitive closure
backward through writes; `needs_i32_slot` requires
`index_used_locals.contains(id)` alongside the existing checks. Pure
accumulators stay on the f64 slot at full 53-bit mantissa precision;
image_convolution's `xx → idx → array[idx]` transitive chain is
preserved.

Closes #435.

fix(codegen): #442 — Windows inline Button bg color (v0.5.497)

`extern "C" fn(handle: i64, …)` (void return). The dispatch-table
path used by the explicit setter `widgetSetBackgroundColor(...)`
correctly went through `UiReturnKind::Void → call_void`, emitting

the inline `Button(label, onPress, { backgroundColor })` form
emitted `%rN = call double @perry_ui_widget_set_background_color(...)`
— a function-type mismatch the LLVM verifier silently accepts but
produces inconsistent IR.

Fix: import VOID from crate::types; flip every styling FFI
declaration from DOUBLE to VOID and every block().call(DOUBLE, …)
to block().call_void(…). Covers all 13 callsites: borderRadius /
opacity / borderWidth / tooltip / hidden / enabled / backgroundColor
/ color (text) / borderColor / padding / shadow / textDecoration /
gradient.

Verified: post-fix IR for both forms emits `call void
@perry_ui_widget_set_background_color(...)` consistent with

28/28 pass. New regression test test-files/test_issue_442_inline_button_bg.ts
(skip-listed in compile-smoke since UI tests need a windowing

perf(codegen): #436 close image_convolution gap — strict-i32-bounded gate + clamp inlining

#436 documented a 5%-target gap on image_convolution (377 ms baseline →
≤281 ms target). While investigating I discovered v0.5.496's #435 fix
silently regressed image_convolution from ~320 ms to ~440 ms — the new
`index_used_locals` gate at the Let-site i32-shadow allocation
correctly excludes pure accumulators (`sum += compute(i)`, the #435
overflow shape) but also excludes image_convolution's `rAcc / gAcc /
bAcc / k` accumulators which are bounded by the unrolled 5×5 kernel
and the FNV-1a `h` accumulator which is bounded by the explicit
`(h ^ dst[i]) | 0` and `imul32(h, K)` write coercions. The maintainer's
v0.5.496 commit (837d73aa) included the `Uint8ArraySet.value` /
`BufferIndexSet.value` seed extension that recovers most of the
regression by routing rAcc/gAcc/bAcc/k back through index_used_locals
via the typed-array store value subtree, but the FNV-1a `h` (read by
console.log, not stored to a typed array) was still left on f64.

Two changes in this commit close out #436's plan:

(1) `perry-codegen/src/collectors.rs`: new
`is_strictly_i32_bounded_expr` rejects the dangerous
`Add | Sub | Mul`-of-int-stable arm that motivated #435, but accepts
pure bitwise / `expr | 0` / `expr >>> 0` / Buffer-byte loads /
`MathImul` / `Update` / calls to clamp / returns_integer functions.
New `collect_strictly_i32_bounded_locals` walks all writes to each
local (Stmt::Let init, LocalSet, Update) and returns the set where
EVERY write passes the strict check. Image_conv's `h` accumulator
qualifies (writes `(h ^ dst[i]) | 0` is `Binary { BitOr, ...,
Integer(0) }` and `imul32(h, K)` is `Call(returns_int)`); #435's
`sum`, `prod`, `acc`, `i`, `big`, `c` all fail (their writes are
bare `Add | Sub | Mul` of int-stable operands).

(2) `perry-codegen/src/stmt.rs::needs_i32_slot` extended to allow
the i32 fast path when a local is `index_used_locals.contains(id)
|| strictly_i32_bounded_locals.contains(id)`. Threaded through
`FnCtx::strictly_i32_bounded_locals` at all 6 codegen entry points
(compile_function, compile_init main + harvest, compile_method,
compile_closure, compile_static_field).

#436 plan #1 (clamp inlining) also implemented in
`perry-transform/src/inline.rs::is_inlinable` — `is_clamp3` and
`is_clamp_u8` short-circuit the inliner so the `Expr::Call {
callee: FuncRef(clamp_fn_id) }` shape survives at every call site.
Codegen's existing i32-context `lower_expr_as_i32` arm and a new
f64-context arm in `lower_call.rs` emit inline `@llvm.smin.i32` /
`@llvm.smax.i32` directly, avoiding the inliner-emitted `do { ... }
while (false)` block with internal `break`-rewritten `return`s. No
measurable perf impact on image_convolution (LLVM collapses both
forms identically to `csel` branchless asm), but produces cleaner
IR (66 inline smin/smax calls replace dowhile blocks at every
call site).

Plans #2 (drop dead double mirrors) and #3 (paired src/dest noalias
scopes) were investigated and shown not applicable on the current
codegen — DSE already eliminates dead double mirror stores in the
hot blur loop (verified: 0 `str d` instructions), and the existing
implementation is already correctly per-buffer-paired (`!alias.scope
!201` for src reads, `!202` for dst writes, with cross-listed
`!noalias !301`/`!302`).

Verified: image_convolution checksum `2ba2e053` (matches Bun
byte-for-byte); json_pipeline_full hash `b7e8a588` unchanged (matches
v0.5.495 baseline); test_issue_435_int32_truncation.ts still matches
Node byte-for-byte across all 9 bug shapes + control; perry-codegen
unit tests 28/28 pass; perry-transform unit tests 14/14 pass; 15-run
image_conv timing stable at 0.31-0.32 s median (recovers v0.5.495
baseline from the v0.5.496 regression).

The remaining ~30-40 ms gap from current 320 ms to #436's 281 ms
target is from LLVM auto-vectorization not firing on the outer y/x
loops — verified empirically (literal H/W vs `const H = 2160` give
identical timing, so const-prop is not the bottleneck) and via
`-Rpass-missed=loop-vectorize` remarks ("could not determine number
of loop iterations" + "value used outside the loop"). Closing this
remaining gap is a structurally larger LLVM-level optimization
beyond #436's stated plans #1/#2/#3.

fix(codegen): #431 — cross-module class-name collision emitted method bodies under the wrong module prefix (v0.5.499)

When two TypeScript modules each declared a class with the same name
(e.g. `DroppingStrategy` in `internal/queue.ts` and `internal/pubsub.ts`,
or Effect's `Class` / `Refinement` / `Composite` / `ParseError` /
`PropertySignatureTransformation` reused across 8 modules), perry's
codegen mangled the consumer module's method bodies under the
*defining* module's prefix while its own dispatch table still expected
the consumer's prefix — clang rejected the IR with `error: use of
undefined value '@perry_method_<consumer>_ts__<C>__<m>'`.

Cross-module sibling of #336 (intra-module collision, fixed in v0.5.405
via the `_<n>` discriminator on `@perry_class_keys_*`); #336
disambiguated the keys-array global, but the method-body symbol prefix
is keyed off `imported_class_prefix` which had no shadowing-by-local-
class guard.

Root cause in `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs::compile_module`:
the `imported_class_prefix: HashMap<name → source_module_prefix>` map
(consulted at line 1106 by the `method_names` registry that
`compile_method` looks up to choose its LLVM symbol name) was
populated for *every* `opts.imported_classes` entry without checking
whether `hir.classes` already had a same-named local class. The
downstream `class_table.entry(stub.name).or_insert(stub)` loop
correctly preserved the local class entry, so the receiver of
`imported_class_prefix.get(&c.name)` ended up being a local class but
the value handed back was the imported module's prefix —
`compile_method` then emitted local-class methods as
`@perry_method_<imported_module>__<C>__<m>` while the dispatch-table
builder at line 3614 (which keys off `module_prefix`, not
`imported_class_prefix`) still referenced them as
`@perry_method_<local>__<C>__<m>`.

Fix in one place (`codegen.rs:569`): skip imports that collide by name
with a local class when populating `imported_class_prefix`
(`if hir.classes.iter().any(|c| c.name == *effective_name) { continue;
}`).

`test-files/test_issue_431_cross_module_class_collision.ts` + 1-file
fixture under `test-files/fixtures/issue_431_pkg/b.ts` exercises the
issue's exact 2-file shape: both files declare
`class DroppingStrategy<A>` with intentionally inverted semantics (A's
`handleSurplus` returns `length === 0`, B's returns `length > 0`) so
the output proves each module's call sites resolve to ITS OWN class
body — `a.handleSurplus: false / a.surplusSize: 0 /
b.handleSurplus: true / b.surplusSize: 1` matches
`node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte.

Verified: cargo build clean; `cargo test -p perry-codegen --lib` 28/28
pass; the issue's literal arrow-fn-export repro flips from
`clang -c failed: use of undefined value '@perry_method_a_ts__DroppingStrategy__handleSurplus'`
(compile abort) to clean compile + link; post-fix IR emits

(correct local prefix) where pre-fix had
`@perry_method_b_ts__DroppingStrategy__surplusSize`. With #431 closed,

fix(stdlib): closes #422 — net.Socket connect/error events + factory variant (v0.5.501)

Three layered gaps in the `net` module surface together blocked any
pure-TS TCP client (Postgres / MySQL / MQTT / custom binary protocols)
from working end-to-end:

(1) `new net.Socket()` was a Member-callee `new` expression that landed
    in `lower_new`'s Non-identifier callee arm and lowered to
    `Expr::NewDynamic`, whose codegen fallback returns an empty
    ObjectHeader placeholder. Subsequent `sock.connect/.on/.write` all
    silently no-op'd; TCP socket was never opened, no events fired.

(2) `sock.connect(port, host)` had no dispatch entry — only the eager
    `net.createConnection(port, host)` factory was wired. The deferred-
    connect shape (canonical for pure-TS drivers — listener registration
    sits between alloc and connect) needs a separate FFI.

(3) `net.connect(port, host)` (spec'd alias for createConnection) fell
    through to the unknown-method path returning TAG_UNDEFINED, so
    `typeof net.connect(...)` evaluated to "undefined".

Fix in 5 places:
- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/net/mod.rs`: add `pending_rx` field to
  SocketState; new `js_net_socket_alloc()` (constructor allocator) and
  `js_net_socket_method_connect(handle, port, host_ptr)` (deferred
  connect, takes rx out and spawns the same tokio task body as
  `spawn_socket_task`).
- `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs::NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE`: 3 new
  rows — `("net","Socket")` → `js_net_socket_alloc`, `("net","connect")`
  factory alias, `("net",receiver:Socket,"connect")` instance method.
- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_new.rs`: recognize `new net.Socket()`
  (Member callee) at the top of `lower_new`, reroute to
  `Expr::NativeMethodCall { module: "net", method: "Socket", ... }`.
- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs`: extend Stmt::Let native-instance
  registration with `("net","Socket") => Some("Socket")`.
- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/common/dispatch.rs::dispatch_net_socket`:
  add `connect` arm for the dynamic-handle path.

New regression test `test-files/test_issue_422_socket_connect.ts`
exercises both reproducer shapes (`new net.Socket()` + `.connect(1, ...)`
to force ECONNREFUSED, plus `net.connect(1, ...)` typeof check) and
matches `node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte.

fix(hir): closes #444 — import.meta.main / .url / .dirname / .filename (v0.5.502)

`import.meta.url` returned `0` and `import.meta.main` returned `NaN`
because `lower_meta_prop` lowered bare `import.meta` to an
`Expr::Object(...)` literal at module top level, which trips the
long-standing module-globals NaN-boxing bug where string fields read
back as 0. The user-visible symptom: `if (import.meta.main) main()`
never fired and `new URL("./x", import.meta.url)` got nonsense.

Fix folds `import.meta.<prop>` directly to a string/bool literal at
the Member-expression lowering site, bypassing the broken Object path
entirely. Surface aligned with Node 20+ spec — `url`, `main`,
`dirname`, `filename`. Bun-only aliases (`dir` / `path` / `file`)
intentionally omitted to keep Perry → Node migration silent.

Code changes already landed in 95da3b2c (rolled into the v0.5.501
commit alongside #422 + #431 work). This commit ships the v0.5.502
version bump + the missing CLAUDE.md changelog entry for #444.

fix(codegen,hir): closes #446 — bind class-method PropertyGet + flow type-only-import class metadata (v0.5.503)

`obj.method` PropertyGet on a class instance returned `undefined` for any
method reference — `typeof obj.method === "undefined"`, `let f = obj.method`
non-callable, `arr.map(obj.method)` silently dropped its mapper. The
1f0bbfc3 followup (v0.5.476) had restored the *call* path through
CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY so `obj.method(args)` worked, but read-as-value still
fell through `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::PropertyGet` to the generic
`js_object_get_field_by_name_f64` lookup — which only sees own-fields.
Class methods live in the prototype vtable, not the object's field bag, so
every method-as-value reference returned undefined regardless of how the
class was imported.

Compounded for `import type { Foo }`: `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs::
lower_module_decl` early-returned on `import_decl.type_only` before any
specifier flowed class metadata into `imported_classes`. The runtime
CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY fallback (#392 followup) saved the call path, but
the new method-binding path needs `ctx.methods` populated at codegen time —
which the early-return blocked. @codehz/ecs's `world.set` path tripped this
in the wild.

Fix in three places:
1. `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs` — new `js_class_method_bind(
   instance, name_ptr, name_len)` allocates a 3-capture
   `BOUND_METHOD_FUNC_PTR`-sentinel closure (same machinery that backs
   `js_native_module_bind_method`); the closure dispatches through
   `js_native_call_method` → CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY for both local and
   cross-module classes.
2. `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::PropertyGet` — after the field-
   fast-path GEP+load, before the generic property-bag fallback, when
   `(class_name, property)` is in `ctx.methods`, emit `call double
   @js_class_method_bind(recv, ptrtoint(@.str.<N>.bytes), <len>)`. Bytes
   pointer is per-module rodata, stable for the program's lifetime — no
   per-call allocation. Companion declare in `runtime_decls.rs`.
3. `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs::lower_module_decl` — drop unconditional
   early-return on `import_decl.type_only`; only short-circuit for native
   modules (no class info there). For TS modules, fall through and
   propagate `whole_decl_type_only || named.is_type_only` into the existing
   per-specifier `is_native` skip (mirrors the v0.5.405 per-specifier
   `import { type Foo }` fix).

fix(codegen): #447 partial — skip alwaysinline for was_plain_async wrappers (v0.5.506)

Removes the infinite-microtask-loop hang from nested async-await
(test_async.ts pattern: `await asyncFn()` where asyncFn itself awaits).
The async-to-generator pre-pass rewrites such functions into a generator
+ recursive `__step()` closure; when the body is ≤8 statements the
small-leaf-function alwaysinline gate fired and inlined the wrapper into
its caller. Inlining broke GC-root coverage of the step closure's iter
capture, so iter.next() returned NULL_OBJECT_BYTES and the chain looped
forever at 100% CPU.

Adding `&& !f.was_plain_async` to the gate keeps these wrappers in their
own LLVM functions where the shadow-stack push/pop matches what
closure-conversion expected.

Partial fix: removes the hang, but the rewritten body still doesn't
execute correctly — `console.log(x)` inside `run()` doesn't fire and
js_box_get warns about a null pointer, suggesting a deeper closure-
capture bug in the async-to-generator pre-pass. Issue #447 stays open
for follow-up; the 6 skip-listed test_async* tests remain skip-listed.

Workspace tests 646/646 pass with this change; simple async (single-
level) still works.

fix(runtime,codegen): closes #450 — bind `this` to obj for defineProperty getter/setter (v0.5.507)

`Object.defineProperty(obj, k, { get(){}, set(){} })` registered the
accessor (round-trips via `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`) but invoked the
getter/setter with the descriptor literal as `this` instead of `obj` —
`obj.value` returned NaN (`this._backing` resolved against the
descriptor's empty field bag, the multiplication produced NaN).

Fix in two layers:

1. codegen (expr.rs): OR the runtime's `CAPTURES_THIS_FLAG` (0x8000_0000)
   into the closure's cap_count when allocating `captures_this:true`
   closures. Activates the existing-but-dead-code flag at line 49 of
   closure.rs. Without this signal, the runtime can't detect "this
   closure has a reserved this-slot that needs rebinding."

2. runtime (closure.rs + object.rs): new `clone_closure_rebind_this`
   helper that clones an accessor closure and overwrites its reserved
   this-slot with the target object. `js_object_define_property` calls
   it on each get/set descriptor before storing, so the accessor sees
   `obj` as `this` instead of the descriptor literal.

Limitation deliberately out of scope: function-expression-form
descriptors (`get: function() {...}`) still don't bind correctly because
`lower_fn_expr` always sets `captures_this: false`. Method-shorthand
form (the issue's primary repro) is fully fixed.

fix(codegen): closes #448 + #451 — js_object_set_field ABI mismatch (v0.5.508)

`*[Symbol.iterator]()` class generators iterated via for…of hung
allocating until OOM (5+ GB RSS), and `test_gap_json_advanced.ts`
SIGSEGV'd partway through. Independent investigations of both issues
landed on the same root cause: the shape-cache fast path of
`lower_object_literal` declared `js_object_set_field` as
`(I64, I32, DOUBLE)` but the runtime takes `(*mut ObjectHeader, u32,
JSValue)` where `JSValue = #[repr(transparent)] u64`. On AArch64 /
x86_64 SysV / Win64 these use disjoint register classes — clang
puts the value in xmm0/d0 (FP) but the runtime reads from rdx/x2 (GP),
getting whatever stale GP-register contents were sitting there.

For the generator iter object's three closure fields (next/return/throw)
the GP register read 0, so iter.next() dispatched against undefined and
the for-of loop never observed done=true → OOM (#448).

For `JSON.stringify({ raw: 1, toJSON() { return {f:"ok"}; } })` the
toJSON closure pointer also stored as 0; subsequent dereference inside
the JSON walker SIGSEGV'd (#451).

Fix in two files (3 functional lines):
- crates/perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls.rs:1195 — flip the third arg
  from DOUBLE to I64.
- crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::lower_object_literal — bitcast the
  lowered double to i64 before the call so the value rides in the same
  register class the runtime reads.

fix(transform): closes #393 — NativeMethodCall arg closures hidden from FuncId scan (v0.5.514)

`compute_max_func_id` in `crates/perry-transform/src/generator.rs` walked
`Expr::Call` / `Expr::New` args but had no arm for `Expr::NativeMethodCall`,
so closures inside `app.post('/r', async (req, reply) => …)` and
`wss.on('listening', () => …)` (registered as `NativeMethodCall { args:
[String, Closure { func_id, … }] }`) were invisible to the scan. The
async-to-generator pass then started `next_func_id = max_id + 1` below
those existing ids and the synthesized iter step closures collided with
them. At codegen, the alloc site emitted `js_closure_alloc_with_captures_singleton(..., i32 1, …)`
(one slot, matching the user closure's capture count) while the body —
the iter step's body that won the func-id race — read `capture[16]`,
scribbling `js_box_set` over whichever string handle / port number lived
past the end of the allocation. perry-hub had at least three colliding
ids (125, 127, 128); the runtime guard added in #401 caught the bad
pointers but the data was still corrupt.

Fix: add `NativeMethodCall` plus `StaticMethodCall` / `SuperCall` /
`SuperMethodCall` / `CallSpread` / `NewDynamic` arms to both
`scan_expr_for_max_func` and `scan_expr_for_max_local`. perry-hub
(`../hub`, 2239 lines) now starts cleanly with no `[PERRY WARN] js_box_set`
warnings; parity sweep stays at 209 pass / 2 known-fail (#456, #457).

fix(codegen): closes #407 — console.log(...arr) printed only first element (v0.5.515)

The Expr::Call console-dispatch in crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs is
only reached when the HIR has zero spread args. Spread calls produce
Expr::CallSpread which fell through to the generic closure-spread path
(js_closure_call_apply_with_spread) and treated console.log as a closure
value, dropping most arguments.

Add a console.{log,info,warn,error,debug} fast path at the top of the
Expr::CallSpread arm that bundles every regular + spread arg into a single
accumulator array (push for CallArg::Expr, js_array_concat for
CallArg::Spread) and dispatches to the matching js_console_*_spread runtime
fn.

fix(runtime+codegen): closes #434 — SSO strings vs heap strings in Set/Map/object lookup (v0.5.516)

`Set.has` / `Map.get` / `obj[key]` returned false / undefined / 0 when the
lookup key was a ≤5-byte string from `JSON.parse` even though `===` reported
equal. Root cause was a representation mismatch: literals at compile sites
land as heap STRING_TAG (0x7FFF) while JSON.parse emits inline
SHORT_STRING_TAG SSO (0x7FF9, v0.5.216+). The `JSValueKey::hash` /
`jsvalue_eq` content-equality paths in set.rs / map.rs only knew about
heap-pointer tags, so SSO bits hashed by raw u64 and compared as not-equal
to STRING_TAG entries; Map's side-table additionally treated SSO as a
"safe numeric key" and short-circuited the linear-scan fallback for
size > 8 maps. The codegen IndexGet/IndexSet last-resort fallback only
matched top16 == 0x7FFF so SSO keys fell into the numeric branch and
read past the object header.

Fix:
- Add SSO-aware `string_view_from_bits` helper in set.rs / map.rs that
  decodes inline payload bytes for content hashing and equality.
- Exclude SHORT_STRING_TAG from `is_safe_numeric_key` in map.rs so SSO
  keys force the linear-scan path.
- In codegen expr.rs, detect both 0x7FFF and 0x7FF9 in the IndexGet /
  IndexSet last-resort string-key check, and route through
  `unbox_str_handle` (which materializes SSO via
  `js_get_string_pointer_unified`) instead of bare AND POINTER_MASK.

All four reproductions from the issue now match node; parity sweep
stays at 208 pass / 1 known fail / 2 known compile-fails.

fix(ui): closes #443 (followup to v0.5.498) — SSO inline strings still rendered "NaN" through state bindings (v0.5.517)

but it only matched heap `STRING_TAG` (0x7FFF). Since v0.5.216, short
strings (≤5 bytes) are encoded as inline `SHORT_STRING_TAG` (0x7FF9)
SSO values — those still fell through both branches, leaving
`format!("{}", value)` to print "NaN" for any short string-typed

MULTI_TEXT_BINDINGS.

- Widen `is_nanboxed_string` to accept 0x7FFF or 0x7FF9.

fix(transform): closes #456 — unroll pass aliased LocalIds and FuncIds across cloned iterations

The static-trip-count for-loop unroll pass (v0.5.495) cloned the body N times
but reused the same `LocalId` for body-internal declarations across all
copies, and the same `FuncId` for cloned `Expr::Closure`s. At module-init
level, codegen emits one `@perry_global_*__<id>` per referenced `Stmt::Let`,
so five copies of `let captured = i; fns.push(() => captured)` produced five
duplicate global definitions → LLVM "redefinition of global" error.

Even after dedup, every cloned `() => captured` shared one FuncId, so codegen
collapsed all five closures into a single compiled body that read the same
global — `fns[i]()` returned 0 for every i instead of 0..4.

Fix in `crates/perry-transform/src/unroll.rs`:
  * Seed `next_local_id` and `next_func_id` once per module (mirroring the
    helpers in `generator.rs` / `async_to_generator.rs`).
  * After cloning each iteration's body and substituting `LocalGet(iv) →
    Integer(N)`, walk the clone and assign fresh `LocalId`s to every binding
    it declares (`Stmt::Let`, `Closure::params`, `CatchClause::param`) and
    rewrite all in-scope references (`LocalGet`/`LocalSet`/`Update`,
    `Closure::captures`/`mutable_captures`, `Array*::array_id`, `SetAdd`).
  * Bump each cloned `Closure::func_id` so codegen emits one body per
    iteration's closure.

Removed `test_edge_closures` from `test-parity/known_failures.json` and from
the inline `SKIP_TESTS` list in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (the smoke gate
keeps its own skip mechanism separate from the parity gate's known_failures).

fix(transform): closes #457 — skip inlining generator functions (v0.5.521)

The function inliner expands a same-module call by copying the callee's
body into the caller as a `do { ...body... } while (false)` wrapper, with
every `return e` rewritten to `LocalSet(let_id, e); break`. Correct for
ordinary functions but catastrophic for generators: the `yield` exprs
leak into the caller's statement list with no iterator state machine
(which `transform_generators` would have synthesized had the call
survived), and the call site collapses to whatever the generator's
terminating `return value` evaluates to instead of producing a Generator
iterator. So `gen()` no longer returned an iterator — it returned the
bare return value, breaking every downstream `g.next()` / `for…of` /
`yield*` consumer.

Fix in `crates/perry-transform/src/inline.rs::is_inlinable`: bail with
`false` when `func.is_generator` is set. One-line addition alongside the
existing `is_async` / captures / shape bails.

`test_gap_generators.ts` now matches node byte-for-byte across all 27
lines (basicGen, controllableGen with .return/.throw, yield* delegation,
range generator, infinite take(N), Symbol.iterator class, generators-of-
generators, recursive flatten). Removed the entry that v0.5.510 had added
to `test-parity/known_failures.json` — file is now `{}` again.

fix(cli): closes #467 — sanitize scoped package.json names before they hit the linker (v0.5.522)

`perry run` / `perry compile` derive the output filename from the
project name. When `package.json` carries an npm-scoped name like
`@foo/bar`, ld64 expanded the leading `@` as a response-file directive
(`ld: open() failed for '@foo/bar'`), failing the link.

`read_app_metadata` now passes the name through `sanitize_app_name`,
which strips a leading `@` and flattens `/` to `-` (`@foo/bar` →
`foo-bar`), making the result safe both as an output path and as a
default bundle-ID component.

fix(codegen+hir): closes #460 — `export { local as keyword }` re-exports of TS contextual keywords now emit definitions (v0.5.523)

Function-decl renames (`function _void(){}; export { _void as void }`)
left `_perry_fn_<mod>__void` link-undefined because codegen mangled
`f.name` only. Const-binding renames (`const _await = core.deferredAwait;
export { _await as await }`) never reached `exported_functions` and
`is_exportable` excluded the function-reference initializer shapes, so
no symbol was emitted at all.

Fix: emit a forwarding wrapper after the user-function loop for every
`(exported, func_id)` where exported ≠ f.name; widen `is_exportable` in
lower.rs to cover `LocalGet`/`FuncRef`/`ExternFuncRef`/`PropertyGet` and
also pin the local name into `exported_objects` so the global-emission
gate fires; emit a duplicate value-getter under each renamed exported
name; suppress the value-getter when the name is already a function
alias (avoids clang `invalid redefinition` collision).

Closes Effect's 14 keyword-name link errors (`void`/`async`/`await`/
`try`/`delete`/`continue`); the remaining 3 (`Order`/`Union`/`Emit`)
are class-as-function symbols carved out by #460 as a separate
follow-up. Parity sweep stays at 209 pass / 2 known fails.

feat(runtime+cli): closes #464 — stub registry + first-call runtime diagnostic for no-op stubs (v0.5.524)

auto-generated stub (and the runtime-only `js_ws_*` / `js_readline_*`

(tracking: <issue>)` once per symbol per process. `PERRY_STUB_DIAG`
env var: `off|silent|0|false` silences, `verbose|all|every` prints
every call, default = first call only.

`perry-runtime/build.rs` walks `perry-dispatch`'s four tables + the
hand-listed `direct_call_stubs` and emits a `STUB_MANIFEST: &[StubEntry]`
constant alongside the stub function bodies. Manifest is always
populated (independent of `ohos-napi`) because `perry check` runs on

`perry check --target harmonyos` (also `harmonyos-simulator`) walks

fix(codegen): refs #461 — emit fallback `perry_fn_<mod>__<exported>` undefined-stub for class/interface/type-alias exports (v0.5.525)

After #460 closed the `export { local as keyword }` rename gap, three
residual link errors remained when compiling Effect (`bun add effect &&
perry compile test_minimal.ts`):

  _perry_fn_node_modules_effect_src_Order_ts__Order
  _perry_fn_node_modules_effect_src_SchemaAST_ts__Union
  _perry_fn_node_modules_effect_src_internal_channel_subexecutor_ts__Emit

Two distinct symptom classes shared the same root cause — no export-side
emission of `perry_fn_<mod>__<exported>`:

  (1) exported classes (`export class Union<M>` / `export class Emit<R>`)
      emit `perry_class_keys_*` + `perry_method_*` + a constructor symbol
      but no value-getter shaped like `perry_fn_<mod>__<ClassName>`.
      Consumer-side `AST.Union.make(...)` resolves `AST.Union` through
      lower_call.rs's `ExternFuncRef` arm, which always builds
      `perry_fn_<src>__<name>` — link-fail.

  (2) exported interfaces / type aliases (`export interface Order<in A>`
      in Order.ts) are type-only at runtime, but type annotations like
      `order.Order<RuntimeFiber<unknown,unknown>>` in
      `export const Order: order.Order<…> = internal.Order` (Fiber.ts:308)
      leak into the value-position symbol resolver, emitting a load of
      `perry_fn_<Order_ts>__Order` that never had a definition.

Fix: one block in `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs` after the #460
forwarding-wrapper pass walks `hir.exports` for `Export::Named { exported }`,
computes `perry_fn_<modprefix>__<sanitize(exported)>`, skips when the
new `LlModule::has_function` helper reports the symbol is already claimed
by an earlier emission path (function body, module-variable getter, #460
forwarding wrapper), and otherwise emits a `() -> double` stub returning
NaN-boxed undefined. Mirrors the consumer-side no-op wrapper at
codegen.rs:1955 — cross-module class/type-only references link cleanly

fix(codegen+runtime): closes #462 — TypeError on property access against undefined / null (v0.5.526)

PropertyGet codegen previously routed every non-pointer/non-string
receiver through the silent-undefined branch in `pget.recv_bad`.
That violated spec for the two cases that should throw — `undefined.foo`
and `null.bar` — and turned loud bugs into invisible ones (the
issue describes a JWS/AES PoC that "ran to completion" while every
line was no-oping against an unstubbed `crypto.subtle`).

Split `pget.recv_bad` into a TAG_UNDEFINED/TAG_NULL nullish check
followed by a call to `js_throw_type_error_property_access(is_null,
prop_ptr, prop_len)`. The helper prints a node-shaped
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of {undefined|null} (reading
'<prop>')` to stderr and `process::exit(1)`s — exception machinery
arrives later (see issue's "Out of scope"). Other invalid receiver
shapes (numbers, bools, raw f64) keep the silent-undefined fall-
through since Perry has no primitive auto-boxing yet, and changing
their semantics would regress unrelated call sites.

Optional chaining and nullish coalescing already short-circuit at
the HIR layer (lower.rs `OptChain` → `Conditional`) before reaching
PropertyGet, so they continue to no-op on undefined/null receivers.

Test: test-files/test_issue_462_nullish_property_access.ts +
matching expected-output file (parity runner falls back to expected-
output mode since node also throws).

Parity sweep stable at 210 pass / 2 known fails.

fix(runtime): closes #470 — Buffer.{read,write}{U,}Int{BE,LE}(offset, byteLength) variable-byteLength forms (v0.5.527)

`dispatch_buffer_method` only handled the fixed-width
`readUInt8/16/32` / `writeUInt8/16/32` cases — the parametric
`buf.readUIntBE(offset, byteLength)` and `buf.writeUIntBE(value, offset, byteLength)`
families fell through to `TAG_UNDEFINED` / silent no-op. BSON
`ObjectId`'s 3-byte counter was the textbook break: every generated
`ObjectId` came out identical (counter bytes never written) so
`insertMany(N)` ended up with `ninserted: 1` after mongod rejected
the rest with `E11000 duplicate key`.

Added 8 runtime functions in `crates/perry-runtime/src/buffer.rs`
(`js_buffer_{read,write}_{uint,int}_{be,le}`, byteLength 1..=6,
sign-extends through `(n*8)`-bit two's complement for the signed reads,
returns `undefined` / no-ops on out-of-range byteLength to match the
rest of the buffer dispatch's tolerant-on-bad-args convention) and
wired the 8 method-name arms into `dispatch_buffer_method`. The
codegen-side `try_emit_buffer_read_intrinsic` fast path is opt-in by
exact method name (`classify_buffer_numeric_read` doesn't list these)
so the variable-byteLength calls naturally fall through to the
runtime dispatch — no codegen changes needed.

Output now matches Node 25.8.0 / Bun 1.3.12 byte-for-byte for the
issue repro plus signed/LE coverage.

  `os` (`platform`/`arch`/…/`EOL`), `path` (`join`/`dirname`/…/`sep`),

## #463 compile-time check (Phase B)

In `expr_member.rs::lower_member`, after `Expr::PropertyGet`'s receiver
is lowered, if it's `NativeModuleRef(M)` and the property is an Ident
`P`, look up `module_has_symbol(M, P)`. When absent and
`module_has_any_entries(M)` is true (i.e. the module is enumerated and
strict), bail with `LowerError` pointing at `member.span`. Existing
`perry check` and compile-error machinery formats the file:line:column.
Modules with zero manifest entries fall through to current permissive
behavior so coverage can land incrementally without breaking unrelated
working code — adding entries promotes the module to strict mode
automatically.

Stubs (`stub: true`) are NOT errored — those are intentional no-ops
surfaced by #464's runtime first-call warning.

Two escape hatches:
- `PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1` skips the check entirely (downgrades to

  followup will fix without forcing an unrelated change in this PR.

## Enforcement

`NativeLibraryManifest::abi_version: Option<String>` populated
from `pkg.perry.nativeLibrary.abiVersion` in
`parse_native_library_manifest`. New
`resolve::validate_abi_version` runs the declared range through
`semver::VersionReq` and checks it covers the bundled `perry-ffi`
version (currently `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` since perry-ffi
ships in lockstep with perry through the v0.5.x cycle).

Bare-major declarations (`"0.5"`) auto-promote to `^0.5` so
wrappers don't have to learn caret syntax to express the common
case. Same pragma cargo's manifest parser uses.

Behavior on this branch:
- `None` → stderr warning naming the package, compilation
  continues. (Transitional v0.5.x rule. v0.6.0 will flip to a
  hard error.)
- Range matches → silent OK.
- Range excludes the bundled version → `anyhow::Error` with
  actionable text:

  ```
  native library `<pkg>` declares perry-ffi ABI "0.5" but this
  Perry build ships perry-ffi 0.6.1. Update the package or use a
  Perry release whose perry-ffi version matches the declared
  range.
  ```

- Unparseable string → error pointing at the offending package.

Wired into both arms of `collect_modules.rs` (NativeCompiled and
Interpreted paths) so the validation runs regardless of which
codegen path the consumer's TS lands on.

## Parser

`crates/perry/src/commands/compile/well_known.rs` exposes:

```rust
pub struct WellKnownBinding {
    pub package: String,
    pub krate: String,
    pub lib: String,
    pub tracking: Option<String>,
}

pub fn lookup_well_known(package: &str) -> Option<&'static WellKnownBinding>;
pub fn iter_well_known() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static WellKnownBinding>;
pub fn bundled_staticlib_path(workspace_root: &Path, binding: &WellKnownBinding)
    -> Option<PathBuf>;
```

Embedded toml via `include_str!`, parsed once into a `BTreeMap`
behind an `OnceLock`. `node:` prefix stripped on lookup so
`import 'node:dotenv'` resolves the same as `import 'dotenv'`
(matches the rest of Perry's resolver conventions, even though
no real npm package uses the prefix).

`bundled_staticlib_path` is the hook the linkage flip in step 2
will consume — given the workspace root from
`find_perry_workspace_root`, it returns the path to
`target/release/lib<lib>.a` if the file exists.

feat(perry-stdlib+perry): refs #466 — well-known dotenv resolution flip (v0.5.533)

Phase 4 step 2: completes the resolution path that step 1 set up.
`PERRY_USE_WELL_KNOWN=1 perry compile <ts>` now routes
`import 'dotenv'` to perry-ext-dotenv's bundled `.a` instead of
the perry-stdlib copy, with the `_js_dotenv_*` symbols defined
exactly once in the resulting link.

## Feature gate

New `bundled-dotenv` feature in perry-stdlib (default-on,
included in `default = ["full"]`) gates `pub mod dotenv;` and
`pub use dotenv::*;`. Programs that don't opt into the
well-known path see byte-identical behavior because the feature
is on by default. `stdlib_features::module_to_features("dotenv")`
now maps to `&["bundled-dotenv"]` so the auto-optimize path
turns the feature on exactly when the user imports dotenv.

Both build paths verified compile cleanly:
```
$ cargo build -p perry-stdlib                          # default → with dotenv
$ cargo build -p perry-stdlib --no-default-features    # minimal → without dotenv
```

## Resolution flip

`OptimizedLibs::well_known_libs: Vec<PathBuf>` carries bundled
archives from `optimized_libs::build_optimized_libs` to
`link::build_and_run_link`. The flip runs after
`compute_required_features`:

```rust
if std::env::var_os("PERRY_USE_WELL_KNOWN").is_some() {
    for module in &ctx.native_module_imports {
        if let Some(binding) = well_known::lookup_well_known(module) {
            let lib = bundled_staticlib_path(&workspace_root, binding)?;
            for feat in module_to_features(module) {
                features.remove(feat);
            }
            well_known_libs.push(lib);
        }
    }
}
```

In the linker, the well-known archives are concatenated right
after `stdlib_lib` so they fill the symbol gap the rebuild just
opened. Both branches of `build_and_run_link` (default + Android+UI)
get the new args.

```
$ ./out
env: hello-from-bundled
```

The auto-optimize log confirms `bundled-dotenv` was stripped

`process.env` correctly through perry-ext-dotenv's

## Why env-var gated

Default behavior is byte-identical until the route is proven

Perry's tokio runtime + Promise machinery. Two acceptance tests
(`perry-ext-bcrypt` and `perry-ext-argon2`) ride along to prove the

## perry-ffi v0.5.x async surface

```rust
pub struct JsPromise(*mut Promise); // Send
impl JsPromise {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub unsafe fn from_raw(*mut Promise) -> Self;
    pub fn as_raw(&self) -> *mut Promise;
    pub fn resolve_string(self, &str);
    pub fn resolve_bool(self, bool);
    pub fn resolve_number(self, f64);
    pub fn resolve_undefined(self);
    pub fn resolve_null(self);
    pub fn reject_string(self, &str);
}

pub fn spawn_blocking<F>(f: F)
where F: FnOnce() + Send + 'static;

pub fn nanbox_string_bits(*mut StringHeader) -> u64;
pub use perry_runtime::Promise;
```

The NaN-boxing tag values (STRING_TAG, POINTER_MASK, TAG_UNDEFINED,
TAG_NULL) are duplicated into perry-ffi as private constants so the
perry-ffi semver promise binds to them — a perry-runtime rename
bumps perry-ffi major.

## Layered architecture

Three layers, each with a stable contract:

1. **perry-stdlib** ships `#[no_mangle] extern "C"` shims in
   `src/perry_ffi_async.rs` (gated on `async-runtime` feature):
   `perry_ffi_promise_new`, `perry_ffi_promise_resolve_bits`,
   `perry_ffi_promise_reject_bits`, `perry_ffi_spawn_blocking`.
   These wrap async_bridge's public Rust functions.

2. **perry-ffi** declares those symbols `extern "C"` and exposes
   safe Rust wrappers above. perry-ffi has zero direct dependency
   on perry-stdlib — at link time the `perry_ffi_*` symbols are
   resolved by perry-stdlib's archive (already in the link
   surface for any program using async features).

3. **perry-ext-** wrappers depend only on perry-ffi. Their
   `.a`s carry unresolved `perry_ffi_*` references that resolve
   at final link time. Verified:

   ```
   $ nm libperry_ext_bcrypt.a | grep "perry_ffi"
   U _perry_ffi_promise_new
   U _perry_ffi_promise_resolve_bits
   U _perry_ffi_promise_reject_bits
   U _perry_ffi_spawn_blocking
   ```

## perry-ext-bcrypt + perry-ext-argon2

Both ports use the new surface end-to-end:

```rust
let promise = JsPromise::new();
let raw = promise.as_raw();
spawn_blocking(move || match bcrypt::hash(&password, cost) {
    Ok(hash) => promise.resolve_string(&hash),
    Err(e) => promise.reject_string(&format!("Bcrypt error: {}", e)),
});
raw  // returned to TS — runtime delivers the eventual resolution
```

`JsPromise` is marked `unsafe impl Send` so it can cross the
`spawn_blocking` boundary; the closure consumes it (FnOnce) and
the runtime guarantees the underlying Promise is alive for the
async lifetime. perry-ext-bcrypt exposes 5 FFI symbols (hash,
compare, genSalt async + hashSync, compareSync); perry-ext-argon2
exposes 5 (hash, verify, needsRehash + hashSync, verifySync).

The `crypto` umbrella forks for the two password-hashing
bindings:

```toml

bundled-bcrypt = ["dep:bcrypt", "async-runtime"]
bundled-argon2 = ["dep:argon2", "async-runtime"]
```

Existing `--features crypto` builds keep producing byte-identical
archives (the umbrella pulls everything in transitively).

## Resolution flip plumbing

`stdlib_features::module_to_features` now dispatches per-binding
for `bcrypt` and `argon2`. The well-known flip in
`optimized_libs::build_optimized_libs` special-cases async
wrappers — when stripping `bundled-bcrypt` / `bundled-argon2`,
re-assert `async-runtime` so perry-stdlib's `perry_ffi_async`
shims still compile (otherwise the wrapper's `.a` would link-fail
on `perry_ffi_*`). `well_known_bindings.toml` gains both
entries; `every_entry_references_a_workspace_crate` keeps
passing.

feat(perry-ffi+perry-ext-lru-cache): refs #466 — handle registry surface, first handle-based port (v0.5.539)

Phase 1.2 of the perry-ffi v0.5 surface (after strings v0.5 and
async v0.5.1) — adds the third dimension wrappers need: opaque
integer handles to long-lived Rust objects. Brings the wrapper
port count to 9.

## perry-ffi handle registry

```rust
pub type Handle = i64;
pub const INVALID_HANDLE: Handle = 0;

pub fn register_handle<T: 'static + Send + Sync>(value: T) -> Handle;
pub fn with_handle<T, R>(handle: Handle, f: impl FnOnce(&T) -> R) -> Option<R>;
pub fn with_handle_mut<T, R>(handle: Handle, f: impl FnOnce(&mut T) -> R) -> Option<R>;
pub fn get_handle<T>(handle: Handle) -> Option<&'static T>;
pub fn get_handle_mut<T>(handle: Handle) -> Option<&'static mut T>;
pub fn take_handle<T>(handle: Handle) -> Option<T>;
pub fn drop_handle(handle: Handle) -> bool;
pub fn handle_exists(handle: Handle) -> bool;
```

Storage is a process-wide `DashMap<i64, Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>>`
behind a `Lazy<>`. Counter starts at 1 so `0` is reserved as
[`INVALID_HANDLE`] — perfect alias for JS `null` since `if
(handle)` becomes false for the sentinel. Unlike perry-stdlib's
analogous registry (which lives at `crates/perry-stdlib/src/common/handle.rs`),
perry-ffi's registry is its own integer space — they don't
share entries. The well-known flip means only one is used per
program, so collision is structurally impossible.

The Rust generics monomorphize per call site, but `pub static
HANDLES` in perry-ffi's rlib resolves to a single symbol at link
time — every wrapper crate using perry-ffi's registry sees the
same DashMap. Wrapper authors use private newtypes (e.g.
`pub struct LruCacheHandle { cache: LruCache<i64, f64> }`) so
their type-ID never collides with another wrapper's.

perry-ffi gains `dashmap = "6"` and `once_cell = "1"` direct
deps. Both already in the link surface via perry-stdlib's
transitives, so this is zero binary-size growth in practice.

8 unit tests cover round-trip + mutable access + type-mismatch
miss + handle uniqueness.

8 FFI exports (`js_lru_cache_new`/`get`/`set`/`has`/`delete`/
`clear`/`size`/`peek`). Uses `lru = "0.16"` directly. Keys +
values both stored as `f64` bit patterns — same homogeneous-FFI
trick perry-stdlib's copy uses; string-keyed caches NaN-box the
string pointer into the f64 at the call site.

6 unit tests: basic round trip, LRU eviction at max size,
delete+clear, peek-doesn't-bump-recency, missing-key-returns-NaN,

clients, and any wrapper returning structured data needs.
First db driver ported as the acceptance test. Foundation for
#424 (Tursodb) which will use this same recipe.

## perry-ffi JsValue surface

```rust
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct JsValue(pub u64);

impl JsValue {
    pub const UNDEFINED: Self;
    pub const NULL: Self;
    pub const TRUE: Self;
    pub const FALSE: Self;

    pub const fn from_bool(b: bool) -> Self;
    pub fn from_number(n: f64) -> Self;
    pub const fn from_int32(n: i32) -> Self;
    pub fn from_string_ptr(p: *mut StringHeader) -> Self;
    pub fn from_object_ptr<T>(p: *mut T) -> Self;

    pub const fn is_undefined(self) -> bool;     // and null/bool/string/pointer/int32
    pub fn is_number(self) -> bool;              // covers int32 + real f64

    pub fn to_bool(self) -> bool;
    pub fn to_number(self) -> f64;
    pub fn to_int32(self) -> i32;
    pub fn as_string_ptr(self) -> *mut StringHeader;
    pub fn as_pointer<T>(self) -> *mut T;

    pub const fn bits(self) -> u64;
    pub const fn from_bits(b: u64) -> Self;
}
```

`JsValue` is `#[repr(transparent)]` over u64, so `extern "C" fn(JsValue) -> JsValue`
uses the same C ABI as `extern "C" fn(u64) -> u64` — single
register pass-by-value on every target.

NaN-box tag values are now part of perry-ffi's stable contract.
Runtime renumbering bumps perry-ffi major.

## Object/array primitives

```rust
extern "C" {
    pub fn js_array_alloc(capacity: u32) -> *mut ArrayHeader;
    pub fn js_array_push(arr: *mut ArrayHeader, value: JsValue) -> *mut ArrayHeader;
    pub fn js_array_get(arr: *const ArrayHeader, index: u32) -> JsValue;
    pub fn js_array_set(arr: *mut ArrayHeader, index: u32, value: JsValue);
    pub fn js_object_alloc_with_shape(
        shape_id: u32, field_count: u32,
        packed_keys: *const u8, packed_keys_len: u32,
    ) -> *mut ObjectHeader;
    pub fn js_object_get_field(obj: *const ObjectHeader, field_index: u32) -> JsValue;
    pub fn js_object_set_field(obj: *mut ObjectHeader, field_index: u32, value: JsValue);
}

pub fn build_object_shape(keys: &[&str]) -> (Vec<u8>, u32);
```

`build_object_shape` produces the (packed_keys, shape_id) pair
the runtime's `js_object_alloc_with_shape` expects.
`0x4646_0000` ("FF" prefix) namespaces perry-ffi-built shapes
from perry-stdlib's `0x5143_0000` ("SQ").

6 unit tests cover constants, round trips, type predicate
disjointness, shape-hash determinism, packed-keys format.

## perry-ffi additions

```rust
// Binary-bytes — no UTF-8 validation.
pub fn read_bytes(handle: JsString) -> Option<&'static [u8]>;
pub fn alloc_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> JsString;

// Generalized promise resolution for non-string/bool/number cases.
impl JsPromise {
    pub fn resolve(self, value: JsValue);
    pub fn reject(self, value: JsValue);
}
```

`read_string` is now a thin `read_bytes + str::from_utf8` wrapper
— same external surface, refactored to share the underlying
header walk. `alloc_bytes` calls the same runtime
`js_string_from_bytes` that `alloc_string` uses; the difference
is purely at the perry-ffi typed-API layer.

`JsPromise::resolve` / `reject` take any `JsValue`, used by
zlib's async path (which resolves with a POINTER_TAG-tagged
binary buffer that none of the typed `resolve_string` /
`resolve_bool` shortcuts cover).

## perry-ext-zlib

Eight FFI exports — gzipSync / gunzipSync / deflateSync /
inflateSync (sync) + gzip / gunzip / deflate / inflate (async
via spawn_blocking). Same flate2 backend perry-stdlib uses; same
public surface.

Async results NaN-box as `JsValue::from_object_ptr` (POINTER_TAG)
rather than STRING_TAG, because gzip output isn't valid UTF-8.
TS-side `Buffer` / typed-array consumers see them as opaque
pointers with the raw bytes underneath — same trick the
existing perry-stdlib zlib uses, now exposed to external
wrappers through perry-ffi's `JsValue::from_object_ptr` API.

3 unit tests cover the pure-Rust gzip / gunzip / deflate /
inflate round trips. The FFI round trip can't be unit-tested in
debug mode — `js_string_from_bytes` calls `compute_utf16_len`
which goes through `from_utf8_unchecked` and trips std's
debug-only `unsafe_precondition` panic on non-UTF-8 inputs.
Release mode skips the assertion (the `utf16_len` value ends up
meaningless but the StringHeader payload is intact and binary
is recoverable through POINTER_TAG access). End-to-end TS smoke
test covers the path under release.

## perry-ffi closure surface

```rust
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct JsClosure(*const ClosureHeader);  // Send

impl JsClosure {
    pub unsafe fn from_raw(*const ClosureHeader) -> Self;
    pub fn as_raw(self) -> *const ClosureHeader;
    pub fn is_null(self) -> bool;
    pub unsafe fn call0(self) -> f64;
    pub unsafe fn call1(self, arg0: f64) -> f64;
    pub unsafe fn call2(self, arg0: f64, arg1: f64) -> f64;
    pub unsafe fn call3(self, arg0: f64, arg1: f64, arg2: f64) -> f64;
    pub unsafe fn call4(self, arg0: f64, arg1: f64, arg2: f64, arg3: f64) -> f64;
}
pub use perry_runtime::ClosureHeader as RawClosureHeader;
```

perry-runtime's `js_closure_call0..8` are already `extern "C"`,
so perry-ffi just declares them as externs and wraps with type
safety. Higher-arity calls (5..8) deferred until a real wrapper
demands them — the v0.5 surface stays minimum-viable.

`JsClosure` is `unsafe impl Send` so wrappers can hand a closure
to `spawn_blocking` for retry loops, background event handlers,
etc. — the underlying `ClosureHeader` is reference-counted by
the runtime.

Wrapper authors construct closure args via `JsValue::*` and
decode return values the same way. Single 64-bit register
(NaN-boxed f64) carries any JS value across the call boundary.

Ports the npm `exponential-backoff` package's `backOff(fn)`

Faithful re-port — kept the trick from perry-stdlib's existing

the user closure returns a POINTER_TAG-tagged Promise, we

Pure-Rust, no extra deps. 2 unit tests cover `is_valid_result`

## Async-Rust → Perry-async bridge

turso's API is async-first (`Builder::new_local(path).build().await`).
Bridged via `tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(async {
  ... })` inside `spawn_blocking` closures — same pattern Tursodb
itself recommends, and the same shape as bcrypt / argon2 / zlib's
async paths. The handle-current call works because perry-ffi's
spawn_blocking runs the closure on perry-stdlib's shared tokio
blocking pool, which has a runtime context.

## perry-ext-iroh

[Iroh](https://www.iroh.computer/) is a Rust library for direct
peer-to-peer QUIC connections, with hole punching + relay fallback.
The wrapper exposes a TypeScript surface for the absolute basics:

| TS | Rust async signature |
|---|---|
| `iroh.bind()`              | `Endpoint::bind(presets::N0).await` |
| `iroh.nodeId(handle)`      | `endpoint.online().await; endpoint.addr().id.to_string()` |
| `iroh.close(handle)`       | `endpoint.close().await` |

`presets::N0` gives sane defaults: discovery via n0's number-DNS,
n0 relay servers as the hole-punch fallback. nodeId is the
hex-encoded Ed25519 public key — what users share so peers can
connect to them.

## What's deferred

Full peer-connection / stream API (`open_bi` / `read_to_end` /
event callbacks for incoming connections) waits on a separate
followup. The blocking question is API design, not perry-ffi
surface — closure invocation was shipped in v0.5.542, so the
event-callback machinery is already available. The open
question is the right ergonomic shape over QUIC stream semantics
(Promises vs. AsyncIterables, who owns lifetime when a peer
disconnects, etc.). Punted to a focused design pass.

## perry-ext-axios

5 method exports — get / post / put / delete / patch — all
return `Promise<Response>`. 3 response accessors — status (f64),
statusText (string), data (string). Uses reqwest under the hood,

## Implementation

Refactored the 5 methods around a single `run_request` helper
that takes a `FnOnce(reqwest::Client, String) -> RequestBuilder`,
dedupes the per-method boilerplate (~50 LOC saved relative to
perry-stdlib's copy-paste-per-verb shape).

Async bridge uses the established pattern:

```rust
spawn_blocking(move || {
    let result = tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(async move {
        let response = client.get(&url).send().await?;
        let status = response.status().as_u16();
        let data = response.text().await?;
        Ok(AxiosResponseHandle { status, status_text, data })
    });
    match result {
        Ok(resp) => promise.resolve(JsValue::from_object_ptr(register_handle(resp) as *mut ())),
        Err(msg) => promise.reject_string(&msg),
    }
});
```

POINTER_TAG-tagged handle (`JsValue::from_object_ptr`) — issue
#340 NaN-box trick preserved from perry-stdlib's original.
Without it, the awaiter sees a subnormal float that decays to
undefined on `r.status` accesses.

## perry-ffi GC scanner surface

```rust
/// Visit every registered handle whose stored type matches T.
pub fn iter_handles_of<T, F>(f: F)
where T: 'static + Send + Sync, F: FnMut(&T);

/// Register a GC root scanner with perry-runtime.
pub fn gc_register_root_scanner(scanner: fn(&mut dyn FnMut(f64)));
```

`gc_register_root_scanner` is a thin re-export of
perry-runtime's existing scanner registration — the runtime
already has the registry; we just expose it through perry-ffi
for binding-stable access.

`iter_handles_of<T>` walks the registry and downcasts to T,
calling `f` on each match. Wrappers pair the two:

```rust
fn scan_my_roots(mark: &mut dyn FnMut(f64)) {
    iter_handles_of::<MyHandle, _>(|h| {
        for cb in &h.callbacks {
            mark(nan_box_pointer(*cb));
        }
    });
}
```

Without this, a malloc-triggered GC between `.on(cb)` and
`.emit()` sweeps cb (issue #35 pattern in perry-stdlib's
existing wrappers).

## perry-ext-events

Full EventEmitter port: 7 FFI exports (new / on / emit /
emit0 / removeListener / removeAllListeners / listenerCount).

Listeners stored as raw i64 closure pointers (Send + Sync —
same trick perry-stdlib uses; the underlying ClosureHeader is
GC-managed, our i64 is just an index). The GC scanner walks
every EventEmitterHandle, reconstructs each i64 as a
POINTER_TAG-tagged f64, and forwards to the runtime's `mark`
callback.

`std::sync::Once` guards the scanner registration so multiple
EventEmitter constructions don't double-register.

4 unit tests cover the listener-management surface (empty /
add / remove-listener / remove-all). The actual emit dispatch
needs a tokio context to invoke real closures — covered by
end-to-end TS smoke in release mode.

## perry-ext-decimal

30 FFI exports covering the full decimal.js / bignumber.js
arithmetic surface:

- Constructors: `from_number(f64)`, `from_string(*StringHeader)`.
- Binops (handle + handle): plus / minus / times / div / mod.
- Binops (handle + number): plus / minus / times / div for the

Macros (`binop_handle!` / `binop_number!`) dedupe the basic
arithmetic operators — saves ~80 LOC vs perry-stdlib's
copy-paste-per-op shape.

Same dispatch decisions as perry-stdlib's existing copy:

- divide-by-zero returns ZERO (Perry convention; matches the
  npm packages' "no exceptions in primitive ops" model);
- `pow(n)` and `sqrt()` fall back to f64 round-trip since
  rust_decimal lacks arbitrary-base/exponent ops directly.

Booleans cross the FFI as f64 (1.0 / 0.0) — Perry's standard
sync-FFI bool encoding.
