feat(perry-ext-tursodb): refs #424 — queryAll / queryOne (v0.5.553)

Closes the row-object construction gap from v0.5.543 — user code
can now `await db.queryAll("SELECT * FROM users")` and get back
`Array<{ id, name, email, … }>` row-objects keyed by column name.

Implementation walks `Statement::columns()` for the column-name list,
calls `build_object_shape(&[name1, name2, …])` to get the
(packed_keys, shape_id) pair perry-ffi v0.5 wants, then for each row
builds the object with `js_object_alloc_with_shape` and fills fields
by index using `js_object_set_field`. Values map turso `Null` →
`JsValue::NULL`, `Integer` (i32-fitting) → `from_int32`,
`Real`/large-Integer → `from_number`, `Text` → `from_string_ptr` over
a fresh `alloc_string`, `Blob` → lowercase-hex `from_string_ptr`
(matches perry-stdlib sqlite.rs convention to avoid pulling `hex`
into the link).

All shape construction runs inside `spawn_blocking` so the main
thread stays responsive while turso fetches — `JsValue` is
`repr(transparent) u64` and `Send`, so resolving the promise from
the worker thread crosses the boundary cleanly.

API_MANIFEST gains `tursodb.queryAll` / `tursodb.queryOne` so #463's
check accepts user code that calls them.

Param-binding (`?` placeholders) is the next gap — needs a JS
`Array<JsValue>` reader on the perry-ffi side that maps onto turso's
`IntoParams`.

feat(perry-ext-iroh): refs #425 — peer-connection + stream surface (v0.5.554)

perry-ext-iroh gains the full request-response peer-to-peer surface:
  - connect(endpoint, nodeId) / acceptOne(endpoint) — connection
    handshake on both sides
  - openBi(conn) / acceptBi(conn) — bi-directional stream pair
  - streamWrite / streamFinish / streamReadToEnd — push bytes,
    close the send half, drain the recv half
  - connClose — clean QUIC shutdown

Server flow: bind() -> acceptOne() -> acceptBi() -> streamReadToEnd()
+ streamWrite() + streamFinish().
Client flow: bind() -> connect(serverNodeId) -> openBi() ->
streamWrite() + streamFinish() + streamReadToEnd().

ALPN is hardcoded to `b"perry-iroh/0"` for v0 — js_iroh_bind
switched from `Endpoint::bind(presets::N0)` to
`Endpoint::builder(presets::N0).alpns(vec![PERRY_IROH_ALPN.to_vec()]).bind()`
so the same endpoint can serve both client and server roles.

New handle types:
  - IrohConnection wraps iroh::endpoint::Connection<HandshakeCompleted>
  - IrohBiStream wraps (SendStream, RecvStream) in a pair of
    tokio::sync::Mutex so the async write_all / read_to_end /
    finish calls hold their lock across awaits cleanly.

js_iroh_conn_close follows the take_handle pattern from
js_iroh_close so closing is idempotent. EndpointId::from_str
parses the base32-hex node id strings users share.

streamReadToEnd returns the bytes UTF-8-decoded as a JS string;
the binary-bytes payload variant is deferred — it needs the same
JsValue::from_object_ptr trick zlib uses.

API_MANIFEST gains 8 new method entries so #463's check accepts
user code that calls them.

Together with v0.5.553's tursodb queryAll/queryOne extension,
this completes the meaningful-implementation pass on both #424
and #425.

fix(perry-hir): closes #463 — extend unimplemented-API gate to chained method calls (v0.5.562)

The v0.5.528 unimplemented-API gate fired for standalone property
accesses (`const x = crypto.subtle` errored cleanly) but missed
chained method calls (`crypto.subtle.encrypt(...)` compiled cleanly
and silently returned undefined).

Root cause: the `module.Class.staticMethod()` arm in
expr_call.rs pattern-matches the AST shape directly and
short-circuits the chain into a single NativeMethodCall HIR
variant, never recursing through lower_member where the gate
lived.

Fix is a parallel manifest check at the same site — before
constructing the NativeMethodCall, consult
`perry_api_manifest::module_has_symbol(module_name, &class_name)`
and bail with the same `(#463)` diagnostic when the manifest knows
about the module but doesn't list the class/sub-namespace.

The 4 sub-namespaces in the existing exclude list
(fs.promises / fs.constants / path.posix / path.win32) keep
working — they're allowed-listed before the manifest check fires.
Same PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1 escape hatch as the lower_member
gate.

  - `crypto.subtle.generateKey()`        → ❌ #463 error
  - `crypto.subtle.encrypt()`             → ❌ #463 error
  - `await crypto.subtle.encrypt()`       → ❌ #463 error
  - `crypto.subtle.foo`                   → ❌ #463 error (was already)
  - `crypto.randomBytes(16)`              → ✅ compiles

docs(perry-ffi): document the v0.5.x git-URL consumption + v0.6.0 crates.io plan

Until the type-source-of-truth refactor planned for v0.6.0,
perry-ffi re-exports types from perry-runtime, which keeps it
un-publishable to crates.io (perry-runtime is private and
shouldn't be on crates.io). Wrappers depend on perry-ffi via a
git URL during the v0.5.x cycle:

    perry-ffi = { git = "https://github.com/PerryTS/perry", branch = "main" }

PerryTS/tursodb-bindings and PerryTS/iroh-bindings already use
this shape and cargo build against live main end-to-end.

The v0.6.0 followup inverts type ownership — perry-ffi becomes
the source of truth, perry-runtime depends on perry-ffi for the
ABI types. At that point perry-ffi can publish to crates.io as

feat(perry-ext-cron): refs #466 — port cron (v0.5.564)

New `crates/perry-ext-cron/` ports the npm `node-cron` scheduler.
14 `js_cron_*` exports — full surface:

  - User-facing: validate / schedule / job_start / job_stop /
    job_is_running / next_date / next_dates / describe
  - Codegen event-loop hooks: timer_tick / timer_has_pending
  - Symbol-surface placeholders matching perry-stdlib's existing
    no-op behavior: set_interval / clear_interval / set_timeout
    / clear_timeout

Architecture parallels perry-stdlib's existing copy:

  - Global CRON_TIMERS queue holds every scheduled job.
  - js_cron_timer_tick() — called from codegen-emitted event-loop
    pump in module_init.rs — walks expired entries and invokes
    JsClosure::call0 on each non-cleared, running callback.
  - js_cron_timer_has_pending() returns 1 while any job is live so
    the event loop keeps the process alive.
  - GC root scanner pins each callback closure pointer so a
    malloc-triggered sweep between schedule and tick can't free it
    (issue #35 pattern).

Codegen calls js_cron_timer_tick and js_cron_timer_has_pending by
symbol name, so as long as perry-ext-cron's `.a` exports them, the
well-known flip can swap perry-stdlib's copy out without touching
codegen.

perry-stdlib's `scheduler` umbrella retained for backwards-compat
but flipped to `["bundled-cron"]`; new `bundled-cron = ["dep:cron",
"dep:tokio-cron-scheduler", "async-runtime"]` per-binding gate is
what the well-known flip toggles.

feat(perry-ffi): refs #466 — add event_pump surface (notify_main_thread)

Re-declares perry-runtime's `js_notify_main_thread` extern with a
safe `notify_main_thread()` wrapper. Same crate-internal pattern as
json (just shipped) / bigint / buffer.

Unblocks the event-driven wrapper ports — `ws` / `http` / `net` /
`fastify` / `streams` all push events from tokio worker threads
onto per-wrapper queues, then call notify_main_thread to wake the
main loop's `js_wait_for_event` call so the pump tick drains them
promptly instead of waiting on the 1-second heartbeat cap.

wrapper-specific and doesn't need a perry-ffi entry; perry-codegen
already calls those symbols by name from `module_init.rs`'s event
loop, the same way it does for cron / readline / etc.

fix(hir+runtime): refs #421 — primitive-literal exports + new Set(string) (v0.5.574)

Two pre-existing bugs surfaced while shaking out hono compilation under
`perry.compilePackages`:

* HIR's `is_exportable` matcher in `ExportNamed` lowering omitted primitive
  literals — `var X = "literal"; export { X };` (the canonical shape pre-
  bundled npm packages use for string/number/bool constants) failed to
  populate `exported_objects`. Importer's `imported_vars` set then missed
  the name, codegen's `ExternFuncRef`-as-value path took the closure-
  pointer branch instead of the value-getter call branch, and the importer
  saw `typeof X === "function"` + `X.toString()` → `[object Object]`.
  Hono's `var METHOD_NAME_ALL = "ALL"` triggered it. Extended the matcher
  to include `Expr::String` / `Expr::Number` / `Expr::Bool` /
  `Expr::BigInt` / `Expr::Null` / `Expr::Undefined`.

* `new Set(string)` SIGSEGVed because `Expr::SetNewFromArray` codegen
  blindly cast the input handle to `*const ArrayHeader` and called
  `js_set_from_array`, which read garbage when the input was a
  `*StringHeader`. Hono's top-level `var regExpMetaChars = new Set(".\\+*[^]$()")`
  hit it. Added `js_set_from_iterable(value: f64)` runtime function that
  dispatches by NaN-box tag — STRING_TAG / SHORT_STRING_TAG iterate
  UTF-8 codepoints (matches JS spec: `new Set("abc")` → `{"a","b","c"}`),
  POINTER_TAG falls through to the existing array path, undefined / null /
  number → empty set. Codegen's `Expr::SetNewFromArray` flipped to call
  the new function with the NaN-boxed value directly.

With both fixes, `import { Hono } from 'hono'; const app = new Hono();`
compiles and runs through to route registration.

Followups still tracked under #421: hono `Response.status` reads as
`undefined` (field access on hono's `Response` class returns wrong value);
full request/response round-trip not yet end-to-end.

fix(codegen): refs #421 — `new Response(body, optsVar)` extracts status/headers at runtime (v0.5.575)

Perry's `new Response(body, init)` codegen only inspected `init` when
it was a literal object — when it was a runtime variable bound to an
options object (the canonical pattern frameworks use to build response
options), perry dropped the status entirely (defaulted to 200) and
ignored statusText / headers.

Hono's `c.text(text, status)` builds `{ status, headers }` inside its
internal `#newResponse(text, arg, headers)` and passes that to
`new Response(text, opts)` — every hono response was reaching user
code with status undefined.

Fixed by extracting `.status` / `.statusText` / `.headers` at runtime
via `js_object_get_field_by_name_f64` when `args[1]` isn't an object
literal. Object-literal short-circuit preserved.

`const opts = { status: 404, statusText: "Not Found" }; new Response("hi", opts)`
now round-trips correctly. Hono's full dispatch chain still doesn't
fire route handlers (separate, deeper bug under #421 — class-private-
fields + closure-call in compose() / RegExpRouter); shipping this fix
since it benefits any framework using the same pattern.

fix(codegen): refs #420 — internal linkage on `__perry_wrap_perry_unknown_func` (v0.5.576)

The v0.5.337 fallback wrapper for unresolvable `Expr::FuncRef` ids was
emitted with default (external) linkage. Multi-module programs (drizzle-
orm has 5+ modules each emitting it) failed link with `duplicate symbol
___perry_wrap_perry_unknown_func`.

Flipped to `internal` linkage matching the surrounding `__perry_wrap_extern_*`
wrappers (their comment block explicitly calls out the same pattern).

End-to-end: `import { pgTable, serial, text, integer } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core'`
plus a 6-line schema definition compiles and runs through to schema
construction. Closes the link-blocking issue for any multi-module
program that has at least one `Expr::FuncRef` site falling through to
the fallback path.

fix(hir): closes #482 — flip class.is_exported on `export { Class }` (v0.5.577)

`class Foo {}` followed by `export { Foo }` in a separate clause was
lowered with `is_exported = false` (because the decl wasn't a syntactic
`export class Foo {}`). The CLI driver's `exported_classes` lookup at
`crates/perry/src/commands/compile.rs:1684` filters on
`class.is_exported`, so the class never reached the importer's
`imported_classes` registry — `new Foo()` from another module fell
through to the empty-object placeholder, and method calls like
`f.add(...)` returned undefined.

Hono's `RegExpRouter` / `Trie` / `Node` / `HonoBase` all use this
pattern (either `var X = class { ... }; export { X };` or `class X {};
export { X };`), so route registration silently no-op'd and
`app.fetch()` returned a default Response with no status/body.
Drizzle schema construction had the same shape.

Fix is one block in HIR's `ExportNamed` arm: after pushing the export
clause, walk `module.classes` for one whose name matches the local and
flip its `is_exported = true`.

Hand-written `class Foo { add() {} }; export { Foo };` from a
`compilePackages` package round-trips correctly post-fix.

Hono now progresses past route registration but `app.request()`
returns undefined (deeper bug under #421 — class-field arrow methods
on classes with private fields). Drizzle schema works end-to-end.

fix(perry-ext-net+ffi): refs #421/#420 — net regression: tokio features + reactor (v0.5.578)

The v0.5.571 perry-ext-net port introduced 5 parity regressions
(test_net_min / test_net_socket / test_net_upgrade_tls /
test_issue_422_socket_connect / test_sock_write_map) all crashing
with "there is no reactor running" or "Cannot start a runtime from
within a runtime". Two cooperating bugs:

1. Tokio feature mismatch — perry-stdlib's tokio was declared with
   the reduced set ["rt-multi-thread", "sync", "time", "net",
   "macros", "io-util"]; perry-ext-net pulled tokio with "full" from
   workspace. When `auto-optimize` rebuilds perry-stdlib in its own
   target dir, cargo can't unify them — two distinct tokio
   compilations linked, each with its own thread-local runtime
   context. perry-ext-net's `Handle::current()` looked at the wrong
   tokio's statics. Flipped perry-stdlib to tokio = "full".

alongside `method_param_counts` in `compile_module`, threaded through

dispatch + virtual-override arm to emit the same `js_array_alloc +
js_array_push_f64` sequence the freestanding-call path already uses.

feat(audio): implement WAV recording on macOS/iOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS/Android/Windows

PR #458 introduced `audioSetOutputFilename` / `audioStartRecording` /
`audioStopRecording` with a working PulseAudio implementation on Linux
(GTK4) plus Web (MediaRecorder), but left every other platform stubbed.
This commit replaces the seven `pub fn ... {}` stubs with real WAV
recording that hooks into each platform's existing audio capture loop.

Per-platform integration:

- macOS / iOS / tvOS / visionOS — append channel-0 samples inside the
  AVAudioEngine `installTapOnBus` callback whenever `RECORDING` is set.
  Sample rate is captured live from `outputFormatForBus:` so the WAV
  header matches whatever the input device negotiates (typically 48kHz).

- watchOS — same AVAudioEngine pattern, slightly simpler audio.rs.
  Also fixes the watchOS `lib.rs` FFI wrappers, which were `_filename_ptr`
  (param ignored) no-ops in the original PR — they now route through the
  existing `str_from_header` helper into `audio::set_output_filename` /
  `start_recording` / `stop_recording`.

- Android — append samples inside the existing AudioRecord JNI read loop
  in the spawned capture thread. Sample rate is fixed at 48kHz to match
  the AudioRecord constructor's `sample_rate` arg.

- Windows — append channel-0 samples inside the WASAPI capture loop,
  honoring the `is_float` / `bits_per_sample` branch already present
  for the dB metering. Sample rate captured live from the WASAPI mix
  format. Wraps in a `Vec<f32>` per packet so the existing per-sample
  loop only does the lock-extend once.

Single shared 16-bit mono PCM WAV writer per crate (header + samples,
clamp-to-i16). 0 dBFS = 1.0 maps to i16::MAX.

Bug fix in PR #458 itself: the per-platform `lib.rs` FFI wrappers used
`crate::string_header::StringHeader` which only exists on macOS (the
macOS UI crate has its own local `string_header.rs` module to avoid
linking perry-runtime). iOS / tvOS / visionOS / Windows depend on
perry-runtime directly and need `perry_runtime::string::StringHeader`;
the PR copy-pasted the macOS path so those four crates never compiled.
Switched all four to the perry-runtime path.

Verified: `cargo build --release --workspace --exclude perry-ui-{ios,
tvos,watchos,visionos,android,windows,gtk4}` clean on macOS host;
`cargo check --target aarch64-apple-ios -p perry-ui-{ios,tvos,visionos,
watchos}` clean. Android + Windows cross-builds need their respective
toolchains (NDK / xwin) — not run here, but the audio.rs additions
mirror the iOS/macOS pattern that did compile.

Recording state lives in module-level statics
(`AtomicBool` + `Mutex<Vec<f32>>` + `Mutex<String>` + `AtomicU64`
sample-rate-of-bits-of-f64) per crate, populated only when the
recording flag is set so non-recording capture pays no extra cost
beyond a relaxed atomic load per buffer.

fix(runtime+codegen): closes #493 — closure rest-param bundling at runtime via func_ptr → fixed_arity registry (v0.5.589)

A closure stored as an instance property (`this.cb = (...args) => …`
inside a constructor) was unreachable through perry's HIR-level
rest-bundling pass — the call site `obj.cb(a, b, c)` resolves through
`js_native_call_method` → field scan → `js_native_call_value` →
`js_closure_callN`, none of which knew the closure declared `...rest`.
The closure body was compiled with K+1 fixed params expecting the rest
array as the K+1-th arg, but the call passed N positional args, so the
rest param ended up bound to the first positional arg as a scalar
(`args = "a"` instead of `["a","b","c"]`).

Hono's `app.get('/', cb)` route registration silently no-op'd because
`args.forEach((handler) => this.#addRoute(...))` couldn't iterate over
`"a"`.

Three coordinated fixes:

  1. New runtime side-table `CLOSURE_REST_REGISTRY: thread_local!<
     HashMap<func_ptr, fixed_arity>>` with public
     `js_register_closure_rest(func_ptr, fixed_arity)` + a
     `dispatch_rest_bundled(closure, func_ptr, args, fixed_arity)`
     helper that bundles trailing args into a fresh JS array and
     dispatches by K to the appropriate transmute (K=0..7).

  2. Every `js_closure_callN` (N=0..6) now consults the registry
     between the BOUND_METHOD check and the existing transmute —
     when found, dispatches through `dispatch_rest_bundled`.

  3. Codegen emits `js_register_closure_rest(@perry_closure_<…>, K)`
     at module init from `emit_string_pool`, walking the
     `closure_rest_params` map already built at codegen.rs:1607.

The static-bundling path in `lower_call.rs::Expr::LocalGet` was
REMOVED — letting the runtime do it avoids the double-bundle that
produced `[[1,2,3]]` instead of `[1,2,3]` (caught by
`test_edge_rest_spread_defaults` regressing in the first iteration).
FuncRef calls keep their static-bundling because they don't go
through `js_closure_callN`.

Plus a small followup: `js_native_call_method`'s array-method
dispatch tower learned `forEach` so `args.forEach(cb)` on any-typed
receivers iterates instead of falling through to undefined.

fix(codegen+compile): closure-bound exported var calls fetch via getter then closure-call (v0.5.590)

Cross-module `Call { callee: ExternFuncRef }` for an imported VARIABLE
binding (`var mergePath = (b, s, ...r) => …` exported from another
module) now correctly fetches the closure value via the zero-arg
getter and dispatches through `js_closure_callN`. Previously the call
site emitted `perry_fn_<src>__<name>(args)` directly, treating the
GETTER as if it were the function body — the getter ignored the args
and returned the closure handle as the call's result, so
`mergePath('/', '/foo')` returned a function reference (`typeof ===
'function'`) instead of a string.

Two coordinated changes:

  1. `compile.rs::1869` now adds EVERY exported-object name to
     `imported_vars` (not just primitives). Closures-assigned-to-const
     are in BOTH `exported_objects` AND `exported_func_param_counts`,
     but their `perry_fn_<src>__<name>` symbol IS the getter, not the
     function body. New `is_function_decl` exclusion keeps real
     `function foo(){}` decls out (their `perry_fn_<…>` IS the body).

  2. `lower_call.rs::ExternFuncRef` Call path checks
     `imported_vars.contains(name)` BEFORE the standard
     `perry_fn_<src>__<name>(args)` direct-call dispatch — when
     present, calls the getter with 0 args, treats the result as a
     closure value, dispatches through `js_closure_callN`. The
     runtime's closure-rest registry (issue #493) bundles trailing
     args correctly when the closure has `...rest`.

End-to-end: hono's `app.get('/', cb)` now registers routes with actual
string paths (vs `[object Object]` pre-fix). Path string still shows
extra leading slashes (`////` instead of `/`) — separate
template-literal + optional-chaining bug, not blocking.

fix(codegen+runtime): closes #471 — Record<number,T> writes corrupted neighboring heap (v0.5.592)

Codegen's IndexSet/IndexGet numeric-key fallback emitted an inline
`obj+8+idx*8` store/load that assumed an `ArrayHeader` (8-byte header)
layout. For plain objects (`ObjectHeader` is 24 bytes + max(field_count, 8)
inline slots), the inline write at offset `8 + 22*8 = 184` overflowed
the ~88-byte allocation and trampled the keys_array of the next
arena-allocated object — surfaced in @perryts/mongodb as
`insertMany(50)` producing on-the-wire BSON docs containing only `_id`.

`js_object_get_index_polymorphic` dispatch by GC type — arrays/lazy
through the array setter/getter (preserving forwarding-chain follow),
plain objects through stringify-the-index + `js_object_set_field_by_name`.
The codegen IndexSet/IndexGet numeric fallbacks now call these helpers.

Also incidentally fixes 3 previously-silently-wrong parity tests
(test_edge_enums_const, test_edge_iteration, test_gap_typed_arrays)
which were masking the same ObjectHeader-as-ArrayHeader bug.

repro: insertMany(50) now returns full 7-field docs from findOne().

fix(codegen+runtime): closes #510 — throw TypeError on method calls against primitive receivers (v0.5.593)

`s.lengt()` where `s: any = "hello"` was silently no-op'ing because
codegen refines `Any` to `String` from the literal initializer, routes
through `lower_string_method`, and the unknown-method catch-all
returned `Ok(recv_box)` — evaluating the call to the receiver itself
("hello") and continuing execution. Same shape on number/bool primitives
fell through `js_native_call_method` to a `NULL_OBJECT_BYTES` sentinel.
Three coordinated changes:

(1) `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_string_method.rs:650` — catch-all
    now emits `js_throw_type_error_not_a_function("string", "<prop>")`
    + `unreachable` instead of returning the receiver. Args still get
    lowered for side effects.

(2) `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs::js_native_call_method` —
    catch-all detects non-string primitives (number/int32/bool/bigint)
    and throws via the same helper. Real-object receivers keep the
    null-object sentinel fallback (separate concern; many call paths
    use this dispatcher as a generic shortcut).

(3) `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs::skip_native` — added
    `Expr::NativeModuleRef(_)` alongside `Expr::GlobalGet(_)`. NativeModuleRef
    lowers to literal `0.0`, which the runtime catch-all would otherwise

prop_len)` runtime helper in `error.rs` + extern decl in `runtime_decls.rs`.

fix(codegen+runtime): closes #514 — IndexGet on any-typed string returns char not byte_len (v0.5.594)

`s[0]` / `s.at(-1)` on a parameter typed `any` that holds a string
now correctly returns the indexed character. Pre-fix the IndexGet
fallback emitted `arr_handle + 8 + idx*8` direct memory reads
unconditionally — when the runtime value was a NaN-boxed
`*StringHeader`, the offset 8 read landed on the string's `byte_len`
field, returning the LENGTH as a subnormal f64 (e.g. `'/'[0]` →
`5e-324`).

Hono's `mergePath = (base, sub, ...rest) => …` triggered this — every
`base?.[0] === "/" ? "" : "/"` returned the byte length of `base`
instead of the first char, so route paths arrived as `////api`
instead of `/api`.

Four coordinated fixes:

  1. New runtime `js_dyn_index_get(value, index)` in
     `crates/perry-runtime/src/value.rs` — strings route to
     `js_string_char_at`, everything else uses the same
     `raw_ptr + 8 + idx*8` direct-read offset hack the existing
     IndexGet fallback uses (load-bearing for
     Object-with-numeric-keys / TypedArrays / Records). LAZY_ARRAY
     / FORWARDED arrays chase through `js_array_get_f64`.

  2. Codegen `expr.rs::IndexGet` adds a new branch BEFORE the
     existing array fast path: when receiver's static type is
     genuinely unknown (`Type::Any` / `Type::Unknown`) AND index
     is numeric, emit `js_dyn_index_get`. The narrow gate keeps
     existing TypedArray / Object / class-instance fast paths
     intact.

  3. `js_native_call_method` adds a string-method dispatch arm
     BEFORE the issue #510 catch-all — `s.at(-1)` / `s.charAt(0)`
     / `s.charCodeAt(0)` / `s.slice(start[, end])` / `s.toString()`
     / `s.valueOf()` on `(s: any)` route to the matching
     `js_string_*` helper instead of triggering #510's TypeError
     throw.

  4. HIR `expr_call.rs` gates `Expr::ArrayAt` emission on a
     statically-known array type (`Type::Array(_)` or TypedArray)
     — `at` is shared between String.prototype and Array.prototype,
     so for `(s: any).at(-1)` perry can't tell which one the user
     means; the gate falls through to runtime tag-aware dispatch.

End-to-end: `(s: any) => s[0]` with `s = '/foo'` returns `'/'`;
hono's `mergePath('/', '/api')` returns `/api`; `app.routes`
registers entries with correct paths `/` and `/api`.

fix(runtime): refs #519 — vtable dispatch NaN-boxes \`this\` pointer (v0.5.596)

`call_vtable_method` was bit-casting the raw pointer `this: i64`
directly to f64, producing a subnormal float (no NaN-box tag). The
dispatched method body's `this` parameter then arrived as a
"number" — every nested method call inside the body fell through
to the issue #510 catch-all and threw \`TypeError:
(number).<method> is not a function\`.

to f64 when the bits look like a raw pointer
(\`0 < bits ≤ 0x0000_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF\`); already-NaN-boxed values
pass through unchanged.

dispatches to SmartRouter.match with a real instance pointer as
\`this\`. The INNER \`router.match(method, path)\` call inside
SmartRouter's body still trips a different path that doesn't
reach call_vtable_method — only the outer dispatch is unblocked.
Tracking under #519.

fix(hir): closes #461 — pre-register local for `const f = (arrow)` decls so nested closures resolve self-references (v0.5.600) (#524)

fix(codegen): closes #509 — eliminate parallel-codegen race on temp .ll/.o paths (v0.5.602)

Two rayon codegen workers entering compile_ll_to_object within the same
microsecond ended up with identical /tmp/perry_llvm_<pid>_<nanos>.{ll,o}
paths because SystemTime::now().as_nanos() resolves to microseconds on
macOS. Both workers overwrote the same .ll, both clang invocations
compiled the same IR, and both read back identical bytes — leaving
sibling .o files (e.g. consumer_type_only.o and consumer_value.o) with
one module's symbols stamped onto the other's filename, breaking the
final link.

Fix: mix a strictly-monotonic AtomicU64 counter into the temp path
alongside the existing pid + wall-nanos. The counter guarantees
in-process uniqueness regardless of clock resolution; pid + wall-nanos
stay for cross-process distinctness.

Removes test_issue_446_import_type_method_typeof and
test_issue_310_namespace_reexport from known_failures.json — both link
cleanly and produce byte-identical output to node --experimental-strip-types
across 30 stress iterations at RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4/8/16. New unit test
spawns 16 threads × 16 fetches and asserts all 256 counter values are
distinct.

Parity: 210 pass / 3 known fails / 0 compile fails / 13 skipped (no
regressions vs v0.5.601 baseline).

fix(hir): refs #519/#421 — register Request/Response/Headers param types as native instances (v0.5.603)

The v0.5.601 IMPLICIT_THIS fix unblocked hono's `RegExpRouter.match`
chain; the next downstream blocker — `app.fetch(req)` reading
`req.url` inside hono's compiled `fetch` arrow — surfaced because
`Request` / `Response` / `Headers` parameter type annotations weren't
registered as native instances at HIR lowering. Without the
registration, `r.url` on a typed `(r: Request)` parameter went
through the generic-object-property-get fallback which tries to
interpret the runtime handle id (a small integer like `1.0`) as an
ObjectHeader pointer — `unbox_to_i64` of `1.0` returns 0, so
`js_object_get_field_by_name(NULL, "url")` returned undefined, and
downstream `url.indexOf("/")` threw "Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'indexOf')".

Fix is one block in each of:
- crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_function.rs (arrow params, line 67+)
- crates/perry-hir/src/lower_decl.rs (function-decl params, line 292+)

When a parameter's `Type::Named` matches `"Request"` / `"Response"` /
`"Headers"`, call `ctx.register_native_instance` with the same
module/class strings the local-init paths in `destructuring.rs`
already use for `const r = new Request(…)`. After registration,
codegen's `Request.url` / `Response.status` / `Headers.get` static
dispatches at `lower_call.rs:3503+` fire and route directly to
`js_request_get_url(handle)` etc.

End-to-end smoke verified with the minimal repro `function
takeReq(r: Request): string { return r.url }` — pre-fix returned
`undefined`, post-fix returns the URL.

Hono itself is still blocked because its compiled JS (via
compilePackages) has TypeScript types stripped, so `(request) =>`
(no annotation) doesn't trigger the registration; proper hono
support needs a runtime-side handle-detection path (separate, larger
followup — likely NaN-boxing handle returns with POINTER_TAG or
detecting raw small-integer values as handles in the property-get
dispatcher).

Parity sweep: 210 pass / 3 known fails / 13 skipped (98.5%, no
regressions vs main).

fix(hir,codegen,runtime): closes #515 (round 2) — tighten with-fold gates and add layered fallbacks (v0.5.605) (#527)

The v0.5.595 fix gated the with-fold catch-all on `!recv_is_class`, but
that predicate only matched four specific receiver shapes (Ident with
class type, `new C()`, `this`, `this.field`). Three new variants from
the comment fell through:

- Object-literal receivers — `const obj = { with(a, b) { return 99 } };
  obj.with(1, 2)` returned `[]` because `Type::Object(_)` flowed through
  the OTHER `with` arm at expr_call.rs:2897 (the bare-ident array fast
  path) where unknown-typed Idents fold optimistically as "array-only
  methods" via `is_not_string`'s final-else.
- Chained method-call receivers — `world.spawn().with(1, {…}).build()`
  returned `[ 6.79e-313 ]` because `ast::Expr::Call(_)` falls into
  `_ => false` in `recv_is_class`.
- Computed-property — `world.spawn()["with"](...)` is a separate
  pre-existing computed-property-on-class dispatch issue (a 1-line
  repro with `["tag"]` instead of `["with"]` on a class instance fails
  identically). Tracked separately.

Three coordinated fixes, layered defense:

1. expr_call.rs:2897 — bare-ident `with` arm: only fold when receiver
   is `Type::Array(_) | Type::Tuple(_)` or one of the 11 typed-array
   `Type::Named` shapes. Typed-array list mirrors the existing
   `is_typed_array` predicate at line 2730 verbatim — without it,
   `new Int32Array(...).with(1,99)` regresses.

2. expr_call.rs:4029 — catch-all `with` arm: replaced `!recv_is_class`
   with an inverted "is array-like" predicate (Ident with Array/Tuple
   type or inline `[…]` literal). Sibling arms (`map` / `filter` /
   `reduce`) keep their optimistic fold because the runtime has
   dispatch fallbacks for them at object.rs:4120/4127/4145/4159; `with`
   had none until (3).

3. lower_array_method.rs:538+ — added `with` arm to codegen's
   array-method dispatcher (catch-all at line 531 silently returned
   the receiver unchanged for unknown methods); object.rs:4179+ —
   defensive `with` arm in `js_native_call_method`'s array dispatch
   tower for receivers that bypass `is_array_expr` (e.g. inlined
   `(x: any).with(...)`).

End-to-end smoke verified: original v0.5.595 5-line repro keeps
producing `result === obj: true` / `result.val: 3` / `obj.val: 3` /
`chain: 7` / `1-param chain: 10`; new variant A returns `99`; new
variant B returns `99`; `[1,2,3,4,5].with(2, 99)` continues to fold to
`[1,2,99,4,5]`; `arr.with(-1, 0)` works; `(x: any).with(0,42)` on a
real array works through codegen + runtime fallbacks; `new Int32Array
([10,20,30]).with(1,99)` returns `Int32Array(3) [ 10, 99, 30 ]`.

(98.1%, identical to pre-fix main baseline).

fix(api-manifest): closes #526 — escape JS reserved words used as method names in generated .d.ts (v0.5.606)

`tsc -p .` against a fresh `perry init` project failed with TS1359 on
`export function delete(...)` for axios.delete — `delete` is a reserved
word, can't be a function-declaration name.

emit_dts now routes reserved-word names through `function _<name>(...);
export { _<name> as <name> };` — the `as <reserved>` rename slot accepts
arbitrary identifiers. New is_ts_reserved_word covers the strict-mode
reserved set + strict-only contextual keywords pre-emptively, so future
manifest additions like axios.try or axios.new don't silently re-break.

Two regression tests: targeted axios.delete shape assertion, plus a
parity sweep over API_MANIFEST that fails any module-level method whose
name is reserved if it leaks through as `export function <name>(`.

Verified: `perry init my-app && bun install typescript && tsc --noEmit
-p .` exits 0; axios.delete / axios.get / the default callable export
type-check cleanly through the alias-export shape.

Bumped to 0.5.606 (PR #527 took 0.5.605 for #515-round-2 while this was
in flight).

fix(hir): closes #529 — fold static-string computed-member access to PropertyGet/Set on class instances (v0.5.607) (#530)

`obj["method"](args)` and `obj["prop"]` on a class instance returned
`undefined` because the `MemberProp::Computed` arm in
`crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_member.rs` always emitted
`Expr::IndexGet`, which codegen routes through the generic
property-by-name read (`js_dyn_index_get`). That path only sees object
fields; class methods live in the vtable populated by
`js_register_class_method`, so it misses them entirely.

The dot form `obj.method` lowers to `Expr::PropertyGet` which codegen
routes through `js_class_method_bind` + vtable lookup, so the two
syntactically-equivalent forms diverged.

Fix: fold static-string `IndexGet` to `PropertyGet` at HIR lowering
time when the index is a literal string that does NOT parse as a
non-negative integer. The numeric-string carve-out keeps spec-compliant
element-access semantics for `arr["0"]` etc. The mirrored fold in
`expr_assign.rs` handles the `IndexSet` analog so `obj["count"] = 7`
parallels `obj.count = 7`.

End-to-end smoke verified:
- `c["greet"]("world")` on a class instance returns `"hello world"`
  (was `undefined`)
- `const fn = c["greet"]; typeof fn` returns `"function"` (was
  `"undefined"`)
- `new World().spawn()["build"]()` returns `99` (was `TypeError`)
- The deferred variant C from #515 (`new World().spawn()["with"]
  (1, {x:0,y:0}).build()`) now returns `99`
- Plain-object computed access (`obj["foo"]` / `obj["bar"]`) unchanged
- Numeric-string indices (`arr["0"]`) keep IndexGet path
- `arr["length"]` continues to work via PropertyGet

Parity sweep: 210 pass / 3 known fails / 0 compile fails / 13 skipped
(98.5%) — improved from the 209/4 baseline. The recovered test is
`test_gap_array_methods`; zero regressions.

fix(runtime+stdlib+codegen): refs #421 — Phase 1 of handle-NaN-boxing unification (Web Fetch slice; unblocks `request.url` in untyped position) (v0.5.608)

Web Fetch handle constructors (Request/Response/Headers/Blob) now NaN-box
their return values with POINTER_TAG via `js_nanbox_pointer`, so handles
flow through the runtime's existing pointer dispatch path the same way
ObjectHeader/ArrayHeader/StringHeader pointers do. Untyped property access
on a Request — `(request) => request.url` in hono's compiled JS, where the
`Request` annotation has been stripped — strips the tag in
`js_object_get_field_by_name`, sees a small id, and routes through
`HANDLE_PROPERTY_DISPATCH` to the new `dispatch_request_property` helper
in fetch.rs. Pre-fix the constructor returned `id as f64` (float `1.0` =
bits `0x3FF0_..._0000`) which failed both the strip path (top16 < 0x7FF8)
and the small-handle range check (huge bit value), so the dispatcher
treated it as an ObjectHeader pointer and dereferenced garbage.

Migration scope (Phase 1 of the broader unification — refs #421's
documented architectural framing):

 - 25 fetch.rs FFI functions migrated. Constructors wrap with
   `handle_to_f64`; accessors unbox via tolerant `handle_id` (accepts both
   the new NaN-boxed form AND the legacy raw-float form so streams/ws/net/
   DB — still Phase 2 — keep round-tripping their handles).
 - 5 i64-typed `js_fetch_response_*` accessors flipped to f64 signatures;
   codegen `runtime_decls.rs` + `lower_call.rs::module=="fetch"` arm
   dropped the 5 `fptosi` conversions — handles flow as DOUBLE end-to-end.
 - 4 new internal `dispatch_*_property` helpers in fetch.rs
   (Request/Response/Headers/Blob), wired into perry-stdlib's
   `js_handle_property_dispatch` after the Fastify/Axios arms. Property
   name + registry membership disambiguates between subsystems whose
   integer ids collide.
 - 16 string methods added to the any-typed dispatch tower at
   `js_native_call_method` (`indexOf`/`includes`/`lastIndexOf`/
   `startsWith`/`endsWith`/`concat`/`toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase`/`trim`/
   `trimStart`/`trimLeft`/`trimEnd`/`trimRight`/`substring`/`repeat`/
   `split`) — fills v0.5.510/v0.5.593's coverage gap so hono's
   `request.url.indexOf("/")` works in untyped position. Each arm calls
   the existing `js_string_*` runtime helper.

End-to-end smoke: hono's `(request) => request.url` returns the URL
correctly through both the typed and untyped paths;
`request.url.indexOf("/")` returns 7 instead of throwing
`(string).indexOf is not a function`. Next downstream blocker is hono's
internal `RegExpRouter.match` returning `[[], []]` despite
`app.routes[0]` showing the route registered — separate bug class
documented in v0.5.601's notes, not in scope. Phase 2 (streams/ws/net/DB)
and Phase 3 (codegen cleanup — remove the `obj_handle > 0x100000` IC
miss guard once all subsystems NaN-box) follow the same canonical
pattern; each phase DELETES detection branches rather than adds them.

Parity: 209 pass / 4 known fails / 13 skipped (98.1%, no regressions vs
main; all 4 failures are pre-existing `known_failures.json` entries —
`test_edge_destructuring`, `test_edge_objects_records`,
`test_gap_object_methods`, `test_net_upgrade_tls`).

fix(codegen+runtime): refs #421 — `recv.method(...args)` on any-typed receivers + `replace`/`replaceAll` in any-typed string dispatch (v0.5.610)

Two fixes that together unblock hono's `app.fetch(req)` past
SmartRouter.match (the route-registration-to-matcher pipeline blocker
documented in v0.5.601's notes).

(1) **Spread method calls on any-typed receivers were silently no-op'd.**
`Expr::CallSpread`'s closure-callee fallback evaluated `recv.method` as
a property read via `js_object_get_field_by_name`, which returns
`undefined` for class-prototype methods on dynamically-typed receivers,
and `js_closure_call_apply_with_spread` then no-op'd. Hono's
`SmartRouter.match` does `router.add(...routes[i])` on the inner
RegExpRouter/TrieRouter (typed `any` because read from the SmartRouter's
`#routers` private field) — the inner routers never received the route
entries, so match returned empty `[[],[]]` even when `app.routes` showed
the route registered. Fix: new `recv.method(...args)` arm in
`crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::Expr::CallSpread` before the closure
fallback. Bundles every arg (regular + spread) into a single JS array
via `js_array_alloc` + `js_array_push_f64` / `js_array_concat`, then
calls the new `js_native_call_method_apply` runtime helper. Skips the
same callee shapes as the regular-Call path (GlobalGet, NativeModuleRef,
ExternFuncRef). New `js_native_call_method_apply` in
`crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs` reads the args array, materialises
elements into a temp `Vec<f64>`, and forwards to `js_native_call_method`
— same dispatch surface as the regular method-call path. Declared in
`runtime_decls.rs` with signature `(DOUBLE, PTR, I64, I64) -> DOUBLE`.

(2) **`replace` / `replaceAll` added to the any-typed string method
dispatch tower.** Hono's `mergePath` and URL building paths use these
on dynamically-typed strings; without the arms, the issue #510 catch-all
threw `(string).replace is not a function`. New arms in
`js_native_call_method`'s string-receiver branch match `"replace"` /
`"replaceAll"`, detect RegExp pattern via NaN-box POINTER_TAG check
(routes through `js_string_replace_regex`), and otherwise call the
plain-string variants (`js_string_replace_string` /
`js_string_replace_all_string`). Function-replacement form (regex with
callback) is deferred — needs closure dispatch and isn't on hono's
hot path.

End-to-end smoke: 4-line repro `f.bar(...args)` on `f: any` correctly
invokes the method (was silent no-op pre-fix). Hono's
`await app.fetch(req)` runs through `SmartRouter.match` past route
matching now; remaining errors are deeper closure-box and
context-finalization issues in hono internals (pre-existing, separate
bug classes — `js_box_get: invalid box pointer 0x0` then
`Context is not finalized` then `(number).set is not a function`).

Parity: 209 pass / 4 known fails / 13 skipped (98.1%, no regressions
vs main; 4 fails are pre-existing `known_failures.json` entries).

fix(transform): closes #531 — add `Expr::ArrayPush`/`ArrayPushSpread` arms to generator's max-id scanners (v0.5.611)

`compute_max_func_id` and `compute_max_local_id` in
`crates/perry-transform/src/generator.rs` had no arms for
`Expr::ArrayPush` / `Expr::ArrayPushSpread`, so any closure buried
inside an array push — e.g.
`ops.push(await runOp('name', N, async () => ...))` lowered to
`ArrayPush { value: Await(Call { args: [..., Closure { func_id: K, ... }] }) }` —
was invisible to both scanners. The generator transform's
`next_func_id` started below K, and the synthesized `__async_iter`
`next` / `return` / `throw` closures got func_ids that collided with
K. Codegen emits one LLVM function per func_id, so one definition
wins; the other closure's invocation runs through a mismatched-shape
capture array, calling `js_box_set` with a NULL or stale pointer.
Symptom in the @perryts/mongodb bench: `findOne_by_id_movie` and
`find_movies_*` op closures' bodies never executed, with 3×
`[PERRY WARN] js_box_set/get: invalid box pointer 0x0` warnings
during their warmup loops.

Mirrors the existing #154 / #393 / #212 arms for ArrayForEach /
NativeMethodCall / etc. Verified: bench's 9 ops now all execute
correctly with 0 warnings, fingerprints match (find_movies = count
50, was count 1). Parity unchanged: 209 / 4 / 13 (98.1%).

fix(runtime+codegen): refs #421 — int-tag string-method results + closure arity padding (v0.5.612)

Two separate hono blockers, both surfaced while tracing
`await app.fetch(req)` through hono's compiled-natively dispatch chain.

(1) **`indexOf`/`lastIndexOf` returned INT32_TAG NaN-boxed values, breaking
comparisons.** v0.5.607's any-typed string-method dispatch tower returned
`JSValue::int32(i).bits()` for these arms, but INT32_TAG values ARE
NaN-pattern f64s — any comparison with a regular number returns false.
Hono's `getPath()` does `for (; i < url.length; i++)` after
`i = url.indexOf("/", colonIdx + 4)` — the loop's `i < url.length`
was always false (NaN compare), `getPath` returned empty, the route
never matched, dispatch fell through to compose, and "Context is not
finalized" fired. Fix: return `i as f64` directly (matches the typed
string-method path which uses `sitofp` in `lower_string_method.rs`).
Also added `replace`/`replaceAll` arms (string + RegExp pattern);
function-replacement form deferred (needs closure dispatch).

(2) **Closures called with fewer args than declared got garbage in
missing slots.** Calling `c.text('hello')` (1 arg) on a
`(text, arg, headers) => …` arrow stored as a class field went through
`js_native_call_method` field-scan → `js_native_call_value(args_len=1)`
which transmuted func_ptr to a 1-arg signature; the closure body's
args 2 and 3 read from random stack registers. In hono's case, the
`headers` slot evaluated to a tiny denormal float, the fast-path
condition `!headers` was false, slow-path `setDefaultContentType` ran,
and the resulting header object was processed through
`responseHeaders.set(k, v)` which hit the issue #510 catch-all
`(number).set is not a function`. Fix: new `CLOSURE_ARITY_REGISTRY`
thread-local in `crates/perry-runtime/src/closure.rs` mapping non-rest
closures' func_ptr → declared arity, populated at module init via new
`js_register_closure_arity` extern (parallel to closure-rest registry).
`js_native_call_value` consults the registry; when the closure's
declared arity exceeds `args_len`, pads trailing slots with
TAG_UNDEFINED and dispatches to the matching higher-arity
`js_closure_callN` (1-8). Codegen `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs`
builds a `closure_arities: HashMap<u32, u32>` alongside
`closure_rest_params` and `emit_string_pool` registers each entry.

Net hono progress this session: `request.url.indexOf("/")` works,
`getPath()` returns the right path, route matches, `c.text('hello')`
takes the fast path correctly, `new Response('hello')` returns a
proper Response. Remaining hono blocker is a SIGSEGV deeper in the
fetch dispatch chain — separate, distinct bug class.

Parity: 209 pass / 4 known fails / 13 skipped (98.1%, no regressions
vs main; same pre-existing `known_failures.json` entries).

fix(runtime+stdlib): closes #421 — hono compiles end-to-end (v0.5.613)

`await app.fetch(req)` against a 4-line hono program now returns the
correct Response with `status: 200` and `body: 'hello'`. Three bugs
fixed:

(1) **`console.log(handle)` and `handle instanceof Promise` segfaulted.**
Both `format_jsvalue` (`crates/perry-runtime/src/builtins.rs`) and
`js_instanceof` (`crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs`) dereferenced
the small registry-id payload of a NaN-boxed POINTER_TAG Web Fetch
handle as if it were an ObjectHeader pointer, reading at `obj - 8`
for the GC type tag — that lands on unmapped memory like
`0xfffffffffffffff9` and SIGSEGVs. Added `(ptr as usize) < 0x100000`
guards: `format_jsvalue` falls back to printing `{}`, `js_instanceof`
returns false unconditionally (handles aren't user-class instances).

(2) **`response.status` returned undefined despite the Response being
valid.** Web Fetch handle id namespaces are disjoint between
registries (Request id 1, Response id 1, Headers id 1, Blob id 1 are
all different objects) but `dispatch_request_property` returned
`Some(undefined)` for unknown properties on a known Request,
shadowing the next handler. Hono's typical flow has both a Request
(id 1, the input to fetch) and a Response (id 1, what the handler
returned) live simultaneously; user-side `res.status` resolved
through Request's dispatcher first and got the catch-all undefined.
All four `dispatch_*_property` arms in `crates/perry-stdlib/src/fetch.rs`
now return `None` for unknown properties so the dispatcher falls
through to the next type's handler.

(3) **Method dispatch on any-typed Web Fetch handles wasn't wired.**
`await res.text()` returned NaN because `js_handle_method_dispatch`
(in `crates/perry-stdlib/src/common/dispatch.rs`) had no Web Fetch
arm — the previous v0.5.608 work added the property arms but missed
methods. Added `dispatch_response_method` (`text` / `json` /
`arrayBuffer` / `blob` / `clone`), `dispatch_blob_method` (`text` /
`arrayBuffer` / `bytes` / `slice`), and `dispatch_headers_method`
(`get` / `set` / `has` / `delete` / `forEach`) in fetch.rs with the
same membership + name-gate discipline as the property dispatchers.
Wired all three into `js_handle_method_dispatch`'s fallback chain
right before the unknown-handle return.

End-to-end smoke: 4-line hono program (`new Hono(); app.get('/', c
=> c.text('hello')); await app.fetch(new Request('http://localhost/'))`)
now produces `status: 200` / `body: hello`, exit 0. Further hono
surface (middleware, routes with params, mergePath, JSON responses,
custom headers, hono/cors) is beyond this release's scope but the

fix(hir+codegen+runtime): refs #420 — computed-key class fields, source-order static init, closure-arity padding (v0.5.614)

Three coordinated fixes for drizzle-orm compile-end-to-end shake-out:

(a) Computed-key class fields like `[Parent.Symbol.X] = init` and
`[SymA] = []` were silently dropped at AST→HIR lowering — `lower_decl.rs`
matched only `PropName::Ident` / `PropName::Str` and `continue`d on
`PropName::Computed`. drizzle's `Table` and `PgTable` use this shape
~6 times; without the fields reaching codegen, the constructor
preamble had nothing to emit and `instance[Symbol] === undefined` for
every Symbol-keyed field.

Fix: extend `ClassField` with `key_expr: Option<Expr>` (lowered key
expression; `name` becomes a synthetic placeholder for HIR identity),
update `lower_class_prop` to handle `PropName::Computed`, remove the
skip in `lower_class_from_ast`, and update
`apply_field_initializers_recursive` to emit `Expr::IndexSet { This,
key_expr, init }` for computed-key fields. The IndexSet path already
dispatches Symbol-keyed writes through `js_object_set_symbol_property`.

(b) Static field initializers that reference top-level consts
(drizzle's `static Symbol = { Schema, Columns, ... }`) were
initialized to `undefined` because `init_static_fields` runs ALL
static fields at the top of `main`, before user `Let` bindings.

Fix: at HIR class-decl lowering, inject
`Stmt::Expr(Expr::StaticFieldSet { ... })` into `module.init` at the
position the class appears in source order. The upfront pass stays —
inline statements correctly overwrite once consts are bound.

(c) Closure arity padding via new dispatch_with_arity helper +
CLOSURE_ARITY_REGISTRY consult in js_closure_callN.

End-to-end: drizzle's minimal computed-key class field repro now
returns "col-default" matching Node (was undefined pre-fix).

fix(codegen+hir): refs #420 — cross-module static class fields (v0.5.615)

When `class Sub extends Base` is in a different file from Base, child-class
declarations like `[Base.Symbol.X] = init` produced undefined because:
1. HIR lowering's `StaticFieldGet` route only fires when class_statics

2. Codegen's static_field_globals map is populated only from hir.classes;
   imported classes' static fields had no entry, falling back to 0.0.
3. Source-side static-field globals were internal linkage.

Three coordinated fixes:

(b) Add static_field_names to ImportedClass; declare external globals on
    consumer + register in static_field_globals.
(c) Expr::PropertyGet codegen: when receiver is ExternFuncRef(Base) and

fix(codegen+runtime): refs #420 — drizzle ctor chain + dispatch fixes (v0.5.616)

Squashes 7 followup commits from the drizzle-fix-a14efd6f worktree
(originally v0.5.615-v0.5.621) into one. Together they get drizzle's
pgTable schema construction byte-for-byte matching Node and column-builder
dispatch through cross-module 3-level inheritance chains working.

(a) `crates/perry-stdlib/src/common/dispatch.rs`: gate `crate::fetch::*`
calls on `feature = "http-client"`. Without this, auto-optimize for
non-http-client packages (drizzle) hit 4× E0433 errors and silently fell
back to prebuilt libs, hiding all runtime iteration.

(b) `compile.rs::imported_vars` cross-module re-export resolution. drizzle
exports `pgTable` from `pg-core/table.js` and re-exports through
`pg-core/index.js`; the lookup `(index.js, "pgTable")` missed against
`exported_var_names` (keyed by ORIGIN path). Fix walks `all_module_exports`
to find the origin path. Also filters synthetic `__computed_field_*` names
out of `ImportedClass.field_names`/`field_types` at all 6 sites.

(c) `class_field_global_index` filters computed-key fields when computing
inline-slot indices, matching the `packed_keys` layout. Without this,
classes mixing computed-key + regular fields had `this.field = X` writes
land at shifted indices, surfacing as `instance.field === number 0`.

(d) Cross-module super() chain through ctor-less ancestors. drizzle's
`PgSerialBuilder extends PgColumnBuilder extends ColumnBuilder` (only
ColumnBuilder defines `this.config = {…}`) silently produced
`instance.config === number 0` because `Expr::SuperCall` only inlined the
IMMEDIATE parent's body. Fix walks past empty-bodied ancestors and
through cross-module ctors with `param_count==0` until an ancestor with a
real ctor is found, then forwards args. `compile_method` standalone-ctor
emission adopts the closest ancestor-with-ctor's params as the
synthesized signature and emits a call to the parent's standalone ctor
with all args forwarded.

(e) `lower_new` walks chain to imported ancestor with real ctor. drizzle's
`new PgSerial(table, this.config)` from inside `b.build(table)` had the
new object returned without ctor work because the parent chain ran
through ctor-less imported stubs and the fallback at
`imported_class_ctors.get(class_name)` missed (class_name is the LOCAL
class). Fix walks past empty-bodied ancestors AND through cross-module
ctors with `param_count==0` until an ancestor with a real cross-module
ctor is found.

(f) Inherited methods in the dynamic-dispatch table. The `obj.method()`
dispatch tower for `obj: any` only registered classes that DIRECTLY
declared the method. Walk every `class_id`'s parent chain to find the
first ancestor that declares the method, registering
`(start_cid → ancestor's fn_name)`.

(g) Runtime `js_native_call_method`'s vtable lookup walks parent chain
(both sites in `object.rs`). For receivers whose class isn't in the
importing module's `class_ids`, the codegen-side dispatch tower has
nothing to match — the runtime needs its own walk via
`get_parent_class_id`, depth-bounded at 32.

End-to-end: drizzle's `serial("id").primaryKey()` now returns the same
instance with `config.primaryKey: true`; probe7's `users.id` shows full
real column data ({name:'id', primary:true, dataType:'number',
columnType:'PgSerial', config:{...}}) matching Node byte-for-byte.

test_query.ts still SIGSEGVs because `eq(users.name, ...)` uses drizzle's
`sql\`...\`` tag which depends on the IIFE-assigned-methods pattern
`((sql2) => { sql2.empty = empty })(sql)` — function-property assignment
is a separate feature gap.

fix(compile): refs #486 — classify relative imports inside compile packages as NativeCompiled (v0.5.617)

The relative-import branch of `resolve_import` (`crates/perry/src/commands/compile/resolve.rs`)
classified `./c.js` as `ModuleKind::Interpreted` whenever `is_in_compile_package` returned false
— and that helper checks only the literal `node_modules/<pkg>/` substring. `file:./` deps and
symlinked package roots both canonicalize to paths *outside* any `node_modules/` segment, so
even though `compile_package_dirs["lib3"]` was already populated by the bare-specifier resolution
of `'lib3'`, a relative re-export `export { C } from './c.js'` inside the package looked
external. The dependent file never entered `ctx.native_modules`, so importing modules saw
`imported_classes=[]` for symbols re-exported through the package's index file, and `new C()`
emitted `js_object_alloc(class_id=0, field_count=0)` with no constructor body call.

Mirror the membership check that `collect_modules.rs` already uses for the entry-file
classification — accept either the substring match OR `canonical.starts_with(dir)` for any
value in `compile_package_dirs` (excluding nested `node_modules/`).

End-to-end: minimal repro `lib3/index.js` re-exporting `class C` from `lib3/c.js` now constructs
C instances with the constructor body actually running and `c.test()` dispatching to
`C.prototype.test`. Hono logger middleware (issue #486) now progresses past the previous
`(number).replace is not a function` failure that was rooted in this same missing-class-metadata
path. Five sanity tests (test_inheritance, test_gap_class_advanced, test_gap_closures,
test_gap_async_advanced, test_edge_promises) all pass.

fix(codegen+runtime+stdlib): refs #486 — class field defaults, response.headers, cross-module getter dispatch (v0.5.620)

Forward-port of the unmerged v0.5.614 hono branch (commit 0136d5d6 on
fix/486-hono-middleware-e2e) onto current main. With v0.5.617's relative-
import-inside-compile-package fix already on main, these three changes now
have the cross-module class metadata they need to actually fire for hono.

Three layered fixes that get hono's `app.get('/', c => c.json({...}))` end-
to-end working under `app.fetch(req)`:

1. **Uninitialized class fields default to `undefined`** —
   `apply_field_initializers_recursive` in `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs`
   previously skipped `class.fields` without an initializer, leaving the
   slot zero-bytes from the allocator. Regular methods saw `undefined` (the
   field-by-name dispatcher returns undefined for absent fields), but arrow-
   class-field bodies that load `this.x` through the captured-`this` slot
   read raw zero bytes — and `0 ?? fallback` takes the wrong branch (0 is
   falsy but not nullish). Hono's `Context.#newResponse` does
   `this.#preparedHeaders ?? new Headers()` which evaluated to `0`; then
   `responseHeaders.set(k, v)` threw `(number).set is not a function`. Now
   we write `Expr::Undefined` for declared-but-uninitialized fields (merged
   with v0.5.614 main's `key_expr` handling for computed-key fields, so
   both string-keyed `#x;` and computed-key `[Symbol.for("k")]` declarations
   get their default-undefined writes).

2. **`response.headers`** — `dispatch_response_property` in
   `crates/perry-stdlib/src/fetch.rs` had no `"headers"` arm, so `res.headers`
   returned undefined. Added a lazy-allocated cached Headers handle on
   `FetchResponse` (snapshot copy of the response's HashMap; spec-perfect
   "live header view" that mutates back through FetchResponse storage is a
   wider refactor).

3. **Cross-module class getter dispatch** — class getters defined in one
   module (e.g. hono's `get req()` in `hono/dist/context.js`) and read from
   another module (`c.req.url` in main.ts) returned undefined because they
   were never registered in `CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY`. Codegen now emits

fix(transform+codegen+runtime): refs #535 — perry/ui state<T> desugar for native targets (v0.5.621)

Layer 1 of issue #535: get the high-level `state<T>(initial)` API working
on macOS / iOS / Android / GTK4 / Windows. Pre-fix, only `--target
harmonyos` worked because perry-codegen-arkts runs its own harvest pass
that rewrites these shapes into setText calls before LLVM ever sees them;
on every other target the strict-API gate (#513) hard-errored with
"'state' is not a known function". The d.ts comment at
types/perry/ui/index.d.ts:263-265 documented this as "deferred to v6.5",
which blocked any multi-screen native app per #535.

Approach: port the arkts harvest's collect_state_bindings +
rewrite_state_calls_in_stmts (lib.rs:1233 / :3725) into a target-agnostic
HIR pass that runs in collect_modules for every target except harmonyos.

- crates/perry-transform/src/state_desugar.rs (new): walk module.init for
  `let x = state(initial)` declarations, assign each a synth id
  (`__state_<N>`), replace the let initializer with Expr::Undefined so any
  not-yet-rewritten escape stays compilable, prepend a synthetic
  `__state_init("synth_id", initial)` call to seed the runtime registry,
  then rewrite every `x.set(v)` / `x.get()` / `x.value` / `x.text()`
  access (recursively into closure bodies and nested expressions —
  children-first traversal so `state.set(state.get() + 1)` evaluates the
  inner read once and pre-rewrite).

- crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native.rs: three new perry/ui method
  arms that lower the synthetic methods to the new runtime FFIs
  (`__state_init` / `__state_set` → `js_state_init` / `js_state_set`;
  `__state_get` → `js_state_get`).

- crates/perry-runtime/src/ui_text_registry.rs: STATE_VALUES Mutex-backed
  HashMap<String, f64> registry plus the three FFIs. `__state_set` writes
  through to the existing perry_arkts_set_text so any
  `Text("initial", "<synth_id>")` widget bound under the same id (via
  perry_ui_text_create_with_id → text_registry.rs::register_text_id)
  re-renders.

- crates/perry/src/commands/compile/collect_modules.rs: wire the pass in
  before the existing transform pipeline, gated off on harmonyos so
  perry-codegen-arkts's own harvest stays the source of truth there.

End-to-end: issue #535's repro `state.text()` lowers to
`Text("loading", "__state_0")` and `state.set("home")` triggers the bound
widget update through the existing setText pipeline.

Limitations:
- Only matches `state(...)` declared at the top level of module.init.
  Function-body declarations are TBD.
- Only matches the canonical method-call shapes — state escaping through
  a function arg or array misses the rewrite. The `let x = undefined`
  shim keeps the program compilable.
- `.text()` snapshots the literal initial-value string at compile time.
  Computed initials get an empty initial; the first `.set()` corrects it
  at runtime.

Layer 2 (visibility binding + NavStack(state, routes) for native multi-
screen) is the next iteration.

v0.5.622 — refs #420 (drizzle entityKind hasOwnProperty: static computed-key Symbol fields)

drizzle's `is(value, type)` brand-check uses `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(SomeClass, Symbol.for("entityKind"))` against every Column / Table / Selection ancestor. Pre-fix, perry skipped computed-key static fields entirely in `lower_class_prop` (only the instance variant lowered), so the static-field side table never populated and `hasOwnProperty.call(C, sym)` always returned false — drizzle's brand-check fell through to "doesn't look like an entity" on every ancestor.

Six coordinated edits:

(1) `lower_decl.rs`: computed-key static fields now flow through `lower_class_prop` and end up in `class.static_fields` with `key_expr: Some(...)`.

(2) New HIR variant `Expr::ClassStaticSymbolSet { class_name, key, value }` in `ir.rs` + walker arms in `walker.rs`.

(3) `lower.rs`: both class-decl arms (export + non-export) emit `ClassStaticSymbolSet` for static fields with a `key_expr`.

(4) `codegen.rs`: `static_field_globals` skips computed-key static fields (no global slot — they live in a side table); `init_static_fields` dispatches to a new `js_class_register_static_symbol(class_id, sym, val)` extern. `Expr::ClassRef` NaN-boxes the class id with `INT32_TAG` so receivers can be distinguished at runtime.

(5) `runtime_decls.rs` declares the new extern.

(6) `symbol.rs`: new `CLASS_STATIC_SYMBOLS: Mutex<HashMap<(class_id, sym_key), value_bits>>` registry populated at module init, plus `class_static_symbol_lookup(class_id, sym_f64)` consumer. `object.rs::js_object_has_own`'s Symbol-key branch checks if the receiver is an INT32-tagged class ref — if so, look up `(class_id, sym_key)` in `CLASS_STATIC_SYMBOLS`; otherwise fall through to the existing `js_object_has_own_symbol` instance-property path.

End-to-end smoke verified: `class C { static [Symbol.for("k")] = "hello" }; Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(C, Symbol.for("k"))` returned `false` pre-fix, returns `true` post-fix matching Node. drizzle's `test_query.ts` no longer throws at brand-check; progress past `is()` exposes a downstream `enumValues` undefined read tracked separately.

Limitations: the static-field VALUE works for the hasOwnProperty.call return, but `(C as any)[sym]` to read it back through normal property access still returns undefined since the Symbol-keyed get path on class refs isn't wired — left for a follow-up since drizzle's pattern only needs the hasOwnProperty.call side.

fix(transform+codegen+runtime+ui-macos): refs #535 — NavStack(state, routes) for native multi-screen (v0.5.623)

Layer 2 of issue #535: makes the documented multi-screen pattern
(types/perry/ui/index.d.ts:370-374) actually work on macOS / iOS /
Android / GTK4 / Windows. Builds on v0.5.621's Layer 1 desugar.

Pre-fix the 2-arg form silently fell through to the 0-arg
`perry_ui_navstack_create()` and the state/routes args were dropped —
the app showed an empty NavStack and `route.set("detail")` had no
effect.

Three coordinated changes:

- crates/perry-transform/src/state_desugar.rs: new `try_rewrite_navstack`
  arm detects `NavStack(LocalGet(state), Array([{name, body}, ...]))`
  for any state-bound local and rewrites it to an IIFE (closure-as-Call
  with empty args, same shape as `try_desugar_reactive_text` at
  lower.rs:7367) whose body allocates the host via 0-arg `NavStack()`,
  then for each route: binds the body widget to a fresh local, calls
  `widgetAddChild(host, body)`, and emits a synthetic
  `__navstack_register_route("__state_X", "name", body)` call. Fresh
  LocalId/FuncId allocation via new `compute_max_local_id` /
  `compute_max_func_id` walkers (mirrors `async_to_generator.rs`'s shape
  but exhaustively scans class methods + try/catch/switch arms so
  allocations don't collide with `ctx.fresh_local()` ids).

- crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native.rs: `__navstack_register_route`
  lowering arm: lowers the body to a widget handle, unboxes to i64,
  calls the runtime FFI, returns the body unchanged so the caller can
  keep chaining.

- crates/perry-runtime/src/ui_text_registry.rs: NAVSTACK_REGISTRY
  Mutex<HashMap<String, Vec<NavRoute>>> per-state-id route table, the
  `js_navstack_register_route(synth_id, name, handle)` FFI (records and
  sets initial visibility — hides the widget if its name doesn't match
  the current state value), the `SetWidgetHiddenHandler` registration
  FFI (`js_register_widget_hidden_handler`), and a
  `navstack_dispatch_state_change` hook called from `js_state_set`
  after every state write that walks the registered routes for the
  changed synth id and toggles each route's visibility through the
  platform handler.

- crates/perry-ui-macos/src/app.rs: registers
  `navstack_set_widget_hidden` (a thin wrapper around
  `widgets::set_hidden`) at app startup alongside the existing
  text/toast handler registrations.

End-to-end: `NavStack(route, [{name: "home", body: ...}, {name:
"detail", body: ...}])` lowers to the construction IIFE, builds both
screens at App-build time, hides the inactive one at first paint, and
`route.set("detail")` flips visibility through the registered handler
chain. Visual verification of the running app requires a GUI session
(compile-time HIR rewrite + runtime registration both verified).

Limitations:
- Routes with computed (non-literal-string) names bail to the 0-arg
  fallback for now.
- Each route's body is evaluated eagerly at App-build time so closures
  referenced from buttons stay alive.
- Nested NavStacks work syntactically but their state synth ids are
  independent (no parent-child route coordination).

The arkts harvest's existing visibility-binding pass stays the source
of truth on harmonyos (gated off in collect_modules.rs).

fix(hir): closes #541, #542, #543 — Map iteration through `Map | undefined` parameters (v0.5.624)

#541 was already fixed in v0.5.522 via `sanitize_app_name` in `crates/perry/src/commands/run.rs`; closing as already-fixed against the v0.5.503 repro.

#542 (entity ID corruption) and #543 (`query.forEach` callback never fires) reduce to two coordinated HIR-lowering bugs in iteration over `Map<K, V> | undefined` parameters carrying f64-sized negative-bigint keys (codehz/ecs encodes relations as `-(componentId * 2^42 + targetId)`):

(a) `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call.rs:2991` unconditionally folded `m.entries()` / `m.keys()` / `m.values()` to `Expr::ArrayKeys` etc. when the receiver type was unknown. Those methods are shared between Array, Map, and Set — for an `Any`-typed receiver the fold ran `js_array_keys` against a real `MapHeader`, reading `size` as `length` and producing `[0..N-1]`. Fix: only fold to the Array variant when the receiver is statically known to be `Type::Array` or `Type::Tuple`; otherwise fall through to runtime dispatch which has the proper `is_registered_map` check. Same Union-aware gating applied to the `forEach` arm.

(b) `crates/perry-hir/src/lower_decl.rs:3815` and `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs:5709` only accepted the bare `Type::Generic { base: "Map", .. }` shape for `is_iterable_map` / `is_iterable_set`. A `Map<K, V> | undefined` parameter is `Type::Union([Generic{Map}, Void])` even after the early-return narrowing — perry doesn't propagate the narrow through the union — so `for (const [k, v] of m)` fell through to array iteration and either skipped the loop or yielded swapped/garbage pairs. Fix: extend the checks to also accept `Type::Union(variants)` where any variant is `Generic{Map}`/`Generic{Set}`, and extract Map's K/V type-args from whichever variant carries them.

End-to-end: codehz/ecs at 159e292 — `inventory-system-relations`, `parent-child-hierarchy`, `spatial-grid`, `tag-filtering`, `state-machine`, `collision-detection`, `advanced-scheduling`, `simple` — all match `bun run` byte-for-byte. New regression test in `test-files/test_issue_542_map_keys_optional.ts` exercises both paths against Node. Parity: 207 pass / 3 known fails / 13 skipped (98.5%, no regressions vs main).

v0.5.625 — refs #420 (drizzle: class field initializers must run AFTER parent ctor body)

Pre-fix, perry applied ALL field initializers (root → leaf) at the top of
constructor lowering, BEFORE any constructor body ran. drizzle's
`class PgText extends PgColumn extends Column { enumValues = this.config.enumValues }`
read `this.config` (set in Column's ctor body via `this.config = config`)
before Column's body ever ran — `this.config` was undefined, the field init
threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'enumValues')`,
and `pgTable("users", { name: text("name") })` blew up at
`colBuilder.build(rawTable)` time.

Per ECMAScript spec, derived-class field initializers run at the top of
[[Construct]] but logically AFTER super() returns — i.e. after the parent
body has run. This change interleaves field-init application with body
inlining across four lowering paths:

(1) `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs` — new `FieldInitMode` enum
    (`All` / `AncestorsOnly` / `SelfOnly`) on `apply_field_initializers_recursive`.
    `lower_new` now applies `AncestorsOnly` up front, inlines the chosen body
    (own-ctor or walked-parent), then applies `SelfOnly` for the leaf class
    after the parent-body chain. Base classes (no extends) keep the simpler
    "All up front" path.

(2) `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::Expr::SuperCall` — after inlining the
    parent body inside an own-ctor body, applies the current class's
    `SelfOnly` field inits so JS-spec "fields run immediately after super()"
    is preserved.

(3) `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs` standalone-ctor emit (used for
    cross-module class metadata) — uses `AncestorsOnly` for derived classes
    plus `SelfOnly` after the explicit parent-ctor symbol call (no-own-ctor
    case).

(4) `crates/perry-codegen/src/stmt.rs` scalar-replacement path — independent
    bug discovered along the way: `Stmt::Let { init: Expr::New { .. } }` for
    non-escaping construction took its own scalar-replace fast path that
    NEVER inlined the parent body when the leaf had no own ctor.
    `class.constructor.clone()` returns `None` for default-ctor classes, so
    the parent body was simply skipped — `this.config = config` never ran.
    Updated to mirror `lower_new`'s logic: walk parent chain, inline first
    ancestor body with forwarded args, then apply leaf `SelfOnly`.

End-to-end: minimal 2-deep + 3-deep repros (`class Leaf extends Mid extends Base { enumValues = this.config.enumValues }`)
match Node byte-for-byte. drizzle's `test_query.ts` no longer throws the

fix(runtime): closes #549 — Set/Map object-key collisions via misclassified strings (v0.5.628)

validating the GC type at the pointee. The downstream `jsvalue_eq`
content-comparison branch reinterpreted each ObjectHeader as a StringHeader
(class_id became byte_len, data pointer landed at offset 20 inside
keys_array's upper bytes), and two empty {} literals — same class_id, no
fields — compared as equal because zero-length string slices match. Same
mechanism collapsed `{x:1}` / `{x:1}` into one Set entry.

enter content comparison; STRING_TAG (0x7FFF) is accepted unconditionally
(tag is the type proof). POINTER_TAG / raw pointers are now subjected to a
(ptr - GC_HEADER_SIZE)->obj_type == GC_TYPE_STRING check; non-string
pointees fall through to the bit-identity fast path that SameValueZero
semantics call for on object keys.

fix(transform): refs #486 — cross-module method inlining loses class metadata for non-exported classes (v0.5.638)

Lib3 exports class C with populate() { this.children['a'] = new Inner(); },
where Inner is a sibling class declared in the same module BUT not exported.
The HIR-level inliner harvested populate as cross-module-inlinable (the
is_cross_module_safe filter only rejects FuncRef / ExternFuncRef / GlobalGet
/ Closure — NOT Expr::New { class_name } against an unexported local class).
Body got copied verbatim; consumer's lower_new("Inner") fell into the
no-class-metadata fallback and emitted js_object_alloc(0, 0); subsequent
inst.method() dispatch found class_id=0 and fell through to NULL.

helpers to crates/perry-transform/src/inline.rs. Methods whose body
references any local non-exported class via Expr::New / ClassRef /
StaticFieldGet / StaticFieldSet / ClassStaticSymbolSet / StaticMethodCall
are excluded from the cross-module inline candidates. Such methods stay as
real cross-module method calls (bl perry_method_<src>__C__populate), where
the source module's codegen — which DOES have the class metadata — emits
the correct inline-alloc with the right class_id.

__AnonShape_* content-addressed shapes are deliberately KEPT inlinable
because they're already propagated via extra_anon_classes so the
destination module synthesizes the same definition.

fix(hir+codegen+transform): refs #486 — class-expression self-binding alias resolution (v0.5.641)

`var X = class _X { ... new _X() ... }` is the npm-dist convention for class
declarations (hono's `var Node = class _Node {...}`, plus countless others —
Babel emits this shape for every `class X { ... }` it transpiles to ES5). The
inner self-binding name `_X` is scoped to the class body and references the
same class as the outer `X`. Pre-fix, perry's HIR lowering registered the
class only under the outer name; references to `_X` from inside the class
body lowered as `Expr::ExternFuncRef("_X")` because `lookup_class("_X")`
returned None, then `new _X()` lowered as `Expr::NewDynamic { callee:
ExternFuncRef("_X") }` and codegen's `try_static_class_name` couldn't
resolve it to a class — falling through to the `js_object_alloc(0, 0)`
placeholder path that stamps `class_id=0` on the new instance. Subsequent
method dispatch on those instances hit the `class_id != 0` gate in
`js_native_call_method` and fell through to NULL_OBJECT_BYTES.

Five coordinated fixes:

1. **`crates/perry-hir/src/ir.rs`** — new `aliases: Vec<String>` field on
   `Class`. Tracks self-binding aliases so codegen can register them in the
   class lookup tables.

2. **`crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs::lower_stmt`'s `var X = class _X` arm**
   now PRE-REGISTERS the inner name as a class alias BEFORE lowering the
   class body, so `Ident("_X")` inside method bodies resolves through the
   existing `lookup_class` → `Expr::ClassRef` path. The class id is
   allocated via `ctx.fresh_class()` and registered under both names; the
   lowered Class struct gets the inner name pushed onto its `aliases`.

3. **`crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::try_static_class_name`** now also
   recognizes `Expr::ExternFuncRef { name }` whose `name` is in
   `ctx.class_ids`. Covers the `Expr::NewDynamic { callee: ExternFuncRef }`
   path that fires in any case where the ExternFuncRef route still triggers.

4. **`crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs::compile_module`** populates
   `class_table`, `class_ids`, `method_names`, and `class_keys_globals_map`
   with every alias entry. The method/getter symbol-emission loops at
   codegen.rs:4253 / :4336 skip alias keys (`if *class_name != class.name
   { continue; }`) so the alias keys don't double-emit
   `perry_method_<modprefix>__<class>__<method>` symbols (the alias-prefixed
   `perry_method_<mod>___X__method` would have an extra leading underscore
   from `sanitize("_X")` that doesn't match the canonical body emission and
   the link would fail with "use of undefined value").

5. **`crates/perry-transform/src/inline.rs::collect_nonexported_class_names`**
   adds inner-alias names to the rejection set even when the OUTER name is
   exported. This prevents the inliner from copying a method body that
   references the inner alias into a destination module that only has the
   outer name in its `imported_classes` (the v0.5.637 fix's logic, extended
   to cover aliases).

End-to-end: `var X = class _X { spawn() { return new _X(); } method() {
return 'hello'; } }; new X().spawn().method()` now returns `'hello'`
matching Node (was returning `[object Object]` pre-fix). The hono Node case
(`var Node = class _Node { #children = Object.create(null); insert(tokens,
index) { ...; this.#children[token] = new _Node(); ... } }`) compiles into

fix(cache): closes #544 — per-module .o cache invalidates on perry binary change (v0.5.642)

rebuilding without bumping the version left the cache key identical —
`.perry-cache/objects/<target>/<key>.o` served the previous pass's output and
the new pass appeared to do nothing at runtime.

Add `perry_build_id()` — a `OnceLock<u64>` that hashes the running perry
executable on first call and reuses the value across all rayon workers in
the same process. Mixed into the cache key alongside the existing version
field. Any rebuild of perry-codegen / perry-transform / perry-hir produces

fix(runtime+codegen): refs #486 — dynamic string-or-number add for type-uncertain operands (v0.5.643)

Hono's `Node.buildRegExpStr` does `k + c.buildRegExpStr()` inside a for-of
loop over `Object.keys(...)` results. Both operands lower as plain f64s
with inferred type Any — the static-string-concat fast path at expr.rs:1118
doesn't fire (`is_definitely_string_expr` returns false for both because
neither has a static narrowing), and the previous fallback path called
`js_number_coerce` on each side then `fadd`'d the results — turning
`"c" + ""` into `Number("c") + Number("") = NaN + 0 = NaN`. Every recursive
level then propagated NaN into the parent's `prefix + tail` concat, until
`Trie.buildRegExp`'s `regexp.replace(...)` threw `(number).replace is not
a function` because `regexp` had become NaN.

New runtime helper `js_dynamic_string_or_number_add` in
`crates/perry-runtime/src/value.rs` checks NaN-box tags at runtime:
- STRING_TAG / SHORT_STRING_TAG → string concat (coerces non-string side
  via `js_jsvalue_to_string` + `js_string_concat`)
- BIGINT_TAG → `js_bigint_add`
- otherwise numeric `fadd` (with `js_number_coerce` on non-numeric operands
  the same way the previous static path did)

Codegen in `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::Expr::Binary` dispatches there
for `op==Add` when neither operand is statically narrowed (`!is_numeric_expr
&& !is_bigint_expr` on both sides). The static numeric/bigint paths stay
on `fadd` to keep the inline codegen for hot arithmetic loops — paying the
runtime-dispatch cost only when type information genuinely allows either
string or numeric result.
