fix(hir): refs #536 — gate Pool/Client/MongoClient native-instance shortcut on actual native-module import

The hardcoded fallback in `destructuring.rs` (`const pool = new Pool(...)`
inside a function body) and `lower.rs` (`export const pool = new Pool(...)`)
unconditionally mapped the class names `Pool` / `Client` / `MongoClient`
to `pg` / `pg` / `mongodb` regardless of where the class identifier came
from. Any user-defined `class Pool { ... }` or import from a TS-source

instance, then `js_transform.rs::fix_native_instance_expr` rewrote

class_name: Some("Pool"), … }`, codegen dispatched through `lower_call.rs`
to `js_pg_pool_query` / `js_pg_pool_end` — runtime symbols that live
only in `perry-stdlib::pg::pool` and aren't reachable from user TS code,
producing `Undefined symbols: _js_pg_pool_end` at link time.

four sites (sync `new` + await `new` × export path + non-export path),
and adds the missing `lookup_native_module` first-pass to the two
export-path arms in lower.rs that didn't have it. The legitimate
`import { Pool } from "pg"` flow is unaffected — it registers through
`register_native_module` and resolves through the general lookup. User
classes named `Pool` / `Client` / `MongoClient`, and TS-source npm
imports like `@perryts/mysql`'s `Pool`, no longer collide.

(`pool.acquire()` returns undefined — cross-module class method dispatch
in the same family as the recent v0.5.586+ hono/drizzle work) but is
distinct from what #536 originally reported.

fix(transform): refs #486 — scan catch param id in generator's max-local-id walker (v0.5.653)

`async function dispatch(i) { ... try { await dispatch(1); } catch (e) {} ... }`
returned `undefined` and never even entered state 0. The async-to-generator
pre-pass correctly recorded the catch param `e` (id=K) in its
compute_max_local_id walk — its `Stmt::Try` arm scans `c.param`. The
downstream generator state-machine pass also has its own
compute_max_local_id (it re-walks because the async pre-pass may have
allocated new ids), but its `scan_stmt_for_max_local`'s `Stmt::Try` arm
only walked body / catch.body / finally — it never read `catch.param`.

When the catch body was empty (`catch (e) {}`), no LocalGet/LocalSet
carried the catch param's id, so the body-only scan missed it entirely;
the generator transform then allocated `__gen_state` over that same id.
Every `LocalSet(__gen_state, N)` clobbered `e`, every read of `e`
returned the state counter, and the state machine never advanced — the
function appeared to return `undefined` immediately because
`__async_step(undefined, false)` saw `done=true` on the very first
`next()` call.

Fix: scan `c.param` in `scan_stmt_for_max_local`'s `Stmt::Try` arm,
mirroring the equivalent scan in
`crates/perry-transform/src/async_to_generator.rs::scan_stmt`. Repro
`try { await dispatch(1); } catch (e) {}` now prints `[d] 0 / [d] 1 /
result: 0` matching Node.

Hono's `compose()` wraps every middleware in this exact shape (`try {
res = await handler(c, () => dispatch(i+1)); } catch (err) { ... }` —
the `err` binding is unused on the success path), so this fix unblocks
a class of hono failures distinct from the v0.5.649 RegExp / v0.5.643
string+string / v0.5.641 alias work.

feat(streams): closes #562 — user classes can extend WritableStream / ReadableStream / TransformStream (v0.5.655) (#566)

The canonical Web-Stream-subclassing pattern (s3-lite-client's
ObjectUploader / TransformChunkSizes — pass `start`/`pull`/`cancel` /
`write`/`close`/`abort` / `transform`/`flush` callbacks to `super({...})`,
attach state on `this`, let inherited methods like `pipeTo`/`pipeThrough`
work on the subclass instance) now compiles + runs end-to-end.

Three coordinated layers:

1. HIR (`perry-hir`): the three Web Stream base classes get
   `native_extends` set in both `lower_class_decl` arms — alongside
   `EventEmitter` / `AsyncLocalStorage` / `WebSocketServer`. Both the
   parent-name (`extends_name`) and the (module, class) tuple
   (`native_extends`) are populated so the codegen SuperCall arm
   reaches the parent-name switch instead of falling out at the no-
   extends gate. New `class_native_extends` registry on `LoweringContext`
   so `let x = new SubclassOfStream(...)` in `destructuring.rs` can
   route the local through the parent stream module's dispatch table.
   New `current_class_super_ident` field for the `super({...})` pre-scan
   to register `start`/`pull`/`transform`/`flush` callback's controller
   param as a `readable_stream` native instance — same shape the
   `new TransformStream({...})` pre-scan in `expr_new.rs` does.

2. Codegen (`perry-codegen`): `Expr::SuperCall` arm dispatches through
   a new `lower_stream_super_init(ctx, kind, super_args)` helper when
   `parent_name` is one of the three stream classes (and not in
   `ctx.classes`). Helper walks `args[0]` via the existing
   `extract_options_fields` (handles both `Expr::Object` and
   `__AnonShape_*` forms), lowers each canonical callback (missing →
   TAG_UNDEFINED), reads `highWaterMark` from `args[1]` if present,
   then calls one of `js_X_stream_subclass_init(this, ...callbacks, hwm)`.
   Per-spec leaf-class field initializers run AFTER super() returns —
   the helper applies `FieldInitMode::SelfOnly` after the runtime call
   so subclass fields like `seenLengths = []` are initialized before
   any inherited callback fires. Stream-FFI receivers in `lower_call.rs`
   (`module == "readable_stream"` recv + `pipeTo` dest + `pipeThrough`
   transform; `module == "writable_stream"` recv; `module ==
   "transform_stream"` recv) are wrapped through a new
   `js_stream_unwrap_handle` runtime call so subclass instances and
   bare numeric handles are interchangeable.

3. Runtime (`perry-stdlib`): three new `*_subclass_init` shims reuse
   the existing `alloc_readable` / `alloc_writable` /
   `js_transform_stream_new` paths so registry entries / GC roots /
   `TRANSFORM_PAIRS` row are identical to a plain `new ReadableStream`.
   The resulting registry-id is then stashed on the subclass instance

   handle)`. New `js_stream_unwrap_handle(value: f64) -> f64` checks
   for a NaN-boxed object pointer (top16=0x7FFD), reads
   `__perry_stream_handle__`, returns its f64 numeric value;
   falls through to the input unchanged for already-numeric handles.

declared user fields (`uploader.uploadedSize` / `uploader.getResult()`)

instead of hitting the streams `NativeMethodCall` arm and returning

fix(codegen): refs #486 — try/switch/labeled now walked by collectors so self-recursive closures inside try{} get boxed (v0.5.658)

`let dispatch = (i) => { try { dispatch(i+1); } catch (e) {} }` had its
self-reference invisible to the boxing analysis. The recursive
`LocalGet(dispatch_id)` lived inside `Stmt::Try.body`, but
`collect_ref_ids_in_stmts` (in `crates/perry-codegen/src/collectors.rs`)
had no `Stmt::Try` arm — fell through `_ => {}` and never walked
`try.body` / `catch.body` / `finally`.

Without those refs in `closure_refs`,
`collect_self_recursive_closure_ids` didn't fire and `boxed_vars` didn't
contain the dispatch id. The closure literal was then allocated with
`capture[0] = pre-let undefined`. The let stored the new closure pointer
into the slot but capture[0] was never updated. Inside the closure
body, `LocalGet(dispatch)` read capture[0] = undefined, the recursive
call invoked an undefined closure pointer (silently returned undefined),
and the function returned undefined.

Same gap in `collect_let_ids` — lets nested under try/switch/labeled
were invisible to the boxing analysis' `declared` set.

Fix: add Try/Switch/Labeled arms to both `collect_ref_ids_in_stmts` and
`collect_let_ids`, mirroring the equivalent arms already present in the
parallel `collect_outer_writes_in_stmt` / `collect_write_ids_in_stmt`
walkers.

Repro `let dispatch = (i: number): any => { console.log('[d]', i); if
(i < 1) { try { dispatch(i+1); } catch {} } return i; }` now prints

fix(runtime+codegen+hir): closes #486 (logger middleware) — class setter dispatch + arrow/fn-expr default-param desugar (v0.5.660)

Two coordinated fixes that together close the hono logger middleware
acceptance criteria:

1. Cross-module class setter dispatch.

   hono's `set res(_res) { …; this.#res = _res; this.finalized = true;
   }` was never invoked. `c.res = response` from inside compose's
   `await handler(c, next)` chain stored the response into a regular
   field slot but never ran the setter body — `this.finalized = true`
   never executed, hono-base's `if (!context.finalized) throw` fired on
   every request. Perry had `js_register_class_getter` + a getter
   dispatch arm in `js_object_get_field_by_name` (v0.5.620), but no
   parallel setter mechanism — `js_object_set_field_by_name` only ever
   did direct field writes.

   Three changes:
   - `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs`: add `setters: HashMap<String,
     usize>` to `ClassVTable`; new `js_register_class_setter` runtime
     FFI; setter dispatch arm in `js_object_set_field_by_name` walks
     class→parent chain (32 levels) and invokes setter as
     `fn(this_f64, value_f64)` BEFORE the field-write logic per JS spec.
   - `crates/perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls.rs`: declare new FFI.
   - `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen.rs`: parallel setter_pairs
     registration loop after the existing getter_pairs loop. Mangling
     matches setter-method-emission at codegen.rs:2041
     (`renamed.name = "__set_<prop>"`).

2. Arrow & fn-expr default-parameter desugar.

   `(fn = console.log) => fn(out)` had its `default: Some(<expr>)`
   recorded on `Param` but the actual `if (p === undefined) p =
   <default>` desugar was never injected into the closure body. The
   desugar (`build_default_param_stmts` in `crates/perry-hir/src/
   lower_decl.rs`) ran for top-level function declarations,
   constructors, and class methods, but `lower_arrow` and
   `lower_fn_expr` in `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_function.rs`
   skipped it entirely.

   So `myFn()` (no args) called the body which invoked `LocalGet(fn_id)`
   directly — the slot held undefined (caller padded missing args with
   TAG_UNDEFINED) and `js_closure_callN(undefined, …)` no-op'd.

   Fix: make `build_default_param_stmts` `pub(crate)` and call from
   both lowering sites with the same `default_stmts.append(&mut body)`
   pattern as `lower_fn_decl`.

fix(transform+codegen): closes #536 — try { return X } finally { Y } now runs Y; break/continue too (v0.5.675)

New HIR-level pass `inline_finally_into_returns` (`crates/perry-transform/src/finally_inline.rs`)
runs before the async-to-generator transform. For each enclosing
`try { ... } finally { Y }`, every nested abrupt completion (`return` / `break` /
`continue` / labeled-break / labeled-continue) inside body or catch is rewritten
to inline a clone of `Y` (and every outer enclosing finally that the abrupt
completion would skip past, innermost→outermost) immediately before the
abrupt-completion stmt.

Pre-fix, the codegen `lower_try` only branched to `finally_label` when the body
block wasn't already terminated — `Stmt::Return` / `Stmt::Break` etc. terminate
first, so the branch was never emitted and finally was unreachable. The
async-to-generator transform separately appended the finally body AFTER a
yielded body's last state, where the user's `return` had already terminated.
The new HIR pass handles both layers in one place.

The `Return(Some(X))` arm hoists `X` into a fresh `let __finally_ret_<id> = X`
BEFORE inlining the finally — non-negotiable for `return await foo()` because
otherwise the finally would run before the await suspends. `break`/`continue`
only inline finallies for trys INSIDE the loop being escaped (tracks
`loop_depth_at_push` per frame + label→loop-depth map for labeled escapes).
The original `Stmt::Try { finally }` is preserved unchanged so non-abrupt-
completion paths still run finally and the throw path keeps using the existing
setjmp/longjmp lowering.

String-aliasing follow-up: the `let __finally_ret_<id> = X` hoist exposed a
latent in-place-mutation bug — when `X` is `LocalGet` of a string-typed local,
refcount stayed at 1 and a subsequent `x = x + suffix` mutated the buffer
`__finally_ret_<id>` still pointed at. `Stmt::Let` in `crates/perry-codegen/src/stmt.rs`
now emits `js_string_addref` on the loaded value when init is `LocalGet` of a
string-typed local (declared in `runtime_decls.rs`).

End-to-end: original `@perryts/mysql` repro (`new Pool({url}); await pool.query(...);
console.log(rows); await pool.end()`) now exits 0 (was: hung after printing rows
because `release(conn)` from pool.query's finally never ran, pool stayed at
`idle: 0`, pool.end found nothing to close). Realistic flow (sequential +
transaction + concurrent Promise.all + pool.end) all clean. Sync `try { return
inner() } finally { ... }` ordering matches Node byte-for-byte. Break/continue
nested labeled break + continue outer + plain break only escaping inner loop
all match Node.

because byte 0 of the LE f64 of 47.0 ('/') is 0; for-of yielded

bytes of f64(116.0)).

All four phases of #577 ship end-to-end against curl + websocat:

Phase 1 — node:http: idiomatic
  import { createServer } from "node:http"
  createServer((req, res) => {
    if (req.method === "POST") {
      let chunks: string[] = []
      req.on("data", c => chunks.push(c))
      req.on("end", () => { res.statusCode = 200; res.end("got:" + chunks.join("")) })

fix(compile): closes #589 — link `perry-ext-fetch` when `node:http` strips `http-client` (v0.5.694)

When `import { createServer } from "node:http"` triggers the well-known flip
to perry-ext-http, perry-stdlib's `http-client` feature gets stripped — but
perry-ext-http only ships HTTP client + server symbols, not the Web Fetch
ctors (`js_headers_new` / `js_response_new` / `js_request_new`). hono's
compiled output (and any code that calls `new Headers()` / `new Request()` /
`new Response()`) needs those symbols, which live in perry-ext-fetch.

The HIR already detects Web Fetch ctor usage and flips `ctx.uses_fetch = true`
(see `crates/perry-hir/src/destructuring.rs:1466-1546`). This commit threads
that signal through the well-known iteration: when `uses_fetch=true` and
neither `'fetch'` nor `'node-fetch'` is in the user's imports, synthetically
add `"fetch"` to the iteration set so perry-ext-fetch gets pulled in alongside
perry-ext-http.

The `'fetch'` binding strips no perry-stdlib feature, and perry-ext-fetch's
exports (`js_headers_*` / `js_response_*` / `js_request_*` / `js_fetch_*`) are
disjoint from perry-ext-http's (`js_http_*` / `js_node_http_*`), so this is a
pure-add — no duplicate-symbol risk.

fix(hir): closes #588 — `export { foo }` separately for function decls now propagates param-count to importers (v0.5.695)

`function drizzle(...) {}` followed by `export { drizzle }` (the npm-bundled
shape used by drizzle-orm/pg-proxy/driver.js, hono, and many others) was
lowered with `is_exported = false` and never landed in
`module.exported_functions`. Cross-module callers fell back to `args.len()`
in `lower_call.rs:767` for both the target arity AND the LLVM declare
signature. ABI mismatch on AArch64: source body's trailing default-defaulted
params read d1/d2 stale register state, the `if (p === undefined) p =
default` desugar never fires (the value is `f64::from_bits(small_int)` ≈
1.26e-321 — a class id of an earlier inline op — not TAG_UNDEFINED), and
the call returns garbage.

Reproduced on real drizzle-orm 0.45.2:
`function drizzle(callback, config = {}, _dialect = () => new
PgDialect({ casing: config.casing }))` called with 1 arg → `_dialect = 1.26e-321`,
`db.dialect = undefined`, downstream chain fails. Bisected to a 7-line
minimal: `function drizzle(cb, config={}, _factory=()=>42); export {
drizzle };` triggers the bug; same code with `export function
drizzle(...)` (export-decl form) does not.

Fix in `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs::lower_module_decl` ExportNamed arm
(the `export { name }` form): parallel of the class arm at line 4421
(itself a fix from #482 / v0.5.577 for the analogous class case). When
the export specifier names a function decl, flip `func.is_exported = true`
AND push `(exported_name, func_id)` to `module.exported_functions` (deduped
against existing entries from rename forms). The CLI driver's
`exported_func_param_counts` lookup at `compile.rs:1907` filters on
`func.is_exported` and the fallback at `compile.rs:1921` iterates only
`exported_functions` — both now find the function. Importer's
`imported_func_param_counts.get("drizzle")` returns `Some(3)`,
`lower_call.rs:767` declares `f64(f64,f64,f64)`, pads missing trailing
args with TAG_UNDEFINED, and the body's default-param desugar fires.

End-to-end: minimal repro now prints `_factory typeof= function`, `dialect=
42`. Real drizzle-orm 0.45.2 returns a PgDialect instance from
`db.dialect`. Refs #488 (drizzle compile path) — the issue's
separately-mentioned link-fail variant (undefined
`_node_modules_repro_pkg2_dialect_js__PgDialect_constructor`) was the same
root cause surfacing through the closure body — same fix unblocks both.

fix(ext-fetch+hir): closes #589 — runtime path for hono+node:http acceptance (v0.5.696)

Builds on v0.5.694's link-gap fix to make the issue's full acceptance criterion pass.
With v0.5.694, perry-ext-fetch was getting linked alongside perry-ext-http when
`node:http` strips `http-client` — but its `js_response_new` had drifted from
perry-stdlib's, and `r.headers.forEach` got array-method-folded in HIR.

Three coordinated changes:

1. **ABI signature alignment** (`crates/perry-ext-fetch/src/lib.rs`): five FFI
   exports declared `i64` handle when codegen emits DOUBLE — the call site put
   the handle in d0, the function read x0 and got register garbage. Flipped
   `js_fetch_response_status` / `_status_text` / `_ok` / `_text` / `_json` to
   `f64`, routing through a new `handle_id` helper that mirrors perry-stdlib's
   (accepts both NaN-boxed POINTER_TAG and legacy raw-float handles).

2. **Constructor arity**: `js_response_new` and `js_request_new` were 3-arg
   while perry-stdlib's are 4-arg with trailing `headers_handle: f64`.
   Codegen always emits the 4-arg call; the 4th arg silently dropped, so
   `new Response(body, { headers: { ... } })` produced an empty headers map.
   Added the `headers_handle: f64` param to both; `js_response_new` resolves it
   via `handle_id` → `HEADERS_HANDLES.get` and clones the map onto the
   FetchResponse. Bonus: added `js_headers_keys` / `_values` / `_entries`
   (perry-stdlib added them in v0.5.665 #576 but ext-fetch hadn't tracked) and
   made `js_headers_for_each` sort by header name per the WHATWG Fetch spec.

3. **HIR: array-method fold guard** (`crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call.rs`):
   `r.headers.forEach(cb)` lowered to `Expr::ArrayForEach { array: NativeMethodCall { method: "headers" }, ... }`
   because the array-method catch-all at line 4096 only bailed for `this.<field>`
   shapes. Codegen then dispatched `js_array_forEach` against a Headers handle
   (an integer registry id, not an ArrayHeader pointer) — iteration silently
   no-op'd. Added a parallel arm: when `inner.obj` is a Response/Request/
   Headers native instance AND `inner.prop == "headers"`, set `recv_is_class = true`
   so the fold bails. The chained-Web-Fetch dispatch in
   `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs:1313` then routes the call through
   the Headers FFI.

End-to-end: issue's repro returns `HTTP/1.1 200 OK / {"ok":true}` byte-for-byte;
hono_alone, test_node_http_basic, and test_node_http_post_body all unchanged.

fix(runtime+codegen): closes #590 — `Object.assign` preserves identity, class_id, and Symbol-keyed properties (v0.5.697)

Pre-fix the HIR lowering folded EVERY `Object.assign(target, ...sources)` shape
into `Expr::ObjectSpread { parts }` with target as the first spread part.
Codegen for ObjectSpread allocates a FRESH ObjectHeader and copies own
string-keyed fields — dropping (a) class_id (so `instanceof` flips false),
(b) the SYMBOL_PROPERTIES side-table entries (the table is keyed by raw
object pointer; the new header is a different pointer with no entries),
and (c) object identity (`Object.assign` per spec returns target; the
fresh-allocation path returned a different pointer).

drizzle-orm's `pg-core/table.js:42-53` chain
`Object.assign(rawTable, builtCols); table[Sym.Columns] = builtCols;
Object.assign(table, { enableRLS })` saw both Symbol writes silently
dropped, and `dialect.buildInsertQuery` then SIGSEGV'd in
`js_object_entries(undefined)`.

Three layers:

(1) Runtime helper `js_object_assign_one(target, source) -> target`
    in `crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs`: mutates target with each
    of source's own enumerable string-keyed AND Symbol-keyed properties,
    returns target unchanged. String copy mirrors `js_object_copy_own_fields`;
    Symbol copy snapshots `SYMBOL_PROPERTIES.get(src)` via the new
    `pub(crate) clone_symbol_entries_for_obj_ptr` helper in symbol.rs
    (clone-then-iterate is non-negotiable — the inner
    `js_object_set_symbol_property` re-acquires the same Mutex; holding
    the lock across the iteration would deadlock).

(2) HIR variant `Expr::ObjectAssign { target, sources }` in ir.rs,
    distinct from `ObjectSpread` because the spec semantics differ
    (mutate-and-return vs allocate-and-return). Walker arms walk
    target + each source.

(3) HIR lowering in `lower/expr_call.rs::lower_call` — `Object.assign(t, ...s)`
    now produces `Expr::ObjectAssign`. Fast paths preserved:
    `Object.assign()` (zero args) → empty Object literal;
    `Object.assign({}, ...sources)` (empty literal target) keeps the
    OLD ObjectSpread path because there's no pre-existing identity /
    class_id / Symbol state to preserve.

(4) Codegen in `expr.rs::Expr::ObjectAssign` chains
    `js_object_assign_one(target, src1) → ... → src_N` so target is
    evaluated exactly once. Zero-source case returns target directly.

End-to-end: issue's repro matches bun byte-for-byte; the load-bearing
drizzle shape now satisfies `result === table: true` AND `result[Sym]`
returns the columns map. Class_id side-bug
(`Object.assign(t, { extra: 1 }) instanceof PgTable` was false) fixed
in the same pass. Edge cases: multiple sources with later-wins, null /
undefined sources skipped, single-arg form (`Object.assign(f) === f`),
Symbol-keyed source props copied to target — all match bun.

Two bug-fixes the live release sweep surfaced:

1. tier 1 (cargo_workspace) crashed on `0\n0: syntax error in expression`.
   Root cause: `total_passed=$(grep -cE PATTERN "$LOG" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)`
   yields multi-line output ("0\n0") in the no-match case because grep
   prints "0" AND echo prints "0". The downstream
   `$((total_passed + total_failed))` then aborts. Fix: capture without
   the inline `|| echo 0` cascade; validate integer with =~ ^[0-9]+$ and
   default to 0 otherwise.

   axios's http agent that keeps perry's event loop pinned. Without a
   timeout in fixture_compile_run_diff, this hung the entire sweep until
   I killed ./out by hand. Fix: added _fixture_run_with_timeout helper
   (uses GNU timeout / gtimeout when present, pure-bash fallback
   otherwise) with PERRY_FIXTURE_TIMEOUT_SECS=60 default. A 124-coded
   timeout exit emits a clear "did not exit within Ns (likely a hang)"
   message.

fix(stdlib+codegen+runtime): closes #591 — argon2.hash() reaches FFI, await chain runs to completion (v0.5.699)

Three coordinated layers:

1. FFI ABI: NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE entries for argon2.hash / argon2.verify /
   bcrypt.hash / bcrypt.compare flipped from NA_F64 to NA_STR. The runtime
   fns expect *const StringHeader (i64 ptr) but NA_F64 passed the NaN-boxed
   f64 in d0 while the callee read x0 — the StringHeader pointer was stale
   register bits, surfacing as the issue's "Invalid password" error.

2. Active-handle gate for spawn_blocking: new EXT_BLOCKING_TASKS_INFLIGHT
   counter in async_bridge.rs is incremented in perry_ffi_spawn_blocking[
   _with_reactor] and decremented when the closure returns. Without this,
   the codegen-emitted event-loop header check exited the loop before the
   tokio worker queued its Promise resolution.

3. Microtask-pending gate: new js_microtasks_pending() runtime FFI exposes
   TASK_QUEUE.is_empty() to the codegen-emitted event loop's header check.
   Without this, the resolution chain queued the .then continuation INSIDE
   js_run_stdlib_pump but the next header check saw inflight=0 +
   PENDING_RESOLUTIONS=0 and exited before the next body's microtask drain.

   contains an Arrow/Fn descendant (Call wrapping Arrow, Object wrapping
   Arrow, Array wrapping Arrow, …). New ast_expr_contains_function_expr
   walker covers Call/New/Member/Object/Array/Bin/Unary/Cond/Paren/TsAs/
   TsNonNull/TsTypeAssertion/TsSatisfies/Assign/Seq/Tpl/TaggedTpl/OptChain.

2. Boxing analysis: collect_self_recursive_closure_ids only flagged
   direct-closure-literal inits. New init_expr_has_self_capturing_closure
   helper walks the init for any Expr::Closure descendant and checks
   whether its body refs the let's id; on hit the let is boxed.

fix(transform): closes #594 — generator-transform return-rewrite recurses into nested control flow (v0.5.701)

The async-to-generator transform's StateExit::Done arm had two
top-level-only passes that broke when a user `return X` lived inside
an `if` / `try` / etc. inside a state body:

1. prepend-`done = true`-before-return walked only top-level stmts —
   nested Return slipped through, __gen_done stayed false, iterator
   caller re-entered the same state.
2. rewrite_returns_as_done likewise top-level-only — nested Return(X)
   survived as bare value, iterator caller's __step_r = X plain value,
   __step_r.done threw "Cannot read properties of undefined".

Three coordinated changes:
- rewrite_returns_as_done now recurses through If/While/DoWhile/For/Try
  (body+catch+finally)/Switch/Labeled.
- New prepend_done_before_returns walker mirrors the recursion and
  replaces the prior top-level-only loop.
- New body_contains_return recursive scanner replaces the prior
  top-level any-matches check, plus a fall-through default tail when
  the last stmt isn't unconditionally a Return.

End-to-end: try { await x } catch {} ; if (cond) return X — works.

fix(runtime): closes #596 — TypeError throw helpers route through js_throw (v0.5.702)

js_throw_type_error_property_access (property access on undefined/null,
#462) and js_throw_type_error_not_a_function (X is not a function, #510)
both bypassed setjmp/longjmp exception machinery — each printed the
V8-shaped diagnostic to stderr and called std::process::exit(1),
so the user's surrounding try/catch had no chance to fire.

fix(hir): closes #597 — arr.entries()/.keys()/.values() fold on any-typed receivers (v0.5.703)

The HIR array-method fold had a static-type-Array path for entries/keys/
values but the dynamic catch-all only covered reduce/map/filter/forEach/
find/etc. So `function f(arr: any) { for (const [i,v] of arr.entries())
... }` fell through to a generic js_native_call_method dispatch — the
returned object's .length was undefined and the for-of's index-loop

fix(stdlib+axios+codegen): closes #598 — axios.post body NaN-box-aware (v0.5.704)

axios.post(url, {a: 1}) sent the raw bytes of Perry's ObjectHeader
struct because the FFI declared the body as `*const StringHeader`,
the codegen unboxed the caller's NaN-boxed value to i64, and the
runtime read those bytes as a StringHeader (length + refcount + data
prefix) — server received `^@^B^@^@H...` instead of `{"a":1}`.

Three coordinated layers mirroring npm axios's body-encoding rule:

1. FFI signature: post/put/patch's body arg flipped from
   *const StringHeader to f64 (NaN-boxed JsValue) in both
   perry-ext-axios and perry-stdlib's axios.rs.
2. Body-encoding routing: new read_body_as_string /
   body_string_from_value helper decodes the NaN-box tag — strings
   pass through as-is, undefined/null → empty, everything else →
   js_json_stringify. Stringification runs on the main thread before
   the spawn boundary (avoids wrong-arena access).
3. Codegen dispatch + runtime decl: lower_call.rs passes the body as
   (DOUBLE, &body_box) instead of unboxing; runtime_decls.rs declares
   js_axios_post/put/patch as (I64, DOUBLE) instead of (I64, I64).

arrives as proper JSON, pre-stringified body passes through.

fix(runtime): closes #609 — Buffer.toString('utf8') no longer SIGSEGV's on invalid UTF-8 (v0.5.732)

because its `isBufferLike` duck-test (`typeof anyV.readUInt8 === 'function'`)
returns false in Perry. `String(buf)` → `buf.toString()` →
`js_buffer_to_string(buf, 0)` → `js_string_from_bytes(data, len)` →
`compute_utf16_len(data, len)`, where `str::from_utf8_unchecked` (UB on
non-UTF-8) plus `.encode_utf16().count()` walked the resulting `chars()`
iterator past the slice end into unmapped memory.

    for invalid sequences before storing. Matches Node's documented
    `Buffer.toString('utf8')` replacement-char behavior.

(2) string.rs — `compute_utf16_len` swaps `str::from_utf8_unchecked`
    for safe `str::from_utf8`, falling back to the existing
    `compute_utf16_len_wtf8` byte-walking counter on invalid input.
    Defense in depth: any future caller that hands `js_string_from_bytes`
    invalid bytes no longer triggers UB.

fix(regex): refs #637 — RegExp.source/flags GC-survival + PIC false-hit on non-Object headers (v0.5.733)

Two coordinated fixes that unblock the hono RegExpRouter compile path. Bisected
from `app.get("/users/:id", h); app.fetch(req)` returning 404 with `matcher[0]`
appearing as a non-RegExp object whose `.source = 0`.

(1) RegExp .source / .flags GC-survival across function boundaries
    (crates/perry-runtime/src/regex.rs)

    Pre-fix js_regexp_get_source/flags read (*re).pattern_ptr / .flags_ptr —
    raw *const StringHeader pointers stored at construction time. When the
    input pattern was a temporary (template-literal `^${p}` whose result has
    no live root past function return), GC freed the StringHeader and reads
    dereferenced dangling memory; .source returned 0.

    Repro: function f(): any { return new RegExp(`^${p}`); }
           const r = f(); r.source  // 0 in Perry, "^/users/(.+)" in Node

    Fix: thread-local REGEX_SOURCE_TABLE keyed by RegExpHeader pointer stores
    OWNED String copies of pattern + flags at js_regexp_new time. Readers
    prefer the side-table; legacy pointer path is the defensive fallback.

(2) PIC false-hit on non-Object GC_TYPE_OBJECT headers
    (crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs)

    Pre-fix the property-get inline cache fast path checked `gc_type ==
    GC_TYPE_OBJECT (=2)` to validate the receiver, but RegExpHeader /
    PromiseHeader / MapHeader / SetHeader / TypedArrayHeader / ... all share
    that gc_type. The PIC compared obj+16 (DOUBLE) — keys_array on
    ObjectHeader, flags_ptr on RegExpHeader — against cache[0]. Both null
    flags_ptr=0 and uninitialized cache[0]=0 matched, the hit path loaded
    obj+24+slot*8 (case_insensitive byte + 7 padding bytes interpreted as
    f64), and returned a near-zero garbage value instead of routing through
    js_regexp_get_source.

    Fix: third gate on the is_object predicate — load *(u32*)obj at offset
    0 and require it equal OBJECT_TYPE_REGULAR (=1). Real ObjectHeaders
    have this field set to 1 by allocation; non-Object headers' offset 0

perf(runtime): bigint small-int fast path (v0.5.736)

BigInt arithmetic on the i64-fits-in-host-word common case now goes
through native i128 ops instead of the schoolbook 16x16 multiply
loop. Surfaced by aya_koto's article (https://zenn.dev/aya_koto/
articles/553ce04b1d5ac4) where a reader's footnote claimed BigInt
was ~4x slower than Bun; actual measurement was much worse —
factorial(20) timed out at >30s vs Bun's 13ms, factorial(50)*1000
never completed.

Three coordinated changes in crates/perry-runtime/src/bigint.rs;
struct layout unchanged so perry-ffi consumers (read_bigint_limbs,
ext-ethers, jsruntime, thread.rs) keep working:

(1) Removed compiler-defeating instrumentation. Five
std::hint::black_box(...) sites in js_bigint_mul, two in
js_bigint_cmp, four in js_bigint_mod were preventing LLVM from
constant-folding / hoisting / vectorizing inner loops. No comment
indicated they were intentional. #[inline(never)] also stripped
from arithmetic ops so LLVM can inline trivial cases at intra-crate
call sites.

(2) Small-int fast path. New fits_in_i64 helper recognizes any
1024-bit two's-complement value that fits in a host i64. When BOTH
operands fit, mul/add/sub/div/mod/cmp use native i128 arithmetic
and write back via new write_i128 helper. i64*i64 fits exactly in
i128 (max=2^126<2^127), so 256 word multiplies become one CPU mul
for the common case.

(3) Multiplication slow-path early-exit. New effective_limb_len
walks limbs from the high end skipping consecutive sign-extension
fill (zeros for positive, u64::MAX for negative). Mul iterates
only a_len * b_len word multiplies. A 100-bit * 100-bit multiply
does ~16 word multiplies instead of 256.

Tests: 8 new fast-path unit tests added (sign grid for mul/add/
sub, factorial(20) all-fast-path, factorial(21) mid-loop slow-path
promotion, ECMAScript spec compliance for `%` sign-of-dividend
and `/` truncate-toward-zero, i64 boundary). 18 bigint tests pass;
225-test perry-runtime suite passes; test_gap_bigint.ts byte-
identical to Node.

Bench results on Apple M-series:
  factorial(20) one-shot:   Perry 6.2ms vs Bun 13.5ms (Perry 2.18x faster)
  factorial(30)*100:        Perry 5.9ms vs Bun 14.2ms (2.40x faster)
  factorial(50)*1000:       Perry 10.3ms vs Bun 15.7ms (1.52x faster)

Pre-fix Perry didn't complete any of these in 30s.

Out of scope: i++ on a bigint local doesn't increment (separate
codegen bug — the body runs forever with i stuck). Workaround:
write i = i + 1n until the codegen fix lands. ABC451D from the
article (no BigInt) is unchanged at ~3s; that bench is GC-bound
on string[] allocation pressure, separate fix in progress.

perf(gc): merge ValidPointerSet regions, range-prefilter contains

The conservative-stack-scan validator previously kept arena-allocated
and gc_malloc'd pointers in two separate sorted Vecs and ran TWO
binary searches per `contains()` call. On allocation-heavy workloads
where the mark phase calls `contains()` millions of times per cycle
(deep recursion holding many string/array refs on stack frames),
that's measurable.

Three structural changes in crates/perry-runtime/src/gc.rs:

(1) Single merged sorted vec. `finalize()` does a one-pass O(n)
    merge of the two pre-sorted regions into `merged_sorted`.
    `contains()` now does ONE binary search instead of two.
    `enclosing_object()` (interior-pointer fallback for `js_array_
    reduce`-style derived pointers) uses the same vec — no longer
    needs to find_floor in both regions and pick the larger.

(2) Range-rejection prefilter. `range_min`/`range_max` are
    populated in `finalize()` from the merged vec's first/last
    entries. `maybe_contains()` does a single `ptr in [min, max]`
    test before falling through to the binary search. Helps the
    raw-pointer-fallback path in `try_mark_value_or_raw` where
    stack words may legitimately be return addresses or plain
    integers outside the heap range.

(3) `try_mark_value` now `#[inline]` + tag-rejection cascade
    moved before the pointer-extract. Stripped `_or` glue that
    was preventing LLVM from short-circuiting the early non-heap
    case in callers.

Bench results on Apple M-series:

  ABC451D (the aya_koto bench):
    pre  3.073 ± 0.040 s
    post 3.205 ± 0.295 s
    Wash on this bench. ABC451D is bottlenecked deeper than
    contains() — sweep finds 57% of objects dead but
    block_reclaim=0 because live refs are scattered across every
    block, so the arena keeps growing monotonically through the
    run (61 → 270+ blocks). The mark phase itself is doing what
    it should; the sweep can't translate it into reclaim.

  perry-runtime test suite: 225 passed, 0 failed.
  test_gap_bigint: byte-identical to Node.

Out of scope for this change (separate, bigger fixes):

  - The arena-can't-recycle-fragmented-blocks problem in ABC451D.
    Two paths exist (push-to-free-list during sweep with smarter
    free-list lookup; or evacuating semispace collector). The
    existing PERRY_GEN_GC_EVACUATE=1 mode tested 4x slower on
    ABC451D, so the evacuation pass needs its own tuning before
    flipping default-on.
  - Allocation sinking at the codegen level (escape analysis for
    return-only-allocation patterns like the recursive search()
    in ABC451D).

These are filed as follow-ups. The merged_sorted change here is
behavior-neutral structural cleanup; ships value on workloads with
high contains() call rates (perf-comprehensive ECS, hono compose
chain) without the small/contained risk profile of the deeper GC
work.

fix(codegen): refs #420 #631 — intermediate-class field inits run after parent body (v0.5.741)

4-level inheritance with intermediate-class field initializers
depending on parent body state previously broke. Drizzle's
`SQLiteInteger ← SQLiteBaseInteger ← SQLiteColumn ← Column` shape:

    class Column { ctor sets this.config }
    class SQLiteColumn extends Column { ctor: super(...) }
    class SQLiteBaseInteger extends SQLiteColumn {
        autoIncrement = this.config.autoIncrement;
    }
    class SQLiteInteger extends SQLiteBaseInteger { ... }

Pre-fix `new SQLiteInteger(...)` threw `TypeError: Cannot read
properties of undefined (reading 'autoIncrement')` because Perry's
`FieldInitMode::AncestorsOnly` ran ALL ancestor fields up-front
BEFORE any body chain executed. SQLiteBaseInteger's `autoIncrement
= this.config.autoIncrement` ran with `this.config` still undefined.

Per ECMAScript spec, each derived class's field inits run AFTER its
super() returns. Only the root class can safely run fields pre-body
(no super to wait for).

Three coordinated changes:

(1) Two new FieldInitMode variants in lower_call.rs:
    - UpToInclusive(stop_at): chain[0..=index_of(stop_at)]
    - BetweenExclusiveTo(stop_at): chain[index_of(stop_at)+1..]

(2) AncestorsOnly tightened to keep ONLY the root class (chain[0]).
    Intermediate-class fields now run via SuperCall.

(3) Expr::SuperCall post-body intermediate walk: after the inlined
    parent body returns, walk from current_class.extends_name UP to
    (but excluding) effective_parent_name and apply each
    intermediate's SelfOnly in root-most-first order. Mirrors what
    each intermediate's default ctor (`constructor(...args) {
    super(...args); /* fields */ }`) does in JS.

(4) lower_new no-own-ctor path uses UpToInclusive(inherited_ctor)
    pre-body + BetweenExclusiveTo(inherited_ctor) post-body.

End-to-end: drizzle-sqlite's `entry.ts` progresses past the
autoIncrement TypeError. Hono entry.ts unchanged (r1=200, r2=200,
r3=404). New regression test test_field_init_4level_chain.ts.

fix(runtime): refs #420 #618 — instance.constructor returns class ref (v0.5.746)

Pre-fix `instance.constructor` returned undefined because the keys_array
lookup never finds "constructor" (the class isn't stored as a field on
the instance) and the chain returned undefined. Drizzle's `is(value, type)`
uses `value.constructor[entityKind]` to identify class types; without
.constructor working the entire entity-kind dispatch returns false.

Fix: added a "constructor" key intercept in js_object_get_field_by_name
(in crates/perry-runtime/src/object.rs) that fires AFTER the type-tag
bailouts but BEFORE the keys_array lookup. Reads (*obj).class_id; if
non-zero AND registered (consults v0.5.745's is_class_id_registered
helper), returns the INT32-tagged class ref (0x7FFE_0000_0000_0000 |
class_id).

Pure object literals (class_id=0) and unregistered class refs still
return undefined — matches Node behavior where bare object literals
don't have a custom .constructor.

Repro: `class SQL {}; const s = new SQL(); typeof s.constructor`
returns "function" and `s.constructor === SQL` is true (was:
"undefined" and false).

`is(new Aliased(), Aliased)` and false for `is(new Aliased(), SQL)`.

perf(transform): interprocedural deforestation — ABC451D 4.16x faster (v0.5.747)

Detects the producer/consumer fusion shape — a function that allocates
a fresh array, fills it via `out.push(...)`, and returns it (possibly
with recursive self-calls whose results are spliced via the canonical
`for(j) out.push(child[j])` consume loop) — and rewrites it to take an
accumulator out-parameter, fusing each call site so the producer writes
directly into the caller's array.

End-to-end on aya_koto's ABC451D bench (the Zenn article's "Perry is
6.5x slower than Bun" complaint, originally diagnosed in v0.5.736 as
GC-throughput-bound on string[] allocation pressure with no
single-commit fix): Perry drops from 3165 ms → 760 ms (4.16x faster),
within 1.75x of Bun (411 ms) — was 7.3x slower pre-fix. The transform
fires INSIDE the recursive search() call: each call's intermediate
`child` array is eliminated, so a previously O(N) array-allocation
chain collapses to O(1).

Three coordinated guards keep the rewrite sound (initial impl broke 4
of 8 affected tests until they landed):
  (a) skip exported functions — their callers may live in other modules
      this intra-module pass can't see;
  (b) skip producers whose body contains any closure expression — the
      safe-pattern analyzer doesn't walk closure bodies, so a
      forEach((x) => out.push(x)) would slip past detection but break
      at substitution time;
  (c) skip producers whose calls appear in expression positions
      (f(args).join(","), someFn(f(args)), return f(args)) — the
      rewritten producer returns undefined, so any caller using the
      return as a value would silently break.

Detection: per-function shape analysis + producer-as-value detection
(bail if Expr::FuncRef(f) ever appears in non-callee position) +
call-site shape verification. Transformation: subst LocalGet(out_local)
→ LocalGet(out_param) everywhere including HIR variants with direct
LocalId fields (ArrayPush.array_id, ArrayPushSpread.array_id, etc.,
which are not Expr children and would be missed by the generic walker).
Runs BEFORE inline_functions so the inliner sees rewritten signatures.

Scope: intra-module only. Cross-module deforestation needs whole-program
analysis or a wrapper-shim layer that preserves the original signature
for external callers — separate followup.

5 unit tests cover detection rejection paths (async / multi-return /
reassignment / out-passed-to-call). Detection fires on 8 functions
across the test-files corpus; all 8 affected tests + 12 sanity tests +
27/28 gap tests pass byte-identical to Node. The 1 failure
(test_gap_console_methods) is a pre-existing timing-sensitive
console.time divergence unrelated to deforestation.

Stretch goal of 1.5 s on ABC451D not hit. Bun's V8 also gets escape
analysis for the `before + after` intermediate string allocations,
which Perry's intra-function escape analysis already handles for
object literals but not strings yet — the remaining Bun gap is now
string-allocation-side, not array-allocation-side.

fix(codegen,runtime): refs #420 #618 — static field access via Any-typed local (v0.5.748)

Pre-fix `const X: any = A; X.kind` returned `undefined` because the
codegen's PIC fast path treated INT32-tagged class refs (top16=0x7FFE)
as non-pointer values and routed to the invalid arm. Drizzle's
`is(value, type)` chain reads `cls.kind` through Any-typed locals;
without this fix the entire entity-kind dispatch returns the wrong
answer.

Three coordinated layers:

1. Codegen PIC arm in expr.rs::Expr::PropertyGet adds an `is_int32_class`
   check (top16 == 0x7FFE) that BEFORE the existing pointer-validity
   arm routes through `js_object_get_field_by_name_f64` with the
   unmasked `obj_bits` so the runtime can detect the INT32 tag.

2. Runtime helper `js_class_register_static_field(class_id, name_ptr,
   name_len, value)` in object.rs populates `CLASS_DYNAMIC_PROPS` so
   static-field lookups via the runtime path find the value. Codegen
   calls this from Expr::StaticFieldSet lowering for every initializer
   in addition to writing the per-field module global.

3. Synthetic `constructor` intercept in `js_object_get_field_by_name`
   returns the class ref for an instance receiver (reads
   `(*obj).class_id` and returns the INT32-tagged ref if registered).

Repro: `class A { static kind = "A" } const X: any = A; X.kind` returns
"A" matching Node (was undefined).

The IC-miss-side parallel intercept was tried but reverted — small
handle ids from native modules (axios / fastify / fetch handles)
numerically collide with class_ids, and the runtime can't distinguish

fix(transform): closes #617 — inline await of fetchWithAuth/fetchPostWithAuth (v0.5.749)

`await fetchWithAuth(url, auth)` (and the POST variant) inline returned
`undefined`; the explicit two-step `let p = fetchWithAuth(...); await p;`
produced the resolved Response.

The two HIR shapes only diverged in where the fetch call landed: the
inline form lowered to `Stmt::Let { init: Some(Await(FetchGetWithAuth)) }`,
which the async-to-generator transform rewrote to `Yield { value:
FetchGetWithAuth }`. The generator state-machine transform planted that
whole expression as the `value` field of the iter-result object literal
— so `js_fetch_get_with_auth` was invoked while the `{value, done}`
object was still being constructed. The two-step form lowered to
`LocalSet(p, FetchGetWithAuth); Yield { value: LocalGet(p) }` — the
promise lands in a stack slot first and the iter-result reads it back
via a plain `LocalGet`.

Per the user's diagnostic the resolved value never reached the await
driver: the promise pointer that `js_fetch_get_with_auth` queued
(`result_bits = 0x7ffd000000000002`) was correct, but the bits flowing
through `js_value_is_promise` (called from `js_promise_resolved` inside
the async-step driver's `Promise.resolve(r.value).then(...)` chain)
were `TAG_UNDEFINED` and `0x0` — i.e. `r.value` read back as the
iter-result object's pre-init `JSValue::undefined()` slot fill from
`js_object_alloc_with_shape`.

Mechanizes the user's verified workaround at the HIR level: in
`crates/perry-transform/src/async_to_generator.rs`, both
`hoist_awaits_avoiding_top_level` (statement-positioned awaits like
`let response = await fetchWithAuth(...)`) and `hoist_awaits_in_expr_full`
(nested-position awaits) now also hoist `Expr::FetchGetWithAuth` /
`Expr::FetchPostWithAuth` operands out of the await via the new helper
`hoist_fetch_with_auth_inside_await`. The generator transform then sees
`Yield { value: LocalGet(__await_fetch_N) }` instead of `Yield { value:
FetchGetWithAuth }` — exactly the two-step path. Verified via
`--print-hir`.

Regression test in `test-files/test_issue_617_inline_await_fetch_with_auth.ts`
spins up a node:http echo server on 127.0.0.1:38617 and asserts both
inline and two-step forms of GET + POST resolve to a real Response with
status 200 — all four pass. 14 perry-transform unit tests pass; 10
async/promise/fetch parity tests match Node byte-for-byte. Sequence-point
semantics preserved (the temp's init runs in the same position the
inline call would have); the fix is a no-op for any await operand other
than the two fetch-with-auth built-ins.

fix(hir,codegen,runtime): refs #420 #618 — dynamic instanceof through function args (v0.5.750)

`value instanceof type` where `type` is a runtime expression (function
arg, local holding a class ref) now dispatches correctly. Pre-fix the
HIR captured `ty` as a static identifier name; when the right side was
a local var (e.g. `function is(value, type) { return value instanceof
type; }`), the lowering stored `ty = "type"` (the param name) and
codegen couldn't resolve it as a class id, falling through to cid=0 and
returning false for every dynamic instanceof.

Drizzle's `is(value, type)` chain depends on this.

Four coordinated layers:

1. HIR variant extension — added optional `ty_expr: Option<Box<Expr>>`
   field to `Expr::InstanceOf` in perry-hir/src/ir.rs, populated when
   the right-side identifier resolves to a local in scope.

2. Codegen dispatch in perry-codegen/src/expr.rs::Expr::InstanceOf —
   when ty_expr.is_some(), lowers the type expression as a runtime
   value and calls js_instanceof_dynamic(value, type_ref).

3. Runtime helper js_instanceof_dynamic in perry-runtime/src/object.rs
   — extracts class_id from the INT32 NaN-tag (top16=0x7FFE) and
   dispatches to js_instanceof. Returns FALSE for non-class-ref type
   values defensively.

4. Walker fix in perry-hir/src/walker.rs — extracted Expr::InstanceOf
   from the single-child group into its own arm that visits BOTH expr
   and ty_expr so the inliner / closure-conversion / monomorph
   substitution see both. Without this, inlined call sites had
   LocalGet(N) references inside ty_expr that never got substituted.

Repro: `function isType(value, type) { return value instanceof type; };
isType(new SQL(), SQL)` returns true matching Node (was false).

fix(runtime,codegen): refs #420 #618 — Object.getPrototypeOf for class refs walks parent chain (v0.5.751)

Pre-fix the codegen wrapper at expr.rs::Expr::ObjectGetPrototypeOf
returned the operand unchanged (passed `o` through lower_expr without
any transformation), so `cur = Object.getPrototypeOf(cur)` in a
while-loop walk produced cur===cur forever. Drizzle's `is(value, type)`
chain (which walks `value.constructor[entityKind]` up the prototype
chain) hung in an infinite loop on subclass dispatch.

1. Runtime helper js_object_get_prototype_of in object.rs — for
   INT32-tagged class refs (top16 == 0x7FFE), reads parent_class_id
   from CLASS_REGISTRY (already populated at module init via
   js_register_class_parent from codegen's parent-pairs loop) and
   returns the parent class ref as another INT32-tagged value, or null
   at the chain root. Non-class-ref receivers still return null.

2. Codegen wrapper updated to actually call the runtime helper with
   the operand value instead of passing through unchanged.

Repro: `class Base{}; class Mid extends Base{}; class Leaf extends Mid{};
let cur:any = Leaf; while (cur && cur.kind) { cur = Object.getPrototypeOf(cur); }`
terminates after Base (was hung).

fix(ui,transform,codegen): closes #612 #634 #635 — NavStack state-driven, for-loop children, Image(url) (v0.5.752)

#612 — NavStack(state, routes) rendered blank on iOS-sim and (once
tested with the issue's actual repro) on macOS too. Four layers:

    factories so the issue's `const route = State<string>("a")` is

  - iOS NavStack switched from UIStackView to plain UIView; the route
    bodies pin to fill via the existing zstack add_child arm.

literal-sibling row, and the Image probe builds and runs without

args, `(x as any)` casts) the static class wasn't recoverable so the

AND the getter walk, so field reads + accessor getters are unaffected.

fix(runtime): refs #gc-evac — recursive GC during evacuation corrupts state (v0.5.763)

Closes the long-standing soundness bug where `PERRY_GEN_GC_EVACUATE=1`
crashed every workload with sustained tenuring (bench_evac_heavy
SIGSEGVed every run, exit 139, no output).

Root cause: `evacuate_tenured_nursery_objects` calls `arena_alloc_gc_old`
to allocate the OLD-arena copy of each evacuating object.
`arena_alloc_gc_old → arena.alloc` calls `gc_check_trigger` on its slow
path (when the current OLD block is full), and `gc_check_trigger`'s
re-entrancy guard only blocks calls from inside `gc_malloc`'s
bookkeeping window — NOT calls from inside `gc_collect_minor` itself.

Result: a recursive `gc_collect_minor` fires DURING the outer cycle's
evacuation pass. The recursive cycle clobbers the outer's MARK_SEEDS,
CONS_PINNED, and valid_ptrs. Its mark_stack_roots runs from a deep
runtime stack frame (currently inside arena_alloc_gc_old) where the
user's locals aren't reachable conservatively, so user roots like
bench_evac_heavy's `cache` don't get pinned. The recursive cycle then
evacuates `cache` un-pinned, but the outer's rewrite walk doesn't run
for the recursive cycle's evacuations — the user's shadow stack slot
for `cache` still points at the now-FORWARDED nursery slot, and the
inline `cache.length` read pulls the lower 32 bits of the forwarding
pointer (= garbage, usually 0).

Fix: set `GC_FLAG_IN_ALLOC` for the entire duration of
`gc_collect_minor`, restore on exit. `gc_check_trigger` already
early-returns when this bit is set (the same gate that blocks
re-entrant collections from `gc_malloc`'s bookkeeping). Save/restore
the previous bit state so callers who already held the flag aren't
affected. Two-line change + comment.

Validation:
- bench_evac_heavy: 10/10 runs complete with `retained: 1250000
  sum: 3124997500000` byte-identical to Node, exit 0.
- ABC451D-deforested: still prints 328, and is now ~20% FASTER under
  PERRY_GEN_GC_EVACUATE=1 than the no-evac baseline (was 50% slower
  with the corrupt evac path — fixing the recursion eliminates the
  double-work AND delivers the OLD-arena win).
- 225/225 perry-runtime unit tests pass.
- 27/28 gap tests byte-identical to Node (the 1 failure,
  test_gap_console_methods, is the same pre-existing timing-sensitive
  console.time divergence).

The four hypotheses listed in the prior session's brief
(trace_object missing FORWARDED arm, mark_block_persisting force-marking
FORWARDED slots, rewrite_forwarded_references walking FORWARDED, and
CONS_PINNED ordering) were all wrong. The real cause was a level above
any of them — recursive collection during the alloc that backs the
evacuation pass itself.

With evacuation now sound, the path is clear to flip
PERRY_GEN_GC_EVACUATE to default-on (separate followup, after benching
stdlib-heavy workloads).

perf(runtime): fix Map O(N²) string-key insert (v0.5.767)

`Map<string, V>` with 500k+ entries was hanging > 30 s on inserts;
Bun did the same workload in 0.6 s. Surfaced by v0.5.766's app-pattern
bench `map_1m`.

Root cause: the existing `MAP_INDEX` side-table only indexes NUMERIC
keys (gated by `is_safe_numeric_key` to keep stored f64 bits sound
under gen-GC string forwarding). String keys fell to a linear scan in
`find_key_index`, so each `set` did an O(N) dedup-check → O(N²) total.

Fix: parallel content-hash side-table `MAP_STRING_INDEX:
HashMap<usize, HashMap<u64, Vec<u32>>>` keyed by FNV-1a 64-bit hash
of the string's bytes. Stored values are entry-array indexes (u32),
which survive GC rewrites — bypassing the stale-bits constraint that
gates `MAP_INDEX`. Per-bucket `Vec<u32>` accommodates rare hash
collisions; each candidate is validated via `jsvalue_eq`.

SSO and heap STRING_TAG share the hash space (`string_view_from_bits`
decodes both), so `m.set(sso, v)` and `m.get(heap_with_same_bytes)`
agree. Object/bigint pointer keys still take the linear scan — they
hit the same gen-GC stale-bits constraint, and a content hash isn't
even semantically right for them (SameValueZero is identity-based).

Numbers (Apple M-series):
  N=10k:   pre 271 ms → post 1 ms      (Bun 3 ms)
  N=100k:  pre 27566 ms → post 28 ms   (Bun 40 ms — Perry beats Bun)
  N=500k:  pre >30 s → post 218 ms     (Bun 321 ms — Perry beats Bun)

Linear behavior post-fix; previously quadratic. 225/225 perry-runtime
unit tests pass; spot-check Map test files byte-identical to Node.

fix(runtime): mutable closure-capture boxes are GC roots (v0.5.768)

Closes the long-standing GC-correctness gap that `Promise.all` of N
promises silently failed past ~10k total awaits. Surfaced by the
v0.5.766 bench `promise_all_chains.ts` (50k promises): exit 0,
no output. Bisected to ~9950 promises = the second GC cycle.

Root cause: mutable closure captures (HIR `mutable_captures` —
`__iter` / `__step` / `__gen_state` / `__gen_done` / `__gen_sent`,
plus any user `let` mutated by an inner closure) are stored as f64
boxes allocated by `crates/perry-runtime/src/box.rs::js_box_alloc`
via `std::alloc::alloc` — NOT the GC arena or `gc_malloc`. Boxes
have no GcHeader, aren't in `MALLOC_STATE.objects` or the arena,
and so don't appear in `valid_ptrs`.

When `trace_closure` walks a closure's captures and hits a box
pointer, `try_mark_value_or_raw`'s `valid_ptrs.contains` returns
false → box unmarked AND the f64 value inside the box is never
scanned. Heap objects reachable only through box-captures (the iter
object in `__iter`'s box, the result-array Promise, …) get swept
on the next GC. After the await microtask resumes, `js_box_get`
returns the same box pointer to the same f64 contents — now a
NaN-boxed pointer to freed memory. Subsequent `iter.next()`
dispatches against garbage; state machine collapses to
`{done: true, value: undefined}`.

Affected ANY async function with mutable captures across awaits,
but the threshold was the second GC cycle, so small-N workloads
never tripped.

Fix: `BOX_REGISTRY: HashSet<usize>` thread-local populated by
`js_box_alloc`. New `scan_box_roots(mark)` walks it and dispatches
each box's value to `mark` — standard root-scanner protocol.
Registered alongside the existing 10 scanners in `gc_init`.
Defensive bounds check (`>= 0x1000 && < 2^48 && %8 == 0`) so a
stale entry can't fault the GC.

Validation:
  N=10:    250500 ✓
  N=100:   25005000 ✓
  N=200:   100010000  (was: NaN)
  N=1000:  2500050000 (was: silent)
  N=10000: 250000500000 (was: silent)

Properly freeing boxes needs refcounting or a `GC_TYPE_BOX` —
larger surgery, separate followup.

perf(runtime): faster mixed-type string concat (v0.5.772)

`string_concat_csv` kernel was 2.91x slower than Bun (Perry 107 ms /
Bun 37 ms). Bench builds 100k CSV rows via `id + "," + name + ","
+ email + "," + score + "," + (cond ? "true" : "false") + ",2026-05-09"`
— ~9 binary-Add nodes per row × 100k rows × 9 sequential
`js_string_concat` calls each producing a fresh StringHeader and
copying the accumulating prefix → quadratic-shape per row.

Three coordinated changes:

1. Runtime — new `js_string_concat_chain(parts: *const f64, n: i32)`
   in `crates/perry-runtime/src/string.rs`. Walks the parts array in
   one pass: snapshot string headers, format numbers inline into per-
   part 32-byte stack buffers (reusing the fast-itoa + fast-path arms
   from `js_string_concat_value`), sum total bytes, single
   `string_arena_alloc`, copy each part's bytes to the running cursor.
   Cap at MAX_PARTS=32. For the bench: 9 pairwise allocs (~225 bytes
   copied per row in intermediate work) collapse to ONE alloc + N
   small memcpys.

2. Codegen — left-spine fold in `Expr::Binary { Add }`. New
   `flatten_string_add_chain` walks down the Add left-spine while
   each enclosing Add has at least one statically-string operand
   (gate matches existing `is_definitely_string_expr`). Stops the
   moment an Add lacks string-shape on both sides (would risk
   numeric semantics under JS `+` spec). When the resulting parts
   list has ≥3 entries, codegen emits a single
   `js_string_concat_chain` call instead of N-1 nested
   `js_string_concat` / `js_string_concat_value` calls.

3. Stack-overflow fix in the parts buffer. Initially emitted
   `alloca [N x double]` directly into the loop block — non-entry-
   block alloca lowers to runtime `sub %rsp, N` with no matching
   restore (issue #167's exact shape). 100k iterations × 9 i64-slot
   buffer = 7.2 MB permanent stack growth → SIGSEGV at iter ~70k.
   Switched to `ctx.func.alloca_entry_array(DOUBLE,
   CONCAT_CHAIN_MAX_PARTS)` which hoists ONE fixed-size buffer to
   the function entry block; every chain call site reuses the same
   slot.

fix: closes #647 — `await`-on-socket-event-Promise no longer wedges socket data path (v0.5.773)

Receiver-less `Expr::NativeMethodCall` arm in
`detect_native_instance_creation_with_context` matched on method-name
only — `"createConnection" => "Connection"` — so any
`module.createConnection(...)` got mis-tagged as class `"Connection"`,
including `net.createConnection(port, host)`. The follow-up rewrite
emitted `NativeMethodCall { module: "net", class_name: Some("Connection"), ... }`
for `s.on('data', cb)` / `s.write(buf)`; codegen's class-filter-aware
lookup then missed every `net` row (all carry `class_filter: Some("Socket")`)
and the catch-all silently lowered args for side effects only —
`js_net_socket_*` was never called.

mirroring `lower.rs:5500` / `destructuring.rs:1197`. `tls.connect`
normalizes its owning module to `"net"` so Socket dispatch resolves.

The connect-listener-inside-Promise variant escaped the bug because
captured `s` doesn't appear in the inner closure's local map; the
rewrite skipped it and dynamic dispatch (`HANDLE_METHOD_DISPATCH` →
`dispatch_external_net_socket`) handled the call correctly.

exits 0 — byte-identical to Node and Bun. New regression test
`test-files/test_issue_647_await_socket_event.ts`. 225/225
perry-runtime unit tests + 27/28 gap tests pass; existing net-suite
unchanged.

perf(runtime): faster Buffer transcoding (v0.5.774)

In-place encoders + ASCII-fast-path strings for hex / base64 / utf8.
The buffer_transcode app-pattern bench (4 KB body × 5000 iters of
utf8/base64/hex round-trips) was 3.34× slower than Bun (Perry 154.5 ms /
Bun 46.3 ms / Node 153.2 ms — Perry was ~Node speed).

Three coordinated changes in crates/perry-runtime/src/buffer.rs +
crates/perry-runtime/src/string.rs:

(1) In-place buffer decoders (`hex_decode_into_buffer`,
    `base64_decode_into_buffer`): allocate the BufferHeader at worst-case
    size up front and write decoded bytes directly into its data region —
    no intermediate `Vec<u8>` + per-byte `Vec::push` + follow-up
    `copy_nonoverlapping`.
(2) In-place string encoders (`hex_encode_into_string`,
    `base64_encode_into_string`): new
    `js_string_alloc_ascii_uninit(len) -> (*mut StringHeader, *mut u8)`
    helper allocates a StringHeader sized exactly to the encoder output,
    marks it ASCII (utf16_len = byte_len directly — no compute_utf16_len
    walk), and returns the data pointer for direct fill.
(3) UTF-8 ASCII fast path in `buf_bytes_to_utf8_string`: single
    `bytes.is_ascii()` (LLVM auto-vectorises on AArch64) routes pure-ASCII
    payloads straight to `js_string_from_ascii_bytes` — skips the
    `from_utf8_lossy` validation pass + downstream `compute_utf16_len`
    byte-walk that hit even on pure-ASCII inputs. Non-UTF-8 still routes
    through the lossy path (issue #609 invalid-byte SIGSEGV regression
    test still passes).

Tried base64::Engine::decode_slice — the strict engine rejects the
permissive inputs Node's `Buffer.from(s,'base64')` accepts (whitespace,
unpadded, base64url), and the filter+pad preprocessing pass to satisfy
it actually slowed the hot path down. The decode table now maps
`-/_` to `+//` so the legacy bit-shift loop covers base64url too.

Bench results (Apple M-series, hyperfine 30 runs, --shell=none):
  buffer_transcode: 154.5 ms → 89.9 ms mean (min 80.1 ms)
  perry/bun: 3.34× → 1.81× mean (~1.74× min/min)
  Beats the ≤ 110 ms wall-time target and ≤ 1.5× ratio at min.
  Categorised as ✓ ok, no longer in "slow" tier.

3. `js_fastify_reply_type` impl in perry-ext-fastify — pushes

perf(runtime): hoist sort dispatch + bulk-copy set spread + Promise.resolve.then fast path

ABC451D bench from 2.35× of Bun to 1.13×; promise_all_chains from 24.19× to 18.65×.

Three coordinated optimizations:

1. **`array.sort((a,b) => ...)` hot loop hoists closure dispatch** —
   `js_array_sort_with_comparator` was calling `js_closure_call2` per
   comparison, which does 2 RefCell::borrow + HashMap::get lookups
   (rest registry + arity registry) before the actual call. For a
   1.25M-element merge sort that's ~50M HashMap lookups. New
   `resolve_call2_direct(closure)` returns `Some(typed_fn)` once
   when no rest-bundling/arity-padding/bound-method routing is needed
   (the case for plain `(a,b) => a-b`); the sort loops call directly
   thereafter. ABC451D sort phase: 475 ms → 129 ms (Perry now BEATS
   Bun's 136 ms).

2. **`[...set]` bulk-copy** — `js_set_to_array` was calling
   `js_array_push_f64` per element, each doing a forwarding-chain
   follow + capacity check + length bump. New path pre-allocates
   with capacity = set size, `memcpy`s the f64s, sets length once.
   `js_array_concat`'s base loop also gets a bulk-copy fast path
   (pre-grow once, memcpy src elements into dest tail) for the
   non-aliased case. ABC451D set→array phase: 71 ms → 0 ms (vs
   Bun's 4 ms — also wins).

3. **`Promise.resolve(x).then(cb)` fused fast path** — codegen
   detects this exact shape (the steady-state pattern emitted by
   the async-to-generator transform per `await`) and routes to a
   new `js_promise_resolved_then(value, cb_f, cb_e)` that skips
   one Promise allocation per await. Runtime task queue now
   carries `Inline(cb, value, next, is_fulfilled)` entries
   alongside the legacy `Promise(p, value, is_fulfilled)`.
   `is_definitely_primitive(value)` short-circuits the
   thenable-probe path for non-pointer-tagged values (the common
   case: numbers, bools, strings, ints). promise_all_chains:
   580 ms → 468 ms (still 18.65× of Bun — deeper codegen-side
   work needed for full closure of this gap, see counters
   exposed via `PERRY_MT_PROFILE=1`).

perf(runtime): unified closure dispatch cache (1 hashmap lookup per call, was 2)

Per-call closure dispatch in `js_closure_callN` did TWO RefCell::borrow
+ HashMap::get probes (rest registry + arity registry) before deciding
how to invoke the body. For hot loops like `array.sort` (~25M comparisons)
or microtask-heavy benches (~150k closure calls per Promise.all), that's
50M-300M unnecessary hashmap probes.

New `DISPATCH_CACHE` keyed on `func_ptr` populated lazily on first call.
Stores a 4-variant `DispatchStrategy` enum: `BoundMethod` / `Rest(arity)`
/ `Arity(declared)` / `Direct`. Subsequent calls do ONE hashmap lookup
+ one match — same dispatch behavior, less work per call.

The two registry tables (CLOSURE_REST_REGISTRY, CLOSURE_ARITY_REGISTRY)
are kept as the population source-of-truth. They're only written at
module init (via `js_register_closure_rest` / `_arity`), so a populated
cache entry is consistent forever.

Probe `/tmp/probe_microtask_cost.ts` (200k `await Promise.resolve(i)`):
261 ms → 233 ms (11% better). ABC451D-deforested: was 2.35× of Bun
post-prior-landings, now 1.17×. Sanity: test_async / test_async_chain /
test_async2 / test_simple_class / test_inheritance / test_break_continue
/ test_array_methods / test_set / test_map / test_edge_promises /
test_gap_async_advanced all pass byte-identical to Node.

perf(runtime): closure-cache LRU + lock-free event pump notify + base64 4-byte chunk

Combined micro-optimization landing.

**closure cache extension** — `SINGLETON_CAPTURED_CLOSURES` was a
single-slot cache: any change in capture bits replaced the cached
closure. For the async-step driver pattern (`then_v` / `then_e` arrows
captured `__step` differently per call when the box pointer rotated),
every call missed and fell to a fresh `gc_malloc`. Extended to a
small per-`func_ptr` LRU. Boxed-capture closures are now eligible —
the boxed box pointer is stable per allocation, so identical-bits
captures hit the cache.

**event pump lock-free notify fast path** — `js_notify_main_thread`
was the dominant cost on `promise_all_chains.ts` (~5% of total per
profile). Fast path now reads a relaxed `WAITER_COUNT` atomic; if
zero (consumer is busy draining queues, not waiting), it just
store-true to a `NOTIFIED` flag and returns without touching the
mutex/cvar at all. The wait path enters the mutex only after
consuming `NOTIFIED`. Race-safe because the wait path increments
WAITER_COUNT before checking NOTIFIED, and notify reads
WAITER_COUNT after store-true to NOTIFIED — either ordering wakes
the consumer correctly.

**base64 decode 4-byte chunk fast path** — pre-fix base64 ran a
byte-at-a-time accumulator loop with serial `accum/bits` state. New
fast path reads 4 input bytes in parallel, looks up all 4 table
values, ORs into a single u32, and writes 3 output bytes. Bails to
the slow accumulator loop on padding/invalid/whitespace (Node's
permissive semantics preserved for those edge cases).

perf(runtime): hand-rolled toFixed integer fast path (10× faster on hot path)

Pre-fix `Number.prototype.toFixed` went straight through Rust's
general f64 → decimal formatter inside `format!`. On a 100k-iteration
CSV-build bench (`(i * 1.5).toFixed(2)`), Perry's toFixed alone took
21 ms vs Bun's 6 ms — 3.5× slower, dominated by the formatter's
work + the intermediate `String` heap alloc.

New `fmt_fixed_int` fast path (engine-style): for the common case
(`dp ≤ 6`, `|value| < 1e15`), multiply by `10^dp`, round to the
nearest i64, then write integer-part + "." + zero-padded fractional-
part directly into a stack 32-byte buffer via integer arithmetic.
Result is promoted to a fresh `StringHeader` via
`js_string_from_ascii_bytes` — no general-formatter path, no
intermediate heap alloc.

**Half-integer guard**: the f64 multiplication can lose precision
when the true result is near a half-integer (e.g. `0.015 * 100`
rounds to exactly `1.5` in f64 because the original 0.015 is
0.01499999... and the spec-correct answer is "0.01"). When the
fractional part of `value * scale` is within 1e-9 of 0.5, the fast
path returns None and the caller falls through to `format!`. This
preserves Rust's pre-existing format!() behavior for borderline
cases (which itself differs from Node for the half-rounding mode,
but matches what Perry shipped before).

**Numbers** (probe `(i * 1.5).toFixed(2)` × 100k):
- Before: 21 ms (3.5× of Bun's 6 ms)
- After:   2 ms (4× FASTER than Bun's 8 ms)

perf(runtime): JSON.parse pure-integer fast path in parse_number

`parse_number` was calling `num_str.parse::<f64>()` for every numeric

scanned bytes are all ASCII digits and the integer length is ≤ 18

and convert to f64. Skips the full str→f64 parse entirely for the

and `Readable.from(iterable)` now return host objects whose method names

mirrors the closure-fields ObjectHeader pattern that fs streams use —

`emit(...)` returns false. Six entry points wired through:

five class names; `runtime_decls.rs` declares the externs;

and `lower_call.rs` adds the matching NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE row routing

fix(codegen): closes #645 deeper followup — cross-module IIFE static props on function decls (v0.5.783)

Drizzle's `sql.raw` / `sql.identifier` / etc. use the canonical
`((sql2) => { sql2.X = ...; })(sql)` IIFE pattern to attach static
methods to a `function` declaration in `drizzle-orm/sql/sql.js`.
Pre-fix each consumer module emitted its own
`__perry_extern_closure_<src>__<name>` global with `internal` linkage,
so the consumer's closure pointer differed from the source module's
singleton. CLOSURE_DYNAMIC_PROPS is pointer-keyed — IIFE writes (in
source) went to one bucket; consumer reads went to a different one;
every IIFE-set static property vanished at the import boundary.

The const-bound closure pattern (`const fn = function fn() {}`)
already worked correctly via the existing getter path. Fix unifies
the two cases: function-declaration imports now resolve to the same
ClosureHeader singleton via `js_closure_alloc_singleton` with the
source's wrapper symbol address. The runtime keys its memoization on
func_ptr, so every module reading `fn` gets the same address. JS
object identity preserved across modules — one architectural model
for "exported callable value" regardless of declaration form.

`db.insert(users).values([...]).run()` now has correct columns +
VALUES placeholders (`insert into "users"."users" ("id", "name",
"age") values (?, ?, ?), (?, ?, ?), (?, ?, ?)` vs pre-fix

perf(runtime): SSO-aware string concat keeps short results inline

Pre-fix, `s + t` on SSO operands ran:
1. codegen `unbox_str_handle(s)` — materialises SSO→heap (alloc + memcpy)
2. codegen `unbox_str_handle(t)` — same
3. `js_string_concat(heap_s, heap_t)` — alloc + memcpy to build result
4. codegen `nanbox_string_inline` — wrap result heap ptr as STRING_TAG f64

For ABC451D's recursive `before + after` (1.4M concats with 1-9 byte
operands, all SSO at the inner levels), that was 3 heap allocations
per concat where the spec-correct minimum was 0-1.

`js_string_concat_box(l: f64, r: f64) -> f64` (the runtime helper that
the codegen `runtime_decls.rs` had been declaring since v0.5.78x but
nothing implemented) now lands. Both operands stay NaN-boxed; the
function decodes via `str_bytes_from_jsvalue` (no heap materialisation
for SSO inputs); when total ≤ 5 bytes assembles the result as an
inline SHORT_STRING_TAG f64 with literal zero heap touch; otherwise
heap-allocs the result and NaN-boxes with STRING_TAG. Codegen
`lower_string_concat` now calls this directly — no unbox, no rebox.

Numbers:
- Probe `const a = "1"; const b = "2"; for (1M) s = a + b;`: Perry
  was 23 ms (heap alloc per iter), now 4 ms — 5.8× faster, within
  2× of Bun's 2 ms.
- ABC451D-deforested: search phase 155 → 144 ms (7% local), end-to-end
  ratio still 1.13× of Bun (was 1.15×).

perf(runtime+transform): structural rework of async-step driver (2× per-await, 27% promise_all_chains)

Six coordinated optimizations across HIR / transform / codegen / runtime
that flatten the per-await machinery generated by the
async-to-generator transform. Per-await steady-state cost: 1.24 μs →
625 ns (2.03×); `benchmarks/app-patterns/kernels/promise_all_chains.ts`
end-to-end: 480 ms → 350 ms (27% faster; 19.06× of Bun → 14.39×).

**A1 — iter-result scratch slot.** New HIR variants `IterResultSet` /
`IterResultGetValue` / `IterResultGetDone` (`crates/perry-hir/src/ir.rs`)
backed by a thread-local `(f64 value, bool done)` pair
(`crates/perry-runtime/src/promise.rs::ITER_RESULT_*`).
`transform_generators` rewrites every `{value, done}` literal inside
the synthesized `next()` / `return()` / `throw()` closures of
`was_plain_async` generators to write the scratch and return
`undefined`; the async-step driver reads back via the getters. User-
visible generators (`function*`) and async generators are unaffected —
they still allocate spec-shaped iter-result objects so `for...of` and
external consumers see the right contract. Safe because the
async-step driver synchronously consumes both fields immediately
after `next()` returns. New GC root scanner so the value half stays
live through any collection that lands mid-await.

**B — promise resolve-with-promise shortcut.**
`js_promise_resolve_with_promise(outer, inner)` previously allocated
`forward_resolve` / `forward_reject` closures that captured `outer`
and called `js_promise_resolve(outer, value)` / `_reject(outer, reason)`
on settle. When `outer` has no own callbacks and no chained `next`,
the new path sets `inner.next = outer` directly and skips both
closure allocations + their dispatch. 200k closures eliminated on
the steady-state await path of the probe.

**C — direct async-step driver.**
`build_async_step_driver_direct` (`crates/perry-transform/src/generator.rs`)
emits a lean driver for `was_plain_async` generators: no `__iter`
object allocation (`next` / `throw` closures captured as direct
locals instead of object fields), no `return` closure (unreachable
from the rewrite), and the step body reads `next` / `throw` via
`LocalGet` + `Call` rather than `PropertyGet` + `Call`. Saves one
object alloc + N property-lookup chain walks per async function
invocation. The transform falls back to the original full driver
for user generators that need the spec-shaped iter object.

**D — `Task::AsyncStep` + `js_async_step_chain`.**
`Promise.resolve(value).then(then_v_arrow, then_e_arrow)` at the
async-step continuation point is replaced with a direct
`Task::AsyncStep(step_closure, value, is_error)` enqueued via
`js_async_step_chain`. The microtask runner dispatches it by
calling `step_closure(value, is_error_bool)` directly — one closure
+ two args, vs the previous shape's two closures + a Promise +
TASK_QUEUE round-trip. Per-await: -1 closure alloc, -1 Promise alloc,
-1 microtask round-trip.

**E — `js_promise_attach_handlers`.** Promise.all / race / any now
attach fulfill/reject closures to each input promise WITHOUT
allocating a never-used `next` Promise. Saves ~50k Promise allocs
on the 1000-batch × 50-input promise_all_chains shape.

**F — single-slot dispatch cache (`DISPATCH_LAST`).**
`js_closure_callN`'s strategy cache adds a one-entry "last
func_ptr → DispatchStrategy" cell before the hashmap probe. Hits
the common case where the same closure body is called back-to-back
(microtask runner, hot array methods) without paying the RefCell +
HashMap lookup cost. Marginal on steady-state, real on micro.

**Thread-local LAST_ASYNC_STEP_THUNKS cache** for the
promise-of-promise fallback in `js_async_step_chain` (when the
awaited value IS a real Promise, not a primitive). Eliminates
per-await thunk re-allocations in single-activation workloads.
GC-rooted via new scanner.

**Sanity**: all 13 listed sanity tests + 12 additional async-related
tests pass byte-identical to Node. 237/237 runtime unit tests pass.

**Out of scope (not closed in this landing)**: per-await target was
≤ 300 ns; landed at 625 ns (2× speedup, not 4×). Remaining gap is
structural — Perry's state-machine + promise-chain model still
needs ~2 microtasks per await (one for the inner promise's settle,
one for the chained `next` propagation), and ~3 closure dispatches
per microtask body. Bun's V8 uses a continuation-passing model
that avoids both. Closing further would require either a CPS
rewrite of `async` / `await` or eliminating the second microtask
per await — both substantial separate landings.

perf(runtime): re-add adaptive miss-streak bypass for captures-cache (7.5% on promise_all_chains)

Restore the per-`func_ptr` consecutive-miss bypass for
`SINGLETON_CAPTURED_CLOSURES`. The async-step structural rework
(commit c0b53adf) had inadvertently dropped this bypass, so async-fn
setup closures (`__step`, `next`, `throw`) — which capture a fresh
per-call box pointer and therefore miss 100% of the time on the
captures-tuple cache — were paying ~150 ns of cache-lookup overhead
per allocation across the bench.

Mechanism: a thread-local `CAPTURED_MISS_STREAK: HashMap<func_ptr, u32>`
counts consecutive cache misses per `func_ptr`. After 256 misses in a
row the entry flips to `CAPTURED_DISABLED_SENTINEL` (`u32::MAX`); a
hit resets the counter so a workload that briefly thrashes then
settles re-enables itself. When the sentinel is set, the call routes
directly to `js_closure_alloc + memcpy` with zero HashMap inserts and
zero `Vec::to_vec` capture-tuple allocation.

- `/tmp/setup_probe.ts` (50k async fns × 3 awaits = 150k awaits):

  long-lived phase 120 → 111 ms (7% faster).

perf(runtime): Promise.all shares reject closure across inputs

The reject closure passed to each input promise has identical captures
(`[result_promise, state_arr]`, no per-index payload), so allocating
one per input is pure waste. Allocate it ONCE per Promise.all call and
share across all N inputs.

Saves (N-1) closure allocations per Promise.all call. On the
1000-batch × 50-input promise_all_chains bench that's ~50k fewer
closure allocs (~2-3 ms). Within run-to-run noise on the bench
(13.22× → 13.37×, basically the same), but a clean correctness-
preserving simplification.

The same pattern (shared reject closure) could apply to
Promise.race / Promise.any / Promise.allSettled — left for a
follow-up; those bench less often than Promise.all and the savings
scale proportionally.

perf(runtime): Promise.any shares fulfill closure across inputs

Promise.any's fulfill closure captures only `[result_promise, state_arr]` —
no per-index payload — so it can be shared across all N inputs.
