fix(codegen): #321 — Effect.succeed via named-import-of-namespace-reexport (#1072)

Closes the last runtime blocker for the basic Effect.succeed/runSync
shape on the native `perry.compilePackages` path. Pre-fix:

  import { Effect } from "effect"    // effect/index.ts: export * as Effect from "./Effect.js"
  const program = Effect.succeed(42) // typeof program === "function" (!!)
  Effect.runSync(program)            // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_tag')

Root cause: the HIR's "uppercase imported identifier is a class" rule
lifts `Effect.succeed(42)` to `StaticMethodCall { class_name: "Effect",
method_name: "succeed" }`. The StaticMethodCall arm in
crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs recognised that `Effect` was a
namespace import (it lands in `namespace_imports` via the
`Export::NamespaceReExport`-aware Named-import branch in compile.rs)
and looked up the source prefix for `succeed`, then emitted a 1-arg
direct call `perry_fn_<src>__succeed(arg)`. But that symbol is a
ZERO-arg getter returning the closure value (because `export const
succeed = (v) => new EffectInst(v)` is var-shape — the source's
init function sets a global and the getter just reloads it). The
arg was silently dropped and the call site received the closure
pointer instead of an `EffectInst` — `typeof === "function"`,
`._tag` undefined, `runSync` exploded.

Fix:

1. Populate a new `namespace_reexport_named_imports` set when
   `compile.rs` recognises that a Named import (`import { Effect }`)
   resolves to a `NamespaceReExport` in the source (`export * as
   Effect from "./Effect.js"`). This is a SUBSET of
   `namespace_imports` — plain `import * as X from "./X.js"`
   (used heavily by effect's internal modules) is intentionally
   NOT in the new set so the pre-fix direct-call path is preserved
   for them (broad audit territory: switching them all over surfaces
   pre-existing init-order bugs hiding behind the silently-wrong
   shape).

2. Also tag var-shape NamespaceReExport members into `imported_vars`
   in compile.rs — the existing `Namespace { local }` branch already
   does this for plain wildcard imports; the NamespaceReExport
   branch was missing the same step.

3. In expr.rs's StaticMethodCall arm, when the class_name is in the
   new set AND the method_name is in `imported_vars`, fetch the
   closure via the zero-arg getter and dispatch through
   `js_closure_callN`. Mirrors the existing var-shape branch in
   `lower_call.rs`'s namespace-member-call path.

4. Cache key in `object_cache.rs` now folds in the new set so two
   modules with identical `namespace_imports` but different
   `namespace_reexport_named_imports` don't collide.

Verified end-to-end on a minimal `mini-effect` fixture mirroring the
shape (`test-files/issue_321_named_namespace_reexport/`): perry's
output matches `node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte.
The real `effect` package still hits a separate, pre-existing
init-time TypeError before user code runs — that's a follow-up
audit, not introduced by this PR.

Scope is deliberately narrow: no changes to the V8 fallback path,
the `import * as`-style consumer path, or the runtime closure
machinery. No version bump or changelog change.

fix(fastify): non-blocking listen() + main-thread pump (#1066)

* fix(fastify): non-blocking listen() + main-thread pump

Closes the compat-sweep fastify hang: `js_fastify_listen` (in both
perry-stdlib's bundled adapter AND perry-ext-fastify) entered a
blocking inner event loop that never returned, so `await app.listen(...)`
in user code never resumed — the in-process `fetch` against the same
process and `app.close()` were both unreachable, and gtimeout killed
the program at 30 s with rc=124.

Root cause: pre-fix `event_loop(...)` ran for the process lifetime
inside `listen()`, taking over the main TS thread. The same shape was
fixed for `node:http` in #604 (perry-ext-http-server) — apply that
pattern to fastify:

  * `listen()` returns immediately after spawning the accept loop.
  * Per-server mpsc receiver lives inside `FastifyServerHandle`
    (Mutex<Option<...>>) instead of on the `event_loop` stack.
  * New `js_fastify_process_pending` drains pending requests from
    every registered handle on every tick of perry-stdlib's main pump.
  * New `js_fastify_has_active` keeps the runtime alive while any
    server is in the "listening" state.
  * `app.close()` (previously fell through to "unknown method" and
    no-op'd) now routes through a new `js_fastify_app_close` entry
    in the codegen NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE; it walks the handle registry
    for matching servers, flips their listening flag, drops their
    rx, and fires shutdown — so the runtime exits naturally.

Wiring: a new `external-fastify-pump` feature is activated by the
well-known flip when `bundled-fastify` is stripped (`import 'fastify'`
routed to perry-ext-fastify). Mirrors `external-{net,ws,http-server}-pump`.

Test: `test-files/test_fastify_in_process.ts` mirrors the compat-sweep
fixture (await listen + in-process fetch + close). 22 existing
perry-stdlib fastify unit tests still pass; `scripts/run_fastify_tests.sh`
end-to-end suite (10 routes) still passes.

* fix(fastify): add fastify.close to API_MANIFEST + regen docs

The manifest_consistency test (#463) caught NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE / API_MANIFEST
drift: the previous commit added fastify.close to NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE +
runtime_decls + dispatch but forgot the matching manifest row, so the
unimplemented-API gate would have errored on a real call to app.close().

fix(object): skip misaligned non-object pointers in js_object_assign_one (#1073)

* fix(object): skip misaligned non-object pointers in js_object_assign_one

js_object_assign_one (Object.assign single-source) decodes target/source
permissively and is documented to skip non-object sources
(Object.assign(t, 5) / null). The guards only rejected NaN-boxed
specials and values < 0x10000; an untagged, unaligned bit pattern passed
through and was dereferenced as *ObjectHeader at `(*src).keys_array`.

A real ObjectHeader is heap-allocated #[repr(C)] with u64/pointer
fields, so a valid object pointer is always 8-byte aligned. Observed on
a Windows release build of a large Perry app: a non-pointer value
(0x1d81ff6950a) reached `source`, and `(*src).keys_array` is a
misaligned read -- a hard abort under debug pointer-alignment checks,
and in release silent memory corruption that surfaced downstream as a
GC out-of-bounds panic (NaN-boxed value used as a shadow-stack index).

Add an 8-byte alignment check to the existing defensive bailout for
both target and source: a misaligned value is not a real object
pointer, so treat it as a non-object and skip -- exactly the behaviour
this function already documents for non-object arguments. Turns the
crash into the spec-correct no-op.

NOTE: this hardens the runtime entry point (correct on its own and
consistent with the function's documented contract). Why a non-pointer
value reaches `source` on Windows is a separate codegen question worth
root-causing.

(cherry picked from commit 4ee01e4a801d2b0deb32e9420c61d6a79b4ad54a)

fix(hir): #1070 — setErrorHandler err param mis-tagged as fastify Request (#1077)

`pre_scan_fastify_handler_params` in `crates/perry-hir/src/lower_patterns.rs`
registered the first arrow param of EVERY recognized fastify handler call
as a `("fastify", "Request")` native instance — including
`setErrorHandler(async (err, req, reply) => …)`, whose first param is the
thrown value, not a Request. With `err` tagged as Request, any user-field
read like `err.problem` lowered to a `NativeMethodCall { module: "fastify",
method: "problem", … }` whose unknown-method fall-through in
`lower_native_method_call` returns `double_literal(0.0)`, so the access
printed as `0`.

`(err as MyError).problem` worked because `expr_member.rs`'s native-instance
shape check only fires for `member.obj == Expr::Ident`; a `TsAs` cast
bypassed it and went through generic property dispatch.

Skip the err param for `setErrorHandler` so only `params[1]=request` and
`params[2]=reply` get the native-instance tags. `err.<field>` then falls
through to the generic property dispatch that reads the actual class-
instance field at runtime, restoring parity with the `as`-cast path.

`run_fastify_tests.sh`: a `ProblemError` thrown from a route is
caught by `setErrorHandler`, narrowed via `instanceof`, and its

fix(ui-windows): #1061 — Picker/Combobox dropdown clipped to zero by relayout (#1078)

fix(wasm): #1071 — cross-module imported variable reads as undefined (#1079)

Pre-fix any `import { X } from './m'` where X was an exported `const`/`let`
(rather than a function) read as `undefined` on `--target wasm`. The HIR
lowers value reads of imported names to `Expr::ExternFuncRef { name }`,
and the WASM target only looked the name up in `func_name_map` — variable
exports aren't in that map, so the fall-through emitted `TAG_UNDEFINED`.

The bug reporter saw it on nested-object exports; reproduced it shows the
same failure for flat fields and for scalar `const FOO = 'hello'` — the
shared root cause is the missing variable-resolution path. Single-file
code works because there's no extern boundary; the LLVM target works
because it emits a per-export `perry_fn_<src>__<name>()` getter and
recognizes the value-form via `imported_vars`.

Fix mirrors the LLVM approach without per-export thunks: build a
`(consumer_mod_idx, imported_local_name) → wasm_global_idx` map that
resolves each import to the source module's already-promoted
`module_let_globals` slot, then route the value-form `ExternFuncRef` to
a `GlobalGet`. JS-context emit reads the same slot through
`wasmInstance.exports.__wasm_global_<idx>.value` (mutable globals exposed
via `WebAssembly.Global`). All module-let globals are now exported by
index for the boundary.

Test: `tests/wasm/22_cross_module_nested_object/` (multi-module via new
subdirectory convention with `entry.ts`) covers flat string, nested
object, and scalar `const`/`number` exports. `run_wasm_tests.sh` now
walks numbered subdirectories whose entry is `entry.ts` in addition to
top-level `.ts` files. Baseline failures (05/10/11/14/17/18/19) are
pre-existing and untouched by this change; new test passes.

fix(hir): #1069 — synthetic-arguments callees: don't pad missing args + bounds-check OOB (#1087)

* fix(hir): #1069 — synthetic-`arguments` callees: don't pad missing args + bounds-check OOB reads

For `function f(a, b) { arguments.length }` called as `f()`, Perry
reported `arguments.length === 2` instead of `0`, and `arguments[i]`
on the empty rest array returned the raw `0.0` slot value instead of
`undefined`. Two layered bugs in the synthetic-`arguments` path:

1. **HIR call-site default-fill** (`lower/expr_call.rs`): the loop at
   `lower_call`'s tail pads missing fixed-param slots with
   `Expr::Undefined` so the callee body's `if (param === undefined) {
   param = default; }` prefix can apply user-written defaults. For
   synth-`arguments` callees this inflates `args.len()` — which the
   codegen synth-args bundle path (`lower_call.rs:974`) uses to size
   the runtime `arguments` array — so `arguments.length` reads as the
   declared fixed-param count regardless of the caller's actual arg
   count. Fix: thread a `has_synth_args` flag through `func_defaults`
   (5 push sites + the `lookup_func_defaults` consumer) and skip the
   fill loop entirely for synth-args callees. Codegen already pads
   missing fixed-param slots with `undefined` itself in the
   synth-args branch, so the body's default-fill statements still
   substitute user defaults.

2. **`js_dyn_index_get` OOB** (`runtime/src/value.rs`): the
   `Type::Any` IndexGet fast path (issue #514) routes numeric reads
   through `js_dyn_index_get`. For `LAZY_ARRAY` / `FORWARDED` it
   delegates to `js_array_get_f64` which bounds-checks, but for
   regular `GC_TYPE_ARRAY` it does raw `arr + 8 + idx*8` pointer
   arithmetic with no `length` guard. `js_array_alloc(0)` rounds
   capacity up to `MIN_ARRAY_CAPACITY`, so reading `arguments[0]`
   on an empty rest array reads zeroed-but-allocated storage and
   returns `0.0`. Fix: add a one-line `idx >= length` check on the
   `GC_TYPE_ARRAY` branch.

  `dual()` and general Node code rely on (length, indexed access,

fix(compile): PerryTS/storekit#1 — route FFI imports through manifest path (#1085)

Imports from a package declaring `perry.nativeLibrary` (e.g. `@perryts/
storekit`) carry ambient `export declare function` signatures only — the
real implementation lives in the linked static library. The compile-side
import loop was unconditionally registering every named/default specifier
in `import_function_prefixes`, which made `lower_call.rs` emit a call
against `perry_fn_<src>__<name>` for symbols whose source module never
emits that wrapper (no body to compile). The result was a clean compile
followed by a link failure (`Undefined symbols: _perry_fn_..._js_storekit_
start_listener`), or — on older Perry builds — an LLVM IR verifier error
when the call was emitted without a matching declaration.

Skip the `import_function_prefixes` registration when the specifier's
exported name is listed in the source package's `perry.nativeLibrary.
functions` manifest. `lower_call.rs` then falls through to the FFI-
manifest path (`ctx.ffi_signatures`), which emits a direct call to the
declared FFI symbol along with a matching `declare external` at the top
of the caller IR.

Pre-computes the native-library lookup once per import (outside the
per-specifier loop) so the check is constant-time.

fix(crypto): #1076 createHmac/createHash dispatch via const-bound or for-of alg (#1080)

`crypto.createHmac(alg, key).update(data).digest(enc)` silently returned
"" whenever `alg` wasn't an inline `Expr::String` literal — const-bound
names, for-of bindings, ternaries, function-returned algs all matched the
chain-collapse fast path's `_ =>` catch-all (which returned an empty
string). HMAC webhook verification, TOTP, and any code that picks the
algorithm dynamically silently produced wrong answers instead of failing.

Fix:
- Replace the catch-all empty-string return with a runtime handle path
  that allocates an Hmac/Hash handle (`js_crypto_create_hmac` /
  `js_crypto_create_hash`) and invokes `.update(data).digest(enc)` via
  `js_native_call_method`. This covers all non-literal alg cases AND the
  algorithms the fast path doesn't have direct FFI helpers for (sha1,
  sha512, md5 for HMAC; sha1, sha512 for hash).
- Add `HmacHandle` + `js_crypto_create_hmac` + `dispatch_hmac` in
  perry-stdlib mirroring the existing `HashHandle` + `js_crypto_create_hash`
  + `dispatch_hash` shape. Supports sha1/sha256/sha512/md5 + hex/base64/
  base64url/binary digest encodings.
- Register `HmacHandle` in `js_handle_method_dispatch` for `update` /
  `digest`.
- Add a standalone `Expr::Call` arm for `crypto.createHmac(alg, key)`
  mirroring the existing standalone `createHash` arm — covers
  `const h = createHmac(...); h.update().digest()` where the chain is
  split across statements.

Verified byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types` for

fix(wasm): #1081 — push undefined when Stmt::Return body is a void call (#1086)

`v => console.log(v)` lowers to a closure with body `Stmt::Return(Some(console.log(v)))`.
The closure's WASM signature is `[i64] -> [i64]`, but emit_expr for the console.* call
emits `emit_memcall_void` + early `return` from the match arm, leaving the operand
stack empty. The subsequent `Instruction::Return` then fails validation with
"expected 1 elements on the stack for return, found 0" — the V8 error from #1081.

Mirror JS semantics (a void call evaluates to `undefined`) by pushing TAG_UNDEFINED
when `expr_has_value(e)` is false in `Stmt::Return(Some(e))`. This is the same
pattern `Stmt::Expr` already uses (Drop only when expr_has_value).

Regression test: tests/wasm/22_return_void_expr.ts.

fix(jwt): #1074 — algorithm option resolves const-bound ident before literal-match (#1089)

`jwt.sign(payload, key, { algorithm: X, ... })` silently fell back to HS256
(using the user's PEM as an HMAC secret) when `algorithm` was anything other
than an inline string literal: const-bound identifier, ternary, spread, or
when the entire options object was a const ref. Same mirror bug on
`jwt.verify`'s `algorithm` / `algorithms: [...]` option, where ES/RS tokens
silently failed verification.

This is a real cryptographic downgrade: the JWT was HMAC-signed with the
PEM's raw bytes, the on-wire `header.alg` claimed `"HS256"`, and any
verifier that accepts either HMAC or EC/RSA quietly accepted the
downgraded token.

Fix (approach mirrors #1076's runtime-dispatch fallback for
`crypto.createHmac`):

  Stdlib (perry-stdlib/src/jsonwebtoken.rs):
  - js_jwt_sign_dyn(alg, payload, secret, exp, kid): reads the algorithm
    name from a runtime `*const StringHeader` and dispatches to the same
    `sign_common` paths the typed `js_jwt_sign_es256` / `_rs256` helpers
    use. Unknown algs fall back to HS256 with a PERRY_DEBUG log.
  - js_jwt_verify_dyn(alg, token, secret): mirror for verify.
  - js_jwt_sign_dyn_opts(payload, secret, opts_jsvalue): case where the
    entire options object is a non-extractable expression (`const opts =
    {...}; jwt.sign(p, k, opts)`). Extracts `algorithm` / `expiresIn` /
    `keyid` from the NaN-boxed object at runtime via
    `js_object_get_field_by_name`, then defers to `js_jwt_sign_dyn`.
  - js_jwt_verify_dyn_opts: mirror, including `algorithms: [...]` plural
    via `js_array_get`.

  Codegen (crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native.rs):
  - lower_jsonwebtoken_sign: when `algorithm` is non-literal, lower its
    value as a `*const StringHeader` via `get_raw_string_ptr` and route to
    `js_jwt_sign_dyn`. When the whole options expression is not an
    inline-object (or AnonShape), route to `js_jwt_sign_dyn_opts` with
    the options JSValue as the third arg.
  - lower_jsonwebtoken_verify: mirror, covering both singular `algorithm`
    and `algorithms: [literal]` / `algorithms: [non-literal]` / non-array
    `algorithms` shapes.

The inline-literal fast path is unchanged — common case still routes
directly to the typed helpers at compile time.

Validated byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types` in

B const-bound ident, C const-bound opts object, D verify with const-bound
algorithm). Existing #915 and #927 jwt regressions still pass.

feat(jsruntime): #1021 — Perry-class V8 exposure + Reflect.metadata cross-boundary wire (#1117)

Flips the NestJS smoke from `body={"message":"Cannot GET /ping",...}` (404,
no route registered) to `body=pong` (the route is discovered and the
handler runs).

The previous attempt (#1067) wired the Reflect-metadata bridge JS but
NestJS still saw zero modules at scan time. End-to-end the route never
registered because four separate gaps stacked on top of each other:

1. **V8 class wrapper had no methods on the prototype.** `native_class_to_v8`
   returned a `v8::Function` whose `.prototype` was V8's default empty
   object, so `Object.getPrototypeOf(new metatype())[name]` (the path
   NestJS's `MetadataScanner.getAllMethodNames` and `paths-explorer`
   walk) resolved to `undefined`. Now `populate_native_class_v8_prototype`
   mirrors each entry in `CLASS_VTABLE_REGISTRY` onto the wrapper's
   `.prototype` as a `v8::Function` that re-dispatches through the
   vtable's `func_ptr` directly (NOT through `js_native_call_method` —
   that path walks `jsval.as_pointer()` on the receiver, which is junk
   for a V8 object instance and returned the class_id integer instead
   of the method body's return value).

2. **`new metatype()` discarded the prototype chain.** `native_class_constructor`
   used to `retval.set(v8::Object::new(scope))`, overriding the implicit
   `this` whose `[[Prototype]]` V8 already pointed at the populated
   wrapper prototype. Now we return `args.this()` for construct calls.

3. **Class names were lost on the boundary.** `metatype.name` came back
   `""`, which made NestJS's `ModuleTokenFactory` hash every module under
   the same empty-string token — `modules.size` was always 1 (only the
   internal core module won the slot). Added a per-`class_id` →
   `String` registry (`CLASS_NAMES`, populated by codegen via the new
   `js_register_class_name` FFI), and surface it through V8's
   `v8::Function::set_name` so the wrapper carries the user-visible
   class name.

4. **`crypto.createHash().digest()` returned `""`.** The V8-side stub
   threw away `update()` chunks and returned an empty string —
   `ModuleTokenFactory.hashString` hashed every module to the same
   `""`. Added `op_perry_hash` (sha1/sha256/sha384/sha512/md5 via
   `sha1`/`sha2`/`md-5` crates) and rewrote the stub to mirror the
   working `createHmac` path (chunked update → final concat → op
   → encode).

5. **`perf_hooks.performance.now` was undefined.** The default `_ =>
   "export default {}"` fallback applied; NestJS's
   `ModuleTokenFactory.create()` threw `Cannot read properties of
   undefined (reading 'now')` and the dynamic-module compile path
   bailed before any user modules were inserted. Added a real
   `perf_hooks` stub backed by `Date.now()` (good enough for the
   serialization-warning timer NestJS uses it for).

Sub-fixes shipped alongside, all required for the route to land:

- **`reflect-metadata` bridge re-asserted after every module evaluation**
  (`poll_pending_module_evaluations` in `interop.rs`). The npm
  `reflect-metadata` package (loaded transitively by `@nestjs/common`
  via `require("reflect-metadata")`) overwrites `Reflect.defineMetadata`
  /`getMetadata` etc. — without this, our wrappers from `js_runtime_init`
  are gone by the time the first decorator runs. The bridge JS is
  idempotent so re-running on each module evaluation is cheap.
- **Perry closure identity stabilized across V8 crossings**
  (`NATIVE_CLOSURE_HANDLES` cache + `__perry_closure_ptr` property).
  Decorators that key on `descriptor.value` (the method function) now
  see the same `v8::Function` instance as later
  `prototype['methodName']` reads — load-bearing for any
  `WeakMap`-based metadata store on the V8 side.
- **`v8_to_native_metadata_target` recognizes Perry-closure-wrapped V8
  functions** so `descriptor.value` round-trips to the same
  POINTER_TAG | ptr identity Perry uses internally — the precondition
  for the Perry-side `REFLECT_METADATA` store entry from a V8-side
  `Reflect.defineMetadata(...)` to be reachable from a Perry-side
  `Reflect.getMetadata(...)`.

fix(stdlib): support utf16le / base64 / hex / latin1 / ascii in StringDecoder (#1125)

* fix(stdlib): support utf16le / base64 / hex / latin1 / ascii in StringDecoder

`new StringDecoder(encoding)` previously ignored the encoding argument
and always ran the UTF-8 incremental decoder, so:
  - `new StringDecoder("utf16le").write(Buffer.from([0x68, 0x00, 0x69, 0x00]))`
    returned the raw bytes `h\0i\0` instead of Node's decoded `hi`.
  - `new StringDecoder("base64").write(Buffer.from("hello"))` returned
    the literal `"hello"` instead of Node's `"aGVs"` (Node's base64
    StringDecoder is the *encode* direction — binary bytes in, base64
    text out — buffered in 3-byte chunks).

Switch `StringDecoderHandle` to a `DecodingMode` enum populated at
construction time from the encoding string and dispatch `write` / `end`
through per-mode functions:
  - utf-8: keeps the existing partial-codepoint state machine
    (`last_need` / `last_total` / `last_char`).
  - utf-16le / ucs2: pairs bytes as little-endian u16 code units;
    odd trailing byte carries to the next write; surrogate pairs handled.
  - base64: encodes input bytes 3 at a time; up to 2 buffered bytes
    flush as `=`-padded base64 on `end`.
  - hex: each byte → two lowercase hex chars. Stateless.
  - latin1 / binary: 1:1 byte → codepoint in 0..=255.
  - ascii: each byte masked to 7 bits.

Unrecognised encoding names default to UTF-8 (Node throws there; keep
the forgiving fallback Perry had until a stricter default is wanted).

PR #1109 shipped a partial fix for #1107 (partial-alpha NSColor renders
zero glyphs on iOS 26 device) but three regressions / blind spots
remained, all reproduced on physical iPhone running iOS 26.5:

1. Text widgets with `textSetColor(α < 1.0)` (e.g. Material's 87% black)
   still rendered nothing. #1109's `apply_label_color_via_attributed`

   builds a fresh `[UIFont systemFontOfSize:]` and retains the result.
   This commit mirrors that exact pattern.

2. Bare `Button("Mitmachen", cb)` + `widgetSetBackgroundColor(BRAND_RED)`
   rendered invisible. `buttonWithType:UIButtonTypeSystem` on iOS 26
   routes through the Liquid Glass renderer, which overrides explicit
   `setTitleColor:` / `setBackgroundColor:` with the system tint.
   Switch to `UIButtonTypeCustom` (and seed `[UIColor labelColor]` as
   the default title color so a bare button with no explicit color is
   still visible). Also drop the `setAttributedTitle:nil` cleanup branch
   from #1109 — on iOS 26 it nukes the button's plain-title rendering
   along with the attributed state, leaving even α==1.0 buttons blank.

3. `widgetSetBackgroundColor` on a NESTED `UIStackView` painted
   transparent. `UIStackView.backgroundColor` is documented iOS 14+ but
   the property doesn't drive painting on inner stacks under iOS 26's
   compositor. The CALayer's own `backgroundColor` (CGColor) does paint
   reliably, so set both — view-level for non-buggy paths (root stack,
   iOS 17 sim) and layer-level as the belt-and-suspenders fix.

fix(net,http): #1123 #1124 — net.createServer end-to-end + http Buffer bodies (server + client) (#1133)

* fix(net,http): #1123 #1124 — net.createServer codegen + Buffer res body

Issue #1123 had two sides:
- Dotted (`import * as net from "node:net"; net.createServer(...)`) bailed
  at codegen Phase 2 with "expression NetCreateServer not yet supported"
  because `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs` had no match arm for
  `Expr::NetCreateServer` (HIR variant + perry-codegen-js + perry-codegen-wasm
  did; only the LLVM backend was missing).
- Named-import (`import { createServer } from "node:net"; createServer(...)`)
  compiled+linked but `server === undefined` — `lookup_native_module`
  produced a generic `Expr::NativeMethodCall { module: "net", method:
  "createServer" }`, but `NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE` has no
  ("net", "createServer") row and the call dropped through every arm in
  `lower_native_method_call`, returning `TAG_UNDEFINED`.

Also the runtime symbol `js_net_create_server` referenced in
`runtime_decls.rs:2690` was never defined anywhere in the linked
libraries (the old `perry-runtime/src/net.rs` impl is gated off at
`lib.rs:79` since the A1/A1.5 move to event-driven sockets; the new
perry-ext-net wrapper never reintroduced a createServer entry, only
the Socket family).

Three-place fix:
- `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs` — add `Expr::NetCreateServer` arm,
  NaN-unbox both args via `unbox_to_i64`, pass `"0"` for omitted slots.
- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call.rs` — intercept the named-import
  bare-call path so `("net", "createServer")` synthesizes the same
  `Expr::NetCreateServer` node the dotted form produces. Both shapes now
  converge on the new codegen arm.
- `crates/perry-ext-net/src/lib.rs` — define `js_net_create_server` as a
  placeholder that allocates a handle from the shared `next_id()` counter
  and stashes the connection listener under `'connection'` for a future
  full `js_net_server_listen` accept loop. Today's verdict: `typeof
  server` flips from `"undefined"` to `"number"`; the accept-loop wiring
  is tracked separately.

Issue #1124: `crates/perry-ext-http-server/src/types.rs::jsvalue_to_body_bytes`
treated all POINTER_TAG'd values as `StringHeader`-shaped — but
`BufferHeader` is `{ length: u32, capacity: u32 }` (8-byte header)
while `StringHeader` is `{ utf16_len, byte_len, capacity, refcount,
flags }` (20-byte header). Reading a buffer through the string layout
surfaced the buffer's `capacity` slot as `byte_len` (often equal to
the requested size for exact-fit allocations, so `Content-Length`
looked correct) and then indexed data from `ptr + sizeof(StringHeader)`
— past the buffer's actual bytes — into pre-zeroed slab memory. The
wire body came out as N zero bytes instead of the user's data.

Fix: probe the runtime's BUFFER_REGISTRY via the existing C-exposed
`js_buffer_is_buffer(ptr) -> i32` (`crates/perry-runtime/src/buffer.rs:601`)
before falling back to the StringHeader layout. Mirrors the pattern in
`crates/perry-stdlib/src/crypto.rs::bytes_from_ptr`. String bodies
unchanged.

Regression tests:
- `test-files/test_issue_1123_net_createserver.ts` (+ expected output)
  pins both call shapes returning `typeof === "number"`, truthy,
  distinct handles, > 0. Self-terminating (no `.listen`).
- `test-files/test_issue_1124_http_buffer_body.ts` (+ expected output)
  binds a server, prints LISTENING + CLOSED, exits cleanly via a 750ms
  self-close timer.
- `test-files/run_test_issue_1124.sh` — wire-byte assertion harness.
  Boots the TS fixture in background, curls 127.0.0.1:18993, asserts
  body hex is `89504e470d0a1a0a` (PNG file-magic). Required because
  perry-ext-http's client-side `data` listener dispatch
  (`crates/perry-ext-http/src/lib.rs:737`) routes the body through
  `alloc_string(str::from_utf8(...).unwrap_or(""))` — invalid UTF-8
  (0x89 byte) collapses to an empty string before the listener sees it,
  so we can't do the assertion in-process. Client-side binary delivery
  is a separate item.

Validated: all three regression checks pass; original /tmp repros
(test_net_server.ts dotted, test_net_server2.ts named, test_http_binary.ts
PNG magic) compile + run + wire-byte intact; text body still works.

* feat(net): #1123 followup — Server.listen + 'connection' accept loop

The initial #1123 fix in v0.5.1011 unblocked `net.createServer(...)`'s
codegen + named-import paths so the call returned a non-undefined
handle, but the handle was inert: `server.listen(port, cb)` threw
`TypeError: (number).listen is not a function`. The placeholder
`js_net_create_server` registered a handle id and stashed the user's
connection listener under `'connection'` but never bound a socket or
ran an accept loop, and `NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE` had no rows for net's
Server instance methods.

This follow-up wires the full lifecycle, mirroring
`perry-ext-http-server::js_node_http_server_listen` for the raw-TCP
shape:

- `crates/perry-ext-net/src/lib.rs` — added `ServerState` (separate
  `statics::servers()` map) + 4 new `PendingNetEvent` variants
  (`ServerConnection`/`ServerListening`/`ServerClose`/`ServerError`)
  + 4 new FFIs (`js_net_server_listen` / `_close` / `_address` /
  `_on`). Accept loop uses `spawn_blocking_with_reactor` →
  `tokio::spawn` with the same LTO-defeating dance the socket
  runner uses; accepted streams are wrapped in fresh Socket
  handles that share the existing `run_socket_task` machinery, so
  the new connection-side socket sees `.write/.end/.destroy/.on`
  dispatch through the same path as `net.connect(...)`-shaped
  sockets. Listening-server handles are now counted by both
  `js_net_has_pending` and `js_ext_net_has_active_handles` so the
  runtime stays alive until `.close()`.

- `js_net_create_server` return type flipped from `f64` to `i64`.
  The previous `id as f64` shape arrived at codegen as bare `1.0`;
  `unbox_to_i64` on the receiver in `server.listen` masked the
  lower 48 bits of `0x3FF0_0000_0000_0000` and got 0, so the FFI
  ran with handle=0 and silently bailed. Now the runtime returns
  the raw `i64` and codegen NaN-boxes with `POINTER_TAG` (matches
  the `js_node_http_create_server (I64, &[I64])` convention).

- `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs` — 5 new
  `NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE` rows for `("net", true, METHOD,
  Some("Server"))`: `listen`, `close`, `address`, `on`,
  `addListener`. Wired identically to the http-server equivalents.

- `crates/perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls.rs` — declares the 4
  new FFIs + flipped `js_net_create_server` to `I64` return.

- `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr.rs` — `Expr::NetCreateServer`
  arm now wraps the FFI return through `nanbox_pointer_inline`
  (matching the `NR_PTR` arm in `lower_native_module_dispatch`).

- `crates/perry-codegen/src/ext_registry.rs` — added the 5 new
  symbols with `OwnerKind::WellKnown("net")` so codegen-emitted
  calls auto-link `libperry_ext_net.a` even when the user TS
  doesn't `import "node:net"` explicitly (compile-package paths).

- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower.rs` + `lower_decl.rs` —
  `const s = net.createServer(...)` / bare `createServer(...)`
  let-bindings register as `("net", "Server")` so subsequent
  `s.listen/.close/.on/.address` calls find the new class-filter
  dispatch rows. Pre-fix the registration was missing entirely
  because `Expr::NetCreateServer` is a distinct HIR variant (not
  a `NativeMethodCall`), so the existing `("net", "createConnection")`
  arm never matched.

- `crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs` — 4 new
  `method("net", METHOD, true, Some("Server"))` rows so the
  manifest-consistency test in `crates/perry-codegen/tests/`
  stays green.

- `test-files/test_issue_1123_listen.ts` +
  `test-parity/expected/test_issue_1123_listen.txt` — new
  regression test that runs the full lifecycle in-process:
  createServer → listen → connect from a client →
  `client.write(Buffer.from('ping'))` → server receives 4 bytes
  → both sides close → server.close → exit 0. Self-terminating
  with a 1500ms safety timer.

- `test-files/test_issue_1123_net_createserver.ts` +
  `test-parity/expected/test_issue_1123_net_createserver.txt`
  — updated expectations to `typeof: object` (matching Node's
  `net.Server extends EventEmitter`) instead of the `typeof:
  number` the v0.5.1011 placeholder briefly surfaced. The
  switch from bare-number to NaN-boxed POINTER (above) is what
  drives the typeof change. Dropped the `=== / > 0`
  comparisons that don't make sense on a NaN-bit-pattern
  receiver.

Still TODO (tracked separately): `js_net_socket_write` and
`js_net_socket_end(data?)` read their byte payload through the
`BufferHeader` layout. A bare-string arg (`sock.write("ping")`)
reads garbage out of the `StringHeader` field layout — same
shape as the #1124 server-side bug but on the outbound side.
The new regression test passes `Buffer.from(...)` explicitly.

Validated: new test_issue_1123_listen.ts passes (LISTENING +
SERVER GOT len=4 + CLOSED + exit 0); pre-existing
test_issue_1123_net_createserver.ts still passes (with updated
typeof: object expectations); pre-existing

* fix(http): #1124 followup — client preserves binary response body

The v0.5.1011 server-side #1124 fix made `res.write(buf)` /
`res.end(buf)` actually surface the user's bytes on the wire. The
other half of the same bug lived on the HTTP CLIENT side of
perry-ext-http: when `http.get(url, cb)`'s response delivered its
body to the `'data'` listener, the bytes routed through
`alloc_string(str::from_utf8(&body).unwrap_or(""))`. Any byte
sequence that wasn't valid UTF-8 (PNG file-magic 0x89, gzip-frame,
raw binary) collapsed to the empty string before user code ever
saw a byte. `Buffer.concat(chunks)` on the receiving side gave
back an empty Buffer — the existing v0.5.1011 harness bypassed
the in-process client entirely and curl-and-xxd'd the wire bytes
from an external process to make the assertion.

The data-event dispatch in `js_http_process_pending` (line 736)
swapped from `alloc_string` to `perry_ffi::alloc_buffer`:

- Allocates a JS Buffer over the body bytes via the runtime's
  stable `js_buffer_alloc` extern.
- Tags the result with `POINTER_TAG` instead of `STRING_TAG` so
  `chunk.toString(enc)` / `chunk.length` / `Buffer.concat(...)`
  all light up on the listener arg.
- TODO comment for encoding-aware data events (Node's
  `res.setEncoding('utf8')` semantics) — default to Buffer
  today; revisit when a caller needs the string form.

The Buffer-shaped data dispatch only matters if `res.on('data',
cb)` + `res.on('end', cb)` actually register listeners. Pre-fix:

- `http.get(url, (res) => …)`'s `res` arrow param was untagged
  in HIR. `res.on('end', cb)` lowered as a generic
  `Call { callee: PropertyGet }` (not a NativeMethodCall), so
  the receiver hit `js_native_call_method` → handle dispatch
  → no IncomingMessage arm → TAG_UNDEFINED.

Two coordinated fixes:

1. `crates/perry-hir/src/lower_patterns.rs` — new
   `pre_scan_node_http_client_callback_params` matches
   `http.get(url, cb)` / `http.request(opts, cb)` /
   `https.{get,request}` and returns the `cb`'s arrow first-param
   name (the IncomingMessage). Mirrors the existing
   `pre_scan_node_http_create_server_params` shape.

2. `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call.rs` — invokes the
   pre-scan from the call-lowering preamble and registers the
   matched name as `("http", "IncomingMessage")` BEFORE the
   arrow body is lowered. After this, `res.on(...)` resolves
   to a `NativeMethodCall { method: "on", class_name:
   Some("IncomingMessage") }` and codegen dispatches via the
   existing `("http", "IncomingMessage", "on")` row →
   `js_node_http_im_on`.

3. `crates/perry-ext-http-server/src/request.rs` —
   `js_node_http_im_on`'s receiver-handle lookup gates on
   `get_handle_mut::<IncomingMessage>(handle)`. That registry
   lives in perry-ext-http-server and only knows about
   SERVER-side IM handles. Client-side IM from perry-ext-http
   missed the lookup and the function returned TAG_UNDEFINED
   without registering the listener. Now the miss path
   forwards to perry-ext-http's existing `js_http_on` extern
   (extern declared inline — perry-ext-http-server doesn't
   carry a Rust dep on perry-ext-http, so the symbol resolves
   at link time the same way `js_buffer_alloc` resolves for
   perry-ffi). The client-side IncomingMessageHandle.listeners
   map gets the callback, and the pump's terminal `'end'`
   dispatch fires correctly.

- `test-files/test_issue_1124_client_buffer.ts` +
  `test-parity/expected/test_issue_1124_client_buffer.txt` —
  server binds 18993, replies with `Buffer.from(PNG_MAGIC)`;
  client does `http.get(url, resp => resp.on('data', c =>
  chunks.push(c)).on('end', () =>
  console.log(Array.from(Buffer.concat(chunks).slice(0,8)).join(','))))`.
  Expected stdout: `137,80,78,71,13,10,26,10` + `CLOSED`.
  Pre-fix printed an empty Buffer.concat and never reached
  console.log because `'end'` didn't fire either way.
- The param is named `resp` instead of `res` to sidestep a
  separate HIR scope-leak (outer createServer's `res`
  registration visible inside the listen callback's
  http.get arrow body). The new pre-scan registration solves
  the correctness issue for typical Node patterns; the leak
  case is tracked separately.

* fix(hir): #1132 — arrow-param native-instance tags shadow correctly across scopes

An outer arrow callback's native-instance param tag (e.g. `res`
from http.createServer = ServerResponse) leaked into an inner
arrow callback re-binding the same name (inner `res` from
http.get, which should be IncomingMessage). The inner
`res.on('data')`/`res.on('end')` misrouted through ServerResponse
dispatch and silently never registered.

Two compounding bugs: (1) `lookup_native_instance` was first-match
over a push-only Vec, so the outer tag always won; (2) the
pre-scans register handler-param tags BEFORE the handler arrow's
scope, so they never got scope-truncated and leaked into the
enclosing scope.

Fix (issue option 2): last-match-wins `lookup_native_instance`
(inner registration shadows outer) + split `lower_call` into a
scope-managing wrapper that snapshots `native_instances.len()`
and truncates back on return, so pre-scan param tags are scoped
to the call that owns the handler arrow. Nested calls each get
their own snapshot, so an inner http.get's `(res)` tag is dropped
when the inner call returns, re-exposing the outer createServer's
`(res)`.

triple-nest shadowing. Full workspace tests green; all

fix(runtime): #1140 — Buffer numeric indexing reads registry-backed buffers (#1141)

`buf[i]` on an `any`-typed receiver lowers to `js_dyn_index_get`, which
read a GcHeader at `raw_ptr - GC_HEADER_SIZE` to dispatch on obj_type.
Registry-backed Buffers (the chunk an http/net `'data'` listener gets,
allocated via `alloc_buffer`/`js_buffer_alloc`) carry no GcHeader and
store 1 byte/element after an 8-byte BufferHeader. The bogus obj_type
never matched GC_TYPE_ARRAY, so the path fell through to an 8-byte-f64
inline read at `raw_ptr + 8 + idx*8`, reinterpreting the buffer's data
bytes as a denormal f64 that printed 0. `.length`/`.toString()`/
`Array.from()` all probe BUFFER_REGISTRY and were correct — that
asymmetry was the tell.

Probe `is_registered_buffer(raw_ptr)` before the GcHeader fall-through;
on a hit, bounds-check against BufferHeader.length and read the byte via
`js_buffer_get` (same source the working accessors use). In-range → byte
0..255; out-of-range/negative → undefined (Node semantics). Mirrors the
#1131/#1124 BUFFER_REGISTRY-probe pattern. JS-constructed Buffer.from()
indexing path is unchanged (regression-guarded in the test).

fix(stdlib): implement node:querystring (escape / unescape / parse / stringify)

`node:querystring` had no bindings on main — `import * as querystring
from "node:querystring"` failed at compile time with the
"namespace would compile to an empty object" error. Adds a greenfield
implementation matching Node 24's surface for the four documented
module-level functions plus the two `decode` / `encode` aliases.

Runtime (`crates/perry-stdlib/src/querystring.rs`):
  - `js_querystring_escape(s)` — Node's percent-encoder. Encodes every
    byte outside `[A-Za-z0-9-_.!~*'()]`, hex-uppercase, byte-wise over
    the UTF-8 representation.
  - `js_querystring_unescape(s)` — lenient `%XX` decoder. `+` maps to
    space (matches the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` rule);
    malformed `%XX` keeps the literal `%` and continues (Node 18+
    behaviour, not the legacy throw).
  - `js_querystring_parse(input, sep?, eq?)` — splits on `sep`
    (default `&`), each pair on `eq` (default `=`), unescapes both
    sides, accumulates into a plain Object. Repeated keys promote
    string → 2-element array on second hit, then push thereafter.
  - `js_querystring_stringify(obj, sep?, eq?)` — iterates the object's
    `keys_array` in insertion order, encodes each `(key, value)`,
    joins with `sep`. Array values produce repeated `key=v1&key=v2`.

Wiring:
  - `perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs`: add `"querystring"` to
    `NATIVE_MODULES` and `method(...)` entries for the six call
    shapes (the `#463` strict gate now recognises the surface).
  - `perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls.rs`: declare the four extern
    runtime functions.
  - `perry-codegen/src/lower_call.rs`: six `NativeModSig` rows in
    `NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE`. `decode` / `encode` route to the same
    `runtime` symbols as `parse` / `stringify`, so the test's
    `decode === parse` identity-equality check passes naturally
    (both closures resolve to the same function address).
  - `perry-stdlib/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod querystring;` + glob re-export.

Removes the now-obsolete `test_parity_querystring` entry from

feat(parity): granular node:path suite + path runtime/codegen fixes (#1163)

Splits the monolithic `test_parity_path` fixture into ~50 per-method
case files under `test-parity/node-suite/path/<method>/<case>.ts` and
adds a `--suite node-suite` selector to `run_parity_tests.sh` so the
new suite can be run on its own (with optional `--module path` to
scope further). Backwards-compatible: the default `--suite all` still
walks `test-files/*.ts` unchanged.

The granular split surfaces the long tail of `path.*` edge cases that
the single-line monolithic fixture only sampled. Fixing the cases
that diverged from `node --experimental-strip-types` flipped both the
new suite and the original `test_parity_path` from FAIL → PASS:

  crates/perry-runtime/src/path.rs:
    - `dirname("//foo")` preserves both leading slashes (`"//"`), as
      Node does. Three-or-more slashes collapse.
    - `path.resolve("")` returns the current working directory (was
      empty string).
    - `path.parse("/")` returns `{root: "/", dir: "/", base: "", …}`
      — root is part of the dir for the bare-root case (was `dir: ""`).
    - `path.format({name, ext: "txt"})` auto-inserts the separator
      dot (`"file.txt"`), matching Node's leading-`.`-tolerant rule.
    - `path.basename(base, ext)` strips the suffix even when the
      input has no slashes (`basename("foo", "foo") === ""`).
    - `path.relative(from, to)` resolves both sides through the
      cwd-aware helper, not just `normalize`, so relative inputs
      round-trip correctly.

  crates/perry-codegen/src/expr/mod.rs:
    - `Expr::PathResolve(p)` no longer no-ops back to its argument.
      The arm now lowers to a `js_path_resolve` runtime call so the
      cwd-relative absolute-path resolution that the test fixtures
      (and any real `path.resolve(x)` user) expect actually happens.

  crates/perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls.rs:
    - Declares `js_path_resolve` so the new codegen arm has a callable
      target.

  crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call/mod.rs:
    - Three arms for `path.resolve()` with zero args: lower to
      `Expr::PathResolve(Expr::String(""))` so the runtime returns
      `process.cwd()`. Without these, the no-arg form previously fell
      through to the variadic arm's `!args.is_empty()` guard and
      produced no codegen.

fix(net,ws,http): #1114 — per-tick scratch-Vec in net/ws/http pumps (#1164)

e538caa7 (#1144) fixed the fastify half of #1114 but `@perryts/mysql`
is a pure-TS driver whose bytes ride `net.Socket`, not fastify — so the
JobLoop's `setInterval` + async-MySQL tick still wedged on v0.5.1014.

`js_net_process_pending` had the *exact* `Vec::drain(..).collect()`
shape the fastify pump had pre-e538caa7: a fresh `Vec<PendingNetEvent>`
heap alloc on EVERY generated-event-loop iteration AND every inline
`await`-poll iteration via `js_stdlib_process_pending`. Under the
~1 kHz spin-throttle ceiling, that's the GC `madvise` page-churn shape
the original report's `sample` profile leaf showed.

Same `drain(..).collect()` exists unfixed in `js_ws_process_pending`
(bundled-ws) and `js_http_process_pending` (bundled-http client), both
reachable from shop-admin via the realtime broker + outbound HTTP.

Mirror the e538caa7 pattern in each pump:

  thread_local! {
      static SCRATCH: RefCell<Vec<...>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
  }
  let mut events = SCRATCH.with(|s| std::mem::take(&mut *s.borrow_mut()));
  events.clear();
  { let mut g = X.lock().unwrap(); events.append(&mut *g); }
  for ev in events.drain(..) { /* dispatch */ }
  SCRATCH.with(|s| {
      let mut slot = s.borrow_mut();
      if events.capacity() >= slot.capacity() { *slot = events; }
  });

`mem::take` makes a re-entrant pump (a user callback that inline-awaits
back into the loop) safe — it gets a fresh empty Vec, and the outer
call restores whichever buffer ended up larger. `Vec::append` moves the
queue contents into our scratch buffer without allocating, where
`drain+collect` always materialised a fresh Vec for the collect target.

fix(android): unblock build + JNI bridge for the default Android target (#1159)

Discovered while bringing up a Perry-targeted app on the Android emulator
from `main` — the Android target wasn't compilable, dlopenable, or
runnable end-to-end. None of the changes here are Android-specific
behavior tweaks; each one repairs a contract that other platforms
already honor.

## Build (compile-time)

- `perry-ui-android` `perry_system_take_screenshot` referenced
  `crate::screenshot` unconditionally, but `pub mod screenshot;` is
  `#[cfg(feature = "geisterhand")]`. Default builds failed with
  `E0433: cannot find 'screenshot' in 'crate'`. Cfg-gate the function:
  return an empty base64 string when geisterhand is off, matching the
  documented "returns empty string if capture is unavailable" contract.

- `PerryBridge.kt` `granted` expression had `==` / `||` at line *start*
  (invalid Kotlin) — fixed by moving operators to line ends.

- `richTextToggleSpan`'s inline-fun `factory: () -> T` and
  `matches: (T) -> Boolean` lambdas were called from inside
  `uiHandler.post { ... }`. Kotlin 2.0.21 rejects this without
  `crossinline`. Added.

- `PerryFirebaseMessagingService` / `PerryNotificationReceiver`
  referenced four `nativeNotification*` externs that didn't exist on
  PerryBridge. Added matching `@JvmStatic external fun` declarations
  (the Rust side already exports the JNI symbols in `system.rs`).

## Link / dlopen

- `perry-ui-android` didn't export `perry_ui_lazyvstack_set_row_height`;
  every Perry app that calls `lazyvstackSetRowHeight(list, …)` therefore
  failed `dlopen(libperry_app.so)` at launch with
  `cannot locate symbol "perry_ui_lazyvstack_set_row_height"`. Added a
  no-op stub matching the iOS one.

(The original branch also stubbed `js_gc_note_slot_layout` /
`js_gc_write_barriers_emitted` as no-ops to unblock `dlopen`; #1146 has
since landed real implementations of both on `main`, so the stubs were
dropped during this rebase.)

## JNI bridge (runtime)

- `perry-ui-android/src/widgets/securefield.rs` called
  `PerryBridge.setTextWatcher`, but the actual Kotlin entrypoint is
  `setTextChangedCallback` (textfield.rs / textarea.rs already use it).
  The mismatch aborted with `JNI DETECTED ERROR ... NoSuchMethodError`
  the moment a SecureField was constructed. Renamed the JNI call.

- Deep-link bridge (`perry-ui-android/src/deeplinks.rs` is the spec
  comment) had no Kotlin implementation: `appOnOpenUrl(J)V`,
  `appGetLaunchUrl()Ljava/lang/String;`, and
  `nativeInvokeDeepLinkCallback` were all missing. Since
  `set_handler()` discards the JNI result, the `NoSuchMethodError`
  exception stayed pending and the next JNI call (NewLocalRef from
  NavStack `get_activity`) tripped CheckJNI and aborted. Added the
  three Kotlin entrypoints + the `external fun
  nativeInvokeDeepLinkCallback` declaration on `PerryBridge`, plus
  cold-start (`onCreate`) and warm (`onNewIntent`) intent.data capture
  on `PerryActivity` that funnels through `deliverDeepLinkUrl`.

Splits node:querystring parity into per-method case files under

The new cases surfaced three real divergences from
`node --experimental-strip-types`, all fixed in
crates/perry-stdlib/src/querystring.rs:

  - `querystring.unescape` no longer rewrites `+` to space. Node only
    does that during `parse` (the historical x-www-form-urlencoded rule);
    `unescape` itself leaves `+` alone. `percent_decode` now takes a
    `plus_as_space` flag — `parse` passes true, `unescape` passes false.

    `maxKeys` (default 1000; 0, negative, NaN, or Infinity disable the
    limit). Native table + runtime decl widened from 3 to 4 f64 args.

    code split on the first byte only, so `parse(s, ";;", "::")` silently
    misbehaved. `parse` now uses string-based splitting and matches
    Node's empty-separator semantics (empty `sep` → single pair, empty
    `eq` → key-only).

non-primitive objects emit empty strings (matching Node's filter),
factored into `querystring_scalar_to_string`.

fix(codegen): #1126 declare cross-module method wrappers in consumer TU (#1170)

`Expr::SuperPropertyGet` (value form `const f = super.foo`) emits
`js_closure_alloc_singleton(@__perry_wrap_<fn>)` against the resolved
parent method's wrapper symbol. When the parent class lives in a
*different* module (the common npm-package pattern of a derived class
overriding hook methods on an imported parent — rxjs's
`OperatorSubscriber extends Subscriber` delegating `_next` / `_error` /
`_complete` to `super`), the wrapper's `define` is in the source class's
LLVM TU but the consumer TU never forward-declared the symbol. clang
failed per-TU IR validation with:

  error: use of undefined value '@__perry_wrap_perry_method_..._Subscriber___complete'

That cascaded: `OperatorSubscriber.ts` couldn't compile, the empty-stub
fallback only emits the `__init` symbol (not class methods/constructors),
so every downstream rxjs operator that referenced
`OperatorSubscriber::unsubscribe` or its constructor failed to link
(`LNK2019` on MSVC, `Undefined symbol` on macOS ld). 226 modules
succeeded, 1 failure, link death. The repro is the canonical 5-line
`import { Subject } from 'rxjs'; new Subject().subscribe(...); .next(1)`.

Fix in `crates/perry-codegen/src/expr/mod.rs` `Expr::SuperPropertyGet`:
push `(__perry_wrap_<fn>, double, [i64])` into `pending_declares` before
the singleton call. `LlModule::declare_function` (`module.rs:67`) is
dedupe-by-name and the comment explicitly notes "If a function with
the same name is later *defined* in this module, the declaration is
dropped at `to_ir` time" — so this is safe for the same-module case
(becomes a no-op) and unblocks the cross-module case. Signature is
informational per the existing pattern at `expr/mod.rs:12331` ("The
signature is for LLVM-IR well-formedness only — the runtime
closure-call machinery casts the func_ptr to its own ABI at dispatch
time").

Verified:
- 5-line rxjs repro from the issue body: pre-fix
  `Error compiling module 'OperatorSubscriber.ts'` + 28 downstream
  `LNK2019` undefined-symbol errors. Post-fix all 227 modules compile,
  link succeeds, the 2.0 MB binary prints `1`.
- Same-module value-form `super.foo` smoke test:
  `class B { greet(n){...} } class D extends B { f(n){ const g =
  super.greet; return g(n) } }` still prints `Hello, world` (declare
  drops at to_ir, no LLVM duplicate-symbol).
- `cargo test --release -p perry-codegen` clean
- `cargo test --release --workspace --exclude perry-ui-...` clean

The cascading link-error path from #1126's body (empty-stub fallback
doesn't synthesize method/constructor symbols) is not separately
fixed, but no longer fires because there's no failed-module to stub.

fix(transform): #1135 const-fold NavStack route names + warn on bail (#1168)

`NavStack(state, routes)` silently fell through to the 0-arg `NavStack()`
stub (plain UIView, no routes) when a route entry's `name` wasn't an
`Expr::String` literal at the call site. The canonical pattern of
factoring route names into shared `const`s —

    const ROUTE_HOME = "home";
    NavStack(route, [{ name: ROUTE_HOME, body: ... }])

— hit that guard because `ROUTE_HOME` lowered to `Expr::LocalGet`, not
`Expr::String`. Result: completely blank screen, zero compile diagnostics
(also reproduces with non-LocalGet state args, non-Array route args, and
non-2-field route shapes).

Fix in crates/perry-transform/src/state_desugar.rs:

1. Const-fold same-module `const X = "literal"` bindings at the `name:`
   slot. `run()` walks the top of `module.init` once into a
   `LocalId → String` env, stashed on `FreshIds`. `resolve_route_name`
   accepts `Expr::String` directly or `LocalGet(id)` ∈ env. Covers Ask #1.

2. Promote every silent bail to a `Warning:` line that names the failing
   guard and the unresolved expression kind (via `expr_kind_for_diag`).
   Imported route-name `const`s from sibling modules still need inlining
   at the call site — the warning explicitly says so. Covers Ask #2.

3. NavStack TSDoc in `types/perry/ui/index.d.ts` documents the
   string-literal / same-module-const requirement, the cross-module
   limitation, and the new bail warning. Covers Ask #3.

The 0-arg fall-through is preserved (don't break apps that lean on the
legacy stub) — the warning gates whether the user should care, not
whether the call succeeds.

  HIR shows `__navstack_register_route(..., String("a"), ...)`, no warning
- `/tmp/test_1135_bail.ts` with `name: lookupName(0)` →

fix(stdlib+ext-fastify): #1120 — fastify reply Buffer / Uint8Array bodies + auto-HEAD-for-GET (v0.5.1017) (#1172)

Closes #1120 end-to-end. Three coordinated behaviors:

1. **Body integrity** — `return Buffer.from(...)` / `return new Uint8Array([...])` used to be JSON-serialized via Buffer.toJSON / numeric-key-object form, with `reply.type(...)` overwritten by `application/json`. fix(hir+codegen): #1177 chained Buffer.concat(x).slice(...) → real Buffer.slice (#1180)

`Buffer.concat(chunks).slice(0, 8)` written inline (no intermediate
`const`) returned a "string" of length 8 whose bytes were all
empty/undefined — the user-visible bug from the #1132 verification
detour. Storing the concat result in a local first made `.slice` work
correctly, which is why the bug went unnoticed (every example in
real code happened to use the local-bound form, until someone wrote
the natural one-liner).

## Root cause

The buffer-method dispatch block at
`crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call/mod.rs:3809` is guarded by
`if let ast::Expr::Ident(arr_ident) = member.obj.as_ref()` — it only
fires when the `.slice` receiver is a bare identifier. For a chained
`Buffer.concat(chunks).slice(0,8)` the receiver is itself a `CallExpr`,
so the buffer-aware path is skipped.

The `.slice` arm at `:5396` then folded receivers like `ArrayMap`,
`ArraySort`, `Array(_)`, etc. to `Expr::ArraySlice`, but `BufferConcat`
/ `BufferFrom` / `BufferSlice` weren't in the list. Generic Call
fallthrough routed `.slice` through `js_native_call_method` which
picked String.slice semantics on the NaN-boxed Buffer pointer
— producing `typeof === "string"`, `isBuffer === false`, `length=8`,
all bytes empty.

## Fix

Two small pieces:

1. **HIR fold** (`expr_call/mod.rs:5396`): before the existing
   ArraySlice fold, recognize `BufferConcat` / `BufferFrom` /
   `BufferSlice` receivers and emit `Expr::BufferSlice { buffer,
   start, end }`. Must come BEFORE the Array shapes so a Buffer
   receiver isn't misrouted to `ArraySlice` (which would call
   `js_array_slice` on a Buffer pointer).

2. **Codegen** (`expr/mod.rs`): `Expr::BufferSlice` had a HIR variant
   declared and walked but no codegen lowering. Added an arm that
   lowers start/end to i32 (default `0` and `i32::MAX` for the
   "no end" case — `js_buffer_slice` clamps end to length) and calls
   `js_buffer_slice` directly, NaN-boxing the resulting fresh
   `BufferHeader` with POINTER_TAG. `js_buffer_slice` already
   `ptr::copy_nonoverlapping`'s bytes into a newly allocated Buffer
   registered in BUFFER_REGISTRY, so the result has its own backing
   storage independent of the parent's lifetime.

## Verified

- Issue-body repro `Array.from(Buffer.concat(chunks).slice(0, 8)).join(",")`
  → `137,80,78,71,13,10,26,10` ✓ (was `, , , , , , , `)
- `typeof Buffer.concat(c).slice(0,8) === "object"` ✓ (was `"string"`)
- `Buffer.isBuffer(Buffer.concat(c).slice(0,8)) === true` ✓ (was `false`)
- Chain of slices `Buffer.concat(c).slice(0,8).slice(2,4)` → `78,71` ✓
- `Buffer.from([1,2,3,4,5]).slice(1,4)` → `2,3,4` ✓
- Default-end `Buffer.concat(c).slice(2)` → `78,71,13,10,26,10` ✓
- Pre-existing stored-then-slice form `const b = Buffer.concat(c); b.slice(0,8)`
  still works (regression check) ✓
- Existing #1132 verification repro
  (`http.createServer` → `http.get` → `chunks` → `slice`) unchanged
- `cargo test --release -p perry-hir -p perry-codegen` clean

fix(runtime): #1114 — spin throttle is bypassed by the NOTIFIED fast-path reset (#1181)

The #1114 spin throttle (added to catch wedges where a timer deadline
reads as due-now on every iteration) reset its streak counter on every
`NOTIFIED`-fast-path return. `js_notify_main_thread` is called from
inside every `js_promise_resolve`, every `js_async_step_chain`, and
every net/ws/http event push — so a tight async tick that does any
internal promise work flips `NOTIFIED` on essentially every iteration
of the event loop. The streak counter therefore never accumulated
enough consecutive `budget_ms == 0` returns to cross the threshold,
and the throttle was structurally bypassed exactly when it was needed.

Fix: only the `cvar.wait_timeout` sleep path counts as "real progress"
for streak-reset purposes. The NOTIFIED fast-path return (both the
top-of-function atomic-load variant and the under-the-lock recheck
variant) leaves the streak untouched — neither incrementing nor
resetting it. Increments only come from the `budget_ms == 0` branch,
as before. The designed sub-µs async hot path is preserved (calls
that never hit `budget_ms == 0` never grow the streak), but a true
"timer pinned in the past + hot internal notifies" wedge now
accumulates streak across iterations and the throttle fires.

Regression test `notified_interleave_does_not_mask_wedge` reproduces
the bug shape: alternate `js_notify_main_thread() + js_wait_for_event()`
with a perpetually-due 0 ms timer past `SPIN_THROTTLE_AFTER`, then
measure one further budget-0 call. With the bug, the measured call is
~125 ns (throttle never fires). With the fix, it's ≥1 ms (throttle
sleeps as designed).

NOTE: this fix resolves the structural defect the spin-throttle was
intended to address, but shop-admin's specific JobLoop wedge has at
least one additional trigger downstream of `js_wait_for_event` —
after the throttle is correctly fitted, the first `claimJobs()` tick
through `@perryts/mysql` still leaves the server unable to respond
to subsequent HTTP requests (first request OK at 100 ms, second
times out at 30 s, server alive). The sample profile no longer shows
the previous `madvise`-thrash pattern; the main thread now shows
`__psynch_cvwait` dominant, which suggests the wedge is now about
something else holding the runtime back (perhaps tx-release in the
@perryts/mysql pool, or a tokio scheduler interaction). Leaving #1114
open with this fix as one of two components.

fix(transform): #1196 rewrite user returns in StateExit::Goto state bodies (#1197)

+ `prepend_done_before_returns` to state bodies exiting via `Yield`

inside such a state body (e.g. an `if (...) return X` immediately
before a `for ... await ...` loop) fell through to
`rewrite_returns_to_labeled_break`, which rewrote the return to
`[Expr(X), LabeledBreak]` — value discarded, IterResult never set.

The post-step code then read stale IterResult from the previous
yield (done=false) and dispatched `AsyncStepChain`, re-invoking the
step closure on the same state — an infinite loop that allocated
~5 MB of arena per outer call. Visible signature: ~123 MB arena per
call, GC every ~250 ms, 90%+ CPU. Discovered while debugging #1114;
shop-admin's `claimJobs` job loop tripped this on every tick.

Applies the same conditional rewrite the other two arms already do.

fix(querystring): #1175 store proto-shadowed keys (constructor, toString, …) as own properties (#1188)

`querystring.parse("a=1&__proto__=evil&constructor=ctor")` silently
dropped the `constructor` (and any other Object.prototype-shadowed) key
on Perry: `Object.keys(r)` returned `['a', '__proto__']` instead of
`['a', '__proto__', 'constructor']`, and `r.constructor` came back as
`[Function (anonymous)]` instead of `'ctor'`.

## Root cause

`push_parsed_pair` in `crates/perry-stdlib/src/querystring.rs` used
`js_object_get_field_by_name(obj, key)` for duplicate detection. That
helper walks the prototype chain, so for keys that exist on
`Object.prototype` — `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`,
`hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf`, `propertyIsEnumerable`,
`toLocaleString` — it returned the inherited `[Function]` instead of
`undefined`. The `existing != undefined` arm then misclassified the
[Function] pointer as an existing value, took the "promote to array"
branch, and called `js_array_push_f64` on a function pointer cast to
`*mut ArrayHeader`. The set silently failed (no key landed in
`keys_array`) and the user value never got stored.

Node sidesteps this entirely by building the parse result on a
null-prototype object (`Object.create(null)`), so no key is ever
shadowed by a prototype-chain entry. Perry doesn't have full
null-prototype support today, but we can get the same observable
behavior by asking explicitly for own-field values.

## Fix

Swap the duplicate-check from `js_object_get_field_by_name`
(proto-walking) to `js_object_get_own_field_or_undef` (own-field
lookup that returns undefined for non-own keys). Repeated keys still
read through `js_object_get_field_by_name` for the actual value bits
only after own-field membership is confirmed — at that point no
proto-chain walk can lie about the value.

Added a GC-header `obj_type == GC_TYPE_ARRAY` check on the "POINTER_TAG
→ push onto existing array" branch, mirroring the same guard
`append_stringify_value` already had.

Added `js_object_get_own_field_or_undef` to the `perry_runtime`
crate-root re-export list so perry-stdlib can call it without reaching
into the private `object::object_ops` module path.

## Why not `js_object_has_own`

First attempt used `js_object_has_own` (own-keys-array membership) for
the duplicate check. That broke the parity test because of a subtle
interaction with the transition-cache shape-sharing optimization:

Object1 is allocated. `set_field("a")` records the null→"a" transition
and stores a fresh `["a"]` keys_array. `set_field("b")` then mutates
the SAME unshared keys_array in place — it now reads `["a","b"]`. The
transition cache still points at this same array.

Object2 is allocated. `set_field("a")` hits the cached null→"a"
transition, stamps SHAPE_SHARED on the (now `["a","b"]`) array, and
sets `(*obj2).keys_array` to that shared array. From here, walking
`obj2.keys_array` finds BOTH "a" and "b" — but `obj2.fields[1]` is
still `undefined` because nothing has actually set "b" on obj2 yet.

`js_object_has_own` walks keys_array only, so it returned TRUE for
"b" on the fresh obj2 and the parse logic promoted to an array
containing `[undefined, "2"]`. `js_object_get_own_field_or_undef`
walks keys_array AND reads the field-slot value, so it returns
`undefined` for the bogus shared key and the parse logic does the
right thing.

## Verified

- Issue-body repro:
  `parse("a=1&__proto__=evil&constructor=ctor")` →
  `Object.keys = ['a', '__proto__', 'constructor']`,
  `r.constructor === 'ctor'`. Byte-for-byte match with Node.
- Prototype-pollution defense: `{}["evil"]` is `undefined` after the
  parse — the `__proto__` key is stored as a regular data property.
- Transition-cache poisoning regression: ordered parses
  `parse("a=1&b=2&a=3")` → `parse("a=1&b=2")` → `parse("a:1;b:2", ";", ":")`
  now all produce correct results (pre-amend the second and third
  fell into the `[null, "2"]` promote-to-array trap).
- Existing parity test `test-parity/node-suite/querystring/parse/basic.ts`
  and the new `prototype-pollution-keys.ts` both byte-match Node.
- `cargo test --release -p perry-runtime -p perry-stdlib` clean
  (347 + 64 passing).

## Out of scope

`Object.getPrototypeOf(parse(...))` still returns the result object's
contents rather than `null` — Perry doesn't implement true
null-prototype objects (`Object.create(null)` and `{}` are
observationally identical, both expose `Object.prototype.constructor`).
The pollution-defense goal #1175 cites is met without that machinery
because Perry doesn't implement `__proto__` as an accessor either, so
the `__proto__=evil` key naturally stays a regular data property.
Filing the null-prototype gap separately is the right next step if we
want full `[Object: null prototype]` parity.

* fix(runtime): #1199 honor console.dir(value, { depth }) inspect cap

`console.dir(obj, { depth: N })` previously ignored the options arg —
codegen routed `console.dir(x, opts)` through `js_console_log_dynamic(x)`
and dropped `opts`, so nested objects always collapsed at the hardcoded
Node-default depth of 2.

four `depth > 2` checks in `format_jsvalue` / `format_jsvalue_for_json`
with `depth > inspect_max_depth()`. Add `js_console_dir_with_options`
which decodes `options.depth` from a NaN-boxed object literal:
- missing key / non-object options → default 2
- `null` → `usize::MAX` (Node's unlimited)
- non-negative integer → that many levels of nesting
- negative / NaN / -Infinity → clamp to 0 (Node coerces to zero)
- +Infinity → unlimited

no-options case keeps the existing fast path (no behavior change). The
thread-local override is restored on return, so callers further up the
stack (concurrent `console.log` inside the format closure if any) are
unaffected.

fix(runtime): #1202 preserve function names for console output parity (#1229)

`console.log(namedFunction)` previously printed `[Function (anonymous)]`
because the runtime had no way to recover the JS name from a closure's
compiled function pointer — codegen-emitted symbols are local and the
macOS linker's `-dead_strip` removes their names from the binary, so a
`dladdr` lookup at runtime comes back empty.

Add a sidecar `FUNCTION_NAME_REGISTRY` keyed on the compiled-function
address. Codegen emits a `js_register_function_name(ptr, name_bytes,
len)` call in each module's `__perry_init_strings_<prefix>` for two
shapes that Node also labels:
  - top-level `function name() {}` declarations — registered against
    the singleton-wrapper `__perry_wrap_<name>` (the address that
    `js_closure_alloc_singleton` actually stamps into ClosureHeader for
    FuncRef references)
  - arrow / function-expression bindings at module top-level (`const
    arrow = () => 1`) — registered against the inline closure symbol
    `perry_closure_<modprefix>__<func_id>` that `js_closure_alloc` uses

`format_jsvalue`'s GC_TYPE_CLOSURE branch consults the registry: a
match yields `[Function: <name>]`, miss falls back to the previous
`[Function (anonymous)]` (matching Node for nested / truly anonymous
closures). Names with empty / underscore-prefixed identifiers
(synthesized factory/iife/lambda names) are skipped so we don't label
internal scaffolding.

Tests: `node-suite/console/output/function-format` now matches Node
byte-for-byte (`function: [Function: named]` / `arrow: [Function:
arrow]`). Existing `node-suite/util` (24 tests) still 100% pass.

fix(runtime): #1204 detect circular refs in console formatting (#1228)

Previously, `console.log({ a: a })` (or any self-referencing object/array)
recursively expanded until the hardcoded depth-2 fallback collapsed nested
structures to `[Object]` / `[Array]`. Node detects cycles up front and
emits Node-compatible reference markers — `<ref *N>` at the cycle's head,
`[Circular *N]` at the back-edge.

Add a thread-local `INSPECT_CIRCULAR` state (ancestor pointer stack + per-
pointer ref-ID map + monotonic counter), reset at every top-level entry
into `format_jsvalue` / `format_jsvalue_for_json`. At each of the four
object/array branches, the new `inspect_enter_circular` / `inspect_finish_
circular` helpers wrap body formatting:

  1. Cycle check FIRST — back-edges win over the depth-2 truncation so
     `a={b:{c:{d:a}}}` still prints `<ref *1> { b: { c: { d: [Circular *1] } } }`
     even though depth=3 would otherwise collapse to `[Object]`.
  2. Depth check — unchanged token (`[Object]` / `[Array]`) but routed
     through `inspect_finish_circular` to keep the stack balanced.
  3. Compute body via existing logic, then `inspect_finish_circular` pops
     the pointer and prepends `<ref *N> ` if a back-edge to it was found.

two-object mutual cycle, and self-referencing array — matches Node byte-
for-byte. Existing `node-suite/util` (24 tests) still 100% pass.

which never invokes `toString` / `Symbol.toPrimitive` — exactly what
the `no-tostring-on-string-format` test asserts (the user's `toString`
must NOT fire during inspect formatting).

Sorting by key makes the output deterministic across runs even though
the side-table is a HashMap.

`console.dir(obj, { showHidden: true })` previously printed
non-enumerable properties as if they were ordinary keys (`{ visible: 1,
hidden: 2 }`). Node wraps them in brackets (`{ visible: 1, [hidden]: 2 }`)
when showHidden is truthy and hides them entirely when it isn't. Wire
the option through:

     (truthy / null / undefined / numeric / non-object) and flip the
     guard for the duration of the print.

     key when `descriptors_in_use()` is true:
       - enumerable → `key: value` (unchanged)
       - non-enumerable + showHidden → `[key]: value` (Node bracketing)
       - non-enumerable + !showHidden → skip
     The global-descriptors-in-use flag means objects that never had
     `Object.defineProperty` called on them still hit the hot path
     with zero per-key lookup overhead.

fix(codegen-wasm): #1081 sibling instances — constructors, statics, async imports (#1239)

* fix(codegen-wasm): #1081 sibling instances — constructors, statics, async imports

Three call shapes still produced WASM that failed validation with
"expected i64 but nothing on stack" / "expected i64 but got nothing"
after #1081's narrow fix landed. All three share the same root cause:
the function signature was declared `... -> i64` in the type/function
section, but body emission was driven by a different (looser) heuristic
that disagreed about whether the function returns a value.

1. Class constructors. `func_section` declares them as
   `(this, ...params) -> i64` unconditionally, but
   `compile_class_constructor` passed `in_returning_func=false` to
   `emit_stmt`. An explicit `return;` inside a constructor body emitted
   a bare `Instruction::Return` with empty operand stack. Fix: pass
   `in_returning_func=true` so `Stmt::Return(None)` pushes UNDEFINED.

2. Class static methods. `func_section` also declares them
   `(params) -> i64` unconditionally, but `compile_function` derived
   the signature from `body.iter().any(has_return) || name == "main"`.
   A static method whose only exit was `throw` (no `return`) compiled
   to a body that returned no value while the WASM type declared one.
   Fix: split `compile_function` into a thin wrapper plus
   `compile_function_with_signature(force_returning: bool)` and call it
   with `true` for static methods.

3. Async function imports. `__async_<name>` is declared as
   `(i64 × param_count) -> i64`, but `func_param_counts` skipped async
   funcs entirely, so the call-site padding in
   `Expr::Call → ExternFuncRef` never fired. A source-level
   `await foo(a, b)` against `async function foo(a, b, c?)` emitted
   exactly two `i64` pushes before `call __async_foo`, which V8
   rejected. Fix: insert the async import index into
   `func_param_counts` alongside `async_func_imports`.

Discovered against Mango's `--target web` build, which exercises all
three shapes (TLS upgrade constructor, SCRAM credential static helpers,
optional-arg `authenticate(cmd, creds, speculative?)`). All three were
needed to get the bundle to validate; after this change, the Mango
WASM passes `wasm-tools validate` and boots in headless Chrome.

## Approach

For each file: extract topical function groups into sibling .rs files
under a new directory (`foo.rs` → `foo/mod.rs` + `foo/{group_a,...}.rs`).
mod.rs is a re-export hub with **explicit named re-exports** —
`pub(crate) use foo::*;` does NOT transitively expose names through
an outer `pub(crate) use crate::module::*;` glob, so external callers
would silently lose visibility (this was the root cause of the broken
sibling agents' work earlier; fixed by enumerating every `pub fn` by
name in mod.rs). Sibling files use `use super::*;` to access each
other's items via mod.rs's named re-exports.

Cross-sibling shared types/constants (e.g. `MAX_SCALAR_ARRAY_LEN`,
`ExactReceiverFact`, `NativeArgKind`) are `pub(crate)` or `pub(super)`
in their defining sibling and re-exported through mod.rs.

The native_table dispatch table (5,875 LOC of `pub(super) const
NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE: &[NativeModSig] = &[ ... ]`) was switched to
`pub(super) static NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE: LazyLock<Vec<NativeModSig>>`
that concatenates per-family `*_ROWS` slices from 13 sub-modules in
declaration order. All consumers used `.iter()` only, so the
const→static change is source-compatible and `iter_native_module_table`
still yields the same `&'static NativeModSig` projections in the same
order (preserves the `perry-api-manifest` drift contract).

existing `lint` job. Excludes generated artifacts (Cargo.lock, .po
translations, generated API docs, binary fixtures, CHANGELOG.md) and
honors a one-line allowlist (`gc.rs` for now). On violation, prints
the offending files + an inline pointer to this commit's recipe.

Threshold is configurable via `PERRY_FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD` env var;
default 5000. The eventual target is 2000 — to tighten, ship one or

* fix(runtime+stdlib): #1175 querystring.parse returns null-prototype object

Node's querystring.parse uses Object.create(null) so __proto__ /
constructor land as own data properties and Object.getPrototypeOf(result)

allocator.

fix(stdlib+runtime): #1182 preserve UTF-16LE lone surrogates from StringDecoder (#1245)

* fix(stdlib+runtime): #1182 preserve UTF-16LE lone surrogates from StringDecoder

`StringDecoder('utf16le').end()` was emitting U+FFFD whenever a lone high
surrogate was buffered across writes, because Perry's runtime string was
strictly UTF-8. Node returns the raw surrogate code unit, so

`JSON.stringify` to escape lone surrogates as `\uXXXX` while re-pairing
adjacent (high, low) WTF-8 triples back into the astral codepoint's UTF-8.

fix(ui-ios): #1178 wire appGroupSet/Get/Delete to UserDefaults(suiteName:) (#1256)

#675 shipped the perry/system App Group surface but the iOS bridge was
a placeholder — calls landed in an in-process HashMap, so widget
extensions sharing the App Group container never saw the values the
host app wrote.

Resolution chain:

1. `[ios] app_group = "group.com.example.shared"` in perry.toml is read
   by `read_app_metadata` into a new `AppMetadata.app_group` field.
2. perry-codegen emits a single `perry_app_group_init(ptr, len)` call
   at the top of `main`'s prelude (skipped when no suite is
   configured).
3. New `perry-runtime::app_group` module stores the suite in a
   process-global `OnceLock<String>` and exposes both a Rust accessor
   and a C-ABI `perry_app_group_suite_name` shim so platform FFI
   crates that intentionally avoid a perry-runtime Cargo dep (macOS)
   can still reach it.
4. perry-ui-ios's stub is replaced with `UserDefaults(suiteName:)`
   reads/writes. When no suite is configured the FFI emits a clearer
   first-call diagnostic naming the missing `[ios] app_group` key
   instead of silently lying about cross-process behavior.
5. perry-ui-macos picks up the baked suite first, then falls back to
   `PERRY_APP_GROUP` (kept for the existing dev/CI override) and
   finally the `group.perryapp` fallback.
6. bundle_ios.rs auto-writes (or augments) `app.entitlements` with
   `com.apple.security.application-groups` so the user's codesign
   flow picks the entitlement up without manual editing — idempotent
   with the deeplinks pass that may already have written the file.
