* fix(widget): #1179 entryFields nested types + render formatter whitelist

Two codegen gaps the issue flagged in passing — fixed alongside the
ts_source landing so #1179 closes the whole user story.

1. `entryFields` arrays-of-objects no longer collapse to `String`.
   The old parser only recognized string-literal values (`'number'`,
   `'boolean'`, otherwise `String`), so any nested shape was lost and
   SwiftUI `ForEach` over the field was broken. The new
   `parse_entry_field_value_spec` recursively handles:
   - `'string' | 'number' | 'boolean'` + `?` / `[]` suffixes;
   - `[X]` array literal → `Array<X>`;
   - `{ k: <spec>, ... }` object literal → `Object`.

2. Whitelisted function calls inside `render` text content. Previously
   `Text(Math.round(entry.x))` or `Text(entry.x.toFixed(2))` fell into
   `parse_text_content`'s catch-all and silently produced `Text("")`.
   The new `WidgetTextContent::Formatted` carries a small whitelist
   (`String(x)`, `Number(x)`, `x.toString()`, `x.toFixed(n)`,
   `Math.round/floor/ceil(x)`) that the three widget codegen crates
   (SwiftUI, Glance, Wear Tiles) transpile to native equivalents.
   Calls outside the whitelist still fall back to an empty literal so
   the user can switch to a supported formatter or pre-format in the
   provider.

Stable-hash impls + the IR re-exports follow the new variants so
nothing downstream sees a hole.

fix(ui-macos): #1198 stateBindTextfield two-way binding cursor reset (#1255)

The macOS bind_textfield path had no suppress flag: every state.set()
inside the user's onChange ran the TEXTFIELD_BINDINGS loop and re-wrote
the field via setStringValue, which resets the cursor / selection on
each keystroke. Windows and GTK4 already use a per-binding Cell<bool>
suppress to skip the echo-back during user-initiated edits; this brings
macOS in line.

- TextFieldBinding is now Rc-shared and holds a `suppress: Cell<bool>`.
- A new TEXTFIELD_TO_BINDING map lets the textfield change observer
  in widgets/textfield.rs find the binding for the textfield it fired
  on and toggle suppress around the user closure call.
- state_set's TEXTFIELD_BINDINGS loop skips suppressed bindings and
  wraps the setStringValue call in suppress=true so nested state_set
  re-entries also short-circuit.
- bind_textfield now seeds the field with the current state value on
  registration (matches GTK4 / Windows behavior).

* deps: bump RustCrypto digest stack to 0.11 family (#1238)

Coordinated migration of the digest 0.10 -> 0.11 stack across our direct
deps. AEAD stack (aes/aes-gcm/aes-kw/cipher) stays on 0.8/0.10/0.3
pending aes-gcm 0.11 (still RC).

Bumps:
  sha1   0.10 -> 0.11   (perry-stdlib, perry-jsruntime)
  sha2   0.10 -> 0.11   (perry-stdlib, perry-jsruntime, perry-updater, perry)
  md-5   0.10 -> 0.11   (perry-stdlib, perry-jsruntime)
  hmac   0.12 -> 0.13   (perry-stdlib, perry-jsruntime)
  pbkdf2 0.12 -> 0.13   (perry-stdlib; `simple` feature replaced by `hmac`)
  hkdf   0.12 -> 0.13   (perry-stdlib)

Call-site updates for the digest 0.11 / hmac 0.13 API:

- `Hmac::new_from_slice` now lives behind the `KeyInit` trait (moved out
  of the `Mac` trait import). Added `use hmac::KeyInit;` everywhere the
  call appears: perry-stdlib `webcrypto.rs`, `crypto.rs` (`js_crypto_hmac_sha256`,
  `js_crypto_hmac_sha256_bytes`, `js_crypto_create_hmac`), and
  perry-jsruntime `ops.rs::op_perry_hmac`.
- `Sha256: io::Write` impl was removed in sha2 0.11, so the
  `std::io::copy(&mut file, &mut hasher)` shortcut in
  `perry-lock::sha256_of_file` no longer compiles. Replaced with the
  same explicit 64 KiB read loop that `attest.rs::sha256_hex` already
  uses (and which is what `io::copy` was doing internally anyway).
- `Sha256::finalize()` now returns `hybrid_array::Array<u8, N>` instead
  of `generic_array::GenericArray`. `Array` doesn't impl `LowerHex`, so
  `format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize())` in `attest.rs` was replaced with
  the equivalent `hex::encode(hasher.finalize())` (perry already depends
  on `hex = "0.4"`).

`cargo tree` still shows two digest versions — that's expected. The
transitive consumers (jsonwebtoken, sqlx, elliptic-curve, ed25519-dalek,
curve25519-dalek, p256/p384, argon2/blake2) all still pin digest 0.10
internally; they don't leak into our code, and the same coexistence
already holds for cipher (0.4.4 + 0.5.1).

Dependabot ignore list narrowed to just aes/aes-gcm/aes-kw/cipher —
those still need to land in a coordinated AEAD-stack PR once aes-gcm
0.11 ships stable. The original noise pattern (one-at-a-time digest
breaking PRs like closed #1157) is now resolved by the actual bump.

fix(android): unblock build path — bionic libc + Kotlin 2.0 errors (#1258)

Two unrelated build-time errors prevent `cargo build --target
aarch64-linux-android` and `./gradlew assembleDebug` from succeeding
on a clean tree. Both surfaced while trying to reproduce #1160 (the
HWUI destroyed-mutex SIGABRT) — without them the repro can't even

  (returns `[0,0,0]` on Android).

- perry-ui-android template `PerryBridge.kt`: two Kotlin 2.0
  errors in code that previously compiled under older Kotlin:
  * `requestGeolocationPermission`: a multi-line `||` expression
    with `==` at the start of the continuation line — Kotlin
    terminates the statement at the `)` of the first line, so the
    rest parses as a fresh expression and `if (granted)` sees an
    `Int`. Restructured so each line ends with the dangling
    operator (`==` then `||`).
  * `richTextToggleSpan` inline fun passes its `factory` and
    `matches` lambdas into a `uiHandler.post { ... }` block. Kotlin
    2.0 requires `crossinline` on lambdas that may be invoked from
    a different scope. Added.

* fix(api-manifest): register dispatch entries added in #1257

The cargo-test CI's `every_dispatch_entry_has_manifest_counterpart`
drift guard requires every row in NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE to have a
matching API_MANIFEST entry. PR #1257 added 14 dispatch rows
(__primitive_box::Number/String/Boolean, util/types and util.types
isNumberObject/isStringObject/isBooleanObject/isBoxedPrimitive,
buffer::isAscii, buffer::isUtf8, events::on module-level) without
registering them in the manifest.

* fix(api-manifest): hide internal pseudo-modules from docs / .d.ts

The PR added dispatch + manifest entries on two pseudo-modules
(`__primitive_box` for `new Number/String/Boolean(...)` boxing and
`util.types` as the namespace-access alias of `util/types`). Registering
them satisfied the dispatch-entry-needs-manifest guard but broke two
others:

  * `known_modules_consistent_with_manifest` rejected them because
    neither was in `NATIVE_MODULES`.
  * `api-docs-drift` would have leaked `__primitive_box` and
    `util.types` into the public Markdown + .d.ts artifacts.

accepts entries from either list; the Markdown / .d.ts emitter (and
its `*_contains_every_module` tests) skip them. Regenerate the docs.

* refactor(hir): replace `__primitive_box` pseudo-module with dedicated IR variant

`new Number(x)` / `new String(x)` / `new Boolean(x)` used to lower to
`NativeMethodCall { module: "__primitive_box", method: ... }`, abusing
the module-dispatch table with a synthetic module name. That forced
the dispatch-table guard to demand matching API_MANIFEST entries,
which in turn forced `INTERNAL_MODULES` + emit-side filters to keep
`__primitive_box` out of the public Markdown / .d.ts.

variant — mirroring the `DateNew` / `MapNew` / `SetNew` pattern other
global constructors already use. Codegen lowers it directly to
`js_boxed_{number,string,boolean}_new`, no dispatch table involved.

- 3 `__primitive_box::*` rows from `API_MANIFEST`.
- `__primitive_box` from `INTERNAL_MODULES`.

fix(fastify): #1240 request.json() returns parsed body (#1259)

The native dispatch table routed the `json` method to `js_fastify_ctx_json`
(the Hono `c.json(data, status?)` reply helper) regardless of which side of
the request/reply pair the receiver came from — both share the FastifyContext
handle, so codegen can't disambiguate at lowering time. A zero-arg
`request.json()` therefore arrived in the reply shim with both args padded
to NaN-boxed undefined; the shim serialized the string "undefined" as the
response body and set `ctx.sent = true`, silently 400-ing every POST
endpoint that used the Fetch-style accessor.

Detect the zero-arg shape (`data == NaN-boxed undefined`) inside
`js_fastify_ctx_json` and route to `js_fastify_req_json`, mirroring the
Fetch API `Request.json()` semantics. Applied in both perry-stdlib and
perry-ext-fastify since they ship duplicate dispatch shims.

Adds test-files/test_issue_1240_fastify_request_json.ts + run_test_issue_1240.sh
as a wire-level regression harness.

fix(jsruntime): #1195 default-import member name → "default" (#1263)

`import YAML from "yaml"` (default import of a V8-fallback module) bound
the local alias only into `import_function_v8_specifiers` — the
`import_function_origin_names` map was left untouched. When the user
later wrote `YAML.parse(...)`, the StaticMethodCall arm in
`expr/static_method.rs` looked up the local name in
`import_function_origin_names`, missed, and fell back to the local name
itself ("YAML"). The V8 bridge then asked the module namespace for the
property "YAML", which doesn't exist (the proxy module re-exports the
default under the literal "default" key), so the call returned undefined.

Insert the local→"default" override in the Default import-specifier arm
of compile.rs alongside the existing prefix / specifier registrations.
This mirrors the Named-with-rename arm which already records the
local→imported mapping for the same reason.

Verified locally with the yaml@2.9.0 repro: `YAML.parse("a: 1\nb:...")`
now returns a real object instead of undefined.

Follow-up scope (not in this PR): V8-handle arrays don't yet support
`arr[i]` indexing from compiled native code. `obj.b.length` works (V8
dispatch path), but `obj.b[0]` returns undefined. That needs a separate
dispatch-table entry for `js_handle_array_get` along the `[]` lowering.

feat(host-embed): #1088 --output-type staticlib + Event Loop FFI (#1266)

Adds two pieces of host-embedding surface so Rust / C / C++ hosts (winit,
Qt, GTK4) can link compiled TypeScript into their own process and drive
the event loop themselves.

  1. `perry compile --output-type staticlib` produces a `.a` / `.lib`
     archive. Codegen reuses the existing `is_dylib` branch (now also
     triggered by `output_type == "staticlib"`), so the entry-module
     emits `perry_module_init` instead of `main`, skips the embedded
     event-loop poll body, and skips app-group / geisterhand init that
     only makes sense for a stand-alone executable. The link step uses
     `ar crs` (Unix) or `lib.exe /OUT:` (Windows) and skips
     runtime/stdlib archiving — the host links those alongside.

  2. Unified host-embedding FFI in `perry-runtime/src/event_pump.rs`:

     - `perry_poll() -> i32`              drains microtasks + stdlib +
                                          jsruntime pumps; returns the
                                          microtask count
     - `perry_has_work() -> i32`          1 while microtasks pending,
                                          any of the 3 timer queues has
                                          a deadline, or stdlib /
                                          jsruntime has active handles
     - `perry_next_wake_ms() -> f64`      min of the 3 timer-queue
                                          deadlines, or -1 if none
     - `perry_set_wake_callback(cb, ctx)` register host wake hook;
                                          invoked from
                                          `js_notify_main_thread` on
                                          top of the existing condvar
                                          path so hosts sleeping on OS
                                          primitives (winit's
                                          EventLoopProxy, eventfd, …)
                                          wake instantly instead of
                                          polling

`js_notify_main_thread` invokes the wake callback before the
WAITER_COUNT fast-path return — single atomic-load when no host is
listening, so callers that never register pay essentially nothing.

Adds `test-files/test_issue_1088_staticlib.ts` + `run_test_issue_1088.sh`:
the run script compiles the TS as a staticlib, asserts the archive has
no `T main` symbol and does export `T perry_module_init`, links a C
smoke host that walks all four facade functions + the wake-callback
round-trip, and runs it.

Closes #1088.

fix(stdlib): #1193 cheerio chain through any-typed intermediates (#1267)

`cheerio.load(html).select(".x").text()` worked as a direct chain because
the codegen's static NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE dispatch preserved the cheerio
receiver-type tag end-to-end. The moment user code landed an intermediate
in a `let` binding (`const sel = $.select(".x")`), the SelectionHandle
came back NaN-boxed as a generic pointer and the follow-up `.text()` saw
a number-typed receiver. The static path then declined the call and it
fell through to `js_handle_method_dispatch` — which until this commit had
no cheerio arm, so every `.text()` / `.length` / `.attr(...)` surfaced as
`(number).<method> is not a function`.

Adds a runtime-side `dispatch_cheerio` arm in
`perry-stdlib/src/cheerio.rs` and wires it into
`common/dispatch.rs::js_handle_method_dispatch`, gated on a disjoint
method set so colliding handle ids from other registries can't fall
through to a cheerio shim. Routes both `CheerioHandle` (document-level
`select`) and `CheerioSelectionHandle` (selection-level `text` / `html`
/ `attr` / `length` / `first` / `last` / `eq` / `find` / `children` /
`parent` / `hasClass` / `is` / `toArray` / `texts` / `attrs`) to their
existing FFI calls.

Adds `test-files/test_issue_1193_cheerio_chain.ts` +
`run_test_issue_1193.sh` covering the two regression shapes — bound
selection (`const sel = $.select(".x"); sel.text()`) and bound document
(`const doc = $; doc.select(".x").text()`) — both via the runtime
fallback path.

## Not in this PR

The user's original `$(sel)` callable form still throws `value is not a
function`. Making it work requires the codegen to recognise a Call
expression whose callee resolves to a value of type CheerioHandle and
either rewrite it to `.select(sel)` at HIR-lower time or route the
function-call shape directly to `js_cheerio_select`. Tried a
runtime-side closure wrap on `js_cheerio_load`; it makes `$()` work but
breaks the static `$.select(...)` path (the codegen sees the closure-
wrapped receiver as a function value and stops dispatching through the
cheerio NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE rows). The clean fix is at the codegen layer
and tracked as a follow-up on #1193.

fix(runtime): #1136 #1129 lower iOS-device heap-pointer guards (#1281)

`for…of` over a `String.split()` result and object-literal-return +
destructure both silently returned wrong values on the iOS *device*
target (no error, no crash) because three categories of pointer
guards rejected legitimate libsystem_malloc pointers:

1. Cfg-gated 2 TB `HEAP_MIN` on macOS that also covered iOS / tvOS /
   watchOS / visionOS — `clean_arr_ptr`, `js_array_grow` forwarding,
   `js_value_length_f64` (POINTER_TAG + raw-bitcast paths), and
   `is_valid_obj_ptr`. iOS device libsystem_malloc lands in the same
   low GB range as Android/Linux, so every real pointer was null-ed.
   `js_value_length_f64` returning 0 is what made `arr.length` collapse
   to 0 in the failing `for…of`, and made `segments.length === 0`
   wrongly true after the destructure.

2. Unconditional 16 MB pointer floor (`< 0x1000000`) in five object
   field-access helpers — `js_object_get_field` (×4 variants),
   `js_object_get_field_by_name`, `js_object_set_field_by_name`,
   `js_object_has_own`, `ensure_key_in_keys_array`,
   `own_key_present`, `js_object_get_own_field_or_undef`. iOS device
   heap pointers below 16 MB hit this gate and silently routed through
   the small-handle dispatch path (or returned undefined), which is
   why the destructured `segments` came out empty.

3. Same as (2) for the iOS family on macOS's `is_valid_obj_ptr` — the
   downstream `GcHeader.obj_type` check is the real liveness guard,
   so lowering these thresholds to 64 KB (matches the bar already used
   in `js_object_get_field_ic_miss`) does not weaken correctness.

The macOS host, iOS simulator (mimalloc on the host), Linux, Windows,
and Android paths are unchanged in behavior: the simulator's
allocations still land above 2 TB and pass the lowered guard cleanly,
and the GcHeader/obj_type validation downstream still rejects bogus
pointers.

fix(hir): #1193 dispatch $(sel) on a CheerioAPI handle to cheerio.select (#1285)

* ci(test): gate doc-tests behind opt-in + label/dispatch trigger

Aligns doc-tests with parity and compile-smoke: PRs no longer pay the

- workflow_dispatch with `run_extended_tests=true` (maintainers)

* fix(hir): #1193 dispatch $(sel) on a CheerioAPI handle to cheerio.select

`const $ = load(html); $(sel).text()` lowered the inner `$(sel)` to a
generic `Call { callee: LocalGet($) }`, which the runtime tried to
invoke as a function and threw "TypeError: value is not a function" the
moment cheerio's canonical entrypoint ran. The native dispatch table
already has cheerio rows for `select`/`text`/etc., but nothing in
fix_local_native_instances knew that `load()`'s return value is a
callable handle, so the rewrite to `NativeMethodCall` never happened.

This change extends the local-native rewriter so:

- `load`/`loadFragment` register the local as a ("cheerio", "CheerioAPI")
  handle.
- `Call { callee: LocalGet(id) }` on such a handle becomes
  `NativeMethodCall { module: "cheerio", method: "select", object: id }`.
- Chained `<NativeMethodCall>.method(args)` where the inner method
  returns a CheerioSelection (select/find/children/parent/first/last/eq)
  becomes a cheerio NativeMethodCall, so `$(sel).text()`,
  `$(sel).find(x).html()`, etc. all route through the existing dispatch
  rows.
- `PropertyGet` with property `length` on the same shapes also rewrites,
  since cheerio models length as a zero-arg method row.

Adds a perry-hir unit test that asserts the chained
`$('.x').text()` / `$('.x').length` IR shape after lowering, and an
issue_1193 repro under test-files/.

fix(runtime): #1225 Buffer.from(buf) shares .buffer identity with source (#1287)

Node carves `Buffer.from(src)` from a shared 8 KiB pool slab so
`src.buffer === cp.buffer` even though the bytes are copied.  Perry had
no pool, so the `.buffer` getter returned each BufferHeader pointer and
the identity check was always false.

Track an ArrayBuffer-identity alias per buffer in a thread-local map.
`Buffer.from(buf)` (the buffer-source branch in `js_buffer_from_value`)
propagates src's resolved alias onto the copy; the `.buffer` getter in
field_get_set.rs and value/dynamic_object.rs returns the alias when set.
Uint8Array sources are skipped — Node's `Buffer.from(uint8Array)`
spec-allocates a fresh ArrayBuffer and never shares with the source.

Bytes remain a real copy (mutation isolation preserved).  Only the
`.buffer` `===` identity is shared, which is what the issue asks for;
the full pool model (unrelated `Buffer.from(string)` calls sharing
`.buffer` until 8 KiB is exhausted) is left for a follow-up.

fix(perry-ext-events): #1274 sync emit signature with perry-stdlib (variadic args) (#1289)

`import 'events'` and `import 'node:events'` route to perry-ext-events
through `well_known_bindings.toml`, so listeners installed via the
`node:events` shim ended up dispatching against perry-ext-events'
`js_event_emitter_emit` — not perry-stdlib's. PR #1186 changed the
perry-stdlib signature from

    fn js_event_emitter_emit(handle, name, arg: f64) -> bool

to

    fn js_event_emitter_emit(handle, name, args_ptr: *mut ArrayHeader) -> f64

so the codegen native_table now lowers `emit` calls with `NA_VARARGS`
(single `*mut ArrayHeader` slot) and `NR_F64` return. perry-ext-events
was never updated to match — when the linker resolves to its old
single-`arg: f64` symbol, the args-array POINTER value gets reinterpreted
as `arg: f64`. High-bit heap pointers happen to satisfy the IEEE 754
NaN tag pattern, so every listener observes `NaN` instead of the real
payload — `test_express_mount` saw `hitCount: NaN` / `parentName:
undefined`, `test_issue_850_eventemitter` saw `once values: [ NaN ]` /
`addListener/removeListener: [ NaN ]`.

Mirrors perry-stdlib::events exactly:

- `js_event_emitter_emit`: takes `args_ptr: *mut ArrayHeader`, returns
  `f64` (NaN-boxed `TAG_TRUE` / `TAG_FALSE`). Extracts `args_ptr[0]`
  via `js_array_get` for the closure-call-1 dispatch.
- `js_event_emitter_emit0`: same return-type swap (bool → f64) so both
  emit variants round-trip through codegen's f64 ABI.
- `drain_pending_once_promises`: takes the full args array instead of
  synthesizing a 1-element `[arg]` wrap — matches Node's `events.once`
  semantics where the resolution value is the full args tuple, and
  matches perry-stdlib's behaviour.

Local repro on macOS arm64 after rebuild:

  Before fix: `inside listener, x: NaN`
  After fix:  `inside listener, x: 7`

Events parity suite (`test-parity/node-suite/events/**`):

  Before fix: 18 passed, 19 failed
  After fix:  26 passed, 11 failed  (-8 regressions cleared)

The remaining 11 failures are pre-existing perry-ext-events behavior
gaps (setMaxListeners ignored, newListener/removeListener meta-events
not emitted, `error`-without-listener doesn't throw, etc.) — unrelated
to this signature fix.

Closes #1274.

feat(host-embed): #1088 emit `<output>.linkdeps.json` next to staticlib (#1290)

Follow-up to #1266. When `--output-type staticlib` produces an archive,
also write a sidecar JSON manifest enumerating the extra archives the
host has to add to its own link line. Perry already resolves this set
(auto-built `libperry_runtime.a` / `libperry_stdlib.a`, every
`perry-ext-*` staticlib the well-known table flipped in, and
jsruntime / wasm-host / UI libs when needed) — previously the only
way for a host build to discover those paths was to scrape Perry's
stdout or re-implement the well-known-bindings resolver itself.

Shape:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "archive": "/abs/.../libperry_tslib.a",
  "entry_symbol": "perry_module_init",
  "target": "native",
  "link_archives": [
    {"role": "runtime",    "path": "/abs/.../libperry_runtime.a"},
    {"role": "stdlib",     "path": "/abs/.../libperry_stdlib.a"},
    {"role": "well-known", "path": "/abs/.../libperry_ext_dotenv.a"}
  ]
}
```

`role` covers `runtime`, `stdlib`, `jsruntime`, `wasm-host`, `ui`, and
`well-known`. Paths are canonicalized when possible (falls back to the
literal path if canonicalize fails, e.g. cross-compile outputs that
don't exist on the host fs yet). Write failures warn but don't fail
the build — the archive is the load-bearing artifact.

Extends `run_test_issue_1088.sh` to assert the sidecar exists, has the
`runtime` entry, and carries the `perry_module_init` entry-symbol
declaration.

fix(setup): validate keystore output path in `perry setup android` and re-prompt instead of crashing (#1291)

`perry setup android` invokes `keytool -genkeypair` with whatever path
the user typed at the "Output path" prompt. A typo like
`~/../release-key.keystore` expands to `/Users/<you>/../release-key.keystore`
= `/Users/release-key.keystore`, which the user almost certainly cannot
write to. keytool then exits non-zero, the wizard bails, and the user
loses their alias + password entries.

Add a `prompt_output_path` helper that:

- expands `~/` (existing behavior),
- canonicalizes the *parent* directory (collapsing `..` segments so the
  error message names the directory the OS will actually refuse),
- probes write access with a `.perry-write-test-<pid>` create/remove
  round-trip — `permissions().readonly()` lies about effective-uid
  permission on Unix, so a real probe is the only honest check,
- on failure prints a red ✗ + the resolved-parent + errno kind and
  re-prompts.

Wire it into android.rs's keystore-generation branch in place of the
prior `Input::interact_text` + `expand_tilde` pair. The other inputs
(alias, password) come after the path now succeeds, so a slip on the
path no longer wastes the user's password retype.

Reuse target later: the same helper fits the other wizards' "where do I
save this generated cert/key" prompts, but no behavior change there
yet — staying scoped to the bug Ralph hit.

fix(perry-ui-gtk4): #1246 follow-up — restore image.rs resolve_asset_path access (#1298)

PR #1246 ("Drop all files to <2k LOC + tighten size gate") split
`crates/perry-ui-gtk4/src/lib.rs` and moved `resolve_asset_path` into
`ffi::layout`, leaving the function private. `widgets/image.rs:33` still
calls `crate::resolve_asset_path(path)` — root-level — so the gtk4 build
on the linux-aarch64-gnu release target broke with:

    error[E0425]: cannot find function `resolve_asset_path` in the crate root
      --> crates/perry-ui-gtk4/src/widgets/image.rs:33:27
       |
    33 |     let resolved = crate::resolve_asset_path(path);
       |                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ not found in the crate root
       |
    note: function `crate::ffi::layout::resolve_asset_path` exists but is inaccessible

Local macOS builds didn't hit this because perry-ui-gtk4 is gated off on
macOS workspace builds (gtk4 system-libs only ship on Linux). It surfaced
on the v0.5.1020 release-packages run (#26249481496) when the
`linux-aarch64-gnu` matrix entry tried to link perry-ui-gtk4 and failed
the whole release pipeline (winget / homebrew / npm / apt / apt-repo all
got skipped via fail-fast).

Two-line fix:

- `ffi::layout::resolve_asset_path`: `fn` → `pub(crate) fn` so neighbour
  modules can reuse the exact resolution rule without duplicating it.
- `widgets::image::create_file`: `crate::resolve_asset_path(path)` →
  `crate::ffi::layout::resolve_asset_path(path)` to point at the new
  module path.

Refs #1246. Unblocks v0.5.1020 release-packages re-tag.

fix(bcrypt): #1292 — bcrypt.hash() returns a real string, not a string-like object (#1307)

The async bcrypt.hash/genSalt resolution path NaN-boxed the result
StringHeader with JSValue::pointer (POINTER_TAG) instead of
JSValue::string_ptr (STRING_TAG), and allocated the string on the tokio
worker arena rather than the main thread. The awaited value was therefore
a string-like *object*:

  typeof raw          === "object"   (should be "string")
  "" + raw            === "[object Object]"
  String(raw)         === "[object Object]"
  mysql2 prepared bind  serialized the object repr (>255 bytes) → MySQL
                        error 1406 "Data too long for column"

(.length read 60 and JSON.stringify saw the underlying string only by
coincidence of the StringHeader layout / JSON's own pointer handling.)

Fix: route the hash/salt/error resolutions through
queue_deferred_resolution so the StringHeader is built on the main thread
(correct arena) and tag it via JSValue::string_ptr (STRING_TAG). This
mirrors the pattern spawn_for_promise already uses for its error strings,
and the tag the sync hashSync path already gets right. The compare()
boolean-success path is unchanged; its error strings get the same
string_ptr treatment for consistency.

Verified end-to-end: typeof is now "string", +/String() return the
60-char hash, methods (startsWith/substring) work, JSON.stringify still
works, and compare() round-trips against the freshly produced hash.

fix(fastify): #1293 route (request as any).json()/.body through external-fastify handle dispatch (#1308)

The `as any` cast in the canonical Fastify body-parse pattern
(`const body = (request as any).json(); if (!body) ...`) erases the
static type, so codegen lowers the access to a *generic* dynamic
dispatch (`Call { callee: PropertyGet }` / `PropertyGet`) instead of a
`NativeMethodCall { module: "fastify" }`. At runtime that lands in
perry-stdlib's `js_handle_method_dispatch` / `js_handle_property_dispatch`.

Those dispatchers probed only perry-stdlib's own handle registry
(`with_handle::<crate::fastify::FastifyContext>`). But the well-known
flip routes `fastify` to perry-ext-fastify, whose FastifyContext lives
in perry-ffi's *separate* registry. The probe missed, the call fell
through, and `(request as any).json()` came back as a bare NaN
(`typeof "number"`) while `(request as any).body` came back `undefined`
— a silent 400 on every POST that used the Fetch-style accessor. The
`if(!body)`-vs-`typeof` distinction in the report was incidental: the
value was wrong in all cases.

Fix mirrors the established `external-net-pump` pattern:
- perry-ext-fastify exports `js_ext_fastify_is_context_handle`, a
  membership probe over its own perry-ffi registry.
- perry-stdlib's method/property dispatch grow `external-fastify-pump`
  arms (gated `not(http-server)`) that consult it and forward to the
  linked `js_fastify_*` exports — full parity with the bundled
  `http-server` arms.

Adds test_issue_1293_fastify_request_json_as_any.ts + run_test_issue_1293.sh
(wire-level: typed json(), (as any).json(), (as any).body all return the
parsed object) and a perry-ext-fastify unit test for the membership probe.

Add diagnostics_channel parity support (#1297)

* Add diagnostics_channel parity support

* style: apply cargo fmt for lint CI

* fix(diagnostics_channel): address review findings + add regression tests

- Add proper `process.once(event, handler)` HIR variant + runtime
  `js_process_once`, instead of aliasing `once` to `on`. The earlier
  alias would have made a real `once` listener fire repeatedly.
- Partition process listeners by event name (`uncaughtException`,
  `exit`, others) so the uncaught-drain hook no longer invokes every
  `process.on('exit', …)` callback as an uncaught handler.
- Drop the `value as usize as *const StringHeader` fallback in
  `decode_string_value` — a large numeric argument used to be cast
  into a wild pointer dereference.
- Replace the substring-match `.code` shim in `field_get_set.rs` with
  a side table keyed on the Error's message pointer. Now only errors
  thrown by the diag-channel validation paths report an `ERR_*` code;
  a user `new TypeError("The argument is invalid")` no longer
  inherits `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`.
- Add empty-subscriber fast path to `publish_channel` (no Vec clone
  when nobody is subscribed).
- Cache the five `console.*` channel ids in `AtomicI64` slots and
  gate the publish on `ANY_SINGLETON_ALLOCATED` so `console.log` no
  longer allocates a `"console.log"` string on every call when no
  diag channel exists.
- Fix `tracingChannel#traceCallback` event order to match Node:
  `start | (fn runs) | asyncStart | [error] | asyncEnd | end`,
  including the `error` event when the callback is invoked with a
  truthy err.
- Validate handler shapes in `tracingChannel#subscribe`: a
  present-and-defined handler that isn't callable now throws
  `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`; `undefined`/`null` are silently skipped to
  match Node's `validateFunction` semantics.

Tests:
- `channel/error-code-isolation.ts` — user-thrown `TypeError` with
  the same message text must NOT pick up `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`.
- `channel/has-subscribers-numeric.ts` — non-string arg returns false
  without crashing.
- `tracing/subscribe-non-callable.ts` — present-but-non-callable
  handler throws; `null` doesn't.
- `tracing/trace-promise-error-ordering.ts` — explicit Node-order

* Improve app pattern performance gaps

* fix(promise): resolve all Promise.all states when same pending input is shared

When the same pending promise is fed into multiple Promise.all([...]) calls
(legal JS), only the first registered state was being drained on settle
because promise_all_take_handler used swap_remove on the first match. The
second Promise.all would never resolve.

Replace the take handler with promise_all_take_all_handlers, which drains
every PROMISE_ALL_STATES entry keyed on the settling promise. Both
js_promise_resolve and js_promise_reject in then.rs now enqueue one
PromiseAll task per drained state.

Adds a unit test in promise/combinators.rs (promise_all_with_shared_pending_input_resolves_both)
that registers two Promise.all calls sharing a pending input and verifies
both settle after the shared promise resolves.

* perf(gc): document 128 MB threshold cap and clarify step-doubling dead path

With GC_THRESHOLD_INITIAL_BYTES now equal to GC_TRIGGER_ABSOLUTE_CEILING
(both 128 MB after app-pattern tuning), the C4b-delta-tune hard cap on
next_trigger supersedes any adaptive doubling. Add an inline note above
the doubling branch explaining the cap and preserving the 1 GB
GC_THRESHOLD_MAX_BYTES bound as an intentional escape hatch for future
threshold raises or env-driven bisection.

* fix(runtime): document js_array_map barrier elision invariant

The length<=64 fast path skips the generational write barrier and only
records layout metadata, on the assumption that the freshly-allocated
result array stays in the nursery for the life of the loop. Document
the invariant explicitly so a future GC policy change that tenures
aggressively (or PERRY_GC_FORCE_EVACUATE stress runs) doesn't silently
break the remembered set for this code path.

* fix(codegen): drop PropertyGet from discard-map purity check

TypeScript classes can declare `get` accessors with arbitrary side
effects, and the discard-map optimization has no general way to prove
that a PropertyGet on the callback parameter targets a plain data slot.
Remove PropertyGet from the discard_pure_expr arms — anonymous-shape
constructions still flow through the Expr::New { __AnonShape_… } arm,
which is the intended target of the optimization.

* fix(codegen): throw TypeError on spread of null/undefined

Per ES2015 §12.2.5, `[...x]` invokes GetIterator(x) which throws a
TypeError when x is null or undefined. The single-spread fast path
previously routed straight through js_array_clone, which silently
returns an empty array for those inputs (kept for back-compat with
Array.from's not-iterable behavior).

Add a dedicated runtime entry point js_array_clone_for_spread that
inspects the NaN-box tag bits on the raw boxed value and throws a
TypeError("<receiver> is not iterable") for null/undefined before
forwarding to js_array_clone. Update the codegen single-spread arm
to call it. Array.from's behavior is unchanged.

* refactor(codegen): simplify property_set has-slots bookkeeping

The (target_has_slots, slot) tuple where target_has_slots was always
literally true was a noisy leftover from an earlier shape of this
branch. Collapse it to a plain Option<slot> lookup.

fix(process): #1312 unset process.env.X is undefined (nullish), so ?? applies (#1314)

Reading an unset env var via the process.env.X / process.env[key] fast

unconditionally tagged the result with STRING_TAG. A null pointer OR'd
with STRING_TAG is a malformed value: typeof reads "string", JSON.stringify
emits null, it is falsy under || but NOT nullish under ??, so the idiomatic
process.env.X ?? default silently kept the bogus value instead of the
fallback.

unset var (matching Node, where process.env.UNSET is undefined) and the
string otherwise. A var set to the empty string still returns "" (falsy
but not nullish), so ?? won't clobber a legitimately empty value. Both the
static (EnvGet) and dynamic (EnvGetDynamic) codegen paths now call it.

unset / set / empty-string / dynamic-access cases (test_issue_1312_env_nullish.ts).

fix(runtime): thread-safety hardening for cross-thread runtime statics (#1319)

* fix(runtime): thread-safety hardening for cross-thread runtime statics

`perry/thread` workers run user JS code on background OS threads, but
several runtime hot paths held process-wide `static mut`s that both
raced under concurrent access and stored arena-local pointers that
became use-after-free when the originating thread exited.

Partitions the offending state:

- INTERN_TABLE, TRANSITION_CACHE_GLOBAL, SMALL_INT_CACHE → thread_local!
- exception state (jump_buffers, try_depth, current_exception,
  has_exception, in_finally) → single per-thread ExceptionState in TLS
- HANDLE_METHOD_DISPATCH / HANDLE_PROPERTY_DISPATCH /
  HANDLE_PROPERTY_SET_DISPATCH → AtomicPtr with Acquire/Release
- Symbol.for / well-known symbol descriptions → process-lifetime
  Arc<str> side table; readers materialize a fresh StringHeader in the
  caller's arena on demand
- arena::ArenaBlock::alloc bump arithmetic → checked_add

No codegen changes: every removed `static mut` was grep-confirmed
unreferenced from crates/perry-codegen.

* fix(runtime): publish symbols only after side tables are populated

Review feedback on #1319: Symbol.for / well_known_symbol inserted the
pointer into the SYMBOL_REGISTRY / WELL_KNOWN_SYMBOLS map before
recording its description and adding it to SYMBOL_POINTERS. A
concurrent reader observing the pointer through the map would see:

  - registered_symbol_description() = None
  - description field = null
  - is_registered_symbol() = false

…producing transiently wrong sym.description / sym.toString() /
Symbol.keyFor() / is_symbol() results — exactly the half-initialized
visibility pattern this PR was supposed to eliminate.

Populate REGISTERED_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTIONS and SYMBOL_POINTERS first, then
publish into the registry/cache. Lock order is
SYMBOL_REGISTRY → SYMBOL_POINTERS → REGISTERED_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTIONS;
no reader takes them in the reverse order.

test(runtime): de-flake event_pump::wait_returns_when_timer_due (#1421)

The test scheduled a 50ms timer and asserted js_wait_for_event() blocks
>= 40ms. But js_wait_for_event returns early when the process-global
NOTIFIED flag is set or when any timer in the process-global queue reads as
due — and the SERIAL lock only serializes the other event_pump tests, not
parallel non-event_pump tests that call js_notify_main_thread or schedule
sooner timers mid-wait. Under CI's full parallel load the wait often
returned in ~0ms, panicking the >= 40ms assert (it passed in isolation).

js_wait_for_event is correct; the test's "blocks ~50ms" assumption is what's
fragile under shared global state. Rewrite it to retry: re-arm the timer and
re-measure until one clean, uninterrupted window is observed (the common
case is the first attempt). Each attempt drains past-due timers (so a
leftover can't pin the budget at 0) and clears the stale NOTIFIED flag.

Verified by running the full perry-runtime suite under parallel load.

feat(crypto): implement createSign / createVerify (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5) (#1364) (#1417)

createSign/createVerify hit the #463 gate — unimplemented. Add a SignHandle
mirroring the Hash/Cipher small-integer handle pattern:
createSign(alg)/createVerify(alg) allocate a handle; .update(data)
accumulates the message; .sign(privateKeyPem, enc?) and
.verify(keyPem, sig, enc?) hash the message and RSA-sign / RSA-verify.

RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 over sha1/sha224/sha256/sha384/sha512. Keys are PEM
(PKCS#8 or PKCS#1); verify also accepts the matching private key (derives
the public key), matching Node. Signatures encode as Buffer (no encoding)
or hex/base64/base64url string.

Note on the digest version skew: the `rsa` 0.9 crate pins `digest` 0.10,
but the workspace's sha1/sha2 are the newer 0.11 family, so
`Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<D>()` won't accept them. We hash with the workspace
crates and build the PKCS#1 DigestInfo prefix by hand (RFC 8017 §9.2),
then sign/verify via `Pkcs1v15Sign::new_unprefixed()` — identical bytes,
no trait-bound conflict.

Wired through codegen, the handle dispatch allowlist, FFI decls, and the
API manifest (+ regenerated docs).

Verified byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types`: the exact
deterministic RSA-SHA256 signature (hex), verify true/false, sha512
round-trip (base64), and verify accepting the private key.

EC (ECDSA/p256) and ed25519 sign/verify are follow-ups (the deps are
present); RSA is the dominant createSign use case.

Closes #1364

fix(codegen): typeof of native-module methods is "function" (#1343) (#1415)

typeof crypto.randomBytes (and any native-module method read as a value)
returned "undefined": the member is only addressable through the call-
dispatch arms, so reading it as a plain value yields the module's 0.0 stub,
which js_value_typeof classifies as undefined/number.

Add a NativeModuleRef arm to the typeof short-circuit in literals_vars.rs:
look the member up in the API manifest and emit "function" for Method/Class
entries. Properties fall through (None) so their materialized value types
correctly — process.pid stays "number", os.EOL "string", crypto.constants
"object". General fix: any manifest-registered native method now reports
"function" (crypto.*; process.* once those methods are registered).

Verified vs `node --experimental-strip-types`: typeof of randomBytes /
createHash / randomUUID / pbkdf2Sync / scryptSync / timingSafeEqual /
getHashes is "function", crypto.constants is "object", and call-result /
string regressions are unchanged.

Closes #1343

feat(crypto): implement crypto.hkdfSync (#1362) (#1416)

hkdfSync wasn't wired to the crypto namespace (hit the #463 gate). The
existing js_crypto_hkdf_sha256 was sha256-only with hex-string I/O and the
wrong arg shape, so it couldn't back Node's hkdfSync(digest, ikm, salt,

Wired through codegen, FFI decls, API manifest (+ regenerated docs).

Verified byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types`: sha256/
sha512/sha1 derivations, no-salt, Buffer inputs, and ArrayBuffer interop
(Buffer.from / Uint8Array / byteLength).

Closes #1362

feat(perf_hooks): implement PerformanceEntry#toJSON() (#1387) (#1459)

mark/measure entries are plain shaped objects, so `entry.toJSON` missed
the keys_array and `typeof entry.toJSON` was "undefined", while
`entry.toJSON()` was mis-lowered to the Date `toJSON` intrinsic (the
receiver isn't statically a non-Date class) and read the entry pointer's
bits as a timestamp, returning null.

Two-part fix:

Runtime (perry-runtime):
- Recognize an entry object by keys_array pointer identity (all entries on
  a thread share one cached keys_array for PERF_ENTRY_SHAPE) — a single
  pointer compare, no per-key matching and no GC-tracked registry of
  movable entry pointers.
- js_object_get_field_by_name: synthesize a non-enumerable `toJSON`
  bound-method closure for entry receivers (so `typeof` reports
  "function" without polluting Object.keys / spread / console.log).

fix(inspect): object field that is a 2-element array crashed console.log (#1457) (#1460)

format_jsvalue_for_json (the object-field inspector) detected Error values
by reading the value's first 32-bit word as an object_type. For an
ArrayHeader that word is `length`, so a 2-element array field collided with
OBJECT_TYPE_ERROR (== 2): the array was misread as an Error, its element
bits were dereferenced as name/message StringHeader pointers, and
console.log/util.inspect segfaulted. `console.log({ a: [1, 2] })` crashed
regardless of PERRY_JSON_TAPE (the lazy-array case #1457 reported was one
instance — a length-2 lazy array hit the same collision).

Classify the heap type from the GC header instead (mirroring the main
`format_jsvalue` formatter): read GcHeader.obj_type, materialize a lazy-tape
array, then dispatch Error via gc_type == GC_TYPE_ERROR. Also guard small
registry-id handles (< 0x100000), which carry no GC header.

Verified: the crash is gone tape-on and tape-off; length-1/3, string,
nested, mixed-element and array-of-objects shapes all match Node; Errors
still format. util + console node-suite counts are unchanged vs origin/main
(util 30/21, console 101/16 — no regression); cargo-test perry-runtime
green. Adds node-suite/console/output/object-array-fields regression test.

Closes #1457.

fix(process): forward trailing args from process.nextTick (#1351) (#1461)

`process.nextTick(cb, a, b)` now invokes `cb(a, b)` instead of dropping the
trailing args. Plumbing mirrors the `setTimeout(fn, delay, ...args)` path
shipped under #665:

- HIR variant `ProcessNextTick` switches to a struct with `callback` + `args`.
- Codegen emits `js_queue_next_tick_args(cb, ptr, n)` when args are present,
  packing them into a stack buffer of NaN-boxed doubles (no-arg form keeps
  the simpler `js_queue_next_tick` to avoid the alloca).
- Runtime queue entry grows a `Vec<f64>`; the drain dispatches via
  `js_closure_call0..9` based on arg count.
- GC scan walks the trailing args alongside the callback closure so heap
  pointers survive a collection between schedule and drain.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/nexttick/with-args.ts is byte-identical
to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

fix(process): process.send / process.disconnect undefined without IPC (#1407) (#1462)

Node leaves `process.send` and `process.disconnect` as `undefined` when
the process wasn't spawned with an IPC channel. Perry was returning the
0.0 sentinel for unknown process props, which `typeof` then reported as
`"number"` — so `if (process.send) { ... }` guards always ran the IPC
branch and `typeof process.send === "undefined"` checks failed.

Short-circuit the two property reads (bare `process.X` and
`globalThis.process.X`) to `Expr::Undefined` in HIR lowering. Calls
through this property still throw (`undefined` is not callable), matching
Node's `TypeError: process.send is not a function`.

fix(process): process.connected undefined without IPC (#1397) (#1465)

Same shape as #1407: when the process wasn't spawned with an IPC channel
(the default), Node reports `process.connected` as `undefined`, not a
falsy primitive. Perry's previous fallback returned the 0.0 sentinel, so
`typeof process.connected` came back as `"number"` — and
`process.connected === undefined` was `false`, breaking any code that
distinguishes "no IPC at all" from "IPC channel closed".

Extend the bare-`process.X` and `globalThis.process.X` arms that #1407
added to also short-circuit `connected` to `Expr::Undefined`.

fix(process): wire process.ref / process.unref as no-op functions (#1410) (#1464)

Both methods exist on Node's `process` and return `undefined` — they're
intentionally no-ops since the main process always keeps the event loop
alive. Perry was reading them as bare numbers, so feature-detection
(`typeof process.ref === "function"`) saw "number" and any actual call
threw "value is not a function".

- HIR lowering: `process.ref()` / `process.unref()` calls fold to
  `Expr::Undefined` in `native_module.rs`.
- typeof fold: `typeof process.ref` / `typeof process.unref` returns the
  literal "function" string in `lower_expr.rs`, matching the
  perf_hooks-instance pattern already used there for observe/disconnect.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/methods/ref-unref.ts is byte-identical
to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(process): implement process.abort() (#1374) (#1463)

* feat(process): implement process.abort() (#1374)

`typeof process.abort` reported `"undefined"` because `process` lowers to
the `GlobalGet(0)` sentinel and the value-read path had no route for the
`"abort"` property. The call form fell through to the generic
NativeMethodCall dispatch (no-op).

Wire it up via the established pattern (mirrors how #1371 handled cwd /
nextTick / exit etc. on the process-node-suite branch):

- New `Expr::ProcessAbort` HIR variant; native_module.rs lowers
  `process.abort()` to it.
- Codegen calls runtime `js_process_abort`, which raises SIGABRT
  (`libc::abort()` on unix, `std::process::abort()` elsewhere).
- For the value-read form (`typeof process.abort`, `const f = process.abort`),
  PropertyGet routes the GlobalGet receiver + `"abort"` property through
  `js_native_module_property_by_name("process", "abort")`, and
  `is_native_module_callable_export` returns true so the helper hands
  back a bound-method closure (typeof "function").
- api-manifest gets a `method("process", "abort", ...)` entry so the
  compile-time typeof short-circuit and SBOM audit see the surface.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/methods/abort` verifying
  `typeof process.abort === "function"`.

* docs(api): regenerate manifest after process.abort entry

fix(process): implement process.memoryUsage.rss() fast-path call (#1395) (#1466)

Node exposes `process.memoryUsage.rss()` as a fast-path that returns
just the resident-set-size as a number, avoiding the
`{ rss, heapTotal, heapUsed, external, arrayBuffers }` object allocation
of `process.memoryUsage()`. Perry didn't have it: the call hit the
generic property-call path against `process.memoryUsage` (a 0.0 sentinel
when read as a value), so it threw `TypeError: (number).rss is not a
function`.

Add `try_process_memory_usage_rss` to the nested-namespace dispatch
table (mirroring `process.hrtime.bigint()`). Lowers
`process.memoryUsage.rss()` to `(process.memoryUsage()).rss` — same
numeric value Node's fast path returns. We pay the object-allocation
cost the fast path was meant to avoid, but parity is restored and the
call form works in user code.

The bare `typeof process.memoryUsage.rss` value-read is still tracked
separately (same class as the namespace-method-typeof gap from #1320 /
#1343 — out of scope here).

feat(process): implement process.execArgv (#1349) (#1468)

Node's `process.execArgv` is the array of CLI flags the interpreter was
started with. Perry was returning the property as a 0 sentinel, so
`Array.isArray(process.execArgv)` was `false` and any `.length` /
iteration crashed. Perry binaries are AOT — there's no runtime flag
list to forward — so the empty array is the correct shape.

Lowered in `expr_member.rs` (both the bare `process.execArgv` and the
`globalThis.process.execArgv` paths) to `Expr::Array(Vec::new())`.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/exec-argv/exec-argv.ts asserts
shape (Array.isArray + every-string + length type) so it stays parity-
clean regardless of which flags Node was invoked with.

feat(process): implement process.release (#1348) (#1470)

Node's `process.release` is the object describing the current runtime
release — at minimum `{ name, sourceUrl, headersUrl }`. Perry was
returning a 0 sentinel, so `process.release.name === "node"` feature-
detection returned `undefined` and downstream `.sourceUrl` access
threw on undefined.

Lowered in `expr_member.rs` (both the bare `process.release` and the
`globalThis.process.release` paths) to an inline `Expr::Object` literal
with `name: "node"` and empty `sourceUrl` / `headersUrl` strings. Perry
binaries are AOT and shouldn't pretend to be a Node download tarball,
so the URLs are empty rather than fabricated — feature-detection only
keys off `name`.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/release/release-name.ts is
byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types` on the shape
assertions (typeof, name, sourceUrl/headersUrl typeof).

feat(process): implement process.umask() (#1373) (#1471)

`typeof process.umask` reported `"undefined"` and `process.umask()` threw
`value is not a function` because the property was not in the api-manifest
or callable-export set, the GlobalGet PropertyGet path had no route for
it, and there was no HIR variant for the call form.

Wire it up the same way #1374 handled `process.abort`:

- New `Expr::ProcessUmask(Option<Box<Expr>>)` HIR variant; native_module.rs
  lowers `process.umask(mask?)` to it.
- Codegen routes the no-arg form to `js_process_umask` (read-and-restore
  via libc::umask(0) + libc::umask(prev)) and the arg form to
  `js_process_umask_set(mask)` which sets the new mask and returns the
  previous one.
- For the value-read form (`typeof process.umask`, `const f =
  process.umask`), PropertyGet routes the GlobalGet receiver + `"umask"`
  property through `js_native_module_property_by_name`, and
  `is_native_module_callable_export` returns true so the helper hands
  back a bound-method closure (typeof "function").
- api-manifest entry `method("process", "umask", ...)` keeps the
  compile-time typeof short-circuit, SBOM audit, and .d.ts in sync.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/methods/umask` verifying
  `typeof process.umask() === "number"`.
- docs/api regenerated.

feat(process): implement process.features (#1378) (#1474)

Node's `process.features` is an object of boolean capability flags
(`tls`, `ipv6`, `inspector`, `openssl_is_boringssl`, ...) — consumers
branch on individual fields to detect what the runtime links in.
Perry was returning a 0 sentinel, so reading any field came back
`undefined`.

Lowered in `expr_member.rs` (both bare `process.features` and the
`globalThis.process.features` paths) to an inline `Expr::Object`
literal built by a new `process_features_literal()` helper. Values
reflect what Perry's runtime actually supports — TLS/IPv6 true,
inspector/debug/boringssl/quic false, `typescript: "transform"` to
distinguish Perry's native TS compilation from Node's `"strip"` mode.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/features/features.ts asserts
*shape* (typeof per field) rather than specific values, so the parity
check survives any future Node version bumping individual flags.

feat(process): implement sourceMapsEnabled + setSourceMapsEnabled (#1400) (#1480)

`process.sourceMapsEnabled` is the boolean getter exposing Node's
runtime source-map state; `process.setSourceMapsEnabled(bool)` toggles
it. Perry compiles AOT and ships no source-map resolver, so the
getter is always false and the setter is a no-op returning undefined.

Lowered in `expr_member.rs` (both bare and `globalThis.process.X`
paths) to `Expr::Bool(false)`, with the call form returning
`Expr::Undefined` from `native_module.rs`. `typeof
process.setSourceMapsEnabled` now folds to `"function"` in
`lower_expr.rs`, sitting next to the `ref`/`unref` arm from #1410.

Without this:
- `typeof process.sourceMapsEnabled` returned `"number"` (the 0
  sentinel), so libraries doing `=== "boolean"` checks bailed.
- `process.setSourceMapsEnabled(...)` threw "value is not a function".

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/methods/source-maps-enabled.ts
asserts shape (typeof + setter return) — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(process): implement process.threadCpuUsage() (#1411) (#1476)

`typeof process.threadCpuUsage` reported `"undefined"` and calling it
threw `value is not a function`. Should return `{ user, system }`
microseconds for the current thread.

Wire it up the same way #1374 / #1373 handled process.abort / umask:

- New `Expr::ProcessThreadCpuUsage` HIR variant (no args); native_module.rs
  lowers `process.threadCpuUsage()` to it.
- Codegen routes the call to `js_process_thread_cpu_usage`, which uses
  `CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID` on macOS / Linux to read the current thread's
  total CPU time and reports it as `{ user, system: 0 }`. The macOS clock
  doesn't expose a user/system split for the calling thread, so we put
  all of it in `user` and leave `system` at 0 — the API shape (object
  with two numeric fields) is what callers depend on.
- For the value-read form (`typeof process.threadCpuUsage`), PropertyGet
  extends the GlobalGet→`js_native_module_property_by_name` arm and
  `is_native_module_callable_export` returns true so the bound-method
  closure has `typeof "function"`.
- api-manifest entry `method("process", "threadCpuUsage", ...)` for the
  compile-time typeof short-circuit, SBOM audit, and .d.ts.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/cpu/thread-cpu-usage` verifying the
  object shape.
- docs/api regenerated.

fix(process): process.moduleLoadList is now an empty array (#1412) (#1477)

Node exposes `process.moduleLoadList` as a string array of built-in
modules already loaded into the interpreter. Perry was hitting the 0.0
sentinel and reporting `typeof process.moduleLoadList === "number"`,
which crashed any code probing the shape (Array.isArray, .length,
.includes(name)).

Perry AOT-compiles every reachable module into the binary — there is no
runtime module loader and no observable "load list". The spec-compatible
value is an empty array. Lower bare `process.moduleLoadList` and
`globalThis.process.moduleLoadList` to `Expr::Array(vec![])` so the
shape checks pass.

feat(process): implement availableMemory() + constrainedMemory() (#1377) (#1485)

Both threw `value is not a function`. Should return numbers.

Wire them up the same way #1411 / #1373 / #1374 did:

- `Expr::ProcessAvailableMemory` / `Expr::ProcessConstrainedMemory` HIR
  variants (no args); native_module.rs lowers `process.availableMemory()`
  / `process.constrainedMemory()` to them.
- `js_process_available_memory` delegates to `js_os_freemem` (the
  existing macOS host_statistics64 / Linux sysinfo / Windows
  GlobalMemoryStatusEx path).
- `js_process_constrained_memory` reads the cgroups v2 memory limit on
  Linux (memory.max, fallback to v1 memory.limit_in_bytes); returns 0
  when unconstrained or "max", and 0 on non-Linux — matches Node when
  no container limit applies.
- For the value-read form, `PropertyGet` extends the GlobalGet routing
  arm to include both names, and `is_native_module_callable_export`
  registers them so the bound-method closure has `typeof "function"`.
- `api-manifest` gets `method("process", "availableMemory", ...)` and
  `method("process", "constrainedMemory", ...)` for typeof / SBOM /
  .d.ts.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/memory/available-memory` verifying
  both return numbers.
- docs/api regenerated.

feat(process): implement process.finalization control surface (#1482) (#1487)

Node 22 added `process.finalization` as a control surface for
FinalizationRegistry-like lifecycle hooks:

  process.finalization.register(target, cb)
  process.finalization.registerBeforeExit(target, cb)
  process.finalization.unregister(target)

Perry had no implementation; the bare read hit a 0.0 sentinel so
`typeof process.finalization === "object"` failed and any property
deref crashed.

Lower bare `process.finalization` and `globalThis.process.finalization`
to an inline object literal carrying the three documented method names
(values are currently `undefined` — wiring the actual registry up to
Perry's GC is tracked separately). Closes the shape-only gap (typeof,
Object.keys) — Object.prototype.toString.call(process.finalization)
returns the generic '[object Object]' just like Node does for this
specific object.

Closes #1482.

feat(process): implement POSIX credential accessors (#1408) (#1489)

`process.getuid()` / `geteuid()` / `getgid()` / `getegid()` all reported
`typeof "undefined"` and threw `value is not a function`. They should
return numeric ids on POSIX (and 0 on non-unix targets).

Same shape as #1374 / #1373 / #1411 / #1377 but folded into one HIR
variant to keep `crates/perry-hir/src/ir/expr.rs` under the 2000-line
cap:

- New `PosixCredentialKind` enum in `crates/perry-hir/src/ir/constants.rs`
  with `{Uid,Euid,Gid,Egid}` variants, re-exported through `ir/mod.rs`.
- One `Expr::ProcessPosixCredential(PosixCredentialKind)` HIR variant
  carries the kind so the four entry points share lowering, walker,
  monomorph, audit, escape, and stable-hash code paths.
- `native_module.rs` maps each method name (`getuid`/`geteuid`/`getgid`/
  `getegid`) to the corresponding kind.
- Codegen routes each kind to its dedicated runtime fn
  (`js_process_getuid` etc.), each a `libc::getuid()` / `geteuid()` /
  `getgid()` / `getegid()` wrapper inside `#[cfg(unix)]`. Non-unix targets
  return 0.0.
- `PropertyGet` extends the GlobalGet routing arm to include the four
  method names; `is_native_module_callable_export` registers the pairs
  so `typeof process.getuid === "function"` holds.
- `api-manifest` gets four `method` entries for typeof / SBOM / .d.ts.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/unix/uid-gid` verifying all four
  return numbers.
- docs/api regenerated.

feat(process): populate process.versions sub-fields (uv, modules, ...) (#1381) (#1490)

Pre-fix `process.versions` only exposed `node` / `v8` / `perry`, so
shape-only consumers (`typeof process.versions.uv === "string"`,
`process.versions.modules` for NAPI ABI gates, semver checks against
`openssl` / `napi` / `zlib`) all came back `undefined`. The long tail of
npm packages that feature-detect on these treated Perry as some
outdated, unknown Node host.

Extend `js_process_versions` to 14 fields:
  node, v8, perry, uv, modules, openssl, zlib, ares, icu, unicode,
  napi, llhttp, nghttp2, undici

Values are strings everywhere. We target Node 22 at the spec level but
don't statically link libuv / OpenSSL, so:
  - `uv` / `zlib` / `unicode` carry the upstream version we target,
  - ABI counters (`modules`, `napi`) carry `"0"` to flag "do not
    assume this is a real Node host" without breaking `typeof` checks.

Closes #1381.

feat(process): implement process.config (#1379) (#1484)

Node's `process.config` is the build-time config object —
`{ variables, target_defaults }` populated by node-gyp at build
time. Perry was returning a 0 sentinel, so `process.config.variables`
threw on undefined and `Object.keys(process.config)` crashed.

Perry has no gyp file to surface, so the sub-objects are empty. The
shape preserves consumer feature-detection paths
(`process.config?.variables?.target_arch`, etc.).

Lowered in `expr_member.rs` (both bare `process.config` and the
`globalThis.process.config` paths) to an inline `Expr::Object` literal
sitting next to the `release` / `features` arms.

Test fixture force-added (root `.gitignore` shadows the directory
name `config` for top-level binary outputs; the parity test path is
fixed by the issue's repro).

Fifth-pass audit. 3 new cases. New passing: PerformanceObserver disconnect()

feat(geisterhand): register widgetSetOnClick callbacks with geisterhand (iOS) (#1492)

Closes #1486.

Geisterhand previously only saw clickable widgets that have a dedicated
type (Button, Picker, Slider, Toggle, TextField, SecureField). Any
widget with a tap gesture attached via widgetSetOnClick — list rows
built on VStackWithInsets, "link"-styled Text, custom card components —
was invisible to `GET /widgets` and unreachable via `POST /click/<h>`.

set_on_tap (iOS) now also calls perry_geisterhand_register under
cfg(feature = "geisterhand") with widget_type 9 ("clickable region")
and callback_kind 0 (CB_ON_CLICK), so /widgets enumerates them and
/click/<h> dispatches the tap callback the same way it does for
Buttons.

Verified end-to-end on a real iPhone (gscmaster.com mobile app): the
dashboard's site rows (which use VStackWithInsets + widgetSetOnClick to
open site detail) now appear in /widgets and respond to /click,
unblocking e2e drive-through of list-cell navigation.

Same treatment likely wanted on perry-ui-macos in a follow-up; this
patch is iOS-only.

feat(process): implement process.emitWarning() (#1375) (#1493)

`typeof process.emitWarning` reported `"undefined"`. Should be a
callable that writes a formatted warning to stderr (Node also emits a
'warning' event we don't replicate).

Same shape as #1374 / #1373 / #1411 / #1377 / #1408:

- New `Expr::ProcessEmitWarning(Vec<Expr>)` HIR variant (positional
  args); native_module.rs lowers `process.emitWarning(...)` to it.
- Codegen passes the first three args (warning / type / code) plus
  TAG_UNDEFINED slots for missing ones to `js_process_emit_warning`,
  which coerces each to a string via `js_jsvalue_to_string` and writes
  `(node:<pid>) <Type> [<CODE>]: <message>` to stderr. The 4th `ctor`
  arg (Node's trace anchor) is accepted but ignored — Perry doesn't
  capture stack traces here.
- For the value-read form, `PropertyGet` extends the GlobalGet routing
  arm to include `"emitWarning"`, and `is_native_module_callable_export`
  registers the pair so the bound-method closure has `typeof "function"`.
- `api-manifest` gets `method("process", "emitWarning", ...)` for the
  typeof short-circuit, SBOM, and .d.ts.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/methods/emit-warning` (typeof
  shape only — Node and Perry differ on the relative ordering of stdout
  vs stderr and on the `(Use --trace-warnings ...)` hint, so the test
  doesn't actually invoke it).
- docs/api regenerated.

feat(process): implement process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags (#1380) (#1494)

Node's `process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags` is the Set of `NODE_OPTIONS`
/ V8 flags the runtime will honour from the environment. Perry was
returning a 0 sentinel, so `.has(...)` / `.size` / `for...of` iteration
all crashed with "value is not a function".

Perry binaries are AOT and don't honour runtime CLI flags from the
environment — the empty Set is the spec-compatible shape. Lowered in
`expr_member.rs` (both bare `process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags` and
the `globalThis.process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags` paths) to
`Expr::SetNew`, sitting next to the `config` / `release` / `features`
arms shipped in #1378 / #1379 / #1348.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/env/allowed-flags.ts asserts
`instanceof Set`, `.size` typeof, and `.has(...)` behavior — byte-
identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`. The `typeof
process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags.has === "function"` shape is the
broader #1320-class method-as-value typeof gap and intentionally not
asserted here.

feat(process): implement process.report control surface (#1396) (#1491)

Node 22's `process.report` is the diagnostic-report control surface
(`compact` / `directory` / `filename` / `signal` and the four
`reportOn*` booleans, plus `getReport` / `writeReport` methods). Perry
was returning the 0.0 sentinel, so `typeof process.report === "object"`
failed and any property deref crashed.

Lower bare `process.report` and `globalThis.process.report` to an inline
object literal carrying all eleven documented keys with the same default
values Node ships out of the box (compact=false, signal="SIGUSR2", the
reportOn* booleans false, empty directory/filename, methods undefined).
Closes the shape-only gap (typeof, Object.keys, individual property
reads). Real diagnostic-report generation is tracked separately.

Closes #1396.
