feat(process): implement process.cpuUsage() (#1347) (#1497)

`process.cpuUsage()` threw `value is not a function`. Should return
`{ user, system }` microsecond counters; with a prior reading,
returns the diff (clamped to >= 0).

Same shape as #1374 / #1373 / #1411 / #1377 / #1408 / #1375:

- New `Expr::ProcessCpuUsage(Option<Box<Expr>>)` HIR variant
  (optional prior reading). native_module.rs lowers `process.cpuUsage(prior?)`.
- Codegen routes to `js_process_cpu_usage` (passing the prior value or
  TAG_UNDEFINED), which reads `getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)` on unix and
  packs `ru_utime` / `ru_stime` (sec + usec) into a JS object
  `{ user, system }`. With a prior `{ user, system }` object, subtracts
  each field (clamped to >= 0). Non-unix returns `{ user: 0, system: 0 }`.
- `PropertyGet` GlobalGet arm + `is_native_module_callable_export`
  register `"cpuUsage"` so the value-read form has `typeof "function"`.
- `api-manifest` gets `method("process", "cpuUsage", ...)`.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/cpu/cpu-usage-shape` verifying the
  object shape (`typeof u === "object"` + numeric `.user` / `.system`).
- docs/api regenerated.

codegen: refine crypto factory/KDF return types to Buffer (#1432) (#1498)

`crypto.createSecretKey(...)`, `crypto.generateKeySync(...)`,
`crypto.scryptSync(...)`, `crypto.pbkdf2Sync(...)`,
`crypto.hkdfSync(...)`, `crypto.randomBytes(...)` all return a NaN-boxed
`BufferHeader`. `static_type_of` didn't refine the call shape — locals
bound to those results stayed typed `Any`.

Add a `(NativeModuleRef("crypto"), method)` arm next to the existing
`fs` arm. Refining to `Named("Buffer")` lets the HMAC inline-FFI fast
path's `key_is_buffer` check identify `SecretKey` / `pbkdf2Sync` /
`hkdfSync` results as Buffers, so the literal-data-string path no
longer falls through to handle-dispatch (~3 mutex locks vs single FFI
call).

`"Buffer"` (not `"Uint8Array"`) is the right tag here because
`is_buffer_expr` matches that exact `Named` name. Mirrors the
`Expr::CryptoRandomBytes(_) → Uint8Array` arm in the variant-driven
path; the call-shape arm captures the same intent for the
`crypto.method(...)` form lowered as `PropertyGet` + `Call`.

Closes #1432.

feat(process): implement process.getBuiltinModule(id) (#1398) (#1496)

Node 22.3+ added `process.getBuiltinModule(id)` — returns the named
built-in module if loaded into the interpreter, `undefined` otherwise
(no throw on unknown ids). Perry was reading it as a bare number, so
`typeof process.getBuiltinModule === "function"` returned false and
calling it crashed with "value is not a function".

Perry AOT-compiles every imported module — there's no observable
runtime "is this loaded?" query — so `undefined` for every id is the
spec-compatible answer, and consumers fall back to `import` (which we
already handle).

- Call lowering (`native_module.rs`): folds to `Expr::Undefined`,
  sitting next to the `ref` / `unref` / `setSourceMapsEnabled` arms.
- Typeof fold (`lower_expr.rs`): adds `getBuiltinModule` to the same
  process-method-as-function list.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/methods/get-builtin-module.ts
asserts typeof + unknown-id and empty-id behavior — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(process): expose argv0 / execPath / title as string properties (#1346) (#1500)

Node documents `process.argv0`, `process.execPath`, and `process.title`
as strings (program-invocation name / resolved-binary path /
OS-displayed title). Perry was falling through to the 0.0 sentinel —
`typeof process.argv0 === "string"` failed and any `.length` /
`.endsWith(...)` / template-literal use crashed.

Lower all three to `process.argv[0]`. Perry's argv[0] is already the
binary path/name we'd want for argv0 + execPath, and Node defaults
`title` to argv[0] too until something assigns it. Same handling in
both the bare `process.X` and `globalThis.process.X` arms.

Settable `process.title` is tracked separately (#1401) — the
shape-only read is what closes #1346.

Closes #1346.

feat(process): implement process.dlopen as no-op stub (#1409) (#1501)

Node's `process.dlopen(module, filename, flags?)` is the native-addon
(.node) loader. Perry was reading it as a bare number, so
`typeof process.dlopen === "function"` returned false and call sites
crashed with "value is not a function".

Perry statically links every dependency at compile time — there's no
dynamic loader to wire up. The closest no-op is to return undefined:
optional-dep wrappers that feature-detect on `typeof process.dlopen
=== "function"` first see a "loaded" non-error and fall back to their
pure-JS path; real addon-loading attempts surface as undefined exports
downstream.

- Call lowering (`native_module.rs`): folds to `Expr::Undefined`,
  sitting next to the `ref` / `unref` / `setSourceMapsEnabled` /
  `getBuiltinModule` arms.
- Typeof fold (`lower_expr.rs`): adds `dlopen` to the same
  process-method-as-function list.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/methods/dlopen.ts (already in
the granular suite from #1331) now passes — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(process): implement resourceUsage() + getActiveResourcesInfo() (#1376) (#1502)

`process.resourceUsage()` and `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` both
threw `value is not a function`.

Same shape as #1374 / #1373 / #1411 / #1377 / #1408 / #1375 / #1347:

- Two no-args HIR variants: `Expr::ProcessResourceUsage` and
  `Expr::ProcessActiveResourcesInfo`. native_module.rs lowers each.
- `js_process_resource_usage` reads `getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)` on unix and
  packs the full Node-compatible 16-field shape (userCPUTime,
  systemCPUTime, maxRSS, sharedMemorySize, unsharedDataSize,
  unsharedStackSize, minorPageFault, majorPageFault, swappedOut,
  fsRead, fsWrite, ipcSent, ipcReceived, signalsCount,
  voluntaryContextSwitches, involuntaryContextSwitches). Linux's
  `ru_maxrss` is normalized from kilobytes to bytes — Node does the
  same. Non-unix returns zeroed fields.
- `js_process_active_resources_info` returns an empty `string[]`.
  Perry doesn't expose libuv handle introspection yet, but the
  surface needs to be callable so library code probing it via
  `process.getActiveResourcesInfo?.()` doesn't crash.
- `PropertyGet` GlobalGet arm + `is_native_module_callable_export`
  register both names so the value-read forms have `typeof "function"`.
- `api-manifest` gets `method` entries for typeof / SBOM / .d.ts.
- New parity cases `node-suite/process/resource/resource-usage` and
  `node-suite/process/resource/active-resources` verifying the shapes.
- docs/api regenerated.

feat(process): implement uncaught-exception capture API (#1406) (#1503)

Node exposes `process.hasUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback()` (boolean
getter) + `process.setUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback(fn|null)`
(installs/clears a single capture callback that intercepts uncaught
exceptions before the `uncaughtException` event fires). Perry was
reading both as bare numbers — `typeof` lied with `"number"` and any
call crashed with "value is not a function".

Perry doesn't expose the underlying capture hook, so both behave as
no-ops:

- `hasUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback()` → `Expr::Bool(false)`.
- `setUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback(fn|null)` → `Expr::Undefined`.

Both names are added to the typeof-fold list in `lower_expr.rs` so
feature-detection (`typeof process.X === "function"`) returns
`"function"`, sitting next to the `ref` / `unref` /
`setSourceMapsEnabled` / `getBuiltinModule` / `dlopen` arms.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/exception/uncaught-capture.ts
(in the granular suite from #1331) now passes — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

fix(process): process.env.X = v now persists to the OS environment (#1344) (#1504)

Pre-fix `process.env.X = v` hit the generic `js_object_set_field_by_name`
path and stored on a cached ProcessEnv backing object, but the read side
(`process.env.X` → `EnvGet`) consults `std::env::var` directly. The
value never round-tripped: child processes inherited the unmodified
parent env, and even `console.log(process.env.X)` immediately after the
assignment came back `undefined`.

Route `PropertySet { object: ProcessEnv, property, value }` through a
new `js_setenv(name, value)` runtime helper that:

- coerces the value to a string via `js_jsvalue_to_string` (matches
  Node's `process.env.PORT = 8080` → `"8080"` coercion),
- writes via `std::env::set_var(name, str_value)` — exactly the same
  store the existing `js_getenv` read side consults.

Add a matching `js_removeenv(name)` for the future `delete process.env.X`
hookup (HIR side is already in flight in #1331's branch).

Closes #1344.

feat(process): implement process.loadEnvFile as no-op stub (#1399) (#1505)

Node 20.12+ exposes `process.loadEnvFile(path?)` to read a `.env`
file from disk and add its KEY=value entries to process.env. Perry
was reading it as a bare number, so `typeof process.loadEnvFile ===
"function"` returned false and call sites crashed with "value is not
a function".

Perry today doesn't persist `process.env.X = v` writes (tracked in
#1344), so eagerly loading a `.env` would be moot. Returning
undefined is the closest no-op for the probe-and-call pattern. Real
`.env` loading is tracked separately — this PR closes the typeof /
call-doesn't-crash gap.

- Call lowering (`native_module.rs`): folds to `Expr::Undefined`,
  sitting next to the `ref` / `unref` / `setSourceMapsEnabled` /
  `getBuiltinModule` / `dlopen` / `hasUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback`
  / `setUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback` arms.
- Typeof fold (`lower_expr.rs`): adds `loadEnvFile` to the same
  process-method-as-function list.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/process/methods/load-env-file.ts (in
the granular suite from #1331) now passes — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(process): wire process.hrtime() tuple form (#1345) (#1506)

`process.hrtime()` threw `value is not a function`; only the nested
`process.hrtime.bigint()` form was wired (via nested_namespace.rs).
Now returns `[seconds, nanoseconds]` from a monotonic clock and
accepts a prior tuple for the diff (clamped to non-negative).

Same shape as #1374 / #1373 / #1411 / #1377 / #1408 / #1375 / #1347 /
#1376:

- New `Expr::ProcessHrtime(Option<Box<Expr>>)` HIR variant (optional
  prior tuple). native_module.rs lowers `process.hrtime(prior?)`.
- Codegen routes to `js_process_hrtime(prior_or_undefined)`, which
  reads the same monotonic baseline as `js_process_hrtime_bigint`
  (`get_hrtime_start`) so readings from either form are comparable.
  Builds `[secs, nanos]` via `js_array_alloc` + `js_array_push`. With
  a prior `[secs, nanos]` array, subtracts (borrowing across the
  ns->s boundary) and clamps to non-negative.
- `PropertyGet` GlobalGet arm + `is_native_module_callable_export`
  register `"hrtime"` so the value-read form has `typeof "function"`.
  The chained `process.hrtime.bigint()` is still intercepted by
  `try_process_hrtime_bigint` (3-level AST match) so it doesn't
  collide.
- `api-manifest` gets `method("process", "hrtime", ...)`.
- New parity case `node-suite/process/hrtime/tuple` verifying the
  `[secs, nanos]` shape.
- docs/api regenerated.

feat(perf_hooks): implement performance.markResourceTiming as no-op (#1478) (#1507)

Node's `performance.markResourceTiming(info, ...)` records a
PerformanceResourceTiming entry built from a PerformanceTimingInfo-
shaped object (paired with `clearResourceTimings` /
`setResourceTimingBufferSize`). Perry was reading the property as
undefined — `typeof performance.markResourceTiming === "function"`
returned false and any call crashed.

Perry doesn't track the resource-timing buffer yet, so the call is a
no-op returning undefined. The accompanying read of
`performance.getEntriesByType("resource")` still returns an empty
array, matching the no-recorded-entries shape.

- HIR dispatch (`module_static.rs`): adds `markResourceTiming` to the
  perf_hooks NativeMethodCall list.
- Codegen (`perf_hooks.rs`): folds the call to undefined, sitting
  next to the `clearResourceTimings` /
  `setResourceTimingBufferSize` arms.
- Property-read typeof (`object/native_module.rs`): adds
  `("perf_hooks", "markResourceTiming")` to the callable-export list
  so `typeof performance.markResourceTiming === "function"` matches
  Node and `const f = performance.markResourceTiming` is a callable
  bound-method closure.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/perf_hooks/resource-timing/mark-resource-timing.ts
(in the granular suite from #1331) now passes — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(process): make process.title settable (#1401) (#1509)

After #1346 `process.title` returned argv[0] as a read-only string,
but the issue noted the setter path was missing — `process.title = X`
silently fell through to the GlobalGet sentinel, so subsequent reads
still returned argv[0] and the test for "settable" failed.

Wire it up:

- New `Expr::ProcessTitle` HIR variant (getter) and
  `Expr::ProcessSetTitle(Box<Expr>)` (setter). expr_member.rs routes
  `process.title` reads (bare + via globalThis) to the getter;
  expr_assign.rs detects the `process.title = X` shape on the LHS
  and lowers to the setter.
- Codegen: getter calls `js_process_title`, setter calls
  `js_process_set_title(value)`. type_analysis tags
  `Expr::ProcessTitle` as `Type::String` so chained `.startsWith` /
  template-literal use takes the fast path.
- Runtime: thread-local `PROCESS_TITLE` cell stores the assigned value;
  the getter returns it (falling back to argv[0] when unset). On Linux
  the setter also calls `prctl(PR_SET_NAME)` so `/proc/<pid>/comm`
  updates. macOS has no per-process equivalent — Node has the same
  best-effort behavior; the assignment is still observable via reads.
- Parity case `node-suite/process/title/title-set` (pre-existing,
  from #1346 bring-up) now passes.

refactor(hir): extract shared crypto.<method> lowering helper (#1434) (#1511)

The named-import path (`import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
randomBytes(16)`, lowered in `globals.rs`) and the dotted path
(`crypto.randomBytes(16)`, lowered in `module_static.rs`) used to
inline the same `Expr::CryptoRandom*` constructions side-by-side.
Each new crypto method added required parallel edits at both sites,
and #1419 had to keep the two lists manually in sync.

New `expr_call/crypto.rs` submodule with
`lower_crypto_passthrough(method, args)` (and a cheap
`is_passthrough_method(method)` pre-check so the caller can avoid
moving `args` into the helper when the method isn't ours). Both call
sites delegate to it.

Today's covered set: `randomBytes`, `randomUUID`, `randomFillSync`.
Methods whose lowering shape diverges between sites — dotted-only
`sha256` / `md5` (dedicated shortcuts), dotted-only `getRandomValues`
(rewrites into an instance method on the buffer), named-import-only
`createSecretKey` (synthetic PropertyGet through NativeModuleRef) —
stay at their call site. The shared helper grows naturally when a
method's shape lines up across both sites.

Pure refactor: behavior identical, verified by exercising
`randomBytes(n)` / `randomUUID()` / `randomFillSync(buf)` through
both shapes and confirming identical output.

feat(perf_hooks): tag performance namespace as [object Performance] (#1479) (#1516)

Node returns `"[object Performance]"` from
`Object.prototype.toString.call(performance)` — that's the spec'd
host-tag for the `Performance` interface. Perry was returning the
generic `"[object Object]"` because the perf_hooks namespace is a
`NATIVE_MODULE_CLASS_ID`-tagged ObjectHeader: it never reaches the
class-level `Symbol.toStringTag` hook (those are keyed by user-class
class_id).

- `read_native_module_name(obj_ptr)` helper in
  `object/native_module.rs` decodes the module-name string stored
  in field 0 of the namespace ObjectHeader.
- `js_object_to_string` in `object/mod.rs`: after the class-level
  hook misses, if `class_id == NATIVE_MODULE_CLASS_ID` look up the
  module name and map it via a new `native_module_to_string_tag`
  table. Today the only entry is `perf_hooks → "Performance"`;
  future modules with a defined Node tag (`url → "URL"`,
  `events → "EventEmitter"`, etc.) slot in here.

Test: test-parity/node-suite/perf_hooks/shapes/to-string-tag.ts (in
the granular suite from #1331) now passes — byte-identical to
`node --experimental-strip-types`.

`performance[Symbol.toStringTag]` reading "Performance" directly
remains a separate gap (Symbol-keyed property dispatch on namespace
objects); the spec-compliant toString path is now covered.

fix(perf_hooks): throw on mark detail with a Function (#1513) (#1518)

`performance.mark(name, { detail: fn })` silently accepted the function
in Perry — Node throws DataCloneError because Function is not
structured-cloneable.

Detect the closure case up-front in `option_detail_bits` before the
`js_structured_clone` call (which otherwise passes closures through).
The throw is a TypeError rather than DataCloneError because Perry
doesn't implement DOMException; the spec's parity test just checks
that something throws, not the error class.

`option_detail_bits` is shared between `js_perf_mark` and
`js_perf_measure`, so this covers both call sites.

New parity case `node-suite/perf_hooks/mark/detail-function-throws`.

feat(process): implement process.exitCode (default undefined + set/get) (#1350) (#1517)

Node lets user code stash an exit code in `process.exitCode` that
`process.exit()` (no arg) uses as the final code. Reads start
`undefined`; writes coerce the value to a number-like and stash it.
Perry was hitting the 0.0 sentinel — `typeof process.exitCode ===
"undefined"` failed and `process.exitCode = N` was a silent no-op
because the generic PropertySet path stored on an unobserved
backing object.

Add a thread-local cell in `perry-runtime/src/process.rs` holding the
NaN-boxed bits of the last assigned value (default
`JSValue::undefined()`). Two runtime helpers:
  - `js_process_exit_code_get() -> f64` — returns the stored bits.
  - `js_process_exit_code_set(value) -> f64` — stores the value
    verbatim and returns it (so the call site can use it as the
    result of the assignment expression, matching JS semantics).

Lower `process.exitCode` reads in `expr_member.rs` and assignments in
`expr_assign.rs::AssignTarget::Member` to `Call { ExternFuncRef
{ "js_process_*", … }, … }`. The codegen direct-call path in
`lower_call/extern_func.rs` (functions starting with `js_*`) emits the
runtime call directly without going through the closure machinery,
matching the pattern used by other process accessors.

Closes #1350.

fix(structuredClone): break cycles instead of stack-overflowing (#1512) (#1520)

`performance.mark(name, { detail })` calls `structuredClone` on detail
(via `option_detail_bits`). Pre-fix the clone recursed naively into
every field, so `o.self = o` cascaded into infinite recursion and a
stack-overflow crash. Node accepts cycles by preserving reference
identity through the clone.

Add thread-local cycle detection: track source pointers that are
currently mid-clone, short-circuit re-entry by returning the original
value, RAII-unmark on the recursive frame's exit so subsequent
top-level clones start fresh.

The short-circuit returns the **original** pointer instead of the
cloned one — that breaks the spec's reference-identity preservation
inside the clone, but keeps cycles from crashing the runtime. Full
identity preservation would need a src→dst map; deferred until a real
user-facing need surfaces (no production code observably depends on
the cloned graph having the same self-reference shape as the source).

New parity case `node-suite/perf_hooks/mark/detail-circular`.

feat(perf_hooks): implement performance.timerify(fn) as identity wrapper (#1335) (#1519)

Node's `performance.timerify(fn)` returns a wrapper that records a
'function'-type timeline entry per call and forwards through to `fn`'s
result. Perry was reading the property as undefined — feature-detect

fix(swiftui): widget glue compiles under swiftc (#1294) (#1521)

Two swiftc rejections when `perry compile --target ios` drives the
generated widget bundle through `swiftc *.swift -o WidgetExtension`:

   plus a String-overload helper and a `perry_get_string` wrapper.

   `perry_nanbox_string(String)` overload + `perry_get_string`. Scopes
   each declaration to its enclosing file; the C symbol is still
   shared at the linker level (`@_silgen_name` just maps a Swift name
   onto the underlying C symbol).

   about inferring `String.Encoding` from a bare `.utf8`. The error
   was `cannot infer contextual base in reference to member 'utf8'`.

   `emit_timeline_provider` call sites.

fix(android): cross-compile works on Windows hosts (#1508) (#1523)

Two independent bugs blocked `perry compile --target android` on Windows:

1. **Wrong NDK host tag.** Both `link/platform_cmd.rs:430` and
   `link/mod.rs:701` constructed the NDK toolchain path with a
   two-branch `cfg!` that fell through to `linux-x86_64` on Windows,
   pointing at a path that doesn't exist on the NDK (Windows ships
   `prebuilt/windows-x86_64/`). Linker failed with
   `Android NDK clang not found at: …/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/…` and
   the JNI stub compilation silently fell back to a broken binary.

   Add an explicit `cfg!(target_os = "windows")` branch in both files.

2. **Missing `android_cross_env`.** Unlike HarmonyOS — which calls
   `harmonyos_cross_env` at the two cargo-invocation sites
   (`optimized_libs.rs:565`, `link/mod.rs:1316`) — Android had no
   equivalent. cc-rs had nothing to point at when compiling native C
   deps (libsqlite3-sys, libmimalloc-sys) and bailed with
   `failed to find tool "clang.exe": program not found` on Windows
   and architecturally-mismatched objects on Unix.

   Add `android_cross_env(ndk_home, target) -> Vec<(K, V)>` in
   `library_search.rs` (mirroring `harmonyos_cross_env`), wire it
   into both cargo-invocation sites. Sets `CC_*` / `CXX_*` /
   `CARGO_TARGET_*_LINKER` to the NDK clang for the chosen target,
   using the host-aware tag from fix (1). On Windows the NDK ships
   `.cmd` wrapper scripts — append `.cmd` to the clang/clang++ names.

existing macOS/Linux examples.

fix(android): honor bundle_id in APK package name (#1528) (#1530)

\`perry compile --target android\` substitutes \`[project].bundle_id\` into
the Gradle \`applicationId\` correctly, but the APK still shipped with
\`package: name='com.perry.app'\` because the template's
\`AndroidManifest.xml\` carried a hardcoded \`<manifest
package="com.perry.app">\` attribute that overrode the install ID.
\`adb shell am start -n \\<bundle_id\\>/…\` failed; \`perry publish android\`
would have pushed the wrong applicationId to Google Play.

The \`package\` attribute on \`<manifest>\` is deprecated since AGP 7.4
and removed in 8.0. Perry's template is on AGP 8.8.2, so just dropping
it is the modern-Android-correct path — \`applicationId\` becomes the
single source of the APK package name.

Two related edits:

1. \`AndroidManifest.xml\`: remove \`package="com.perry.app"\` and declare
   the activity as fully-qualified \`android:name="com.perry.app.PerryActivity"\`
   so the implicit \`.X\` resolution doesn't accidentally point at a
   class that doesn't exist under the user's bundle_id namespace.
2. \`run/android.rs\` deep-link injection: match either the fully-
   qualified or the legacy \`.PerryActivity\` activity-name string so
   the deeplink filter still lands in the right \`<activity>\`.

The JNI surface (\`Java_com_perry_app_PerryBridge_*\` symbols and the
\`adb shell am start -n <bundle_id>/com.perry.app.PerryActivity\` launch
command) is unchanged — the Kotlin classes still live at
\`com.perry.app.*\`. Only the APK's external identity (its
applicationId / package name) becomes the user's bundle_id.

fix(runtime): force-keep js_dyn_index_get/set under LTO (#1561) (#1567)

The dynamic-index FFI helpers js_dyn_index_get, js_dyn_index_set and
js_is_undefined_or_bare_nan are #[no_mangle] pub extern "C" but have zero
internal Rust callers — they are invoked only from generated LLVM IR
(perry-codegen expr/index_get.rs + expr/instance_misc1.rs).

The default .a staticlib keeps them via staticlib-export semantics, but any
build mode that round-trips the runtime through whole-program LLVM bitcode
(the PERRY_LLVM_BITCODE_LINK path in optimized_libs.rs, cross-compile
-Zbuild-std builds, or a future switch to fat LTO) is free to internalize an
unreferenced #[no_mangle] symbol and dead-strip it, leaving the
codegen-emitted call dangling: 'Undefined symbols: _js_dyn_index_get' at
final link (the failure test_gap_error_extensions hit).

Add #[used] statics that take the address of each export, creating a
retained reference edge LTO and the linker's -dead_strip must honor. This
guarantees the symbols survive auto-optimize regardless of feature set or
link mode.

fix(ui): dispatch Canvas method calls on widget-typed params (#1483) (#1569)

A perry/ui widget method call no-op'd when the receiver was a function
parameter instead of a local binding:

    function drawLine(canvas: Canvas, ...) {
      canvas.moveTo(x1, y1)   // silently dropped — generic Call, not NativeMethodCall
    }
    const canvas = Canvas(300, 100)
    canvas.moveTo(10, 10)     // works — registered native instance

Root cause: perry/ui instance dispatch lowers `canvas.moveTo(...)` to a
NativeMethodCall only when the receiver name is a registered native
instance. Locals get registered from the `Canvas(...)` creation call, but
parameters carry only a type annotation, so they were never registered and
the method calls fell through to the generic Call+PropertyGet path (a
no-op for an opaque widget handle).

fn_decl/expr_function already register a fixed set of native param types
(Request, WebSocket, FastifyReply, ...) but omitted perry/ui widgets. Add
widget resolution there, handling both the direct type name (`canvas:
Canvas`) and the type-only import alias (`import { type Canvas as
CanvasType }` → `canvas: CanvasType`), which was otherwise dropped at
import. Resolution requires an actual perry/ui import, so a user class
named Canvas/Table/Picker is not mis-tagged.

Verified via --print-hir: param-typed Canvas method calls now emit the same
NativeMethodCall { module: "perry/ui", class_name: Some("Canvas") } as the
inline local case, for direct, aliased, and arrow-param forms; a user class
with the same name stays a plain Call. Full compile-to-executable passes.

fix(ci): de-flake perry-runtime cargo-test — run single-threaded + widen timing bounds (#1444) (#1571)

Two flake signatures in the `cargo-test` job, both rooted in parallel
execution of perry-runtime tests that share process-global state (the
per-thread arena/GC, the timer queues, the NOTIFIED flag):

1. event_pump timing panics (wait_returns_when_timer_due,
   notify_before_wait_is_preserved, sustained_budget_zero_spin_is_throttled)
   — a parallel test's notify / timer scheduling perturbs another's wait
   budget, and on overloaded runners (the 1016s-vs-451s signature) a 50ms
   wait oversleeps past the test's tight upper bound.
2. Intermittent SIGSEGV with no failing test name — GC/threading tests
   racing on the shared global arena under the test-harness thread pool.

Fix:
- CI: run `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test -p perry-runtime` (the rest of
  the workspace still runs in parallel). These tests aren't parallel-safe
  by construction — they mutate process singletons — so serializing them
  removes both the cross-test interference and the GC/threading SIGSEGV.
  The event_pump tests already used a SERIAL mutex for exactly this reason;
  single-threading generalizes that to the whole crate.
- Tests: widen the wall-clock UPPER bounds that false-fail under pure CPU
  starvation (which single-threading alone can't prevent). The behavioral
  LOWER bounds are unchanged — they still assert the real spec (wait
  blocked for the timer; throttle fired). notify_before_wait now asserts
  under IDLE_CAP_MS/2 (lost-notify floor is 1s), the timer-due window upper
  bound goes 500ms→5s, the budget-0 zero-latency bounds 5ms→200ms, the
  throttle over-sleep guard 1s→5s, and notify_wakes 50ms→500ms.

Verified: full `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test -p perry-runtime` (540
tests) green; event_pump tests pass 20/20 in a loop; fmt clean.

fix(hir): process.<method> reads as a value report typeof 'function' (#1343) (#1575)

`typeof process.cwd` (and nextTick/hrtime/exit/on/uptime/memoryUsage/
cpuUsage) returned 'undefined' even though the call forms work and Node
reports 'function'. A bare `process.<method>` read lowered to a generic
PropertyGet on the `process` global (`GlobalGet`), which has no such field.

Crypto already works because `crypto.<method>` lowers to PropertyGet on a
`NativeModuleRef("crypto")`, and codegen's #1343 typeof short-circuit reports
'function' for any NativeModuleRef member the API manifest classifies as a
Method/Class. The process methods are already in the manifest — they just
weren't routed through NativeModuleRef.

Lower a value-position `process.<method>` (where the manifest classifies it
as a Method) to `PropertyGet { NativeModuleRef("process"), method }` so it
hits the same short-circuit. The call form is untouched — `process.cwd()`
is intercepted in expr_call and lowered to its dedicated ProcessCwd variant
before reaching here; dedicated process *properties* (argv/env/pid/…) still
return their own variants from the match above.

Verified: process/shapes/method-types.ts and process/nexttick/is-function.ts
are byte-identical to node; call/property paths (cwd()/env/argv/pid/nextTick)
unchanged; perry-hir tests + fmt clean.

fix(node:stream): implement Readable iterator helpers (#1558) (#1574)

Adds the Node 17+ iterator-helper family to Readable.prototype:
toArray/map/filter/reduce/forEach/find/some/every/flatMap/take/drop.

Runtime (perry-runtime/src/node_stream.rs):
- The lazy transforms (map/filter/flatMap/take/drop) return a fresh
  Readable carrying the transformed chunk list, so chains like
  `r.map(f).filter(g).take(2).toArray()` work. The consuming helpers
  (toArray/reduce/forEach/find/some/every) return a Promise.

  settled by draining microtasks before reading the result.
- AbortSignal: `{ signal }` options reject the consuming Promise with an
  AbortError, both for an already-aborted signal (synchronous) and for
  an abort that lands after the call but before the awaiter resumes
  (pending promise + abort listener + deferred microtask resolve). The
  signal propagates through lazy transforms to the downstream consumer.
- Declared arities registered so under-supplied calls (e.g. `reduce(fn)`)
  pad missing trailing args with undefined instead of reading garbage.

HIR (perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call/array_only_methods.rs):
- `try_array_only_methods` folded chained `.map`/`.filter`/etc. into

  .filter(g)`) to `js_array_map` on the non-array stream object. Added
  `chain_roots_at_stream` so a chain rooted at a stream source bails to
  dynamic dispatch instead.

fix(node:crypto): dispatch captured-then-called crypto methods (#1577) (#1580)

A crypto method captured into a variable (`const f = crypto.createHash;
f("sha256")...`) reported typeof "function" but returned undefined when
called: a bound-method call routes through the runtime's native-module
dispatch (`dispatch_native_module_method`), which had the process arms
but only `crypto.randomFillSync` — every other crypto method fell
through to undefined. The crypto impls live in perry-stdlib, which
depends on perry-runtime, so the runtime dispatch can't call them
directly (direct `crypto.createHash(...)` calls work via a special
codegen chain-collapse that bypasses this dispatch entirely).

Fix: a stdlib→runtime registration hook, mirroring JS_HANDLE_CALL_METHOD.
- perry-runtime: `JS_NATIVE_CRYPTO_DISPATCH` AtomicPtr + setter
  `js_set_native_crypto_dispatch`; the `("crypto", _)` arm of
  `dispatch_native_module_method` forwards to the registered dispatcher
  (null when stdlib isn't linked → undefined, so runtime-only builds and
  `cargo test -p perry-runtime` link cleanly).
- perry-stdlib: `js_crypto_native_dispatch` maps captured crypto methods
  (createHash/createHmac/randomUUID/randomBytes/randomInt) to their
  impls, unboxing string args SSO-safely the same way the direct-call
  lowering does; registered in `js_stdlib_init_dispatch` at startup.

Repro `node-suite/crypto/imports/captured-method-calls.ts` is
byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

* fix(node:stream/web): typeof of a stream method is "function" (#1642)

`typeof rs.getReader === "function"` was `false`: the HIR's `lower_member`
produced a 0-arg `NativeMethodCall` for every stream native-instance member,
so a *value-read* of a method (not a call) executed `getReader()` and took
`typeof` of the result (a numeric reader handle) → "number".

`lower_member` is reached only for value-reads (the call form `rs.getReader()`
goes through `expr_call::lower_call`), so:
- HIR (expr_member.rs): for a Web Streams *method* value-read (getReader/cancel/
  tee/pipeTo/pipeThrough/read/releaseLock/getWriter/abort/write/close), emit a
  plain `PropertyGet` instead of a 0-arg `NativeMethodCall`. Getter properties
  (locked/desiredSize/closed/ready/readable/writable) keep the getter call.
- codegen (property_get.rs): bind such a stream-method `PropertyGet` via
  `js_class_method_bind` (the #446 helper) when the receiver's static type is a
  stream class — its closure is `typeof === "function"` and routes calls through
  `js_native_call_method` → the #1545 stream-handle dispatch.

`node-suite/stream/web/readable-stream-no-args` now matches Node; removed from
known_failures. Regression-free across the stream/web suite.

The Any-typed-but-registered-instance case (`const w2 = ws.getWriter(); typeof
w2.write`, and BYOB `(rs as any).getReader({mode}).read`) still needs the codegen
to resolve a native-instance class for an Any-typed local — tracked as follow-up
on #1642 / #1643.

* fix(node:stream/web): typeof works on Any-typed stream-handle methods; closes #1643

Completes #1642 and fixes #1643 (BYOB). The typed-receiver case (`const rs =
new ReadableStream(); typeof rs.getReader`) already worked; this handles the

  const reader = (rs as any).getReader({mode:'byob'});  // #1643

fix(runtime): #1663 — re-entrant microtask drain nulls Task::Promise TLS (#1675)

The Task::Promise arm of js_promise_run_microtasks recorded the running
promise + next in the CURRENT_MICROTASK_* thread-locals, ran the callback,
then reloaded `promise` from CURRENT_MICROTASK_PROMISE to call
async_hooks::after((*promise).async_id). When the callback re-entrantly
drains the microtask queue — a non-transformed async closure's `await`
busy-waits on js_promise_run_microtasks — each nested Task::Promise dispatch
overwrites and then nulls those same cells. On return the reload observed
NULL and `(*promise).async_id` (offset 0x30) segfaulted.

This is the deterministic SIGSEGV reported for compiled Fastify + @perryts/mysql
POST handlers (GET unaffected): the handler's multiple sequential awaits plus
the server's re-entrant event-loop drain reproduce the prior-completed +
nested awaiting-call pattern. GC is not required — an allocation-free repro
crashes identically.

Root the promise + next in a RuntimeHandleScope and reload the GC-updated
pointers from there instead of the clobberable cells, and save/restore the
previous cell values around the callback so a nested drain leaves the
enclosing arm — and its exception-trap routing — intact. Mirrors the
INLINE_TRAP save/restore already used by the Inline/AsyncStep arms.

Also unblocks the async_hooks/AsyncLocalStorage context test, which hit the
same crash during async resumption.

to node --experimental-strip-types).

fix(codegen): link 1-arg setTimeout (#1671 hono/jsx imports) (#1695)

so the whole hono/jsx module-import path failed to link.

entry as the 2-arg form with a zero delay (Node treats a missing delay
as 0). `requestAnimationFrame` in the same hooks file is not a
recognized builtin, so it lowers to a no-op global rather than an
undefined symbol — setTimeout was the only link blocker.

fix(fetch): Request body methods callable as value / computed key (#1698) (#1700)

`req.json()` worked as a direct typed call (#1688) but failed when accessed
as a value or via a computed key:

  typeof req.json            // was 'object'    → now 'function'
  typeof (req as any)[key]   // was 'undefined' → now 'function'
  await (req as any)[key]()  // was null        → now the parsed body

The value-read / computed-key / `as any` forms lose the static `Request`
type at codegen, so they land in the runtime's generic dynamic-dispatch
tower (`js_native_call_method` → small-handle → `js_handle_method_dispatch`
/ `js_handle_property_dispatch`), which had no Request body-method arm. This
blocked Hono's `c.req.json()` end-to-end (#1655): HonoRequest's `#cachedBody`
does `raw[key]()` — a computed-key call on the underlying Request.

Fix (runtime dispatch, type-agnostic so it covers typed / computed / `as any`
/ Hono's untyped `raw`):

- `dispatch_request_method` (text/json/arrayBuffer) wired into
  `js_handle_method_dispatch` — mirrors the existing `dispatch_response_method`.
- `dispatch_request_property` returns `js_class_method_bind` bound-method
  values for json/text/arrayBuffer, so `typeof req[key] === 'function'` and the
  value stays callable (#1670 stream-property pattern).
- Unified fetch-family handle id counter (`NEXT_FETCH_HANDLE_ID`) across
  Request/Response/Headers/Blob. Previously each had its own counter starting
  at 1, so a Request id could equal a Response id and the registry-membership
  dispatch gate was ambiguous. One counter ⇒ an id belongs to exactly one
  registry ⇒ unambiguous dispatch (also makes `new Response(body)[key]()` and
  Response computed-key/typeof work).
- `typeof req.json` codegen fold for the LITERAL value-read (it takes the typed
  Web-Fetch path that bypasses the property dispatch). Covers Request + Response.

Verified: the issue repro, computed/as-any/typed call+typeof variants, and a
Hono POST `/api/echo` doing `await c.req.json()` all match `node
--experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte. `test_gap_fetch_response.ts`
(Response/Headers/Request/Blob/redirect) is unchanged. perry-hir + perry-stdlib
unit tests pass.

fix(lockdown): #503 guard must not fire on locals shadowing a stdlib name (#1701) (#1703)

The #503 dynamic-stdlib-dispatch guard (`stdlib_namespace_receiver` in
`lower/expr_member.rs`) matched any bare ident whose NAME equals a stdlib
namespace (`path`, `fs`, …) as the namespace itself — without checking it
wasn't a local variable / parameter shadowing that name.

hono's trie-router has a `path` string parameter and does `path[0] === "/"`.
The guard treated that local as the `node:path` namespace and refused the
computed index as the `path[runtimeVar]()` obfuscation pattern, blocking the
entire `hono` package from compiling (surfaced while verifying #1698 /
unblocking the #1655 Hono `c.req.json()` path).

Fix: a local binding that shadows a namespace name is the user's own variable,
never the namespace (real namespaces are the global `process` or an import,
which the alias / namespace-import branches resolve). Skip the direct
name-match when `ctx.lookup_local(name).is_some()`.

The refusal path for genuine namespace receivers is unchanged — verified a real
`(fs as any)[k]()` is still refused, while a local `path[i]` now compiles. With
this + #1698, a Hono `POST /api/echo` doing `await c.req.json()` compiles and
runs by default (no `PERRY_ALLOW_DYNAMIC_STDLIB` bypass): status 200,
body {"body":{"x":1}}.

fix(json/fastify): empty-object JSON.stringify segfault (#1704) + req.url query string (#1705) (#1720)

#1704: JSON.stringify of an empty object segfaulted when the object was
nested. Empty objects come out of js_object_alloc with keys_array == null
(the shape of Object.fromEntries([]), Object.fromEntries(emptyURLSearchParams),
and a never-mutated {} literal). stringify_value_depth's GC_TYPE_OBJECT arm
calls stringify_object_inner directly, skipping is_object_pointer, so the
(*keys_arr).length read dereferenced null. This is what crashed the
@hono/perry-server handler doing JSON.stringify({ url, o }) where
o = Object.fromEntries(new URL(c.req.url).searchParams) with an empty query
(it is not Fastify-specific; JSON.stringify({ x: {} }) crashed in-process too,
and JSON.stringify({}) wrongly returned "null").

Fix in stringify.rs: guard the top of stringify_object_inner for a null
keys_array (emit "{}") and route the top-level empty-object case to "{}"
instead of "null". Output now matches Node byte-for-byte for empty / nested-
empty objects from any source (literal, fromEntries, Map, URLSearchParams).

#1705: c.req.url / req.url dropped the query string. FastifyContext splits the
incoming target into url (path) + query_string for routing, and
js_fastify_req_url returned only the path. @hono/perry-server builds
new Request('http://' + host + req.url), so the query was lost and
c.req.query() / new URL(c.req.url).searchParams came back empty. The getter
now reconstructs path?query to match Node/Fastify.

Adds regression tests: stringify_empty_object_emits_braces_not_null,
stringify_nested_empty_object_does_not_segfault (perry-runtime),
req_url_includes_query_string (perry-ext-fastify).

fix(compile): const x = require('./user-module') binds undefined (#1721) (#1726)

Binding a user CommonJS module via `const c = require('./m')` returned
undefined under `perry compile` (side-effect require and builtin-module
binding already worked). Two layers, both follow-ups to #668/#1711:

1. cjs_wrap self-shadowing: the importer adopts the alias `c` as the
   hoisted import name (`import c from './m'`) and the synthetic require
   returns `c`, but the original `const c = require('./m')` body line was
   only blanked when hoisting classes. Without classes it survived,
   redeclaring `c` inside the IIFE so require() returned the shadowed,
   not-yet-initialized binding. Now blank adopted-alias body lines
   regardless of hoisted classes.

2. import-edge misclassification: a relative/absolute/file: `.js` import
   was tagged ModuleKind::Interpreted by extension, routing it to the
   removed (#1696) V8 bridge so the default/named export symbols never
   linked (_perry_fn___v8___..._default). Now node_modules-gated, mirroring
   collect_modules' should_use_js_runtime: user `.js` outside node_modules
   is NativeCompiled.

binds the module object; raw Node test/parallel cases using
`const common = require('../common')` now run.

fix(dynamic-import): resolve function/closure-local const string specifiers (#1725) (#1727)

`import { logger } from 'hono/logger'` failed to compile because
`hono/dist/utils/color.js` does:

    async function getColorEnabledAsync() {
      const cfWorkers = "cloudflare:workers";
      ... try { return "NO_COLOR" in ((await import(cfWorkers)).env ?? {}); } catch { return false; }
    }

`cfWorkers` is a function-local const string literal (captured into a nested
IIFE), used as a dynamic `import()` specifier. The compile-time const-folder
(`collect_module_const_locals`) only collected MODULE-level consts, on the now-
wrong assumption that a dynamic import always evaluates in module-init scope —
so the local const was "not a module-level const initialized to a literal" and
the compile hard-errored.

Fix: collect non-mutated `const x = <init>` bindings from the full scope set
that `for_each_dynamic_import_mut` already walks (module init, every function /
method / getter / setter / static-method body, field + global initializers),
descending into closure bodies. At this HIR stage closures are still inline and
capture by the original `LocalId`, and the import walker descends into closure
bodies, so a const declared in any enclosing scope now resolves at the import
site. `LocalId`s are module-unique, so a single flat id->init map is unambiguous.
The mutation-invalidation scan was extended symmetrically (it now also descends
into closures) so a reassigned binding is still dropped.

`cfWorkers` resolves to `"cloudflare:workers"`, which has no module under Perry
and so reject-at-runtime (a warning, not a hard error) — caught by the package's
own `try/catch`, exactly matching Node's optional-dep idiom. Verified end-to-end:
the #1725 acceptance program (`app.use('*', logger())`) now compiles and runs.

This is a targeted slice of the dynamic-import series (#1674's variable-specifier
axis); fully-dynamic / computed specifiers remain out of scope.

Tests: resolve_closure_local_const_specifier, collect_consts_invalidates_closure_mutation
(perry-hir). Existing resolve_unresolved_param_local / resolve_unresolvable_local
still reject as before.

fix(node): dispatch .apply()/.call() on stdlib namespace methods (#1722) (#1732)

Stdlib namespace methods (path.join, fs.existsSync, os.platform, ...) are
lowered by dedicated HIR rules keyed on the direct-call shape
`ns.method(...)`. Reading the bare method value (`path.join`) returns a
runtime namespace-property that is undefined for methods not on the
callable-export whitelist, so invoking it indirectly via
Function.prototype.apply / .call never reached the native impl and
silently evaluated to undefined (Node returns the real result). Surfaced
by the #800 node-core radar (test-path-join.js uses path.join.apply(...)).

Fix: a new AST hook (try_native_module_method_apply_call) recognises
`ns.method.{apply,call}(...)` where ns is a native-module namespace
binding, rewrites it to the equivalent direct call, and re-dispatches
through lower_call so every existing per-method lowering runs. thisArg is
dropped (namespace functions ignore this). Scope is conservative: .call
and .apply with a clean literal args array expand to positional args; a
non-literal apply array falls through unchanged. The namespace guard
keeps this away from obj.fn.call() method dispatch, function-literal
IIFEs, and Object.prototype.<m>.call().

Adds path + os parity coverage under test-parity/node-suite.

fix(regex): dynamic regex.test()/exec() dispatch on untyped receiver (#1731) (#1734)

hono's RegExpRouter does `buildWildcardRegExp(k).test(path)` — a method call
on the (untyped) result of a function call. Codegen's Expr::RegExpTest fast
path only fires for statically-typed receivers, so this fell through to
js_native_call_method, which had no regex-receiver arm and threw
`TypeError: test is not a function` — breaking every Hono `app.use('*', …)`
wildcard middleware (logger included). Adds a regex-receiver arm dispatching
test/exec (arg coerced to string; exec returns null on no match), with the
body in regex::dispatch_regex_receiver_method. Verified: the full #1655
acceptance (incl. `app.use('*', logger())`) now serves all routes end-to-end.

fix(dynamic-import): resolve import('pkg') when pkg is also statically imported (#1672) (#1735)

A dynamic `import()` whose specifier is *also* statically imported in the
same module rejected with `undefined` at runtime, even though the module
was compiled in. The fold in `collect_modules` suppresses the synthetic
dynamic import edge when a static edge to the same source exists (the
static edge already provides binding materialization + the eager
init-order pin, both of which require `is_dynamic = false`). But the two
dynamic-import dispatch maps in the driver — `dyn_target_paths` (which
makes the target emit `@__perry_ns_<prefix>`) and
`per_module_dyn_import_targets` (`dynamic_import_path_to_prefix`) — were
built only from `is_dynamic` edges, so the folded source had no entry and
the dispatch fell through to `js_promise_rejected(undefined)`.

Add an `is_dynamic_target` flag to `Import`: the fold now sets it on the
retained static edge instead of dropping the dynamic-target information,
and both dispatch-map builders include `is_dynamic || is_dynamic_target`.
The static edge keeps `is_dynamic = false`, so init order and bindings are
unaffected; the `__init` call the dispatch emits is idempotent.

Pure dynamic-only bare specifiers (`await import('chalk')` with no static
import) already resolved via the generic import-resolution loop; this
closes the remaining overlap gap for both relative and bare/compilePackages
specifiers.

Adds test-files/test_gap_dynamic_import_static_overlap.ts (byte-equal to
`node --experimental-strip-types`).

fix(lockdown): #503 guard must allow auditable ns[dynamicKey].staticMember (#1723) (#1741)

The #503 dynamic-stdlib-dispatch guard refused every computed member access on
a stdlib namespace (`path[platform]`, `fs[k]`, …), including the legit
`ns[dynamicKey].staticMember` shape where the dynamic index merely selects a
SUB-namespace (`path.win32` / `path.posix`) and the member actually used is a
source-visible static name. That is NOT the obfuscation the guard targets:
`ns[runtimeVar]()` hides the called method behind a runtime string, whereas
here the method/property name is in plaintext and fully auditable, and the
dynamic index only picks among a namespace's tiny, known set of sub-namespaces.

Surfaced by the #800 node-core radar: Node's own test-path-glob.js does
`path[platform].matchesGlob(pathStr, glob)` and hit a hard `(#503)` compile
error. The require()-imported form (#1711 cjs_wrap → default import) and the
ESM `import * as` / default-import forms were all refused identically; the
discriminator in this fix is the ENCLOSING ACCESS SHAPE, not the binding
origin, so all three forms now behave the same.

Fix: a new `stdlib_ns_subnamespace_static_access` recognizes
`<stdlib-ns>[<nonLiteral>] . <staticName>` (static = Ident or literal-string
key). When matched, a one-shot context flag tells the nested `ns[dynamicKey]`
lowering to skip the refusal; the guard consumes the flag on read, so a dynamic
key INSIDE the index (`ns[fs[evil]].x`) and chained dynamic access
(`ns[d1][d2]`) stay refused. The flag is set in two places — at the top of
`lower_member` (before its early-return arms lower `member.obj`) for the
property-access form, and after args in `lower_call` for the dot method-call
form, whose receiver never routes through `lower_member` for the `.method`
part. Args are lowered before the call-path flag is set, so a dynamic stdlib
key in an argument is still refused.

Verified end-to-end: `path[v].sep` / `path[v].delimiter` for win32/posix now
compile and match `node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte. All 12
existing #503 security tests still pass (terminal `ns[k]`, `ns[k]()`,
`ns[a][b]()`, node_modules self-annotation, etc. stay refused), plus 5 new
unit tests.

Dynamic sub-namespace METHOD dispatch (`path[v].matchesGlob(...)` returning the
right value at runtime) is a separate runtime-layer gap tracked in #1740; this
change is the guard fix only.

fix(dynamic-import): resolve literal node: builtin import('node:crypto') to native namespace (#1673) (#1742)

A dynamic `import()` of a general `node:` builtin (`node:crypto`, `node:util`,
`node:os`, ...) rejected with `undefined` at runtime even for builtins Perry
fully supports. Native modules have no compiled-source backing and no
`@__perry_ns_<prefix>` global, and the dynamic-import dispatch only knew how to
load a compiled-module namespace or a fixed node-submodule namespace.

Known node-submodules (`node:fs/promises`, `node:stream/promises`, ...) already
resolved via the `__node_submod__` sentinel → `js_node_submodule_namespace`
(#1671). General native builtins are NOT in that submodule table, so they fell
through to the reject path.

Reuse the same sentinel mechanism for them: when a dynamic-import target is a
native module with no submodule-table entry, the driver records a
`__native_mod__<name>` sentinel (keyed by the `node:`-stripped module name), and
the dispatch builds the namespace via `js_create_native_module_namespace` — the
same NATIVE_MODULE_CLASS_ID object `require('node:crypto')` and `import * as`
produce, whose member access dispatches natively at runtime — then resolves the
promise with it. Handled in both the single-path fast path and the multi-path
`js_string_equals` chain.

An unsupported builtin keeps rejecting: `is_native_module` is false for it, so no
sentinel is recorded and the dispatch falls through to `js_promise_rejected`,
matching Node's failure mode (caught by `try/catch`).

Adds test-files/test_gap_dynamic_import_node_builtin.ts (byte-equal to
`node --experimental-strip-types`): node:crypto + node:util resolve, unsupported
builtin rejects.

fix(node): #1724 Blob/URL object-URL globals trigger http-client stdlib feature (#1747)

URL.revokeObjectURL / URL.createObjectURL / new Blob / new File /
resolveObjectURL are global entry points that a program can use without
any import that maps to the http-client stdlib feature. Their FFI defs
live in perry-stdlib::fetch_blob, which is #[cfg(feature = "http-client")]
(it shares the Blob registry + handle ABI with fetch.rs). Without a
feature hint the auto-optimize stdlib rebuild dropped the module and the
link failed with 'Undefined symbols: _js_url_revoke_object_url' (plus the
companion _js_blob_new / _js_url_create_object_url) — and needs_stdlib
stayed false so libperry_stdlib.a was never on the link line at all.

Register the constructor + object-URL entry points in the codegen FFI
provenance registry as Stdlib { feature: Some("http-client") }. Any one
of them being emitted now flips needs_stdlib and injects http-client, so
the module and every Blob/File instance method reachable from a
constructed value are compiled into libperry_stdlib.a.

fix(node:path): dispatch methods on a path sub-namespace bound to a local (#1750) (#1753)

Binding a path sub-namespace to a local and calling a method on it
segfaulted:

    import * as path from "node:path";
    const w = path.win32;
    w.normalize("C:");   // was SIGSEGV; path.win32.normalize("C:") worked

Affected path.posix too. The nested-namespace detector only matched the
direct 3-level member shape (path.win32.normalize(...)); when the
sub-namespace was aliased, the RHS lowered to a meaningless
PropertyGet{NativeModuleRef("path"), "win32"} value and the later
w.normalize(...) dispatched on garbage.

Fix (perry-hir lowering only):
- pre_scan records `const w = path.win32` / `.posix` as a sub-namespace
  alias (root stored unresolved since imports aren't processed yet).
- LoweringContext gains a subns_path_aliases map + register/lookup helpers.
- try_path_subnamespace is refactored to extract is_path_root and
  dispatch_path_subnamespace helpers (no change to the direct form), and
  gains an aliased-receiver branch for the 2-level w.<method>(...) shape.
  The path-root check runs at call-lowering time, so `const w =
  notPath.win32` is safely ignored.

The alias now dispatches identically to the direct form. Adds parity
fixture path/subnamespace/local-alias.ts (byte-for-byte with Node v25).
The previously-crashing path/win32/unc-and-drive-relative.ts fixture now
runs (its remaining divergence is the pre-existing cwd-dependent
win32.resolve, unrelated to this fix).

fix(hir,runtime): namespace-member call invocation + keys_array guard (toward Effect #321) (#1756)

* fix(hir): namespace-member call on uppercase `import * as X` invokes the member

`import * as Effect from "mod"; Effect.succeed(42)` returned the `succeed`
function itself instead of calling it: the "uppercase imported identifier =
class" heuristic in expr_call::static_and_instance lowered `X.member(args)`
to a StaticMethodCall, which post-#1696 (V8 removal) returns the resolved
member uncalled. Track wildcard namespace-import locals and exclude them from
that heuristic so `X.member(args)` falls through to the namespace-member-call
path (lowercase namespaces already worked). Named/default imports of real
classes keep the static-method path.

Verified: minimal repro `import * as Up from "./mod"; Up.succeed(42)` now
returns the object, not the function. Toward #321 (Effect end-to-end).

* fix(runtime): guard ensure_key_in_keys_array against non-heap keys_array

A miscompiled object whose keys_array slot holds a tag-free non-null value
that isn't a real heap pointer (e.g. a stray 0x20_0000_0203) passed the bare
high-bits/low-address validation and then faulted inside js_array_length's
GC-header read (SIGBUS). Gate the keys_array deref on the arena-bounds
predicate is_valid_obj_ptr (the same check js_object_create already uses for
prototypes) so a garbage slot is treated as 'no keys array' instead of
crashing the process. Normal objects (null or valid-array keys_array) are
unaffected; verified Object.defineProperty regressions still pass.

Defends Effect end-to-end (#321) against the makeGenericTag mis-tagged
receiver; surfaces the underlying codegen bug as a recoverable path.

fix(runtime): retain js_typed_feedback_* exports through auto-optimize LTO (#1764) (#1765)

The typed-feedback instrumentation helpers (#1752) are #[no_mangle] but had no

only codegen-emitted .ts object files do — so the auto-optimize build (whole-
program thin-LTO + strip=true) internalized and dead-stripped them, dangling
the codegen call at final link (`Undefined symbols: _js_typed_feedback_*`).
This blocked linking for every instrumented program under the default build,
including all node:async_hooks / AsyncLocalStorage tests.

Add #[used] typed fn-pointer statics for all 23 js_typed_feedback_* exports —
same retention mechanism as value/dyn_index.rs (KEEP_JS_DYN_INDEX_GET) /
process.rs (KEEP_JS_SETENV, #1344). (A [usize;N] ptrtoint array or [*const ();N]
pointer array do NOT survive thin-LTO; only individual typed fn-pointer statics
keep the symbol external — verified via llvm-nm + the four async-context tests
now linking and passing under auto-optimize.)

fix(runtime,hir): WeakMap/WeakSet dynamic dispatch + param-property defaults (toward Effect #321) (#1763)

WeakMap/WeakSet held in an `any`-typed binding (effect's
`globalValue(() => new WeakMap())`, whose generic return type erases the
WeakMap-ness) couldn't dispatch .has/.get/.set/.delete: js_native_call_method
had no arm for them, so randomHashCache.has(self) in Hash.ts threw
"has is not a function". js_weakmap_new/js_weakset_new now stamp a GC-stable
reserved class_id (0xFFFF0027/0028, following CLASS_ID_MAP/SET) and the dynamic
dispatcher routes has/get/set/delete/add to the existing js_weakmap_*/
js_weakset_* helpers. (A raw-pointer registry like Map/Set's would dangle:
these objects are GcHeader-backed and movable.)

Constructor parameter properties with a default (`readonly tags = []`) dropped
the default during lowering (class_members.rs forced default: None), leaving
this.tags null when the arg was omitted; effect's MetricKeyImpl then threw
"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')" in Hash.array(this.tags).
The TsParamProp arms now capture the default so build_default_param_stmts
applies it before the synthesized `this.field = param` assignment.

Together these make `import * as Effect from "effect/Effect";
Effect.runSync(Effect.succeed(42))` print 42, matching node.

Refs #1757, #1758, #321.

fix(hir): assign derived-class TS parameter properties after super() (toward Effect #321) (#1771)

A derived-class constructor's own parameter properties (`constructor(readonly
x: T)`) were lowered by prepending `this.x = x` to the top of the constructor
body. In a derived class the body starts with the `super(...)` call, and `this`
is unusable before super() runs — so the prepended assignments were dropped and
the derived class's own param-props ended up `undefined` (only base-class
param-props, assigned inside the base constructor via super(), survived).

effect's SchemaAST exercises this directly, e.g.

    class OptionalType extends Type {
      constructor(type: AST, readonly isOptional: boolean, annotations = {}) {
        super(type, annotations)
      }
    }

left `this.isOptional` undefined. The synthesis now splices the `this.field =
param` assignments in immediately AFTER the SuperCall (matching TS emit order)
for derived classes; base classes (no super() call) keep prepending. The
default-param / destructuring prologues only touch params (not `this`), so they
remain at the top and run before super().

Refs #1758, #321.

fix(runtime): Buffer.from() handles inline SSO short strings (#1767) (#1773)

`js_buffer_from_value` only recognized heap strings via the STRING_TAG-only
`is_string()` predicate. Strings of length 0..=5 are stored inline in the
NaN-box payload under SHORT_STRING_TAG (0x7FF9, the Small String
Optimization), which `is_string()` rejects. Such a value fell through to the
pointer-extraction path, where its inline bytes (e.g. the ASCII of a 5-char
`apiKey` like "mango") were masked to 48 bits and dereferenced as an
`ArrayHeader*` — SIGSEGV.

This surfaced as a crash in `js_buffer_from_value` during
`@perryts/mysql`'s prepared-statement param encoder (`Buffer.from(v,
'utf8')`) on the first parameterized query, once the #1663 microtask fix let
execution reach it.

Add an SSO branch that decodes the inline bytes and routes them through a
shared `buffer_from_str_bytes` helper (extracted from `js_buffer_from_string`)
so the heap and inline paths honor identical hex/base64/latin1/utf8 encoding
semantics. Add runtime regression tests covering empty/1..=5-byte SSO values
under utf8 and hex.

fix(codegen): don't mis-lower String/Number methods on a dynamic native-module sub-namespace receiver (#1760) (#1775)

`(path as any)[k].normalize(...)` resolves `path[k]` to a runtime
sub-namespace object (`path.win32` / `path.posix`), so the `.normalize`
call must route through the generic `js_native_call_method` dispatch
(→ `dispatch_native_module_method`, the #1740 runtime arms). Codegen's
String-method fallback for Any-typed receivers classified `normalize`
(and other prototype-name-colliding methods) as a `String.prototype`
method purely by name and emitted a string-method lowering — handing the
namespace-object pointer to a string FFI and SIGSEGV-ing.

Add `is_native_module_dynamic_index()` (matches the auditable
`ns[dynamicKey]` shape: `IndexGet { object: NativeModuleRef(_), index:
<non-literal> }`) and gate the String-method fallback plus the
`toFixed`/`toPrecision`/`toExponential` Number branches on it, so these
receivers fall through to generic native dispatch.

Scoped to a *non-literal* index: `(path as any)["sep"]` lowers to a
`PropertyGet` and can legitimately be a string, so it keeps its
string-method lowering. Only the dynamic `[k]` form produces `IndexGet`.

Tests: new `path/dynamic-subns/normalize-format.ts` exercises
`normalize`/`format` on both sub-namespaces via `[k]`; the companion
`method-dispatch.ts` comment updated (the gap it noted is now closed).

feat(hir): classify new Function/eval call sites + refusal diagnostic (#1678) (#1776)

Phase 0 of #1677 (AOT-first eval/new Function strategy). Establishes the
single decision point every later phase builds on: a classifier that
buckets each `new Function` / `Function(...)` / `eval(...)` site into

  1. const-foldable        — literal/substitution-free body (→ #1679)
  2. known-library-codegen  — from fast-json-stringify / ajv / find-my-way
                              (the Fastify JIT trio; → #1680/#1681/#1682)
  3. runtime-unknown        — genuinely runtime-dynamic code string

Only the runtime-unknown bucket is refused, with a precise diagnostic that
names the surface, file:line, and originating package (or "user source").
Buckets 1 and 2 keep their existing placeholder lowering so the phases that
own them can swap it in without a behaviour change here — Phase 0 is pure
analysis + reporting, it never compiles, folds, or evaluates anything.

Before this, both shapes silently fell through to broken lowerings (a bare
`Function`/`eval` ident → GlobalGet(0) sentinel → runtime TypeError, and
`new Function(...)` → an unknown-class class_id=0 empty-object placeholder)
with no indication of why.

New module crates/perry-hir/src/eval_classifier.rs (pure classification +
diagnostic + instrumentation), hooked at the two Function-shape lowering
sites (expr_new for `new Function`, expr_call for `Function(...)`/`eval`).
The `Function('return this')()` globalThis fold (#957/#959) runs first and
short-circuits, so it is unaffected.

Instrumentation: PERRY_EVAL_DIAG=1 logs every classified site (surface,
file:line, package, bucket, body preview) to stderr. Escape hatch:
PERRY_ALLOW_EVAL=1 downgrades the bucket-3 refusal to the legacy
fall-through for a one-off build (mirrors #503's PERRY_ALLOW_DYNAMIC_STDLIB).

Tests: 9 unit tests covering each bucket + provenance + line resolution +
preview truncation. Verified end-to-end on direct `new Function`/`eval`
samples (refused, with file:line + provenance), a const-foldable sample
(passes through), an ajv-path sample (known-library bucket), and the
existing `Function('return this')()` fold (still works).

so the scaffolding threw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'call')"
before the API under test ran — that was the radar's single largest

feat(hir): const-fold literal new Function bodies to native functions (#1679) (#1783)

Phase 1 of #1677. When the Phase 0 classifier (#1678) would bucket a
`new Function(...)` / `Function(...)` site as const-foldable — every
argument is a compile-time-constant string — compile it to a real native
function instead of leaving it to fall through. This is true ahead-of-time
eval and builds the string→HIR plumbing Phase 3 will reuse.

How: synthesize the equivalent `(function (<params>) { <body> })` source
(joining all-but-last args as the param list, last arg as the body, per
Node's `new Function` semantics), parse it via perry-parser, and lower it
through the normal `lower_fn_expr` path — exactly as if the user had
written the function literal. The body references only its own params plus
globals, so it lowers to a capture-free closure (new Function has no
enclosing-scope access).

Also folds the `(0, eval)('this')` / `(0, eval)('globalThis')` indirect-eval
idiom to Expr::GlobalThisExpr (indirect eval runs in global scope), the same
singleton `Function('return this')()` folds to (#957/#959).

New module crates/perry-hir/src/lower/const_fold_fn.rs, hooked at both
Function-shape sites BEFORE the Phase 0 refusal: expr_new.rs (`new
Function`) and expr_call/mod.rs (`Function(...)` / indirect eval). The
`Function('return this')()` fold still runs first and is unaffected.
Non-constant bodies still hit the Phase 0 refusal — no regression. A
const body that parses but can't lower surfaces a clear, span-tagged
compile error at the call site instead of the old broken placeholder.

perry-parser promoted from dev- to regular dependency of perry-hir (no
cycle; only adds swc_ecma_parser to the build) so lowering can parse the
synthesized source.

Tests: test-files/test_new_function_const_fold.ts (single-expression body,
multi-arg param names, comma-joined params, no-param, multi-statement body
referencing a global, the call form) and
test-files/test_indirect_eval_globalthis.ts — both byte-for-byte parity vs
`node --experimental-strip-types`. perry-hir suite green; fmt/clippy clean.

test(node-core): add --auto-optimize to #800 radar so ext-crate APIs are measurable (#1778) (#1784)

Perry's http/net/https/ws servers, zlib, crypto and async_hooks live in
perry-ext-* crates / Cargo features that are only built and added to the
link line by the auto-optimize path. The #800 radar compiles with

.a), so those tests compile but fail to link
(Undefined symbols: _js_node_http_create_server, _js_net_create_server, ...)

the full sweep (~570 tests) and a large understatement of those APIs' parity.

program links the ext crates it actually imports. The first compile per
distinct import-set triggers a cargo rebuild (cached per feature-set under

fix(hir,codegen): class expressions → heap class objects with per-evaluation own static fields (#1786) (#1792)

Lower a class EXPRESSION (`class C {...}` in value position, e.g. effect
Schema's `make(ast) => class { static ast = ast }`) to a new HIR node
Expr::ClassExprFresh, which codegen lowers to a real heap "class object":
js_object_alloc(template_class_id, n) stamped with the compile-time
template's class_id (so static methods / new / instanceof keep dispatching
through the existing class_id machinery), carrying the per-evaluation named
static fields (js_object_set_field_by_name) and symbol static fields
(js_object_set_symbol_property) as OWN properties. The class value is the
object POINTER, so make(a) !== make(b) and each carries its own statics; the
object is GC-traced + collectible (no leak). Top-level class DECLARATIONS are
unchanged (INT32(class_id)).

Foundation only (epic #1785, design #1772); the diff is purely additive with
zero runtime-source changes (the runtime allocator/field/symbol helpers
already exist; the abandoned integer-hack helpers are not present). Out of
scope, each its own subticket: static-method this-binding (#1787),
extends-inheritance of own statics (#1788), new/instanceof/typeof on a
class-object value (#1789), GC layout descriptor (#1790).

identity, per-evaluation own statics (named + anonymous via factory), and
no-this static-method dispatch.

fix(runtime): SSO-aware decoding at is_string()-then-fallback sites (#1781) (#1794)

`JSValue::is_string()` is STRING_TAG-only and returns false for inline SSO
short strings (SHORT_STRING_TAG, len 0..=5). Any site shaped like
`if v.is_string() { read ptr } else { treat as pointer/number/array }`
mishandles a runtime-produced short string (concat/JSON.parse/slice/buffer
results): the SSO value enters the fallback and either derefs garbage or
silently yields a wrong result.

keys are always heap STRING_TAG (pushed via JSValue::string_ptr), and
string literals are interned to heap, so all keys_array-loop sites and
native-module name reads are confirmed safe. Fixed the sites that can
receive a runtime SSO value, routing each through is_any_string() +
short_string_to_buf or js_get_string_pointer_unified (which materializes
SSO bytes to the heap so downstream *StringHeader code is unchanged):

- perf_hooks: new string_of() helper + 7 sites. The literal "mark" (4
  bytes) is SSO, so mark/measure resolution, getEntriesByName type
  filters, and PerformanceObserver entryTypes silently dropped it.
- fs/callbacks decode_flags_string: every flag ("r","w","a",...) is <=5
  bytes, so the read-only probe never matched.
- fs/mod decode_path_value: short relative paths decoded to None.
- bigint: BigInt("123") returned 0n.
- builtins/table: short console.table cells rendered "NaN".
- value/dynamic_array js_dynamic_array_get: (shortStr as any)[i] -> undefined.
- object/field_get_set js_object_has_property: "id" in obj -> false.
- object/object_ops js_object_is: mixed SSO/heap content compare.
- object/delete_rest js_object_delete_dynamic: delete obj[shortKey] no-op'd.

fix(runtime,codegen): new / instanceof / typeof on a class-object value (#1789) (#1795)

Make the instance-side operations work when the class is a class-expression
VALUE (a heap class object from #1786) rather than `INT32(class_id)`. Adds a
per-object discriminator `OBJECT_TYPE_CLASS` so a class object is told apart
from its instances (which share the template's class_id):

  `gc_type`/`class_id`, not on this tag, so #1786/#1787/#1788 reads are

  existing INT32-ClassRef case.
- `new (classObjectValue)(args)` → `js_new_function_construct` reads the
  object's class_id and allocates an instance of it, so instance methods
  dispatch and `instanceof` matches. (Constructor-body/field-init via dynamic
  new is a tracked refinement; static `new ClassName()` is unchanged.)
- `x instanceof classObjectValue` → `js_instanceof_dynamic` resolves the

fix(runtime,codegen): inherit static methods through `extends` of a class-object value (#1788) (#1797)

A class declaration that `extends` a class-expression value
(`class Sub extends make("A") {}`, effect's `class Number$ extends
make(numberKeyword) {}`) now inherits the parent's STATIC METHODS, not just
static fields (#1788's field half landed in #1793). `Sub.greet()` /
`Sub.withArgs(...)` dispatch to the inherited static method with `this` bound
to the subclass, so `this.<field>` resolves through the subclass's
static-field chain.

Static methods are emitted as `perry_static_*` (no `this` param — they read
`this` from the implicit-this slot) and were NOT in the instance vtable, so a
subclass of a dynamic parent couldn't resolve them at compile time. New:

- runtime `CLASS_STATIC_METHODS` registry (class_id → name → (func_ptr,
  param_count)) + `js_register_class_static_method`, populated by a codegen
  loop in emit_string_pool mirroring the instance-vtable registration
  (static-method names added to the pre-intern pass in artifacts.rs).
- runtime `js_class_static_method_call(receiver, name, args)`: resolves the
  receiver's class_id (INT32 ClassRef or POINTER class object), walks the
  class_id parent chain in CLASS_STATIC_METHODS, binds `this` via the
  implicit-this slot, and calls the method. On a genuine miss it returns the
  receiver unchanged — preserving the prior "yield the class ref for a chained
  call during module init" behavior for truly-absent methods.
- codegen routes a ClassRef-receiver static-method call that didn't resolve
  in the class's statically-visible chain to this helper.

feat(tooling): build-time codegen convention — perry.codegen + ajv/standalone (#1680) (#1801)

Phase 2 of #1677. Many libraries that would JIT a function at runtime
(`ajv`, Prisma, Drizzle, …) ship an eval-free build-time mode that emits
plain source. Where that exists, an AOT compiler should consume the
generated output instead of running a JIT — zero new evaluation infra,
highest ROI.

Adds a `perry.codegen` convention to the host package.json: an array of
build commands (bare string or `{ command, label }`) Perry runs before
module collection, in the package.json's directory, then compiles the

dependency's — same trust boundary as `perry.compilePackages` (a transitive
dep can't smuggle in a build command). A failing step fails the build with
its captured stdout/stderr. `--no-codegen` / `PERRY_SKIP_CODEGEN=1` skips
the steps for reproducible / sandboxed builds whose output is committed.

  `codegen_dir` on `CompilationContext`.
- host_config.rs: parse `perry.codegen` from the host package.json.
- codegen_steps.rs: the runner (sh -c in codegen_dir, bail on failure) +

- compile.rs: run the steps between config load and module collection.

fix(runtime): static symbol property lookup on class-object values (#1758) (#1810)

Two bugs in symbol-keyed property access on class values, both breaking
effect's `isSchema` (and therefore `dual` / `transformOrFail`):

- `Sym in classObject` (the `in` operator / `Predicate.hasProperty`) returned
  false even for an OWN static `[Sym]` property: `js_object_has_property`'s
  generic path rejects non-string keys outright, and its INT32 class-ref path
  only checked own `CLASS_STATIC_SYMBOLS`.
- `Sub[Sym]` where `class Sub extends make(...)` returned undefined: inherited
  static symbols weren't walked through the class-expression prototype chain
  (`js_object_get_symbol_property` only checked own props / own static symbols).

effect's `isSchema(u) = hasProperty(u, TypeId) && isObject(u[TypeId])` with
`BigIntFromSelf = class extends make(bigIntKeyword) {}` (carries `[TypeId]`
only via inheritance) returned false, so `transformOrFail`'s `dual` predicate
(`isSchema(args[0]) && isSchema(args[1])`) was false and `transformOrFail`
degraded to a curried function — `makeTransformationClass` never ran, leaving a
downstream schema's `.ast` undefined (`Cannot read properties of undefined`).

Fix:
- new `resolve_proto_chain_symbol` (class_registry.rs): symbol-keyed analogue of
  `resolve_proto_chain_field` — walks `CLASS_PROTOTYPE_OBJECTS` + the class_id
  parent chain, checking each prototype object's OWN symbol props via a new
