feat(compiler): self-hosted build-time precompile() — Perry runs its own codegen, no node/V8 (#1681) (#1814)

Phase 3 of #1677, prototype. The premise of the original issue is obsolete:
`perry-jsruntime`/V8 was already removed, and re-embedding an engine would
contradict the tracker's goal. Instead Perry evaluates build-time codegen
*itself* — it compiles the program to native and runs its own output — so
there is no node dependency and no engine in the shipped binary.

Surface: `precompile(EXPR)` — a build-time intrinsic. `EXPR` is evaluated at
build time and must produce a *function-source string*; that source is then
compiled natively and substituted for the call.

Two-stage mechanism (no node, no V8):
1. Capture stage: the driver compiles the entry via Perry's OWN binary
   (`current_exe`) with `PERRY_PRECOMPILE_CAPTURE=1`. In that mode each
   `precompile(EXPR)` lowers to `console.log("<marker>" + JSON.stringify(EXPR))`,
   keyed by the call site's `(source_file, span.lo)`. The driver runs the
   produced binary — Perry executing its own compiled output — and parses the
   emitted generated sources.
2. Main compile: each `precompile(EXPR)` site is replaced by the captured
   source, parsed and lowered as a function (reusing the Phase 1 string→HIR
   path). A site with no captured result, or a result that isn't a function
   expression, is a hard compile error — no silent fallback.

Implementation:
- perry-hir: `PRECOMPILE_CAPTURE` / `PRECOMPILE_RESULTS` thread-locals
  (ir/constants.rs); `try_precompile` + `lower_precompiled_source`
  (expr_call/intrinsics.rs), wired into `lower_call_inner`.
- perry: `precompile_capture.rs` driver (capture subprocess + marker parser,
  3 unit tests); `precompile_capture`/`precompile_results` on
  CompilationContext, re-installed on the lowering thread before each
  `lower_module_full` in collect_modules (rayon-safe, same pattern as the
  #665/#503 thread-locals — set-once-on-main doesn't reach worker threads).

Restrictions (by design): only build-time-knowable, deterministic codegen is
supported. Genuinely runtime-dynamic `new Function(runtimeData)`/`eval` stays
refused by Phase 0 — there's nothing to evaluate at build time, and an AOT
binary shouldn't fake it.

Verified: `test-files/test_precompile_basic.ts` (+ expected output) — Perry
compiles+runs the capture helper itself, captures two generated functions,
compiles them natively, and produces the expected output; the binary links 0
V8 symbols. Normal programs (no `precompile(`) are unaffected. `make_*`
generators returning function sources, the call form, and the
not-a-function error path all checked.

This prototype proves the self-hosted two-stage mechanism. fast-json-stringify
end-to-end is a follow-up: it additionally needs fjs's Serializer helpers
compiled via compilePackages and the codegen-correctness fixes (#1802/#1803)
for byte-parity.

fix(hir): nested local must not reuse a module const's forward-declared id (#1758) (#1815)

The module-level forward-declaration pass pre-registers a LocalId for each
module-level `const`/`let` so forward references resolve. The var-decl lowering
reused that pre-registered id whenever a binding of the same name was lowered —
including a NESTED local inside a function body. So:

  const merge = (s, t) => zipWith(s, t);          // forward-refs module zipWith
  function helper() { const zipWith = 5; ... }     // local shadow
  const zipWith = (a, b) => a + b;                 // module const

`helper`'s local `zipWith` consumed the module var's pre-registered id, so the
local and the module binding shared one id; the real `zipWith` function landed
on a fresh id; and `merge`'s closure — which forward-resolved `zipWith` to the
pre-registered id — pointed at the wrong (uninitialised) slot →
`TypeError: value is not a function`. (Order-dependent: only triggers when a
local shadow precedes the module const.)

This blocked the entire `import { Effect } from "effect"` barrel: effect's
`layer.merge = dual(2, (self, that) => zipWith(self, that, ...))` references the
module `zipWith` (exported at internal/layer.ts:1191), and a local `zipWith`
(L1180, inside another function) precedes it — so `TestContext.ts` module init
threw.

Fix: gate the `pre_registered_module_vars` id-reuse (both the simple-ident and
destructuring-fallback sites in `destructuring/var_decl.rs`) on MODULE scope
(`scope_depth == 0 && inside_block_scope == 0`), mirroring `define_local`'s own
module-level tagging. A nested local of the same name now gets a fresh id.

With this, `import { Effect } from "effect"; Effect.runSync(Effect.succeed(42))`
prints `42` byte-identical to node — the full effect framework now works
end-to-end (deep import, Schema init, Schema decode, barrel). New gap test
`test_gap_module_const_local_shadow.ts` (core shape + dual-indirection +
independent-nested-local guard), byte-identical to node.

fix(codegen): cross-module function using `arguments` returns undefined (#1816/#321) (#1817)

* fix(codegen): cross-module function using `arguments` (synthetic-arguments param) (#1816)

A cross-module/cross-package function that references `arguments` returned
`undefined` for calls passing fewer args than its (inflated) param count.

Perry appends a synthetic `arguments` rest param (`name:"arguments",
is_rest:true`) to any function whose body uses `arguments` (#677). The
same-module call path (`func_ref.rs`) bundles ALL passed args into that param
(matching `arguments.length` semantics), but the cross-module path
(`extern_func.rs`) treated it like a real `...rest` and bundled only the
*trailing* args (those after the fixed params). So `firstOrCount(5)` (1 arg,
inflated arity 3) saw an empty `arguments` and returned undefined.

and `dual` — the two most-used combinators — both reference `arguments`, so
they returned `undefined` cross-package, cascading through `Effect.map`, the
fiber runtime, and `ParseResult`. (`import { Effect }` barrel's
`runSync(succeed(42))` only "worked" pre-fix because `pipe` returning undefined
harmlessly short-circuited the unused `TestContext.live`/`sink.ts` pipes.)

- propagate "trailing param is the synthetic `arguments`" cross-module via a new
  `imported_func_synthetic_arguments` set (collected in `compile.rs` next to
  `exported_func_has_rest`, built per-importer at the named/namespace/re-export
  sites, threaded through `CompileOptions` → codegen ctx).
- in `extern_func.rs`, when the imported callee has a synthetic `arguments`
  param, bundle ALL args (from index 0) into it instead of just the trailing
  ones — mirroring the same-module `func_ref.rs` path.

fix(hir,codegen,runtime): computed-key class methods + dynamic-key this-binding (#321) (#1818)

Two coupled bugs kept effect's `FiberRuntime` op-dispatch loop
(`this[(cur)._op](cur)`) from working, so any `Effect.map`/`Schema` use
hung or threw:

1. HIR dropped generic computed-key instance methods. A method defined
   with a non-well-known computed key — `[OpCodes.OP_ON_SUCCESS](op){...}`,
   `[Hash.symbol](){...}`, `[KEY](x){...}` — hit
   `Err("Unsupported method key")` and was silently discarded, so
   `inst["OnSuccess"]` read `undefined`. They now lower to a per-instance
   closure field keyed by the runtime-evaluated key expression
   (`this[expr] = function (...) {...}`), reusing the fn-expr path so
   `this` binds dynamically. (lower_computed_key_method_as_field, wired
   into both lower_class_decl and lower_class_from_ast; instance-only —
   static computed-key methods are a deferred follow-up.)

2. Dynamic-key method dispatch dropped `this`. `obj[k](args)` where `k`
   isn't statically a string fell through to a plain closure-call, so a
   method stored as a class field reached by a runtime key saw
   `this === undefined`. New runtime entry `js_native_call_method_value`
   binds `this = obj` for any key type (string keys go through the full
   dispatch tower; symbol/other keys read the property then call with
   `this` bound); codegen routes non-static-string `IndexGet`-callee calls
   through it (numeric-keyed element calls excluded).

Result: `effect/Schema` initializes (`S.String`/`S.Number`/`S.Struct`
all resolve), `effect/Effect` `runSync(succeed(42))` stays green. The
fiber `runLoop` no longer hangs; `Effect.map` via `runSync` now advances
to a separate next blocker (an empty-object defect thrown before the
OnSuccess continuation) tracked for follow-up.

fix(hir): namespace-member call mis-lowered to Array intrinsic (#321) (#1819)

array-method fold, which only excluded the `join` case (its #420 guard).

`export const map = core.map`, so `import * as Effect; Effect.map(eff, f)`
returned `[]` and the fiber never ran (`Effect.map(...)` produced an
empty value instead of an `OnSuccess` effect).

(`import { CHAIN_NAMES }`) are not namespaces, so genuinely-imported
arrays still fold — `NS.items.map(cb)` (array reached through the

fix(codegen,runtime): static class field/method dispatch — same + cross module (#1787) (#1820)

`Class.staticMember(args)` mis-dispatched in two ways:

1. A static FIELD holding a callable — `static make = (x) => ...`
   (effect's `SchemaAST.Union.make` / `.unify`) — is not a static
   METHOD, so the static-method vtable walk missed it. The call then
   fell through to `js_class_static_method_call`, which returns the
   receiver class ref on a method miss → `Class.make(5)` came back as
   `1` (the INT32 class id).

2. Cross-module: even static METHODS on an imported class returned `1`.
   `resolve_static_dispatch_cls` only recognised `ClassRef` /
   `ClassExprFresh` / factory receivers, so an imported-class receiver
   (`ExternFuncRef("C")` from `import { C }`, or a `namespace.Class`
   PropertyGet — effect's `AST.Union.make`) never reached the static
   dispatch tower at all.

from `ParseResult.ts`: it returned undefined and crashed Schema decode
reading `_tag`.

- codegen (property_get.rs): after the static-method walk misses, look
  for a string-named static FIELD on the class chain and, if found, read
  its installed closure via `StaticFieldGet` and invoke it with the args

  recognise imported-class receivers — `ExternFuncRef(name)` and
  `<namespace>.<ClassName>` — gated on known-class membership
  (`ctx.class_ids`), and route them (plus the broadened receiver gate)
  through the runtime static tower.
- runtime (class_registry.rs): `js_class_static_method_call` now, on a
  static-method miss, walks the class_id chain in `CLASS_DYNAMIC_PROPS`
  (where `js_class_register_static_field` records static fields) and
  invokes a resolved callable field. This covers imported classes whose
  compile-time stub carries no static methods/fields.

dynamic `this`, so a plain closure call is correct.

fix(runtime,codegen): expose Symbol.iterator on arrays (#321) (#1822)

Arrays did not expose the iterator protocol as a property:
`Symbol.iterator in arr` was `false` and `arr[Symbol.iterator]` read back a

numeric fast path). for-of worked (it's special-cased), but the
property/`in` exposure was missing.

effect's `Predicate.isIterable(x)` is literally `Symbol.iterator in x`, so
`isIterable([...])` returned false. That broke `Effect.all`: it dispatches
through `forEach`, a predicate-`dual` whose predicate is
`(args) => isIterable(args[0])`. With the predicate false, `forEach` took
its data-last branch and returned a curried *function* instead of the
combined effect — `runSync` then saw a non-effect and produced a `{}`

- runtime (`symbol.rs`): `js_object_get_symbol_property`, for an array
  receiver + the well-known iterator symbol, returns the array's `values`
  method bound via `js_class_method_bind` (the same callable-binding path
  `Symbol.dispose` already uses). This makes both `Symbol.iterator in arr`
  (which routes through `js_object_has_property` → the symbol resolver) and
  the property read resolve to a callable.
- codegen (`index_get.rs`): the array IndexGet fast path now routes a
  `SymbolFor` key to `js_object_get_symbol_property` instead of `fptosi`-ing
  it to a numeric index.

"function", `Predicate.isIterable([...])` → true, and `Effect.all([...])`

(`Effect.all` `runSync` still hits a deeper blocker — the bound iterator

feat(runtime): PERRY_DISPATCH_DIAG — surface silent dynamic-dispatch misses (#1823)

When a dynamic dispatch falls through every resolution tower (vtable,
static-method, static-field, prototype, field-scan, namespace, symbol),
the runtime returns a *silent placeholder* — the receiver class ref, an
empty object, undefined — instead of throwing, because some placeholders
are load-bearing (effect's `.pipe()` chains yield the class ref during
module init, #687). The upside is no spurious crashes; the downside is a
typo'd / unsupported member surfaces far downstream as a stray
`{}`/`1`/`[]`/function, turning each into a multi-hour localization
(this is what made the #321 effect bugs — `Union.make`, `Effect.all` —
so expensive to find).

Add an opt-in diagnostic: `PERRY_DISPATCH_DIAG=1` prints a located,
typed report at the moment of a true miss — the tower that fell through,
the receiver's type/class name, the member name, and the placeholder
being returned — so the bug surfaces at its real call site instead of
downstream. It does NOT change behavior (print-only, gated on the env
var; near-zero cost when off), so the load-bearing placeholders keep
working.

Wired into the silent/swallowed miss points:
- `js_class_static_method_call`'s receiver-return (the `1` from
  `Class.staticMember()` — the `Union.make` case).
- `js_native_call_method`'s recursion-depth-guard empty-object return.
- `js_native_call_method`'s catch-all "<m> is not a function" throw
  (printed *before* the throw, so frameworks with broad try/catch like
  effect's fiber runtime can't swallow the call site into a `{}` defect).

Example (`(C as any).doesNotExist(7)`):
  [perry dispatch-miss] static-member-call: class-ref `C` (id 1).
  "doesNotExist" did not resolve → returning the receiver (class ref).
  ... Check the call site for "doesNotExist".

Verified: quiet (0 reports) on working effect programs (`Effect.map` →
20), reports unchanged program output, zero regressions across the gap
sweep (3 pre-existing fails only). Refs #321.

fix(gc): root IMPLICIT_THIS so moving GC can't strand the dispatch receiver (#1813) (#1825)

The implicit-`this` thread-local cell holds the NaN-boxed receiver for the
duration of a dynamically-dispatched non-arrow method body (set/restored by
js_native_call_method and the codegen js_implicit_this_set save/restore around
js_native_call_value). The receiver is a live heap object for the whole call,
but the cell was plain TLS that no GC root scanner visited.

When a moving GC runs during that body — e.g. @perryts/mysql's Pool.acquire
runs a nested stdlib pump that drains the handshake IO while nativeScramble
allocates — the receiver is evacuated/copied. With no root slot to rewrite, the
cell kept the stale pre-move pointer and the body's next `this`-derived dispatch
dereferenced relocated memory: the concurrent-load SIGSEGV in
js_native_call_method reported in #1813. Objects only move under nursery/RSS
pressure, which is why it only reproduced under concurrency (load-dependent
heisenbug) and across both auth plugins.

Register IMPLICIT_THIS as a GC mutable-root scanner: mark keeps `this` alive,
rewrite tracks its relocation. Non-pointer tags (the TAG_UNDEFINED default) are
no-ops, so scanning the idle cell is free. Every codegen and runtime dispatch
site funnels through this one cell, so a single scanner closes the gap.

fix(gc): restore shadow stack on exception unwind (#1830) (#1837)

A `gc()` inside a `try/catch` can SIGSEGV when the thrown exception
propagated up from a deeper function that had pointer-typed locals.

Root cause: `js_throw` unwinds with `longjmp`, which restores the native
SP/registers to the `setjmp` site without running the epilogues of the
functions being unwound past — so their `js_shadow_frame_pop` calls are
skipped. The precise-root shadow stack's `frame_top` is left pointing at
the orphaned (now-dead) callee frames. The next GC then walks those
frames via `visit_shadow_stack_root_slots`, and the copying/evacuating
collector both reads and writes back through `slot_ptrs` that point into
stack memory that has already been unwound and is being reused by the
catch body. Whether that surfaces as a crash depends on the recycled
stack contents passing the `valid_ptrs` classifier — which is why every
minimal repro passed while a real workload crashed (matches the bug
report and the #1824 profile).

Fix: capture a `ShadowSavepoint` (frame_top + stack length) in
`js_try_push`, before the protected region can push any callee frames,
and restore it in `js_throw` right before the `longjmp`. The orphaned
frames are dropped before any later GC can scan them. This is purely a
runtime change — no codegen changes — and is correct for both inlined
and non-inlined throwing callees.

Tests:
- gc::tests::roots: orphaned callee frames are scanned without the
  restore and dropped with it (value-slot and bound-slot variants).
- exception::tests: js_try_push records the savepoint and the unwind
  path restores it across orphaned frames.
- test-files/test_issue_1830_gc_in_catch_after_deep_throw.ts: a deep
  throw caught at an outer try, then gc() under allocation pressure;
  runs clean and byte-identical to Node (gc() guarded by typeof).

fix(codegen): #1845 nested arrow captures dynamic `this` in computed-key methods (#1848)

A nested arrow that captures `this` inside a computed-key method
(`[expr]() { ... () => this ... }`) snapshotted a bogus 0.0 sentinel
instead of the receiver, so the arrow's `this` arrived as the number 0.

Computed-key methods lower to a per-instance function-expression closure
field (lower_computed_key_method_as_field): their `this` binds
dynamically at call time via the runtime's IMPLICIT_THIS, so the
enclosing codegen frame has an empty this_stack. A direct `Expr::This`
read already falls back to js_implicit_this_get; the nested-closure
captures_this patch sites in expr/closure.rs used the 0.0 sentinel when
this_stack was empty. Fix both sites to fall back to js_implicit_this_get,
matching the direct-read path.

This was effect's Effect.all / Effect.forEach blocker: the fiber-runtime
handler `[OP_WITH_RUNTIME](op){ internalCall(() => op.i0(this, ...)) }`
passed `this = 0` into the WithRuntime body, so `fiber.currentContext`
read undefined and the fiber died with a `{}` FiberFailure — even for
`Effect.all([])`.

feat(util): implement util.promisify (#1779) (#1855)

Wires util.promisify(fn) through a real runtime closure instead of the
prior callable-export stub that read as a function but returned
undefined when called. This unblocks the bulk of Node's

feat(child_process): streaming spawn() ChildProcess + execFile/execFileSync (#1780) (#1858)

spawn() now returns a real streaming ChildProcess — an EventEmitter
(spawn/exit/close/error) whose stdout/stderr are Readable streams
(data/end) and stdin is Writable — instead of the spawnSync result
object whose .stdout was a string (so child.stdout.on(...) threw
"(string).on is not a function"). Also adds execFile (callback) and
execFileSync.

The child's output is captured synchronously at spawn time and the
spawn/data/end/exit/close events are deferred to a setImmediate
macrotask, so handlers registered synchronously after spawn() (e.g.
inside a Promise executor before the first await) are present when the
events fire. Perry has no async subprocess reactor; for the short-lived
commands these APIs target this is observationally identical to Node's
async pipe model once the deferred emission runs on the next tick.

ChildProcess and its stdout/stderr/stdin sub-objects are heap objects
whose methods are real closures (the node_stream.rs build_object
pattern), so child.stdout.on(...) / child.on(...) / child.kill() all
dispatch as ordinary JS object methods — no new codegen method dispatch
is needed; only spawn()/execFile()/execFileSync() get codegen routing.
Listener lists and buffered output live on the heap objects, so the GC
manages their lifetimes (reachable from the user's child reference).

fix(codegen): #26/#321 disambiguate same-named cross-module classes in field layout (#1853)

* fix(codegen): #26/#321 disambiguate same-named cross-module classes in field layout

effect Schema's AST was polluted: `PropertySignature.propertySignatures[0]`
reported 9 enumerable keys (`_tag,actual,annotations,ast,isOptional,isReadonly,
message,name,type`) vs Node's 5 (`annotations,isOptional,isReadonly,name,type`).
The 4 spurious `undefined` fields (`_tag,ast,actual,message`) are ParseResult's
`class Type`, NOT SchemaAST's `class Type` that PropertySignature actually
extends. This corrupted the schema AST that decode/encode/is walk.

Root cause: a class's `extends` parent was resolved by BARE NAME against
name-keyed tables that hold only one same-named class. effect exports a `Type`
from BOTH SchemaAST.ts (fields `type,annotations`) and ParseResult.ts (fields
`_tag,ast,actual,message`); modules that import both (e.g. Schema.ts) resolved
`OptionalType extends Type` to whichever `Type` was registered first, so
PropertySignature (← OptionalType ← Type) inherited the wrong fields. Three
sites colluded: the transitive-import closure (compile.rs) deduped parents by
name and never imported the correct-module `Type`; the keys-array builder and
allocation field-count walk (codegen) picked the first by-name stub; and the
constructor field-initializer chain walk wrote the wrong parent's fields onto
the instance as `undefined`.

Fix — disambiguate by source module (a class's `extends` resolves in its OWN
module's scope):
- compile.rs transitive closure resolves a parent in the child's own source
  path and tracks parent additions by (path,name) so the correct-module parent
  is imported even past the bare-name dedup; worklist keyed by index, not name.
- codegen keeps locally-shadowed imports available for parent resolution, and
  resolves parent chains (keys array, field count via new
  `class_field_counts`, AND constructor field-init via new `class_init_chains`)
  preferring the parent stub whose source prefix matches the child's.

(5 keys). No regressions in the class/object/field/inheritance test-files sweep;
test_class_field_layout produces correct output. The downstream

blocker for `effect/Ref` mutable state inside a gen (part of #321).

desugars identically to the existing `Let`-initializer delegation arm
(GetIterator + drive-and-re-yield while-loop, forwarding the resume
value per #1832), then returns `{ value: <iterator final value>, done:

is buffered across .write() and the codec runs on .end(), with
'data'/'end' deferred onto a queue drained by the main-thread pump so
listeners registered after .write() still fire and .pipe() forwards
chunks (returns dest for chaining).

feature (mirrors external-net-pump): dispatch arm + pump + has_active
externs, activated by optimized_libs when the flip strips compression.

the no-flip path. Also adds Brotli one-shots (brotliCompressSync/

fix(runtime): #36/#321 — class extends function-value inherits static props + setPrototypeOf chain (#1894)

A `class` that `extends` a plain FUNCTION value (not a class) now inherits the
parent function's OWN static properties and any properties on the function's
static prototype (`Object.setPrototypeOf(fn, protoObj)`).

effect's `Context.Tag(id)` returns a function `TagClass` with an OWN static
`key = id` whose `_op: "Tag"` / `[TagTypeId]` / `[EffectTypeId]` live on a
`TagProto` object wired in via `Object.setPrototypeOf(TagClass, TagProto)`. User
code writes `class Svc extends Context.Tag("Svc")<...>() {}`. Pre-fix, reading
`Svc.key` / `Svc._op` / `Svc[TagTypeId]` all returned `undefined`, so effect did
not recognize the Tag as an Effect; the fiber died with a `Cause.die(<TypeError
reading '_V'>)` that pretty-printed as `{}`.

Root cause: Perry only modeled OBJECT (class-expression) superclasses in the
dynamic-parent path, and `Object.setPrototypeOf(closure, obj)` was a no-op, so a
function-valued superclass contributed nothing to static-property lookup.

Fix (runtime side-tables, no codegen change):
- Object.setPrototypeOf(closure, protoObj) records the closure-to-proto link
  (CLOSURE_STATIC_PROTOTYPES); closure string- and symbol-keyed reads walk it.
- js_register_class_parent_dynamic records a closure parent
  (CLASS_PARENT_CLOSURES) when the superclass is a function value; class-ref
  static getters (string + symbol) consult it and the closure's proto chain.

fix(hir): #39/#321 data-last namespace export sort/reverse must dispatch member, not fold to ArraySort (carries #1901 try/finally) (#1912)

* fix(codegen): #37/#321 catch-less try/finally must re-propagate exceptions

A `try { ... } finally { ... }` with no `catch` clause was swallowing
exceptions: the setjmp landing pad ran js_try_end(), fell through to the
shared finally/merge block, and the function returned `undefined` instead
of re-raising. Per ECMAScript the finally must run and then the original
exception must propagate.

Root cause: crates/perry-codegen/src/stmt/try_stmt.rs lower_try() — the
`else` (no user catch) arm of the catch block now captures the pending
exception, runs a dedicated copy of the finally body, and re-raises via
js_throw (unless the finally itself completes abruptly).

Surfaced under effect's internalCall "forced" path
(`try { return body() } finally {}`), which swallowed body()'s return when
body threw, presenting as `(FiberFailure) Error: {}`.

Adds test-files/test_gap_try_finally_no_catch_rethrow.ts (byte-identical
to node --experimental-strip-types).

* fix(hir): #39/#321 data-last namespace export `sort`/`reverse` must dispatch member, not fold to ArraySort

A module-namespace export named `sort` (effect's `Array.sort = dual(2, body)`,
a data-last/pipeable function) was mis-lowered to the `js_array_sort` intrinsic
when called as `NS.sort(cmp)`. `sort` (and the other non-overlapping mutators
`reverse`/`entries`/`keys`/`values`/`splice`/`fill`/...) are NOT in the
array-method `is_overlapping` set, so the existing imported-array namespace
guard didn't cover them: the call fell through to `try_array_only_methods`,
whose `"sort" if !args.is_empty()` arm folded `NS.sort(cmp)` into
`Expr::ArraySort { array: NS, comparator: cmp }`. The compiled binary then ran
`js_array_sort(NS, cmp)`, which returned the namespace object itself (typeof
"object") instead of the curried `(self) => sorted` closure, so the downstream
`pipe(bounds, NS.sort(cmp), ...)` threw "value is not a function".

This surfaced in effect's metric histogram path
(`hook.histogram` -> `pipe(bounds, Arr.sort(number.Order), Arr.map(...))`)
reached from `MetricRegistryImpl.getHistogram` at fiber exit (default
`runtimeMetrics` flag is on), breaking every `Effect.runSync(...)` fiber case.

Fix: in `try_array_only_methods`, bail (treat the receiver as not-an-array) for
ALL method names when the receiver identifier is a module namespace import
(`namespace_import_locals`), so the call dispatches the namespace export and the
data-last curried form is returned correctly.

Also carries the held #1901 try/finally fix (catch-less try/finally must
re-propagate exceptions) — that fix unmasked this bug, and the two land as a
pair so #1901 can be closed in favor of this PR.

fix(fastify): guard request pump against re-entry (#1824) (#1932)

js_fastify_process_pending dispatches each request handler inside a
setjmp try-frame (call_closure2_catching -> js_try_push). A handler that
awaits pumps the event loop (js_async_first_call ->
js_promise_run_microtasks -> js_stdlib_process_pending), which re-enters
js_fastify_process_pending while the outer handler's try-frame is still
open on the native stack. The re-entrant call started another request
handler, whose try-frame nested inside the suspended outer one. Under
concurrent load the nesting grew one level per in-flight request and blew
MAX_TRY_DEPTH (128), aborting with 'Try block nesting too deep' — observed
as a silent SIGSEGV (exit 139) under PM2 on Linux x86_64.

Add a thread-local re-entrancy guard: a nested pump call processes no new
requests and returns 0. Pending requests stay queued in each server's
request_rx and are picked up on the next top-level pump tick once the
current handler unwinds its try-frame. The in-flight handler's own await
still makes progress — its resolution drains through PENDING_RESOLUTIONS
in js_stdlib_process_pending, not through this request loop.

Repro (pre-fix): a Fastify + @perryts/mysql server crashes within the
first few requests under concurrent load (e.g. 500 reqs @ concurrency 30);
sequential load never crashes because requests never overlap. Post-fix:
5000 reqs @ concurrency 100 complete cleanly, server stays up.

fix(runtime): preserve class-ref tag in raw-f64 numeric-array layout (#321 effect Schema SIGSEGV) (#1961)

Fix: reject INT32-shaped values whose payload is a registered class id in value_bits_to_number (the single chokepoint all numeric-layout decisions funnel through). Storing a class ref into a numeric array now downgrades the layout and preserves the tag. A genuine integer that coincides with a registered class id only loses the raw-f64 optimization (still a valid number when read), so correctness is never at stake.

fix(runtime): bind this to receiver for inherited symbol-keyed method calls (#321 effect Context/Layer) (#1969)

A Symbol-keyed method inherited via Object.create(proto) was invoked with
`this` bound to the prototype P instead of the receiver o.

Root cause: object-literal computed-key methods are lowered with
captures_this:true and have their reserved (last) capture slot patched to
the literal object at construction time (symbol.rs::js_object_set_symbol_method).
When o = Object.create(P) resolves o[SYM](), js_native_call_method_value
resolves the inherited closure via the prototype-chain walk in
js_object_get_symbol_property — which returns P's closure verbatim, whose
captured this-slot is hardwired to P. Setting IMPLICIT_THIS = o does not
help because the closure body reads its baked-in this-slot, not IMPLICIT_THIS.

Fix: in js_native_call_method_value, when a symbol-keyed method is NOT an
OWN property of the receiver (i.e. inherited through the prototype chain),
rebind its this-slot to the receiver via clone_closure_rebind_this before
invoking. That helper is a no-op for non-captures_this closures and for
non-closure values, so own symbol methods, class symbol methods, effect's
Tag-class symbol statics (plain data), and the #1758/#36/#321
closure-proto-chain paths are all left untouched.

Repro (Node prints 9, pre-fix Perry printed undefined):
  const EQ = Symbol.for("eq");
  const P: any = { [EQ](this: any) { return this.v; } };
  const o = Object.create(P); o.v = 9;
  console.log(o[EQ]());

fix(async): lower awaits inside labeled and do-while loops (#1824) (#1965)

The async->generator transform splits an async function body into a
state machine at each await. Its body walkers were written for
For/While/If/Try/Switch and never handled `Stmt::DoWhile` or
`Stmt::Labeled`, so an `await` inside `do { ... } while (c)` or
`label: for (...)` was mishandled three ways:

  - collect_vars_recursive (hoisting) skipped those bodies, so loop-body
    `let`s were never boxed and were lost across the await;
  - body_contains_yield missed the buried yield, so an enclosing
    construct would not be split; and
  - linearize_body had no arm for them, so the whole loop fell through to
    the catch-all and was emitted unsplit -- the embedded await never
    became a resume state.

When the lost slot held an object, the resumed continuation dereferenced
a garbage pointer (the SIGSEGV in #1824); with a number it silently
produced a wrong result.

Fixes:
  - collect_vars_recursive, body_contains_yield, scan_stmt_for_max_func:
    descend into DoWhile and Labeled bodies.
  - linearize_body: a DoWhile-with-yield is desugared to a flagged
    `while (__first || c) { __first = false; body }` (preserving
    do-while continue/first-iteration semantics) so the existing While
    arm splits it; a Labeled-with-yield linearizes its wrapped loop after
    rewriting `break/continue label` that target it (from the loop's own
    body level) into plain break/continue. Labeled break/continue from a
    *nested* loop is left as-is -- the single-sentinel scheme can't yet
    distinguish targets, and it was already unsupported.

Regression test test_async_labeled_dowhile_loops.ts covers labeled-for,
labeled break/continue, do-while, and the #1824 object-accumulator shape,
all byte-compared against node --experimental-strip-types.

fix(runtime): construct instances from class-ref values held as first-class values (#321) (#2017)

A bare `class` identifier used as a value lowers to an INT32-tagged
class-ref (`INT32_TAG | class_id`). When such a value reached the dynamic
`new` helper (`js_new_function_construct`) via a LocalGet / PropertyGet

class passed as a cross-module function argument — it matched neither the
heap class-object arm (#1789) nor the pointer-shaped-closure path
(`synthetic_class_id_for_function` requires `is_pointer()`), so the
instance was stamped with class_id 0 and every inherited prototype method
threw `<m> is not a function`.

Detect the INT32 class-ref shape (top16 == 0x7FFE with a registered
class id) and allocate the instance with that class id, so method
dispatch walks the parent chain. Mirrors the #1789 heap-class-object arm:
the constructor body / field initializers are emitted on the static
`new ClassName()` codegen path (there is no constructor-by-class_id
runtime entry), so a dynamically-constructed instance starts with no own
props — fields written afterward and prototype methods work.

Surfaced while chasing the effect Layer/Scope blocker (#321), where a
`Context.Tag` subclass is threaded through generic combinators as a
first-class value.

fix(runtime): bind `this` to the receiver in js_get_iterator for yield*-over-a-Context-Tag (#321) (#2032)

method shared via the prototype chain whose body is
`new SingleShotGen(new YieldWrap(this))`. Perry codegen bakes `this` for
object-literal methods to the defining literal (CAPTURES_THIS_FLAG), so when
`js_get_iterator` invoked the inherited method via `js_closure_call0` (no
receiver), `this` stayed the prototype object instead of the Tag. The YieldWrap
then wrapped the prototype, `yieldWrapGet` returned a non-Effect (`_op`
undefined), the fiber never resolved it nor resumed the generator — empty.

`this` to the original iterable via `clone_closure_rebind_this` before calling,
matching the spec (`iterable[Symbol.iterator]()` runs with `this === iterable`).

Map/Set/string iteration are untouched).

(`js_native_call_method`) had no handling arm for arrays, so it fell
through the object-field scan and returned `undefined`. And `Array.from`
(via `js_array_clone`) on a `GC_TYPE_OBJECT` source always took the
array-like `.length`/`obj[i]` path instead of the iterator protocol.

fix(node:http): keep a listening server alive — chained createServer().listen() + variadic listen() overloads (#2041) (#2054)

Two bugs kept a `node:http` server from serving as a long-lived native
binary, even though it linked cleanly (#1652): the process printed nothing,
never bound the port, and exited in <1s.

1. Chained-factory receiver. `createServer(handler).listen(...)` never
   dispatched to the native listen fn. The native-instance method-call
   lowering only inferred the HttpServer class for an *Ident* receiver
   (`const s = createServer(...); s.listen(...)`), not for the inline
   factory-call receiver. With listen() never called, the event loop's
   active-handle pump was never registered (ensure_pump_registered runs from
   inside listen's spawn_blocking_with_reactor), so main() returned and the
   process exited — the "isn't counted as an active handle" symptom in the
   issue. Fix: infer the native (module, class) of an inline createServer() /
   createSecureServer() receiver in try_static_method_and_instance (covers
   http / https / http2).

2. Variadic listen() overloads. The native sig was fixed at [NA_F64, NA_PTR],
   so listen(port, host, cb) mis-routed the host string into the callback slot
   and dropped the real callback. Positional arg kinds can't express Node's
   floating-callback overloads, so listen now passes every user arg as a JS
   array (NA_VARARGS) and the runtime resolves the overload by value type —
   a standalone string is the host, the single function is the callback,
   wherever it lands — via a new js_value_is_closure C-ABI predicate. Applied
   to http, https, and http2 listen.

Adds tests/release/packages/node-http-serve: the first node:http fixture that
compiles + runs + curls a live socket (the existing test_node_http_*.ts are
compile/link-only), plus parse_listen_args unit tests for the host-override
and non-closure-pointer paths.

fix(runtime): Object.getPrototypeOf returns null for closure receivers, not self (#489) (#2050)

drizzle's is(value, type) walks a prototype chain via
`cls = Object.getPrototypeOf(value).constructor` then loops
`cls = Object.getPrototypeOf(cls)` until null. For an array chunk
(passed through is() during INSERT building) cls becomes the global
Array constructor; js_object_get_prototype_of returned the receiver
itself for any function/heap value, so getPrototypeOf(Array) === Array
— an infinite self-cycle that hung db.insert(...).run() forever.

Return null when the heap receiver is a GC_TYPE_CLOSURE: JS terminates
such a walk at null (Function.prototype -> Object.prototype -> null),
which Perry doesn't model, so null directly breaks the cycle. The two
internal callers (Reflect metadata chain walks) already stop on
next == null or next == current, so closure->null is equivalent to the
old closure->self for them.

Adds test-files/test_issue_489_array_proto_walk.ts.

fix(transform): lift multiple yields in one expression to ordered temps (#321 Effect.gen) (#2084)

Generator linearizer only handled a yield at statement, simple-binding, and
return positions. A yield buried in a larger expression (`return (yield 1) +
(yield 2)`, call args, array literals, short-circuit, ternary) fell into the
catch-all and was lowered by the codegen 'generators not implemented' arm
(returns 0.0), dropping the resumed value and never suspending.

Add a pre-pass (hoist_yields.rs) that hoists every non-top-level yield/yield*
into ordered `let __ygen_N = yield E;` temps before linearization, so the
existing let-init arms split each into suspend/resume states. Evaluation order
preserved; &&/||/?? and ternary lifted into temp + if so a yield on a not-taken
path only runs when taken. Mirrors the established async hoist_awaits pass.

fix(hir,codegen): array-typed class fields named stack/name + param-prop field types — effect SortedSet/RedBlackTree iteration (#321) (#2095)

values) and lost the last node (wrong count). Two distinct, bounded bugs in
how class instance array fields are typed:

   `<x>.message` / `<x>.stack` / `<x>.name` as a string (for caught-Error
   `.stack.includes(...)` chains). It hijacked effect's
   `RedBlackTreeIterator.stack: Array<Node<K,V>>` — `this.stack[i]` lowered to
   string `js_string_char_at` and returned garbage. Now when the receiver is a
   known class/interface that declares a field with that name, the field's
   declared type wins over the Error heuristic (new `declared_field_type`).

   `class_field_types` registry that `infer_type_from_expr` consults for
   `this.<field>`. So `const stack = this.stack` inside `moveNext()` inferred
   `Any`, and `stack[stack.length - 1]` element reads returned garbage nodes —
   the in-order walk lost its last node. Now param-prop field types are
   registered into the early registry alongside `ClassProp` fields.

→ `[1,2,3]` (was `[null,null]`), `fr_sortedset` → `[1,1,2,3]`. No regression

fix(runtime): honor custom toString() in object→string coercion (#321) (#2102)

Object→string coercion (String(obj), template literals, obj + "") only
consulted [Symbol.toPrimitive] and then fell straight back to the default
Object.prototype.toString ("[object Object]"), so a user-defined toString
(own OR inherited) was ignored. Surfaced via effect's Redacted, where
String(secret) must produce "<redacted>".

Root cause: js_jsvalue_to_string implements ToPrimitive(obj, "string") but
skipped the OrdinaryToPrimitive fallback that calls the object's toString
(then valueOf). After the Symbol.toPrimitive miss and the array/buffer/JSX
special cases, it returned the default "[object Object]".

Fix: add ordinary_to_primitive_string in to_string.rs, invoked right before
the "[object Object]" fallback in js_jsvalue_to_string (the single chokepoint
all three coercion forms route through — String() via js_string_coerce,
template/+ via js_string_concat_value/js_value_concat_string). It resolves
toString (own + prototype chain) via js_object_get_field_by_name, rebinds the
closure's this slot to the receiver with clone_closure_rebind_this (so an
inherited Object.create(proto) method reads the right this — mirrors
#1969/#1982), and calls it with this=obj. A primitive result is re-coerced
(strings pass through, numbers via js_number_to_string).

Spec correctness for hint "string": every ordinary object inherits a callable
Object.prototype.toString, so valueOf is reached ONLY when a custom toString
returns a non-primitive. Perry has no discoverable Object.prototype.toString
field, so a toString lookup miss STANDS IN FOR that default and falls back to
"[object Object]" — it does NOT proceed to valueOf. This keeps
String({ valueOf() {…} }) === "[object Object]", matching Node.

A thread-local depth guard caps recursion (a toString that string-coerces
this) so the process degrades to "[object Object]" instead of overflowing the
Rust stack / SIGSEGV.

Verified byte-identical to node --experimental-strip-types: own/inherited/
class-instance custom toString, Symbol.toPrimitive priority, this-reading
toString, toString→number, toString→non-primitive→valueOf fallback,
valueOf-only-string-hint=[object Object], and the regression set (plain {},
arrays, primitives). effect/Redacted String(r) → "<redacted>". New gap test
test_gap_string_coercion_tostring.ts. perry-runtime lib tests: 700 passed.

fix(hir): substitute <T extends Primitive> constraint into param type at lowering (#321) (#2122)

Indexing into a generic-typed `<T extends string>` parameter
produced a value that lost its string tag at the function-call
boundary — surfaced via effect's `Str.capitalize` /
`Capitalize<T>` utilities (`Str.capitalize("foo")` returned
`1.5E-323oo` instead of `Foo`).

Root cause: perry's codegen IndexGet fast path keys off the
receiver's static type. Two paths through HIR lowering dropped
the constraint:

1. `lower_arrow` never entered a type-parameter scope (only
   `lower_fn_decl` did), so the `T` in `(self: T)` resolved to
   `Type::Named("T")` — neither `is_string_expr` nor any other
   primitive predicate matched.

2. `lower_fn_decl` entered the scope but `extract_ts_type_with_ctx`
   just returned `Type::TypeVar("T")`, which also fell out of every
   primitive predicate. Generic-call monomorphization rescued
   direct `FuncRef` call sites, but indirect calls through a
   function-typed local (and arrows, which are never
   monomorphized) lowered the un-substituted body — so IndexGet
   dispatched to `js_object_get_index_polymorphic`, which read a
   `StringHeader*` as `ArrayHeader*` and returned the header's
   leading bytes as a subnormal f64.

Fix: at the `TsTypeRef(T)` site in `extract_ts_type_with_ctx`,
when `T` is an in-scope type parameter with a runtime-narrowing
upper bound (`<T extends string|number|boolean|bigint|U[]>`),
return the constraint type instead of `TypeVar(T)`. The narrow
list keeps existing native-instance-tagging / class-id-propagation
paths intact for `T extends SomeClass` / literal / intersection
constraints — those still produce `TypeVar(T)` so monomorphization
or downstream tagging can substitute a concrete type as before.

Also opens a type-parameter scope inside `lower_arrow` so the
`is_type_param(\"T\")` check fires for arrows the same way it
already does for function declarations, classes, and type aliases.

fix(typedarray): gate index fast path to numeric keys so method access stops returning a number (#2063) (#2068)

`ta[key]` on a TypedArray (Int8Array/.../Float64Array) unconditionally took
the integer-indexed element fast path, which `fptosi`s the key. A NaN-boxed
string coerces to 0, so a method-name key (`ta["copyWithin"]`, or `ta[m]`
iterating method names) read element 0 — `typeof ta[m]` was "number" — and a
numeric string like `ta["2"]` read element 0 instead of element 2.

Gate the element fast path on `is_numeric_expr`: only provably-numeric keys
(literals, loop counters, numeric expressions) take it. Any non-numeric /
unknown-typed key now routes through a new runtime dispatcher
`js_typed_array_index_get_dynamic`, which implements the ECMAScript
IntegerIndexedExotic [[Get]] dispatch:

  * canonical numeric index string -> integer-indexed element read
    (bounds-checked; out-of-range -> undefined),
  * any other string -> ordinary [[Get]] via the same
    `js_object_get_field_by_name_f64` the dotted `ta.copyWithin` PropertyGet
    path uses (resolves the reified method once #2059 lands; undefined until
    then — never a stray element value),
  * a numeric (non-string) key -> integer-indexed element read.

Method-name access no longer returns a number, and numeric-string element
reads (`ta["2"]`, `ta[k]`, OOB `ta["9"]`) are now correct. Full
`typeof ta.copyWithin === "function"` additionally needs built-in prototype
method reification, tracked separately in #2059.

fix(hir,codegen,runtime): run instance-field initializers when constructing from a class-expression value (#1787) (#2074)

`new <classObjectValue>()` — constructing an instance from a class
EXPRESSION held as a value (`const A = mk(...); new A()`) — allocated a
bare instance with no own properties: every instance-field initializer
read back `undefined`, including literal fields (`_tag = "LIT"`) and
fields that capture the factory scope (`cap = tag`). The constructor can't
be inlined at the `new` site the way a static `new ClassName()` is: the
callee is a runtime value, and the class's captured environment lived
where the class expression was evaluated (e.g. inside the `mk(tag)`
factory), not at the (possibly far-away) construction site.

Fix: snapshot the per-evaluation captures onto the heap class object and
replay the class's standalone constructor on the new instance.

- HIR: `Expr::ClassExprFresh` gains `captured_args` — the outer values the
  class closes over, in `synthesize_class_captures`' capture-param order,
  read at the evaluation site where they are still live.
- Codegen: the `ClassExprFresh` lowering stores those captures onto the
  class object as the `__perry_ctor_caps` own array; module init registers
  each class's standalone `<prefix>__<class>_constructor` symbol into a new
  `CLASS_CONSTRUCTORS` table.
- Runtime: the heap-class-object arm of `js_new_function_construct` looks
  the constructor up, fills the user parameters from the `new`-call args
  and the trailing capture parameters from `__perry_ctor_caps`, and invokes
  it via `call_vtable_method` — running the instance-field initializers and
  constructor body exactly as the static `new ClassName()` path does inline.

Only the heap-class-object (`OBJECT_TYPE_CLASS`) `new` path consults the
table, so the INT32 class-ref `new` path (top-level class declarations) is
unchanged. New gap test `test_gap_class_expr_instance_fields.ts` is
byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types` (literal + captured +
computed instance fields, a method reading a captured field through `this`,
user-ctor-arg + capture ordering, and a no-capture literal field).

Scope: per-evaluation class objects still share the compile-time template's
class_id, so cross-evaluation `.constructor` / `instanceof` discrimination
remains the deeper shared-class_id limitation (see the scope note in
test_gap_class_expr_new_instanceof.ts); it is not addressed here.

fix: built-in prototype methods resolve as property values (#2058) (#2077)

Built-in prototype methods (`isPrototypeOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `toString`,
`Function.prototype.{call,apply,bind}`, …) returned `undefined` when read as
property *values* — via the prototype object (`Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf`)
or off a primitive receiver (`n.isPrototypeOf` where `n` is a number). The
primitive-receiver case additionally SIGSEGV'd: a raw, unboxed `number` (Perry
stores `5` as the bare f64 `5.0`, not a NaN-box) fell through every pointer
guard in `js_object_get_field_by_name` and got dereferenced as an
`ObjectHeader`. Direct method calls worked; member-access-as-value did not.

Three parts:

- HIR `typeof` fold (`lower_expr.rs`): extend the #1777 `<Ctor>.prototype.<m>`
  fold to `Object`/`Function` ctors and to the universal `Object.prototype`
  methods inherited by every prototype (new `is_known_object_prototype_method`
  helper). Fixes `typeof Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf`,
  `typeof Number.prototype.hasOwnProperty`, `typeof Function.prototype.call`,
  etc.

- Runtime number-receiver guard (`field_get_set.rs`): before the generic
  pointer logic, detect a raw finite-f64 number receiver (top16 != 0, not a
  NaN-box tag, not a masked pointer, not a registered Date) and return a
  bound-method closure (`js_class_method_bind`) for the inherited
  `Object.prototype` methods, else `undefined` — never dereference. Fixes the
  SIGSEGV and makes `typeof n.toString === "function"` hold with a callable
  value.

- Dispatch arms (`native_call_method.rs`): add `isPrototypeOf` (false for
  primitive receivers), primitive `valueOf` (returns the value) and
  `toLocaleString` (delegates to `toString`) so the bound values are callable.

fix(gc): scope inline-arena resync to the Eden arena (#1824) (#2134)

`Arena::alloc`'s block-reuse forward-scan calls `resync_inline_to_current`,
which mirrors the thread-global `INLINE_STATE` used by the codegen inline
bump-allocator. `INLINE_STATE` is only meaningful for the general nursery-Eden
arena, but the same `Arena::alloc` body backs the old-gen, survivor, and
longlived arenas. When a large-object `await` allocation (e.g. a big JSON
`response.json()` payload, which is born in the old-gen) forward-scanned to
reuse an earlier old-gen block, it repointed `INLINE_STATE` at that old-gen
block. The next general-Eden `arena_alloc` then wrote the foreign block's
offset into the live Eden block, rewinding the bump pointer so a fresh string
allocation landed on top of a still-live, suspended async-step closure. When
that closure was later resumed by the microtask runner, its overwritten
function pointer (now string bytes) was jumped to → SIGSEGV.

This matches the #1824 report exactly: a garbage "function pointer" in
`js_promise_run_microtasks` / the resumed await continuation, reproducible with
no GC cycle (`full_gc=0`/`minor_gc=0`) and surviving every GC escape hatch
(`PERRY_GEN_GC=0`, `PERRY_GEN_GC_EVACUATE=0`, `PERRY_WRITE_BARRIERS=0`) — it is
an allocator-state corruption, not a collection/rooting bug.

Fix: `resync_inline_to_current` no-ops unless `self.space == NurseryEden`.
The Eden forward-scan path is unchanged; only the non-Eden arenas stop
clobbering `INLINE_STATE`.

Regression test reproduces the old-gen forward-scan reuse and asserts the
Eden `INLINE_STATE` is left intact (fails before the fix, passes after).

fix(runtime): guard generic field-get against primitive-number receivers (#2128) (#2141)

drizzle-orm's UPDATE / DELETE / leftJoin on sqlite SIGSEGV'd (rc=139) because
buildQueryFromSourceParams mapped over SQL chunks that included bound-param
numbers (a row id, an age) and routed property access through the generic
js_object_get_field_by_name slow path. That helper had guards for V8 handles
(0x7FFB) and INT32 class refs (0x7FFE) but not for a plain JS number value —
a finite double like 1.0 has bits 0x3FF0000000000000 (top16 0x3FF0, not in
any tag band), slipped through unguarded, and got bit-cast to a pointer.

(*obj).field_count, etc.) dereferenced unmapped memory and SIGSEGV'd.

the value is a primitive number (or canonical NaN) and the property-getter
slow path returns undefined per JS spec for unknown keys. The top16 == 0
raw-I64-pointer convention (module-level objects) is preserved, and all
NaN-tagged values continue past the guard untouched.

fix(hir): bind legacy `arguments` inside object-literal shorthand methods (#321) (#2162)

`lower_method_prop` (object-literal shorthand methods) never synthesized
the trailing `...arguments` rest param that the rest of the HIR pipeline
relies on. `class_members.rs`, `fn_decl.rs`, and `expr_function.rs` all
do this — `expr_object.rs` was the missing site.

This is the exact shape effect's Pipeable trait uses on
`TypeMatcherProto` / `ValueMatcherProto` (and every other Pipeable —
Effect, Match, Either, Option, Cause, Exit, Logger, Console, …):

  const TypeMatcherProto = {
    pipe() { return pipeArguments(this, arguments) }
  }

Without synthesis, `arguments` inside the method body resolved to nothing,
`pipeArguments(this, arguments)` saw zero operands, and `.pipe(...)`
silently returned `this` — dropping every operand. Match.type<>().pipe(
Match.when(...)) produced a matcher with no cases.

Fix mirrors the synthesis already in place at the other call sites:
pre-scan the user-written method body with `body_uses_arguments`, and
if it references `arguments` (and the user hasn't already bound the
name), append a synthetic `...arguments` rest param via
`append_synthetic_arguments_param` BEFORE the body is lowered so the
identifier resolves to the new `LocalId`.

New gap test `test_gap_arguments_in_object_literal_method.ts` covers
four shapes: capture-free body, `this`-using body (the Pipeable shape),
named-params + arguments, and variadic-pipe over arguments. All
byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

fix(hir): typeof + .bind/.call/.apply on namespace statics (#2143) (#2171)

Built-in function values like `Promise.resolve`, `Math.min`, `JSON.parse`
do not inherit `Function.prototype` in Perry's representation — each
direct call is special-cased in codegen, so a bare value-read lowers to
a numeric fallback (`typeof "number"`) and a chained `.bind` / `.call` /
`.apply` either reads as "undefined" or as a number, then throws
"value is not a function" at the outer call.

Two AST-level folds in perry-hir cover the high-frequency shapes:

1. `typeof` fold (`lower_expr.rs`) — `typeof <NS>.<static>` and
   `typeof <NS>.<static>.<bind|call|apply>` evaluate to `"function"`
   when `<NS>` is one of Promise/Math/JSON/Number/String/Object/Array
   (not shadowed by a local) and `<static>` is a known method on it.

2. Call-shape rewrite (`expr_call/intrinsics.rs`,
   `try_namespace_static_method_apply_call_bind`) — drops the
   irrelevant `thisArg` and forwards the args to the direct call:

     `<NS>.<static>.call(t, a, b)`       → `<NS>.<static>(a, b)`
     `<NS>.<static>.apply(t, [a, b])`    → `<NS>.<static>(a, b)`
     `(<NS>.<static>.bind(t, …pre))(…r)` → `<NS>.<static>(…pre, …r)`

The deferred-bind shape (`const f = Promise.resolve.bind(Promise);
f(x);`) still needs a real reified function value and is left as
follow-up — call it out in a separate issue when that becomes the
bottleneck.

Pinned by `test-files/test_gap_2143_builtin_bind.ts` (byte-for-byte
vs `node --experimental-strip-types`).

fix(runtime): extend fs::validate to fsync/fdatasync/fchown/lchown/lchmod/copyFile/write/writev (#2013) (#2181)

Extends the #2035 validator surface to the rest-of-fs slice the #2013
update flagged as still falling through. Same Node-compatible error
shape (TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE] / RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]
with the per-error side table from #2035 carrying `.code`).

New validators in `fs::validate`:

- `validate_fd(value)` — Node-compatible int32 fd check (`>= 0 && <= 2^31-1`).
- `validate_int32(value, name, min, max)` — reused for uid / gid / mode.
- `validate_function(name, value)` — TypeError if the value isn't a Perry
  closure, via `extract_closure_ptr`.

Wired in:

- `fsyncSync` / `fdatasyncSync` / `writeSync*` / `writevSync` — fd.
  `writevSync` skips fd validation when the buffers array is empty
  (matches Node: empty writev returns 0 without touching the fd).
- `fchownSync` — fd, uid, gid.
- `lchownSync` — path, uid, gid.
- `lchmodSync` — path only (mode range deferred; Node opens the path
  first so `ENOENT` wins on non-existent paths).
- `copyFileSync` / async — src, dest, mode (range-checked when supplied).
- `exists` callback — `cb` must be a function (path bad-type is silent in Node).
- `lchown` / `lchmod` async — same as their sync siblings + callback.

To keep the `FileHandle` path safe (it may hold a `-1` fd sentinel from
a failed open), extract `fsync_sync_inner` / `fdatasync_sync_inner` /
`fchown_sync_inner` / `write_string_sync_inner` /
`write_buffer_sync_inner` / `writev_sync_inner` helpers without
validation and route `filehandle_*_impl` through those. The C-ABI
`js_fs_*_sync` entry points still validate as before.

Verification:

- New `test-parity/node-suite/fs/sync/arg-validation.ts` is byte-identical
  to `node --experimental-strip-types` across 27 cases covering fd
  type+range, path-type, uid/gid type+range, copyFile src/dest/mode,
  write/writev fd, and the writev empty-array no-throw contract.
- Direct re-run of `node-suite/fs/fd/{fdatasync, fstat-ftruncate-fsync,
  readv-writev, read-write-optional}.ts`, `callbacks/{chown,
  copyfile-excl, lchmod}.ts`, and `sync/captured-methods.ts` all
  byte-identical with Node — no regressions in the affected paths.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

Follow-ups still in #2013: `lchmodSync` mode + `lchownSync` range on
existing paths (paired with `ENOENT` propagation), required-callback
validation on `fsync`/`fdatasync`/`fchown` async wrappers, and the
non-fs APIs (buffer, net, http, zlib, crypto, process, url, timers).

fix(hir): built-in function `.name` own-property (#2144) (#2185)

A built-in function's `name` own-property read back `undefined`, and
`Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Promise.race, "name")` returned undefined
too. Built-in constructors (`TypeError`, `Promise`, `Array`, …) and the
static functions on built-in namespaces / constructors (`Math.min`,
`Promise.race`, `Array.isArray`, …) are not represented as named closure
values in Perry — bare reads of them produce the `globalThis` lookup's
`0` / undefined sentinel, so `.name` on the result follows suit.
Follow-up to #2075 (#2059), which only covered user-defined function
declarations and expressions.

`assert.throws` reports `expectedErrorConstructor.name` to label thrown
errors (so every built-in `Error` constructor showed as `undefined`
instead of `TypeError`/`RangeError`/etc.) and Test262's
`built-ins/Function` sample is dominated by `Cannot read … (reading
'name')` once the sibling "built-in proto methods are undefined" gap
lands.

- `analysis::is_builtin_static_function_member`: spec-defined static
  function members of built-in namespaces / constructors. Function-typed
  members only — numeric constants like `Math.PI` stay unfolded so
  `(Math.PI).name` keeps producing `undefined` (matching Node).
- `lower/expr_member`: `<BuiltinCtor>.name` and
  `<BuiltinNs>.<staticFn>.name` fold to `Expr::String`. Gated on the
  *lowered* receiver matching `GlobalGet(0)` / `PropertyGet {
  GlobalGet(0), … }`, so a locally-shadowed `const Math = …` lowers to
  a `LocalGet` and bypasses the fold.
- `lower/expr_call/native_module` (`Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`
  arm): `…(<BuiltinFn>, "name")` folds to the spec-compliant data
  descriptor object literal `{ value, writable:false, enumerable:false,
  configurable:true }`. Same lowered-receiver gate as the `.name` fold.
- `lower/expr_call/name_fold` (new): AST recognizer + descriptor builder
  shared by both fold sites.

Parity test test-parity/node-suite/object/builtin-function-name.ts is
byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`. The existing #2075
`function-name-descriptor.ts` parity test still passes. perry-hir lib
tests: 111/111.

Surfaced by the #799 Test262 radar re-harvest (built-ins/Function
~16% — 38× `Cannot read … (reading 'name')`). Part of #793.

fix(node:https,http2): accept Buffer-typed key/cert PEMs (#2132) (#2184)

`https.createServer({ key, cert })` and `http2.createSecureServer`
parsed their options object via `JSON.stringify` → `serde_json` →
`.as_str()`. Node-idiomatic callers pass PEMs as Buffers
(`fs.readFileSync('key.pem')` with no encoding), which round-trip
through that path as `{"type":"Buffer","data":[...]}` — losing the
`.as_str()` extraction and falling through to the
`"no recognized PEM private key"` branch with an empty PEM buffer.

Add a shared `json_value_to_pem_bytes` helper that recognizes the
Node Buffer shape and a bare numeric array, so both helpers accept
either string- or Buffer-typed PEMs. Threads byte buffers (not
`String`) end-to-end since PEM is opaque to the TLS parsers.

This was the diff-bucket cluster surfaced by the node-core radar
for the three https tests cited in #2132 (agent-abort-controller,
agent-keylog, byteswritten); after the fix, agent-abort-controller
flips to pass, the other two move past the PEM error to surface
unrelated downstream gaps (cert version, console output).

Includes unit tests covering string PEM, Buffer-shape JSON, bare
numeric array, and the empty/unknown fallbacks.

fix(codegen): dynamic method-dispatch tower must forward un-bundled args (#321 regression from #2162) (#2199)

PR #2162 added synthesis of `...arguments` for object-literal shorthand
methods that read the legacy `arguments` identifier — necessary for
effect's Pipeable trait, which writes `pipe() { return pipeArguments(this,
arguments) }` on every Pipeable instance. The synthesis itself is
correct, but it exposed a latent codegen bug in the dynamic method-call
dispatch tower (`property_get.rs`'s `try_lower_property_get_method_call`,
the override + default branches): they were filling the
`js_native_call_value` / `js_native_call_method` args buffer from the
POST-rest-bundling `lowered_args` vector.

When a dispatched method has a rest-bundled signature (e.g. effect's
`pipe()` once it gained the synthesized `...arguments` rest), the
upstream bundling step at lines 1318–1338 had already TRUNCATED
`lowered_args` to `[recv, rest_array]`. The override + default branches
then alloca'd `[args.len() x double]`, stored only the rest_array into
slot 0, and told the runtime to read `args.len()` doubles — slots
1..N-1 were uninitialized garbage that landed in pipeArguments's
`arguments[i]`, tripping `value is not a function` at module-init time
on a barrel `import { Effect } from "effect"` (effect's
SchemaAST.ts:3013 `getTitleAnnotation(ast).pipe(orElse, orElse, map)`
chain reached the default branch with uninit slots and crashed).

Pre-#2162, this latent bug was invisible because effect's pipe() saw an
UNBOUND `arguments` identifier, `pipeArguments(this, arguments)` saw
nothing, and `.pipe(...)` silently returned `this` — operands were
dropped without crashing.

Fix: in both the override branch (`js_native_call_value` path) and the
default branch (`js_native_call_method` path), source the args buffer
from `static_user_args` (a Vec<String> captured at line 1263 BEFORE the
rest-bundling / issue-#235 padding mutated `lowered_args`). The
override target and the runtime method dispatcher both run their own
rest-bundling at call time, so they must receive un-bundled user args.
Mirrors the call-time contract the case branches already use via
`arg_slices` (which is fine because each case calls a STATIC method
whose signature matches the post-bundling shape).

Verification:
- `/private/tmp/effect-dod/survey/fr_barrel_init.ts` (the regression
  repro): prints "hello" cleanly in both PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 and
  default modes.
- `survey/fr_match.ts` (the positive case Match.type/.pipe chain):
  byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`.
- Existing #2162 gap test
  `test_gap_arguments_in_object_literal_method.ts`: still byte-identical.
- New gap test `test_gap_arguments_dispatch_tower_default.ts` covers
  the specific shape (a Pipeable user class declares pipe()+arguments,
  forcing rest-bundling; an unrelated object literal's pipe(c1,c2,c3) call
  falls through to the dispatch tower's default branch with 3 stores into
  the 3-double buffer).
- Gap suite: 90 PASS / 2 FAIL — pre-existing test_gap_class_advanced and
  test_gap_json_map_set are the only failures; no regressions.
- `cargo test --release -p perry-hir --lib` and `-p perry-codegen --lib`
  both clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

fix(node:http): register http.createServer(...) result as HttpServer in nested-scope decls + wire Server.address() (#2153) (#2186)

The member-callee var_decl arm in `destructuring/var_decl.rs:401` had
match rows for `mysql.createPool`, `pg.connect`, etc. but missed
`http.createServer` / `https.createServer` / `http2.createSecureServer`.
So `const server = http.createServer(...)` *inside a function body*
(the CJS wrapper closure counts: a raw `.js` user file is wrapped in
`(function(){ ... })()` before lowering) didn't register `server` as
an `("http", "HttpServer")` native instance.

Without that tag, `server.listen(...)` / `.on(...)` / `.close()` /
`.address()` fell through to the generic typed-feedback dispatch via
`js_typed_feedback_native_call_method` → `js_native_call_method`,
which has no HttpServer arm and returned NaN (typeof "number"). The
result chain was broken:

  typeof server.listen(0)  // "number" instead of "object"
  result === server        // false instead of true
  listen callback          // never fired (NaN.call no-op)

After the fix:

  typeof server.listen(0)  // "object"
  result === server        // true
  listen callback          // fires; server.address() returns
                            //   {address, family, port}
  server.close()           // dispatches correctly

Also adds the missing `address` dispatch row for HttpServer /
HttpsServer / Http2SecureServer — the runtime fns
`js_node_http_*_server_address_json` exist and serialize the bind
state as JSON, but no NativeModSig entry routed user calls to them,
so `server.address()` was hitting the same typed-feedback NaN path.

Includes matching manifest entries (drift test catches the gap) +
regenerated `docs/api/perry.d.ts` and `docs/src/api/reference.md`.

Touches:
  crates/perry-hir/src/destructuring/var_decl.rs
  crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native_table/http.rs
  crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs
  docs/api/perry.d.ts (regenerated)
  docs/src/api/reference.md (regenerated)

Test plan:

      `NativeMethodCall { module: "http", class_name:
      Some("HttpServer"), method: "listen" }` (was a plain Call)
- [x] End-to-end test: `createServer + listen(port, cb) +

- [x] `cargo test --release -p perry-codegen --test

fix(codegen): class extending runtime-value function dispatches super() through the closure (#321 / #1787 follow-up) (#2219)

When a class extends a runtime-value FUNCTION/closure (e.g. an IIFE-returned
constructor function — Effect's `Data.Class` shape, issue #66 / #321), the
`super(args)` call site reaches the parent_class=None arm of the SuperCall
lowering: the parent isn't in `ctx.classes`, isn't a stream subclass,
isn't an Error-like built-in, and pre-fix fell through to the no-op
"return undefined" terminal. Result: the parent function body never ran,
`this` stayed null inside the subclass constructor, and instance fields
never appeared on the new object.

HIR already captures `class.extends_expr` for the unknown-Ident shape
(#711, lower_decl/class_decl.rs) and module init already wires the
class_id parent edge via `js_register_class_parent_dynamic` (#1787
foundation). The missing piece was the super-call dispatch itself.

This adds a new arm to `expr/this_super_call.rs` that, before the
existing stream / Error-like / no-op fallthrough, evaluates the
`extends_expr`, binds IMPLICIT_THIS to the current `this`, dispatches
through `js_native_call_value` (the same helper #519 / #2074 use to
call closures with a bound receiver), then restores IMPLICIT_THIS. Field
initializers run after via `apply_field_initializers_recursive` to
match JS spec (subclass fields execute after super() returns).

The new arm is gated on `parent_name` not being a well-known built-in
(Error/TypeError/.../ReadableStream/...). HIR captures `extends_expr`
for those too (unknown Ident → fallback), but they have specialized
arms below that set this.message/this.name or allocate stream handles
— the gate keeps that path preferred.

Verified: `/tmp/repro.ts` (the spec's minimal IIFE-returned parent
function) now matches node byte-for-byte (s.x: 7, parent body runs,
this not null). Effect's `survey/fr_data_class.ts` flips `eq: true`
(instance fields populate via Object.assign(this, args)); the remaining
`Equal.equals: false` is a separate symbol-keyed-prototype-method
dispatch gap, not part of this fix. Gap suite: 37 PASS / 2 FAIL (the
two pre-existing failures, test_gap_class_advanced + the timing-
sensitive test_gap_console_methods, unchanged). Existing #1787/#2074
gap tests + class gap tests still pass; cargo test perry-codegen
+ perry-hir clean; cargo fmt clean.

Refs #321 / #66 / #1787 / #2074.

fix(runtime): wire %TypedArray% intrinsic chain (#2145) (#2196)

Per spec, %TypedArray% is the abstract parent constructor for Int8Array,
Uint8Array, ..., so Int8Array.__proto__ === %TypedArray% and
Object.getPrototypeOf(Int8Array.prototype) === %TypedArray%.prototype.
Perry didn't install that intrinsic, so the test262 TypedArray re-harvest's
prototype walks read null.prototype and typeof Int8Array.__proto__ came
back "number" (codegen's 0.0 placeholder for the lost-receiver path).

- Allocate %TypedArray% (a closure) + %TypedArray%.prototype (object) once
  per process from populate_global_this_builtins; cache pointers in two
  AtomicI64 GC roots so the chain survives copying GC.
- Link each per-kind constructor via closure_set_static_prototype, and
  stamp each per-kind .prototype with OBJ_FLAG_TYPED_ARRAY_PROTO so
  js_object_get_prototype_of resolves it to the shared intrinsic proto.
- Move the #2060 length/byteLength/byteOffset/buffer accessor descriptors
  off each per-kind proto onto the shared intrinsic proto — they're own
  properties of %TypedArray%.prototype per spec and reached via the new
  getPrototypeOf chain.
- Handle .__proto__ reads on closures (field_get_set) by returning the
  recorded static prototype, and have js_object_get_prototype_of return
  the recorded static proto for closures instead of always returning null
  — drizzle's getPrototypeOf-walk still terminates because %TypedArray%
  itself has no further parent recorded.
- HIR: preserve the receiver for <TypedArrayCtor>.__proto__ so codegen
  routes through the real Int8Array closure instead of falling to the
  no-receiver 0.0 sentinel (the "typeof number" symptom).

fix(node:http,https): Server() callable alias + sync bind for address().port (#2132) (#2197)

* fix(node:http,https): Server() callable alias + sync bind for address().port (#2132)

Two related fixes for the runtime-fail cluster in #2132:

1. **`http.Server(handler)` / `https.Server(opts, handler)` as
   callable constructors.** Node treats `Server` and `createServer`
   as interchangeable — the same C++ constructor backs both, with or
   without `new`. Many Node test fixtures (`test-http-abort-client`,
   `test-https-agent`, `test-https-agent-servername`,
   `test-https-agent-additional-options`) use the `Server(...)` form
   directly. Without a dispatch row, Perry returned undefined and
   the next `.listen(...)` crashed with `Cannot read properties of
   undefined (reading 'listen')`. Add `Server` rows to the codegen
   native table aliased to `js_node_http_create_server` /
   `js_node_https_create_server`.

2. **`server.address().port` returned the *requested* port.** The
   listen() FFI wrote `bound_port = port` (e.g. 0) and then spawned
   an async task to actually `TcpListener::bind(...).await`. The
   `listen(port, cb)` callback fired *before* the async bind
   resolved, so `server.address().port` inside the callback was the
   pre-OS-assignment port — `0` for `listen(0, cb)`. Downstream
   `http.get({ port: 0, ... })` connections then couldn't reach the
   server. Bind synchronously with `std::net::TcpListener::bind`,
   read `local_addr().port()`, write the *actual* port into
   `bound_port`, then hand the listener to
   `tokio::net::TcpListener::from_std` for the async accept loop.

Same fix mirrored across `http`, `https`, and `http2` server FFIs.
The synchronous bind also matches Node's observable timing: the
`listen()` callback runs after the socket is actually bound.

After this PR, 3 of the 4 "Cannot read 'listen'" runtime-fail tests
flip to pass (test-https-agent, test-https-agent-servername,
test-https-agent-additional-options); the fourth (test-http-abort-client)
moves past the listen crash to surface a distinct downstream gap
(serverRes.on undefined) — separate follow-up.

* fix(api-manifest): register http.Server / https.Server callable entries

CI's `every_dispatch_entry_has_manifest_counterpart` drift test on
PR #2197 caught that the new `Server` rows added to
`NATIVE_MODULE_TABLE` had no corresponding entries in
`API_MANIFEST` — drift here would make the #463 unimplemented-API
gate error on a real implementation. Add `method("http", "Server")`
and `method("https", "Server")` next to the existing `createServer`
rows.

Regenerate `docs/api/perry.d.ts` and `docs/src/api/reference.md` for
the api-docs-drift gate. The diff is exactly the two new `export
function Server(...)` lines under the `http` and `https` modules.

fix(runtime): gate dyn_index_get/set raw-I64 fallback with is_valid_obj_ptr to avoid SIGBUS on denormal f64 receivers (#63 / #321) (#2230)

The js_dyn_index_get / js_dyn_index_set helpers fall back on a 'looks
like a raw I64 pointer' heuristic for module-level objects (which LLVM
ABI passes as DOUBLE). The heuristic only required: not-NaN, non-zero,
< 2^48, 4-byte aligned, >= 0x10000. effect's fiberRefs.ts loop produces
a value with bits ~= 0x8_0000_0000 (a denormal f64 ~ 1.7e-314) that
passes every gate. The unchecked '(*gc_hdr).obj_type' read at
[raw_ptr - 8] then crosses the macOS user/kernel boundary -> SIGBUS,
which exited with code 138 (silent crash) instead of a catchable
TypeError.

Gate the heuristic-derived raw_ptr with crate::object::is_valid_obj_ptr
(platform-aware heap range: macOS host [0x200_0000_0000, 0x8000_0000_0000),
Linux/iOS/Android [0x1000, 0x8000_0000_0000)) before any deref. Values
that arrived via POINTER_TAG are still trusted (codegen asked for a
pointer). Mirror the same gate in js_dyn_index_set so write-side
denormal-as-receiver writes are no-ops instead of corrupt stores.

fix(deforest): exhaustive walker so inline producer calls get bailed (#2047) (#2233)

* fix(deforest): use exhaustive perry-hir walker so inline producer calls in expression position get bailed (#2047)

The deforest pass had a local `walk_expr_children` with a `_ => {}`
catch-all that treated less-common `Expr` variants — including
`JsonStringifyFull` — as leaves. Producer calls hidden inside those
variants slipped past `scan_unsafe_call_sites`, so the candidate was
still rewritten to take a trailing accumulator parameter and `return
out` became `return undefined`. Inline expression-position callers
(`JSON.stringify(f())`, `someFn(f())`, etc.) never received the
rewritten signature and observed `undefined` instead of the array.

Delegate to `perry_hir::walker::walk_expr_children{,_mut}` (the
exhaustive walker other transform passes already use). This also
tightens the `OutUsageAnalyzer` / `SubstituteLocal` / funcref-misuse
scans that share the same walker — previously they could silently miss
`LocalGet(out)` references hidden inside the same variants.

Repro from the issue now matches Node byte-for-byte; added the gap
test to lock that in.

fix(runtime): guard alloc_error against non-pointer message arg (#321 / #2230 family) (#2235)

new Error(value) lowers by handing 'value' straight to
js_error_new_with_message even when 'value' is not a string pointer
(e.g. effect's Cause.ts ends up calling new Error(...) with a tag value
like 1 along certain pretty-printer paths). alloc_error then reads
(*message).byte_len at offset 4 → reads 0x5 → SIGSEGV (silent exit
139). This affects Effect.runSync + Effect.provide + Layer chains, but
the codegen-side hole is general (any new Error(value)/new TypeError
(value)/... on a non-string value).

Gate the message pointer in alloc_error with
crate::object::is_valid_obj_ptr (the same platform-aware heap predicate
#2230 added to dyn_index_get and that already guards js_object_keys
and the by-name field setters). Non-pointer values — small ints,
NaN-boxing tag bits, garbage from non-pointer dataflow — coerce to an
empty-string message instead of being dereferenced. Real string pointers
(the hot path) are untouched.

Because alloc_error is the central chokepoint for all error-allocation
entry points, this single change covers js_error_new_with_message,
js_error_new_with_name_message, js_error_new_with_cause,
js_typeerror_new, js_rangeerror_new, js_referenceerror_new,
js_syntaxerror_new, and js_aggregateerror_new symmetrically.

  exit: 139 (silent SIGSEGV in alloc_error)
After:
  Effect Layer chain produces a throwable error instead of crashing
  (the underlying Effect-runSync-with-Layer behavior is a separate
  frontier task and not regressed by this).
