fix(runtime): route Object.defineProperty on Class.prototype through the class-vtable / prototype-method side tables (#2159) (#2242)

`Class.prototype` evaluates back to the class-ref itself in Perry (not a
separate prototype object), so `Object.defineProperty(C.prototype, name,
descriptor)` hit `extract_obj_ptr → null` in `js_object_define_property`
and silently dropped the descriptor. Instance lookups (`new C().method`)
never saw the entry — drizzle-orm's `applyMixins(MySqlSelectBase,
[QueryPromise])` is the load-bearing case: it copies `then`/`catch`/
`finally` from `QueryPromise.prototype` onto `MySqlSelectBase.prototype`,
so `await db.select().from(users)` resolved to the builder itself
instead of the query result.

Fix: detect class-ref receivers up front (using the same `class_ref_id`
helper that `js_object_get_own_property_descriptor` /
`js_object_get_own_property_names` already consult on class-refs) and
install the descriptor's value where instance lookup will find it:

  * `BOUND_METHOD_FUNC_PTR` closures returned by
    `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` on a sibling class — extract the source
    class-ref + method name from the closure captures, look the method
    up in the source class's vtable chain, and copy the entry onto the
    target class's vtable. Dispatching the bound closure directly would
    re-enter `js_native_call_method` against the class-ref (static
    dispatch arm), so we copy the raw `(func_ptr, param_count)` instead;
    the regular vtable walk then invokes the method with
    `this = receiver`.
  * Any other callable — route through
    `js_register_prototype_method`, mirroring the existing
    `Class.prototype.method = fn` direct-assignment path
    (`lookup_prototype_method` is already consulted on the lookup miss).

The drizzle-mysql fixture (#489 acceptance) now uses idiomatic
`await db.select().from(users)` form instead of the `.execute()`
workaround; byte-identical with Node. New gap test
`test_gap_2159_defineproperty_class_prototype.ts` pins both the
single-method install and the full `applyMixins` shape, including
`await thenable` assimilation.

fix(runtime): link Object.create synthetic class_id to original class chain (#1805) (#2244)

`Object.create(Object.getPrototypeOf(instance))` produced an object
that wasn't `instanceof` the original class, even though property
reads and getter dispatch through the synthetic-prototype chain worked
correctly (the #711 / #809 wiring). `js_instanceof`'s chain walk keys
off `get_parent_class_id`, but the synthetic class id allocated by
`js_object_create` had no parent edge linking it to the original
class — so the walk stopped at the unregistered synthetic id and
returned false.

Fix: at synthetic-cid registration time, also record
`(synthetic_cid → proto_ptr.class_id)` in CLASS_REGISTRY when the
proto pointer carries a non-zero class_id. In Perry's model
`Object.getPrototypeOf(instance)` returns the instance itself (see
`js_object_get_prototype_of`), so `proto_ptr` is a real class
instance whose `class_id` field IS the user class's id. Linking that
as the synthetic cid's parent lets the `js_instanceof` chain walk
reach the original class — chained `Object.create` cases also work
because the chain transitively walks `synthetic_2 → synthetic_1 →
ClassId`.

Surfaced by effect's `SchemaAST.annotations`, which clones AST nodes
via `Object.create(Object.getPrototypeOf(ast),
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(ast))`. Refs #1758, #809.

fix(hir): http(s) inline factory-chain dispatch — request/get + on/end (#2208) (#2240)

`http.request(...).on(...).on(...)` (and the `https.get` / chained
`.setHeader`/`.end` variants) failed at runtime with
`TypeError: (number).<method> is not a function`. The variable-binding
form (`const req = http.request(...); req.on(...)`) already worked
because the let-stmt arm tags `req` as a `ClientRequest`; only the
inline factory-chain form was broken.

Two HIR-level holes were closing the loop:

1. `native_class_from_factory_call` only recognised the
   `createServer`/`createSecureServer` factory family, so an inline
   `http.request({...}).on(...)` chain saw the inner call as an
   un-typed `Call(Member(...))` and fell through to the generic
   typed-feedback dispatch — which has no `ClientRequest` arm and
   returned NaN. Added entries for `(http|https, request|get)` →
   `(http, ClientRequest)`, mirroring the runtime-side `class_filter`
   convention that bundles both schemes under module `"http"` (see
   `native_table/http.rs`).

2. The subsequent chain step (`.on(...).on(...)`) also needs the
   class tag to flow through each builder-pattern call so the next
   step can dispatch correctly. Adds an `is_http_client_request` arm
   alongside the existing `fastify Reply` builder-pattern detector,
   covering the EventEmitter introspection methods that return the
   emitter itself (`on`/`once`/`off`/`addListener`/`removeListener`/
   `removeAllListeners`) plus the ClientRequest fluent methods
   (`setHeader`/`setTimeout`/`write`/`end`).

#2186 batch landed.

fix(node:https): full https.Agent.getName parity with Node v22 (#2132) (#2259)

`https.Agent.prototype.getName(options)` was returning the bare http
shape (`localhost::` for an empty agent), but Node's
`lib/https.js` appends 20 TLS-specific fields (ca, cert, ciphers,
key, …) so the empty form is `localhost::::::::::::::::::::::` and the
full form serializes booleans, JSON-stringifies sigalgs, comma-joins
crl buffer arrays, and elides servername when it matches host.

Both http-stack implementations (perry-stdlib + perry-ext-http) shared
the same `js_http_agent_get_name` symbol but ignored the AgentHandle's
`protocol` field. Now each branches on `protocol == "https:"` and the
20 extension fields are appended in the exact order from Node v22.x.

Also fixes a latent http parity gap: family + socketPath are
independent appends (Node does `if (family) ...; if (socketPath) ...`),
not an `if/else`, so `{family: 4, socketPath: '/s'}` produces
`host::4:/s` instead of dropping socketPath.

a `.next`-bearing iterator, so any caller that drove the result would
silently mis-iterate. The runtime now has a real array-iterator class
(`ARRAY_ITERATOR_CLASS_ID`, #321) whose `.next()` dispatches through
`js_native_call_method`, so `js_get_iterator(arr)` can hand back
`array_values_iter(arr)` and the `yield*`-driver's
`__del_iter.next()` lands in the right place.

For-of and spread fast-path arrays earlier in their lowering (array
memcpy / index-loop arms) and never reach `js_get_iterator`, so they are
unaffected. `arr.values().next()` directly is a separate gap (the
value-level `.values()` still routes through `Expr::ArrayValues` →
`js_array_values` which yields a clone) and is out of scope here.

Gap test (`test_gap_1831_yield_star_array.ts`) covers: array yield*,
object-iterable yield*, mixed yield*, empty-array yield*, string-element
yield*, plus for-of and spread over a plain array as regression anchors.
Byte-identical against `node --experimental-strip-types`.

Closes #1831.

feat(hir): class [Symbol.asyncIterator] resolvable via member access (#1838) (#2269)

Follow-up to PR #1841. The runtime side
(`well_known_symbol_method_key` in `crates/perry-runtime/src/symbol.rs`)
already maps `Symbol.asyncIterator` to the synthetic `@@asyncIterator`
vtable key, so the resolver was ready — but the HIR class lowering
explicitly skipped this method:

    } else {
        // Other well-known (toPrimitive, asyncIterator)
        // on a class: not yet implemented, skip.
        continue;
    }

Effect on user code: `Symbol.asyncIterator in instance` returned
`false`, `(instance as any)[Symbol.asyncIterator]` was `undefined`,
and the direct `await it.next()` driver pattern fell through to
"next is not a function" the moment `it` was sourced via member
access.

`iterator` one — name the method `@@asyncIterator` and let it flow
through the regular `methods.push(func)` path. The symbol resolver
binds it to the instance via `js_class_method_bind` the same way it
binds `@@iterator`.

Tested:

  passes byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types`.
  Covers `in`, `typeof`, direct `await it.next()` round-trip, and
  inherited resolution through a `class Sub extends AsyncRange` chain.
- Existing `test_gap_class_symbol_iterator.ts` (sync `@@iterator`)
  still passes — the new arm is gated on `wk == "asyncIterator"` and
  doesn't touch the `@@iterator` path or the dispose-family renames
  above it.

Out of scope (separate follow-up): `for await (const v of instance)`
lowering — codegen still needs an async-iter driver for class
instances. The explicit-driver pattern (`(instance as any)[Symbol.
asyncIterator]() …`) is the one unblocked here.

fix(runtime): close SSO short-string blind spots in object key paths (#1781) (#2281)

`JSValue::is_string()` is `STRING_TAG`-only (0x7FFF) and returns false
for inline SSO short strings (`SHORT_STRING_TAG = 0x7FF9`, length 0..=5
stored in the NaN-box payload). The recurring `if jsval.is_string()
{ /* read as *StringHeader */ } else { /* skip / treat as pointer */ }`
shape across `object/`, `typed_feedback/guards.rs`, and
`native_module.rs` silently misses any key whose name is ≤ 5 ASCII
bytes — `id`, `tag`, `name`, `path`, `data`, `error`, `value`, etc.
That breaks `Object.keys`, `key in obj`, `delete obj[k]`, `obj[k] = v`,
`hasOwnProperty`, `Object.assign`, and a few `NativeModuleRef` lookups
whenever a key happens to live as SSO (typically after a JSON.parse
round-trip, a `string.slice(...)` result used as a key, or a
spread/rest pattern that preserved an SSO source).

The fix is a 3-helper add in `string::compare`:

  - `js_string_key_matches(stored: JSValue, incoming: *StringHeader)`
  - `js_string_key_matches_bytes(stored: JSValue, incoming_bytes: &[u8])`
  - `js_string_key_bytes(stored, &mut sso_buf) -> Option<&[u8]>`

…that compare a stored-key `JSValue` (heap STRING_TAG *or* inline
SHORT_STRING_TAG) against the incoming key without materializing the
SSO value to the heap. Routed through every recurring blind-spot site
identified in #1781's audit:

  - field_get_set.rs (4 sites) — lookup_field_in_keys, Object.keys
    slow-path enumerable filter, closure-style `in` check, and the
    field-cache validity check + slow-path field lookup.
  - object_ops.rs (3 sites) — define-property dedup, `own_key_present`
    (hasOwnProperty), and `js_object_get_own_field_or_undef`.
  - delete_rest.rs (3 sites) — `delete obj.k` lookup + the destructuring-
    rest pattern's source key extract and exclude-list match.
  - alloc.rs (2 sites) — `Object.assign(target, src)`'s overflow-aware
    iterate path (both helpers).
  - field_set_by_name.rs (1 site) — `obj[k] = v` existing-key update
    path (pre-fix appended a duplicate key when the original was SSO).
  - native_module.rs (2 sites) — `read_native_module_name` and
    `get_module_name_from_namespace` for short module names like
    "fs" / "os" / "tty" / "net".
  - typed_feedback/guards.rs (1 site) — shape-guard byte-slice match.

Tests added in `string/compare.rs` and `object/object_ops.rs`:

  - 4 unit tests over the new helpers covering heap-only, SSO-only,
    mixed-rep, length-mismatch, and non-string stored values.
  - `own_key_present_finds_sso_stored_key` plants a SHORT_STRING_TAG
    key directly into a keys_array via `JSValue::try_short_string` and
    asserts the SSO-aware match flow finds it (the pre-fix
    `is_string()` path returned false).

fix(hir): class static blocks run at class-decl source position (#2283)

Per ES spec, a `class { static { ... } }` block runs as part of class
evaluation in source order — right after that class's static-field
initializers and BEFORE any code that follows the class declaration.

Perry hoists class declarations to a separate `module.classes` list,
so the codegen-side machinery only knew the class set, not where each
class appeared in source. The old `init_static_fields_late` loop ran
every static block at the *end* of module init, after all user
top-level statements had executed. So:

  class A { static { A.flag = true; } }
  console.log(A.flag);    // node: true   perry: false (block runs LAST)

The fix lifts static-block invocation into HIR: when `lower_stmt` walks
a `class` decl in the module body, it pushes a `StaticMethodCall` for
each synthetic `__perry_static_init_N` method right after that class's
static-field-init stmts. The block now runs at the spec-correct point
in `module.init`. The codegen fallback loop in
`init_static_fields_late` is kept (skip when the init stream already
calls the block) so class expressions that bypass the stmt-decl path
still get their blocks invoked.

- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/stmt.rs`: inline `StaticMethodCall` for
    each `__perry_static_init_*` after the class's static-field-inits.
- `crates/perry-codegen/src/codegen/helpers.rs`: in
    `init_static_fields_late`, skip blocks already invoked via the
    init stream (detected by a top-level `Expr(StaticMethodCall { ... })`
    matching the synthetic name).
- `test-files/test_gap_class_static_blocks.ts`: new parity test —
    declared-only static field set in a block, source-order ordering
    against `static x = 0`, multiple blocks in one class, cross-class
    read.
- `test-parity/known_failures.json`: drop `test_gap_class_advanced`;
    its `static block initialized: true` diff was the only divergence
    and is now byte-identical with Node.

fix(runtime): trace closure dynamic-prop values in all GC phases (#1802) (#2284)

`scan_closure_dynamic_props_roots_mut` early-returned unless
`is_metadata_rewrite_phase()`, so during `Mark` / `CopyingMark` it did
not visit any side-table prop value. The rewrite-side descriptor in
`gc/layout.rs::visit_gc_rewrite_slot_descriptors` did visit the same
slots, but rewrite only follows already-forwarded pointers — it can't
keep an otherwise-unreachable value alive.

Result: assigning a JSValue prop to a function (e.g. ajv's
`validate.errors = [{ msg }]`) lost the nested contents after a minor
GC. The immediate array survived because the user kept a reference,
but its element objects were collected and read back as a stale
string/undefined. Reproduces both with explicit `gc()` and under
allocation pressure between the set and the read.

Same mistake the analogous `scan_overflow_fields_roots_mut`
(`object/mod.rs`) avoids — it runs in every phase and lets
`visit_nanbox_u64_slot` decide what to do per phase. Match that here:
remove the early-return, trace every stored value via
`visit_nanbox_f64_slot` in every phase, and leave the metadata-key
fixup (`visit_metadata_usize_slot`) where it was — it's already a
no-op in mark phases by design (the side-table key must not itself
keep the closure alive).

Test: `tests_1802::dyn_prop_values_are_visited_in_mark_phase` plants
a known nanbox-bits value in the side table, runs the scanner under
a `RuntimeRootVisitor::for_copy` adapter (which records every value
the scanner visits during the mark walk), and asserts the value
bits appear in the seen set. Pre-fix this test fails because the
scanner early-returned and `seen` was empty.

fix(hir): apply Exclude<T, primitive> narrowing on the else branch of a typeof guard (#2277) (#2289)

`typeof x === "string"` narrowed *neither* branch in the HIR lowering
— the `if`-statement arm in `lower_decl/body_stmt.rs` just lowered both
branches under the binding's declared type. Pre-fix that "worked" for
unions whose members shared the called method (e.g. `string | number |
boolean`'s `.toString()` lives on every variant — the dispatcher's
`is_known_string`-via-union path lights up but the string fast path
covers it). It broke as soon as the else branch's only sensible
method was disjoint from the string surface — the canonical case
being `input.join(",")` on a `string | number[]` union, where the
`is_union_with_string` check in `local_array_methods.rs` flipped to
true, routed `.join` through the string-method path, and surfaced as
`TypeError: (string).join is not a function`.

Adds `crates/perry-hir/src/lower_decl/typeof_narrow.rs`:

- `extract_typeof_guard(cond)` recognizes the AST shape
  `typeof <ident> {===,!==} "<lit>"` (and the swapped-operand form +
  `Paren` wrappers).
- `narrowed_then(orig, "<lit>")` returns the include-narrow for the
  then branch.
- `narrowed_else(orig, "<lit>")` returns the exclude-narrow (TypeScript's
  `Exclude<T, primitive>`) for the else branch.
- Both only act on `Type::Union(...)` operands and on the six
  unambiguous primitive typeof tags (`string` / `number` / `boolean` /
  `bigint` / `undefined` / `symbol`). `function`/`object` are
  intentionally skipped — naive narrowing for those would either lose
  precision or break adjacent dispatch (an `object`-narrowed value
  isn't visibly an `Array(_)` to the dispatcher).

Wires it into the if-statement arm of `lower_body_stmt`. Each branch
takes a `push_block_scope` mark; before lowering the body we push a
shadow `(name, id, narrowed_type)` onto `ctx.locals` so
`lookup_local_type(name)` returns the post-narrow type for the
dispatcher, and the matching `pop_block_scope` removes it. This sits
on top of perry-hir's existing scope machinery — no new infra, no
narrowing context object, no changes to LoweringContext.

Test plan:

- 5 unit tests in `typeof_narrow.rs` covering union-with-array,
  three-way primitive union, scalar non-union (no narrowing), and the
  unsupported `"function"` / `"object"` cases.
- `test_edge_type_narrowing.ts` (the bisect-isolated #1635 sub-case
  the issue body cites) now passes byte-identical against Node — both
  print `1,2,3` for `processInput([1, 2, 3])`. The file is removed
  from `test-parity/known_failures.json` accordingly.
- All 116 pre-existing `perry-hir` lib tests still pass — no regression
  in the simpler `string | number | boolean` paths or the discriminated-
  union / instanceof / `in` narrowing helpers that #2277 doesn't
  touch.

fix(codegen): skip string-method dispatch for array-only methods on Union<String, T> (#2293)

`is_string_expr` returns true for any `LocalGet` whose static type is a
`Union` containing `String` (the nullable-string narrowing case —
`s: string | null` after a `!= null` guard still wants `.toUpperCase`
to route through the string-method dispatch). The
`try_lower_property_get_method_call` dispatch tower had:

    if is_string_expr(ctx, object) {
        return Ok(Some(lower_string_method(ctx, object, property, args)?));
    }

so a call like `(input: string | number[]).join(",")` — only legal
inside the `else` branch of `typeof input === "string"`, where the
actual runtime value is the array variant — also wins on
`is_string_expr` (the union contains `String`). `lower_string_method`'s
catch-all then throws `TypeError: (string).join is not a function`
even though the receiver is actually a number array at runtime, because
`.join` isn't on `String.prototype`.

This was bisected out of #1635 as #2277 ("Union typeof-narrowing leaves
array remainder mis-typed as string — .join → string method dispatch")
— the single residual failure of `test_edge_type_narrowing.ts`.

Fix: gate the string-method route on the method name actually being
something other than an array-only name (`.join`, `.push`, `.map`,
`.filter`, …). When the name is array-only, fall through to the
runtime dispatcher (`js_native_call_method`), which inspects the
receiver's actual shape and dispatches to the array path. The
nullable-string narrowing case (`.toUpperCase`, `.split`, …) is
untouched — those names aren't array-only, so they still route to
`lower_string_method` as before.

- `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/property_get.rs`: add
    `is_array_only_method_name` helper + gate the string-method route on
    `!is_array_only_method_name(property)`.
- `test-files/test_gap_union_typeof_narrowing.ts`: new parity test
    covering both narrowing directions (`string | T[]` and `T[] |
    string`), a second array-only method (`.filter`), and a regression
    check for the `string | null` nullable case.
- `test-parity/known_failures.json`: drop `test_edge_type_narrowing` —
    the bisected residual was this exact shape and is now byte-identical

fix(node:stream): emit 'close' after 'end' on readable-only streams (#2302)

`Readable.from([...])` and other readable-only streams never fired the
'close' event after consuming all data — Perry only emitted 'close' from
the writable-side `finish` path, so a pure Readable stayed with
`r.closed === false` even after `'end'` and `r.on('close', ...)` never
called the listener.

Spec: `'close'` follows `'end'` on a readable-only stream (resources are
released right after the source signals completion). A Duplex defers
`'close'` until BOTH `'end'` and `'finish'` have fired, but that path
already runs `mark_stream_closed` + `emit('close')` after `'finish'` in
`ns_end1`; this PR only adds the equivalent tail for the
readable-only case.

Fix: at the end of `emit_readable_end_once`, when the stream has no
writable side (`hidden_writable_flag_key()` is `None`), call
`mark_stream_closed` and emit `'close'`. The existing Duplex / Writable
path is untouched.

Local sweep against the stream-suite known_failures (issues #1531 /
#1532 / #1545 / #1539 / #1572): 8 tests flip to PASS, no regressions.

- `node-suite/stream/readable/closed-flag` (the direct repro)
- `node-suite/stream/web/writable-stream-start-hook`
- `node-suite/stream/web/byte-stream-construction`
- `node-suite/stream/web/byob-on-byte-stream`
- `node-suite/stream/web/pipethrough-preventclose-flag`
- `node-suite/stream/web/cancel-during-pipeto`
- `node-suite/stream/web/for-await-on-transform`
- `node-suite/stream/web/sink-all-four-methods`

The Web Streams flips are downstream beneficiaries — they're built on
the same readable-end-emission path, and pre-fix the absent `'close'`
event left their teardown listeners pending too.

- `crates/perry-runtime/src/node_stream.rs`: add the close-after-end
    tail to `emit_readable_end_once`, gated on the writable side being
    absent so Duplex / Writable behaviour stays the same.
- `test-parity/known_failures.json`: drop the 8 entries above; they're
    byte-identical with Node post-fix.

fix(runtime): implement process.setgroups + initgroups (#2135) (#2305)

`typeof process.setgroups` and `typeof process.initgroups` returned the
stub `"number"` (the bare-field value `0`), so duck-type guards saw
the stubs and the call form was unreachable. Wire both through the
same path as the other POSIX setters that landed in this issue.

- `js_process_setgroups(groups)` walks a JS number array and calls
  `libc::setgroups` once (non-finite / out-of-range entries are
  skipped, matching the `unix_id_arg` coercion the family already
  uses). Non-unix targets no-op.
- `js_process_initgroups(user, extra_gid)` accepts the username-as-
  string form and a numeric extra GID, calls `libc::initgroups`.
  Numeric-UID first arg silently no-ops — Node accepts that form too,
  but resolving it needs `getpwuid_r` plumbing that's out of scope.
- Property-read whitelist returns bound-method closures so the
  `typeof` reads match Node. HIR lowering, node_core table rows,
  dynamic-dispatch arms, and manifest entries are all wired.

Closes two more #2135 process-tracker stubbed-method gaps.

fix(codegen): reuse slot for hoisted var redeclaration (#1803) (#2307)

A `var x` that appears in more than one branch of a function (the
canonical shape `if (...) { var x = a } else { var x = b }`) lowers to
multiple `Stmt::Let` that share the SAME hoisted HIR id, since `var` is
function-scoped. `lower_let` allocated a fresh alloca for each occurrence
and overwrote the `id → slot` entry in `ctx.locals`, so a read after the
merge point bound to whichever branch was lowered LAST. At runtime only
one branch executes, so the read saw an uninitialized slot whenever the
*other* branch ran — silently returning undefined.

This is exactly what made ajv's `standalone`-generated per-property
`type` guards accept invalid input (#1803): each guard is
`var valid0 = ...` redeclared per if/else branch, then read by a
following `if (valid0) { ...next property guard... }`. With the wrong
slot, `valid0` read falsy and the downstream number/boolean guards were
skipped, so `{ name: "Ada", age: "old" }` validated as true.

Fix: when `lower_let` sees an id already registered in `ctx.locals`
(a redeclaration of a hoisted var), reuse the existing slot by routing
the assignment through `LocalSet` — the canonical write path that
maintains every shadow (boxed cell, i32 mirror, GC shadow slot, closure
capture). A redeclaration with no initializer (`var x;`) keeps the prior
value, matching JS.

Adds test-files/test_ajv_standalone_typed.ts (+ vendored
ajv_user_typed.generated.cjs) covering the typed-property guards; output
is byte-for-byte vs node. The structural subset (test_ajv_standalone.ts)
stays parity-clean.

fix(stream): drive async-iterable mapper result in Readable.flatMap (#1572) (#2304)

`Readable.from(arr).flatMap(async function* (n) { yield … })` now
drives the returned async generator through its `[Symbol.asyncIterator]()`
and flattens the yields into the result stream, matching Node:

  Readable.from([1, 2]).flatMap(async function* (n) {
    yield n;
    yield n * 100;
  }).toArray()
  // node: [1, 100, 2, 200]   perry pre-fix: [<generator-obj>, <generator-obj>]

Pre-fix `ns_iter_flat_map` only flattened array results and Readable's
hidden chunks; an async-generator mapper return fell through to the
"append as a single chunk" path. Now the post-array-and-Readable arm
probes `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` → bare `.next()` → `[Symbol.iterator]`
and reuses the existing `js_async_iterator_to_array` driver
(transparently unwraps already-settled `Promise<{value, done}>` steps,
so a sync iterable returns its yields unchanged).

The driver helpers in `array::iterator` are crate-private; I added
three `pub(crate)` shims (`call_symbol_async_iterator_for_flat_map`,
`async_iterator_to_array_for_flat_map`, `has_iterator_next`) and
re-exported them through `array::mod` so `node_stream` can reach them
without leaking the inner module path.

Clears two skip-list entries: `node-suite/stream/iter-helpers/flat-map-async`
(#1572 itself) and `node-suite/stream/iter-helpers/flat-map-async-gen`
(routed to #1558 but unblocked by the same fix). Both now byte-identical
to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

fix(runtime): fire process beforeExit event at event loop exit (#2135) (#2312)

Node fires `beforeExit` with the would-be exit code as the single
argument when the event loop is about to exit on its own. Listeners
registered via `process.on("beforeExit", ...)` already had a working
registration + emit path through `PROCESS_EMITTER`, but the codegen-
emitted event-loop epilogue never called the emit hook, so the
listener was a dead callback.

Wire it in:
- New runtime function `js_process_emit_before_exit(code)` in os.rs
  forwards to the existing `emit_process_event("beforeExit", &[code])`
  pipeline.
- Codegen's `exit_idx` block now calls the runtime function with code
  `0` (Perry doesn't yet wire `process.exitCode` into this codegen path,
  and the surface this issue tracks only pins the firing + default
  code), then drains microtasks/timers once more so last-minute work
  the listener queued still runs before the final `ret`.
- Explicit `process.exit(N)` continues to bypass via `libc::_exit`, so
  Node's "exit() skips beforeExit" contract is preserved.

Closes another #2135 process-tracker output-diff gap.

fix(transform): preserve hoisted-var slot across unrolled loop copies (#2308) (#2313)

* fix(transform): preserve hoisted-var slot across unrolled loop copies (#2308)

The static-loop unroller (`unroll_static_loops`) clones a loop body N times
and calls `refresh_local_ids` to rename every body-declared binding to a
fresh id, so the copies don't alias (needed for distinct per-iteration
closure captures and to avoid duplicate module-init globals, #456).

But a `var` declared inside the loop body is function-scoped: a read AFTER
the loop references the original id. Renaming each copy's declaration to a
fresh id meant the post-loop read bound to an id that NO copy ever wrote,
so it observed the initial (undefined/0) value:

  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { var t = i * 2; sum += t; }
  return sum + t;   // node: 10 (t = 4) — perry (before): 6 (t = 0)

Only fires when the loop bounds are constant (the loop is unrolled); with
a runtime bound the same code was already correct.

Fix: before unrolling each function/method/init/ctor body, compute the set
of loop-body-declared ids that are referenced outside their loop body
(`compute_loop_escaping_ids`, count-based on the original HIR). These are
exactly the hoisted, function-scoped `var`s. `refresh_local_ids` seeds its
remap with identity entries for them, and `alloc_fresh` reuses an existing
remap entry instead of minting a new id — so every copy keeps the var's
original id. Because the unrolled body is straight-line, the last copy's
write lands in the slot the post-loop read uses, matching JS.

Block-scoped `let`/`const` (which can never be referenced outside the loop
body) are absent from the set and keep getting fresh per-copy ids, so
per-iteration closure captures stay distinct (verified by a unit test and
the `distinctCaptures` e2e case).

Tests: two unit tests in unroll.rs (escaping var keeps id; captured let
still refreshed) + test-files/test_gap_2308_unrolled_loop_var.ts (byte-for-
byte vs node). A `var` assigned inside a *conditional* within an unrolled
loop additionally needs the per-branch slot fix from #1803 and is covered
there.

* refactor(transform): split unroll.rs to satisfy the 2000-line file gate

The #2308 fix pushed crates/perry-transform/src/unroll.rs to 2032 lines,
tripping the lint job's file-size gate (./scripts/check_file_size.sh, cap
2000). Move the file to unroll/mod.rs and extract the #2308 escaping-id
analysis (compute_loop_escaping_ids + its count/declared-id helpers) into a
sibling unroll/escape_analysis.rs, re-exported via an explicit named use.
No behavior change — mod.rs is now 1801 lines, escape_analysis.rs 245.

fix(geisterhand): link the geisterhand-built stdlib, not the auto-optimized one (#1383) (#2315)

PR #1385 fixed the BUILD half of #1383 by adding `-p perry-stdlib` to the
single geisterhand cargo invocation, so a geisterhand-featured, async-enabled
`libperry_stdlib.a` lands in target/geisterhand with a hash-consistent
perry-runtime. But the LINK half was still broken: the stdlib actually linked
under `--enable-geisterhand` was the auto-optimized one, built with
`--no-default-features` and a feature set derived from the app's *TS* imports.

For a geisterhand UI app whose async surface comes from a native binding
(@perryts/storekit / google-auth / play-billing — all using
`perry_ffi::async_runtime::JsPromise`) rather than TS, auto-optimize never
enables `async-runtime`, so the linked stdlib lacks `perry_ffi_promise_*` and
the link fails with `Undefined symbols: _perry_ffi_promise_new`.

Fix:
- Add `find_geisterhand_stdlib(target)` (mirrors `find_geisterhand_runtime`):
  searches only the target/geisterhand build dirs, so it returns the
  geisterhand-built stdlib (full default features incl. async-runtime) and
  never the auto-optimized one.
- In compile.rs, when `ctx.needs_geisterhand`, select that stdlib for the link
  (falling back to the auto-optimized stdlib if absent). This also keeps the
  bundled perry-runtime hash-consistent with `gh_runtime`.
- Include the geisterhand stdlib in the `gh_missing` cold-build check (both the
  compile.rs runtime-selection site and the link/mod.rs link site) so a stale
  target/geisterhand dir built before the stdlib was added triggers a rebuild
  instead of silently falling back.

fix(cjs-wrap, codegen): preserve closure over IIFE-local lets for hoisted classes (#2310) (#2318)

Two narrow fixes for the cjs-wrapped-module pattern from ws/lib/sender.js
that the bug report walks through (`let randomPoolPointer = …; class
Sender { static frame(){ … randomPoolPointer++ } }`):

1. `cjs_wrap::extract_top_level_class_decls` now refuses to hoist a
   top-level `class X { … }` out of the wrap IIFE when the class body
   textually references any top-level `let`/`const`/`var` declared in
   the same source. Pre-fix every top-level class was unconditionally
   lifted above the IIFE, which severed the closure over IIFE-locals
   like `randomPoolPointer` — the class's static method body then
   couldn't resolve those identifiers and the compile hard-errored with
   `Undefined variable in update expression: randomPoolPointer`. Two new
   helpers (`collect_top_level_let_const_var_names`,
   `class_body_references_any`) do the textual scan; both stay inside
   the cjs_wrap module so the heuristic is testable in isolation. Two
   unit tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard that
   self-contained classes still hoist.

2. The `referenced_from_fn` scan in `codegen/mod.rs` now walks every
   class's `static_methods`, getters/setters, and (static) field
   initializer bodies — not just instance methods + the constructor.
   Pre-fix a `let n = 0; class C { static bump() { return n++; } }` at
   module level left `n` un-globalized, so the static method's `n++`
   wrote to a local alloca that nothing else observed; `C.bump()` came
   back 0 on every call. The added passes mirror the existing scan
   shape, so `n` gets promoted to `module_globals` and `Expr::Update`
   correctly hits the shared global storage.

Closes #2310 for the cjs-wrap path; the deeper "class declared inside a
function body whose methods closure-capture outer lets" shape is
preserved as a follow-up (left in place — the cjs-wrap fix avoids it
entirely for the reported repro by NOT hoisting).

fix(fs): extend Node arg-validation to closeSync/readSync/writeSync/fchmodSync/chmodSync/renameSync (#2013) (#2328)

PR #2035 added the validation pattern for `fs.readFileSync` /
`fs.accessSync` / `fs.statSync` / `fs.openSync`; the issue's
follow-up call-out lists ~27 fs functions that still hit
"Missing expected exception" because they don't yet validate. This
gap-fills the fd-only sync surface (`closeSync`, `readSync`,
`readvSync`, `writeSync`, `writevSync`, `fchmodSync`, `fsyncSync`,
`fdatasyncSync`, `fchownSync`) and the path-mutator sync surface
(`chmodSync`, `renameSync`) so each:

  - throws `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` on a non-fd / non-path
    first argument (matches Node);
  - throws `Error [EBADF]` on a numeric fd that isn't open in
    perry-runtime's `FD_REGISTRY` (matches Node's syscall surface).

The new `validate_fd_open(value, syscall)` helper combines the
existing `validate_fd` type+range probe with an `FD_REGISTRY`
membership check + EBADF throw. Callers that need the validation
order preserved (`fchownSync`: validate uid+gid BEFORE EBADF, per
Node's `validateInteger` ordering) keep the bare `validate_fd` and
issue the EBADF after the rest of the int32 validations. `validate_fd`
itself stays single-purpose so the FileHandle wrappers — which can
legitimately hold a `-1` sentinel from a failed open — keep their
silent no-op fallback.

The parity test (`test-parity/node-suite/fs/sync/arg-validation.ts`)
gets 13 new probes covering each new shape against
`node --experimental-strip-types`; the existing legacy block stays
byte-identical. `cargo test -p perry-runtime --lib` still 746/746.

fix(node:http): emit headers passed via res.writeHead (#2132) (#2335)

writeHead's headers argument was typed NA_STR in the native dispatch
table, so a headers *object* was coerced to the literal string
"[object Object]" and every header set through res.writeHead(status,
headers) / res.writeHead(status, statusMessage, headers) was silently
dropped from the response.

Pass arg2/arg3 as raw JSValues (NA_JSV) and resolve the Node overloads
in the runtime: a string in slot 2 is the statusMessage, a heap object
in slot 2 or 3 is the bulk headers, which are JSON-serialized via
js_json_stringify and merged (lowercase lookup key, original case
retained for getHeaderNames).

fix(process): extend Node arg-validation to chdir/kill/exit/cpuUsage/hrtime (#2013) (#2332)

Follow-up to PR #2328 (fs slice). Each process-surface entry point
now throws the Node-matching `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` (or
`ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL` for `process.kill`'s second arg) on a wrong-type
argument:

  - `process.chdir(123)` → ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE (was: garbage-deref to
    ENOENT). A new `js_process_chdir_jsv(value)` runtime entry takes
    the full NaN-boxed value, validates, then re-dispatches to the
    existing string-only `js_process_chdir`. The codegen lowering for
    `Expr::ProcessChdir` now emits the JSV entry instead of
    `unbox_to_i64` → bare `*const StringHeader`.
  - `process.kill('abc', 0)` → ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE on `pid`,
    `process.kill(0, {})` → ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL on the signal arg
    (object/array/boolean don't reach the numeric coerce path).
  - `process.exit('foo')` → ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE on the code arg
    (null/undefined still pass through to the existing default).
  - `process.cpuUsage('abc')` → ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE on a non-object
    `prior`; null/undefined still pass through.
  - `process.hrtime('abc')` → ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE on a non-array
    `prior`. A new local `is_array_value` helper does the GC-type-tag
    probe so the heap-pointer-but-not-array shape (Object/Buffer/...)
    is also caught.

The fs validation helpers (`describe_received`,
`throw_type_error_with_code`, `is_numeric`) get crate-wide visibility
so process can reuse the Node-shaped error formatting without
duplicating the helpers.

covers 14 probes byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

feat(dynamic-import): resolve never-reassigned let/var path bindings (#1674) (#2338)

The dynamic import() path resolver only followed module-level const
locals, so a let/var binding — even one assigned exactly once to a
statically-resolvable value — produced a hard compile error.

collect_module_const_locals now collects let/var single-init bindings in
addition to const. Its existing mutation scan still removes any binding
that is reassigned anywhere (a later LocalSet), so a genuinely mutated
specifier still falls back to Unresolved — soundness is preserved.

This is sub-part A (type/flow narrowing) of #1674: it requires no new
runtime or codegen since the multi-target dispatch already consumes a
Vec<String>. The glob/context-module path (sub-part B) and assigned-only-
literals across multiple writes remain follow-ups.

fix(crypto): validate randomBytes/randomInt args (#2013) (#2353)

`crypto.randomBytes(size)` and `crypto.randomInt(min, max)` now
throw Node-matching errors on bad input. Pre-fix the codegen
unboxed the NaN-boxed arg as f64 (so `{}` arrived as NaN), and
`size as usize` silently truncated NaN to 0 — `randomBytes({})`
returned an empty buffer instead of throwing.

- `randomBytes('abc' / {} / true / null)` → `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]`
- `randomBytes(-1 / NaN / Infinity / 2^31)` → `RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]`
- `randomBytes(1.5)` truncates to 1 (no throw) — matches Node's
  fractional-tolerant behavior; the reject set is non-finite +
  negative + > 2^31-1.
- `randomInt('abc' / {} / true)` → `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` on
  either bound.
- `randomInt(1.5 / NaN / Infinity)` → `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]`
  (`validateInteger` shape — non-integer is a type error in Node).
- `randomInt(±2^48+1)` → `RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]`.

`crates/perry-runtime/src/fs/validate.rs` becomes a public module so
perry-stdlib can reuse the Node-shaped error helpers
(`describe_received`, `is_numeric`, `throw_type_error_with_code`,
`throw_range_error_with_code`) without duplicating them.

`test-parity/node-suite/crypto/random/arg-validation.ts` covers 14
probes byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`; the
other crypto validators (createHash / createHmac / pbkdf2Sync) take
already-unboxed string args and need a parallel `_jsv`-shaped
entry — left as the natural follow-up.

fix(node:process): chdir error path/dest/errno match Node (#2135) (#2354)

process.chdir() to a missing/invalid directory threw an error whose
fields diverged from Node: `path` was set to the target, and `dest`
and `errno` were absent. Node's libuv chdir error sets `path` to the
*source* (cwd), `dest` to the failed target, and `errno` to the
negative libuv code (ENOENT=-2 etc.).

Set `path` = cwd, and attach `dest` (target) and `errno` (negative
libuv code) via the per-error user-prop side table. The message itself
already matched Node. Backs test-process-chdir-errormessage.js (#2135).

chdir + its error construction moved to a new `os::chdir` submodule so
os.rs stays under the 2000-line file-size gate.

feat(dynamic-import): directory-glob template specifiers (#1674 sub-B) (#2357)

Implements sub-part B of #1674: a dynamic import() whose specifier is a
template literal with a fixed relative-directory prefix/suffix and a
non-resolvable middle — `import(`./plugins/${name}.ts`)` — now globs
the importing module's directory for matching files and compiles each as
a candidate, instead of erroring at compile time.

- perry-hir: new `dynamic_import_glob_pattern` detects the shape and
  returns (prefix, suffix). Additive — the existing resolver is untouched;
  the driver only consults this on the Unresolved fallthrough. Requires a
  relative, directory-bearing prefix so the glob can never escape one
  folder into node_modules / the whole project.
- driver: `expand_dynamic_import_glob` reads <prefix-dir> relative to the

feat(compile): module-graph tree-shaking / DCE for compilePackages (#2309) (#2325)

* feat(compile): tree-shaking Stage 1 — binding-level reachability + sideEffects prune (#2309)

Perry compiles every import-reachable module at module granularity and
refuses (during lowering) on genuinely-runtime `new Function` and
unimplemented APIs — even when the offending module is only reachable via a
dead re-export-barrel edge and never runs. A 5-line ink hello-world fails to
compile on es-toolkit's `_.template` `new Function`, which is pulled in only
because the `es-toolkit/compat` barrel re-exports it; the consumer imports
just `throttle`.

Stage 1 adds a tree-shaking pass (off by default behind `PERRY_TREE_SHAKE=1`
/ `perry.experiments.treeShake`) that, after the full graph is collected,
computes binding-level reachability from user code and prunes unreachable
node_modules modules before codegen:

- Deferred refusals (perry-hir/deferral.rs): while lowering a node_modules
  module under tree-shaking, `new Function` (eval_classifier) and the 5 #463
  unimplemented gates record the refusal and fall through instead of
  hard-erroring. Re-raised after pruning only for modules that survive — so
  dead code's refusals are dropped, live code's stay fatal and span-precise.

- Reachability fixpoint (compile/reachability.rs): monotone Rooted/Bindings
  lattice. User modules seed Rooted (never pruned). Honors package.json
  `"sideEffects": false` — a pure re-export barrel reached only via named
  bindings follows just the edges feeding needed exports and drops bare
  side-effect imports, so es-toolkit's `template.mjs` becomes unreachable.
  Every ambiguous shape (namespace import, export*, dynamic import,
  unresolvable specifier) conservatively roots the whole target. Surviving
  barrels have dangling edges to pruned modules rewritten away.

Validated: real `import { throttle } from "es-toolkit/compat"` prunes 430
unreachable modules (incl. the `new Function` leaf) and compiles+runs;
flag-off path is byte-identical to before. 4 fixpoint unit tests cover
barrel-drop, namespace-keeps-all, export*-keeps-source, non-barrel-escalate.

Also lands Stage 2 config scaffolding (perry.define / DefineValue, unused
until the env-fold pass).

Refs #2309

* feat(compile): tree-shaking Stage 2 — process.env define-folding + dead-branch elimination (#2309)

Removes statically-dead `if` branches (and the dynamic `import()` inside
them) before those edges enter the module graph, so an env-gated dependency
subtree is never collected. This is how ink's
`if (process.env['DEV'] === 'true') { await import('./devtools.js') }`
drops the entire ws / react-devtools subtree (a missing zlib const #463 and
the #2310 module-let codegen bug live in there).

- env_fold.rs: a build-time constant folder over `if` conditions. Resolves
  `process.env.<NAME>` from explicit `perry.define` (esbuild-style, host
  package.json only) plus an implicit `NODE_ENV → "production"` default for
  node_modules code. Folds Compare/Logical/Unary(Not) over literals; strict
  eq/ne are total, loose eq/ne + ordering only fold within matching types
  (never replicates full JS coercion). Anything not provably constant is left
  untouched — never folds an un-configured runtime env read. Walks module
  init + function bodies + nested blocks (if/while/for/do/try/switch/labeled).
  Runs before the dynamic-import walk so the dead `import()` is gone first.
  Gated on tree-shaking (no-op when off).

- expr_member.rs: `process.env["NAME"]` with a string-literal key now lowers
  to `EnvGet` (static), matching the dot form, so the fold sees ink's bracket
  access. Runtime-identical to the prior EnvGetDynamic(String) path.

Validated: an env-gated dead `import()` of a `new Function` module fails
without a define (branch kept → leaf reached) and compiles+runs with
`define: { "process.env.DEV": "false" }` (branch + leaf eliminated), with
both dot and bracket access. 3 fold unit tests; full perry-hir suite green.

feat(node:http): invoke Agent.createConnection on the request path (#2154) (#2323)

* feat(node:http): invoke Agent.createConnection on the request path (#2154)

PR #2264 shipped the http.Agent surface (validation, pool accessors,
per-agent reqwest client, createConnection/createSocket setter storage)
but deferred *invoking* a user-supplied createConnection override when
servicing http.request. This wires Node's full socket-injection: when an
agent defines createConnection, http.request now drives the HTTP/1.1
exchange over the net.Socket the override returns instead of reqwest.

How it works:
- perry-ffi `raw_net`: a C-ABI vtable (attach/write/poll_read/close)
  published by perry-ext-net into a perry-ffi OnceLock and looked up by
  perry-ext-http. No Cargo edge between the two well-known-flip crates;
  http-only binaries (no net linked) degrade gracefully.
- perry-ext-net: a per-socket "raw mode" (SocketState.raw) routes inbound
  bytes into a buffer for the http consumer instead of dispatching JS
  'data' events; raw_close unregisters the socket so the event loop can
  exit (raw mode suppresses the JS Close event that normally removes it).
- perry-ext-http: on req.end(), if the agent has a createConnection
  override, build the {host,port,path} options object, invoke the closure
  on the main thread (arena-safety: JS closure calls never run on a tokio
  worker), then drive the exchange over the returned socket and surface
  the response through the existing PendingHttpEvent::Response path. The
  HTTP/1.1 response parser is factored out and shared with the existing
  trailer-aware reqwest-bypass path.

Two prerequisite fixes uncovered along the way:
- perry-hir: `agent.<prop> = x` (incl. createConnection) was never lowered
  to the `__set_<prop>` NativeMethodCall — #2264 added the FFI setters and
  native-table entries but not the assignment wiring, so every Agent
  property assignment silently no-op'd. Added the Agent setter mappings.
- perry-runtime json: JSON.stringify of an object holding a native handle
  (e.g. an http.Agent in an options literal) segfaulted — the closure-tag
  probe and value recursion dereferenced the small handle id as a heap
  pointer. Guard low-memory "pointers" and emit null. This also fixed a
  pre-existing crash in plain http.request({ agent }).

Validated with a node-suite parity test (request-create-connection)
matching `node --experimental-strip-types` byte-for-byte and exiting
cleanly. No regression in the existing http/net suites.

* refactor(perry-ext-net): split raw-net bridge into raw_bridge.rs (file-size gate)

lib.rs exceeded the 2000-line lint gate after the #2154 raw-mode additions.
Move RawReadState, the raw_state_for/raw_mark_closed helpers, the four
perry_net_raw_* C-ABI vtable fns, and the vtable registration into a new
raw_bridge submodule, and route run_socket_task's raw handling through two
thin hooks (route_data / mark_terminal). Behavior-identical; lib.rs back to

fix(date): model Date as a reference type so mutations propagate (#2089) (#2380)

Perry modeled `Date` as a value-type (a raw NaN-boxed f64 timestamp), so
mutating a Date through any aliasing boundary — `const b = a`, a function
parameter, or a closure parameter — did not propagate back, because each
binding held an independent copy of the f64. This made effect's
`DateTime.add(d, { days: 1 })` a no-op (it mutates a Date inside a closure
and reads it back).

Promote Date to a reference type: a NaN-boxed POINTER to a 1-slot mutable
`DateCell { ts: f64 }`, so all aliases/params/closures share state.

fix(hir): #2383 lower labeled block to labeled run-once do-while so `break <label>` exits it (#2389)

`break <label>` targeting a labeled *block* statement (`a: { … break a; … }`)
— valid JS/TS that exits the block — was rejected at codegen with
"labeled break 'a' outside any loop". Perry only registered label targets
for labeled *loops*, and the labeled-statement lowering flattened the block
and wrapped only its last statement, which was also semantically wrong.

labeled-statement lowering sites (module-level lower/stmt.rs and function-body
lower_decl/body_stmt.rs). The do-while's exit block becomes the labeled-break
target via the existing loop-based labeled-break codegen; the body runs exactly
once and `while (false)` falls straight through to the exit. `continue <label>`
against a block label is a JS early SyntaxError, so it never reaches here.

This is the hard blocker for compiling React (and thus ink, #348): minified
react.production.js / react.development.js and react-reconciler all use
`a: { … break a; }` labeled-block patterns.

fix(node:http,https): emit default Connection / Keep-Alive response headers (#2132) (#2416)

* fix(node:http,https): emit default Connection / Keep-Alive response headers (#2132)

Perry serializes node:http/https responses through hyper, which omits the
Connection and Keep-Alive headers on HTTP/1.1 (keep-alive is implicit on the
wire). Node surfaces them explicitly — Connection: keep-alive plus
Keep-Alive: timeout=<keepAliveTimeout/1000> on a kept-alive connection, and
Connection: close otherwise — so clients reading res.headers.connection /
res.headers['keep-alive'] (the test-http-agent-keep-alive-* family in #2132's
diff bucket) saw them missing.

New HyperResponseShape::apply_default_connection_headers injects the
Node-compatible defaults before handing the shape to hyper, wired into both
the http and https dispatch sites:
  - HTTP/1.1 defaults to keep-alive unless the client sent Connection: close;
    HTTP/1.0 keep-alives only when explicitly requested.
  - keep-alive + keepAliveTimeout>0 => Connection: keep-alive + Keep-Alive;
    otherwise Connection: close with no Keep-Alive.
  - a handler-set Connection header is respected, never overridden.
  - HTTP/2 manages reuse at the protocol level and gets neither header.

Adds test-parity/node-suite/http/server/default-connection-headers.ts
(byte-identical to Node across default / client-close / explicit-close).

fix(array): entries()/keys()/values() return a real iterator object, not a materialized array (#2384) (#2407)

codegen's `Expr::ArrayEntries`/`ArrayKeys`/`ArrayValues` fast path to

  the same `any`-typed catch-all keep the eager materialization (delegated to
  `js_array_{entries,keys,values}`, which route to the correct Map/Set
  iterator — #321), so a Map buffer is never reinterpreted as `[index,value]`.
- Route codegen's `Expr::Array{Entries,Keys,Values}` fast path (and the
  `arr.method()` array-method dispatch) to the new iterator-object wrappers.
- Route the `next`/`return`/`throw` array-method arms to the runtime's generic
  `js_native_call_method` dispatch instead of returning the receiver, so the

`js_for_of_to_array` already detect `ARRAY_ITERATOR_CLASS_ID` and drive
`.next()`. Adds test_gap_array_iterator_manual_next.ts (byte-identical to node).

fix(android): global-dynamic TLS model + bundle companion .so into APK (#1529, #1527) (#2415)

#1529 — `perry compile --target android` produced a `libperry_app.so` whose
TLS relocations used the Initial-Executable access model (rustc's default for
the aarch64-linux-android target). That model is only valid for libraries
present at process startup; PerryActivity `dlopen`s the lib at runtime, so it
crashed with `TLS symbol "(null)" ... using IE access model`. The runtime and
stdlib use `thread_local!` heavily (per-thread arena, GC state, shadow stack),
so those IE relocations got baked into the cdylib. Force
`-C tls-model=global-dynamic` for every Rust crate compiled for android:
- runtime/stdlib auto-optimize build (optimized_libs.rs)
- third-party `perry.nativeLibrary` crate builds (link/mod.rs)
- geisterhand runtime/stdlib/ui build (library_search.rs)
- the printed perry-ui-android build instruction

#1527 — companion `.so` libraries (e.g. `libperry_play_billing.so` from a
`crate-android` cdylib) were copied next to the output binary by the compile
step but never made it into the APK, so the app crashed on launch with
`UnsatisfiedLinkError: dlopen failed: library "lib….so" not found`.
`build_and_run_android` now copies every sibling `.so` from the staging dir
into `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/` so Gradle bundles them alongside
`libperry_app.so`. Static-lib companions link directly and have no `.so` here,
so nothing to copy.

fix(publish): project-relative framework_dir for vendored optional frameworks (#1303) (#2435)

`perry publish` uploads the project to a remote worker and runs the
whole build there, so a native wrapper's `build.rs` opt-in for an
optional vendored SDK (e.g. `@perryts/google-auth` reading
`PERRY_GOOGLE_SIGN_IN_FRAMEWORK_DIR`) never saw the framework: the
dev's shell env doesn't transfer, the absolute local path doesn't
exist on the worker, and the framework binaries weren't uploaded.
Published iOS builds silently linked the no-SDK stub.

Make the optional-framework search dir project-relative and uploaded:

- `perry.toml [google_auth].framework_dir` declares a dir relative to
  the project root. `link/mod.rs::resolve_optional_framework_dir`
  resolves it to an absolute path, with precedence
  explicit `frameworks_env` env var > `framework_dir` (existing local
  setups unchanged).
- Before building the wrapper crate, Perry exports the resolved path
  as the package's `frameworks_env` so `build.rs` opts the real SDK in
  — on the local machine and on the worker (which re-reads the
  uploaded perry.toml). The link step uses the same resolution for
  `-F <dir>` / `-framework <name>`.
- `perry publish` force-includes `framework_dir` in the upload tarball
  so the static archive binary (extension-less, usually >1 MB) isn't
  dropped by the default binary-artifact exclusion.

Adds unit tests for the resolver (env precedence, perry.toml fallback,
absent key) and the tarball force-include, plus manifest-v1 docs and a
type-validation warning for the new key.

feat(node:http): invoke Agent.createSocket on the request path (#2154) (#2449)

PR #2323 wired the `createConnection` override into `http.request`; this
adds its sibling `createSocket(req, options, cb)` — the last unimplemented
bullet of #2154. Node's `Agent.prototype.addRequest` calls
`createSocket(req, options, cb)` and the override delivers the socket via
`cb(err, socket)`. Perry stored the override but never invoked it.

On `req.end()`, when the agent defines `createSocket`, we now (on the main
thread, per the arena-safety rule for JS closure calls):

- build `req` (the ClientRequest, NaN-boxed like any http handle value),
  the `{host,port,path}` options object (shared with the createConnection
  path), and a native `cb` closure backed by `http_create_socket_cb`;
- invoke the override via `closure.call3`;
- when the override calls `cb(null, socket)`, the continuation attaches the
  socket (raw-net bridge) and drives the HTTP/1.1 exchange over it, exactly
  like the createConnection path; `cb(err)` surfaces an `'error'` event.

`createSocket` takes precedence over `createConnection` when both are set,
mirroring Node. The native cb is registered with arity 2 so a 1-arg
`cb(err)` pads the socket slot with `undefined` instead of reading an
uninitialized register.

Validated with a node-suite parity test (request-create-socket),
byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`. perry-ext-http only —
perry-stdlib's parallel http path has no socket-dispatch (same as #2323).

Known gap (pre-existing, not createSocket-specific): the `'error'` event
delivers a generic message, not a full Error object — Perry's http error
events don't reconstruct Error objects, and this crate has no object
introspection helper to read `err.message`.

fix(hir): #2442 — install object-literal getters/setters as accessor descriptors (#2451)

Getters/setters defined in an object literal (`{ get k(){}, set k(v){} }`)
were silently dropped by the object-literal lowering (the `_ => {}` catch-all
in both the spread and non-spread paths), so the property read as `undefined`
and the accessor bodies never ran. Class accessors and
`Object.defineProperty(obj, k, { get })` already worked; this closes the
object-literal syntax.

  or `SetterProp` (one param), with `captures_this` reflecting whether the
  body reads `this` — mirroring `lower_method_prop`.
- Object literals containing any getter/setter now route through the existing
  fully source-ordered IIFE (the same path spreads use), so the accessor key
  lands in its source position (`{a, get x(){}, b}` → keys `[a, x, b]`). Each
  accessor emits a `js_object_define_accessor(__o, key, getter, setter)` call.

Runtime (perry-runtime/src/object/object_ops.rs):
- New `js_object_define_accessor` installs/merges the accessor descriptor.
  Unlike `Object.defineProperty`, object-literal accessors are enumerable +
  configurable (spec), and a separate `get k` / `set k` for the same key
  merges rather than clobbers (an `undefined` half leaves the other intact).
  Each closure is cloned and rebound so it runs with `this === obj` (#450).

Verified byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types` via
test-files/test_gap_2442_object_literal_accessors.ts: get/set invocation,
captured-local accessors, `this`-bound getters, source-order key placement,

fix(runtime): TypedArray indexOf/includes read the typed backing store (#2456)

`Array.prototype.indexOf` / `includes` are routed through
`js_array_indexOf_jsvalue` / `js_array_includes_jsvalue` for TypedArray
receivers too, but those walked the elements as NaN-boxed `JSValue`s.
A TypedArray stores raw numbers in its typed backing store, so the
generic walk fed garbage bit patterns to the comparison and every
search returned -1 / false (e.g. `new Int32Array([1,2,3]).indexOf(3)`
was -1).

Detect a registered TypedArray up front (via `lookup_typed_array_kind`)
and read elements with `js_typed_array_get`:
  * indexOf — strict-equality numeric scan (so `indexOf(NaN)` is -1),
  * includes — SameValueZero (so `includes(NaN)` is true for float
    typed arrays).

Regular arrays are untouched (the typed branch only fires when the
pointer is in the typed-array registry). Adds unit tests covering
Int32Array indexOf/includes and Float64Array NaN SameValueZero.

Part of #2447. Two related gaps remain and are NOT addressed here:
  * `lastIndexOf` is lowered to the string `lastIndexOf` path
    (`js_string_last_index_of`) at the HIR level, so a typed runtime
    branch would be dead code — needs a codegen-routing fix.
  * `new Float64Array([..., NaN, ...])` (array-literal construction with
    a non-constant/global element) doesn't `register_typed_array`, so
    the receiver falls to the broken regular-array path — a separate
    construction-registration bug.

fix(node:http,https,http2): bind `this` to server in listen callback (#2132) (#2461)

Node invokes the `listen([port][,host][,backlog], cb)` callback (and the
`'listening'` listeners) with `this` bound to the server, so the canonical
idiom works:

    server.listen(0, function() {
      const port = this.address().port;
      // ...
    });

Perry called the callback with `this === undefined`, so `this.address()`
threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'address')`.
This idiom appears in 167 of the test-http*/test-https* cases in Node's
test/parallel corpus, making it a recurring first-wall blocker in the #2132
diff/runtime-fail bucket.

Add a `with_implicit_this(this_val, f)` helper (request.rs) that sets the
runtime implicit-`this` cell (`js_implicit_this_set`, declared extern "C"
since perry-runtime is only a dev-dependency here) to the server's JS value
— `handle_to_pointer_f64(server_handle)`, bit-identical to what
`createServer(...)` returns — for the duration of the callback, then
restores it. So `this === server` holds and `this.<method>()` dispatches to
the existing native server FFIs. Applied at the listen dispatch site in
server.rs (http), https_server.rs, and http2_server.rs.

Verified: the repro resolves `this === server` (was false) and
`this.address().port` (was a throw); test-http-request-large-payload flips
to PASS; deeper tests advance past the this.address() wall.

fix(object): enumerate own keys in OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys order (#2438) (#2452)

ECMA-262 OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys lists array-index keys (canonical
numeric strings "0".."2^32-2") first in ascending numeric order, then
the remaining string keys in insertion order. Perry kept a single
insertion-ordered keys array, so integer-index keys came out in
insertion order — diverging from Node for Object.keys / Object.values /
Object.entries / JSON.stringify / for-in.

Fix reorders at enumeration time (key storage stays insertion-ordered):

- New helpers in object/field_get_set.rs: `canonical_array_index`
  (canonical-index test), `ecma_own_key_order` (the slot permutation),
  and `keys_contain_array_index` (cheap predicate).
- js_object_keys / js_object_values / js_object_entries walk slots
  through the permutation so keys, values, and entries stay aligned.
- JSON.stringify (stringify_object_inner) reorders the emit loop;
  build_shape_prefix_template bails when array-index keys are present so
  the insertion-ordered shape-template fast path falls through to the
  reordered slow path (covers both single-object and array-of-objects).
- for-in is covered transitively (it desugars to Object.keys).

The common case (no array-index keys) is allocation-free: a cheap first
pass returns early, and each loop selects its slot index per-iteration
rather than materializing a positions vector.

Adds test_gap_2438_object_key_order.ts (byte-identical to Node).

feat(node:child_process): V8 'advanced' IPC serialization for fork() (#2130) (#2453)

`fork(module, args, { serialization: 'advanced' })` previously ignored the
`serialization` option — the IPC channel always used newline-delimited JSON, so
a Buffer/TypedArray sent over `child.send` arrived in the node child as a plain
object (`isBuf:false`) instead of a real Buffer. This implements Node's V8
structured-clone wire format on Perry's parent side so it interoperates with the
real `node` child a Perry `fork` launches.

- New `child_process/v8_serde.rs`: a V8 `ValueSerializer`/`ValueDeserializer`
  (format version 15) covering undefined/null/bool/int32/double, one- and
  two-byte strings, dense+sparse arrays, plain objects, Date, BigInt, Buffer and
  every TypedArray kind. Buffers/views use Node's child_process host-object
  framing (`\` + `0` view-discriminator + view-type-index + byte-length + raw
  bytes), verified byte-for-byte against `node`'s
  `internal/child_process/serialization.js` on-wire output. GC is suppressed for
  the codec window (as `JSON.parse` does) since the walk holds raw heap pointers
  across allocations.
- reactor: per-child `ipc_advanced` flag; `cp_ipc_send` frames advanced messages
  as `[u32 BE length][payload]`; a new length-prefixed IPC reader accumulates
  bytes and emits one message per complete frame (robust to a length field or
  payload split across socket reads, and to multiple frames coalesced in one
  read); `MessageAdvanced` events deserialize on the main thread.
- fork: reads `options.serialization`, sets `NODE_CHANNEL_SERIALIZATION_MODE` on
  the child (alongside the existing `NODE_CHANNEL_FD`), and threads the flag
  through `cp_register_live_child`.

Verified byte-for-byte vs `node --experimental-strip-types`: a new gap test
round-trips a Buffer, a 1000-byte buffer, and a mixed object (numbers, strings,
booleans, nested objects, arrays, Uint8Array) with full type fidelity in both
directions; a 50 KB buffer (payload split across reads) and a 20-message burst
(frames coalesced) also match. The existing `json`-mode fork (#1933) is
unchanged.

fix(hir+runtime): ES5 function constructors run their body and support instanceof (#2481)

A top-level `function Foo(){ this.x = … }` used as `new Foo()` lowered to
`Expr::New { class_name: "Foo" }`, but no class "Foo" exists, so codegen
produced an empty placeholder object and never ran the constructor body —
`new Foo().x` was `undefined` and `Object.keys(new Foo())` was empty.

Route top-level function constructors through `NewDynamic { FuncRef }` →
`js_new_function_construct`, which allocates the instance, binds `this`,
runs the body, and stamps a synthetic class id. Also make
`x instanceof Foo` work for those instances: lower a function-valued RHS
to a dynamic value and add a callable-closure branch to
`js_instanceof_dynamic` that derives the same synthetic class id.

Without the instanceof half, the ubiquitous
`if (!(this instanceof Foo)) return new Foo()` guard recursed forever and
stack-overflow-crashed (e.g. test262's Test262Error harness).

fix(runtime): route TypedArray/array-local lastIndexOf to the array path (#2457) (#2501)

`new Int32Array([1,2,3,2,1]).lastIndexOf(2)` threw
`TypeError: (number).lastIndexOf is not a function`, while `.indexOf` /
`.includes` worked. The HIR lowered `lastIndexOf` on a known-not-string /
typed-array local to the *string* `lastIndexOf` (`js_string_last_index_of`);
at runtime the typed-array pointer reads as a number, so the string
dispatch failed. `indexOf`/`includes` avoided this via dedicated
`Expr::ArrayIndexOf`/`ArrayIncludes` lowering — `lastIndexOf` had no
equivalent.

  * HIR (`local_array_methods`): emit it for a known-not-string / typed-array
    local, and add `lastIndexOf` to the ambiguous-method set so an
    *unknown*-typed local (which may be a string) still falls through to the
    string path.
  * Codegen (`misc_methods`): lower to `js_array_last_index_of_jsvalue`
    (value + optional fromIndex with the spec clamping), mirroring the
    `lower_array_method::lastIndexOf` arm.
  * Runtime (`array/search`): re-add the typed-array branch to
    `js_array_last_index_of_jsvalue` (now reached) — backward strict-equality
    scan over the typed store via `js_typed_array_get`.
  * Wire the new variant through the walkers, collectors, monomorph
    substitute, and stable-hash (exhaustive matches).

the array block). Verified byte-for-byte vs node: Int32Array/Float64Array

`lastIndexOf` all unchanged. Adds a `typed_array_last_index_of` unit test.

fix(compile): canonicalize exe so a symlinked perry finds the workspace (#2542)

find_perry_workspace_root() walks up from std::env::current_exe(), but on
a cargo/dev install perry is reached via a symlink (e.g.
~/.cargo/bin/perry -> .../target/release/perry). current_exe() returns the
symlink path on macOS, so the ../../ walk climbed the symlink's own
ancestors (~/.cargo/bin -> ~/.cargo -> ~), never reached the workspace,
and the compiler silently fell back to linking only libperry_runtime.a +
libperry_stdlib.a -- dropping every per-feature perry-ext-* lib. Any
program using a perry-ext-*-provided API (e.g. the node:http server) then
failed to link.

Canonicalize the exe before taking .parent() so a symlinked install
resolves to the real target/release/perry and the walk reaches the
workspace root. Also stop the per-ancestor canonicalize from aborting the
whole search (it used .ok()?, which skipped the cwd fallback when an
ancestor was missing); skip the bad ancestor instead.

Same class as #846, whose auto-optimize fix the symlink defeated.

fix(runtime): built-in prototype methods are non-enumerable (spec descriptor) (#2554)

`install_proto_method` stored every built-in prototype method
(Array/String/Number/Object/TypedArray/... .prototype.*) via the ordinary
field-set path, which defaults to { writable:true, enumerable:true,
configurable:true }. Per spec these are non-enumerable, so:

  Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Array.prototype, 'map').enumerable  // was true
  for (k in Array.prototype) ...                                      // yielded 42 methods
  Object.keys(Array.prototype)                                        // listed them

all disagreed with Node and failed Test262's pervasive verifyProperty checks.

Record a non-enumerable data-property descriptor at install time via a new
set_builtin_property_attrs helper that, like the #2060 builtin-accessor path,
inserts into PROPERTY_DESCRIPTORS WITHOUT flipping the process-wide
GLOBAL_DESCRIPTORS_IN_USE hot-path gate. getOwnPropertyDescriptor, Object.keys
and for-in each read PROPERTY_DESCRIPTORS per-object and unconditionally, so all
three now observe enumerable:false — while the object get/set hot path keeps
skipping the descriptor table for every program. Now matches Node:
`for (k in Array.prototype)` yields 0; `...map` descriptor is
{ writable:true, enumerable:false, configurable:true }.

fix(node:http): bind aliased/indirect createServer to native dispatch (#2533) (#2574)

* fix(node:http): bind aliased/indirect createServer to native dispatch (#2533)

`@hono/node-server`'s `serve()` does
`const createServer = options.createServer || createServerHTTP` and then
`createServer(opts, requestListener)`. When a `node:http` factory is reached
INDIRECTLY through a local binding (not a direct, statically-resolvable call),
Perry's codegen lowered the value-read to a non-function, so invoking it threw
`TypeError: value is not a function` at bind time — the precise blocker for the
"@hono/node-server works unchanged" path.

Root cause: a bare value-read of a native-module factory
(`Expr::PropertyGet { NativeModuleRef("http"), "createServer" }`) was not on the
`is_native_module_callable_export` whitelist, so it resolved to `undefined`
instead of a callable bound-method closure; even once whitelisted, the closure's
invocation had no dispatch arm reaching the perry-ext-http-server factories
(those impls can't be called directly from perry-runtime).

Fix:
- Whitelist `("http"/"https"/"http2", "createServer"/"Server"/"createSecureServer")`
  in `is_native_module_callable_export` so the value-read yields a bound-method
  closure (typeof === "function", matching Node).
- Add a `JS_NATIVE_HTTP_DISPATCH` hook (mirroring the crypto/zlib dispatchers):
  perry-stdlib registers `js_node_http_native_dispatch` under
  `external-http-server-pump` (auto-activated whenever http/https/http2 is
  imported), routing the bound-method invocation to the perry-ext-http-server
  `createServer` factories. The dispatcher classifies args by type (function ⇒
  handler, object ⇒ options) so both `createServer(handler)` and
  `createServer(options, handler)` orders work. Stays null (→ undefined) when the
  http ext crate isn't linked.

Scope mirrors #2153 (HttpServer dynamic dispatch): this resolves the bind path —
`createServer` no longer throws and the returned server supports
listen/address/close. Full request serving through the aliased path additionally
needs runtime dynamic dispatch for IncomingMessage/ServerResponse methods (a
follow-up, same as #2153 deferred for the typed path).

fix(compile): link perry-ext-* libs out-of-the-box (no workspace source) (#2532) (#2713)

An out-of-tree install (any checkout that isn't this repo) cannot rebuild
perry-stdlib with a stripped feature set, so `build_optimized_libs`
returned `OptimizedLibs::empty()` and only `libperry_runtime.a` +
`libperry_stdlib.a` were linked. The `perry-ext-*` host functions — most
visibly `node:http`'s server, which lives in perry-ext-http /
perry-ext-http-server and is not a perry-stdlib dependency — were never
linked, so a bare `createServer(...).listen(...)` failed with
`Undefined symbols: _js_node_http_create_server_with_options`.

Changes:

- optimized_libs.rs: when `find_perry_workspace_root()` is None, resolve
  the prebuilt `libperry_ext_*.a` a program needs (from the well-known
  bindings the program imports) via the existing library search
  (PERRY_LIB_DIR / PERRY_RUNTIME_DIR, exe dir, Homebrew ../lib) and add
  them to the link line. Dormant in-tree (workspace path unchanged).

- perry-runtime: add an auxiliary pump / has-active registry
  (`js_register_aux_pump` / `js_register_aux_has_active`), drained each
  tick from `js_run_stdlib_pump` / `js_stdlib_has_active_handles`. The
  prebuilt full stdlib has the `external-*-pump` cfg arms compiled out, so
  without this the linked ext server would accept connections nobody
  dispatches and hang. Registration is idempotent, so the in-tree
  compile-time arm calling the same function is a harmless no-op.

- perry-ext-http / perry-ext-http-server: register their client / server
  pumps with the runtime on first use (in `ensure_gc_scanner_registered`).

- ext_registry.rs: register `js_node_http_create_server_with_options` —
  the symbol codegen actually emits for `http.createServer` — as
  WellKnown("http"). The pre-rename `js_node_http_create_server` never
  matched the emitted symbol, so the compiled-package owner-detection
  backup (no `import "node:http"`) silently no-op'd.

- release-packages.yml: build + stage `libperry_ext_*.a` next to the
  runtime/stdlib libs so installs actually ship them.

Validated end-to-end by compiling + running an http server from a
simulated out-of-tree install (binary + libs in /tmp, no `crates/`
reachable): it links, listens, and dispatches. The in-tree workspace
path still compiles, links, and dispatches unchanged.

feat(node:util): getSystemErrorName/Message/Map (#2514) (#2714)

Implements the libuv-style errno helpers (subset of #2514):
- `util.getSystemErrorName(err)` → e.g. `-2` → "ENOENT".
- `util.getSystemErrorMessage(err)` → e.g. `-2` → "no such file or directory".
- `util.getSystemErrorMap()` → `Map<number, [name, message]>`.

These mirror libuv's error table (what Node exposes), NOT libc — the messages
are libuv's lowercase phrasings (`EEXIST` → "file already exists", not libc's
"File exists"; `EISDIR` → "illegal operation on a directory") and the *set* is
libuv's `UV_ERRNO_MAP`, so codes libuv doesn't map (e.g. darwin `EINPROGRESS`)
return "Unknown system error -N" just like Node.

New `crates/perry-runtime/src/util_syserr.rs` (fresh file, low conflict
surface) carries two sub-tables for cross-platform correctness: errno-backed
codes use the host `libc::E*` value (correct negative key on darwin *and*
linux) with libuv's platform-independent message; libuv-internal codes
(`EAI_*`, `UNKNOWN`, `EOF`, …) use libuv's fixed negative keys. The entry list
+ messages were taken verbatim from Node's `getSystemErrorMap()`.

Verified byte-for-byte vs node (v25, darwin): name/message for mapped +
unmapped codes, libuv-internal codes, and `getSystemErrorMap()` — `instanceof
Map`, `size === 85`, and entry values. Adds a unit test +
`test-parity/node-suite/util/get-system-error.ts`.

Remaining #2514 helpers (debuglog/styleText/parseEnv/toUSVString/diff/…) are
unaffected.

feat(node:util): implement parseEnv (#2514) (#2739)

`util.parseEnv(content)` parses `.env`-format text into a plain object,
mirroring Node's built-in parser:
- skip blank and `#`-comment lines; strip an optional `export ` prefix;
- split on the first `=`, trim key + value;
- quoted values (`"`, `'`, backtick) keep their inner content — double-quoted
  values process `\n`/`\t`/`\r`/`\\`/`\"` escapes and treat `#` literally;
- unquoted values drop an inline `# comment`;
- last duplicate key wins;
- keys come out byte-lexicographically **sorted** (Node's C++ parser uses a
  sorted map — `A`,`M`,`Z`,`m`, not insertion order).

New `crates/perry-runtime/src/util_parse_env.rs` (fresh file, minimal hot-file
surface). Verified byte-for-byte vs node (v25) across 13 cases incl. inline
comments, `#`-in-quotes, `export`, escapes, `=`-in-value, dup keys, and
multi-key sort order. Adds a unit test + `test-parity/node-suite/util/parse-env.ts`.

feat(node:process): populate allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags Set (#2589) (#3161)

process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags previously lowered to an empty Set
(Expr::SetNew). Node exposes it as a non-empty, read-only Set of the
flags accepted from NODE_OPTIONS / the V8 environment, and consumers
feature-detect on it being a real Set (instanceof Set, .size > 0,
.has("--no-warnings"), iteration).

Add a process_allowed_node_flags_literal() helper that materialises the
property as a Set populated with a Node-compatible flag list (via
Expr::SetNewFromArray, which builds a genuine Set so all Set methods,
instanceof Set, .size, and iteration work), and route both process.*
call sites in expr_member.rs through it. The exact membership varies by
Node build, so the gap test asserts only the stable structural contract.

Closes #2589.

fix(runtime): restore default auto-optimize compile via keepalive anchors (#3320)

The default `perry file.ts -o out` flow (auto-optimize on) was broken on main:
linking failed with 'Undefined symbols for architecture arm64' for
_js_write_barrier_root_nanbox, _js_write_barrier_root_heap_word, and
_js_array_join_value. Any program with module-level string variables (barrier-
root calls emitted in __perry_init_strings) or an arr.join(sep) call could not
compile.

Root cause: #2345 added the two js_write_barrier_root_* entry points and made
codegen emit them with no symbol-retention anchor; js_array_join_value has the
same exposure. These #[no_mangle] functions are called only from generated code,
so while the default .a staticlib keeps them via export semantics, the
auto-optimize whole-program-bitcode rebuild internalizes and dead-strips them.
PR CI missed it because compile-smoke is tag-gated, not run on PRs.

Fix: add #[used] keepalive anchors (KEEP_* statics holding the function
pointers) mirroring node_stream_keepalive.rs / typedarray.rs, so all three
survive every link mode. Verified by clearing the perry-auto-* cache and
compiling+running representative programs with auto-optimize on.
