fix(node:assert): validate AssertionError options + generate default message (#3034) (#3345)

`new assert.AssertionError(options)` now matches Node:

- A missing/null/primitive `options` throws
  `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` ("The \"options\" argument must be of
  type object. Received ...") instead of silently constructing an instance
  from an empty bag.
- When `message` is omitted, the default is the comparison summary
  `<actual> <operator> <expected>` (each rendered via String(), so absent
  operands/operator become "undefined") with `generatedMessage: true`,
  e.g. `{}` -> "undefined undefined undefined" and
  `{actual:1,expected:2,operator:"==="}` -> "1 === 2". Previously the
  message defaulted to just the operator string ("===").
- An absent `operator` surfaces as `undefined` rather than "" (the
  assert.* helpers always pass a non-empty operator, so only the
  direct-construction path is affected).

Verified byte-for-byte against `node --experimental-strip-types` over the
issue's full case surface (parity test added).

fix(string): coerce missing/undefined/NaN char index to 0 (#2787) (#3131)

String.charAt/charCodeAt/codePointAt/at rejected omitted arguments and
lowered the index through fptosi(DOUBLE -> I32), which is undefined
behavior on a NaN bit pattern (undefined/NaN). Per JS ToIntegerOrInfinity,
a missing/undefined/NaN index must coerce to 0.

Add js_string_index_to_i32 (NaN -> 0, truncate toward zero, clamp to i32)
and route all four char-access methods through it, defaulting a missing
argument to 0. The runtime helpers already return the correct
out-of-bounds shapes for integer indices (charAt -> "", charCodeAt ->
NaN, codePointAt/at -> undefined, at negative -> relative).

fix(string): ToUint16 fromCharCode + fromCodePoint RangeError (#2788) (#3174)

String.fromCharCode now coerces each argument with ToUint16, so negative
and out-of-range values wrap modulo 65536 (e.g. -1 -> U+FFFF) instead of
returning "". String.fromCodePoint throws RangeError for negative,
non-integer, and > 0x10FFFF code points instead of silently returning "".
Zero-argument static calls return "".

Both helpers now take the raw NaN-boxed f64 (codegen drops the fptosi that
was UB on a NaN and truncated 3.14 -> 3) so the wrap / validation is
observable in the runtime. RangeError message matches Node
("Invalid code point <n>").

* fix(fetch): honor Response.json() init status/statusText/headers (#2638)

Response.json(data, init) now honors the optional init argument's status,
statusText, and headers, matching Node's WHATWG Response.json factory.
Previously init was dropped: every Response.json(...) had status 200, empty
statusText, and only the default content-type: application/json.

The runtime helper js_response_static_json is widened identically in BOTH
crates that define it (perry-stdlib/src/fetch/mod.rs and
perry-ext-fetch/src/lib.rs) to (value, init_status, init_status_text_ptr,
headers_handle): init_status NaN/0 -> 200; init_status_text used verbatim or
"" (Node does not derive statusText from the status code for this factory);
user headers applied first with content-type defaulted only if unset.

Codegen (lower_call/options/fetch.rs) now mirrors the new Response(body, init)
extraction path to pull status/statusText/headers from the init object literal,
and the extern decl in runtime_decls/strings.rs is updated to the 4-arg
signature. Default Response.json(data) is unchanged.

Adds gap test test-files/test_gap_fetch_response_json_init.ts (byte-identical
to node --experimental-strip-types).

* fix(ext-fetch): use HEADERS_HANDLES registry in js_response_static_json

ext-fetch stores headers in HEADERS_HANDLES, not HEADERS_REGISTRY (the
stdlib name). The #2638 init-headers change referenced the stdlib symbol,
breaking the perry-ext-fetch build.

* test(ext-fetch): update js_response_static_json call to 4-arg init signature

fix(runtime): don't count caught throws toward the throw circuit-breaker (#3511)

The #922 throw_not_callable anti-runaway guard counted every
"value is not a function" throw and aborted the process at 100k,
regardless of whether the throw was caught. Valid JS that throws-and-
catches a non-callable many times (route handlers, retry loops, the

reaches an open try (try_depth > 0) — a caught throw is not a runaway.
Genuinely uncaught runaways still exit(1) on the try_depth == 0 path,
and the async-step guards in promise/microtasks.rs still bound async
re-entry.

fix(codegen): guard closure display-name registration on materialized closures (#3527) (#3537)

Branch (c) of display-name emission in `emit_module_artifacts` iterated all
of `hir.closure_display_names` and emitted a `js_register_function_name`
call for every entry, without checking the closure was actually materialized
as a `@perry_closure_*` LLVM global. A named function expression assigned to
an unbound target (e.g. `module.exports = function sign(){}`) records a
display name at lower time, but CJS export lowering materializes a different
func_id for the function — leaving the original fid stale. Registering a name
for the stale fid emitted a call referencing an undefined `@perry_closure_*`
global, so `clang -c` failed with "use of undefined value".

Guard branch (c) on the materialized closure set (the `closures` slice that
`compile_closure` already iterates) so stale display-name entries are
skipped. Branches (a) and (b) were already safe — they use `__perry_wrap_*`
symbols and `Stmt::Let`-bound closures, which are always materialized.

Regression class of #318/#343 (the collector walk itself is exhaustive; this
is a registration/materialization mismatch, not a missing collector arm).

On the Express dependency tree this drops clang codegen failures from 49 to 1
(the remaining one is an unrelated high-arity indirect-call limit in qs).

fix(node:fs): propagate rename/copyFile/link/symlink/truncate errors (#3541)

The void fs mutators rename/copyFile/link/symlink and path-based truncate
collapsed std/libc errors to a 0/1 status sentinel, and the callback and
promise wrappers discarded that status — so failures (missing source,
missing destination parent, existing destination, EISDIR/EACCES on
truncate) looked like successful no-ops.

Each op now has a shared `*_result() -> Result<(), f64>` helper that builds
a Node-shaped fs error. The sync FFI throws it, the callback wrapper passes
it to cb(err), and the promise thunk rejects with it. Two-path ops carry
`code`/`syscall`/`path`/`dest` via a new dest side table + `.dest` getter;
truncate carries `code`/`syscall: open`/`path`. Dangling symlink targets
still succeed (Node behavior).

fix(codegen): support indirect/closure calls with more than 16 args (#3527) (#3543)

Indirect calls (callee resolved via a local holding a closure, e.g. a
recursive named function expression that references itself) were capped at
16 args: `try_lower_closure_call_fallthrough` only handled `args.len() <= 16`
via the per-arity `js_closure_call0..16` helpers, then returned `Ok(None)`,
so `lower_call` bailed with "Call callee shape not supported (LocalGet) with
N args". qs's `stringify` declares 18 params and self-calls with 18 args,
which made the qs package fail to compile.

Codegen: route calls with >16 args through the existing variadic
`js_closure_call_array(closure, args_ptr, argc)`, marshaling args into an
entry-block `[N x double]` stack alloca (same pattern as the native-call
path). Declare `js_closure_call_array`'s args pointer as PTR (ABI-identical
to I64) so an alloca can be passed directly. The <=16 fast path is unchanged.

Runtime: `js_closure_call_array`'s catch-all arm previously delegated to
`js_closure_call16`, silently dropping args past index 15. Replace it with a
full-slice dispatch through the strategy resolver (registered call / rest /
declared arity) so the body receives ALL its args. `dispatch_with_arity`
only had concrete transmute arms up to 8 (returning `undefined` above that),
which would have mis-called an 18-arg body; extend it to 32 via an `arm!`
macro so dynamically-dispatched high-arity closures call their real
N-arg signature.

Verified: 18- and 20-arg recursive self-calls now compile and return the
correct numeric results (no dropped args); 3- and 16-arg calls unchanged.
On the Express tree this clears the last codegen failure
(`qs/lib/stringify.js`) after the closure-display-name fix (#3537).

fix(node:http2): implement settings packing helpers (#3168) (#3548)

Add Node-compatible `http2.getDefaultSettings()`, `getPackedSettings()`,
and `getUnpackedSettings()`.

These are pure functions, but they must live in `perry-ext-http-server`
(the crate that owns the HTTP/2 surface) rather than `perry-runtime`,
because `getPackedSettings` returns a `Buffer` and `getUnpackedSettings`
reads one. An earlier `perry-runtime` attempt hit a staticlib
thread-local divergence: importing `node:http2` links `perry-ext-http`,
which bundles its own runtime copy, so the buffer-registry lookups split
across copies (returned Buffers were unrecognized, input Buffers failed
the registry check). Routing Buffer alloc/recognition through the
`perry-ffi` extern shims keeps those lookups in the one runtime copy the
program-side dispatch resolves to.

  `.code` + throw in one extern, so registration and the `.code` read
  resolve through the same runtime copy) and `js_value_buffer_or_typedarray_data`
  (registry-safe byte reader for Buffer/TypedArray). Both pinned with
  `#[used]` anchors since they are referenced only from the prebuilt ext
  archive.
- perry-ffi: `throw_with_code` / `value_byte_slice` / `ErrorKind` wrappers.
- perry-ext-http-server: the three helpers, dispatched via the existing
  http2 NativeModSig path; getDefaultSettings/getUnpackedSettings return
  JSON reparsed via NR_OBJ_FROM_JSON_STR, getPackedSettings returns a
  Buffer via NR_PTR.
- perry-codegen: NativeModSig rows, FFI decls, ext-registry entries.
- perry-ext-http: force-link anchors for the new symbols.

fix(compile): honor "*"/"@scope/*" wildcard in perry.compilePackages routing (#3527) (#3551)

The `"*"` (and `"@scope/*"`) wildcard in `perry.compilePackages` passed the
#497 *trust* gate (`allowlist_matches` honors it) but was a silent no-op for
compile *routing*: `is_in_compile_package`, the HIR `COMPILE_PACKAGES_OVERRIDE`
lookup, and every `compile_packages.contains(name)` site match exact package
names, so a literal `"*"` left every dependency routed to the removed JS
runtime — strictly worse than naming each package. This is blocker #4 of the
Express-compile inventory (#3527).

Fix: expand the wildcard into concrete installed package names at config-load
time. `enumerate_installed_packages` walks the project node_modules tree
(flat deps, `@scope/pkg`, and non-hoisted transitive deps under nested
node_modules), and `apply_pkg_and_toml_config` materializes `"*"`/`"@scope/*"`
into those names before the #497 check and routing. This also removes the need
to hand-enumerate every transitive dependency (the Express tree is 65 packages).

Verified: with `compilePackages: ["*"]` + `allow.compilePackages: ["*"]`, the
Express 5.2.1 app routes 129 modules as 129 native / 0 JavaScript — identical
to the hand-enumerated 65-package config — and compiles to a native binary
(with the documented eval/unimplemented escape hatches). Unit test covers
flat/scoped/nested enumeration and skipping of npm bookkeeping dirs.

fix(runtime): spec-correct own name/length descriptors on builtin constructors (#3655) (#3715)

Built-in *constructors* (Date, Map, Set, RegExp, ArrayBuffer, DataView,
BigInt, Promise, the native errors, the TypedArray constructors, …) now
carry spec-correct own `name`/`length` data properties — observable through
the full property protocol, not just the compile-time `Ctor.name`/`.length`
folds that #3143 added.

Before, a constructor read as a value (`const C = DataView; C.name`) reported
`name === ""` and `length === 0` (the shared no-op thunk can't carry a name
via the func-ptr registry), and the reflection helpers either returned the
wrong thing or read `keys_array` off a closure out of bounds.

Changes (perry-runtime):
- global_this.rs: register every constructor closure's spec name +
  `builtin_constructor_spec_length(name)` arity, plus the
  `{writable:false, enumerable:false, configurable:true}` attrs.
- has_own_helpers.rs: central `closure_own_key_present(ptr, key)` — `name`
  and `length` are always own (constructors also own `prototype`); deleted
  slots and user props are honored.
- object_ops.rs: `Object.hasOwn` / `propertyIsEnumerable` closure arms.
- native_call_method.rs: `obj.hasOwnProperty(k)` / `propertyIsEnumerable(k)`
  method + `.call` arms now answer correctly for closures (previously fell
  through to an unconditional `true`).
- descriptors.rs: `getOwnPropertyNames` lists `length, name, …, prototype`
  for closures; `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` honors deletes.
- delete_rest.rs: `delete fn.name` etc. records the deletion (configurable:true).
- field_get_set.rs: value reads honor deletes.
- closure/dynamic_props.rs: deleted-key side table (GC-rekeyed on move) +
  `closure_has_own_dynamic_prop` / `closure_delete_own_dynamic_prop`.

The `in` operator already delegates to the closure value-read path, so it
follows automatically.

Adds a byte-for-byte parity test exercising getOwnPropertyDescriptor,
hasOwnProperty (method + direct `.call`), propertyIsEnumerable, for-in,
getOwnPropertyNames, the `in` operator, and delete across a spread of
constructor arities, plus a user-function control.

Note: test262's `verifyProperty` reaches these through
`Function.prototype.call.bind(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty)` (the
uncurry-this idiom), which is a separate reification gap (returns `undefined`
even for plain objects) tracked separately; the direct `.call`/method forms
this PR fixes are the spec-equivalent path.

fix(runtime,codegen): make Object.hasOwn a real first-class value (#3527) (#3751)

`Object.hasOwn` worked as a direct call but not as a first-class value:
`typeof Object.hasOwn` folded to "function", yet reading the value (e.g. to
store it in a variable and call it indirectly) produced the `0.0`/undefined
sentinel — a non-callable. The const-alias call-fold (`const k = Object.hasOwn;
k(o, x)`) hid this, but iconv-lite's `merge-exports.js` assigns it through a
ternary into a `var`:

    var hasOwn = typeof Object.hasOwn === "undefined"
      ? Function.call.bind(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty)
      : Object.hasOwn
    ...
    if (hasOwn(module, key)) target[key] = module[key]

The ternary defeats the fold, so `hasOwn` held a non-callable and
`hasOwn(module, key)` threw `TypeError: value is not a function` during
iconv-lite init — a hard blocker compiling Express (#3527).

Two parts:
- Runtime: reify `Object.hasOwn` as a callable static on the `Object`
  constructor closure (`object_hasown_thunk` → `js_object_has_own`), alongside
  the existing `keys`/`values`/`assign`/… thunks. This makes the rebound form
  (`const O = Object; O.hasOwn(o, x)`) dispatch correctly.
- Codegen: when `Object.hasOwn` is read as a VALUE (`PropertyGet { GlobalGet(0),
  "hasOwn" }`), resolve the reified `Object` constructor closure and read the
  `hasOwn` static off it — mirroring the existing `Error.captureStackTrace`
  value path — instead of emitting the `0.0` sentinel.

Now `typeof Object.hasOwn === "function"`, and the value computes correctly
whether called directly, stored in a var, passed through an array, or rebound.
The Express compile advances past iconv-lite's merge-exports. Coverage added to
test_gap_object_methods.ts (byte-identical to Node).

The broader "Object.keys/values/… as escaping values" gap is unchanged and
remains a known limitation; this fixes the ES2022 `hasOwn` case that Express's
dependency tree actually exercises.

fix(hir): resolve bare `eval` as a value instead of ReferenceError (#3527) (#3776)

`expr_call::intrinsics::check_eval_function_call` classifies the eval surface

eval-removal gate still applies — only the value read changes.

fix(hir): infer `bool && value` as the value's type, not Boolean (#3527) (#3771)

`infer_type_from_expr` typed a logical `A && B` / `A || B` as A's type
whenever B inferred to `Any`. But `&&` yields B's value when A is truthy, so
the result can be the (unknown) right value — A's type is wrong. This mistyped
a common idiom:

    var hasMap = typeof Map === "function" && Map.prototype;  // → Boolean (!)

`hasMap` holds an object at runtime but was typed `Boolean`, so codegen treated
it as a boolean in a later `hasMap && d && typeof d.get === "function"` chain
(object-inspect's Map-size feature-detect), miscompiling the short-circuit and
dereferencing `null` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading
'get')` while compiling Express (#3527).

Fix: when the right operand is `Any`, the logical result is `Any` (the value
could be that right operand), not the left operand's type. The concrete-right
heuristic (`x && knownTyped` → knownTyped) is unchanged. This only makes the
inferred type more dynamic (always codegen-safe), never less.

Verified: object-inspect's init works; the Express tree advances past it.

fix(cjs): make module/exports reassignable so `var module = X` works (#3527) (#3764)

The CJS→ESM wrapper declared `const module = { exports: {} }` and
`const exports = module.exports`. A CJS body that rebinds either —
`var module = X`, `module = X`, or `exports = X` — silently failed: the
reassignment collided with the `const` and was dropped, so reads still saw the
wrapper's object. iconv-lite's `encodings/index.js` does exactly this:

    for (var i = 0; i < modules.length; i++) {
      var module = modules[i]
      mergeModules(exports, module)   // reads module.<key> → undefined
    }

`module` stayed the wrapper object (no `cesu8`), so `module[key]` read
`undefined`, throwing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cesu8')`
during init — a hard blocker compiling Express (#3527).

In Node, `module`/`exports` are wrapper-function *parameters*, freely
reassignable; rebinding the local is harmless because Node reads the real
exports from its own module reference. Mirror that: introduce a stable
`__cjs_module` (read back by `return __cjs_module.exports`) and make `module`
and `exports` reassignable `var`s aliasing it. A body reassigning its `module`
local can no longer clobber what the module exports, and `var module = X` now
binds as expected.

Verified: the iconv-shape repro and the Express tree advance past it; normal
`module.exports = X`, `exports.foo = …`, and `module.exports.bar = …` are
unchanged. Unit test asserts the reassignable-var + stable-ref wrapper shape.

fix(runtime): make Function.prototype.call.bind(method) uncurry-this work (#3716) (#3846)

Reading `.bind`/`.call`/`.apply` as a *value* off a function previously
returned `undefined`, and the special-cased `call.bind(target)` produced a
bound function that never applied the bound `this` (the target method). The
"uncurry-this" idiom `Function.prototype.call.bind(method)` therefore yielded
`undefined` even for plain objects.

1. field_get_set: reading `.bind`/`.call`/`.apply` off any closure now reifies
   a BOUND_METHOD closure bound to that function as receiver, so the value is a
   real callable (typeof "function") that routes back through
   js_native_call_method.

2. js_native_call_value: a built-in prototype method invoked *as a value*
   (backed by the shared no-op thunk) is re-dispatched by name through
   js_native_call_method using IMPLICIT_THIS as the receiver, instead of
   silently no-op'ing to undefined. Gated on a recorded built-in .length so
   bare no-op-backed global constructors are excluded.

This is the exact shape test262's harness/propertyHelper.js uses
(`Function.prototype.call.bind(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty)` etc.), so it
unblocks the verifyProperty-based slice of the suite.

fix(runtime): guard hasOwnProperty against misaligned non-object receivers (#3527) (#3733)

Compiling a standard Express app (with the documented eval/unimplemented
escape hatches) SIGBUS'd during module init, before any user code ran.
Root cause: `own_key_present` (backing `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty`)
dereferenced a GcHeader at `[ptr-8]` on a value that isn't a real GC object.

Two shapes hit it: (a) a misaligned receiver pointer, and (b) a real-looking
object whose `keys_array` field held misaligned garbage — the value read when
a native-module namespace sentinel (`require('buffer')` in safer-buffer's
`for (key in buffer) { if (!buffer.hasOwnProperty(key)) … }`) is mis-treated
as an object. The existing guards checked null / `< 0x10000` / upper-bits but
not alignment, so a garbage address like `0x280000203` slipped through to the
`[keys-8]` header read → EXC_BAD_ACCESS.

Every GC allocation is `align.max(8)`-aligned, so a genuine object pointer
always has its low 3 bits clear. Add that invariant as a guard in:
- `extract_obj_ptr`'s raw-I64-pointer fallback (root: stops a misaligned
  non-object value from being handed out as an ObjectHeader at all), and
- `own_key_present`'s receiver and `keys_array` checks (defense at the deref
  sites, since the crash reached it via a caller that bypasses extract_obj_ptr).

A non-object receiver now correctly returns `false` (a non-object has no own
properties) instead of crashing. With this, the Express app advances past the
init SIGBUS. Regression test covers both misaligned shapes.

fix(runtime): implement Proxy apply/construct trap dispatch (#3656) (#3875)

* fix(runtime): implement Proxy apply/construct trap dispatch (#3656)

Implements the Proxy [[Call]] and [[Construct]] exotic behaviors per spec:

- Trap absent / undefined / null → forward the operation to the target
  (recursing through proxy targets), threading thisArg for [[Call]] and
  newTarget for [[Construct]].
- Trap present but not callable → TypeError (a present-but-non-function
  trap like `apply: {}` no longer falls through as a silent no-op).
- Trap present → Call(trap, handler, «target, thisArg, argArray») for apply
  and «target, argArray, newTarget» for construct, with the handler bound as
  the trap's `this`. The construct trap's result must be an Object, else
  TypeError (symbols are primitives and rejected).

Removes the old pragmatic "trap returned undefined → call the target anyway"
fallback in js_proxy_apply, which broke traps that legitimately return
undefined or a custom value without calling the target.

Routing fixes so the new dispatch is actually reached:
- p.call(thisArg, ...) / p.apply(thisArg, args) on a proxy now route through
  the proxy's [[Call]] (apply trap) with thisArg bound, instead of reading
  `.call`/`.apply` off the forwarded target and invoking the target directly.
  Handled both at codegen (ProxyGet("call"|"apply") callee) and in the runtime
  Function.prototype.call/apply arms.
- A proxy value invoked as a function or constructor through the generic
  value-call / dynamic-new paths (e.g. `record.proxy()` off Proxy.revocable)
  now dispatches to js_proxy_apply / js_proxy_construct instead of reading the
  encoded proxy id as a closure pointer and segfaulting.

Threads newTarget through Reflect.construct's 3rd argument (new field on
Expr::ReflectConstruct) so forwarded construct traps observe the right
NewTarget.

fix: run real Hono apps natively (regex char-class, destructured-param mutability, ReadableStream Response body) (#3971)

* fix(regex): accept a literal '[' inside a character class

`js_regex_to_rust` passed JS character classes straight to the Rust
`regex` crate, which — unlike JS (no `v` flag) — rejects a bare `[`
inside `[...]`. So `/[[]/`, valid in JS and accepted by Node, failed to
construct with "invalid pattern".

Hono's RegExpRouter escapes path segments with `/[.\\+*[^\]$()]/g`, which
contains a literal `[`, so every Hono app threw on its first request.

Track whether we're inside a class and escape an unescaped `[` to `\[`
when we are. Escaped `\[`/`\]` already flow through the backslash arm and
don't toggle class state. Verified: `/[[]/`, `new RegExp("[[]")`, and the
full Hono escape pattern now construct and `.source` round-trips the
original JS text.

* fix(hir): bind destructured function parameters as mutable

`generate_param_destructuring_stmts` lowered array/object parameter
patterns via `lower_pattern_binding(.., false)`, marking the extracted
locals immutable (const). But function parameters are mutable bindings
(like `let`), and JS lets you reassign a destructured param:

    const f = ([a, b]) => { b -= 1; return b; };

That threw "Assignment to constant variable 'b'" at runtime. The bug hit
Hono's RegExpRouter, which does `handlers.map(([h, paramCount]) => { …
paramCount -= 1; for (; paramCount >= 0; paramCount--) … })`.

Pass `true` so destructured params are mutable — matching the function's
own doc comment, which already describes the output as `let a = param[0]`.
Verified with array- and object-destructured params reassigned via `-=`
and `--`.

* fix(fetch): drain a ReadableStream body in the Response constructor

`new Response(body, init)` lowered the body via `get_raw_string_ptr`,
which stringifies any value. A ReadableStream handle (e.g. another
Response's `.body`) is a plain numeric f64 id allocated from 0x40000 with
no NaN-box tag, so it was coerced to its number ("262144") and stored as
the literal body — the real bytes were dropped.

Hono mutates response headers after `next()` via
`c.res = new Response(c.res.body, c.res)`, so every response that passed
through a header-touching middleware came out with a corrupt body (and,
once read as a stream downstream, surfaced as a bare thrown Symbol()).

Add `js_response_body_init_ptr` (in `fetch/dispatch.rs`, the untyped Web
Fetch dispatch module, to keep `fetch/mod.rs` under the 2,000-line gate):
if the body value is a live readable stream (id in [0x40000,0x100000) and
`js_stream_handle_kind == 1`), drain its buffered chunks via the existing
`drain_readable_into_bytes` and use those bytes; otherwise fall back to
the normal string coercion, so plain `c.json`/`c.text` bodies are
unaffected. Codegen routes the Response body through it. Verified:
`new Response(orig.body, orig)` now yields the original bytes; `.clone()`
and string bodies still work.

fix(json): materialize SSO short strings before JSON.parse (#3980)

`JSON.parse(s)` lowered the operand with `unbox_to_i64`, which extracts the
raw NaN-boxed bits. For a heap string that's the `StringHeader*` (fine), but
for an SSO short string it's the INLINE character bytes — handed to
`js_json_parse`, which dereferences them as a `*StringHeader` and reads
`byte_len` off a garbage address → SIGSEGV.

So any short, runtime-built string crashed: `JSON.parse('e' + 'n')`,
`JSON.parse('enabled'.slice(0,2))`, `JSON.parse(String(1))`, etc. Heap strings
(string literals, large concatenations) happened to work, which is why it hid
until a real workload parsed many short values — e.g. @perryts/mysql decodes a
JSON column and the consumer re-`JSON.parse`s the short results, segfaulting a
whole HTTP service.

Lower both the generic and typed (`js_json_parse_typed_array`) arms through
`js_get_string_pointer_unified`, which returns the heap pointer for heap
strings and materializes SSO / number receivers to the heap first. Verified:
`JSON.parse('e'+'n')` now throws a catchable SyntaxError instead of crashing;
short valid inputs (`'1'`, `'42'`, `'true'`) parse correctly.

fix(instanceof): support Response/Request/Headers/Blob fetch handles (#3978)

`new Response(...) instanceof Response` returned `false` (likewise Request,
Headers, Blob). These WHATWG fetch types are represented as pointer-tagged
small-integer stdlib handles, not heap objects with a prototype chain, so
`js_instanceof` rejected them at the small-handle guard and fell through to
`false`.

Hono's SmartRouter guards its route-fallback with `res instanceof Response`,
and the admin gate redirects with `if (auth instanceof Response) return auth`
— so a `false` here skipped the guard and read `.id` off the redirect
Response, crashing every protected admin page.

Follow the existing Web-Streams/EventEmitter handle-probe pattern: add a
`fetch_handle_kind_probe` (0=none,1=Response,2=Request,3=Headers,4=Blob) that
the stdlib registers at init from the fetch registries, reserved class ids
0xFFFF0028/29/2A (+ existing 0xFFFF0026 for Blob), an `instanceof` arm that
consults the probe for those ids, and codegen name→class-id mappings. Verified
`new Response()/Request()/Headers() instanceof` resolve true and don't
cross-match (Response is not a Request).

fix(modules): promote `Symbol()` locals exported via `export { X }` (#3999)

`const X = Symbol(); export { X }` did not preserve the symbol's identity
across modules: an importer received a DIFFERENT symbol than the defining
module's binding, so `imported === X` was false.

Cause: the `is_exportable` allowlist that promotes an `export { name }` local
to a shared module-global (so importers route through the value getter instead
of a closure-pointer wrapper) listed `Expr::SymbolFor` but not plain
`Expr::SymbolNew`. So `Symbol.for(...)` worked (added for drizzle's
`entityKind`) but unregistered `Symbol()` did not — the local stayed
module-private and each importer got its own value.

Hono's RegExpRouter is built on exactly this shape:
`var PATH_ERROR = Symbol(); … export { PATH_ERROR }`, and its SmartRouter
fallback guards with `throw e === PATH_ERROR ? new UnsupportedPathError : e`.
Under Perry that `===` was false, so instead of falling back to TrieRouter the
bare `PATH_ERROR` symbol escaped `app.fetch` and every request 500'd once a
route the RegExpRouter can't represent was registered.

Add `Expr::SymbolNew(_)` to the allowlist. Verified: `var X = Symbol();
export { X }` now compares equal across a module boundary, and a real Hono app
(Skelpo CMS) serves correctly on the stock default `SmartRouter` — no
TrieRouter workaround.

fix(runtime): Buffer no longer misidentified as a Date cell in property reads (#4003) (#4008)

gunzipSync(c).length/.byteLength returned undefined for a bound-local
Buffer input, while indexing/toString/isBuffer/Buffer.byteLength worked.

Root cause: Buffers are raw-alloc'd WITHOUT a GcHeader, but
date::is_date_cell_addr read the word at addr-GC_HEADER_SIZE and compared
it to GC_TYPE_DATE_CELL, assuming every pointer has a valid GC header. For
some buffer addresses (the first gunzipSync result) that adjacent word
coincidentally held the DATE_CELL tag, so js_object_get_field_by_name took
its Date branch and returned undefined for .length/.byteLength. Call-ordinal/
address-dependent, which masqueraded as a GC stale-ref.

Fix: is_date_cell_addr now confirms !is_registered_buffer(addr) before
reporting a Date cell (a registered buffer is never a DateCell). The lookup
runs only in the rare tag-match case, so the non-Date hot path is unchanged;
hardens every caller incl. is_date_value.

Verified vs node: gunzipSync .length/.byteLength -> 11 for all calls; Date
reads unchanged; date (21) + buffer (41) unit tests green.

fix(diagnostics_channel): drop non-Node withStoreScope; null bindStore transform throws (#4029)

Two node:diagnostics_channel store-subsystem parity fixes (epic #3839):

1. withStoreScope removed. Node's Channel prototype is exactly {subscribe,
   unsubscribe, publish, bindStore, unbindStore, runStores, hasSubscribers} --
   there is no withStoreScope. Perry registered one, so typeof
   ch.withStoreScope was "function" (Node: "undefined") and
   using scope = ch.withStoreScope(...) ran a block instead of throwing.
   Dropped the registration; the unwired helper is retained #[allow(dead_code)].

2. null transform is non-callable. bindStore(store, null) classified null as
   the no-transform case (like undefined), so runStores passed data straight
   into the store. Node (v25.x) treats a null (or any non-callable,
   non-undefined) transform as a function call that throws
   TypeError: transform is not a function when runStores invokes it, leaving
   the store unset. Narrowed StoreTransform::None to only undefined; null and
   other non-callables now map to NonCallable.

Fixes diagnostics_channel/stores/with-store-scope.ts and non-callable-transform.ts.

fix(stream): #3663 — wire on/write/pipe + data pump on all stream construction paths (#4076)

* fix(stream): #3663 — wire on/write/pipe on aliased stream constructors

new Readable()/Writable()/Duplex()/Transform()/PassThrough() only produced a
fully-methoded object on the ESM named-import path (lowered to Expr::New ->
lower_builtin_new). The CJS-destructure form (const { Readable } =
require('stream')) and namespace-member form (new stream.Readable()) lower to
NewDynamic, which fell through to an empty-object placeholder, so .on()/.write()/
.pipe() threw 'is not a function' — the bulk of issue #3663's 65 parity failures.

Two routing fixes:
- codegen new_dynamic.rs: NewDynamic { callee: PropertyGet { NativeModuleRef(
  "stream"), Ctor } } routes to lower_builtin_new (import * as stream).
- runtime js_new_function_construct: when the callee resolves to the stream.<Ctor>
  bound-method closure, dispatch to js_node_stream_*_new. Covers every aliasing
  shape (require destructure, require-into-namespace, const alias).

* fix(stream): #3663 — register CJS/namespace stream ctors as native instances

The classic-stream method routing (.pipe/.on/.write -> NativeMethodCall real
pump) fires during lowering only when the receiver local is tagged as a
('stream', Ctor) native instance. That tagging keys off lookup_native_module,
which the ESM named-import path populates but CJS require-destructure does not —
so const { Readable } = require('stream') left Readable a plain local, the
instance was never tagged, and methods dispatched to no-op stub closures.

Register destructured stream constructors (and the new stream.Ctor() member
form) as native-module aliases so the existing instance-registration +
method-routing machinery treats them identically to import { Readable }.

* fix(stream): #3663 — detect require('stream') destructure for instance tagging

is_require_builtin_module's allowlist is only fs/path/crypto, so it didn't
recognize require('stream'); add require_literal_specifier which returns the
specifier verbatim and let the caller match 'stream'. This makes the direct
const { Readable } = require('stream') form (what Node's own test files use)
tag the stream instance so .pipe/.on/.write route to the real pump.

* test(stream): #3663 parity fixture for new stream.Readable() namespace construction

Exercises the NewDynamic -> stream-constructor path (import * as stream;

fix(node): throw spec arg-validation errors for fs/process/zlib (#3662) (#4082)

Node-core argument-validation sub-cluster of #3662: make `zlib`, `process`,
and `fs` builtins throw the spec-mandated `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` /

zlib option validation — new shared `js_zlib_validate_options(opts, min_wb)`

(perry-ext-zlib, used by the auto-optimize build) codecs from `gzipSync` /

one throws the matching RangeError.

non-string/Buffer/TypedArray/DataView/ArrayBuffer first argument to the
gzip/gunzip/deflate/inflate sync codecs in the ext path (stdlib already did so

the `type` positional (string), matching Node's ordering.

fix(runtime): implement Function.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance] (#3662) (#4098)

`Function.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance]` was undefined: `typeof` reported
"undefined", reflective use (`Function.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance].call(C, v)`
or `C[Symbol.hasInstance](v)`) threw, and a class `static [Symbol.hasInstance]`
was the only way to reach the protocol. This is the missing-method slice of the
#3662 builtins cluster (Function.proto apply/call/bind landed in #4073).

Install the method on Function.prototype keyed by the real well-known
`Symbol.hasInstance` (not an @@-string own property, which would leak into
getOwnPropertyNames). It performs OrdinaryHasInstance via the operator's full
constructor-resolution path (js_instanceof_dynamic), which — crucially — differs
from the `instanceof` operator: a non-callable `this` yields `false`, not a
TypeError. A thread-local suppress flag makes js_instanceof_dynamic return
`false` instead of throwing at its unresolved-RHS tail for this path only.

Also teaches js_instanceof_dynamic to resolve the Map/Set/RegExp/ArrayBuffer
global constructor *values* (mirroring the synthetic class ids the compile-time
operator emits), so both reflective hasInstance and a dynamic `x instanceof
ctorVar` work for them. Array/Object/Date constructor values are not yet
identified on the dynamic path (they aren't noop-thunk closures) — a known gap
for the dynamic form; the literal-RHS operator handles them at compile time.

New gap test test_gap_3662_function_hasinstance.ts is byte-identical to
node --experimental-strip-types in both build paths.

fix(runtime): stop size-accessor install corrupting Map/Set.prototype.set (#4099) (#4111)

* fix(runtime): stop size-accessor install corrupting Map/Set.prototype.set data slot (#4099)

`Map.prototype.set.call(null, 1, 2)` crashed the process (SIGBUS) instead of
throwing the spec TypeError, masking the rest of the #3662 collection
brand-check test. Root cause: in collection_proto_thunks the `size` *accessor*
getter was installed AFTER the data-method thunks. Installing an accessor
descriptor onto a prototype that already holds data properties desyncs the
accessor/data-field bookkeeping and clobbers a sibling data slot — here
`Map.prototype.set` read back as a garbage subnormal number (bits
0x2800000203). `typeof Map.prototype.set` was "number"; a later reflective
`.call` dereferenced that number as an object pointer and faulted.

(The user-facing `Object.defineProperty` accessor path is unaffected — it uses
a different, correct code path. Only the builtin manual install sequence
desynced.)

Fix:
- collection_proto_thunks.rs: install the `size` accessor BEFORE the data
  methods for both Map and Set, so the lone accessor never lands on a proto
  that already has data slots to corrupt. WeakMap/WeakSet have no size getter
  and were never affected.
- boxed_primitives.rs: defense-in-depth — `boxed_primitive_payload` is a
  type-probe over arbitrary f64 bits, so gate the candidate on the real heap
  range (`is_valid_obj_ptr`) before reading `class_id`, instead of the weak
  `< 0x100000` guard that let a subnormal double through to a faulting deref.

New gap test test_gap_4099_map_set_accessor_corruption.ts is byte-identical to
node --experimental-strip-types in both build paths; the pre-existing
test_gap_3662_collection_brand_check.ts (which crashed on main) now passes too.

* fix(runtime): keep small-handle floor in boxed-primitive probe (#4099)

is_valid_obj_ptr alone uses HEAP_MIN=0x1000 on Linux, so fetch-family
handle ids like 0x40001 fall inside its valid range and get dereferenced,
crashing the boxed_primitive_probe_rejects_pointer_tagged_native_handles
test on the Linux CI runner. Restore the 0x100000 small-handle floor
alongside the heap-range gate.

`fn.toString()` returned the generic `"[object Object]"` because Perry never
retained function source and the value-to-string path had no closure case.
`Function.prototype.toString.call(nonFunction)` also silently returned a string

Source retention:
- HIR now captures each function's original source by slicing the installed
  module source against the AST span at lowering time (function declarations,
  function expressions, arrows), stored in `Module.closure_source_text` keyed by
  FuncId. `async` is re-prepended when SWC's span excludes the modifier.
- Codegen emits `js_register_function_source(func_ptr, src, len)` alongside the
  existing name registration, keyed by the same wrapper/closure address the

fix(runtime): cap field_count to inline capacity in ensure_key_in_keys_array (#4099) (#4113)

`Map.prototype.set` / `WeakMap.prototype.set` (and `Map.prototype.values`,
`Set.prototype.values`) invoked reflectively on an invalid receiver crashed
the process with SIGBUS instead of throwing the spec `TypeError`. The fault
was a type-confusion deref in `js_native_call_method`'s NaN-box-tag check,
reached before the thunk's brand check ever ran — because reading
`Map.prototype.set` returned a raw, untagged non-pointer value.

Root cause: an object's physical inline field capacity is `max(field_count, 8)`
(`js_object_alloc`), and the read path (`js_object_get_field`) treats
`index < field_count` as inline and the rest as the overflow map. A builtin
collection prototype has 9 string-keyed methods, so `values` spills to the
overflow map (index 8). Installing the `Map.prototype.size` accessor then went
through `ensure_key_in_keys_array`, which unconditionally bumped `field_count`
to the new key's index + 1 (8 → 11). That pushed the boundary past the proto's
8 physical slots, reclassifying the overflowed `values` slot and the last
inline `set` slot as inline reads that dereference past the allocation into
adjacent-heap garbage.

Fix: in `ensure_key_in_keys_array`, only bump `field_count` when the new key
lands in an in-bounds inline slot (`new_index < max(field_count, 8)`). A
keys-only entry — a built-in accessor, or a key whose data spilled to overflow
— must not move the inline/overflow boundary. This mirrors the cap already
used by `js_object_set_field_by_name`.

Verified: the original repro now throws `TypeError` (byte-identical to Node),
the #3662 collection brand-check gap test passes byte-identical and is no
longer truncated, reflective set/add/values/get work on valid receivers, and
data fields installed after a prototype accessor still read back correctly.

Number/Boolean/Symbol/BigInt prototype methods (valueOf/toString/
toLocaleString) did not perform the spec `this` brand check when invoked
reflectively (e.g. `Number.prototype.valueOf.call({})`). They fell back to

fix(runtime): link generator/async-generator instance prototype chain (#4141)

Perry lowers `gen()` to a `{next,return,throw}` object literal but never
linked its `[[Prototype]]`, so reflective access via the instance —
`Object.getPrototypeOf(Object.getPrototypeOf(gen()))` — landed on the wrong
object instead of `%Generator.prototype%` / `%AsyncGenerator.prototype%`.
That broke the instance-side brand-check / descriptor cases (issue repro #2,
test262 `AsyncGeneratorPrototype/.../this-val-not-async-generator`). The
function-side descriptor + brand-check layer was already correct on main
(#4086); this fills the remaining instance-chain gap.

`transform_generators` now wraps the returned iterator object in a new
`Expr::LinkGeneratorPrototype { obj, is_async }`. At runtime
`js_generator_attach_prototype` interposes a fresh intermediate object as the
instance's `[[Prototype]]` whose own `[[Prototype]]` is the sync/async
generator prototype, reproducing Node's two-hop
`instance -> g.prototype -> %Generator.prototype%` chain. Both links go
through the GC-traced static-prototype side-table.

- New HIR variant handled in both `walk_expr_children` walkers, `stable_hash`,
  and `boxed_vars`' nested-closure walker (so generator state locals still box).
- `function_body_returns_generator_object` unwraps the new wrapper so the
  generator-function registration (drives `g.prototype`, isGeneratorFunction)
  still fires.
- Escape analysis leaves the wrapped, unanalyzed iterator allocation on the
  heap — correct, since a generator object always escapes via the return.

Verified byte-identical to Node for descriptors, brand checks (sync throws /
async rejects), stateful generators, for-of, yield*, class/object generator
methods, and nested generators. New node-suite test
globals/generator-prototype-chain.ts.

Known limitation: the interposed prototype is per-call, so
`Object.getPrototypeOf(gen()) === gen.prototype` is currently false (the
intermediate is not the closure-cached `gen.prototype` object — that requires
the generator closure at instance-construction time, which is not in scope
there). Brand-check / descriptor semantics are unaffected.

fix(typedarray): throw on prototype accessor reads off-instance (#4140)

The `%TypedArray%.prototype` `buffer`/`byteLength`/`byteOffset`/`length`
getters are installed as reflection-only builtin accessors that deliberately
don't flip the `ACCESSORS_IN_USE` hot-path gate (#2060). On top of that, the
per-kind prototypes (`Uint8Array.prototype`, …) carry no recorded
`[[Prototype]]` link in the chain the property getter walks — they resolve to
the shared `%TypedArray%.prototype` only through `Object.getPrototypeOf`'s
`OBJ_FLAG_TYPED_ARRAY_PROTO` flag. So a plain value read off the prototype
(`Uint8Array.prototype.buffer`) never reached the inherited accessor and
silently returned the empty slot (`undefined`) instead of Node's `TypeError`
(test262 `built-ins/TypedArrayConstructors/<T>/prototype/not-typedarray-object.js`,
11 types).

Resolve the getter off the shared intrinsic for both the intrinsic itself and
any object flagged `OBJ_FLAG_TYPED_ARRAY_PROTO`. A genuine concrete typed
array short-circuits far earlier in `js_object_get_field_by_name`, so the
receiver here is never a real instance and the getter throws — matching Node.
Guarded by a cheap key filter + heap-pointer/`GC_TYPE_OBJECT` check so ordinary
reads (and non-pointer `obj` values threaded through the generic getter) pay
nothing and are never dereferenced.

New parity fixture `typedarray-prototype-accessor-throws.ts` exercises all 11
typed-array types, the intrinsic, an `Object.create`-derived object, and real
instances; byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`.

runtime: shared %IteratorPrototype% objects for built-in iterators (#4209)

Built-in iterator objects (Array/Map/Set/String iterators) now have real
shared `%...IteratorPrototype%` singleton prototypes that chain up to a
shared `%IteratorPrototype%`, so test262's verifyProperty checks pass:

  - `Object.getPrototypeOf([][Symbol.iterator]())` returns a shared
    singleton (same object every call), not the iterator instance.
  - `.next` is an OWN property of that prototype (instance inherits it)
    with `{writable:true, enumerable:false, configurable:true}`.
  - `proto.next.name === "next"` (non-writable/enum, configurable),
    `proto.next.length === 0`.
  - Each family prototype's [[Prototype]] is the shared %IteratorPrototype%
    carrying `[Symbol.iterator]` (returns this).

Mechanism (mirrors the #3664 generator-tower model):
  - New `object/iterator_prototypes.rs` lazily builds the five singletons
    (one shared parent + four families), GC-rooted via atomics scanned in
    `scan_object_cache_roots_mut`. `next` is installed via the existing
    `install_proto_method` (#3143 descriptor machinery), so name/length/
    descriptor attrs are spec-correct for free.
  - Each iterator allocator links the instance's [[Prototype]] to its
    singleton (`attach_iterator_prototype`), so `getPrototypeOf` and the
    inherited `it.next` value-read resolve through existing chain machinery.
  - New `string/iter_object.rs` adds a real String iterator object
    (STRING_ITERATOR_CLASS_ID, codepoint-aware); `str[Symbol.iterator]()`
    and `arguments[Symbol.iterator]()` now route to real iterators.

The class-id `.next()` CALL fast path is untouched, so for-of / spread /
Array.from keep driving `.next()` directly. `js_iterator_to_array` (sync +
async) and `array_from_spread_value` / `js_get_iterator` were updated to
only take the stored-closure fast path on an OWN `.next` and to
short-circuit built-in iterators, since `.next`/`[Symbol.iterator]` are now
inherited and the inherited thunks rely on the class-id tower to bind this.

fix(array): materialize array-like receivers for Array.prototype.*.call (#4231)

Array.prototype.<method>.call(arrayLikeObject, ...) was broken across the
whole read-only Array method surface (map/filter/reduce/reduceRight/some/
every/forEach/find/findIndex/findLast/findLastIndex/at/indexOf/lastIndexOf/
includes/slice/join/flatMap). A generic array-like receiver — a plain object
with a `length` property and indexed keys, e.g. {length:3, 0:"a", 1:"b"} —
was treated as a raw ArrayHeader: methods read garbage (8.48e-314) or threw
"value is not a function" / TypeError.

Two orthogonal root causes, both fixed:

1. HIR (primary): `try_builtin_prototype_method_apply_call` rewrote
   `Array.prototype.map.call(like, fn)` into `like.map(fn)`, which the normal
   member-call fast path only routes to `js_array_*` when the receiver is
   statically array-typed; for an Any/object receiver it lowered to a dynamic
   method lookup that found no `map` field and threw. Now, when the resolved
   method is a known read-only Array method, the receiver is materialized into
   a REAL array via `Expr::ArrayFrom` (→ js_array_from_value → js_array_clone,
   which already detects `{length, 0:…}` array-likes) before the dedicated
   `Expr::Array*` variant is built. This also fixes the methods whose codegen
   is INLINED (e.g. forEach reads `(*arr).length`/`arr[i]` directly rather than
   calling js_array_forEach) — the inlined loop now sees a genuine ArrayHeader.

2. Runtime (defense-in-depth): add `normalize_array_receiver`, used at the
   entry of the read-only `js_array_*` helpers in place of `clean_arr_ptr`. It
   reads the GC-header obj_type; for GC_TYPE_OBJECT (a plain array-like) it
   materializes via `js_array_from_arraylike`, otherwise it falls straight
   through to `clean_arr_ptr`. Real arrays (GC_TYPE_ARRAY) pay only one
   already-warm header-byte read + an integer compare — the registry lookups
   and materialization are reached only for plain-object receivers, so the
   `[1,2,3].map(...)` hot path is unchanged. This catches array-like receivers
   that reach the runtime through indirection the HIR fold can't see statically.

Mutators (push/pop/shift/unshift/splice/sort/reverse/fill/copyWithin) and
concat are intentionally left as-is: mutators need spec write-back of indexed
props + length to the receiver (out of scope for this pass), and concat's
array-like receiver has non-spreading single-element semantics that differ
from the array algorithm.

Verified byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types` across all
read-only methods on a {length:3,0,1,2} array-like, plus regression cases on
real arrays (map/filter/reduce/for-of/spread/slice/indexOf) and a TypedArray
(both PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE and default auto-optimize builds). 974/974
perry-runtime lib tests pass.

fix(runtime): brand-check %TypedArray%.prototype methods on the value path (#4332)

%TypedArray%.prototype methods (map/filter/reduce/.../slice/subarray/...)

fix(runtime): implement TypedArray integer-indexed [[DefineOwnProperty]] (#4353)

TypedArrays are Integer-Indexed exotic objects: Object.defineProperty /
Reflect.defineProperty with a canonical numeric index key must validate
the index against the view length and constrain the descriptor to a
writable/enumerable/configurable data property (writing the element on a
valid in-bounds value descriptor), rather than routing through ordinary
[[DefineOwnProperty]] (which treated the view as non-extensible and
rejected every index).

Adds object/typed_array_define.rs implementing the spec algorithm
(CanonicalNumericIndexString round-trip, IsValidIntegerIndex, descriptor
constraints, IntegerIndexedElementSet for both the BufferHeader-backed
Uint8Array and TypedArrayHeader-backed representations). Object.define
throws TypeError on rejection; Reflect.define returns false. Non-canonical
keys and symbols fall through to ordinary define unchanged.

Reduces test262 TypedArrayConstructors/internals/DefineOwnProperty
failures 40 to 24; remaining are separate pre-existing gaps (BigInt
typed-array element storage, TA expando properties, integer-indexed
[[GetOwnProperty]], detached buffers). No regressions.

fix(runtime): TypedArray integer-indexed [[GetOwnProperty]] descriptors (#4357)

Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(ta, i) on a TypedArray returned undefined
for every index because the lookup routed through the ordinary keys table.
Per the Integer-Indexed exotic [[GetOwnProperty]], a canonical numeric
index resolves to the element as a { value, writable: true, enumerable:
true, configurable: true } data property (valid in-bounds index) or to no
own property (out-of-bounds / non-integer / -0). Reuses the canonical
index + view machinery added for [[DefineOwnProperty]]; covers both the
BufferHeader-backed Uint8Array and TypedArrayHeader-backed kinds. Symbols
and non-canonical keys fall through to ordinary [[GetOwnProperty]]
unchanged.

fix(transform): scan PutValueSet closures when seeding generator func/local ids (#4366)

A module containing any generator (`function*`) mis-compiled every
function expression assigned to a member via strict PutValue
(`obj.f = function(){...}`) into the generator's synthesized iterator:
calling `obj.f(...)` returned `{value: undefined, done: true}` instead of
invoking the function.

Root cause: the generator state-machine transform seeds its synthesized
`next`/`return`/`throw` closure ids from `compute_max_func_id(module) + 1`,
but `scan_expr_for_max_func` (and its local-id sibling) had no `PutValueSet`
arm — the assigned Closure was invisible to the scan, so `max_id` stayed
below it and the synthesized closures reused its func_id. At codegen one
LLVM function per func_id wins, so `obj.f` dispatched into the generator's
`next`. Adds `PutValueSet` arms to both scanners (mirrors the existing
PropertySet / ArrayPush / NativeMethodCall collision fixes).

fix(date): ECMAScript ToNumber for Date arguments (Symbol/BigInt throw, single valueOf) (#4393)

Date argument coercion (the `new Date(v)` numeric path, `Date.UTC`, the
multi-arg `new Date(y,m,d,...)` constructor, and `Date.prototype.set*`
components) read raw NaN-boxed bits for any non-string/non-sentinel value,
so a Symbol/object/array/boolean produced garbage or an Invalid Date
instead of following ToNumber:

- `new Date(Symbol())` / `d.setHours(Symbol())` / `Date.UTC(2020, Symbol())`

  (`new Date(2020, {valueOf(){...}})` — valueOf invoked exactly once).

branch, and the multi-arg constructor's `coerce` through one ToNumber that
handles Symbol/BigInt (throw), Date (time value), and object/array
(OrdinaryToPrimitive) before the primitive numeric coercion.

fix(date): brand-check this on Date.prototype getters (reflective dispatch) (#4397)

* fix(date): brand-check this on Date.prototype getters (reflective dispatch)

Date.prototype getters (getDate/getDay/getFullYear/getHours/.../getUTC*,
getTimezoneOffset, getTime, valueOf, legacy getYear) were installed as
generic no-op thunks, so the reflective value path mis-behaved:

each thunk reads IMPLICIT_THIS, brand-checks via is_date_value (TypeError
on mismatch), and dispatches to the same js_date_get_* helper the instance
fast path uses. Installed after the OBJECT_PROTO_METHODS no-op block so the
generic Object valueOf does not re-clobber Date.prototype.valueOf.

The instance fast path (d.getDate()) is lowered directly by codegen and is
unchanged. test262 built-ins/Date: -36 (158->122 on top of the ToNumber
fix; no regressions). Node-identical in both build modes.

horizontally aligned (CSS `text-align`) without wrapping it in an extra
alignment container.

  - watchOS  NodeData.text_alignment + SwiftUI-host introspection getter
  - Web      el.style.textAlign (wasm_runtime.js)

Plus the cross-cutting wiring: perry-dispatch MethodRow, perry/ui type
declaration, JS/wasm/ArkTS codegen maps, and the styling matrix row.
Justified/natural degrade to the nearest supported alignment where a
platform has no native equivalent.

Verified on macOS: codegen emits `perry_ui_text_set_text_alignment(i64,

fix(runtime): ToNumber/ToInteger(Symbol|BigInt) throw TypeError at numeric coercion sites (#4415)

ECMA-262 ToNumber(Symbol) and ToNumber(BigInt) are both TypeErrors (§7.1.4).
Only the `+` operator enforced this; the other implicit numeric-coercion sites
silently produced NaN/garbage. This adds the missing guards at the shared
runtime entry points:

- `js_number_coerce` (builtins/numbers.rs): a Symbol now throws before the
  pointer/toPrimitive path. This is the coercion the codegen routes through for
  `Number(sym)` and for arithmetic on a non-numeric operand (`sym * 2`, `-sym`,
  binary.rs js_number_coerce fallback), so both explicit and implicit ToNumber
  now match Node. BigInt is intentionally left converting here — `Number(1n)`
  is allowed; the arithmetic-throws-on-BigInt rule already lives at the
  arithmetic call sites (dynamic_arith.rs both_bigint_or_throw).

- `Number.prototype.toPrecision` / `toExponential` (string/format.rs): the
  argument's `ToIntegerOrInfinity` (which routes through js_number_coerce) now
  runs before the non-finite check on the receiver, matching the spec step
  order, so a Symbol fractionDigits/precision throws even when x is NaN/±Inf
  (e.g. `Number.prototype.toPrecision(Symbol())`).

- TypedArray (typedarray/mod.rs): `jsvalue_to_f64` (element store on a numeric
  view) and `js_typed_array_new` (the length argument) now throw on Symbol and
  BigInt. `new Int8Array(5n)` / `new Int8Array(Symbol())` and `ta[i] = sym` now
  throw instead of producing an empty/garbage array. BigInt views are
  unaffected — js_typed_array_set routes ToBigInt separately before these.

Verified byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types` in both the
default and PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE builds; normal arithmetic / Number() /
TypedArray construction & element writes unchanged. test262 built-ins/Number
real parity 71.5% -> 73.3%. perry-runtime unit suite green (979).

Apply ECMA-262 TimeClip in every Date construction/UTC/setter result path so

fix(regex): keep escaped hyphen \- literal inside a character class (#4425) (#4429)

An escaped hyphen `\-` inside a JS character class is always a literal
hyphen, but `push_escaped_literal` emitted a bare `-`. The Rust `regex`
crate then read a `-` flanked by members as a range operator, so

hyphen stays a literal regardless of position.

fix(generator): make try/catch real in the sync generator state machine (#4438) (#4457)

B2 slice of #4438. The catch handler previously existed only inside the
.throw() closure, not in the normal .next() dispatch, so (a) a throw
executing inside a try during a plain .next() escaped uncaught and (b) a
yield inside a catch was swallowed (rewritten to await).

Linearize the catch body into its own states; the happy path skips them.
A sync generator's dispatch loop is wrapped in a try/catch that routes a
thrown error to the matching catch's entry state (running pending finally
and completing the generator when unhandled). .throw() routes the same way
and falls through to the continuation loop so a yield inside the catch
suspends. The runtime-throw path uses an inclusive lower bound since a
throw in a try's first state runs at exactly protected_start.

Async generators are untouched (linearized catch states are dead on the
async path), so behavior is byte-identical.

fix(runtime): pack rest params for zero-arg ctors and apply-dispatched methods (#4441) (#4460)

Two latent rest-parameter bugs surfaced while compiling a Hono SSR site
(the `marked` dependency, pulled in via `@skelpo/site-kit`, crashed at
module init with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'forEach')").

1. Constructor rest-param padded with a spurious `undefined`.
   `fill_default_arguments` padded `new C(...)` args up to the constructor's
   full param count — including a trailing rest param. So `new C()` with
   `constructor(...e)` produced `e = [undefined]` instead of `[]`, and any
   `e.forEach(...)` over that bogus element threw. Fixed by stopping the
   pad at the rest param (mirrors the existing call-site padding in
   expr_call). marked's `new Marked()` -> `this.use(...e)` hit this.

2. Apply-dispatched instance method bound its rest param to a scalar.
   `recv.method(...spread)` routes through `js_native_call_method_apply` ->
   `call_vtable_method`, which only handled a synthesized `arguments` slot,
   never a user rest param. So `method(...args)` set `rest = args[0]` as a
   scalar ("(number).forEach is not a function"). The instance-method vtable
   now tracks `has_rest` (statics already did) and `call_vtable_method`
   bundles the trailing args into the rest array. Also fixes the

fix(hir): don't re-localize a module-level var assigned inside a closure (var hoisting) (#4473)

A closure (or function) that assigns to a module-level `var` declared LATER
in the module lost the write — the value read back as `undefined`:
    var f = function(){ later = 5; }; var later; f(); console.log(later); // was undefined
    function g(){ later = 7; }       var later; g(); console.log(later);  // was undefined

Cause: when lowering the closure body, `predeclare_implicit_assignment_targets`
saw `later = 5` and, because `later` is a pre-registered module `var`, reused
the module var's LocalId but still emitted a localizing `Let <id> = undefined`
INSIDE the closure body. That makes codegen treat the id as a closure-local
(a fresh per-call slot) instead of the module var's global slot, so the write
never reached the module binding the post-declaration read uses.

Fix: in `predeclare_implicit_assignment_targets`, when running inside a closure
(scope_depth > 0) and the name resolves to a module-level binding, skip the
hoist Let — the assignment resolves to the module var's global slot. A
closure-local shadow (`function(){ var x; … }`) has its own non-module id and
is unaffected.

fix(generator): route abrupt completion through yielding finally (#4438 B2) (#4474)

Completes the B2 try-finally slice. After the try/catch state-machine work,
the 6 remaining failures all involved a YIELDING finally (`finally { yield N }`):
abrupt completion (`.throw()`/`.return()`/a runtime throw) while suspended in
the protected try never ran the finally — it was skipped and the error/return
propagated.

Implements completion records:
- linearize.rs: a yielding finally gets a clean entry state + a completion-check
  state. Pre-try code is flushed to its own state so the try's protected
  interval starts cleanly at the try body (otherwise a `throw` between a
  preceding yield and a nested try lands in the nested try's first state and is
  misrouted to its handler).
- lower.rs: two `pending` locals (type: 0 none / 1 throw / 2 return, + value).
  Abrupt completion routes to the innermost enclosing handler — a catch (jump to
  its states) or a yielding finally (record the pending completion + jump in) —
  via one ordered `build_abrupt_routing` chain shared by the dispatch wrapper,
  `.throw()`, and `.return()`. At the finally's completion check the pending
  throw is re-raised (and re-routed to an enclosing handler by the wrapper) or
  the pending return completes the generator. Suspended INSIDE the finally
  supersedes the pending completion (the finally's own states are excluded from
  its protected interval). All three dispatch loops (next + throw/return
  continuations) are wrapped so a catch that rethrows still runs a non-yielding
  finally on the way out.

Async generators are untouched (they never set the pending record; the appended
completion checks are inert on the async path) — byte-identical.

fix(codegen): push with >1 arg/spread inside a method or getter body (#4508) (#4516)

`Array.prototype.push` with more than one argument (two spreads, or a
spread combined with another element) failed native codegen when the
call was inside a class method or getter body:

    array.push_spread expects exactly 1 arg, got 2

The same statement at module top level (local-array receiver) compiled
fine because that lowering path (local_array_methods.rs) already
decomposes multi-arg push into a Sequence of single-arg pushes. The
property-receiver path (array_only_methods.rs) instead packed the whole
arg list into one `push_spread` NativeMethodCall, and the codegen arm
bails on >1 arg — rejecting the entire module. Found in the wild in
zod's `ParseInputLazyPath.get path()`.

Fix: in the array_only_methods push arm, decompose the
multiple-args-with-a-spread case into a Sequence of single-arg native
calls, choosing push_spread vs push_single per-arg from the original AST
spread flag. Each native arm re-reads the receiver and writes back the
(possibly realloc'd) handle, so chaining threads the array correctly;
push returns the final length, which the last Sequence element yields.

Also fixes a latent mis-route: the old code only checked the FIRST arg
for a spread, so `arr.push(0, ...a)` went to push_single and treated
`...a` as a single element. The new any-spread check handles it.

Output verified byte-for-byte against Node for two-spreads, spread+
element, element+spread+element, and plain multi-arg cases.

earlier statement) may legally reference an enum declared later in the file.

a forward reference failed enum lookup, fell through to the unknown-identifier
path, printed a warning, and silently lowered member reads to 0 — corrupting
e.g. zod's ZodFirstPartyTypeKind dispatch.

Add pre_register_module_enums, a pre-scan that registers every module-level
enum (member names + values are computed purely) before any function body is
lowered, mirroring the existing function-hoisting pre-pass. lower_enum_decl
now reuses a pre-registered id instead of minting a duplicate. Enum ids stay
in textual order, so already-working code is byte-identical.

fix(hir): ctor 'this.method = this.method.bind(this)' is a method override, not a field (#4558)

fields and accessors — but NOT method names. So a self-rebind like
`this.parse = this.parse.bind(this)` allocated a field slot for `parse`, and the
codegen field branch (property_get.rs) then shadowed the prototype method on every
read: `this.parse` read the uninitialised slot (`undefined`) BEFORE the assignment
ran, so `this.parse.bind(this)` threw 'Bind must be called on a function'.

/ `z.object()` / `z.coerce` threw at construction. Collect own instance-method
names and exclude them from the inferred-field set (mirrors the accessor exclusion,

fix(runtime): Array/TypedArray.prototype.isPrototypeOf compares by raw heap address (#4552)

Array.prototype is itself an exotic GC_TYPE_ARRAY object and Uint8Array.prototype
a typed-array proto — neither is GC_TYPE_OBJECT. js_object_is_prototype_of_value
resolved the receiver and every prototype-chain link with object_ptr_from_value,
which only accepts GC_TYPE_OBJECT, so it returned None for these and the walk
bailed early. Array.prototype.isPrototypeOf([1,2]) and
Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf([]) both wrongly returned false.

Compare by raw GC heap address (gc_pointer_and_type_from_value) instead, and let
array / typed-array targets reach the generic [[Prototype]] walk (their chains are
already modeled by js_object_get_prototype_of). Fixes test262 Array
S15.4.1_A1.1_T3 / S15.4.2.1_A1.1_T3 and the isPrototypeOf cluster.

Still deferred (separate root causes): ArrayBuffer targets (BufferHeader repr not
resolved by the pointer walk) and class .prototype receivers (class .prototype is
a synthetic class-ref value, typeof === number, not a heap object).

fix(codegen): Array callback/index methods with 0 args compile (runtime-throw or default), not bail (#4556)

The inline codegen fast path for Array.prototype.{map,filter,forEach,find,findIndex,
findLast,findLastIndex,some,every,flatMap,fill,at} hard-failed compilation when
called with 0 arguments ("perry-codegen: Array.X expects 1 arg, got 0"). Per spec
these are valid call sites that resolve at runtime:

- map/filter/forEach/find*/some/every/flatMap with no callback throw a runtime
  TypeError ("undefined is not a function") — pad a missing callback with undefined
  and let js_validate_array_callback raise it.
- arr.fill() with no value fills the whole array with undefined.
- arr.at() with no index reads index 0 (at(undefined)).

A failed inline path aborted the entire module compile (and cascaded to an
"Undefined symbols: _main" link error), so a single 0-arg call broke unrelated code.
Fixes test262 built-ins/Array/prototype/{every,filter,fill,...} 0-arg cases; verified
byte-identical to node for both the throwing and the default-value forms.

fix(hir): new Number/String/Boolean coerce a present argument (explicit undefined distinct from no-arg) (#4560)

new Number(undefined) boxed +0 and new String(undefined) boxed "" — both
collapsed to Expr::Undefined during lowering, indistinguishable from the no-arg
forms new Number()/new String(), so js_boxed_*_new's missing-arg sentinel mapped
both to the no-arg default.

Per spec a *present* argument is coerced: new Number(x) → ToNumber(x),
new String(x) → ToString(x). So new Number(undefined) is NaN and
new String(undefined) is "undefined", distinct from new Number()/new String()
which box +0/"". Wrap a present arg in NumberCoerce/StringCoerce/BooleanCoerce at
lowering; emit the undefined sentinel only for the genuinely no-arg form.

Fixes test262 built-ins/Number/S9.3_A5_T1. Verified byte-identical to node for
Number/String/Boolean across no-arg, explicit-undefined, and value args.

fix(codegen): forward constructor args through a subclass with no own ctor (#4567)

`new Sub(arg)` where `Sub` has no own constructor but its parent does must
forward `arg` to the parent ctor (JS implicit `constructor(...args){ super(...args) }`).
The recursion-guarded symbol-call construction path — taken when `new Sub(...)`
appears inside a method of `Sub` — read the ctor arity from `class.constructor`
(`None` → 0) and truncated all args away. The synthesized standalone ctor
(codegen/artifacts.rs) adopts the ancestor ctor's signature and forwards via
super, so its params then read uninitialized garbage and the inherited
`this.x = arg` stored 0/undefined.

Compute the arity from the closest ancestor-with-a-ctor when the subclass has
none (mirrors the synthesized-ctor signature). Fixes zod `new ZodNumber({…})`
from `_addCheck`/`setLimit` (ZodNumber has no own ctor, ZodType does), which made
`_def` undefined → `z.coerce.number().int()` threw 'undefined is not iterable'.

fix(codegen): run a no-own-ctor subclass's own field initializers after super() (#4571)

The implicit default ctor of `class Leaf extends Base {}` is
`constructor(...args){ super(...args); <own field inits> }`. The inline
construction path applied `UpToInclusive(inherited_ctor_class)` up front — which
keeps `chain[0..=idx(inherited)]` and EXCLUDES the leaf — and then inlined the
inherited ctor body, but never applied the leaf's (and any intermediates') own
field initializers afterward. So a no-own-ctor subclass's `field = <init>` never
ran and the field read the raw-0 slot.

Apply `BetweenExclusiveTo(inherited_ctor_class)` after the inherited ctor body
(the post-super step, mirroring the own-ctor path's SelfOnly-after).

Fixes zod `class ZodObject extends ZodType { private _cached = null }`: `_cached`
was 0 so `_getCached()`'s `this._cached !== null` was true and returned 0; `_parse`
destructured `{ keys }` off 0 and every `z.object({...}).parse()` dropped all
fields. Adds tests/test_subclass_own_field_init_after_super.sh.

fix(hir): namespace 'export const' members are accessible cross-module (#4580)

A TS `namespace`'s exported FUNCTIONS were lowered as static methods of the
namespace class and crossed the module boundary, but its `export const` members
lived only in the defining module's per-module `namespace_vars`. An importing
module therefore read `ns.member` back as undefined/garbage for value members.

the const's value into it via a `StaticFieldSet` appended to `module.init` right
after the const's own `Let` (evaluated once, correct order). `ns.member` then
resolves cross-module through the static-field global; same-module access and
intra-namespace bare references keep using the local.

`ZodObject._getCached` got null keys and every `z.object({...}).parse()` silently
dropped all fields. Adds tests/test_namespace_const_cross_module.sh.

fix(json): format numbers with ECMAScript Number::toString (#4574)

JSON.stringify's `write_number` formatted non-integer / out-of-i64-range
values with `ryu`, which produces shortest round-trip digits but its own
notation. So JSON.stringify diverged from String(n) and Node:
`JSON.stringify(1e20)` was `1e20` (Node `100000000000000000000`), `1e21`
was `1e21` (`1e+21`), and `1e-6` was `1e-6` (`0.000001`).

ECMAScript Number::toString formatter that `String(n)` / template literals
already use (fixed notation for an exponent in -6..=20, else exponential
with an `e+`/`e-` sign). The in-range-integer fast path (itoa) is
unchanged. `js_format_f64` is what `String()` uses, so the two now agree.

fix(runtime): Map/Set keys — a Symbol never equals the empty-string key (#4575)

A description-less Symbol() exposes a zero-length string view, and the Map/Set
key comparator (jsvalue_eq) content-compared any two string-like values. So
jsvalue_eq("", Symbol()) saw two zero-length strings and returned true: the ""
and Symbol() keys collided (size 1 instead of 2, get("") returned the symbol's
value).

Symbols compare by identity only — two distinct symbols are never equal, and a
same-symbol match is already caught by the bit-equality fast path. Guard
jsvalue_eq to return false when either operand is a symbol, before the
string-content path.

fix(codegen,runtime): cross-module function statics, Object.assign fn source, bind-as-value, regex replace lookahead (#4592)

Four independent fixes uncovered compiling a real Hono+Drizzle+Stripe+zod app:

- codegen/property_get: reading a static off a cross-module *imported function*
  (Expr::ExternFuncRef as a PropertyGet base) unconditionally called the
  perry_fn_<src>__<name>() getter — correct only for an exported const/let.
  For a function, that symbol IS the body, so every Fn.staticProp read invoked
  the function with zero args. Gate the getter path on imported_vars; functions
  fall through to the closure-value + dynamic-prop read. (Stripe
  StripeResource.method/.extend.)

- runtime/object.assign: a function/closure source was misread as an
  ObjectHeader; reading keys_array off it produced a garbage key_count and a
  runaway loop. Enumerate the closure's enumerable dynamic props instead.
  (Stripe protoExtend's Object.assign(Constructor, Super) hung at import.)

- runtime/Function.prototype.bind: was a no-op proto method, so bind invoked as
  a value (Reflect.apply(bind, call, [fn]) / bind.apply(fn, ...)) returned
  undefined. Add a real bind thunk reading the target from IMPLICIT_THIS.
  (call-bind-apply-helpers uncurry-this idiom.)

- runtime/regex: String.prototype.replace(re, fn) had no fancy-regex fallback,
  so a lookahead/backreference pattern (never-match placeholder in the regex
  crate) fired the callback zero times. Route the callback-replace through
  fancy-regex. (get-intrinsic stringToPath.)

fix(string): replace/replaceAll with a string pattern processes $ patterns (#4582)

`String.prototype.replace` / `replaceAll` with a *string* searchValue passed
the replacement template to Rust's `replacen`/`replace` verbatim, so the
ECMAScript GetSubstitution escapes were ignored: `"x".replace("x","$$")`
gave `$$` (Node `$`), and `$&` / `` $` `` / `$'` were left literal. The regex
path already handled them via `expand_js_replacement`.

Add `expand_string_pattern_replacement` (GetSubstitution for a string
pattern: `$$`->`$`, `$&`->matched, `` $` ``->prefix, `$'`->suffix; `$n`/
`$<name>` stay literal since a string pattern has no captures) and use it in
both `js_string_replace_string` and `js_string_replace_all_string`. A
replacement with no `$` (or an empty pattern) keeps the existing fast Rust
`replacen`/`replace` path, so the common case is unchanged. UTF-8 safe.

Adds parity fixture string-replace-string-dollar.ts. Verified identical to
Node across $$ / $& / $` / $' / mixed / replaceAll / no-$ / no-match /
empty-pattern / UTF-8 cases; regex replace unchanged; regex + replace unit

fix(codegen): materialize `import * as ns` as an enumerable runtime-export object (#4598)

fix(ext-mysql2): createPool is lazy + synchronous (no eager connect) (#4602)

mysql2's `createPool` is synchronous and opens no connection — it returns a
pool that connects lazily on first query. The native ext instead eagerly
`connect().await`ed, which:
  - returned handle 0 when the DB was unreachable, so the JS pool value was a
    NaN-boxed null — every `pool.constructor` / drizzle `isConfig(pool)` read
    then saw `undefined` and crashed (`Cannot read properties of undefined
    (reading 'name')`), and
  - forced callers to have a reachable DB just to construct the pool at
    module-init.

Switch to sqlx `connect_lazy`. It still spawns the pool's background reaper
(which needs a live reactor), so keep the `spawn_blocking` + `block_on` wrapper
for the Tokio context — the body returns immediately because no connection is
opened. The pool now constructs without a DB, matching mysql2, and
`drizzle(pool, { schema })` builds at import time.

Validated end-to-end: the billing app (Hono + Drizzle + mysql2 + Stripe + zod)
now boots through `createPool` + `drizzle()` and starts listening.

fix: HTTP request handling for Hono apps (object-literal getter this, http2 instanceof, handle symbol read) (#4616)

Four fixes that together let a real Hono + @hono/node-server app serve requests
natively (the app previously booted and listened but crashed/400'd/500'd on
every request):

- hir/object accessors: an object-literal getter/setter (`{ get k(){…} }`) is a
  REGULAR (non-arrow) function — `this` binds dynamically to the receiver at call
  time. Lowering emitted `captures_this: true` (mirroring `uses_this`), capturing
  `this` at object-construction time, so an INHERITED read
  (`Object.create(proto).k`) saw `this === proto` instead of the instance.
  @hono/node-server's request prototype (`get method(){ return
  this[incomingKey].method }`) crashed because `this[incomingKey]` was undefined
  on the prototype. Bind dynamically like `Object.defineProperty` getters
  already did.

- runtime/prototype walk: when an inherited read resolves a class (vtable)
  getter, the recursive `get_field(proto, key)` re-derived the getter's `this`
  from the prototype. Thread the original receiver through an override consumed
  at getter invocation (`resolve_inherited_field` /
  `resolve_proto_chain_field`), so inherited class getters also bind `this` to
  the instance.

- runtime/node:http2: `Http2ServerRequest`/`Http2ServerResponse` imported as
  values resolved to `undefined`; libraries use them only for `x instanceof
  Http2ServerRequest` brand checks, so the `instanceof` RHS threw
  "Right-hand side of 'instanceof' is not an object" and 400'd every request.
  Resolve them to callable class values (instanceof → false for HTTP/1 handles).

- runtime/symbol: a symbol read on a small native handle (HTTP IncomingMessage,
  etc.) dereferenced the handle id as an ObjectHeader (EXC_BAD_ACCESS). Return
  undefined for handle/non-object pointers (gated on `is_valid_obj_ptr` so real
  low-address objects are unaffected); proxies keep their own semantics.

Tests: tests/test_object_literal_getter_this_binding.sh (inherited+own getters,
setters, inherited class getter) and tests/test_http2_server_request_value.sh.
