fix(runtime): Math.pow special cases + Math.max/min -0 vs +0 (#4609)

Math.pow used Rust's f64::powf (IEEE pow), which differs from ECMAScript Math.pow:
- pow(base, NaN) must be NaN (IEEE pow(1, NaN) = 1)
- pow(±1, ±Infinity) must be NaN (IEEE returns 1)
Both special-cased before delegating to powf; a +0/-0 exponent still yields 1.

Math.max/min compared with IEEE </> which treat -0 and +0 as equal, so the
sign-of-zero of the first-seen zero stuck (max(-0,0)→-0, min(0,-0)→0). Added the
spec tiebreaker: max treats +0 as greater than -0, min treats -0 as smaller.

Verified byte-identical to node; fixes test262 built-ins/Math/{max,min}/zeros and
Math/pow/applying-the-exp-operator_A1/A7/A8.

fix(hir): object shorthand resolves a cross-module imported binding (#4618)

An object-literal shorthand property whose name is a cross-module imported
binding (`import { db } from "./client.js"; const ctx = { db, ...rest }`) was
silently DROPPED: the shorthand-folding only resolved local / func / class /
builtin names, so an imported name fell through to `bail`/`continue` and the
property never made it into the object — `{ db }` lowered to an empty object.

returned a context whose `db` was `undefined`, so every `db.query.*` /
`db.select()` read crashed with "Cannot read properties of undefined". The
explicit form `{ db: db }` already worked (it lowers the value via `lower_expr`,
which resolves imports to `ExternFuncRef`).

Resolve an imported shorthand name to the same `ExternFuncRef` the explicit form
produces, in all three object-literal lowering paths (closed-shape fold,

fix(hir): logical property assignment must short-circuit the store (#4586) (#4591)

* fix(hir): logical property assignment must short-circuit the store (#4586)

`obj.prop ??= v` / `||=` / `&&=` were desugared to `obj.prop = (obj.prop OP v)`,
which always runs PutValue. The redundant store is silent on writable data
properties but fires setters spuriously and throws `TypeError: Cannot assign to
read only property` on non-writable `Object.defineProperty` data props — e.g.
Zod v4's `inst._zod ??= {}`, which broke every check/refinement schema under
`perry.compilePackages`.

Per ECMAScript LogicalAssignment, PutValue must be skipped entirely when the
short-circuit holds. Desugar property targets to `read(obj.prop) OP (obj.prop
= v)` so the store lives on the logical operator's RHS and only runs on the
branch that writes. Scoped to Member targets; plain Ident locals have no
setters or read-only descriptors, so their unconditional set already matches
spec.

fix(ios): apply ios-game-loop _main rename to all user objects (#4593)

The ios-game-loop entry transform renames the user's `_main` to
`__perry_user_main` so the perry runtime's `main()` (ios_game_loop.rs)
can own the process entry and drive UIApplicationMain. It located the
entry object via `filename.contains("main_ts")`, but with the object
cache enabled (the default) objects are named by content hash, so the
match fails, the rename is silently skipped, and two `_main` symbols
reach the linker. ld keeps the user's `_main`, drops the runtime's, and
the app launches straight into user code without ever calling
UIApplicationMain — the engine/window is never created and an
ios-game-loop app (e.g. Bloom Engine) crashes on launch ("Engine not
initialized"). Only manifested when the cache was cold-miss-named;
--no-cache happened to work, masking it.

Apply `objcopy --redefine-sym _main=__perry_user_main` to every user
object instead of guessing by filename. The redefine is a no-op on
objects that don't define `_main`, so exactly the one entry object is
rewritten regardless of how the cache named it.

fix(runtime): Proxy forwards [[GetPrototypeOf]] and instanceof to its target (#4645)

A Proxy is a small registered id, not a heap object. `Object.getPrototypeOf(proxy)`
mis-read it and returned `null`, and `proxy instanceof C` walked the proxy's
(non-existent) class chain and returned `false`. Per spec, with no
`getPrototypeOf` trap both forward to the target.

  - `js_object_get_prototype_of` / `Reflect.getPrototypeOf`: route a registered
    proxy to a new `js_proxy_get_prototype_of` (invoke the `getPrototypeOf` trap
    when present, else return the TARGET's prototype).
  - `js_instanceof` / `js_instanceof_dynamic`: unwrap nested proxies to the
    target before walking the class chain.

Drizzle aliases columns as `new Proxy(column, …)` and its brand check
`is(value, type)` does `value instanceof type` and reads
`Object.getPrototypeOf(value).constructor` — the null prototype crashed every
relational query on `null.constructor`. This unblocks that brand check (the
relational-query builder has further gaps tracked separately).

chain, nested proxies, member-access forwarding, the is()-style walk).

fix(runtime): route fused proxy method calls through the proxy, not the handle dispatcher (#4663)

generic dynamic dispatcher `js_native_call_method` with the proxy id intact.

native-module integer handle and routed to `handle_method_dispatch` (when an

`decoder.mapFromDriverValue(value)` on aliased-column proxies, so every
findMany column came back null.

the property read routes through `js_proxy_get`; only the fused form was
broken. Guard the dispatcher: when the receiver is a proxy, do
Get(proxy, method) via `js_proxy_get` then Call(method, proxy, args) with
`this` bound to the proxy, before any small-handle/pointer-deref path.

fix(typedarray): honor byteOffset/byteLength/buffer on ArrayBuffer views (#4103) (#4652)

`new T(buffer, byteOffset, length?)` for the non-Uint8Array kinds produced a
typed array that reported `byteOffset` 0, returned a freshly-copied
ArrayBuffer from `.buffer` (breaking identity), and did not alias the backing
store. The dynamic-constructor dispatch — `new TA(buffer, offset)` where `TA`
is a variable, as test262's `testWithTypedArrayConstructors` uses — dropped
the offset/length arguments entirely, so every view built that way reported
`byteOffset === 0` and the wrong length.

- Add a per-view side table (`TYPED_ARRAY_VIEW_META`: backing ArrayBuffer addr
  + byteOffset). `data_ptr`/`data_ptr_mut` resolve view entries into the
  backing store, so views truly alias the buffer and every sibling view
  (mutations are shared in both directions).
- `byteOffset` getter returns the real offset; `buffer` getter returns the
  stable backing ArrayBuffer via `js_typed_array_backing_buffer` — for plain
  (non-view) arrays it lazily materializes a backing buffer once and rebinds
  the array to alias it, so `.buffer` identity is stable and later mutation is
  shared (V8's model where every typed array is backed by an ArrayBuffer).
- The view constructor still seeds inline storage with the initial bytes so
  the optimized codegen fast path (which reads inline storage directly) stays
  correct — zero regression under optimized builds.
- The dynamic typed-array constructor now routes the `(buffer, offset,
  length?)` form through `js_typed_array_view` for all kinds.

byteOffset/byteLength/buffer/length + ctors/buffer-arg): 33/60 -> 43/60,

O = ToObject(this); len = LengthOfArrayLike(O); then indexed

Array exotics.

3rd argument) and didn't handle function/string/primitive receivers — failing
~127 test262 built-ins/Array/prototype cases.

on the ORIGINAL receiver value: ToObject (incl. Number/Boolean boxing),

an object/function/string slow path via the polymorphic helpers. Covers the
read-only/returning methods: forEach, map, filter, some, every, find,
findIndex, findLast, findLastIndex, reduce, reduceRight, indexOf, lastIndexOf,

3rd argument and binds thisArg; holes are honoured via HasProperty.

js_arraylike_* entry points; try_arraylike_receiver_method now routes the
.call/.apply/bound-local forms there instead of materializing. The hot member

fix(object): retain existing-property attributes in Object.defineProperty (#4697)

Per ES OrdinaryDefineOwnProperty / ValidateAndApplyPropertyDescriptor,
redefining an EXISTING own property must retain the attribute fields the
descriptor omits — they do NOT reset to the new-property `false` default.
`js_object_define_property` previously defaulted every omitted attribute to
`false` (writable to `has_accessor`) on every call, so converting an
enumerable data property to a getter (or back to a value) silently dropped
its enumerability and configurability.

This blocked zod v4 under `perry.compilePackages` (discussion #3438): its
`$ZodObject` constructor swaps the enumerable `shape` data property for a
self-replacing getter via `Object.defineProperty`, expecting `{ ...def }`
to still spread `shape`. Pre-fix `shape` became non-enumerable, the spread
dropped it, `normalizeDef`'s `value.shape` was undefined, and object parsing
crashed with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod')".

Fix: in both the object and closure define paths, capture the property's
current effective attributes before any mutation (all-true when no descriptor
side-table entry exists, matching the JS data-property default) and default
each omitted descriptor field to the existing value. New properties still
default to `false`, preserving prior behavior.

Adds test-files/test_issue_defineproperty_retain_attrs.ts (byte-matches
`node --experimental-strip-types`).

fix(promise): spec-compliant Promise.all/allSettled/race/any combinators (#4521) (#4701)

Replace the simplified native combinator stub with the observable ECMA-262
27.2.4.x algorithm in a new `promise/spec_combinators.rs`:

- NewPromiseCapability(C): constructs `new C(executor)` with the
  GetCapabilitiesExecutor "called twice"/"not callable" TypeErrors and the
  IsConstructor(C) guard (new `js_value_is_constructor`). The intrinsic
  Promise takes a native-capability fast path.
- GetPromiseResolve(C): reads `C.resolve` once (honoring getters/overrides),
  requires it callable.
- Per element: `nextPromise = Call(promiseResolve, C, «next»)` then
  `Invoke(nextPromise, "then", «resolveElement, reject»)` with REAL
  resolve/reject element closures carrying [[AlreadyCalled]] / [[Index]] /
  [[Values]] / [[Capability]] / [[RemainingElements]] (.length === 1,
  non-constructable).

The combinators are now `this`-sensitive, so:
- hir: exclude all/race/allSettled/any from the namespace-static
  `.call`/`.apply`/`.bind` thisArg-dropping rewrite (they read the `this`
  constructor); the reified static thunks read implicit-this.
- class_registry: a constructor returning a Promise (GC_TYPE_PROMISE) now
  overrides the implicit `this`, so the `function P(e){return new Promise(...)}`
  NewPromiseCapability shape yields that promise.

race →88/94, any →92/94. No regression in promise unit tests (48 pass) or
then/catch/finally. Remaining gaps are deeper features (class-extends-Promise
subclassing, lazy IteratorClose, native-promise `.then` expando).

fix(array): spec-complete Array.from constructor/iterator-close/define semantics (#4700)

test262 built-ins/Array/from (34/45 -> 43/45):

  `Construct(C)` (iterator branch) / `Construct(C, «len»)` (array-like
  branch) when `C` IsConstructor, instead of always producing a plain Array.
  Both user `function`s and `class`es are recognized as constructors.

  CreateDataPropertyOrThrow now runs IteratorClose (`iterator.return()`).

  non-configurable index) rethrow a TypeError.

  (overwrites a non-writable "0"), matching the spec's fresh-define.

  mapfn that mutates the source observes the updates.
- Generators / bare iterators (callable `.next`, `@@iterator` via class id)

fix(typedarray): brand-check %TypedArray%.prototype iterators + array-like/iterable constructor (#4702)

* fix(typedarray): brand-check %TypedArray%.prototype iterators + array-like/iterable constructor

Two %TypedArray% gaps surfaced by test262 built-ins/TypedArray:

1. `%TypedArray%.prototype.{entries,keys,values}` invoked directly on a
   prototype object (`Int8Array.prototype.entries()`,
   `TypedArray.prototype.values()`) must `ValidateTypedArray(this)` and throw
   a `TypeError` — the receiver is a prototype, not a real typed array. Codegen
   lowers `recv.entries()` to the eager `Expr::ArrayEntries` fast path
   regardless of the receiver's static type, so the brand check is added to the
   `js_array_{values,keys,entries}_iter_obj` C-ABI entry points via a new
   `object::is_typed_array_prototype` detector (intrinsic proto pointer or a
   per-kind proto carrying `OBJ_FLAG_TYPED_ARRAY_PROTO`).

2. `new TypedArray(object)` for a plain object now follows the spec: an object
   exposing `@@iterator` is iterated, otherwise it is read as an array-like
   (`ToLength(obj.length)` + indexed elements). Previously the object pointer
   was reinterpreted as an `ArrayHeader`, so `new Float64Array({length: 42,
   ...})` mis-read `length` (garbage, usually 1) and produced a length-1 view.
   The plain-object case routes through the shared `Array.from` materialization
   (which performs the iterator/array-like resolution and propagates user
   getter/iterator exceptions). `jsvalue_to_f64` also now runs `ToNumber`
   (`valueOf`) on object elements so `new Int32Array([{ valueOf: () => 5 }])`
   stores 5 rather than 0.

Unblocks the bulk of the suite, which constructs views via
`testWithTypedArrayConstructors`' array-like / iterable factories.

* fix(typedarray): spec-correct fill index coercion + ToBigInt(object) value (#4703)

* fix(typedarray): spec-correct fill index coercion + ToBigInt(object) value

`%TypedArray%.prototype.fill` mis-handled non-number index arguments. The old
`x.is_nan() ? default : x as isize` treated every NaN-boxed non-number
(`null`, `false`, `undefined`, an object) as `NaN` and fell back to the
*default*, so e.g. a `null` end became `len` instead of `ToIntegerOrInfinity(
null)` = 0. Indices now go through `ToIntegerOrInfinity` (`jsvalue_to_f64` +
`trunc`, with ±Infinity saturating to the bounds), and only an explicit
`undefined` end defaults to `len` (spec step 8a).

`ToBigInt` of an object also now runs `ToPrimitive(value, number)` (its
`Symbol.toPrimitive` / `valueOf` / `toString`) before converting, so
`bigIntView.fill({ valueOf() { return 7n } })` stores `7n` (and exactly once)
instead of throwing "Cannot convert NaN to a BigInt".

* fix(typedarray): %TypedArray%.from reads source before requiring a concrete ctor (#4704)

`%TypedArray%.from` evaluated `require_typed_array_constructor_this()` first, so
`TypedArray.from(source)` on the abstract `%TypedArray%` intrinsic threw Perry's
"needs a concrete typed array constructor" TypeError before the source was read.
Per spec the source is materialized first — its `@@iterator` invoked, or its
`length` getter + indexed elements evaluated — so a throwing user iterator /
length getter must propagate. The concrete-constructor requirement is now
resolved lazily and enforced only after materialization.

`js_typed_array_new_from_array` also snapshots the raw source values before any
element conversion, matching the spec's "collect the list, then convert" order:
`Int32Array.from([0, { valueOf() { src.length = 0; return 100 } }, 2])` now
yields `[0, 100, 2]` instead of dropping the trailing element when the
converting `valueOf` mutates the source.

fix(promise): assimilate object-literal thenables via own `then` data property (#4705)

* fix(promise): assimilate object-literal thenables via own `then` data property

js_assimilate_thenable only probed the class-method vtable for `then`, so
object-literal thenables ({ then: function(resolve, reject) { … } }) — whose
`then` is an own data property rather than a class method — passed through
unassimilated. Promise.resolve(thenable) / a combinator's per-element
PromiseResolve then fulfilled with the raw thenable object instead of
following its eventual state.

Add a fallback (assimilate_via_then_property): when the vtable probe misses,
read Get(value, "then"); if callable, allocate a wrapper promise and run
value.then(resolve, reject) per ECMA-262 PromiseResolveThenableJob. Absent /
non-callable `then` resolves plain (value returned unchanged), so non-thenable
objects are unaffected.

Fixes built-ins/Promise/all reject-immed, reject-deferred,
resolve-ignores-late-rejection, resolve-ignores-late-rejection-deferred and
the equivalent race/any/allSettled paths; also corrects Promise.resolve /
await on object-literal thenables generally.

* fix(promise): constructor-aware Promise.resolve / Promise.reject

Promise.resolve / Promise.reject ignored their `this` value and always
produced an intrinsic-Promise result, so Promise.resolve.call(C, x) /
Promise.reject.call(C, r) skipped the spec's NewPromiseCapability(C) step:
a non-constructor / non-object `this` did not throw, a custom constructor's
executor never ran, and the per-element resolve was never the receiver's.

Route the reified `Promise.resolve` / `Promise.reject` statics through new
constructor-aware entries (js_promise_resolve_spec / js_promise_reject_spec):

  * Promise.reject(r): NewPromiseCapability(this) then Call(reject, r).
  * Promise.resolve(x): require `this` be an Object; PromiseResolve(this, x)
    (return x when it is already a promise whose constructor is `this`,
    else NewPromiseCapability + Call(resolve, x)).

The intrinsic `Promise` keeps its optimized fast path — js_promise_resolved
(preserving identity AND object-literal thenable assimilation, which the
generic capability resolve does not do) and js_promise_rejected — so the
combinators' per-element resolve and the common direct-call path are
unchanged.

Fixes the Promise/{resolve,reject} ctx-non-ctor / ctx-non-object /
capability-executor-* / capability-invocation test262 clusters.

Also: allowlist crates/perry-runtime/src/typedarray/mod.rs (2062 LOC) in the
file-size gate — it crossed 2000 on current main via #4702 (independent of
this change); split tracked under #1435.

BigInt.prototype.toString and adjacent BigInt arithmetic:

- BigInt `++` / `--` were no-ops. The generic `Expr::Update` codegen emitted
  a bare `fadd(old, 1.0)`; on a NaN-boxed BigInt that propagates the BigInt's
  NaN payload unchanged, so `for (let i = 0n; i < n; i++)` never advanced
  (infinite loop). Route the type-uncertain update path through new
  `js_value_inc` / `js_value_dec`, which step by `1n` for BigInt operands and
  otherwise return the exact prior `v ± 1.0` (non-BigInt behaviour byte-identical).

- Mixed BigInt/Number relational compares (`10n < 11`) returned the wrong
  answer and could SIGSEGV. The codegen BigInt-compare fast path fired when
  *either* operand was a BigInt but passed *both* to `js_bigint_cmp`, which
  dereferences each as a BigInt pointer — a Number operand's NaN-boxed bits are
  not a valid pointer. Route relational ops through new `js_bigint_relational`,
  which inspects each operand's runtime tag and compares mathematical values
  (BigInt-vs-BigInt stays exact via `js_bigint_cmp`). Equality keeps its
  existing exact path.

- `BigInt.prototype.toString.length` was 1; spec is 0 (the radix is optional).
  Decouple the reported `.length` from the thunk's calling arity (which must
  stay 1 so the radix argument is still passed).

- A throwing/absent `ToPrimitive` on an object radix surfaced a `RangeError`
  instead of the `TypeError` it should (`(10n).toString({valueOf: undefined,
  toString: undefined})`). `radix_arg_to_number` now runs `ToPrimitive(number)`
  on an object radix and throws `TypeError` when no primitive is produced,
  before the range check. Also fixes the same case for Number radix coercion.

- `BigInt.prototype.toString(1)` threw `RangeError` instead of `TypeError`:
  the codegen radix fast path bypassed the brand-checking thunk. Skip the
  fast path when the receiver is literally `BigInt.prototype` so the call
  routes through `js_native_call_method` and `thisBigIntValue` runs first.
  Deliberately scoped to BigInt — `Number.prototype` IS a Number object
  (`Number.prototype.toString()` returns "0"), so it keeps the fast path.

Verified no regression: Number/prototype/toString parity is byte-identical
before/after (36.7%). Remaining 2 BigInt failures (prop-desc global descriptor,
wrapper-object getter-redefinition harness) are unrelated.

are stored internally under #-prefixed names — in a class instance's keys_array
(fields) and the class vtable/static tables (methods/accessors). They leaked into
every reflection/enumeration surface: Object.getOwnPropertyNames, Object.keys/
values/entries, getOwnPropertyDescriptor, hasOwnProperty, the in operator,
propertyIsEnumerable, JSON.stringify, object spread, and Object.assign. Per
ECMA-262 a private name is never an own string property.

all those sites. Instance-side filters are gated on class_id != 0 so plain object
literals that legitimately use #-prefixed string keys (e.g. {"#fff":"white"})
are unaffected; class-ref (prototype/constructor) paths filter unconditionally.

non-[A-Za-z0-9_] char with a single '_', so distinct private methods like #$,
#_, and #(U+2118) all mangled to the same perry_method_...__C____ symbol and
clang aborted the module with 'invalid redefinition of function'. Added an
injective sanitize_member() (escapes each non-alnum char to _<hex>_) and applied
it to the member-name component of method/getter/setter/static-method symbols,
which are module-local (vtable-dispatched by source name). sanitize() itself is
left unchanged because it also derives the module-symbol prefix, which must stay
byte-compatible with the driver's compute_module_prefix or cross-module perry_fn_
references go unresolved at link (native_link_cache) and native_region_slug
diverges (native-region-proof gate).

fix(object): ValidateAndApplyPropertyDescriptor for non-configurable redefines (#4722)

* fix(object): ValidateAndApplyPropertyDescriptor for non-configurable redefines

Object.defineProperty / Object.defineProperties now enforce the non-configurable
branch of ECMA-262 10.1.6.3 ValidateAndApplyPropertyDescriptor for ANY
non-configurable own property — not only properties on a frozen/sealed/
non-extensible object. A property is non-configurable either object-wide
(freeze/seal drop `configurable` on every key) or individually
(`defineProperty(o, k, {configurable:false})`); both surface through the per-key
descriptor side table and are now validated identically.

carried OBJ_FLAG_FROZEN|SEALED|NO_EXTEND, so an individually non-configurable
property escaped validation entirely: flipping configurable/enumerable,
switching data<->accessor, or re-enabling writable silently succeeded instead of
throwing `TypeError: Cannot redefine property: <k>`. Where the property was also
non-writable, the value-write fired first and threw the wrong
`Cannot assign to read only property` message.

  (no entry => default configurable:true => redefinition allowed).
- Factored the full algorithm into `validate_nonconfigurable_redefine`, shared
  by the plain-object AND function-object (closure) define paths, so
  `Object.defineProperty(fn, ...)` is validated too. Accessor get/set compared
  by underlying func_ptr (stored closures are receiver-rebound clones).

  which lifts the object's immutability flags + clears the stale per-key
  writable across the store (rooted so a GC evacuation restores flags on the
  relocated header). [[DefineOwnProperty]] is not subject to the [[Set]]
  writability check, so a validation-approved redefine of a configurable-but-
  non-writable value, or a same-value no-op on a frozen object, now stores/no-ops

fix(codegen): zero-fill inline-allocated object field slots (#4717) (#4726)

The inline bump-allocator fast path in lower_new wrote the GcHeader +
ObjectHeader + keys_ptr but left the max(field_count,8) field slots
uninitialized — diverging from js_object_alloc_with_parent (object/alloc.rs),
which deliberately fills every slot with undefined 'to prevent stale data from
previously freed GC objects from bleeding through.'

A field read-before-write on an inline-allocated instance (or a GC that scans
the still-constructing object) therefore observed stale arena bytes. When those
bytes were a previously-freed undefined/pointer, constructors crashed
nondeterministically with 'Cannot read properties of undefined' — e.g. marked's
this.defaults, or a destructured node:http createServer, on Linux.

Fix: emit a store of TAG_UNDEFINED to each of the alloc_field_count slots in the
merge block (covers both the fast bump path and the slow-alloc path), matching
the runtime allocator. Repro (6/6 on linux-x64, stock 0.5.1125): hono + marked,
register ~80 routes, then await import('node:http') -> createServer undefined.

perry publish only reconnected on a WebSocket *error*. A graceful Close
frame or a clean stream-end (which is what happens when the hub drops
connections while a job sits in the queue) just broke the receive loop —

  no server-side publish (TestFlight/App Store) was confirmed — i.e. the

fix(http): park async request handlers instead of synthesizing a premature empty response (#4728) (#4734)

A node:http handler that finishes the response on a later event-loop tick
(an outbound fetch(), a setTimeout, any await chain that calls res.end()
from a microtask/timer/tokio resolution) returns to process_pending
before res.end() has run. Pre-fix, process_pending then synthesized a
default empty 200 and freed the per-request handles immediately, so the
real res.end(...) later fired on a dropped handle (no-op) and the client
saw an empty/closed reply. Synchronous res.end() flushed inside the one
microtask drain, so static routes worked — the hang was specific to
deferred responses.

Fix: when the handler returns without ending the response, park the
request in an in-flight set instead of synthesizing + freeing. A reaper
(run each pump tick from js_node_http_server_process_pending) finalizes a
parked request once res.end() flushes the real response, or synthesizes
the default + frees the handles after a grace window mirroring Node's
requestTimeout (default 300s; 0/disabled falls back to the default) so a
handler that never responds can't pin a hyper connection forever. The
park/finalize tail is factored into finalize_or_park_request and shared
by the HTTP/1 and HTTPS dispatch paths. has_active now reports active
while any request is parked so the loop doesn't exit before a deferred
res.end() flushes. Parked handles stay in the registry and remain rooted
by the existing GC scanner.

Adds test-files/test_issue_4728_async_handler_res_end.ts covering both the
setTimeout->res.end() and fetch()-inside-handler paths plus clean
server.close() exit.

POINTER_TAG value holding a small registry id in [0x40000, 0x100000),
not a heap object pointer. The own-field probe floored at 0x10000, so a

is_valid_obj_ptr floors at 0x200_0000_0000 there; on Linux the floor is

js_object_get_field_by_name and the class_registry handle guards.

* fix(runtime): built-ins/Object test262 parity

the Object.* builtins, grouped by spec semantics:

1. Object.defineProperty descriptor field detection + spec retention:
   - Detect accessor vs data by OWN-FIELD PRESENCE on the descriptor (not
     is_undefined), so { get: undefined } is distinguished from omitting get.
   - Redefining an existing accessor with a partial descriptor now RETAINS the
     current get/set the descriptor omits; a generic descriptor (only
     enumerable/configurable) no longer clobbers an accessor or data value.

   never validated. Now stores per-index writable/enumerable/configurable in the
   side table (consulted by getOwnPropertyDescriptor), validates
   non-configurable redefines (throws TypeError), supports data<->accessor
   conversion on indices, and reports accessor descriptors for converted indices.

   bag and read each descriptor through [[Get]] (so accessors run); fixes
   Object.create(o, Math)/function-bag cases that wrongly read non-enumerable
   members (e.g. Math.E) as descriptors.

   non-extensible target) for both string- and symbol-keyed properties.

   (non-extensible + all own string/symbol props non-configurable, plus
   non-writable data props for frozen) instead of only checking the GC flag, so
   an empty preventExtensions'd object reports frozen/sealed.

enumerable/configurable counts as present. Perry tested own-key presence only,
so e.g. Object.defineProperty(o,k,childDesc) where childDesc inherits `value`

fix(class): static & computed accessors on class expressions (#4747)

* fix(class): static & computed accessors on class expressions

Static accessors (`static get x()` / `static set x(v)`) worked on class
declarations but were dropped or miscompiled on class expressions
(`var C = class {…}`). Four orthogonal gaps, all fixed against the
class-declaration oracle (Test262 accessor-name-{static,inst} now 84/84,
was 76/84):

1. Integer-like / empty string keys read via `IndexGet` on a class-ref or
   prototype-ref value masked off the `0x7FFE` INT32 tag, so the runtime
   never reached the static-accessor / prototype-vtable lookup —
   `(class { static get 0(){} })['0']` read `undefined` while `['x']`
   (which folds to `PropertyGet`) worked. Broadened the
   `preserve_class_ref_bits` detection in `index_get.rs` to a shared
   `index_object_is_class_or_proto_ref` helper that also recognizes a
   class-aliased `LocalGet` and `<class>.prototype`. The runtime re-masks
   `0x7FFD`/`0x7FFE` internally, so preserving the full bits is safe for
   heap objects too.

2. Class expressions never registered their accessor names
   (`register_class_accessor_names` ran only in `lower_class_decl`), so
   `C.prototype[''] = v` fell to a `RegisterPrototypeMethod` monkey-patch
   instead of invoking the instance setter. Mirrored the registration in
   `lower_class_from_ast`.

3. The `var C = class {…}` binding fast path emitted a bare `ClassRef` and
   dropped the computed-member registrations the general class-expression
   arm sequences in front of the value, so `static get [expr]()` accessors
   and computed methods never reached the side tables. Emit the same
   `RegisterClassComputed*` registrations in the fast path.

4. `static get 0(){} get 0(){}` (a name that is both a static and an
   instance accessor) classified the instance entry as static too — both
   emitted under the same `perry_static_…__get_0` symbol → LLVM "invalid
   redefinition". The static/instance split now keys on the accessor
   function's unique id (`static_accessor_fn_ids`) instead of its name,
   which cannot disambiguate a shared name.

fix(runtime): subclassing native Request/Response exposes working body methods (v0.5.1130) (#4756)

A Web-Fetch Request/Response in Perry is a native registry handle (a small id
NaN-boxed as a pointer) whose methods are resolved by native handle dispatch,
not via a JS prototype chain. `class X extends Request {}` + `new X(...)`
produced an ordinary heap JS object with no link to a native handle, so
`sub.text` was `undefined`, calling it threw, and `sub instanceof Request` was
`false`. This breaks `@hono/node-server` (`class Request extends GlobalRequest`).

Fix: `super(...)` on a Request/Response parent now allocates the underlying
native handle and stashes its id on `this` under `__perry_fetch_handle__`
(mirrors the Web-Streams `__perry_stream_handle__` mechanism). Wired across all
construction paths:
- direct `class extends Request/Response`: codegen super arm + lower_new
  no-ctor hook -> js_request/response_subclass_init;
- aliased parent (`extends GlobalRequest`, where GlobalRequest = global.Request):
  runtime-value super() routes through js_fetch_or_value_super, which identifies
  the parent constructor and attaches;
- dynamic class-expression / ClassRef construction: a fetch-parent side table
  (recorded at js_register_class_parent_dynamic) drives a construction-time
  attach in js_new_function_construct.

At access time, body methods (call + value read), inherited property getters,
and `instanceof` on a subclass instance are forwarded to the native handle.
Non-subclassed Request/Response and other native-builtin subclasses are
unaffected. Regression test: tests/test_request_subclass_body.sh.

   `nativeFunctionMatcher.js` — the `\p{ID_Start}`/`\p{ID_Continue}`
   shims used to validate `Function.prototype.toString` output across
   the whole `built-ins/` tree — spells its identifier classes this
   way, so *every* `assertNativeFunction` call threw `SyntaxError` at
   regex-literal evaluation, failing ~20 toString conformance cases
   (methods, getters/setters, generators, async, private methods,
   bound functions, symbol-named built-ins). `fold_surrogate_pairs`
   now rewrites a high-surrogate unit immediately followed by a
   low-surrogate unit into the astral scalar range(s) it encodes
   (`\x{..}` form). It fires only on genuine pairs, so patterns that
   compile today are byte-for-byte unchanged; surrogate-pair *escapes*
   that previously errored now compile (and match correctly).

2. `Function.prototype.bind` `.name` derivation (closure/dispatch.rs).
   The bound function's name read the declared name from the func-ptr
   registry, which is empty for an anonymous target whose name was set
   via `Object.defineProperty(fn, "name", …)` or a prior `.bind()`.
   Per spec, `.name` is `"bound " + Get(Target, "name")`, so bind now
   reads the target's `name` *property* first (falling back to the
   declared name for plain named functions). Fixes `instance-name.js`
   and `instance-name-chained.js` (`f.bind().bind().name` ===
   "bound bound target").

node-rejects/perry-runs-clean cases driven by Node's CommonJS
top-level `this`=module.exports (and strict `.caller`) harness
semantics — un-winnable artifacts that were timeout false-passes in
the first, heavily-loaded sweep; neither fix can affect them.

fix(class): method-as-value identity + injective private-symbol mangling (test262 class/elements) (#4764)

* fix(class): method-as-value identity + injective private-symbol mangling (test262 class/elements)

Two root causes behind the bulk of language/{statements,expressions}/class/elements
failures:

1. LLVM symbol collision on private/special member names. `sanitize()` collapsed
   every non-[A-Za-z0-9_] character to a single `_`, so distinct private names
   (`#$`, `#_`, `#℘`, `#\u{6F}`, ZWJ/ZWNJ escapes) all mangled to the same
   `perry_method_..__C__..` symbol and clang rejected the module with
   `invalid redefinition of function`. Made `sanitize()` injective: pure
   `[A-Za-z0-9_]` names are byte-identical as before (so every existing symbol and
   cross-module reference is unchanged), and any name with a special character is
   hex-escaped (`u_` tag + `_<hex>_` per non-alnum char) so distinct source names
   always yield distinct symbols. Drops compile-fails in this suite from ~877 to
   ~27.

2. Method-as-value identity. A class method is a single shared function object, so
   `c.m === C.prototype.m` and `c1.m === c2.m` must hold, but every method-as-value
   read minted a fresh per-receiver BOUND_METHOD closure. Routed user-class
   method-as-value reads through one cached canonical per (owner_class, name)
   (`class_prototype_method_value_for_name`), captured the owner's prototype-ref as
   a marker, and taught `dispatch_bound_method` to use the call-site `this`
   (IMPLICIT_THIS) for that marker — so `const f = c.m; f()` runs with the spec
   `this` and the `this.m = this.m.bind(this)` idiom still rebinds correctly.
   An own data property of the same name still shadows the prototype method (the
   bind idiom installs an own `m`); the shadow check is skipped for the prototype
   object itself, which legitimately stores its methods as own fields.
   Actual `obj.method(args)` calls are unaffected — they lower straight to
   js_native_call_method with the real receiver.

Net: language class/elements parity 31.9% -> ~50% (pass 904 -> ~1420), zero new
real compile-fails (the harness's "Wrote executable" mis-bucketing under load
aside).

Files: perry-codegen/src/codegen/helpers.rs (sanitize),
perry-runtime/src/object/native_module.rs (canonical + own-prop shadow +
build_bound_method_closure split), object/class_registry.rs
(method_owner_class_id, is_registered_class_prototype_object),
object/field_get_set.rs (route through js_class_method_bind),
closure/dispatch.rs (call-site this for canonical marker).

* fix(codegen): split injective sanitize_member from sanitize to preserve cross-module symbols

The previous commit made `sanitize` itself injective, which desynced cross-module
symbol references: a module prefix is `sanitize(module_name)` at the definition
site but importing modules re-derive the source prefix from stored metadata, so
`util.ts` defined `perry_fn_u_util_2e_ts__answer` while `main.ts` referenced
`perry_fn_util_ts__answer` — undefined-symbol link failures (broke the
native_link_cache integration test and the compiler-output-regression gate).

Revert `sanitize` to its original lossy mapping (every special char -> `_`), which
keeps module-prefix and static-field-global symbols byte-identical to main, and add
a separate injective `sanitize_member` used ONLY for the class-name / method-name /
static-field-name COMPONENTS of `perry_method_*` / `perry_static_*` symbols. For
pure `[A-Za-z0-9_]` names `sanitize_member` is byte-identical to `sanitize`, so
ordinary symbols are unchanged; names with special characters (private members like
`#$`, `#℘`, `#\u{6F}`, ZWJ/ZWNJ escapes) get an unambiguous `u_`+`_<hex>_` encoding
so distinct names never collide. Applied consistently at every definition AND
reference site (scoped_method_name, scoped_static_method_name, the string_pool
method/getter/setter registrations, the cross-module method/static-field/static-
method declarations).

Restores: cross-module linking, the native_link_cache test, instance private-member
compiles (no clang redefinition), and static private fields/methods (no
`redefinition of global` — these collided on main too).

fix(runtime): @hono/node-server c.req.text()/.json()/.formData() on POST/PUT (#4765)

A Perry-compiled Hono app served by @hono/node-server threw "TypeError: text is
not a function" on every body-reading POST/PUT route. Three layers:

1. The `var C = class {...}` fast path (lower/stmt.rs) lowered the class to a
   bare ClassRef and never emitted RegisterClassParentDynamic (unlike the
   general class-expression and Decl::Class arms). node-server's
   `var Request = class extends GlobalRequest {}` (GlobalRequest = global.Request)
   never registered its fetch-builtin parent, so the subclass instance got no
   native fetch handle. Emit the dynamic parent registration there too.

2. js_fetch_or_value_super identified the parent kind only from the runtime
   parent value, which re-lowered to undefined for an aliased module-var parent
   at super-time. Fall back to the fetch-parent kind registered on the instance
   class id (captured at module init).

3. Body methods were not readable as values: r.text / computed r["text"]
   (node-server uses this[getRequestCache]()[k]()) returned undefined. Return a
   bound method that re-dispatches to the handle. Drain a ReadableStream request
   body via js_response_body_init_ptr, and expose node:http IncomingMessage
   rawBody (the collected body Buffer) so node-server uses its synchronous body
   path (avoids the data-less Readable.toWeb stub, #1540).

Adds tests/test_request_subclass_stream_body.sh. GET unaffected; 50-POST burst
stable; text/json/formData return the real body.

fix: class async / async-generator method test262 parity (#4768)

Brings the 8 in-class async-method / async-generator-method test262 dirs
from 266/516 (51.6%) to 408/516 (79.1%) pass, zero regressions.

Root causes fixed:

1. Async-generator instances had no [Symbol.asyncIterator]. `for await` over
   a class async-gen method hung/yielded nothing (GetIterator(obj, async)
   could not resolve the iterator). Install [Symbol.asyncIterator] (returning
   `this`) on %AsyncGenerator.prototype% (global_this.rs). The sync
   %Generator.prototype% deliberately gets none — the sync for-of path does
   not bind implicit-this, so a this-returning thunk would break `for (x of
   gen())`.

   `yield* asyncIterable` inside an async generator silently produced nothing
   or threw "next is not a function". Made the yield* desugaring async-aware
   (linearize.rs): use GetAsyncIterator and `await` each delegated
   next()/result when the enclosing generator is async (threaded via a
   thread-local set in lower.rs).

   @@asyncIterator, or a callable one returning a non-Object, must throw
   TypeError (not fall back to the sync iterator). Rewrote js_get_async_iterator
   to follow the spec ordering (iterator.rs).

4. Missing trailing arguments were padded with NaN instead of `undefined` in
   the dynamic vtable / static-method dispatch (class_registry.rs
   call_vtable_method + call_static_method). Default parameters lower to
   `param === undefined ? <default> : param`, so a hole padded with NaN never
   triggered the default (e.g. `C.prototype.method` called with fewer args).

5. Private methods never applied parameter defaults at all (direct OR via a
   `this.#m` value): lower_private_method built `param.default` but never
   prepended the `if (param === undefined) param = default` prologue that
   public methods/constructors emit. Added it (private_members.rs). Fixes all
   private method kinds (sync/async/gen/async-gen) and async-private-gen dstr
   default tests.

6. Latent: small typed arrays are raw-alloc'd with no object GcHeader, so
   js_object_is_extensible read garbage `_reserved` and non-deterministically
   reported `false`. Integer-indexed exotic objects are extensible by default;
   short-circuit TAs/buffers to extensible (object_ops_frozen.rs).

* fix: class return-override, TDZ-on-this, super accessors, subclass-builtins instanceof, method default-params

- Inline constructor return-override: explicit return in a (derived) ctor
  no longer emits a function-level ret (was an LLVM result-type compile error);

  derived+primitive->TypeError).
- TDZ-on-this: derived ctor that never calls super() throws ReferenceError.
- Reflective/static method calls pad missing args with undefined (was NaN / 0),

* fix(codegen): apply ctor return-override at construction completion, not at return

The return-override check (object? / derived-primitive TypeError) was emitted

fix(codegen): `new <imported-function>()` runs the constructor body (zod v4 checks; #4698) (#4769)

`new F(args)` where `F` is a function — or a `const`/`let` holding a closure
value — imported from another module silently produced an empty object: the
constructor body never ran, so `this.x = …` and `Object.defineProperty(this, …)`
writes were lost. This is the zod-v4 `TypeError: Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'onattach')` crash (#4698): every string/number schema with a
check (`.min`/`.max`/`.length`/`.regex`/`.gt`/`.lt`/…) builds its check via
`new checks.$ZodCheckMinLength(def)` across the core/checks.ts → core/api.ts
module boundary (where `checks` is `import * as`), and the check came back with
its non-enumerable `_zod` (and everything else) gone.

An imported binding that isn't a registered class fell through to an empty-object
placeholder instead of `js_new_function_construct` (binds `this`, runs the body,
returns the populated instance). The fix lives entirely in codegen: at
HIR-lowering time an imported class and an imported function are indistinguishable
(both unknown to `lookup_class`), and the cross-module class-inline machinery in
`collect_modules` relies on `new <ImportedClass>()` staying as
`Expr::New { class_name }` — so HIR must not reroute it.

- perry-codegen lower_call/new.rs: when `lower_new` finds no class for the name
  but the name resolves to an imported binding (`import_function_prefixes`,
  excluding V8-fallback specifiers), lower it as an `ExternFuncRef` value and
  construct via `js_new_function_construct` instead of the empty placeholder.
  Imported classes are in `ctx.classes` and take the construction path, so they
  never reach this fallback (guarded by the existing
  `dependency_is_transformed_before_importer_for_cross_module_inline` test).
- perry-codegen expr/v8_interop.rs (`try_static_class_name`) + expr/new_dynamic.rs:
  `new ns.Foo()` over a namespace import only takes the class path when `Foo`
  actually names a known class; a closure-valued `const` export (zod's
  `$ZodCheckMinLength = $constructor(...)`) falls through to the NewDynamic
  function-construct route (`ExternFuncRef` added to its callee set). Real
  namespace-imported classes and re-exported builtins are unaffected.

`z.string().min(2).parse("hello")` now prints `hello`; `.max`/`.length`/`.regex`/
`.gt`/`.lt` and nested object schemas with checks match Node byte-for-byte. Full
`perry` bin test suite (469) green. The `safeParse` error-path / `.email()`
error-formatting failures noted in #4698 are a separate, still-open issue. Refs
#793.

* fix(hir): chained optional-call `foo?.bar?.(args)` null-checks the function value (#4699)

A chained optional call whose callee is itself an optional chain only
short-circuited on the receiver (`foo`), never on the function value
(`foo.bar`). When `foo` was a valid object but `foo.bar` was undefined,
the lowering emitted `foo == null ? undefined : foo.bar(args)`, so
`undefined(args)` was invoked and threw "TypeError: X is not a function".

This blocked zod v4 `safeParse` on the validation-failure path, where
`finalizeIssue` probes `iss.inst?._zod.def?.error?.(iss)` /
`config.localeError?.(iss)` error-map callbacks that are normally absent.

Fix (HIR-only): flag the `foo?.bar?.(args)` shape and wrap the call in an
additional LooseEq null-check on the function value, in both the
non-nested and nested-Conditional (deep-chain) paths. The plain
`obj.method?.(args)` shape is untouched.

Adds test_issue_4699_optional_call_chain.ts (matches Node byte-for-byte).

* fix(codegen): `new (A ?? B)(args)` runs the constructor body (#4699)

zod v4 `safeParse` builds its error via `new (_Err ?? errors.$ZodError)(issues)`.
The `??` callee lowers to `Expr::Logical { Coalesce }`, which the NewDynamic
codegen handler did not include in `routes_through_function_construct` — so
`new (A ?? B)(args)` fell through to the Case-4 empty-object placeholder, the
constructor body never ran, and `r.error.issues` was undefined.

Fix: add `Expr::Logical` to the match. The logical expression lowers to a
single closure value that `js_new_function_construct` handles like a LocalGet
callee (binds `this`, runs the body), falling back to the class_id=0 empty
object if non-callable. Covers `new (A ?? B)()`, `new (A || B)()`,
`new (A && B)()`.

Adds test_issue_4699_new_logical_callee.ts. zod safeParse error is now
readable: r.error.issues populated, name 'ZodError', matching Node.

fix: standalone async-generator test262 parity (57.7% → 93.0%) (#4777)

* fix(hir): async-generator destructuring param + default NamedEvaluation parity

Standalone async-generator (and other) expressions dropped two destructuring
behaviors that declarations already had:

1. A param that is both a destructuring pattern AND has a default
   (`async function*([x,y,z]=[1,2,3]){}`) lowered only the default guard, not
   the destructuring binding — x/y/z resolved to
   js_throw_reference_error_unresolved_get. lower_arrow / lower_fn_expr /
   nested_fn_decl now unwrap Pat::Assign to the inner pattern before
   is_destructuring_pattern, mirroring lower_fn_decl.

2. Destructuring defaults skipped NamedEvaluation: `[fn = function(){}]` left
   fn.name empty instead of "fn". pattern_binding now threads the single-name
   binding into ctx.assignment_inferred_name for anonymous fn/arrow/class
   defaults, at all three default sites (array elem, Pat::Assign, object
   shorthand).

* fix(transform): run generator param binding synchronously at call time

Per spec, generator/async-generator parameter binding
(FunctionDeclarationInstantiation) runs synchronously when the function is
called — before the generator object is created — so an iterator /
RequireObjectCoercible / TDZ error during destructuring or default evaluation
throws at call time, not on the first .next(). Perry prepended the param
prologue (default guards + destructuring binding) to the body, which the
generator transform linearized into state 0 of .next(); a test that only calls
f(g) (expecting a synchronous throw) never ran it.

Lowering now records the prologue length per generator func_id
(Module.gen_param_prologue_len); the generator transform lifts those leading
statements out of the state machine and runs them in the outer wrapper, boxing
their bound locals so the state machine still reads the destructured values.
Gated on is_generator (plain async functions keep reject-not-throw semantics)
and inert when there is no destructuring/default param (prologue_len 0).

async-generator dirs: rt-fail 181->21, parity 73.6%->91.7%.

* fix(transform): async-generator yield awaits its operand

Per spec, `yield E` in an async generator is AsyncGeneratorYield(? Await(E)) —
the operand is awaited before being delivered, so `yield Promise.reject(x)`
throws x into the generator and `yield Promise.resolve(v)` yields v (not the
promise). Perry yielded the raw operand. A pre-pass (after hoist_yields)
rewrites each statement-level non-delegate `yield E` into
`let __ayield = await E; yield __ayield`; the await reuses the existing
suspension machinery. yield* delegation is untouched (it awaits via
delegate_await).

* chore: cargo fmt + allowlist generator/lower.rs (>2000 LOC)

The standalone async-generator parity work (param-prologue lift + per-yield
operand Await) grew generator/lower.rs past the 2000-line CI gate; add it to
the check_file_size.sh allowlist (split tracked under #1435).

* fix(runtime): call a method stored as an own accessor (getter)

A fused method call `o.next(args)` where `next` is an own accessor
(`{ get next() { return fn } }` or Object.defineProperty get) mis-resolved to
undefined — js_native_call_method read the raw field slot (no callable for an
accessor-only property) instead of invoking the getter. The decomposed form
`const f = o.next; f(args)` already worked via the getter-aware property read.
Add an early accessor check: invoke the getter (this=receiver), then call the
resolved function. Gated on the ACCESSORS_IN_USE hot-path flag. Unblocks yield*
over a sync/async iterator whose next/value/done are getters (test262
yield-star-* with `get next()`).

Also add gen_param_prologue_len: HashMap::new() to the Module struct literals in
perry-codegen{,-arkts} test fixtures (new Module field).

fix(hir): class field/element initializer test262 parity (v2, native-region-safe) (#4779)

Lifts language/{statements,expressions}/class/elements parity 50.1% → 75.5%
(+722 tests) on the test262 class/elements suite, with the native-region-proof
compiler-output-regression gate green and zero real regressions.

Root causes fixed:

1. `this` was undefined inside static methods. A static method invoked as
   `C.m()` binds `this` to the class constructor; codegen now seeds the
   static-method `this` slot with the class-ref value and sets `class_stack`,
   so `this.x` / `this.#x()` / `this[k]` resolve. (compile_static_method)

2. Private (`#x`) elements leaked into reflection. They physically live in a
   class instance's keys_array / on the static side but are never reflectable.
   Hidden (gated on class_id != 0, so `{"#fff":1}` literals stay visible) from
   Object.keys/values/entries, getOwnPropertyNames, getOwnPropertyDescriptor,
   hasOwnProperty, JSON.stringify, and object spread / Object.assign — on both
   instances and the class constructor (class-ref).

3. Static field/element initializers never ran for class EXPRESSIONS
   (`var C = class { static x = 1 }`): the `var C = class {…}` fast path and
   the general class-expression arm emitted the ClassRef binding but not the
   inline static-field/static-block init the declaration path emits, so reads
   saw the uninitialized (0.0) slot. They now emit inline StaticFieldSet /
   ClassStaticSymbolSet / static-block calls in source order; the per-evaluation
   ClassExprFresh path is reserved for class expressions inside function bodies
   (factories) where freshness is actually needed.

4. Dynamic property get/set on a runtime class-ref VALUE returned/dropped
   silently. `C[key]` / `C[key] = v` where `C` is a runtime class-ref (e.g. a
   function parameter — propertyHelper's `isWritable(C, name)`) fell through to
   the not-a-pointer `undefined`/no-op path. js_dyn_index_get/set now handle the
   0x7FFE tag; the codegen index get/set paths preserve class-ref tag bits at
   runtime (classref_preserving_handle) for runtime-unknown receivers; and the
   array string-key setter guards class-ref receivers (routing to the by-name
   object setter) instead of dereferencing them as a GC header.

Native-region-proof: the compiler-output-regression `native-region-proof` suite
reports status: pass with NO failed_workloads on a debug build locally (the
config CI uses). The class-field codegen change (static-method `this` slot +
runtime class-ref tag select on dynamic property access) does not perturb the
generic array/buffer native-region proofs.

Zero regressions: broad `built-ins language` shard 0/12 went 76.9% → 77.9%
(+61 gains); the 40 apparent shard "regressions" all pass in isolation on both
this branch and origin/main (parallel-run timeout flakiness), confirmed by

fix(transform,runtime): yield* delegation next-capture + object-literal thenable await (#4783)

Spec-aligns `yield *` async/sync delegation and fixes a core async/await
gap that blocked the delegated async-iterator protocol.

test262 (vs origin/async-generator-parity, 0 regressions):
- language/{expressions,statements}/async-generator: 820 -> 838 pass (92.3% -> 94.4%)
- built-ins/Promise: 347 -> 357 pass (60.5% -> 62.2%)  [thenable fix, bonus]
- language/{expressions,statements}/generators: no change, 0 regressions

Root causes addressed:

1. [[NextMethod]] captured once (perry-transform/generator/linearize.rs).
   The `yield*` desugar re-read `del_iter.next` on every loop iteration,
   re-running the iterator's `get next` accessor and an extra property read
   per step. Spec (GetIterator) reads `next` exactly once and reuses the
   captured method. Factored the 3 near-identical desugar sites (statement
   `yield* e`, `return yield* e`, `let x = yield* e`) into one
   `emit_yield_star_loop` helper that captures `__del_next = __del_iter.next`
   once and invokes `__del_next.call(__del_iter, arg)` (reads
   Function.prototype.call, not the iterator's getters; binds `this` for
   builtin/inherited `next` thunks). Falls back to method dispatch when the
   captured value isn't callable (string/typed-array iterators expose no
   readable `next`).

2. First inner pull passes an explicit `undefined`, not argless. Spec inits
   `received = NormalCompletion(undefined)`, so every inner `next()` — including
   the first — gets one argument (test262 yield-star-*-next assert
   `next args.length === 1`).

3. async-from-sync wrapper caches the sync `[[NextMethod]]`
   (perry-runtime/array/iterator.rs). CreateAsyncFromSyncIterator reads `next`
   once; the wrapper re-read (and re-ran the getter) on every `next()` call.

4. Object-literal thenables now assimilate in `await`/`Promise.resolve`
   (perry-runtime/promise/combinators.rs). `js_assimilate_thenable` returned
   early for class_id==0 objects (plain `{ then() {} }` / `{ get then() {} }`),
   so `await { then(r){r(v)} }` resolved with the thenable itself. Route those
   through the existing property-based fallback (spec PromiseResolveThenableJob:
   Get(value,"then") + IsCallable, independent of storage). Also pass the
   resolving functions to user `then` as NaN-boxed function values so
   `typeof onFulfilled === "function"` holds.

The delegated yielded value is intentionally NOT awaited: current
AsyncGeneratorYield does not await its operand (only the `next()` result is
awaited), so a delegated promise value flows through un-unwrapped
(yield-star-promise-not-unwrapped).

fix(runtime): bind this=iterable when calling [Symbol.iterator]() (#4788)

js_get_iterator invoked the [Symbol.iterator]() factory via js_closure_call0
after clone_closure_rebind_this, which only rebinds a closure that *captures*

factory with the wrong this. Set IMPLICIT_THIS=iterable around the call (spec

fix(codegen): destructured-value copies no longer truncate to i32 (#4766 regression) (#4785)

A value pulled from an array binding pattern (const [k, v] = pair, or the
parameter form ([k, v]) => ...) and then copied into another local
(const cb = v) read back as -2147483648 (i32::MIN) instead of the original
object/string; calling a method on it threw
"TypeError: (number).<method> is not a function". This broke every drizzle-orm
schema (Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(cols).map(([name, col]) => { col.setName(name); ... }))),
crashing apps at startup with "(number).setName is not a function".

Regressing commit: #4766 (iterator-protocol array destructuring), which emits a
scaffolding local `let __destruct_N = undefined` per binding element. That
mutable+undefined shape is one of collect_integer_let_ids's seeds (it targets
the clampIdx do-while pattern), so the scaffolding local was optimistically
seeded into integer_locals. The forward closure then propagated integer-ness
down the init-only copy chain (cbBase = __destruct -> cb = cbBase). The
disqualify fixed point only prunes locals via non-int LocalSet writes, so it
removed the scaffolding local (writes are undefined/step.value) but never
re-validated the forward-propagated copies (their Let-init is their sole
definition, no LocalSet). The second hop (const cb = cbBase) ended up both in
integer_locals and strictly_i32_bounded_locals, qualifying for an i32 shadow
slot; storing the NaN-boxed value did fptosi(NaN) = i32::MIN.

Fix: in the disqualify fixed point, also re-validate any candidate Let with no
LocalSet write (collect_non_int_init_only_let_ids) -- every const, plus
never-reassigned lets such as the mutable bindings the parameter-destructuring
path emits -- against its defining init over the current candidate set. When the
source local is disqualified the copy is pruned too, cascading through the
chain. Locals with real int-producing LocalSet writes (clampIdx's xx) stay
governed by those writes, preserving the image_convolution i32 fast paths.

Regression tests in collectors/hir_facts.rs cover the immutable and mutable
(parameter) destructure-copy chains plus an over-pruning guard.

Refs #793.

fix(runtime): function-object descriptors + proxy SetIntegrityLevel parity (#4789)

built-ins/Object test262: route Object.defineProperty descriptor field reads
through a value-level [[Get]] keyed on the descriptor value, and route
Object.seal/freeze/isSealed/isFrozen proxy receivers through trap dispatch.

Cluster 5 (function-object descriptors): a function used as a property
descriptor (Object.defineProperty(o, k, funObj)) is a closure, not an

walk a closure's own dynamic props nor its [[Prototype]] (Function.prototype),

descriptors are unchanged.

proxy registered-id pointer and segfaulted. They now run SetIntegrityLevel via
the [[PreventExtensions]]/[[OwnPropertyKeys]]/[[GetOwnProperty]]/

Object.isSealed/isFrozen run the full TestIntegrityLevel (IsExtensible +
per-key GetOwnProperty in ownKeys order) instead of an extensibility-only
approximation.

fix(watchos/visionos): find the entry object by symbol, not filename (#4799)

The watchOS (`--features watchos-swift-app` / `watchos-game-loop`) and
visionOS link paths rename the user module's `_main` to `__perry_user_main`
(or `_perry_main_init`) with objcopy so the platform's Swift/Rust `@main`
shell owns the real entry point. They located that object by matching the
input file stem (`main.ts` -> `main_ts.o`), but per-module objects are
content-hash-named in `.perry-cache/objects/<hash>.o`, so the match silently
failed, the objcopy no-op'd, and the link died with undefined
`__perry_user_main` (workaroundable only with `--no-cache`, and even then
flakily).

Find the entry object by querying each object's symbol table for a defined
`_main` via `nm` instead; fall back to the old stem heuristic if `nm` is
unavailable. Applies to both the watchOS and visionOS branches.

fix(runtime): for-of/spread over a Headers handle no longer segfaults (#4800)

js_get_iterator calls is_builtin_iterator_class_id(raw_ptr) to short-circuit
values that are already iterators. That helper only floored its pointer-validity
check at GC_HEADER_SIZE + 0x1000 (0x1008), then dereferenced
[raw_ptr - GC_HEADER_SIZE] as a GcHeader.

Web-Fetch handles (Headers, Request.headers, Response.headers) are NaN-boxed
POINTER values whose payload is a small registry id in [0x40000, 0x100000), not
a heap pointer. Such an id is well above the 0x1008 floor, so it sailed past the
guard and the runtime dereferenced unmapped memory -> SIGSEGV.

This was latent until #4786 switched the for...of lowering for opaque
(non-Array/Map/Set/string) iterables from the eager js_for_of_to_array path to
the lazy iterator protocol (GetIterator(obj) -> js_get_iterator). Iterating a
Headers handle then routed through js_get_iterator for the first time, e.g.
@hono/node-server buildOutgoingHttpHeaders (for (const [k, v] of headers) on the
response Headers). The result: every HTTP response from a Perry-compiled Hono
app segfaulted on Linux x86_64 - even GET /healthz. macOS arm64 masked it via a
higher heap floor.

Fix: raise the floor in is_builtin_iterator_class_id to 0x100000, the canonical
small-handle-band threshold already used by Array.isArray and
try_dispatch_instance_method_value. A real built-in iterator is always a heap
object well above this floor, so no true match is lost; native handles in the
band are now correctly rejected and fall through to the normal
[Symbol.iterator]() dispatch (which returns the entries array, wrapped by
array_values_iter). Same bug family as the earlier
js_object_get_own_field_or_undef handle-floor fix
(test_headers_handle_field_probe_segfault).

Adds tests/test_headers_iterator_handle_segfault sh/ts: for-of (with
array-destructuring) and spread over Headers, plus Response.headers and
Request.headers, all laundered through any so codegen routes them through the
generic runtime iterator. Pre-fix: SIGSEGV. Post-fix: PASS.

fix(hir): expression-semantics test262 parity (new/delete/call/spread/compound-assign) (#4802)

Targets language/expressions/{new,delete,call,super,compound-assignment,
logical-assignment} test262 failures. Root causes + fixes, zero real regressions
(verified by failure-set diff vs origin/main on the built-ins+language shard;
the only deltas are flaky contention compile-fails that wrote their executable):

1. Spread via the iterator protocol. `js_array_like_to_array` (the spread
   funnel for `f(...x)`, `new C(...x)`, console.* spread) only handled
   arrays/arguments/typed-arrays/buffers and reinterpret-cast any other object
   as a raw ArrayHeader — so a generic iterable with a custom `[Symbol.iterator]`
   yielded nothing. Drive GetIterator → IteratorStep → IteratorValue for generic
   iterables (real arrays keep the fast path), so spread collects yielded values
   and iterator/`.next()` errors propagate. Fixes call/new spread-* clusters.

2. Unresolved identifier in compound/logical assignment. `x *= 1` /
   `unresolved ||= y` with `x` undeclared hard-errored at compile time
   ("Undefined variable in compound assignment") instead of throwing a catchable
   runtime ReferenceError. The compound-assign read helper now resolves the
   target identifier through the same path as a bare read (GetValue semantics:
   known globals resolve, truly-unresolvable names throw ReferenceError).

3. `delete` semantics:
   - `delete super.prop` / `delete super[expr]` → ReferenceError (new
     js_throw_reference_error_super_delete); the computed key is still evaluated.
   - `delete null.x` / `delete undefined[k]` → TypeError via
     RequireObjectCoercible on the base (key evaluated first for the computed
     form, per EvaluatePropertyAccessWithExpressionKey ordering).
   - Strict-mode `delete` of a non-configurable property → TypeError (new
     js_delete_result boxes the success bit and throws when refused in strict
     mode; sloppy keeps yielding false).

4. `new` spread + primitive-literal callees (carried over): `new C(...spread)`
   preserves spread positions (NewDynamicSpread) and `new <primitive-literal>`
   throws "is not a constructor".

fix(android): make perry-ui-android resilient to a shadowed JNI_OnLoad (#4804)

When the final .so also links a native library that defines its own
JNI_OnLoad (e.g. a Bloom-engine game disabling MTE), ELF keeps only one
JNI_OnLoad and --allow-multiple-definition picks whichever was seen first.
If the library's wins, Perry's JNI_OnLoad never runs, so neither MTE was
disabled (breaking 48-bit NaN-boxed pointers) nor was the JavaVM cached.

Perry's JNI entry points already bind by direct export name (no
RegisterNatives), so they still resolve regardless. This adds two safety
nets so the rest of the init does too:
- a .init_array constructor (PERRY_DISABLE_MTE_CTOR) that disables heap
  tagging at dlopen, independent of which JNI_OnLoad survives linking;
- jni_bridge::ensure_vm(&env), called from nativeInit, which derives and
  caches the JavaVM from the live JNIEnv when JNI_OnLoad didn't.

fix: eval-code / function-code / arguments-object test262 parity (#4808)

Five root causes across the inliner, class static/accessor dispatch,
spread-call lowering, and eval completion-value folding.

1. Inliner substituted `this`/`new.target` across the call boundary
   (function-code 10.4.3 strict-`this`). `is_inlinable` rejected `super`
   but not bare `this`/`new.target`, so `function g(){ return typeof this }`
   got its body spliced into a sloppy caller, rebinding `this` to the
   caller's global object — `typeof this` flipped "undefined"→"object".
   New `body_references_dynamic_this` guard rejects such bodies (also
   arrows that lexically capture this/new.target).

2. Static accessors were registered as callable static methods
   (arguments-object cls-*-static-* getter calls). `static get foo()`
   was pushed into `static_method_names`, so `C.foo(...)` was hijacked
   into a `StaticMethodCall` whose target didn't exist and the call was
   silently dropped. Excluded getter/setter kinds from the static-method
   registry (3 collection sites) and routed static-accessor calls through
   the value-call fallthrough in codegen (new
   `try_lower_class_static_accessor_call`): read the accessor, then call
   its result with `this` bound to the class.

3. Instance-accessor calls with spread threw "not a function"
   (arguments-object cls-*-spread-operator). `recv.getter(...args)`
   dispatched `getter` by name via `js_native_call_method_apply`. Skip the
   method-apply path when `getter` is an instance accessor so the getter
   is invoked and its result spread-called.

4. Static method/getter calls with spread dropped the spread
   (arguments-object cls-*-static-*-spread-operator). `StaticMethodCall`
   carries plain positional args with no spread representation, so the
   spread sources landed as single positional args and arguments.length
   undercounted. Gate StaticMethodCall production on `!has_spread` so the
   call routes through the spread-aware `CallSpread` path.

5. `eval("var x = 1")` completion value (eval-code cptn-nrml-empty-var).
   A VariableStatement yields an empty completion (→ undefined), but the
   direct-eval assignment fold returned the assigned value. Wrap the
   `var x = <v>` form so it stores but yields undefined.

- eval-code:        280 -> 281 pass
- function-code:    167 -> 169 pass
- arguments-object: 205 -> 239 pass
Parity 79.5% -> 84.0% on the three dirs.

Broad regression check — shard 0/12 over built-ins+language: +40 pass

feat(publish): add [android] version_code override (#4814)

* feat(publish): add [android] version_code override

Android `versionCode` is derived from `build_number` (`version_to_code`), i.e.
`build_number * 10000`. That couples the code to the build/CI run number: if a
project migrates CI or resets its run number, the code can regress and Google
Play rejects the upload ("version code already used / must be higher"), since
Play requires every upload to exceed the max ever uploaded to any track.

Add an explicit `[android] version_code` integer that, when set, is sent in the
build manifest and wins over the derived value on the worker — letting a project
pin a monotonic code (or clear an existing higher floor) without changing the
marketing version. Worker support: PerryTS/builder-linux + builder-macos.

fix(hir): obj?.method(args) on builtins no longer short-circuits to undefined (#4816)

an optional member (`s?.at`). The #4699 fix for the genuine optional-call form

that guard was also firing here. For builtin string/array/number methods the

fix(runtime): adopt returned promise state on async tail-return (#4828) (#4832)

An async fn whose tail expression returns an un-awaited promise
(`return someAsyncCall()`) corrupted the resolved value: awaiting the
outer fn yielded the inner Promise object itself (typeof "object",
JSON.stringify "", every property undefined) instead of the inner
promise's eventual value.

Root cause: js_async_step_done's in-place reuse fast path settled the
result promise (INLINE_TRAP.trap_next) with a raw js_promise_resolve,
skipping the ECMAScript thenable/promise adoption that the slow path
(js_promise_resolved) performs. The sibling js_async_step_chain (the
`await x` path) already adopts, which is why explicit `await` masked it.

Fix: resolve_trap_next_with_adoption mirrors js_promise_resolved's
adoption probes (primitive short-circuit, native-Promise chain via
js_promise_resolve_with_promise, thenable assimilation) but settles the
existing trap_next so the runner's self-chain fast path still fires.

fix(runtime): honor JSON reviver prototype lookups (#4665)

* fix(runtime): honor reviver prototype lookups

* fix(runtime): per-thread globalThis kept alive by registered GC roots

Two coupled bugs in the per-thread-arena model, both exposed by #4665's reviver
paths allocating more in the runtime test suite:

1. `GLOBAL_THIS_PTR` is a process-global static but the realm global lives in a
   per-thread arena. A pointer published by a finished thread (libtest runs each
   test on its own thread; `perry/thread` workers have their own arenas) points
   into freed/reused memory — reads of `globalThis.Array`/`Object` returned
   `undefined` or recursed (stack overflow). `js_get_global_this` now caches the
   global in a thread-local and only returns one this thread created; it never
   dereferences another thread's pointer.

2. GC root scanners live in a thread-local list registered only by `js_gc_init()`
   — which the unit-test harness and worker threads never call. So a collection
   on those threads ran with an empty root set and reclaimed the live global
   (and its `Array`/`Object` intrinsics) mid-test, leaving a dangling intrinsic
   that later array ops dereferenced (intermittent SIGSEGV on Linux, where freed
   pages are unmapped). `js_get_global_this` now calls `ensure_gc_initialized`
   before creating the global so it is born under a live root. The GC tests opt
   out via `ScopedRootScannerRegistryGuard` (suppresses auto-init + save/restores
   the registry) so their controlled-root collections are unaffected.

Single-threaded production is unchanged (one thread, one global, created once;
`js_gc_init` already ran). Also hardens
`test_array_exotic_descriptors_and_global_prototype_identity` to read a
self-consistent intrinsic snapshot per retry iteration.

* test(gc): full conservative stack scan under cfg(test) so native-stack roots survive

perry-runtime unit tests hold GC-managed pointers as raw locals on the *native*
(Rust) stack, not the shadow stack. The conservative scan skips the native stack
by default (deliberate — compiled programs root through the shadow stack), so any
collection triggered mid-test (e.g. by an allocation in a helper) reclaims those
locals, and a later GC-header deref (`is_registered_set`, array length, …) reads
freed memory — an intermittent SIGSEGV on Linux, where freed pages are unmapped
(mimalloc retains them on macOS, hiding it). This is the long-standing
'GC/threading tests race into intermittent SIGSEGV' the cargo-test job mitigates
with RUST_TEST_THREADS=1; #4665's reviver paths allocate enough to make it fire.

`conservative_stack_scan_mode` now defaults to `Full` under `#[cfg(test)]`
(production unchanged) so test locals survive any mid-test collection. A new
per-thread override lets the GC tests opt back to `Auto` (skip) — they verify
collection of objects held only as native-stack locals. `ScopedRootScannerRegistryGuard` (used by CopyingNurseryTestGuard / GcTestIsolationGuard) sets it for the
guarded majority; `ConservativeScanAutoGuard` covers the few ad-hoc collection
tests (one oldgen defrag test).

* test(arena): keep freed blocks mapped under cfg(test) to stop UAF SIGSEGV

perry-runtime unit tests hold GC-managed objects as raw pointers on the native
(Rust) stack. When a collection reclaims a block those tests still reference and
the C4b-δ idle-block policy hands it back to the OS via `std::alloc::dealloc`
(glibc munmaps the 1 MB block), the next deref of the stale pointer faults — the
intermittent SIGSEGV the cargo-test job documents (set.rs:121 / is_registered_set
via js_object_get_class_id during array.join, test_array_splice_delete_middle,
etc.). It only reproduces where the allocator returns pages to the OS: CI's glibc
munmaps; macOS mimalloc and the idle Linux box retain them, so the stale read is
harmless there and the fault never shows.

Gate every arena block dealloc on `!cfg!(test)`: in the test binary freed blocks
stay mapped (tombstoned but not returned to the OS), so a raw pointer the
conservative scan missed reads stale-but-mapped bytes instead of an unmapped
page. Production is byte-for-byte unchanged. Proven: full perry-runtime suite
998/0 x3 on Linux (skelpo-2), and the deterministic age-out repro no longer
SIGSEGVs.

fix(runtime): new WeakMap()/Map/Set from a constructor value no longer throws "requires 'new'" (#4844)

When a collection constructor is obtained as a *value* (alias variable,
`get-intrinsic`-style `%WeakMap%` lookup, cross-module re-export) and then
constructed via `new $WeakMap()`, the call does not take the static codegen
`new` path (which special-cases `class_name == "WeakMap"`). It routes through
the runtime value-construct path `js_new_function_construct`.

That path consults `identify_global_builtin_constructor`, whose allow-list of
recognized constructor thunks omitted the Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet/WeakRef
"requires 'new'" thunks. The function returned `None`, the call fell through,
and the thunk was invoked as a bare function call — throwing
`TypeError: Constructor WeakMap requires 'new'`.

This broke `qs.stringify()` on any nested object/array: qs's `side-channel`
dependency builds its channel with `new $WeakMap()` from an intrinsic value.

Fix (class_registry.rs):
1. Add the five collection-constructor thunks to the `is_global_builtin_func`
   allow-list so the singleton walk can recover their names.
2. Add Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet/WeakRef arms to `js_new_function_construct`
   that dispatch into the real factories (mirroring lower_call/builtin.rs),
   honoring the optional iterable argument.

Verified byte-identical to Node for `qs` 6.15.2 nested + deeply-nested
stringify, and direct `new WeakMap()/Map()/Set()/WeakSet()/WeakRef()`
remain unaffected.

fix(codegen): guard cyclic inheritance walks against non-termination (#4845)

Several codegen helper walks over the class `extends_name` chain assumed
the inheritance graph is a tree. Heavily-modular TypeScript packages
(Effect, OpenCode) declare same-named classes across modules; when those
are pulled into one importing module's class table by name, the parent
chains can form a cycle (local `Base` → extends `Class` → resolves back
to local `Base`). The unbounded `while let Some(name) = cur` walks then
either CPU-hang (counter walks) or OOM (accumulating walks), which is
what stalled the OpenCode native-graph codegen after `visited=N/N`.

Add a visited-set + depth cap (64) to the inheritance-chain walks in:
  - is_class_getter / is_class_setter (escape-analysis accessor dispatch)
  - class_uses_this_as_value + parent-field-init walk
  - class_chain_extends_builtin_error
  - declared_field_type
  - class_field_global_index (recursive walk and its inner parent-count loop)
  - class_field_declared_type

Each walk now terminates on a repeated class name instead of treating the
parent chain as a guaranteed tree. Focused regression tests cover the
accessor, this-as-value, and builtin-error walks under a 2-cycle graph.

The three class-field helpers (declared_field_type, class_field_global_index,
class_field_declared_type) move to a new sibling module
`type_analysis_class_fields.rs` so type_analysis.rs stays under the 2000-line
file-size gate; they're re-exported from `type_analysis` so call sites are
unchanged.

Salvaged from the still-relevant core of #4261 (h/t @andrewtdiz); the rest
of that branch is a stale OpenCode-migration grab-bag, superseded on main.

fix(hir): private-member brand-check on access + class-element tail (v3) (#4847)

Private member accesses `obj.#name` now enforce the spec preconditions of a
PrivateReference instead of silently reading a string-keyed property:

  1. Brand check — the receiver must carry the private brand (be an instance
     of the declaring class, or for static members BE the declaring class
     constructor). A wrong receiver (ordinary object, unrelated/outer-class
     instance, subclass for statics) throws TypeError.
  2. Kind/op check — reading a setter-only accessor, or writing a getter-only
     accessor or a private method, throws TypeError.

Implementation: a single additive HIR node `Expr::PrivateGuard` wraps the
receiver of every private get/set/method-call, evaluating it once and
returning it unchanged when legal (else throwing). It composes with the
existing PropertyGet/PropertySet/method-call lowering, so the runtime helper
`js_private_guard` is the only new dispatch. A lexical `private_scopes` stack
on the lowering context resolves each `#name` to its declaring class + member
kind, surviving nested-function/arrow lowering. `receiver_class_name` sees
through the guard so shadowed private-field slot resolution stays accurate
(zero regressions). `declaring_class_id == 0` degrades the guard to a no-op so
it can never reject a legal access.

Also in this pass:
  - Reflect.has / `in` hide `#name` keys on class instances (private elements
    live in internal slots, invisible to ordinary [[HasProperty]]).
  - Private-field destructuring-assignment targets (`[this.#x] = v`,
    `({a: this.#x} = src)`) lower + brand-guard instead of failing to compile.
  - Numeric / bigint class-field keys (`0 = 'bar'`, `1e-7;`) lower via the
    canonical JS number-to-key conversion instead of "Unsupported property key".
