fix(hir,runtime): #5989 — Next.js cacheComponents boot-chain subset (#6014)

Boot-chain hardening behind #5989 (dynamic RSC render evaporation), the subset independent of #5874 (which #6015 reverted mid-review):

1. hir,runtime: strict-mode assignment to an existing global builtin is a property write, not a ReferenceError (spec PutValue) — Next's cacheComponents installs its Date extension via strict 'Date = createDate(Date)', which previously failed at boot. New js_global_assign_existing_or_throw helper; both HIR assign arms via a shared helper; absent bindings still throw the named ReferenceError.
2. runtime: make the Date-extension wrapper construct real Dates — reified Reflect.construct was a no-op stub; Reflect.construct(Date,args,newTarget) didn't brand; constructor-name recovery broke on global reassignment. Fixed all three.
3. runtime: validate keys_array before deref in shape_is_url_search_params — a mid-transition GC_TYPE_OBJECT receiver SIGSEGV'd on the first request; require the eager GC_TYPE_ARRAY layout (try_read_gc_header, #5429/#5943 family).

Includes both CodeRabbit review fixes (reject GC_TYPE_LAZY_ARRAY; shared strict-assign helper). Validated on current main: builds green, integration tests pass, Date extension installs+constructs (proto-constructor matches node), 21/23 class/date/reflect gap with zero new regressions.

The two class-forward-capture fixes are deferred — #6015's revert of #5874 removed the class-lowering machinery they built on; they'll be re-derived against the post-revert base (tracked in #5989).

fix(runtime): fire process.stdin 'end'/'close' listeners on EOF (#6017)

`process.stdin.on/once("end"|"close", fn)` never fired. The native
`process.stdin` on/once/addListener binding only handled "data" and
"readable"; every other event name fell into a `_ => {}` arm and was
discarded. Node fires 'end' on stdin EOF, so code that awaits stdin end
— e.g. a prompt reader that races EOF against a timeout — hung forever:
the 'end' listener never fired, the promise never resolved, and the
awaiting async function stalled before running any code after the await
(silently draining to exit, or hanging if another handle kept the loop
alive).

Register "end"/"close" listeners in dedicated STDIN_END_LISTENERS /
STDIN_END_ONCE registries and dispatch them from the main-thread stdin
pump once the reader hits EOF and the byte buffer has drained (so 'data'
precedes 'end', per Node). Fire at most once, latching only after at
least one listener exists so a listener attached in the small window
right after EOF (the prompt-reader race) still runs. The reader records
EOF and wakes the loop; the new registries are added to GC root scanning.

Adds an e2e regression test covering the once("end") + on("data") shape
with both piped input and empty input.

fix(build,compile): #5928 — codegen-units alignment + cold-build dedup fix for well-known libs (#5980)

* fix(build): #5928 — match codegen-units across perry-stdlib-static and well-known ext crates

perry-stdlib-static/perry-runtime-static override codegen-units=16 (#5140,
preserving #[no_mangle] extern "C" exports from thin-LTO internalization),
but the well-known "shared tokio" (#507) ext crates (perry-ext-fastify/
http/ioredis/net/ws) had no override and used the workspace default of 1.
Cargo builds them in the same invocation as perry-stdlib-static so their
dependency graphs are unified, but that unification doesn't survive a
codegen-units mismatch: rustc partitions each crate's monomorphized code
into that many codegen units, so the "same" shared dependency (e.g.
compiler_builtins) ends up split differently across crates with different
settings, producing non-identical objects perry's strip-dedup can't safely
treat as interchangeable duplicates.

Confirmed via md5: compiler_builtins' codegen units are now byte-identical
between libperry_ext_http.a and libperry_stdlib.a (231/231), versus
divergent sizes before this fix (e.g. the shared `core` unit was 2.4 MB in
the ext lib vs 551 KB in stdlib).

This narrows but does not close #5928's duplicate-symbol gap: most shared
dependencies (tokio, hyper_util, rustls, ring, ...) are pulled into
perry-stdlib-static's own linker-plugin-lto merge and can never be
byte-identical to a plain compile of the same crate regardless of matching
settings — see the follow-up commit and #5928 for the residual analysis.

* fix(compile): #5928 — restore well-known lib dedup on cold auto-optimize builds

build_optimized_libs() has three return paths that construct the final
OptimizedLibs. Two correctly set prefer_well_known_before_stdlib from
whether any well-known libs are in play; the third — reached when the
well-known native libs must be built from scratch (a cold/cleared
auto-optimize cache, not the "archives are fresh" fast path) — hardcoded
it to `false`.

That flag gates whether build_and_run.rs runs strip_bundled_runtime_from_
well_known_lib / strip_bundled_shared_deps_from_well_known_lib at link
time. With it forced false, a program needing 2+ well-known libs together
(e.g. opencode's fastify + http + ioredis + net + ws) skipped dedup
entirely on any build that couldn't reuse cached archives, silently and
non-fatally regressing to raw (undeduped) linking — confirmed by
comparing duplicate-symbol counts with and without a stale auto-optimize
directory present (2152 vs 1382 for the same program).

Match the other two branches: prefer_well_known_before_stdlib should
depend only on whether there are well-known libs to dedup, not on which
of the three build/cache paths produced them.

fix(compile): #5984 — computed-key static fields leak synthetic name into cross-module externs (#5985)

* fix(compile): #5984 — computed-key static fields leak synthetic name into cross-module externs

A computed-key static field (\`static [Symbol.for(...)] = init\`) gets a
synthetic HIR name \`__computed_field_<span.lo>_<span.hi>\`. module_globals_
emit.rs's emission loop correctly skips creating a backing
\`perry_static_<mod>__<class>__<field>\` global for these — computed fields
are stored via a runtime side table instead (#420, #894) — so the defining
module never emits that symbol.

But the cross-module class-export metadata built in run_pipeline.rs
(ImportedClass.static_field_names, populated at 7 call sites) collected
every static field's name, including the computed ones' synthetic
placeholder, with no filter. An importing module took that list at face
value and declared an external global reference for the synthetic name —
which the source module never defines, producing an undefined-symbol
link error whenever a class with a computed-key static field (drizzle-
orm's pervasive \`static readonly [entityKind]: string = "..."\` tagging
pattern, used on dozens of classes) is imported by another module that
also needs its other, non-computed statics.

Filter out computed-key fields (f.key_expr.is_none()) before collecting
static_field_names, matching the filter module_globals_emit.rs already
applies on the defining side.

* cases(#5984): computed-key static field cross-module regression fixture

Base class with a computed-key static field (Symbol-tagged, drizzle-orm's
entityKind pattern) in one module, subclass overriding it in another.
Verified byte-for-byte against Node.

fix(codegen,runtime): super(...spread) dropped spread args and skipped custom iterators (#6018)

`super(...args)` with spread arguments in a derived-class constructor lost the
spread contents at two independent points, so a parent constructor invoked via
the dynamic `super(...spread)` apply path saw zero (or truncated) arguments:

1. Runtime arg forwarding (`js_super_construct_apply`) truncated the
   materialized spread-args array to the parent ctor's DECLARED param count and
   always passed `has_synthetic_arguments = has_rest = false` to
   `call_vtable_method`. A pass-through parent ctor (`constructor() { ...
   arguments ... }`, tsc's emitted pattern, or an implicit derived
   `constructor(...args){ super(...args) }`) declares zero params but reads
   `arguments`, so every spread element was dropped and `arguments.length`
   read 0. Fix: register each ctor's `(has_synthetic_arguments, has_rest)`
   shape (new `js_register_class_constructor_flags` FFI + `CLASS_CONSTRUCTOR_FLAGS`
   side table, emitted by codegen next to the existing ctor registration) and,
   when the parent has a synthesized `arguments` slot or a trailing user rest
   param, forward ALL spread args flat and let `call_vtable_method` pack the
   trailing slot (from index 0 for `arguments`, from the rest position for a
   rest param) — mirroring the non-spread inline super path and
   `replay_registered_class_constructor`. Ctors with capture params keep the
   original fixed-arity path (caps must not be swallowed into `arguments`).

2. Codegen (`this_super_call.rs`) built the spread-args array with
   `js_array_push_spread_any`, which only handles real arrays and array-like
   (`.length`) objects. A plain iterable with a custom `[Symbol.iterator]`
   (`super(...iter)`) has no `.length`, so it contributed zero args, and a
   throwing iterator step/value never propagated its error. Fix: route spread
   operands through `js_array_spread_append` -> `array_from_spread_value`, the
   same full iterator-protocol helper array/call spreads already use — it
   drives custom iterators, spreads the arguments object, and propagates abrupt
   completions. This is a strict superset of the old helper's coverage.

Test262 language/expressions/super: +19 cases (32 -> 46 pass) — the entire
`call-spread-*` cluster (array-literal, expr, custom-iterator, and all 12
`call-spread-err-*` iterator-error-propagation cases) plus 4
object/method-definition generator/name super-prop cases that shared the
spread-append path. Zero regressions across the super / object /
property-accessors / delete / for-of / function slice (1032 -> 1051 pass) and
no super/spread regressions in the language/statements/class corpus.

fix(system): getDeviceModel/getOSVersion return a string, not NaN (#5972) (#6016)

Two stacked bugs; `table[getDeviceModel()]` at module scope crashed at
startup with EXC_BAD_ACCESS (KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x4). Found migrating
a real app (dbmeter, a calibration table keyed by device model).

1. Dispatch return kind. `perry_system_get_device_model` /
   `_get_os_version` return a raw `*mut StringHeader` (i64) via
   `js_string_from_bytes` — same shape as `getLocale`, which is correctly
   `ReturnKind::Str`. But both were declared `ReturnKind::F64`, which the
   LLVM backend lowers as `call(DOUBLE, …)` and passes straight through:
   the pointer bits are reinterpreted as an f64 → `NaN` (`typeof` reads
   "number"). Changed both to `Str` so the i64 handle is NaN-boxed with
   STRING_TAG into a real JS string. (Only the LLVM backend consumes
   `ReturnKind`; the JS/WASM backends use the table solely for the
   method→symbol name map, so they are unaffected.)

2. Null-key segfault guard. When a property-key value doesn't yield a
   usable string handle — e.g. `js_get_string_pointer_unified` returns 0
   for a NaN key that fell through its coercion branches — a null key
   reached `js_object_get_field_by_name`, whose arms deref `(*key).byte_len`
   without a null check → SIGSEGV at offset 4. Added an early guard: a null
   key misses → `undefined`, per JS semantics (same defensive shape as the
   #2128 invalid-key guard). Defense-in-depth so a future type-unsound
   value can't turn into memory corruption. Every in-runtime caller passes
   an interned non-null key, so only the codegen computed-access path is
   affected.

Tests:
- crates/perry/tests/issue_5972_getdevicemodel_object_key.rs — e2e: the
  getDeviceModel-as-object-key repro (typeof is "string", known key hits,
  unknown host model misses without crashing), plus numeric/NaN/float keys
  through a type-erased receiver matching the node oracle
  (NUM one / NAN not-a-number / FLOAT undefined).
- perry-runtime null_key_guard_5972 unit test: js_object_get_field_by_name
  with a null key returns undefined instead of segfaulting.

fix(hir): bracket access with a string-literal key missed builtin static folds (#6019)

`Number["POSITIVE_INFINITY"]`, `Math["E"]`, `Array["prototype"]`, and similar
bracket accesses on a builtin constructor/namespace returned `undefined`, while
the equivalent dot form worked. Per spec `obj["name"]` === `obj.name` for any
string key, so both must resolve identically.

Root cause: the builtin static-member resolution in member lowering keyed only
off `MemberProp::Ident` (dot access). A dynamic key (`Number[k]`) works because
it routes through the runtime `globalThis.Number` object (which has the statics
installed). But a *string-literal* computed key (`Number["POSITIVE_INFINITY"]`)
took the compile-time static path — where the constant-fold arms (Math/Number
constants) never matched, and the `Ctor.prototype` reroute-undo guard did not
recognize the literal `["prototype"]` form. So the receiver collapsed to bare
`globalThis` and the outer key was read off `globalThis` (undefined).

Fix: add `static_member_prop_name`, which yields the property name for EITHER a
dot access or a bracket access with a string-literal key, and use it in the
three affected static-resolution sites:
  - the `Math.*` constant fold (`Math["PI"]`, `Math["E"]`, ...),
  - the `Number.*` constant fold (`Number["MAX_VALUE"]`,
    `Number["POSITIVE_INFINITY"]`, ...),
  - the `Ctor.prototype` / `Ctor.__proto__` reroute-undo guard, so
    `Array["prototype"]` / `Object["prototype"]` keep the reified constructor
    receiver instead of collapsing to `globalThis.prototype`.

Dynamic (non-string-literal) computed keys are unaffected — the helper returns
`None` and the runtime index path is kept.

Test262 language/expressions/property-accessors: +4 cases. Zero regressions
across the super / object / property-accessors / delete / for-of / function
slice and a built-ins/{Math,Number,Array,Object} regression slice (98.3%).
`cargo test -p perry-hir` green, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

fix(compile): #5987 — guard class_canonical_path against ClassId collisions (#6001)

ClassId is meant to be unique across the whole program (module lowering
threads a next_class_id counter forward precisely to guarantee this), but
a real multi-thousand-module compile can still produce two unrelated
classes with the same id — confirmed via debug instrumentation for
effect's two distinct ClientAbort classes (in RpcSchema.ts and
HttpServerError.ts), which resolved to a third, unrelated module
(SchemaAST.ts) that defines neither.

class_canonical_path now stores each entry's class name alongside its
path, and every consumer (canonical_class_source_prefix, plus the
transitive parent-class closure and child-source-path lookups in
run_pipeline.rs) validates the name matches before trusting the entry,
falling back to the caller's already-independently-verified prefix on a
mismatch. This doesn't fix ClassId allocation itself (a colliding id can
still occur), but it stops a collision from silently misattributing the
wrong module — the callers already have a reliable fallback for exactly
this case, since the compound (path, name) key that found the class in
the first place already proves the correct origin.

fix(hir): delete of a module-level var/let/const binding wrongly returned true (#6020)

`delete x` where `x` is a module-top-level `var`/`let`/`const` binding returned
`true` (and removed the binding at runtime) instead of the spec-required `false`
(bindings are non-configurable, `delete` is a no-op returning `false`;
spec 13.5.1.2).

The `delete <ident>` fold already returned `false` for function-scoped
bindings, function declarations, classes, and imports, and `true` for a bare
implicit global (`x = 1`, no declaration). But at module top level it gave up
and deferred a real `var`/`let`/`const` binding to a runtime delete — on the
stale premise that a module-level declaration is indistinguishable from an
implicit global. That premise is wrong: `define_sloppy_implicit_global` records
an implicit global in `sloppy_implicit_global_ids` at scope depth 0 too, so the
implicit-global case already takes the `true` arm above. Any resolvable
module-level binding that reaches the fall-through is therefore a genuine
declaration and must be `false`.

Fix: return `Expr::Bool(false)` for a resolved binding not in the
implicit-global set, at module level as well — removing the runtime-delete
fall-through.

Test262 language/expressions/delete: +5 cases (59 -> 64 pass), including
S11.4.1_A3.3_T4 and the 11.4.1-4.a/5 series. The implicit-global `delete x`
(S11.4.1_A3.2_T1, must stay `true`) is preserved. Zero regressions across the
super / object / property-accessors / delete / for-of / function slice.
`cargo test -p perry-hir` green, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

fix(hir): class own-name binding is const inside the class body (#6021)

Per the class definition semantics, the binding for a class's own name is
an *immutable* (const) binding in the class scope — the environment record
created for the class body. Assigning to that name from anywhere inside the
class body (constructor, method, accessor, or an expression in the heritage
clause) must throw a TypeError. The outer declaration binding introduced by
a `class C {}` statement is a separate, mutable binding, so reassigning `C`
from *outside* the body stays legal.

Perry previously dropped such an assignment silently (the `<Name> = X`
branch in the ident-assignment lowering evaluated the RHS for side effects
and returned, treating the class binding as a no-op target), so none of the
`assert.throws(TypeError, ...)` cases fired.

This tracks the source-level inner binding name on the lowering context
(`current_class_inner_name`, saved/restored around each class body, and fed
for class *expressions* via `pending_class_inner_name` since those receive a
synthetic dedup registration key rather than the user-visible name). When an
identifier assignment target matches that inner name — and no local/param
shadows it — the lowering now evaluates the RHS and then throws via the
existing `js_throw_type_error_const_assignment` runtime helper.

Fixes the test262 language/{statements,expressions}/class name-binding
const cases and the inner-binding-immutability assertions in the
scope-name-lex heritage/no-heritage tests, with no change to outer-binding
reassignment.

fix(runtime): class constructor .caller/.arguments are poison-pill accessors (#6022)

A class constructor is a function, so reading or writing its `caller` or
`arguments` property goes through the %ThrowTypeError% poison-pill accessor
inherited from `Function.prototype` (the accessor has a getter and setter
that both throw, and no [[Set]] fallback). Perry only compiles strict code,
so both the read and the write must throw a TypeError, and neither name is
an own property of the class.

Ordinary closures already routed these through the thrower (in
get_field_by_name_tail), but a class is represented as an INT32-tagged
class-ref, not a closure pointer, so that path never fired — reading
`Class.caller` returned `undefined` and `Class.caller = {}` silently no-op'd.

Add the guard to both class-ref property paths:

- READ (`js_object_get_field_by_name`): after all own static / inherited /
  parent-chain resolution fails, a `caller`/`arguments` read on a
  constructor ref throws. Placed last so any own static field, accessor, or
  parent static of that name still wins; prototype-refs (`C.prototype`, a
  plain object) are excluded.
- WRITE (`js_object_set_field_by_name`): a `caller`/`arguments` write on a
  constructor ref throws unless an own data prop (`CLASS_DYNAMIC_PROPS`)
  shadows it; prototype-refs excluded.

`Class.hasOwnProperty('caller'|'arguments')` stays `false`, and normal
statics (`C.name`, static fields/methods, `constructor.name`) are
unaffected. Fixes the test262 language/{statements,expressions}/class
restricted-properties cases.

fix(runtime): `in` operator throws TypeError on a non-object right operand (#6024)

ECMA-262 13.10.1 (RelationalExpression `in`) step 5 requires the right
operand to be an Object, throwing a TypeError otherwise. Perry's type
erasure let `"x" in 5`, `"x" in null`, `"x" in Symbol()`, `... in ""`,
`... in true`, and `... in 1n` fall through and report `false`; V8/Node
reject each with
`TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for '<key>' in <rhs>`.

Add a dedicated codegen entry point `js_in_operator(obj, key)` that
performs the spec object check and then delegates the actual lookup to
`js_object_has_property`. The guard lives on this new entry point rather
than inside `js_object_has_property` because that helper is also called
internally (Reflect.has, proxy `has` traps, `with`-environment binding
lookup, rest-destructuring exclusion, descriptor validation) with
receivers that are always objects — only the user-visible `in` operator
can legitimately be handed a primitive RHS, so those internal paths stay
byte-for-byte unchanged.

`in_rhs_is_object` mirrors every object-like representation the lookup
already understands, so the throwing guard never rejects a value that
`js_object_has_property` would have handled:
  * heap POINTER_TAG values (objects/arrays/functions/proxies and every
    handle-band registry id), excluding Symbols (pointer-tagged but
    primitive);
  * INT32-tagged *registered* class refs (`"prototype" in SomeClass`);
  * Web Streams handles (raw finite f64 ids in the stream-id band,
    `"closed" in reader`).
Everything else (number/boolean/string/BigInt/null/undefined/Symbol and
any unregistered INT32) is a primitive and throws.

Verified on an internal Linux sweep host: language/expressions/in goes to
16/17 pass (the lone remaining failure is a pre-existing, unrelated LHS
boolean-key ToPropertyKey coercion bug, `true in {"true":1}`). A
regression sweep over language/expressions + built-ins/Object/Reflect/Proxy
shows zero new `in`-operator over-throws (no failure carries the new
TypeError message) and Reflect.has / proxy-has / class-instance / prototype
`in` all match Node.

fix(hir): emit computed-key static fields that have no initializer (#6025)

A computed-name static class field with no initializer (`static [expr];`)
was dropped entirely during lowering — `build_interleaved_static_init_stmts`
bailed with `let Some(init) = &sf.init else { return }` before it ever
looked at the key. That skipped two observable behaviors required by
ClassDefinitionEvaluation:

1. The key expression's side effects never ran.
2. `CreateDataProperty(F, key, undefined)` never happened, so the field was
   not defined — and, critically, a key that evaluates to `"prototype"` never
   reached the runtime `"prototype"`-is-a-TypeError check in
   `js_class_register_static_symbol` (the constructor's `prototype` slot is
   non-configurable, so a static field of that name throws).

Now a field is skipped only when it is BOTH un-initialized AND has no
computed key (a plain named uninit static slot — unchanged behavior). A
computed-key field is always emitted, with `undefined` substituted for a
missing initializer, so its `ClassStaticSymbolSet` runs the key and defines
the property (or throws for `"prototype"`).

Fixes the test262 class-elements cases:
- fields-computed-name-static-propname-prototype
- fields-computed-name-static-computed-var-propname-prototype
- static-field-declaration (statements + expressions)
- static-classelementname-abrupt-completion

fix(runtime): strict arr[i]=v / arr.length=n on a frozen array throws TypeError (#6026)

Perry compiles everything strict, so a source-level array element or `length`
assignment is `Set(O, P, V, Throw = true)`. On a *frozen* array these targets
are non-writable, so the write must throw a TypeError -- Perry silently no-oped
instead, leaving a batch of test262 missed-negatives:

    "use strict";
    const a = Object.freeze([1, 2, 3]);
    a[0] = 9;        // was: silent; now: TypeError read-only property '0'
    a[5] = 9;        // was: silent; now: TypeError not extensible
    a.length = 1;    // was: silent; now: TypeError read-only property 'length'

Adding a NEW index to any non-extensible array (frozen / sealed /
preventExtensions'd) likewise now throws "object is not extensible", matching
V8/Node.

Design -- strict variants beside the silent helpers, so ONLY user assignments
throw and every internal caller keeps its no-Throw contract:

  * js_array_set_f64_extend_strict / js_array_set_index_or_string_strict --
    element writes; share array_strict_index_write_guard (existing index of a
    frozen array -> read-only; new index of a non-extensible array -> not-
    extensible; sealed/non-extensible still permit overwriting an existing
    index, so only is_frozen gates the in-bounds case).
  * js_array_set_length_strict -- frozen `length` write, even for an equal or
    invalid new value (V8 rejects the non-writable write before coercing, so a
    frozen arr.length = -1 is a TypeError, not a RangeError; the guard precedes
    the length parse).

The plain js_array_set_{f64_extend,index_or_string,length} helpers keep their
silent behaviour for their internal callers -- Object.defineProperty (which
uses them as raw [[DefineOwnProperty]] slot-writers), array-object length
coercion, polymorphic_index, and freshly-allocated runtime arrays. The
assignment paths are re-pointed to the strict variants: the arr[i]=v codegen
(js_typed_feedback_array_set_{f64_extend,index_or_string} wrappers, emitted only
for the source assignment, plus the realloc slow path in expr/index.rs), the
arr.length=v codegen (expr/property_set.rs), the generic PutValue helper
js_object_set_field_by_name, and js_put_value_set (strict-flag gated).

Verified on an internal Linux sweep host, matching Node byte-for-byte in both
default (auto-optimize) and PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE builds:
  * frozen element (existing/new) + length (shrink/grow/same) all throw;
  * sealed / preventExtensions add-new-index throws; existing-index overwrite
    still succeeds;
  * normal (unfrozen) element / length / string-index / computed / dense-loop

fix(hir): capture forward-refs bound later in the same `let` declaration (#6028)

A closure in an earlier declarator of a `let`/`const` declaration that
references names bound by LATER declarators of the SAME declaration —
`let z = (w) => { … O … Y … A … }, Y = () => z(false), A = …,
O = setTimeout(z, K)` (the minified `new Promise` executor shape) — failed
to capture them. They lowered to `js_global_get_or_throw_unresolved`
instead of a captured local box.

`pre_register_forward_captured_lets` only recorded a statement's
closure-refs via the trailing `cic_stmt` AFTER the whole declaration, so
intra-declaration forward-references were never seen and the later
declarators were never pre-registered. Record each declarator's
closure-refs immediately (via `cic_expr`) so subsequent declarators in the
same declaration are pre-registered too. Cross-statement forward-refs were
already handled by the trailing `cic_stmt`.

The globalization shifted the closure's capture slots, so the captured
`resolve` read the wrong value: the promise never settled and the awaiting
caller hung forever.

fix(hir): report dynamic-codegen unavailable to `new Function("")` probes by default (#6031)

Perry is ahead-of-time compiled and can never honor a runtime
`new Function(<string built at runtime>)` — such a call throws at
construction. The canonical dynamic-codegen capability probe,
`try { new Function(""), true } catch { false }`, however const-folded
its trivial empty body to a working no-op function, so it reported the
capability as *available* — a lie.

A feature-detecting JIT (e.g. zod 4's object-validator) then enabled its
codegen path and built a real validator via `new Function(dynamicBody)`,
which throws. Uncaught inside the JIT, that rejects the surrounding async
work (for zod 4, the object-validation path), stalling programs that only
needed the interpreter fallback the probe was meant to select.

Flip `eval_csp_probe_unavailable()` to default ON: the empty-body probe
now throws at construction (dynamic-codegen honestly reported as
unavailable), so such libraries take their non-codegen interpreter
fallback, which perry compiles normally. Opt out — restoring the
spec-literal empty-function fold (Node returns an empty function) — with
`PERRY_EVAL_CSP=0` (also `off`/`false`/`no`). Only the trivial no-op probe
is affected: real literal bodies (`new Function("return 42")`, the
`return this` globalThis polyfill) still fold, so those idioms are
unaffected.

Adds an e2e regression test covering the default (probe unavailable, real
literal bodies still fold) and the `PERRY_EVAL_CSP=0` opt-out.

fix(gc): #6010 — Map/Set external buffers exert GC pressure; dead collections finalize everywhere (#6034)

* fix(gc): #6010 — Map/Set external buffers: GC pressure + dead-collection finalization

RSS grew unbounded (1.4GB across the issue's benchmark suite, heap ~20MB)
because Map entry arrays and Set element arrays — raw std::alloc buffers
reachable only through 16-byte arena headers — were invisible to the
collector three separate ways:

1. NO PRESSURE: buffer bytes counted toward no trigger input, so a
   Map/Set-churn workload with a quiet arena never collected at all.
   → external side-alloc churn counter: every 16MB of fresh buffer
   allocation pokes gc_check_trigger(); live buffer bytes are added to
   old_in_use wherever old-reclaim pressure is computed (and to its
   baseline), so tenured-then-dead collections escalate to the full
   mark-sweep whose old-gen sweep runs the side-allocation finalizers.

2. IMMORTAL GARBAGE VIA BLOCK PERSISTENCE: every automatic collection in
   a compiled program runs with the FULL conservative stack+register scan
   (the #5476 direct arms), which already pins register-held objects —
   yet block persistence still resurrected every dead object sharing a
   recent arena block with any live one. Low-allocation workloads never
   rotate the active block out of the 5-block recency window, so dead
   Maps there were re-marked forever, each pinning a multi-MB buffer.
   → skip the block-persistence phase when the cycle's root scan ran the
   full conservative scan (it subsumes the register-safety rationale).

3. NEVER SWEPT IN THE ACTIVE BLOCK: dead collections in the active
   nursery allocation block are never object-walked by any sweeper (the
   block is still being bump-allocated into), and bulk block resets skip
   per-object finalize hooks.
   → registry-driven finalization at sweep entry (marks fresh): free the
   buffers of provably-dead registered Maps/Sets — unmarked ∧ unpinned ∧
   unforwarded, restricted on minor traces to untenured nursery headers
   (the same unmarked-nursery-is-garbage invariant the sweeper uses).

Isolated 100k-entry Map churn (50 iters): RSS 221MB (monotonic, was
climbing ~3.7MB/iter unbounded) → 133MB flattening. Full issue benchmark
suite: 1342MB peak → 306MB peak (node: 315MB reported in #6010, ~250MB
measured locally); the map-set-get phase that jumped to 835MB now peaks
at 135MB. cargo test -p perry-runtime: 1155/1155 serial.

Closes #6010

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(hir): #6037 — refresh class-capture snapshot after a forward-captured var is re-bound by destructuring (#6038)

A class capturing a `var`/`let` declared LATER in the same body reads it
through the decl-site capture snapshot (class captures are value-based).
The snapshot is taken while the forward-decl still holds `undefined` and
refreshed after each later assignment of the captured id. But a
DESTRUCTURING re-bind (`var { t: dSq } = f()`) lowers to a `Stmt::Let`
that REUSES the pre-registered forward-decl id, and
`collect_assigned_locals_stmt` classifies every `Let` as a fresh binding
(not an assignment) — so no refresh fired and the class method read the
capture as `undefined`.

Real-world shape: semver's `Comparator` reading `dSq.COMPARATOR` where
`var { safeRe: QSq, t: dSq } = requireModule()` is declared after the
class (the esbuild `__commonJS` + destructured-exports pattern in the
claude-code / semver bundles).

Fix: in `insert_class_capture_refresh_after_assignments`, treat a
`Let { id, init: Some(v) }` with a non-`undefined` init that re-binds a
watched capture id as an assignment that triggers the refresh (the
`undefined` forward-decl init is skipped — it re-snapshots the same
pre-assignment value the decl-site RegisterClassCaptures already has).

Verified: issue_cjs_destructured_var_forward_capture passes; the semver
repro prints `class: rx` (was a TypeError). Capture-refresh regression
suites green.

feat(runtime): Temporal Dead Zone for forward-referenced lexical let/const (#6044)

Implements a real TDZ mechanism. A lexical `let`/`const` binding that is
forward-referenced by an earlier closure or hoisted function (before its
declaration, at function or block scope) is now seeded with a distinct
uninitialized sentinel `TAG_TDZ` at scope entry. Reading, `typeof`-ing, or
assigning it while still in the dead zone throws a spec `ReferenceError`
("Cannot access 'x' before initialization"); the declaration's own initializer
(or `let x;` -> undefined) ends the dead zone.

Mechanism:
- `TAG_TDZ` sentinel (value/tags.rs), one past the array-hole sentinel in the
  reserved 0x7FFC NaN-box singleton band, a bit pattern no legitimate value
  ever holds.
- `js_box_get_bits` throws on `TAG_TDZ` — the single choke point every boxed
  read routes through (direct, closure-captured, compound). Zero-cost for any
  already-initialized box; GC tracing reads the raw cell so marking an
  uninitialized box is unaffected.
- `js_box_set_bits_tdz_checked` throws on a write to a still-uninitialized
  binding; user LocalSet writes to TDZ boxes route through it while the
  declaration's own initializer write stays on plain `js_box_set_bits`.
- New HIR `Stmt::PreallocateTdzBoxes` variant seeds boxes with the sentinel;
  only genuine lexical forward-decls (tracked in `tdz_forward_ids`) are
  TDZ-seeded, so `var` / hoisted-function / compiler-internal boxes keep the
  historical undefined-seed and never spuriously throw.

Scope: function-local and block-local forward-referenced lexical bindings.
Module-top-level TDZ and direct self-reference-in-initializer are deferred
(they need name-resolution routing orthogonal to the sentinel).

fix(runtime): AbortSignal parity — accept in events helpers + dynamic method dispatch (#6046)

* fix(runtime): AbortSignal parity — accept in events helpers + dynamic method dispatch

Node treats `AbortSignal` as an `EventTarget`; Perry represents it as its
own native object (url/abort.rs) that two dispatch layers didn't know:

1. The module-level `node:events` helpers. `setMaxListeners(n,
   controller.signal)` — how SDKs raise the MaxListenersExceededWarning
   threshold on a shared signal — threw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE: The
   "eventTargets" argument must be an instance of EventEmitter or
   EventTarget`, rejecting the caller's whole request path. The four
   helpers (`setMaxListeners`, `getMaxListeners`, `listenerCount`,
   `getEventListeners`) now recognize signals in both perry-stdlib and
   perry-ext-events: set is a faithful no-op (the warning threshold is the
   call's only Node-observable effect and Perry never emits that warning
   for signals), get reports the EventTarget default, and the listener
   queries report the signal's registered "abort" listeners through two
   new runtime helpers (`js_abort_signal_listener_count`,
   `js_abort_signal_listeners_copy`).

2. Dynamic receivers. The statically-typed form
   (`c.signal.addEventListener(...)`) lowers to the native call, but the
   same method through an untyped local — the shape minified SDK code
   takes — resolved to `undefined` and threw `addEventListener is not a
   function` (the #5964 URLSearchParams dynamic-dispatch class). Both
   dynamic paths are covered: property GET returns a bound-method closure
   (`abort_signal_method_bind` in get_field_by_name_tail), and the fused
   dynamic method CALL pre-dispatches to the natives in
   js_native_call_method (the #5961 precedent) for `addEventListener` /
   `removeEventListener` / `throwIfAborted`. `options` is accepted and
   ignored — a signal only ever fires "abort" once, so `{ once: true }`
   is behaviorally implied.

Two e2e tests cover the helpers surface and the dynamic-receiver forms
(including listeners actually firing on abort and plain objects still
being rejected).

* fix(runtime): guard AbortSignal dynamic-dispatch against small-handle receivers

A native handle (Headers/fetch/timer/...) is nanbox-pointer-tagged but its
"pointer" is a small integer id, not a heap ObjectHeader. Guard the
class_id read in the fused dynamic-call AbortSignal arm with is_small_handle

fix(runtime): Date.prototype.toString brand-check + own-expando method shadow (#6050)

Two receiver-handling gaps in Date method dispatch surfaced by the Test262
built-ins slice (internal Linux sweep host):

1. `Date.prototype.toString` did no `thisTimeValue` brand check. The thunk read
   IMPLICIT_THIS and called js_date_to_string unconditionally, so
   `Date.prototype.toString.call(0)`, `.call({})`, and `Date.prototype.toString()`
   (this === Date.prototype) returned a bogus date string instead of throwing a
   TypeError. The getters/setters already brand-check via require_date_timestamp;
   toString now does the same. Fixes Date/prototype/toString/non-date-receiver.

2. A callable own expando on a Date instance did not shadow the intrinsic
   Date.prototype method. Date instances are DateCell exotics, so own properties
   live in the exotic expando table, not the ordinary keys_array — the dynamic
   Date-method dispatch resolved straight to Date.prototype and skipped the
   override. Mirror the existing Promise own-`then` shadow: look up the method
   name in the Date exotic expando first and, when it is a callable, dispatch it
   with `this` bound to the receiver. A transferred `Number.prototype.toString`
   (which brand-checks and throws) then runs instead of Date.prototype.toString.
   Fixes Number/prototype/toString transfer-to-Date.

Normal Date usage is unaffected: the expando lookup only fires for user-assigned
own callables, and Date.prototype methods still resolve for the common path.

fix(hir): #5951 share a mutated class capture via a one-element array box (#6054)

A class field-init/method closure that MUTATES an outer local captured from
the declaring function got a SPLIT cell: Perry lifts the class out of its
declaring function and threads captures through the VALUE-based
`__perry_cap_*` snapshot, so each side (and each instance) received its own
copy. `function f(){let c=0;class T{b=()=>{c+=1;return c;};}...}` printed
`0 3` instead of node's `2 3`.

Fix — a pre-pass (`lower/shared_mutable_capture.rs`, before
`widen_mutable_captures`) that reuses machinery which already shares
correctly: a heap ARRAY is captured by pointer, so a value-snapshot of an
array preserves identity. It detects a capture that is mutated on either side
(the declaring function after `new`, or a lifted member — the write lands on
the rebind local/param named `__perry_cap_<id>`, excluding the ClassCaptureValue
REBIND itself so read-only captures are never flagged) and desugars it to a
one-element array box: `let c = [<init>]`, every value read/write `c` -> `c[0]`.
Capture sites keep the whole array handle (RegisterClassCaptures, `new` cap-arg,
the `this.__perry_cap_* =` stash, the rebind assignment); the holders are
retyped to `Any` so a scalar declared type can't mangle the array pointer
(string captures). No change to the capture-snapshot codegen.

Verified vs node across 34 direct-compile cases: closure-writes/fn-reads,
fn-writes/closure-reads, interleaved, cross-instance sharing, string/boolean/
object captures, method + field mutation, loops, nested closures, self-
construction — plus the 14-case value-based safety boundary (immutable / read-
only / ctor / getter / static captures) stays byte-identical, and the pass is a
proven no-op on non-capture code. `PERRY_NO_5951=1` disables it (bisection).
Un-ignores the #5951 guard suite (now 7 active shared-mutable guards).

* fix(hir,codegen): #6003 — user 'class Headers' conflated with native fetch Headers

A user-defined class named like a Web-API constructor (`class Headers`,
`class Response`, ...) was conflated with the native built-in by name
alone, so its methods silently dispatched through the fetch FFI and
property stores made by user methods vanished (`Object.keys(h)` came
back empty in the #6003 repro).

Root cause was several unconditional by-name native routings; each now
honors lexical shadowing, mirroring the #5912 `new URL()` fix:

- perry-hir destructuring/var_decl/native_fetch.rs: `const h = new
  Headers()` tagged `h` as a native fetch instance with no
  `shadows_unqualified_global` check, so `h.set(...)` lowered to
  `NativeMethodCall { module: "Headers" }` and the user's method never
  ran (this is the repro's failing path). Gated all direct fetch/
  Web-Streams constructor arms; the Blob/File alias arm checks the
  ALIAS-RESOLVED name (the alias local is itself a binding).
- perry-hir lower_decl/fn_decl.rs + lower/expr_function.rs: params
  typed `(h: Headers)` / `(r: Response)` etc. were re-tagged native
  inside the callee by type name; skip when the annotation resolves to
  a user class.
- perry-codegen expr/instance_misc1.rs: `x instanceof Headers` mapped
  the RHS to the reserved built-in class id before consulting user
  `class_ids`, so `h instanceof Headers` tested against the native id
  and returned false. User class ids now take precedence (class_ids
  holds only user classes, so unshadowed built-ins keep reserved ids).
- perry-codegen expr/property_get.rs (method-value reads), expr/
  literals_vars.rs (`typeof h.get` fold), lower_call/property_get/
  fetch_chain.rs (inline `new Headers().get(...)` chain): the
  `receiver_class_name == "Headers"` native routing now backs off when
  the module defines its own `class Headers`.

Regression test test_issue_6003_user_headers_class_shadow.ts matches
node byte-for-byte (computed stores via user method, typed-param
dispatch, inline chained construction, instanceof, and a sibling user
`class Response`). Verified no behavior change on the native-fetch
side: targeted parity subset (headers/fetch/instanceof/blob/streams,
21 tests) matches pristine main — the only failure,
test_gap_fetch_response_json_init, fails byte-identically on main and

fix(runtime,codegen): TDZ × class-capture-refresh boot regression + JSON.stringify replacer SIGBUS hardening (#5989) (#6055)

* fix(runtime,codegen): class-capture snapshot refresh must tolerate TDZ boxes — un-break SWC-CJS-interop module boot

#6044 gave lexical let/const a real Temporal Dead Zone: forward-referenced
bindings are seeded with TAG_TDZ and any read through js_box_get_bits throws
"Cannot access ... before initialization". That interacted with the #6037
class-capture refresh strategy and boot-broke every module using the standard
SWC CJS interop shape (Next.js dist files, most transpiled npm packages):

  _export(exports, { C: () => C, ... });   // getters forward-ref the class
  const _fs = _interop(require("fs"));     // captured by C's methods
  const _path = _interop(require("path")); // captured by C's methods
  class C { m() { _fs...; _path... } }

The getter closures forward-reference the class, so the class's captured
module consts (_fs, _path) are TDZ-seeded via PreallocateTdzBoxes. The #6037
strategy emits a RegisterClassCaptures snapshot refresh after EACH captured
var's assignment — so the refresh emitted after `const _fs` reads _path's box
while it is still in its dead zone. Pre-#6044 that read snapshotted
`undefined` and the next refresh fixed it up; post-#6044 it throws at module
init ("Cannot access undefined before initialization" — the name-agnostic
captured-box path) and the whole program dies at boot. Trigger needs >= 2
class-captured module consts plus the getter head; the Next.js standalone
server hit it in dist/server/dev/browser-logs/file-logger.js and could no
longer boot at all.

Fix: the snapshot refresh loads are Perry-internal materialization, not user
reads — bracket exactly them in a TDZ-suppression window:

- box.rs: TDZ_SUPPRESS_DEPTH thread-local + js_tdz_suppress_begin/end
  (#[used] keepalives for the auto-opt link). Inside the window a TAG_TDZ box
  reads as `undefined` (the pre-#6044 behavior); outside, TDZ throws exactly
  as before. Only the cold TAG_TDZ branch consults the flag.
- static_field_meta.rs: the RegisterClassCaptures arm wraps its capture loads
  in begin/end. The window contains only side-effect-free LocalGets — no user
  code can observe it.
- runtime_decls/strings.rs: declare the two externs.

Validated: the verbatim file-logger.js repro plus 6 bisect variants go from
ReferenceError-at-boot to working; 5 control variants unchanged; genuine TDZ
violations still throw ReferenceError byte-identical to node (read-before-let
direct and via hoisted function); the closure-created-before-init-called-after
legal shapes still work. The Next.js standalone app boots again.

* fix(runtime): #5989 — harden JSON.stringify replacer path against corrupted/mis-classified pointers (SIGBUS -> null)

The Next.js App Router `/plain` render feeds a value graph to
`JSON.stringify(value, replacer, space)` in which a corrupted / mis-encoded
value reaches the replacer walk. Three deref sites there guarded only
`is_handle_band` (small-id proxy/stream handles), NOT general pointer
validity, so a value whose extracted pointer was mis-aligned or out of the
heap range fell through to `gc_obj_type`, which deref'd its `GcHeader` and
SIGBUS'd the server on the first request (Bus error: 10).

Mirrors the mature `is_object_pointer` pre-load sanity (magnitude + 8-byte
alignment) at the replacer's deref sites:

- new `ptr_derefable(ptr)` — top 16 bits <= 1, >= 0x10000, 8-byte aligned.
- `apply_to_json`: a non-derefable pointer can't carry a `toJSON` method, so
  skip the probe (return the value) instead of a `gc_obj_type` deref.
- `dispatch_pointer_with_replacer`: a non-derefable pointer is unserializable —
  emit "null" (matching the handle-band fallback just above) instead of deref.
- the `GC_TYPE_ARRAY` arm: `gc_obj_type` can mis-read a corrupted structure as
  an array whose `length` reads as garbage (~2.7e9); the `0..len` walk then
  runs OOB. Sanity-cap the length at 10M (mirrors `is_object_pointer`'s
  field-count cap) and emit "null" beyond it.

`JSON.stringify` must never SIGBUS on a bad value. This turns the `/plain`
hard crash back into the pre-existing #5989 render hang — a separate, deeper
issue where the render produces the corrupted value graph (garbage-length
arrays + raw untagged values) UPSTREAM of stringify.

Validated: boots + 5/8 byte-identical vs node v26 (/, /about, /counter,
/api/hello GET+POST); the 3 dynamic routes no longer crash the server (they
hang per #5989). No regression. Runtime-only.

fix(watchos): arm64_32 entry-symbol rename via ld -r (objcopy SIGSEGVs) (#6056)

Default-mode (SwiftUI tree-renderer) watchOS apps failed to link for
arm64_32 device targets with "Undefined symbols: _perry_main_init".

The watchOS link renames the compiled TS `_main` so the Swift `@main`
(default shell) or a native lib's `@main` (game-loop / swift-app) owns
the process entry while the TS init stays reachable. That rename used
rust-objcopy --redefine-sym, which SIGSEGVs writing arm64_32 Mach-O
objects (llvm::objcopy::macho::MachOWriter::writeSections — reproducible
with both the rust-toolchain objcopy and Homebrew LLVM 22.1.4). The code
skipped the objcopy pass for arm64_32 expecting a codegen
PERRY_ENTRY_SYMBOL emit, but nothing sets that env var, so codegen emits
`_main`, the rename never happens, and `perry_main_init` is undefined on
every arm64_32 default-mode link.

Do the arm64_32 rename via `ld -r` instead — a different Mach-O writer
that doesn't crash: -alias exposes the entry symbol at _main's address
and -unexported_symbol demotes the original _main to a local so it can't
collide with the Swift/native @main. arm64 and simulator keep the
objcopy path (the crash is arm64_32-specific).

Verified: nm shows _perry_main_init global (T) and _main demoted to
local (t) after the pass; the arm64_32 link gets past the entry-symbol
stage where it previously failed.

fix(runtime): typed-array integer-indexed [[Set]] follows the spec rejection + coercion rules (#6059)

A typed array is an Integer-Indexed exotic object; its [[Set]] (ECMA-262
§10.4.5.5) and the underlying TypedArraySetElement (§10.4.5.16) have two
observable behaviours Perry was swallowing:

1. Ordinary (non-index) property [[Set]] must report the OrdinarySet
   boolean. A non-writable own data expando, a setter-less accessor, or a
   new key on a non-extensible view must be REJECTED (return false → a
   strict `ta.k = v` throws, `Reflect.set(ta, k, v)` returns false).
   Previously every path returned `true`, so the rejection was silent.
   `typed_array_set_property_by_name` now returns the correct boolean, and
   `own_set_descriptor` consults the typed-array side tables directly
   (they are invisible to the generic address-keyed descriptor lookups,
   which are deliberately gated off for typed arrays) so the
   receiver-threading OrdinarySet reports the right result.

2. TypedArraySetElement runs ToNumber / ToBigInt on the value BEFORE the
   IsValidIntegerIndex bounds check, then drops the store for an invalid
   index. Perry short-circuited on an out-of-bounds index and never
   coerced, so `ta[100] = { valueOf() { … } }` never fired the hook and a
   throwing coercion never threw. The invalid-index paths
   (`js_typed_array_set`, `typed_array_set_numeric_index`, the
   IntegerIndex arm) now coerce for side effects first. The hot
   in-bounds / plain-number path is untouched — the out-of-bounds
   coercion is gated on a non-plain-number value.

Verified on an internal Linux sweep host against test262
built-ins/TypedArray + TypedArrayConstructors (2184 cases): +7 pass,
0 regressions. built-ins/Reflect + Proxy + Object/{defineProperty,freeze,
preventExtensions} (1688 cases): byte-identical, 0 regressions. Newly
passing: Set/key-is-not-numeric-index, key-is-not-canonical-index,
tonumber-value-throws, key-is-out-of-bounds-receiver-is-proto (+ BigInt
variants).

fix(hir): keep the null-guard for an optional method call on a `process.env` read (#6058)

`process.env?.[k]?.method()` (env read accessed inline) silently dropped the
per-receiver null-guard on the `?.` before the method, so the method was
invoked on the `undefined` an unset variable reads as. The result was the
STRING "undefined" (from stringifying the missing value) instead of a
short-circuit to `undefined`.

Cause: `process.env[k]` lowers to `IndexGet { object: ProcessEnv, .. }`, and
the `a?.b?.method()` lowering in `arm_optchain` only re-adds the receiver
null-guard when the receiver is `opt_call_receiver_repeatable`. That predicate
did not list `ProcessEnv` / env reads, so the receiver was deemed unsafe to
evaluate twice and the guard was skipped — leaving `process.env[k].method()`
to dereference the unguarded `undefined`. (Hoisting the env read into a local
first — `const e = process.env; e?.[k]?.method()` — worked, because a
`LocalGet` receiver is repeatable and kept the guard.)

Env reads are pure, side-effect-free, and stable within an expression, so they
are safe to evaluate more than once (guard + call). Add `ProcessEnv`,
`EnvGet`, and `EnvGetDynamic` (repeatable iff its key is) to
`opt_call_receiver_repeatable`.

This shape is ubiquitous: SDKs read config via `readEnv(k)?.trim()`, and a
common HTTP-client base-URL default is `process.env.BASE_URL?.trim() ?? "…"`,
which silently became the string "undefined" and produced
`new URL("undefined/…")` failures.

Adds an e2e test covering computed/static keys, a set var flowing through, and
a raw missing read being JS `undefined` (not the string).

fix(transform): #5975 — labeled `continue` in a yielding switch nested in a labeled loop spins forever (#6060)

A `continue <label>` inside a yielding `switch` case nested in a labeled loop
was never rewritten to a plain `continue`, so it survived verbatim into the
#5868 desugared switch's state machine, where nothing lowers it: the loop
never re-entered its dispatch state and re-ran the same `switch` forever
(generator/async spun at 100% CPU, produced no value).

The labeled-loop linearizer's `rewrite_labeled_bc_in_stmts` rewrites
`continue <label>` -> plain `continue` (so the loop lowering maps it to the
re-entry sentinel) but descended only `if`/`try` and stopped at `switch`;
meanwhile #5868's `switch_cases_have_loop_continue` only detects a plain
`Stmt::Continue`, so a `LabeledContinue` in a case was invisible to both. The
unlabeled `continue;` always worked.

Fix: descend into nested `switch` case bodies to rewrite `continue <label>`
-> plain `continue` (a switch never captures `continue`, so it always
continues the enclosing loop) — the exact path the unlabeled form already
took. `break <label>` inside a nested switch is deliberately left alone (a
switch captures `break`; that remains the pre-existing single-sentinel
limitation already documented on the function).

Repro shape: `loop: while (true) { switch (x) { case k: yield v; continue loop } break loop }`
— hand-written generator lexers use it pervasively (e.g. the `yaml` package's
indicator/block-scalar lexers), so native `yaml.parse()` of non-trivial input,
and a large esbuild-bundled CLI app parsing YAML front-matter during module
initialization, spun forever.

New e2e suite crates/perry/tests/issue_5975_labeled_continue_in_yielding_switch.rs
(generator while/for, async, and a yield*-delegating lexer analogue), each
byte-for-byte vs node and timeout-bounded so a regression fails instead of
hanging. cargo test -p perry-transform: 48 passed.

fix(runtime): OrdinarySet on a distinct receiver rejects a receiver-owned accessor instead of firing its setter (#6063)

the OrdinarySet walk is a data property (or absent, meaning

from the object walked, a RECEIVER-owned accessor makes the algorithm
return false WITHOUT invoking the setter. The receiver's setter only fires
when it is the descriptor found by the walk itself (the Accessor arm in
`ordinary_set_with_receiver`), never through this
CreateDataProperty-on-receiver tail.

setter for that sub-case and returned true, so

data property mis-fired the receiver's setter and reported success.

makes test262

pass (a typed-array element source, an accessor-bearing receiver). Verified

fix(codegen): #5094/#26/#321 — derive GC raw-f64/pointer masks from the authoritative init chain (#6064)

Tolong_Siki — are unknown to regex-syntax (bundled UCD is Unicode 16.0),

each \p{...}/\P{...} reference — across all alias keys (sc/script/scx/

  Sidetic/Sidt     U+10940..10959
  Tai_Yo/Tayo      U+1E6C0..1E6DE, U+1E6E0..1E6F5, U+1E6FE..1E6FF

fix(codegen): #6065 — user `charAt`/`charCodeAt`/`codePointAt` class method mis-lowered to the String builtin (#6066)

* fix(codegen): #6065 — user class method named charAt/charCodeAt/codePointAt mis-lowered to the String builtin

A builtin-named method on a non-provably-string receiver takes the static
String-method fast path gated by an arity heuristic (#5271) so a user method
sharing a String name (`trim(value, schema)`) falls through to runtime dispatch
when the arg count can't match. The char-access methods ignore surplus args per
spec, so `string_only_method_arity_ok` returns true for ANY arg count — the
escape hatch never fires for them, and a user `charAt(n)` on a class instance is
forced onto `lower_string_method` with the receiver coerced to
`"[object Object]"` (so `this.charAt(0)` returns `"["`, `this.charAt(1)` `"o"`, …).

`slice`/`indexOf` are unaffected (excluded from the string-only set for arrays);
only `charAt`/`charCodeAt`/`codePointAt` hit this.

Impact: the `yaml` package's tokenizer is built on
`Lexer.charAt(n) { return this.buffer[this.pos + n]; }`; mis-dispatched, its
`*lex` state machine never advances `this.pos` and spins forever, hanging
`yaml.parse()` (and any large esbuild-bundled CLI app that parses YAML at
module-init time) at 100% CPU.

Fix: don't take the static String path when the receiver's statically-known
class (or an ancestor) defines its OWN method of that name — a user method wins
over a String builtin. Genuine string receivers are unaffected (no known class),
and Any-typed strings still route through the runtime `jsval.is_string()` arm.

fix(runtime): #6067 — OOB index of a generator/async local string returns "" instead of undefined (#6086)

`s[i]` (string indexing) must yield `undefined` for a non-canonical or
out-of-bounds index, unlike `s.charAt(i)` which yields "". Statically
string-typed receivers took the correct static path (`js_string_index_get`,
#3987), but the runtime tag dispatcher `js_dyn_index_get` — reached whenever the
receiver's static type is unknown — called `js_string_char_at` directly in its
string arm (charAt semantics: OOB -> ""), missing the `idx >= len -> undefined`
guard.

A generator/async body is CPS-transformed and its locals are boxed for
cross-state persistence, which erases each local's static type; so `line[i]` on
a `const line = ""` (or any local string) inside a generator/async fn is not
seen as a string and lands in `js_dyn_index_get` -> `js_string_char_at` -> "".

The user-visible bite: the `yaml` package's lexer detects end-of-line with
`line[n] === undefined` (where `line = this.getLine()` is a local); with it
returning "", `parseDocument`'s `switch (line[n])` never matched `case
undefined`, took a non-advancing `default`, and the `*lex` state machine spun
forever — hanging `yaml.parse()` of any non-trivial input (and a large
esbuild-bundled CLI app that parses YAML front-matter at module-init time) at
100% CPU.

Fix: `js_dyn_index_get`'s string arm routes through `js_string_index_get`
(canonical-index validation + OOB -> undefined), matching the static path. This
is strictly more correct (it also rejects fractional / negative / non-canonical
indices the old `index as i32` truncation accepted). Array / typed-array /
object arms are unchanged.

Test: crates/perry/tests/issue_6067_generator_local_string_index_oob.rs
(generator + async local string OOB, in-bounds control, generator
array/typed-array/object indexing unaffected, and a yaml-lexer-shaped scan loop
that only terminates on an OOB `undefined`). The inline `yaml` Lexer now lexes
to completion (was an infinite loop). Part of the #5975 large-bundle async-init
hang (after #6060, #6066).

fix(hir): #6089 — array-box an UNINITIALIZED shared-mutable capture; scope the desugar's id rewrites (#6090)

The #5951 one-element-array-box desugar (ce3eed163) regressed the compiled
Next.js standalone server from 5/8 byte-identical routes to 0/8: every route
returned a 21-byte 500 with `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to
object`. Bisected to ce3eed163 (parent + the #6055 boot fix is 5/8).

Root cause — the declaring-`Let` array-wrap skipped a `let` with NO
initializer:

    if let Some(e) = init.take() { *init = Some(Expr::Array(vec![e])); }

but every use of the flagged id is still rewritten to `id[0]`. SWC emits
exactly this shape for hoisted computed-property temps:

    let prop;
    class NodeNextRequest extends BaseNextRequest {
        static #_ = prop = _NEXT_REQUEST_META = ...;   // mutates `prop`
    }

(next/dist/server/base-http/node.js — the wrapper classes for EVERY request
and response). `prop` is detected as a shared-mutable capture, its uses
become `prop[0]`, but no array is ever allocated — so the static
initializer's `prop[0] = ...` is an IndexSet on `undefined` and throws the
observed TypeError the moment Next lazy-requires the module inside the first
request, 500ing every route. Fix: wrap a None init as `[undefined]`, which
preserves `let prop;` semantics through the box.

Also hardens the pass's id handling (found while isolating the above, both
real unsoundness even though neither caused this app's breakage):

- detection results and rewrites are now scoped to the body that owns the
  ids instead of one module-global set applied to every body (LocalIds are
  not unique across function scopes — member params/lets restart their id
  space);
- within a rewritten region, an id is only desugared when it is UNAMBIGUOUS
  (declared exactly once across deep `Let`s and nested-closure params —
  nested closures restart their id spaces, so a numeric rewrite is only
  sound for unique ids). An ambiguous id keeps the pre-#6054 split-cell
  behavior instead of risking corruption of an unrelated same-numbered
  local.
- diagnostics: `PERRY_5951_SKIP_MODS=<substr,substr>` skips the desugar per
  module; `PERRY_5951_TRACE=1` prints the per-module desugar inventory and
  ambiguous-skip decisions (both compile-time, inert by default, matching
  the existing `PERRY_NO_5951` escape hatch).

Validated: the #5951 suite passes unchanged (10/10); the Next.js standalone
matrix goes 0/8 -> 5/8 byte-identical vs node v26 (/, /about, /counter,
/api/hello GET+POST), server surviving the dynamic-route requests.

fix(runtime): implement Date.prototype[Symbol.toPrimitive] (#6091)

`Date.prototype[Symbol.toPrimitive]` was entirely missing — `typeof
Date.prototype[Symbol.toPrimitive]` was `undefined`, so the 18 test262
`built-ins/Date/prototype/Symbol.toPrimitive/*` cases failed.

Install it per ECMA-262 §21.4.4.45 as a non-enumerable own method of
`Date.prototype`, keyed by the real well-known `Symbol.toPrimitive`
(`{ writable:false, enumerable:false, configurable:true }`, `.name`
"[Symbol.toPrimitive]", `.length` 1). It is a generic `OrdinaryToPrimitive`
dispatcher — not brand-checked to Date, not reading the time value:

  1. If `Type(this)` is not Object -> TypeError.
  2. hint "string"/"default" -> tryFirst string; "number" -> tryFirst number;
     any other hint (undefined, a `new String("number")` wrapper, an object)
     -> TypeError.
  3. Return OrdinaryToPrimitive(this, tryFirst).

- `value/to_string.rs`: a spec-faithful `ordinary_to_primitive_for_toprimitive`
  that Gets each ordered method (js_reflect_get -> accessor getters fire, getter
  throws propagate), calls it only when IsCallable, returns the first primitive,
  and throws TypeError if none yields a primitive. A non-callable slot is
  skipped (not treated as the default), unlike the String()/`+` helpers.
- `symbol/get.rs`: a DateCell receiver resolves symbol reads off its own side
  table then Date.prototype instead of the pointer-deref paths (a DateCell is
  not an ObjectHeader).
- `symbol/iterator.rs`: `js_to_primitive` short-circuits Date values (mirroring
  the existing Temporal short-circuit), so implicit `+`/String()/template
  coercion stays on the proven dedicated Date fast paths. The installed method
  is still reachable through the explicit read+call form, which does not route
  through `js_to_primitive`.

perf(codegen,runtime): #5093 — class-field loop versioning: monomorphic field hot loops run call-free (#6061)

* perf(codegen,runtime): #5093 — class-field loop versioning: monomorphic field hot loops run call-free

The collapse #5093 tracks: for (let i = k0; i < B; i++) whose single
statement is a raw-f64 class-field store (or scalar accumulator) on a
loop-invariant receiver of statically known class now lowers as a
versioned loop pair. The preheader runs the inline shape check ONCE
(enable flag, pointer tag/band, gc-type, not-forwarded, REGULAR,
class_id, field_count, keys identity, typed-layout intact bit, and
not-frozen when the loop stores); the fast clone does bare
GEP+load/store on the preheader-cached object pointer with NO guard and
NO fallback call, so the receiver stays in a register and LLVM collapses
the body to load/fadd/store. Raw stores keep an inline plain-finite
value check that side-exits to the slow clone's preheader BEFORE any
side effect of the current iteration commits (single-effect-last body
shape, per the #6011 range-loop protocol), and the slow clone — today's
guarded loop — resumes at the current i.

Safety (memory-corruption class): the fast clone is call-free ⇒
allocation-free ⇒ no GC can move the receiver or run any runtime path
that mutates class_id / keys / field_count / intact / frozen / the
enable flag mid-loop (all mutation sites are runtime calls; GC triggers
only on allocation). The matcher enforces call-freeness by shape
(pure-arithmetic walker mirroring the packed-f64 range loop's, property
name + class name denylists mirroring every dispatch gate ahead of the
class-field diamonds), and lowering VERIFIES it: the preheader's deref
block is left unterminated until the fast clone's emitted blocks are
scanned for non-intrinsic calls — an unpredicted call wires the
preheader straight to the slow clone instead.

Also fixes the regression that had silently disabled the #5198 inline
class-field fast path in every program: the runtime bootstrap installs
fn.name property descriptors on builtin closures through the generic
defineProperty path, and set_property_attrs/set_accessor_descriptor
flipped the process-global PERRY_CLASS_FIELD_INLINE_GUARD_DISABLED kill
switch on ANY descriptor install. The flip is now scoped to descriptor
targets that can actually shadow a guarded class-field slot access — a
class instance (nonzero class_id) or a registered class prototype
object (exactly what descriptor_blocks_class_field_{get,set} walk).
GLOBAL_DESCRIPTORS_IN_USE is still set unconditionally, so guard calls
keep routing through the full contract whenever any descriptor exists.

vs node ~22ms on the same machine; issue target was <= ~50ms.

fix(codegen,runtime): #6088 — typed-array out-of-bounds index reads 0 instead of undefined (#6092)

An out-of-range canonical integer index of a Uint8Array / Buffer read the 0
byte-sentinel instead of `undefined`. Perry's Uint8Array is Buffer-backed and
`u8[i]` / `buf[i]` lower to the native i32 accessors `js_uint8array_get` /
`js_buffer_get`, whose i32 return type forces `0` for any out-of-range read, so
`new Uint8Array([5,6,7])[9]` read `0` and `typeof` was "number". ECMAScript
IntegerIndexedExotic [[Get]] requires `undefined`. Other typed-array kinds
(Float64Array, Int32Array, …) already routed through the OOB-correct
`js_typed_array_get`, so only the Buffer-backed Uint8Array / Buffer path was
affected; negative and fractional keys already routed to the dynamic-key helper
and stayed `undefined`.

Add JS-value accessors that return `undefined` for out-of-range while returning
the byte as a number in range:
  - `js_buffer_index_get_value` (BufferHeader), sharing `js_buffer_get`'s read
    logic via a new `read_buffer_byte` helper;
  - `js_uint8array_index_get_value`, mirroring `js_uint8array_get`'s dispatch
    (a real Uint8Array TypedArrayHeader vs a Buffer-backed registered buffer).
Route the unproven-bounds slow path of the `Uint8ArrayGet`, `BufferIndexGet`,
and `is_uint8array_receiver` IndexGet lowerings through them. The proven-bounds
inline load is untouched (in-range fast path preserved); the native i32
accessors keep their 0-sentinel contract for their many native callers.

A value-context byte read now lowers to the new getter instead of the i32
accessor, so the compiler-output-regression hot-loop allowlists
(benchmarks/compiler_output/workloads.toml) gain the two getters wherever their
i32 siblings (js_uint8array_get / js_buffer_get) are already permitted.

Adds a runtime unit test and an issue_6088 e2e test (incl. a value-context scan
loop that spun forever pre-fix because 0 !== undefined).

fix(runtime): own_key_present must not OOB-read keys_array on non-object receivers (#6093)

`own_key_present(obj, key)` read `(*obj).keys_array` at ObjectHeader offset 16
after only a null/alignment/range guard, without checking the receiver is a
`GC_TYPE_OBJECT`. A non-object that clears those guards — most importantly a
real `Map`/`Set`, whose header is 16 bytes (`size`/`capacity`/`entries`) with
no `keys_array` field — makes that load read 8 bytes past the header into the
adjacent allocation.

This is reachable from `js_object_get_field_by_name`'s `.size` fast path (the
`class X extends Map|Set` support): an `any`-typed `map.size` — as produced
when a Map's static type is erased through a dynamically-dispatched
`getX(): any` call — is dispatched by name, hits
`name == "size" && !own_key_present(obj, key)`, and dereferences `[obj+16]`.
When the out-of-bounds word is a live neighbour's GC-header value it clears
the keys-pointer guard and then faults on the `[keys-8]` GC-type-tag read
(`ldurb w8,[x20,#-8]; cmp #1`, EXC_BAD_ACCESS).

Arrays/strings/closures already route through their own
`array_own_key_present`/`string_primitive_own_key_present`/
`closure_own_key_present`; `own_key_present` is the object-only variant, so a
`keys_array` read only makes sense for `GC_TYPE_OBJECT`. Gate it on the GC type
tag via the existing `try_read_gc_header` (which safely rejects header-less
slab allocations and non-heap addresses). A non-object has no own string keys,
so answer false and fall through to the type-specific tail, which serves
`Map.size` correctly.

Tests: a perry-runtime unit test plus an e2e compile+run regression.

fix(codegen): #6039 over-filtered module_local_types, breaking receiver-typed throws in harness closures (#6096)

#6039 (#5982 fix) stripped every MODULE-GLOBAL captured local out of
`module_local_types` so the typed-ABI closure specialization would not
read an unset capture slot for a global read through `@perry_global_*`.
That part was right, but `module_local_types` is used for TWO purposes in
`compile_module`:

  1. the typed-ABI closure-clone DECISION
     (`typed_{f64,i1,i32,string}_closure_rejection_reason_with_types`), and
  2. the per-function-body RECEIVER-TYPE oracle — it is handed to
     `emit_module_artifacts` -> `FnCtx.local_types`, which drives
     `static_type_of` / `is_array_expr`.

Removing a module-global's declared type from (2) mis-classified a
captured array receiver as untyped INSIDE a closure. `arr.every()` with an
undefined callbackfn then lowered to the generic dynamic method dispatch
(`js_arraylike_*`) instead of the array-typed path that emits
`js_validate_array_callback`, so the mandatory TypeError was never thrown.
The test262 harness runs every negative case as
`assert.throws(TypeError, function () { ... })` — a module-level closure
that captures the module-global under test — so the swallowed throw
surfaced as 24 conformance regressions:

  - 8 Array HOF callbackfn-not-callable cases
    (every/filter/forEach/map/reduce/reduceRight/some 15.4.4.*-4-1)
  - 3 symbol-strict [[Set]] cases (Object.defineProperty/freeze/seal
    *-strict: obj[sym]=2 on a non-writable prop must throw)
  - the private-async-method / Proxy / Temporal cases that reach the same
    harness-closure path.

Fix: keep the module-globals filter scoped to the typed-ABI specialization
only. Build a dedicated `typed_abi_local_types` (module-locals minus

fix(runtime): any-typed Headers/collection-handle .keys()/.entries()/.values() returned empty (#6095)

An any-typed `.keys()`/`.entries()`/`.values()` call folds to the array-only
`Expr::Array{Keys,Entries,Values}` (perry-hir #597), whose runtime helpers read
the receiver as a heap `ArrayHeader`. A Web `Headers` (and `FormData` /
`URLSearchParams`) instance is a fetch-band registry *handle*, not an
`ArrayHeader`, so `js_array_{keys,entries,values}_iter_obj` read the handle id
as an array length and yielded an empty iterator — while `.has()`/`.get()`
(dynamic dispatch) and the computed `headers["keys"]()` form worked.

Impact: a large esbuild-bundled client SDK builds request headers, wraps them
as `{ values: Headers }`, and merges via `yield* wrapper.values.entries()`.
Because `wrapper.values` is any-typed, `.entries()` folded to `ArrayEntries` →
empty → every header was silently dropped and the request failed its
`validateHeaders` auth check.

`collection_iter_obj_for_receiver` already routes Map/Set receivers to their
iterators; route fetch-band handles through `js_native_call_method` →
`js_headers_{keys,entries,values}` too. Non-collection fetch handles
(Response/Request/Blob) and genuine plain objects still fall through to the
empty-array path. Adds an e2e regression test.

fix(runtime): bundle Unicode 17.0 property-escape data for pre-existing properties (#6097)

Perry's regex engine expands `\p{...}` / `\P{...}` through `regex-syntax`
0.8.11, which bundles the Unicode 16.0 UCD. Test262's
`built-ins/RegExp/property-escapes/generated/*` cases were regenerated against
Unicode 17.0, so every property whose code-point set changed between UCD 16 and
UCD 17 fails: the regex matches the UCD-16 set, the test asserts the UCD-17 set.

#6068 handled the four brand-new self-contained U17 scripts (Beria_Erfe,
Sidetic, Tai_Yo, Tolong_Siki). This covers the remaining 69 failing cases —
U17 changes to *pre-existing* scripts (Han, Latin, Arabic, ...), general
categories (L, M, N, Lo, ...), binary properties (Alphabetic, ID_Start,
XID_Continue, Grapheme_Base, ...) and the Unknown/Zzzz catch-alls.

New `regex/unicode17_data.rs` carries, per affected property, either:
  * Delta  — UCD 17 only *added* code points; the added ranges are unioned into
    the crate's own class (`\p{Prop}` -> `[\p{Prop}<delta>]`). 58 properties.
  * Full   — the crate can't represent the property (Script=Unknown/Zzzz,
    Changes_When_NFKC_Casefolded) or UCD 17 *removed* points (e.g. U+0295 left
    Cased), so a union would over-match; the full UCD-17 range set replaces the
    crate's expansion. 10 properties.

`regex/unicode17.rs` gains `u17_replacement()` (wraps the data into the correct
positive/negated/in-class form, mirroring `script_replacement`), and
`grammar.rs` gains one dispatch arm before the legacy never-match fallback so
the U17 overrides for Script=Unknown / Changes_When_NFKC_Casefolded win.

Every range set is derived offline by diffing each generated test's own
embedded UCD-17 `matchSymbols` against the UCD-16 tables `regex-syntax` ships;
`delta = UCD17 \ UCD16`, promoted to Full automatically when `UCD16 \ UCD17` is
non-empty. This is bundled data, not a dependency bump — `regex-syntax` 0.8.11
is already newest and ships no U17 data.

built-ins/RegExp/property-escapes: 69 runtime-fails -> 0 (585/585, 100%).
built-ins/RegExp regression gate (fix vs clean origin/main, native sweep on an
internal Linux host): 0 new failures, 69 fixed.
