fix(#6728): pi interactive mode renders nothing after Enter — 3 async/codegen fixes (#6740)

* fix(async): multi-await throw leaves no orphaned rejected promise (#6728)

An async function that reaches a `throw` after two-or-more `await`s rejected
its result promise correctly (a surrounding try/catch caught it) but ALSO
surfaced a spurious "Uncaught (in promise)", exiting the process non-zero.

Root cause: `then_backpatch_result` attaches the async-step resume thunks to
the awaited promise. The first `await` (activation result promise not yet
created, `trap_next` null) uses `js_promise_attach_handlers` (no chained
then-result). Every SUBSEQUENT await (`trap_next` non-null) used
`js_promise_then`, which mints an intermediate then-result promise. When the
resumed step later throws, its fulfill thunk returns the step body's fresh
`Promise.reject(e)` (forwarded into `trap_next` by
`forward_swallowed_rejection`), and that then-result promise ADOPTS the
rejection — becoming a rejected promise with no handler attached. The orphan is
reported as an unhandled rejection.

Fix: use `js_promise_attach_handlers` (next = null) for subsequent awaits too
and return `trap_next` (matching the reuse fast paths), so a multi-await async
function that throws rejects exactly one promise — the activation result.

This is the pi interactive-TUI blocker: the Anthropic SDK's makeRequest throws
the 401 APIError after many awaits, so the phantom rejection fired and the
turn's error never rendered.

* fix(async-gen): split control-flow constructs on nested `await` too (#6709 completion, #6728)

#6709 made async-generator `await`s suspend via StateExit::Await, but only for
awaits at a statement-level position the linearizer's main loop visits directly.
An `await` nested inside an `if` / loop / `try` whose branch has NO `yield` was
missed: the split gates (`Stmt::If`, `Stmt::While`, `Stmt::For`, `Stmt::Try`, …
in linearize.rs) are all guarded by `body_contains_yield(...)`, which detected
`yield` but not `await`. So the construct was emitted inline (unsplit), the
`await` inside it never became a StateExit::Await, and it fell through to the
busy-wait poll loop — deadlocking whenever the awaited Promise is settled by an
external producer.

This is exactly pi's EventStream async iterator:
    while (true) {
      if (this.queue.length === 0) { if (this.done) return; await new Promise(...); }
      while (this.queue.length > 0) yield this.queue.shift();
    }
The inner `while` has the yield, so the outer `while(true)` splits — but the
`if (queue.length === 0) { await ... }` has only an await, so it stayed inline
and the await busy-waited forever. pi's turn UI never advanced (no spinner, no
error render). Minimal repro: `await` inside an `if` in an async generator.

Fix: `body_contains_yield` also counts a statement-level `await` (bare / let= /
return / throw) as a suspend point, gated on `linearize_async_generator()` and on
`Expr::Await` (which only survives to the linearizer for async generators), so
plain async functions and sync generators are unaffected. Mirrors the four
`Expr::Await` statement arms #6709 added to linearize.rs.

* test(#6728): regression tests for multi-await-throw phantom + async-gen await-in-conditional

- test_issue_6728_multi_await_throw_no_orphan_rejection.sh: an async fn that
  throws after >=2 awaits, caught by try/catch, must exit 0 with no spurious
  'Uncaught (in promise)'.
- test_issue_6728_async_gen_await_in_conditional.sh: pi's EventStream push/pull
  shape (async gen with an await inside an 'if' in a loop, settled by an
  external producer) must not deadlock.

* fix(codegen): box async-step state locals in class-field initializers (#6728)

A class-field-initializer async arrow whose body contains `await` did not run
its body when called: calling it returned immediately and the `await` on it
resolved with no effect. The same closure written as `const f = async …`, an
object-literal property, a function return, or a constructor-body `this.f = …`
assignment all worked.

Root cause: the async-to-generator transform lowers such a closure into an
async-step state machine whose state locals (__state/__done/__sent/…) are
mutated across resume calls AND captured by the step closure, so they must be
boxed (shared heap cells) — the wrapper allocates the boxes and the step closure
reads/writes them. But `collect_module_boxed_vars` / `collect_module_local_types`
(boxed_locals.rs), which build the module-wide boxed-var and local-type sets,
walked every closure-bearing member kind (functions, methods, getters, setters,
static methods, computed members, constructors, module init) EXCEPT class field
initializers. So a field-init closure's step locals were absent from the boxed
set: the wrapper boxed them, but the step closure emitted raw
`js_closure_set_capture_bits` writes that overwrote the box slots with raw
values, desyncing the state machine — state 0 never ran the user body.

Fix: walk `class.fields` / `class.static_fields` initializers (and computed
keys) in both collectors, mirroring the closure/global collectors that already
do. Verified via LLVM IR: the field-init step closure now boxes its state locals
identically to the constructor-body case.

This is the last blocker for pi's interactive TUI: `_handleAgentEvent` is a
class-field async arrow, so agent events never reached the UI.

fix(string): re-pair split surrogates on `+=` append (node parity) (#6742)

`js_string_append` (the `+=`/string-building path) copied operand bytes
verbatim and never called `canonicalize_surrogate_pairs`, unlike every
expression-concat path. So a lone high surrogate at the end of `dest` plus a
lone low surrogate at the start of `src` were stored as two separate 3-byte
WTF-8 sequences instead of the astral code point's 4-byte UTF-8:

    const e = "a👋b"; const hi = e[1], lo = e[2];
    hi + lo;                      // 👋            (correct — concat canonicalizes)
    let Y = ""; Y += hi; Y += lo; // was: lone high surrogate (cp 55357, len 2)

Node re-pairs adjacent surrogates in both cases; perry only did on concat.
Any string rebuilt one UTF-16 code unit at a time over emoji/astral text
(ANSI stripping, manual parsers, width calc) was silently corrupted —
`codePointAt`/`[...s].length`/grapheme segmentation all disagreed with Node.

Found while testing the pi TUI: pi's `visibleWidth` strips ANSI via
`stripped += clean[i]`, which splits an emoji's surrogate pair across two
`+=` appends → over-counted line width → pi's render invariant aborted on any
emoji in a colored line (a real streamed assistant reply crashed the UI).

Fix: propagate the lone-surrogate flag through append and, when a high→low
pair straddles the dest|src join, canonicalize the result — mirroring
`js_string_concat`. The join is detected in O(1) from the boundary bytes
(both operands are already canonical, so a pair can only newly form there),
so ordinary ASCII appends stay allocation-free and never pay for a scan.

Differential regression test (perry output must byte-match node):
tests/test_string_append_surrogate_repair.sh.

perf(object): O(1) own-key answers for wide-object defineProperty and `in` (#6748) (#6749)

* perf(object): O(1) own-key answers for wide-object defineProperty and `in`

Repeated `Object.defineProperty` and `k in obj` on a wide object (past the
keys-index threshold) were O(N) per call — the define flow ran THREE linear
keys_array scans (`enforce_define_property_invariants` → `own_key_present`,
the existing-attrs check → `obj_value_has_own_key`, and
`ensure_key_in_keys_array`'s duplicate check), and the `in` operator's
own-key walk ran a fourth. Build-then-fill loops were quadratic:

    for (const k of Object.keys(src)) {
      if (k in t && t[k] === src[k]) continue;
      Object.defineProperty(t, k, { enumerable: true, get: () => src[k] });
    }

This is exactly the webpack/Babel CJS re-export module shape. Under perry a
single `@babel/types/lib/index.js` init took ~292ms vs node's 3ms (94x) —
the dominant per-module cost of the pi coding agent's startup. Micro: 2400
getter defines took 527ms, scaling x3.4 per doubling (quadratic).

Fix: answer own-key presence through the same authoritative sidecar hash
index (`KEYS_INDEX`) the [[Set]] fast path already maintains for its
append-without-scan ("the sidecar would have found it if it existed"):

- `ensure_key_in_keys_array`: threshold-gated sidecar probe replaces the
  duplicate-check scan; the append records the new key via
  `keys_index_insert` so the index stays fresh (contiguous, no rebuild).
- new `own_key_present_via_index` (Some(present) when the sidecar is
  applicable; None falls back to the linear paths — native-module
  namespaces with virtual keys always fall back), used by the define
  flow's invariants + existing-attrs checks and by
  `ordinary_has_property`'s own-key step (the `in` operator).
- `keys_index_lookup`'s rebuild/validation now decodes SSO inline keys
  (`js_string_key_bytes`) instead of skipping them (`is_string()` is
  heap-tag-only) — pre-fix, an authoritative miss could duplicate an
  SSO-stored short key; this also hardens the existing [[Set]] append.

After: 2400 getter defines 527ms → 96ms, scaling x2 per doubling (linear);
`@babel/types` re-export init 292ms → 113ms; full jiti/babel.cjs bundle
init 688ms → 609ms. perry-runtime suite 1439/0.

Differential regression test (perry must byte-match node):
tests/test_wide_object_define_in_linear.sh — dedup on redefine, attribute
retention, SSO short keys, delete-then-redefine (index invalidation),
non-configurable redefine throw, non-extensible define throw, `in`
present/absent/deleted, and a scaling sanity bound.

* perf(object): per-array descriptor gates + raw keys-array scans

Second layer of the #6748 grind, found by sampling the `in`-operator loop:

1. `js_array_get_f64` / `array_has_own_index` / the named-setter dispatch
   gated their per-index accessor probe on the PROCESS-GLOBAL
   `descriptors_in_use()` flag — which builtin init flips to true for every
   program — and then paid `index.to_string()` + a `(usize, String)`
   accessor-map probe (two String allocs + TLS) on EVERY checked array
   element read. Since the runtime's own keys_array walks (`in`,
   defineProperty, Object.keys, the sidecar/wide-index builds) read
   elements through this path, every object-key operation was taxed. Gate
   on the PER-ARRAY `OBJ_FLAG_ARRAY_DESCRIPTORS` header bit instead — the
   same flag `js_array_get_f64_unchecked` already trusts, set by every
   `define_array_property` install site.

2. `ordinary_has_property`'s per-prototype-level accessor probe now honors
   `ACCESSORS_IN_USE` + the per-object `OBJ_FLAG_HAS_DESCRIPTORS` gate (the
   address-reuse-safe pattern the [[Set]] path uses) before paying the
   String-key side-table lookup.

3. The keys_array scan loops (`own_key_present`, `ensure_key_in_keys_array`,
   the KEYS_INDEX/WIDE_KEY_INDEX builds and validations) read slots through
   the generic element getter — re-running forward-resolution and the
   lazy/Map/Set registry probes per element. New `keys_array_dense_slots`
   resolves the grow-forward pointer ONCE and hands back the dense backing
   for direct indexing.

Measured (2400-op micros, node in parens): `in` hit/miss 259/267ms →
103/106ms (0.4/0.6ms); getter defines 99→77ms (3.7ms); value defines
90→69ms (3.0ms). Real-world: the pi agent's jiti/babel.cjs bundle init
688ms → 334ms total across both commits (node 44ms). perry-runtime suite
1439/0; wide-object differential test byte-matches node.

perf(codegen): eliminate per-access array-read guard calls in hot masked-index loops (#6750)

* perf(codegen): eliminate per-access array-read guard calls in hot masked-index loops

Array element reads in tight loops compiled to one runtime guard call per
access (js_typed_feedback_numeric_array_index_get_guard and the typed-array
getters), making integer/array-heavy JS 10-15x slower than V8 even though
the element load itself was already inline. bcryptjs's Blowfish S-boxes are
exactly this shape, turning a login's compareSync into seconds of overhead.

Three complementary fixes:

1. Static index windows for the buffer bounds prover (expr/range_facts.rs):
   int_range_expr now understands 'e & K' (always [0, K] for a non-negative
   i32 constant mask, by ToInt32 semantics), 'e >>> k' (ToUint32 result
   bounded by the shift), and non-negative 'a | b' windows. Width-tracked
   typed-array reads like S[i & 1023] / S[256 + ((x >>> 16) & 0xff)] now
   prove bounds against the tracked view length and take the existing
   unchecked inline load instead of an out-of-line getter call. An IndexGet
   range rule (elem-kind value range, gated on the same bounds proof) feeds
   the same machinery. The i32 fast path classifies proven in-bounds loads
   from int-element typed arrays as native i32 leaves, so bit-mixing chains
   stay in add/xor i32 instead of round-tripping f64 through the branchless
   ToInt32 tower.

2. Collector support so const typed-array lookup tables behave like ints
   (collectors/): const S = new Int32Array(<literal>) bindings that never
   escape element-access receiver position are recorded with their length;
   'const a = S[x & 0xff]'-style Lets seed integer_locals (window proven
   inside [0, length)), and the pointer analysis knows numerically-indexed
   typed-array reads never yield pointers - killing the per-iteration GC
   shadow-slot spills and dynamic string_or_number_add dispatch the Blowfish
   round function was paying for.

3. Read-only DENSE tier for the #6011 packed-f64 range loop (stmt/loops.rs,
   typed_feedback.rs): the versioned-loop matcher now also accepts
   multi-statement read-only bodies whose array reads carry static masked
   windows, guarded once at loop entry by a dense window guard (window must
   be hole-free - loads then need no hole check and no side exit, which is
   what makes multi-statement bodies safe to version). Two guard tiers:
   _dense_i32 additionally proves every window value is an i32 integer so
   loads materialize as a bare exact fptosi and LLVM keeps (s + S[i & k])|0
   loops fully in integer registers; _dense keeps raw-double loads for float
   lookup tables. Read eligibility no longer consults the array-kind /
   materialization-hazard facts: mark_unknown_call_escape blanket-hazards
   every function-local array whenever the function contains any call, which
   kept every locally built lookup table off the fast path forever; the
   entry guard re-validates the actual runtime array, so a wrong static hint
   costs one failed guard, never correctness.

Benchmarks (Apple M1-class, 20M reads / 5M Blowfish-F rounds, byte-identical
outputs vs node --experimental-strip-types):

                       node    perry before   perry after
  arith-only (20M)     30 ms       26 ms          26 ms
  plain-Array read     21 ms      200 ms           4 ms
  Int32Array read      16 ms      235 ms          10 ms
  Blowfish-F mimic     18 ms      558 ms          15 ms

An edge-case suite (OOB windows, holes, fractional/huge/NaN elements,
frozen arrays, string elements, shrunk length, mixed counter+masked
indices, all int TA kinds, escape shapes) is byte-identical between this
branch and origin/main; the four pre-existing divergences from node it
found are unrelated to this change and reproduce on main.

* refactor(codegen): split masked-window load helpers into expr/masked_window.rs

The masked-window fact consult + the two load-emission tiers pushed
expr/index_get.rs past the 2000-line lint cap (check_file_size.sh); move
them to a topical sibling module. Pure move plus factoring the shared
raw in-window load emission; no behavior change (benchmarks and the
edge-case suite are byte-identical before/after).

* fix(codegen): rewire the generic-lower masked-window consult to the split module

The module split in the previous commit missed the second consult site
(the generic lower IndexGet arm) — it still called the moved functions
unqualified and the crate did not compile. Verified with a from-scratch
build this time; benchmarks and the edge suite are unchanged.

perf(object): `in` fast path (re-land) + single-pass descriptor decode for defineProperty (#6748) (#6757)

* perf(object): ordinary-object fast path for the `in` operator

`js_object_has_property` ran every receiver through a ~10-arm classification
gauntlet — proxy, handle bands, symbol keys, class refs, fetch subclass,
exotic cells, typed arrays, buffers, Map/Set, SharedArrayBuffer — each arm a
TLS access + registry HashMap probe. For the overwhelmingly-common receiver
(a plain heap object) with a string key, that preamble WAS the cost of `in`:
~44µs per call against node's ~0.2µs, with `_tlv_get_addr` alone 26% of the
profile.

Fast path: one `try_read_gc_header` classifies the receiver. A
`GC_TYPE_OBJECT` cannot be a proxy or handle id (non-heap bands), a typed
array / buffer / Map / Set / promise / error / date / temporal cell (own GC
types), a closure, or an INT32 class ref — so those arms are skipped
wholesale. RegExp cells are the one OBJECT-typed exotic, so a single
exotic-registry probe stays in the path and routes them to the exotic arm
unchanged (`"lastIndex" in re`). The three object-relevant arms are
preserved: the fetch-subclass native forward (now gated on a process-global
"a fetch subclass ever stashed a handle" flag, so programs that never build
one skip its per-call key alloc + property read), `#private`-name hiding,
and native-module virtual keys.

This also accelerates `Object.defineProperty` for free: the spec's
`ToPropertyDescriptor` field probes (`desc_has_field`) route through
`js_object_has_property` per field and now take the fast path.

Measured (2400-op micros, node in parens): `in` hit 103ms -> 0.3ms (0.4ms —
parity); `in` miss 106ms -> 4.0ms (0.6ms); getter defines 77 -> 62ms;
same-key redefine 67 -> 48ms. The pi agent's jiti/babel.cjs bundle init:
334ms -> ~300ms (node 44ms). perry-runtime suite 1439/0; the wide-object
differential test grew an `in` receiver-kind section (object/class
instance/prototype chain/array/Date/RegExp/Map/frozen/null-proto/numeric
keys) that byte-matches node.

A/B against the parent commit confirmed the two remaining `in` divergences
are pre-existing gaps, not introduced here: `"#x" in {"#x": 1}` (a literal
whose key starts with `#`) and inherited `Function.prototype` members
(`"call" in f`).

* perf(object): single-pass descriptor decode + receiver fast-dispatch for defineProperty

Object.defineProperty's remaining per-call constant had two layers:

1. ToPropertyDescriptor field probes: desc_has_field/desc_read_field ran a
   full spec HasProperty/[[Get]] — each a key-string alloc plus the whole
   has/get gauntlet, with ABSENT fields walking the prototype chain — and
   one define issues ~10 of them (validation, invariants, decode). The
   inversion was measurable: a 1-field descriptor cost MORE than a 4-field
   one (5 absent-field walks vs 1).

   New try_decode_descriptor reads all 6 fields in ONE walk of the
   descriptor's own keys (raw dense slots + field-index reads). It only
   fires when nothing spec-visible can differ: plain GC_TYPE_OBJECT, not
   exotic-registered, no accessors/attrs installed on it, default
   prototype, no prototype surface behind its shape id (a literal's
   nonzero class_id admits via three registry misses: no parent, no
   vtable, no C.prototype.x side table), and Object.prototype carrying
   none of the 6 field names as own keys (live pollution falls back).
   Everything else returns None and keeps the per-field spec path. The
   view threads through validation, invariant enforcement, and
   non-configurable redefine checks.

2. Receiver classification: the define entry ran its own probe gauntlet
   (proxy, typed-array define, exotic cells, closures, typed-array-by-
   addr, array [[DefineOwnProperty]]) — each a TLS + registry lookup —
   before reaching the plain-object path. One try_read_gc_header now
   classifies the receiver up front (mirroring the `in` fast path) and

perf(codegen): masked-window read hoist for loop-invariant untyped array params

Follow-up to #6750: the dense masked-index range-loop versioning only fired
for bindings whose STATIC type proved a number array, so an array arriving as
an untyped (any) function parameter — the bcryptjs Blowfish S-box shape —
kept paying one guard call per access (~40x slower than Node on
S[i & 1023] loops).

Two changes:

1. Matcher: read-only DENSE accesses also admit bindings with no usable
   static type (any/unknown/untracked). Safe because the entry guards
   re-validate the actual runtime value; a wrong hint costs one failed
   guard -> slow loop. Untyped plain-Array params now version through the
   existing dense_i32/dense plain-array tiers unchanged.

2. New typed-array tiers ahead of the plain tiers, emitted only when at
   least one accessed binding is untyped and every access carries a static
   window: one O(1) probe per array
   (js_typed_feedback_masked_window_ta_kind: registry lookup + window/length
   compare, detached views rejected via length 0) classifies the receiver as
   Int32Array / Uint32Array / Float64Array; all arrays agreeing on a kind
   branches into a fast copy whose loads go through the preheader-hoisted
   element-0 data pointer (js_typed_array_masked_window_data_ptr) with the
   width-correct inline load: i32 loads stay native i32 in bit-mixing chains
   (values_i32), u32 materializes unsigned (uitofp, never i32-classified),
   f64 loads directly. The hoisted pointer is stable because the fast copy
   is call-free (no allocation -> no GC) and view backings are
   thread-lifetime allocations.

perf(codegen): masked-window region versioning for straight-line unrolled bodies

bcryptjs ships _encipher fully UNROLLED (~130 consecutive masked S/P reads,
no loop), so the range-loop tiers never fire there. Add a straight-line
region versioner reusing the same probe/guard/fact machinery: a maximal run
of scalar LocalSet/Update/pure statements containing >=8 static-window reads
on eligible (number-array or untyped) bindings gets one probe per array at
region entry and three copies: ta_i32 (Int32Array probe, hoisted data ptr,
load i32), plain_f64 (dense window guard, raw-f64 loads), slow (untouched).
Bindings reassigned inside the region are dropped from the eligible set.
The plain dense-i32 tier is deliberately not emitted for regions: its
per-entry window scan is O(window), which a hot small function would pay on
every call.

perf(codegen): fact-aware dispatch + region type refinement for untyped masked reads

Three layers that make the region fast copies actually fast for bcryptjs's
_encipher (untyped locals l/r/n from lr[off] made everything dynamic):

1. Fact-aware IndexGet dispatch: the unknown-receiver routes (the #5525
   guarded inline-TA path and the js_dyn_index_get fallback) now consult
   masked-window facts first, so fact-covered reads are bare inline loads
   even with an erased static type. is_numeric_expr and
   expr_is_known_non_pointer_shadow_value gained the same fact arm, so
   fact-covered reads count as numeric/non-pointer operands and binary ops
   on them skip the js_dynamic_* dispatch tower.

2. Region-local flow type refinement: inside a region fast copy, a local
   written a provably-numeric value (fact-covered read, or any
   ToNumber/ToInt32-producing operator - only '+' needs both sides proven)
   is refined to Type::Number from that statement on, restoring the
   original types before the slow copy. Refined locals' shadow-slot updates
   are suppressed after a one-time clear (numbers need no GC root); an
   un-refinement re-binds the slot from the current value.

3. Region-local privatization: stably-refined locals move into a fresh
   never-escaping entry alloca for the fast copy (original slots escaped
   via js_shadow_slot_bind, blocking LLVM promotion), copied back at region
   end. Gated on try_depth == 0 - without an enclosing try, a mid-region
   throw unwinds the whole frame so the stale original slot is unobservable.

series; Node 71ms). Remaining gap is ToInt32 towers vs native i32 chains

  keys-keyed shapes instead rebuild once per pointer change (fork +

  in js_array_push_f64_grow).

  at a 4-entry LRU that thrashed past 4 wide shapes; now unbounded.

record is consulted regardless of which side built it — a strict superset
of today's acceleration. Trust model unchanged: accelerator, never
authoritative; every hit re-validates stored key bytes, so recycled
addresses and in-place compaction stay harmless. The per-object GC sweep

fix(gc): born-old arrays lose old→young remembered-set edges (JSON.parse data corruption) (#6831)

* fix(gc): born-old arrays filled via note_array_slot_layout_only lost old→young remembered-set edges

`note_array_slot_layout_only` skipped the write barrier on the assumption
that "fresh/suppressed caller sites" never need one. That is false for a
BORN-OLD array (>16KB payload, e.g. a >2048-element JSON.parse result):
the array lives in the old arena from birth, so storing a young child
creates an old→young edge that later minors need in the remembered set —
GC suppression only protects DURING the caller's fill, not after it
returns. JSON.parse's array_push_parse_fast fills arrays through this
helper, so every parse producing a big array of objects left its children
unremembered; minors then swept them while live (old parents are
black-leaves), and the array later read freed/reused memory — observed as
`TypeError: value is not a function` when the clobbered slot was called.

Measured on the claude-code bundle: the old-young-edge verifier reported
155 missing edges (default GC) / 445 (with PERRY_GC_GENERAL_EVAC), every
one `parent=array(old_arena) → child=object(young)`; with this fix both
configs run clean (0 missing).

Fix: after the layout note, emit `runtime_write_barrier_slot` when the
array is old-gen. The check hits the page-generation cache (same array →
same cached range), so nursery-array fills pay ~one cached compare.

Also adds a verifier diagnostic that pinpointed this: with
PERRY_GC_VERIFY_EVACUATION set, the barrier records every old page ever
dirtied (process lifetime), and the verifier's missing-edge panic now
prints `slot_page_ever_dirty` — distinguishing "recorded then lost by a
clear/restore gap" from "the store never hit any barrier" (this bug was
the latter, 3/3 runs). Zero cost when the env is unset.

Repro (before this fix): compile the claude-code bundle, run with
PERRY_GC_VERIFY_EVACUATION=1 — panics ~9s into startup with the missing
edges above.

only region fast copies are affected and non-region code is byte-for-byte
unchanged.

* perf(codegen): lower Math.imul and typed-array-param reads to native ops

Two integer-math JS primitives were compiled as runtime calls and cascaded a
whole hot integer loop into slow f64 ToInt32 towers.

- Math.imul(a,b) -> native `mul i32` when both operands are provable i32 (exact:
  the low 32 bits of the product are identical for signed/unsigned operands).
  Non-finite / fractional / >2^32 operands keep the js_math_imul helper so JS
  ToUint32/ToInt32 semantics are preserved. Because `Math.imul` is defined as
  ToInt32(ToUint32*ToUint32 mod 2^32), an integer-literal operand is exact under
  low-32 truncation even above i32::MAX, so the imul operand check now accepts
  32-bit-representable literals -- fixing the accumulator case
  `a = Math.imul(a, 0x9e3779b1)` (golden-ratio constant 2654435761 > i32::MAX).
  This relaxation is confined to Math.imul operands: a plain `x * BIGLIT | 0`
  evaluates its product in f64 (precision loss above 2^53), so it must stay
  ToInt32(f64_product), never an exact `mul i32`.

  a function parameter, in an i32/ToInt32 context) -> checked inline native
  load: a runtime guard (pointer + inline-storage PERRY_TA_VIEW_GUARD +
  kind-cache) and a header-length bounds check gate a bare width-correct load;
  an in-kind out-of-bounds read yields 0 (== ToInt32(undefined)); every rejected
  shape (view/detached/resizable backing, wrong runtime kind) defers to the new
  js_typed_array_read_int32 fallback. Extends the #6750 typed-array-local bare
  load to parameters, whose length/storage are unknown at compile time.

perf(codegen): inline small hot (in-loop) functions via inlinehint (#6855)

* perf(codegen): inline small hot (in-loop) functions via inlinehint

After native Math.imul + typed-array-param reads (#6850), the only residual
gap of a tight integer-math kernel vs V8 is function-call overhead: V8 inlines
a small hot function into its loop; Perry left it out-of-line. A NaN-boxed
bit-mixer (`mix`, ~10 statements) costs ~800 in LLVM's inline model once GC
shadow-frame calls + typed-array reads + double<->i32 marshaling are counted —
well above the base -O3 threshold — so -O3 kept it as a call.

Bias, don't force. Perry keeps `alwaysinline` only for the genuinely tiny
(<= 8 statements). This adds a distinct `inlinehint` path for functions that
are:
  - small (9..=SIZE_CAP statements, default cap 20),
  - called from inside a loop (a whole-module HIR pre-pass collects callee ids
    with an in-loop call site — approximates "hot" for an AOT compiler), AND
  - called from few total sites (default <= 4).

The linker raises `-inlinehint-threshold` (default 850) so the hinted kernels
actually inline; this lifts LLVM's ceiling ONLY for functions Perry stamped
`inlinehint` — every other function keeps the base -O3 threshold, so cold code
is untouched.

Anti-bloat is the whole point, and it rests on two backstops:
  1. The loop gate: a function only ever called from cold/straight-line code is
     never hinted, so cold utility functions can't bloat the binary.
  2. The call-site cap: `-inlinehint-threshold` raises the ceiling at EVERY
     call site of a hinted callee (LLVM can't tell hot from cold per-site
     through a function attribute), so a hot kernel also called from many cold
     sites would be duplicated at all of them. Capping total call sites bounds
     the duplication.

Measured binary-size delta (flag OFF vs ON), byte-precise __text section:
  - real programs (5 test-files): 0 hints, 0.000% delta;
  - broadly-called helper (300 fns x 40 cold sites): excluded by cap, 0%;
  - large programs (>6MB IR compile at -Os): flag inert, 0%;
  - realistic hot-kernel density: +0.34% (25 kernels), +0.79% (50), +1.57%
    (100); an all-kernels synthetic (250) reaches +3.86% — bounded by the cap
    (without it the same program's optimized IR grew 5.7x).

`mix` 40M-call microbench (min-of-many, contended box load ~27): OFF 1024ms ->
ON 904ms. Structural proof (load-independent): the caller loop no longer emits
a `bl` to `mix` (0 vs 2 BR26 relocations), and `mix` carries `inlinehint`.

Gated behind PERRY_INLINE_HOT_SMALL (default on); PERRY_INLINE_HOT_SMALL_CAP /
_THRESHOLD / _MAX_SITES tune the window, hint threshold, and call-site cap. All
four are folded into the object cache key. Existing `noinline` cases
(try/setjmp/volatile) are respected via to_ir's has_try-first attribute
precedence. Adds test_gap_inline_hot_small.ts (byte-identical to Node ON/OFF
and under PERRY_GC_FORCE_EVACUATE=1).

spreads and let generic dispatch handle it — that path already routes
to the variadic runtime helper and produces correct results today
(verified: an `any`-typed receiver splices spreads correctly on main).

fast path cannot express.

- New flow set collectors::not_bigint_locals (greatest fixpoint): an Any-typed
  local is non-BigInt when every assignment to it is a non-BigInt expression.
  Wired onto FnCtx as RepresentationFacts::not_bigint_locals.

and bigint^bigint still computes a BigInt (both operands must pass the gate).

throwing the spec TypeError (mixed bigint/number), and `(bigintLocal++) * 2`

   to hold an i32 keeps the numeric fast path. An Any local not proven integer
   (could be BigInt) is excluded — so a bigint-local Update operand no longer
   takes the all-numeric operand path (which toint32's the BigInt to 0).

2. is_provably_not_bigint gained an explicit Expr::Update { id, .. } arm before
   the is_numeric_expr shortcut, mirroring LocalGet(id) (not_bigint_locals /
   integer_locals / unsigned_i32_locals). With (1) making l_prim false for a
   bigint Update, the bitwise lowering now reaches this gate, which returns

fix(hir): materialize the implicit undefined for init-less let/const (#6871) (#6877)

A `let x;` declared inside a loop body kept the previous iteration's
value instead of being reset to undefined, whenever the assignment
happened inside a NESTED loop:

    for (let i = 0; i < src.length; i++) {
      let f: string[] | undefined;
      for (const n of src[i]) { if (!f) f = []; f.push(n); }
      // node:  a, undefined, b
      // perry: a, a,         ab
    }

Executing a lexical declaration initializes the binding to undefined
(ECMA-262 CreateMutableBinding + InitializeBinding), and re-executing it
creates a FRESH binding — so each iteration must start from undefined.
HIR faithfully emitted `Stmt::Let { init: None }`, but codegen allocates
the slot once in the entry block and emits no store for a None init, so
the stale value survived the back-edge. Assignment directly in the loop
body was already correct, which is what kept this hidden.

Fixing it in codegen is not possible without new information: `Stmt::Let`
carries no var/let distinction and `ctx.var_hoisted_ids` never reaches
perry-codegen. Lowering is where `is_var_decl` is known, so materialize
the initializer there instead.

`var` is deliberately excluded — it is function-scoped and hoisted, so
re-executing `var x;` keeps the prior value, and the test locks that in.

Found compiling the Milo compiler (32k lines of TS) with Perry. Its
parser collects declaration attributes with exactly this shape:

    let attrs: Attribute[] | undefined;
    while (this.at(TokenKind.At)) { if (!attrs) attrs = []; ... }

so a struct's `@derive(...)` leaked onto every following declaration and
the compiled compiler rejected valid programs with spurious errors
("'@derive' is not supported on functions"). Changing that one
declaration to `= undefined` fixed it, confirming the cause.

fix(compile): keep an optional try-wrapped require as a runtime require (#6873) (#6878)

* fix(compile): keep an optional try-wrapped require as a runtime require (#6873)

`try { x = require("./generated") } catch {}` aborted the build with
"Could not resolve namespace import" whenever the module was not on
disk — the shape every "optional generated/embedded asset" idiom uses.

transform_static_literal_requires hoists literal requires to a
top-level `import * as <tmp>`, which discards both the runtime guard
and the catch, and #629 makes an unresolvable namespace import a hard
error. The #629 rationale (an empty namespace silently no-ops and the
user never learns why) does not apply here: the author explicitly said
this may not exist, and Node/Bun either skip the call or swallow the
throw.

A specifier is OPTIONAL when every one of its call sites is inside a
`try`. An optional specifier that does not resolve on disk is no longer
hoisted — the call stays a runtime `require`, which is exactly what
bare package specifiers already do and reproduces Node's behavior
(throws, caught, binding keeps its prior value; verified byte-identical
against `node --experimental-strip-types`).

Deliberately narrow:
  - optional AND resolvable still hoists, so a module that IS present
    is compiled in and loads (Perry's CJS-interop extension; plain
    node-ESM cannot require at all),
  - one unguarded call site makes the specifier load-bearing again,
  - `try` is matched as a keyword, so `retry {` does not qualify.

Detection runs over the comment/string-masked source, so a miss either
way is safe: a false negative keeps today's hoisting, a false positive
only downgrades an unresolvable module to a runtime require.

fix(hir): descend through every expr variant when fixing imported enums (#6879) (#6881)

A member of an imported enum read as `undefined` in several expression
positions:

    import { TokenKind } from "./tokens";
    String(TokenKind.Ident)      // undefined  (bun: "IDENT")
    `${TokenKind.Ident}`         // undefined
    [TokenKind.Ident][0]         // undefined
    ({ a: TokenKind.Ident }).a   // undefined
    const k = TokenKind.Ident    // "IDENT"  — worked
    ident(TokenKind.Ident)       // "IDENT"  — worked
    "" + TokenKind.Ident         // "IDENT"  — worked

The identical enum declared in the SAME module was correct in all seven
positions, so the trigger was the import.

In an importing module `TokenKind.Ident` lowers to a PropertyGet on an
ExternFuncRef, which the `fix_imported_enums` post-pass rewrites into the
member's constant. That pass carried its own hand-rolled expression
walker ending in `_ => {}`, so any variant it did not list stopped the
walk dead. The unlisted variant was `StringCoerce` — which wraps
`String(x)` and every template-literal interpolation, and being an OUTER
wrapper also hid the array/object cases nested beneath it. That single
gap explains the whole split above.

Rather than adding `StringCoerce` (~200 Expr variants, same trap next
time), delegate descent to `crate::walker::walk_expr_children_mut`. That
match is exhaustive with no catch-all, so the compiler rejects a new
Expr variant that is not classified — its module docs describe exactly
this bug class and note the consumers that had not yet been migrated.
This was one of them. Closure bodies are Vec<Stmt> and the shared walker
deliberately skips them, so those are descended here.

Two adjacent gaps fixed while here:
  - the statement walker's own `_ => {}` was silently skipping
    `do { … } while (…)` and labeled statements; the match is now
    exhaustive,
  - class field initializers and computed keys were never visited, so
    `class P { kind = TokenKind.Ident }` had the same defect.

Found compiling the Milo compiler (32k lines of TS) with Perry. Its
lexer and parser are built on `import { TokenKind } from "./tokens"`, so
`this.expect(TokenKind.Ident)` compared against undefined and every
parse failed:

    error: expected 'undefined', got 'IDENT' ('strContains')

With this fix pristine, unpatched Milo compiles and runs Milo programs.

Tested via unit tests on the pass rather than a test-file: Node's
strip-only mode rejects TS enums outright, so `run_parity_tests.sh`

perf(codegen): inline checked-f64 typed-array-param reads in numeric context (#6883)

* perf(codegen): inline checked-f64 typed-array-param reads in numeric context

A typed-array element read through a parameter (`function f(S: Int32Array)`)
that feeds arithmetic rather than `| 0` — the bcryptjs `_encipher` S-box shape
`n = S[l >>> 24]; n += S[...]` — previously compiled to a per-read
`call js_typed_array_get(ptr, idx)`. The i32 fast path only fires in a ToInt32
(`| 0`) context, so these numeric-context reads stayed on the runtime call.

Lower them to an inline checked f64 load instead: the same guard as the checked
i32 read (pointer + inline-storage PERRY_TA_VIEW_GUARD==0 + kind-cache), a header
bounds check, a bare per-kind load widened to f64 (sitofp/uitofp/fpext/direct),
and — bit-exact with js_typed_array_get — the TAG_UNDEFINED double on OOB /
negative. Guard misses defer to a new memory-safe cold helper
js_typed_array_read_f64 (validates the pointer is a registered typed array
before any header deref, mirroring js_typed_array_read_int32). Gated on a proven
non-negative integer index (a fractional `S[3.9]` must read undefined, not
element 3). Covers every numeric kind incl. Uint32 (unsigned widening) and the
float kinds. Env flag PERRY_TA_PARAM_F64_READ (default on), keyed into the
object cache.

Measured on the real _encipher shape (2.1M calls, quiet M1, min-of-9,
byte-exact): 1787ms -> 1351ms, ~1.32x; the per-read guard costs only ~3% over a
bare load, so no guard hoisting is needed. Stacks with #6860 (inline non-BigInt
bitwise): the dynamic-bitwise baseline was ~3541ms.

fix(string): stop mask-casting SSO values to StringHeader* (#6887) (#6888)

Indexing or iterating a SHORT string produced by concatenation
segfaulted:

    const s = "ab" + "c";
    s.length          // 3        fine
    s[0]              // SIGSEGV
    for (const ch of s) {}        // SIGSEGV
    Array.from(s)                 // SIGSEGV

A short string is an inline SHORT_STRING_TAG (SSO) JSValue whose payload
IS the characters, not a heap address. Two places masked its low 48 bits
and dereferenced the result as a StringHeader*:

  - codegen's `s[i]` fast path (expr/index_get.rs) `unbox_to_i64`'d the
    receiver before calling js_string_index_get, and
  - js_array_from_value did the same mask itself, behind a
    `(bits >> 48) >= 0x7FF8` test that an SSO value passes.

String literals, join() results, and long concatenations were all fine —
literals are heap-allocated at init and a long concat exceeds the SSO
threshold. That is the clean discriminator: a 3-char concat crashes, a
64-char concat does not. `typeof`, `.length` and printing the value work
either way, so nothing looks wrong until something indexes it.

Codegen now passes the receiver STILL BOXED to a new
js_string_index_get_boxed, which decides by tag; an SSO receiver is
materialized to a heap StringHeader and delegated, so the
CanonicalNumericIndexString key semantics stay in exactly one place.
js_array_from_value normalizes an SSO receiver up front. The
materialization costs a small arena allocation per index on an SSO
receiver — worth revisiting if it shows up hot, but the alternative was
a crash.

Test: test_gap_sso_concat_string_index.ts covers indexed reads (in
range, out of range, negative), charAt/charCodeAt/codePointAt/at, an
index-accumulation loop, for-of, spread, Array.from, split, the
`join("") + "\n"` shape this was found on, empty and single-char
concatenations, non-ASCII where UTF-16 indexing differs from bytes, and
a long heap-backed concatenation so the fix cannot regress that path.
Byte-identical to node.

perf(codegen/runtime): #6812 — 3-way dynamic-key write IC (inline hit path, self-healing caches) (#6895)

* perf(codegen/runtime): #6812 w12 — 3-way dynamic-key write IC

Same-receiver dynamic-key stores route through an outlined per-site IC
(same perry_ic_N [8 x i64] global family as the static write PIC):
[shape_token, (key_bits, slot) x 3]. A way's key is the NaN-boxed key
VALUE — SSO keys (<= 5 bytes) compare by CONTENT (move-immune, hits across
distinct string instances), heap keys by identity (a moved or re-built key
misses; identity can never false-hit). The hit path validates everything
against the receiver's LIVE state (ordinary/unblocked/class-tagged object,
current shape token equality, slot within the inline region) — cached
token/slot are compared, never dereferenced, so stale entries self-heal by
missing. No rooting or safepoint bookkeeping on the hot path: that is the
structural difference from the discarded safepointing-RHS approach, whose
per-write rooting measured 2x slower. Miss = full [[Set]] + MRU re-prime
(shape change resets the way set); every call is at worst the generic
path. Distinct-receiver stores keep the receiver-aware generic helper.

* perf(codegen): #6812 w12 v2 — inline hit path for the dynamic-key write IC

When the receiver is a plain local (≡ target) and the value is
compile-proven numeric, the 3-way IC hit is emitted inline: the static
write PIC's exact guard sequence (heap-candidate branch, GcHeader
-8/-7/-6 checks with BLOCKING 0x1907, ObjectHeader regular/class/token
checks with the #6804 discriminated shape-token select), then a 3-way
key-bits compare chain, a floor-4 bounds check on the phi'd slot, and a
raw double store — no barrier and no layout note, sound because numeric
bits never create references and hardware NaNs sit below the 0x7FFA tag
space. Header offset is target-layout derived (ILP32-safe). All misses
and every site failing the inline gate take the outlined helper, which
bottoms out at the generic path.

* perf(codegen): native-i32 residency for int-typed-array-seeded locals

Infer native-i32 residency for integer-valued locals whose init/writes
include a possibly-out-of-bounds INT typed-array element read — the
bcryptjs `_encipher` Feistel accumulators `l`/`r` (`let l = lr[off]`, then

paying an fptosi/sitofp round-trip on every bitwise access.

local ONLY when BOTH hold (soundness-critical — an Int32Array OOB read is
`undefined`, not `0`):

  1. every write is i32-producing — an int-kind typed-array read
     (Int8/Uint8/Uint8Clamped/Int16/Uint16/Int32), a bitwise op, `~`,
     `Math.imul`, an i32 literal, or a Uint8Array/Buffer byte read. NOT
     additive `+`/`-`/`*` (i32 overflow — this is why `n` stays f64), NOT a
     copy/call/anything else; and
  2. every observation is ToInt32-coercing — a bitwise operand or the value
     stored into an int-kind typed-array element. NEVER where undefined is
     distinguishable (array index, additive operand, comparison, call arg,
     return, console.log, String(), typeof, plain-array/field store, …).

Under (2) the value is always ToInt32'd (ToInt32(undefined)==0), and the
i32 slot is seeded with the same 0 for an OOB read, so the i32 and f64
representations are byte-for-byte indistinguishable. Conservative /
under-approximating: params, `++`/`--` targets, closure-referenced locals,
and copy chains are excluded. No fixpoint needed.

The admitted set is merged into `integer_locals` (so the existing i32
shadow-slot + i32-chain machinery fires), gated by `PERRY_INT_VALUED_LOCALS`
(default on; keyed into the object cache). Two supporting codegen fixes:

  - stmt/let_stmt.rs: seed the i32 slot from a possibly-non-finite init with
    the NaN-safe `toint32_wrap` (ToInt32(undefined)==0) instead of a raw
    `fptosi` (LLVM poison — 0 on aarch64 but a garbage sentinel on x86-64).
    Known-finite inits keep the cheaper fptosi path (bit-identical).
  - stmt/let_stmt.rs: refine an `Any`-typed proven-integer local's type to
    `Number` when the structural refiner can't, so the numeric Let/LocalSet
    lowering fires (no conservative Any boxing, no GC shadow-slot pointer
    tracking) and -O3 can collapse the residual round-trips — matching a
    source `| 0`.

enc.ts (2.1M `_encipher` calls, quiet M1, min-of-9): 1347ms -> 1010ms
(1.33x), byte-exact (`lr0=2135713266 lr1=-1949122846`); optimized
`_encipher` fptosi 8 -> 0. Adds gap test test_gap_int_valued_ta_locals.ts
pinning the OOB-observability boundary (eligible accumulator byte-exact even
on an OOB init; ineligible sibling still observes `undefined`).

docs: RFC — type-driven representation selection (unbox-by-default for typed values) (#6901)

* docs: RFC — type-driven representation selection (unbox-by-default for typed values)

Structural proposal to make the native (unboxed) representation canonical for
statically-typed values, confining NaN-boxing to proven-polymorphic values.
Motivated by the bcryptjs _encipher investigation: AOT Perry loses to V8 on
integer-heavy code because typed values round-trip through the NaN-box on every
op and every call (the region-local native-rep overlays materialize back to a
boxed double at every boundary — ABI, heap, loop phi). Phased design (IR
representation property -> unboxed locals -> specialized ABI/monomorphization ->
typed heap) with real unrolled _encipher beating V8 as the acceptance test.

* docs(rfc): v2 — all-type-class coverage + address review findings

Expands the RFC from the numeric case to the full type universe (scalars,
strings, shape-proven objects, typed arrays, closures, small bigints) with a
per-class win/constraint table — pointer reps stay precise rewritable roots
under the moving GC; F64 is bit-identical (win = tag-check elision).

Addresses review: dynamic-JS soundness barriers (proxies/accessors/eval/with/
reflection/delete/proto-mutation/exceptional flow force Boxed); representation-
preserving operation semantics (IEEE-754 double arithmetic untouched, I32 only
in spec-integral contexts or under range proof, F32 storage-only); per-rep
boxed->native acceptance contracts (NaN/Inf/-0/fractional/out-of-range rejected
to checked paths, never silent coercion); bounded monomorphization (rep-tuple
keys, cached entries, size budgets, boxed-entry fallback); specialized-ABI
pointer-param safety across safepoints (spill-to-registered-slot + rebase-
after-safepoint for derived pointers); typed-heap eligibility (escape/alias
analysis, shape transitions, observation equivalence, barriers); reproducible
acceptance protocol (machine/oracle/min-of-9/cache discipline + structural IR
proof + golden vectors).

The deferred layer of #6915: collectors/ptr_numarray.rs proves function-
local number[] bindings for FULLY guard-free element access (RFC §4
Array<number> row / §5.7):

- Provenance: single Let, init new Array(<static n>) (runtime hole-fills,
  sets GC_ARRAY_RAW_F64_HOLES, stamps pointer-free layout) or the empty
  literal []. Density lattice: [] -> Dense, new Array(n) -> HolesOK.
- Containment: every use is a numeric-key element read, an element write
  whose value is numeric-by-construction (one possibly-non-number store
  disqualifies the local outright), .length, a numeric push, or a bare
  end-of-function return. Anything else — bare references (call args,
  JSON/keys/in), aliases, captures, length writes, pop/shift/splice/
  unshift/copyWithin, sort/reverse (method calls), freeze/seal —
  disqualifies. Non-numeric keys could name 'length'/'__proto__', so
  keyed accesses require a provably-numeric key.
- Stale-binding exemption (the #6915 self-heal finding, structural this
  time): containment means no callee can ever grow the array (the
  specialized-ABI caller-allocated pattern cannot occur), every
  in-function growth site writes the live head back to the slot, and
  consumers re-derive the base from the shadow-bound slot per access —
  so a guard-free consumer can never see a forwarded stub.
- Module-wide barrier kill: Phase 3b's §5.2 scan PLUS a new
  ModuleDispatchFacts leg — any indexed write through a .prototype
  object (a polluted prototype changes what a HOLE read observes, and
  the guard-free read cannot consult the runtime pollution byte).
- Consumers (expr/ptr_numarray_access.rs): per-site in-bounds proof
  (int_range max < allocation length — permanent because length can only
  grow — or a bounded-loop-pair fact) gates the bare form: slot reload →
  mask → gep+8 → gep idx<<3 → load/store double. No guard tier, no
  bounds arms, no barrier, no note, no length bump. Guard-free READS are
  number-context only (HolesOK canonicalizes TAG_HOLE/NaN payloads to
  the quiet NaN — bit-exact with ToNumber(undefined); Dense skips even

perf(codegen,runtime): repsel Phase 4b (narrow) — class-field store note/addref elision + INT32 layout-poison fix (#6919)

* perf(codegen,runtime): repsel Phase 4b (narrow) — class-field store note/addref elision + INT32 layout-poison fix

Phase 4b of docs/representation-selection-rfc.md §5.7, scoped down after
recon: full field-unboxing was assessed and REJECTED. `number` fields are
already bit-unboxed (NaN-boxing reserves only 0x7FF9..=0x7FFF, so a number
slot already holds raw IEEE bits; raw_f64_mask is a proof bit, not a storage
change, and Phase 3b already removed the read-side guard). Raw string handles
at rest would break SSO for nothing, and raw i1/i32 slots would need a third
GC mask plus a layout probe at ~25 direct slot-read sites — JSON.stringify,
util.inspect, v8 IPC serde, descriptor reads — which are hot, not the "rare,
already-slow" surfaces the RFC's observation-equivalence bullet assumes. §5.7
records that decision.

4b.1 — every non-raw-f64 class-field store emitted js_string_addref_if_heap_string
and js_gc_note_slot_layout unconditionally. On a Ptr<Shape>-proven receiver both
are provably dead, decided by the object twin of array_store_needs_layout_note:
the note goes when the slot is pointer-masked or the value is a non-pointer by
construction; the addref goes only when the value provably cannot be a heap
string. The generational write barrier is untouched.

Soundness rests on the Ptr<Shape> containment proof. Reaching this arm already
required a class_keys_globals entry, and emit_typed_shape_layout_init keys its
early-out on that same map, so the `new <class>()` that provenance demands
necessarily emitted the descriptor init. Containment then forbids aliasing,
escape to a callee, dynamic keyed writes, delete, freeze/seal and
defineProperty, so the object's layout state is only ever {intact descriptor}
or {UNKNOWN} — and layout_note_slot is a no-op in both. It can never be the
POINTER_FREE/SIDE_MASK-without-descriptor state in which the note is the only
thing that sets the pointer-mask bit the GC scan reads. The mask class itself
is read via class_typed_layout_from_chain over class_init_chains, the same call
over the same chain that compile_module uses to emit the class's mask globals.

The addref elision is keyed on the value expression, NEVER the declared field
type: Perry does not validate declared types at runtime, so a boolean-declared
field legitimately receives a string through an `any`, and a wrong elision there
silently corrupts an aliased string on the next in-place append.

The guarded (non-Ptr<Shape>) class-field store deliberately keeps both calls:
its receiver can be a runtime-constructed object that never had a descriptor
installed, where the note is the only thing that marks the slot as pointer-
bearing for the collector.

4b.2 — layout_note_slot treats any non-raw-f64 bit pattern landing in a raw-f64
slot as a representation change and calls layout_set_typed_unknown, evicting the
object's TypedLayoutDescriptor permanently and one-way. INT32 boxes genuinely
reach object fields from FFI/native modules (sqlite rows, v8 deserialization),
and runtime_store_jsvalue_slot wrote the bits verbatim — one FFI integer cost
that object its fast path forever. It now applies the array precedent
canonicalize_array_numeric_store_bits (INT32 -> raw f64) for raw-f64-masked
slots under an intact descriptor. No observable change: an INT32 box and its
f64 are ===. The gate is tag-first so the hot non-INT32 store never pays the
thread-local probe, and value_bits_to_number supplies the ClassRef exclusion.

Structural proof (--trace llvm, A/B with the predicates forced back to true),
per changed function in the new gap file: layout notes 4/6/2 -> 0/0/0, string
addrefs 4/6/2 -> 3/4/2, write barriers 3/4/2 unchanged. The addrefs that
survive are exactly the string-valued stores. Post-opt -O3, whole module:
notes 41 -> 26, addrefs 56 -> 52.

Tests: test_gap_repsel_p4b_field_store_elision.ts (13 sections) covers each
elision and non-elision case — string-typed field still addrefs under
snapshot-then-grow, union-with-string keeps the demote, declared types are not
enforced, INT32-into-typed-field reads back byte-exact — byte-exact vs the
pinned Node 26.5.0 oracle under default, PERRY_GC_FORCE_EVACUATE=1,
PERRY_GC_VERIFY_EVACUATION=1, both, PERRY_GEN_GC=0, PERRY_WRITE_BARRIERS=0 and
PERRY_PTR_SHAPE_LOCALS=0. Four runtime regression tests in gc/tests/layout_trace.rs
for 4b.2, including the negative controls (a string into a raw-f64 slot must
still evict; no descriptor means bits stay verbatim).

* docs(changelog): add changeset fragment for #6919

* fix(codegen): narrow the 4b.1 layout-note elision to descriptor-independent cases

The pointer-masked arm of class_field_store_needs_layout_note rested on "a
Ptr<Shape>-proven receiver always has a typed-shape descriptor installed at
construction". That premise does not hold: lower_new_impl has an exit — the
force_ctor_call branch where call_local_constructor_symbol yields None
(lower_call/new.rs) — that returns a freshly allocated instance WITHOUT
emitting js_gc_init_typed_shape_layout. Such an object sits at
GC_LAYOUT_POINTER_FREE, where layout_note_slot is the only thing that ever
sets the pointer-mask bit the collector reads, so eliding a pointer store's
note there would strand a live child. Closing that exit is the prerequisite
for the stronger elision; it is not bundled here.

The note elision now rests only on the value being a non-pointer by
construction, which is sound in every layout state the receiver can be in —
UNKNOWN and POINTER_FREE short-circuit inside the note, an intact descriptor
falls through the pointer_mask arm untouched, and under SIDE_MASK the note
would only ever CLEAR the slot's bit, so skipping it leaves a stale set bit
over a non-pointer. That costs one extra visit and nothing else:
mark_field_into_worklist re-validates every slot word (f64 bit patterns fall
outside the 48-bit user-address range and are rejected) and the evacuation
rewrite path routes through the same function.

The addref gate is widened instead, in the direction that needs no descriptor
reasoning at all: js_string_addref_if_heap_string is dead whenever the value
cannot carry STRING_TAG, which is strictly weaker than "cannot be a pointer".
Object literals, array literals and closures qualify — each evaluates to a
freshly allocated POINTER_TAG value with no path to a primitive result.
Expr::New is deliberately excluded: a constructor return override makes what
`new C()` evaluates to a runtime question, and the predicate must not depend
on the answer.

Re-measured structural counts, per changed function of the gap file
(--trace llvm, A/B with the predicates forced back to true):

  compoundStores      note 4 -> 3   addref 4 -> 2   barrier 3 -> 3
  compoundLoop        note 6 -> 4   addref 6 -> 2   barrier 4 -> 4
  compoundSnapshots   note 2 -> 2   addref 2 -> 2   barrier 2 -> 2

compoundSnapshots is the safety case and correctly elides nothing: both stores
are `tag ||= <unique heap string local>`. Post-opt -O3, whole module: notes
41 -> 37, addrefs 56 -> 48. Byte-exact vs the pinned Node 26.5.0 oracle under
the full GC matrix.

fix(gc): mark and rewrite paths must accept the same root-word forms (#6910) (#6929)

* fix(gc): mark and rewrite paths must accept the same root-word forms (#6910)

The mutable-root MARK path and the mutable-root REWRITE path disagreed
about bare (untagged) heap addresses:

  try_mark_value        (shadow-slot marking)   NaN-boxed tags only
  try_rewrite_value     (mutable-root rewrite)  NaN-boxed AND bare
  decode_bits           (copying minor)         NaN-boxed AND bare
  heap_word_candidate_addr (incr. mark barrier) NaN-boxed AND bare

So a bare address in a shadow-stack slot was a root to three of the four
surfaces and invisible to the fourth. If such a slot were the only
reference to an object, root marking skipped it and the sweep freed it —
a use-after-free, not merely a missed rewrite (an unmarked object is
never evacuated, so it never gets a forwarding address for the rewrite
pass to follow).

The failure would also not have been caught: the unit-test build defaults
to ConservativeStackScanMode::Full, whose native-stack scan accepts bare
addresses and would rescue the object, while production resolves
Auto -> SkipDisabled and has no such net. Green tests, prod-only UAF.

No shipped representation puts a bare address in a shadow slot today
(every phase deliberately chose tagged-at-rest), so this was latent. It
is fixed rather than documented because the representation-selection RFC
§5.6 unboxed pointer reps are designed to store exactly that form.

Fix: one decoder, gc/root_words.rs, behind all three non-conservative
surfaces. decode_root_word returns RootWord::{Nanboxed,Bare}; the mark
path (mark_mutable_root_bits), the rewrite path (try_rewrite_value) and
the incremental barrier (heap_word_candidate_addr) all route through it,
so adding a representation teaches them at once and none can drift.
RootWord::encode preserves the stored form across a rewrite (bare stays
bare, a NaN box keeps its tag). mark_global_root_bits folds into
mark_mutable_root_bits — both slot kinds now share one decoding, and
MutableRootSlotKind selects a telemetry bucket only.

try_rewrite_value additionally picks up the arm64_32 (ILP32) payload
guard that heap_word_candidate_addr already carried; on watchOS it was
truncating 48-bit payloads to 32-bit addresses.

Two surfaces deliberately stay outside the shared decoder, and both are
safe because they are supersets rather than subsets: try_mark_value_or_raw
(conservative native-stack scan, also resolves interior pointers) and
CopyingPointerSet::decode_bits (copying minor, additionally requires
8-byte alignment and a live classification, and whose mark and rewrite
are the same operation so it cannot disagree with itself).

Tests: gc::tests::root_words, all four pinned with the conservative scan
explicitly Disabled since the Full default masks the bug. Verified
failing on the pre-fix mark path and passing after:

  - bare_address_in_shadow_slot_survives_a_real_collection
        pre-fix: swept while live (dead churn objects prove the sweep ran)
  - mutable_root_mark_and_rewrite_accept_the_same_word_forms

fix(codegen): initialize typed-shape layout on the standalone-ctor exit (#6921) (#6930)

* fix(codegen): initialize typed-shape layout on the standalone-ctor exit (#6921)

`lower_new_impl` had one exit that returned a freshly allocated class
instance without emitting `js_gc_init_typed_shape_layout`. Every other
`new` exit emits it. An instance produced there is left at
`GC_LAYOUT_POINTER_FREE` with no `TypedLayoutDescriptor` — the one layout
state where the per-store `layout_note_slot` call is load-bearing for GC
correctness rather than a precision hint, because it is the only writer
of the pointer-mask bit the collector reads. That blocks the full
pointer-masked layout-note elision (the larger half of Phase 4b.1 in
#6919, which had to narrow to the value-only predicate because of it).

Emit the layout init on that exit too, so the invariant "a user-class
instance reaching a class-field store carries a typed descriptor, or is
explicitly GC_LAYOUT_UNKNOWN" is total.

REACHABILITY — I could not build a reproducer, and on investigation the
arm appears to be DEAD, which is a stronger claim than #6921 makes.
The issue correctly notes that `force_ctor_call` and `ctor_alias_collision`
both pre-check `local_constructor_symbol_exists` and so cannot reach it,
leaving the `ctx.class_stack` recursion guard as the only way in. But the
missing step is that `call_local_constructor_symbol` returns `None` only
when `ctx.methods` lacks `(class.name, "<Class>_constructor")`, and:

  - `lower_new_impl` resolves `class` exclusively from `ctx.classes`
    (new.rs:237 is the only binding, `ctx.classes.get(class_name)`);
  - `ctx.classes` IS the `class_table` (codegen/mod.rs passes `&class_table`
    to compile_function / compile_method);
  - `build_method_names` iterates `class_table.values()` and inserts
    `(c.name, "{c.name}_constructor")` UNCONDITIONALLY for every entry,
    local and imported alike (method_registry.rs:112-119).

So every class that can reach the branch has the key, and the `None` arm
cannot be taken. Empirically: an instrumented compiler that logs on
reaching the arm reported ZERO hits across all 430 `test-files/test_gap_*.ts`
(codegen-only, `--no-link --no-cache`) plus three hand-written
self-referential construction shapes (self-construction in a method, a
recursive own constructor, and a field initializer constructing its own
class) — all of which do enter the recursion-guarded branch, and all of
which take the `Some` arm that already emitted the init.

The emitter lands anyway: the invariant should hold by construction at
this exit rather than by an accident of the registry that a change to
`build_method_names`, or a new `ctx.classes` population path, could
silently revoke. Cost is zero — dead path today, and
`emit_typed_shape_layout_init` is itself a no-op for a class with no
`class_keys_globals` entry.

Because the arm is unreachable, NO behavioral test can fail before and
pass after; claiming otherwise would be dishonest. What is testable, and
what actually carries the risk, is the premise the fix rests on: the
instance reaching this exit has had NO constructor run, so the layout init
sees all-`undefined` fields. `gc::tests::layout_trace::
typed_shape_layout_init_on_unconstructed_instance_is_conservative` pins
all three properties of that:

  1. `js_object_alloc_class_inline_keys` really does leave the instance at
     GC_LAYOUT_POINTER_FREE with no descriptor (why the note is
     load-bearing there, i.e. why the gap mattered);
  2. a raw-f64 mask over `undefined` fields is REFUSED and the object is
     downgraded to GC_LAYOUT_UNKNOWN — the conservative state — never left
     POINTER_FREE and never given a mask that misdescribes it (why
     emitting the init here is SAFE);
  3. a pointer-only mask over `undefined` fields IS installed, and a
     subsequent raw pointer store into that slot is traced with no
     `layout_note_slot` call at all (why emitting it is USEFUL).

* test(gc): root the #6921 premise test's handles across GC points

CodeRabbit review on #6930. The test held `ptr_only` and `child` as raw
pointers across GC-capable calls — `js_string_from_bytes` allocates, and
evacuation moves arena objects, so the subsequent raw field write and the
`POINTER_TAG | ptr_only` mark could both have named from-space.

This is the same unrooted-handle-across-allocation bug class as #6655, in
a test whose whole job is to validate GC correctness. An unsound test is
worse than no test: it can pass for the wrong reason and mask exactly the
layout/tracing behavior it exists to pin.

Fixed properly rather than minimally:

- every instance is rooted in a `RuntimeHandleScope` the moment it is
  allocated, and re-read through the handle after any later allocation
  (`handle_user`), so no raw pointer crosses a GC point;
- `child_header` is derived from the refreshed child handle at the point
  of use instead of being captured before the trace;
- the hand-driven mark starts from `clear_marks()` so a collection during
  the allocations cannot leave the instance pre-marked and turn the
  `try_mark_value` setup assertion into a false negative.

The registration is the part that is easy to get wrong, so it is now
explicit and documented: `GcTestIsolationGuard` (via
`ScopedRootScannerRegistryGuard`) `mem::take`s the thread's
`MUTABLE_ROOT_SCANNERS`, and the runtime-handle scanner goes with it. A
`RuntimeHandleScope` opened inside that guard roots NOTHING until the
scanner is put back. `register_runtime_handle_root_scanner_for_tests`
moves from `tests/runtime_roots.rs` to `tests/support.rs` (21 call sites
there are unaffected — it is glob-imported) and carries a doc comment
spelling out the trap.

Crucially, the rooting is now LOAD-BEARING rather than decorative. The
test drives a real `collect_minor_trace(GcTriggerKind::Direct)` after the
child write, with `ConservativeScanDisabledGuard` pinning the native-stack
scan OFF — so the raw Rust locals are no longer a safety net and the
handle scope is the only thing keeping the objects alive. Verified: with
the `register_runtime_handle_root_scanner_for_tests()` line removed the
test FAILS (`test_layout_pointer_slot_count` → `None` — the instance and
its descriptor were reclaimed); with it, it passes. That collection also
buys a new assertion worth having: the typed descriptor must survive the
collection and any relocation, since the note-elision premise depends on
it staying intact, not merely on being installed once.

test(gc): handle hygiene in the #6910 root-word tests (#6932)

* test(gc): handle hygiene in the #6910 root-word tests

Follow-up to #6929, prompted by a CodeRabbit finding on the sibling PR
#6930: a GC test that holds raw pointers across GC-capable calls is the
#6655 bug class inside the very tests meant to validate GC correctness.
Audited all four tests landed in #6929; one had a genuine hazard and two
were sound-but-brittle.

1. `mutable_root_mark_and_rewrite_accept_the_same_word_forms` — REAL
   hazard. `mark_target` / `rewrite_target` are `arena_alloc_gc` objects
   held as raw `usize` across two further allocations (`rewrite_target`,
   then `moved` via `arena_alloc_gc_old`), with no trigger suppression.
   Evacuation moves arena objects, so either could have named from-space
   by the time the walks ran.

   Fixed with `GcTriggerThresholdTestGuard::suppress_automatic_triggers()`
   rather than a `RuntimeHandleScope`, and the comment says why: rooting
   alone would NOT have been sufficient here. This test hand-builds a
   `ValidPointerSet` snapshot and hand-sets a forwarding address, neither
   of which survives a real collection no matter how well the objects are
   rooted. The hazard is the collection itself, so the region is made
   collection-free.

   Also moved `build_valid_pointer_set()` after the last allocation so the
   snapshot describes the heap the walks actually run against. Behaviour is
   unchanged — `try_rewrite_raw_addr` returns `Some(moved)` whether or not
   `moved` is in the set (it stops at the first non-forwarded header either
   way) — but "snapshot the heap, then allocate into it" was misleading.

2/3. `bare_address_in_shadow_slot_survives_a_real_collection` and
   `bare_address_in_global_root_survives_a_real_collection` — sound today,
   brittle. `live` is `gc_malloc`-backed and the collector marks malloc
   objects in place (`copying.rs:466`, `CopyingPointerKind::Malloc =>
   Some(addr)`), never relocating them; triggers are already suppressed and
   the collection is driven explicitly. They passed for a correct reason,
   not by luck.

   Still changed to read the survivor back out of the ROOT SLOT
   (`js_shadow_slot_get(0)` / `global_slot`) instead of reusing the raw
   pointer captured before the cycle. That removes the dependence on the
   malloc-never-moves policy and is the stronger assertion anyway: it also
   proves the slot itself was maintained across the collection. The global
   case additionally gains the closure-magic intactness check the shadow
   case already had.

4. `decode_root_word_round_trips_each_representation` — pure bit math over
   synthetic addresses, no allocation, nothing to root. Unchanged.

fix(gc): minor sweep must not finalize unmarked old-gen objects (#6892) (#6933)

* fix(gc): minor sweep must not finalize unmarked old-gen objects (#6892)

A minor trace never marks the old generation: old-gen parents are black
leaves, reached only through dirty remembered-set pages. "Unmarked" in a
minor therefore means "unvisited", not "dead" — the sweep's own
`retain_all_forwarded_stubs` rule already spells this out for forwarding
stubs, and cycle.rs says it again ("Minor traces never mark the old
generation, so deadness there is only trusted for untenured nursery
headers"). `ArenaSweepObjectsState::process_object` did not honour it for
ordinary objects: any unmarked old-gen object took the `reclaim_dead_object`
path.

A minor never frees old-gen memory, so this looked harmless — but
`reclaim_dead_object` still runs `finalize_dead_arena_payload` on the
object, and that calls `layout_clear_for_ptr`, which drops the object's
entry from `LAYOUT_SLOT_MASKS` (plus its payload side tables and external
payload buffers). The live old-gen object is left in state
`GC_LAYOUT_SIDE_MASK` with no mask. The next `layout_note_slot` on it
rebuilds a mask from that single slot, so the following trace visits only
that one element and skips every other pointer slot — and the children
behind them are swept while still referenced. The mutator then reads a
recycled address and gets `undefined`, which is why the reported symptom
was a varying `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '<field>')`.

Fix: `unmarked_is_provably_dead()` — an unmarked object is only provably
dead when the trace covered its generation. Old-gen blocks are exempt in a
minor sweep, except blocks selected for old-page defrag this cycle, whose
live contents were evacuated during the same cycle (and whose block-level
reclaim needs `block_has_live` to stay false). Full traces are unchanged:
they visit every live parent, so mark-based old-gen reclaim stays sound.

Renames `retain_all_forwarded_stubs` to `minor_sweep`, which is what every
call site already passes and what both rules now key off.

Repro (issue #6892): the Milo compiler built by Perry, running
`emit-ir` over a file importing `std/fetch`. Before: throws. After: exits 0
and its LLVM IR is byte-identical to the same compiler under bun. The
env matrix that motivated the report (`PERRY_GEN_GC=0` and
`PERRY_WRITE_BARRIERS=0` pass, `PERRY_GEN_GC_EVACUATE=0` and
`PERRY_GC_VERIFY_EVACUATION=1` fail) is now uniformly green, as are
`PERRY_GC_FORCE_EVACUATE=1` and the two stress flags combined.

Note on old-page defrag input: minors previously fed
`old_page_account_swept_object(live=false)` for every unmarked old object,
i.e. phantom dead bytes derived from mark bits that say nothing about the

GC memory: shape-key typed layouts (#6893) + major-GC pacing; don't link CoreFoundation in every binary (#6939)

* perf(gc): #6893 key typed-shape layout descriptors by shape, not object

TYPED_LAYOUTS and LAYOUT_SLOT_MASKS stored a per-OBJECT copy of what is
per-SHAPE-constant layout data (slot_count + raw_f64_mask + pointer_mask).
On object-churn workloads every one of ~2M identical {v,w} objects got its
own 68-byte descriptor -> ~392 MB (measured: 73% of the live set; churn
peak RSS 830 MB).

Key the descriptor by the shared keys_array pointer (all same-shape objects
share one canonical keys array) via a new SHAPE_LAYOUTS thread_local. The
per-object maps are used only for objects that diverge (ambiguous same-keys/
different-types shapes) or carry no keys_array. Accelerator-only trust model:
a miss / stale entry / ambiguous shape / field-count mismatch all fall back
to the per-object map then the conservative scan -- never a wrong descriptor.
A keys_array pointer change (delete/add key) invalidates the typed layout in
set_object_keys_array (the shared descriptor lookup would otherwise miss the
old store-validation deopt trigger).

Result: churn_fixedarr 830 -> 262 MB peak RSS; behaviour-identical across the
GC benches + a polymorphic/expando/pointer-field stress test; all layout unit
tests pass. Env PERRY_SHAPE_LAYOUT_KEYED=0 restores the per-object maps.

* fix(build): don't drag CoreFoundation into every binary via Temporal

temporal_rs's `sys-local` feature resolves the system time zone through
iana_time_zone, which links CoreFoundation on macOS. Because Temporal's
namespace is registered in the always-linked runtime init, that CF dependency
was pulled into EVERY output binary -- so the runtime-only fast-link path
(which omits framework flags for launch speed) failed to link pure-compute
programs with undefined _CFRelease / _CFString* etc.

Drop `sys-local` and give Temporal.Now perry's own host system: the clock via
std SystemTime, the zone via perry's existing CF-free resolver
(crate::date::host_time_zone_name, TZ / /etc/localtime). Wired through
temporal_rs's public HostHooks traits; the provider-less Temporal.Now.*
convenience methods are gated on `compiled_data` (kept), not `sys-local`.

Net: iana_time_zone is no longer referenced, so no binary links CoreFoundation
for time zones; only binaries that genuinely need a framework link one.
Temporal.Now.* is unchanged (matches Node on timeZoneId/instant/plainDateTimeISO/
zonedDateTimeISO).

* perf(gc): major-GC pacing — escalate minor to full when the arena grows K× past the last full

A non-moving minor sweep cannot free array-growth forwarding stubs
(Array.prototype.push reallocations leave a stub per growth), so churn that
grows arrays accumulates stubs pinning every arena block -> unbounded RSS;
only a full mark-sweep reclaims them. Record the arena's clean live set after
each full (GC_LAST_FULL_ARENA_IN_USE_BYTES) and escalate a minor to a full once
live bytes exceed K x that baseline. Gated by an absolute floor (small heaps
never pay for a full) and the K x ratio (a large *stable* live set — retain
style — hovers near its own baseline, well under K x, so it is not
over-escalated). Env: PERRY_GC_MAJOR_PACING_FLOOR_MB (default 32, 0=disable),
PERRY_GC_MAJOR_PACING_GROWTH (default 2).

Measured (peak RSS, pacing ON vs OFF): churn (growing array) 1736 -> 258 MB;
churn_fixedarr 257 -> 260, tree 241 -> 251, cycles 171 -> 174, retain1 92 -> 92,
deeplist 78 -> 78 (stable-live sets unaffected). Combined with the shape-keyed
layout change, the canonical churn benchmark goes 2186 -> 258 MB.

- layout.rs: the GC_OBJ_TYPED_LAYOUT_INTACT invariant no longer implies a

fix(modules): exports aliasing a declared function are functions, not var getters (#6962)

`export const alias = impl` (where `impl` is a declared function) lands in
BOTH `exported_objects` and `exported_functions` — HIR records the alias
with the origin's FuncId. The var-vs-function classification only excluded
*declaration* names, so the alias was classified as an exported VARIABLE,
whose cross-module convention is a zero-arg getter. But origin-name
resolution points `perry_fn_<mod>__<alias>` at the #460 forwarding wrapper
— the function BODY — so the "getter" call actually INVOKED the function.

Two user-visible failures, both covered by the new test:

- Reading the binding yielded `impl(<zeroed args>)`'s return value instead
  of the closure: `typeof NS.alias` was `number`, and calling it threw
  `TypeError: value is not a function`.
- The source module's own namespace populator hit the same path while
  building its namespace object, so the function RAN during module init.

Fix, in `run_pipeline`:
- exclude `exported_functions` alias names from `exported_var_names`
  (the consumer-side binding read), and
- resolve alias entries in the namespace-entry builder to the ORIGIN
  function's wrap symbol — `LocalFunction` for same-module,
  `ForeignFunction` (under the origin name) for cross-module — instead of
  falling through to the `ForeignVar` getter.

out of this shape (`export const decodeSync = decodeUnknownSync`,
`decodeEffect = decodeUnknownEffect`, …). Diagnosed by disassembling the
module's `__init_body`: sibling exports lowered to
`js_closure_alloc_singleton` while the aliases lowered to a direct
`bl perry_fn_…__decodeEffect` with zeroed argument registers.
